q: Which group gained increased importance in the post-Gupta society due to land grants?
qs.e: In the post-Gupta period, the practice of land grants intensified, where kings and feudatories donated tax-free lands to Brahmins. This made the Brahmin class economically and socially powerful. They not only received income from land but also played roles in administrative and judicial functions. Thus, the political influence of Brahmins increased, and they rose to the highest position in society. Land grants strengthened the feudal system and transformed Brahmins into a landowning class.
qs.kf:
☛ Who received the most land grants in the post-Gupta period? → Brahmins
☛ What was the main reason for land grants to Brahmins? → Religious merit and administrative assistance
☛ What system did land grants give rise to? → Feudal system
☛ What importance did Brahmins gain in the post-Gupta period? → Political and economic importance
☛ Which class became landowners due to land grants? → Brahmin class

q: Under which dynasty the rulers wrote their achievements in prashasti ?
qs.e: During the Gupta period, rulers recorded their achievements in prashastis (eulogistic inscriptions). These were composed in Sanskrit by court poets, detailing the king's genealogy, military victories, and religious activities. The most famous is the Prayag Prashasti of Samudragupta, inscribed on the Allahabad Pillar and composed by poet Harisena. The purpose was to glorify the ruler and legitimize his authority. Gupta kings used prashastis to immortalize their administrative and military accomplishments, establishing a tradition that influenced later dynasties.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed the Prayag Prashasti? → Harisena
☛ Where is Samudragupta's prashasti found? → Allahabad pillar
☛ What language were Gupta prashastis written in? → Sanskrit
☛ What does prashasti mean? → Eulogy or description of achievements
☛ Who was the most powerful Gupta ruler? → Samudragupta

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Who administered the agrahara lands during the post-Gupta period?
qs.e: During the post-Gupta period, the administration of agrahara lands was carried out by Brahmins. Agrahara lands were those donated by the king to Brahmins, often recorded on stone or copper plates. These Brahmins enjoyed tax-free rights and exercised administrative and judicial powers over these lands. This practice became more prominent after the Gupta period and contributed to the strengthening of the feudal system. Village assemblies and feudal lords were associated with the administration of other types of lands, while monks were generally not involved in land administration. Thus, agrahara lands were exclusively administered by Brahmins.
qs.kf:
☛ To whom were agrahara lands donated? → Brahmins
☛ On what were land grants inscribed in the post-Gupta period? → Stone or copper plates
☛ What tax status did agrahara lands have? → Tax-free
☛ Which system strengthened in the post-Gupta period? → Feudal system
☛ What type of land did village assemblies administer? → Common village land

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Harishena was the court poet of:
qs.e: Harishena was the court poet of Samudragupta, a prominent ruler of the Gupta dynasty. Harishena composed the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti), which describes Samudragupta's conquests and achievements. This inscription is written in Sanskrit and is considered a crucial source of Gupta history. Samudragupta is also known as the 'Napoleon of India.' Harishena served as a poet, minister, and envoy. He is famous for detailing Samudragupta's military exploits and administrative skills.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the court poet of Samudragupta? → Harishena
☛ Who wrote the Prayag Prashasti? → Harishena
☛ What is Samudragupta known as? → Napoleon of India
☛ In which language is the Prayag Prashasti written? → Sanskrit
☛ Who was the most powerful Gupta ruler? → Samudragupta

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1
q: What was the officer responsible for looking after military stores during the reign of the Gupta Empire called?
qs.e: During the Gupta Empire, the military administration had designated officers for various duties. The Ranabhandagarika was the officer responsible for looking after military stores, including weapons, rations, and other essential supplies. This role was crucial for maintaining combat readiness. Other options: Pilupati was the officer in charge of elephants, Mahapratihara was the chief gatekeeper or palace guard, and Vishayapati was the provincial governor. The term 'Ranabhandagarika' is derived from 'rana' (war) and 'bhandagara' (storehouse). This position highlights the organized nature of Gupta military logistics.
qs.kf:
☛ Officer in charge of elephants in Gupta Empire → Pilupati
☛ Chief gatekeeper in Gupta Empire → Mahapratihara
☛ Provincial governor in Gupta Empire → Vishayapati
☛ Officer for military stores in Gupta Empire → Ranabhandagarika
☛ Gupta military administration officials → Ranabhandagarika, Pilupati, Mahapratihara

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 2
q: During the Gupta Empire, the terms 'Chata' and 'Bhata' were used for ________.
qs.e: In the Gupta Empire, the terms Chata and Bhata referred to two categories of soldiers. Chata meant regular soldiers, who were part of the permanent standing army. Bhata meant irregular soldiers, who were temporarily recruited during wars. The Gupta military was well-organized, and these troops were used strategically. These terms specifically applied to infantry, distinct from cavalry or elephant riders. Chata and Bhata were essential for maintaining the empire's defense and expansion.
qs.kf:
☛ Chata referred to which type of soldier? → Regular soldier
☛ Bhata referred to which type of soldier? → Irregular soldier
☛ Chata and Bhata were part of which branch of the army? → Infantry
☛ What was the permanent army called in the Gupta Empire? → Chata
☛ What were temporary soldiers called in the Gupta Empire? → Bhata

q: Who of the following is one of the nine gems of Chandragupta II?
qs.e: Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) had 'Navratnas' (nine gems) in his court, comprising scholars and artists. Varahamihira was a renowned astronomer and mathematician, author of 'Panchasiddhantika' and 'Brihat Samhita'. He was one of the navratnas. Other options include Vishakhadatta (playwright, author of Mudrarakshasa) and Brahmagupta (mathematician, author of Brahmasphutasiddhanta), but Brahmagupta lived after the Gupta period. Moggallana was a Buddhist monk associated with Chandragupta Maurya. Thus, only Varahamihira is counted among the nine gems of Chandragupta II.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was not among the navratnas of Chandragupta II? → Brahmagupta
☛ Which book did Varahamihira write? → Brihat Samhita
☛ Vishakhadatta's famous work? → Mudrarakshasa
☛ What was Chandragupta II's title? → Vikramaditya
☛ Which mathematician was in the navratnas? → Varahamihira

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 1
q: The term 'Bhukti' in post-Gupta polity referred to:
qs.e: In the post-Gupta period, the term Bhukti was used for a province in the administrative system. This term is primarily found in inscriptions of later dynasties like the Pushyabhuti dynasty (Harshavardhana) and the Chalukya dynasty. A Bhukti denoted an administrative region that was divided into several Vishayas (districts). The head of a Bhukti was called Bhogika or Uparika. The word is derived from the root 'bhuj', meaning 'an area to be enjoyed or ruled'. Other terms were used for tax, officer, and king in that period.
qs.kf:
☛ For which administrative unit was Bhukti used? → Province
☛ Who was the head of a Bhukti? → Bhogika or Uparika
☛ Bhukti belongs to which period? → Post-Gupta period
☛ From which root is the word Bhukti derived? → Bhuj
☛ Which smaller unit was under a Bhukti? → Vishaya

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Who succeeded Chandragupta I as the ruler of the Gupta Empire?
qs.e: After the founder Sri Gupta, Ghatotkacha Gupta and then Chandragupta I ruled the Gupta Empire. Chandragupta I strengthened his position by marrying the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi. He was succeeded by his son Samudragupta, often called the 'Napoleon of India'. Samudragupta conquered most of northern India and also led expeditions to the south. His victories are recorded in the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), composed by his court poet Harisena. Among the other options, Ramagupta was a lesser-known ruler, Kumaragupta I was a later ruler, and Skandagupta came even later.
qs.kf:
☛ Name of Chandragupta I's wife → Kumaradevi
☛ Samudragupta is known by which title → Napoleon of India
☛ Who composed the Prayag Prashasti → Harisena
☛ Reign period of Samudragupta → c. 335-375 CE
☛ Who was the founder of the Gupta Empire → Sri Gupta

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 3
q: The most important source for Samudragupta's reign is:
qs.e: The most important source for Samudragupta's reign is the Prayagraj Prashasti (also known as the Allahabad Pillar Inscription composed by Harishena). This inscription is written in Sanskrit and provides detailed information about Samudragupta's military campaigns, conquests, administrative policies, and cultural achievements. Harishena, a court poet and minister of Samudragupta, composed this eulogy. The inscription describes Samudragupta with titles such as Kaviraj and Lichchhavi Dauhitra. This pillar inscription is crucial for reconstructing the history of the Gupta period. Other options like Arthashastra (Mauryan period), Milindapanho (Buddhist text), and Vishnu Purana (Puranic text) are not primary sources for Samudragupta.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the court poet of Samudragupta? → Harishena
☛ In which language was Prayagraj Prashasti written? → Sanskrit
☛ Which title was given to Samudragupta? → Kaviraj
☛ Who was the founder of the Gupta dynasty? → Shri Gupta
☛ What was Samudragupta's reign period? → 335–375 CE

q: Which official in the Gupta administration was responsible for peace and war matters?
qs.e: In the Gupta administration, Sandhi-Vigrahika was the official responsible for peace (sandhi) and war (vigraha) matters. This position is comparable to a modern minister of external affairs or defense. Vishayapati was the administrative head of a district or province, handling revenue collection and local order. Mahapratihara served as the chief gatekeeper or security officer of the royal palace. Mahadandanayaka was the commander of the army or a judicial officer, dealing with military and legal affairs. The Gupta administration had a well-organized hierarchy of officials, reflecting efficient governance. Understanding these roles is important for exams covering ancient Indian polity.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was responsible for peace and war in Gupta administration? → Sandhi-Vigrahika
☛ What was the military and judicial chief called in Gupta period? → Mahadandanayaka
☛ What was the role of Vishayapati in Gupta administration? → Provincial administration and revenue collection
☛ Who was the chief security officer of the Gupta royal palace? → Mahapratihara
☛ Which Gupta official was equivalent to a modern defense minister? → Sandhi-Vigrahika

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Who handled judicial matters in the provinces during the reign of the Gupta Empire?
qs.e: During the Gupta Empire, provinces were known as Bhukti and their administration was headed by an Uparika. The Uparika was not only the administrative head but also handled judicial matters in the provinces. He was appointed by the king and had the authority to hear both criminal and civil disputes. At the village level, the Gramika settled minor disputes, while higher judicial cases were heard in the king's court. Ayuktaka is not mentioned in provincial judiciary records. Thus, the Uparika was responsible for judicial affairs in the provinces during the Gupta period.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the head of provincial administration in the Gupta Empire? → Uparika
☛ What were provinces called in the Gupta period? → Bhukti
☛ Who handled judicial functions at the village level in Gupta times? → Gramika
☛ Who appointed the Uparika in the Gupta Empire? → King
☛ Where was the highest court in the Gupta period? → Royal court

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following terms was used for tanks or ponds in Gupta records?
qs.e: In the Gupta inscriptions, the term 'Tadaga' was used for tanks or ponds. This word is derived from Sanskrit and refers to a water reservoir. Among the other options, 'Nadi' means river or stream, 'Kshetra' refers to land or field, and 'Prapa' denotes a water-shed or a place for drinking water. During the Gupta period, water resource management was developed, and tanks were built for irrigation and drinking purposes. Thus, specific terminology was used in Gupta records for water bodies, with 'Tadaga' being the primary term for tanks.
qs.kf:
☛ Which term was used for tanks in Gupta inscriptions? → Tadaga
☛ What does 'Nadi' mean? → River or stream
☛ What does 'Prapa' mean? → Water-shed or drinking place
☛ Why were tanks built in the Gupta period? → For irrigation and drinking water
☛ What language were Gupta inscriptions usually in? → Sanskrit

q: Which era is called golden age of ancient India?
qs.e: The Gupta Empire (c. 320-550 CE) is known as the 'Golden Age' of ancient India. This period witnessed remarkable progress in literature, art, science, mathematics and philosophy. Chandragupta I established the Gupta dynasty in 320 CE, and Samudragupta expanded the empire. Under Chandragupta Vikramaditya, the empire reached its zenith. Renowned figures like Kalidasa (literature), Aryabhata (mathematics), and the establishment of Nalanda University belong to this era. Texts like Bhagavata Purana and Amarakosha were also composed during this period. Thus, the Gupta Empire is called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Gupta Empire? → Chandragupta I
☛ Who was the greatest Gupta ruler? → Samudragupta
☛ Who was the famous poet of the Gupta period? → Kalidasa
☛ Who was the famous mathematician of the Gupta period? → Aryabhata
☛ Which university was established during the Gupta period? → Nalanda University

q: The ‘Prayaga prashasti’ also known as the ‘Allahabad pillar’ is composed in praise of which of the following rulers?
qs.e: The Prayaga Prashasti, also known as the Allahabad Pillar, is an inscription composed in praise of Samudragupta of the Gupta Empire. It was written in Sanskrit by the court poet Harisena. The pillar was originally erected by Ashoka, but later Samudragupta inscribed his achievements on it. The inscription details Samudragupta's military conquests, including his defeat of kings in South India, and his administrative policies. It is a crucial source for understanding the Gupta period history.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed the Prayaga Prashasti? → Harisena
☛ Who originally erected the Allahabad Pillar? → Ashoka
☛ Samudragupta is known by which title? → Napoleon of India
☛ Who was the founder of the Gupta Empire? → Sri Gupta
☛ To which dynasty did Samudragupta belong? → Gupta dynasty

q: Who composed the ‘Prayag Prashasti’ (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), detailing the conquests of Samudragupta?
qs.e: The 'Prayag Prashasti' (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) was composed by Harisena, who was the court poet and commander of Samudragupta. This inscription is written in Sanskrit and is a crucial historical source of the Gupta period. It details Samudragupta's military conquests, territorial expansion, and his personal qualities. Harisena addresses Samudragupta with titles like 'Kaviraj' and 'Lichchhavi Dauhitra'. The inscription provides valuable information about the political and cultural conditions of ancient India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed the Prayag Prashasti? → Harisena
☛ In which language is the Allahabad Pillar Inscription written? → Sanskrit
☛ Which Gupta ruler's achievements are described in the Prayag Prashasti? → Samudragupta
☛ What was Harisena's position? → Commander and poet
☛ What title was given to Samudragupta in the Prayag Prashasti? → Kaviraj

q: According to the Prayaga Prashasti, Samudragupta is compared to which god associated with wealth?
qs.e: The Prayaga Prashasti is an inscription composed by Harishena during the reign of Samudragupta. It praises Samudragupta by comparing him to four gods: Varuna, Indra, Yama, and Kubera. Among these, Samudragupta is compared to Kubera, the god of wealth, highlighting his immense prosperity and economic strength. Kubera is revered in Hindu mythology as the lord of riches and treasures. This comparison underscores the Gupta ruler's wealth and affluence.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed the Prayaga Prashasti? → Harishena
☛ To which gods is Samudragupta compared in the Prayaga Prashasti? → Varuna, Indra, Yama, Kubera
☛ Which god is associated with wealth among them? → Kubera
☛ Prayaga Prashasti belongs to which empire? → Gupta Empire
☛ What was Samudragupta's title? → Parakramanka

q: What administrative change characterized the political structure of post-Gupta India?
o: Formation of a central bureaucracy under one emperor
Introduction of democratic village assemblies across India
Rise of smaller kingdoms under hereditary rulers
Replacement of kingship with religious councils
qs.e: After the decline of the Gupta Empire, India witnessed a shift from a centralized imperial structure to a fragmented political landscape. Numerous smaller kingdoms emerged, each ruled by hereditary rulers who exercised independent control over their territories. This change resulted from the disintegration of the Gupta Empire and the rise of regional powers. The period saw the development of feudalism, where land grants to local chiefs and officials increased their autonomy. Thus, the administrative structure became decentralized, with power passing from one generation to the next within the same family.
qs.kf:
☛ What characterized the political structure of post-Gupta India? → Rise of smaller kingdoms under hereditary rulers
☛ Which administrative system developed after the Gupta decline? → Feudal system
☛ To whom were land grants given in post-Gupta period? → Local rulers and officials
☛ What type of rule did Harsha's empire represent? → Centralized but dependent on feudatories
☛ On what basis was kingship acquired in post-Gupta India? → Hereditary basis

q: Who were the "Samantas" in the post-Gupta period?
qs.e: In the post-Gupta period, the term 'Samantas' referred to feudal lords who received land grants from the king. These Samantas held administrative, economic, and military power in their regions. They provided revenue and military support to the king but governed their territories with autonomy. This system was part of the feudal structure that led to decentralization of power through land grants. The rise of Samantas occurred after the decline of the Gupta Empire and shaped the medieval Indian political framework. They were not religious heads, farmers, or architects, but feudal rulers who controlled local administration and collected taxes.
qs.kf:
☛ What did 'Samantas' mean in the post-Gupta period? → Feudal lords
☛ In what form did Samantas receive land? → As grants
☛ What did Samantas provide to the king? → Revenue and military aid
☛ After the decline of which empire did Samantas emerge? → Gupta Empire
☛ Which system were the Samantas a part of? → Feudal system

q: What was the role of guilds (shrenis) in post-Gupta India?
qs.e: In post-Gupta India, shrenis (guilds) played a crucial role in regulating trade and crafts. These organizations set commercial standards, ensured product quality, and resolved disputes among members. They also assisted in tax collection and provided financial support to the king. Shrenis were not responsible for administration, military service, or religious reforms. They had their own rules and banners, and sometimes participated in local governance, but their primary focus was on commerce and craftsmanship.
qs.kf:
☛ What did shrenis regulate? → Trade and crafts
☛ What was the main function of shrenis in post-Gupta period? → Regulation of trade
☛ What did shrenis have? → Their own rules and banners
☛ In what did shrenis assist? → Tax collection
☛ In which area were shrenis active? → Commerce and crafts

q: The first residential university of the world, Nalanda, was established under the patronage of which of the following rulers?
qs.e: Nalanda University, the world's first residential university, was established under the patronage of Kumaragupta I (415-455 CE), a ruler of the Gupta dynasty. Located in present-day Bihar, it became a major center for Mahayana Buddhism and attracted students from across Asia. Chinese travelers like Xuanzang and Yijing provided detailed accounts of its grandeur. The university was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji in the 12th century. It housed thousands of students and a vast library, and its curriculum included subjects like philosophy, medicine, and astronomy.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Nalanda University → Kumaragupta I
☛ Destroyer of Nalanda → Bakhtiyar Khilji (1193 CE)
☛ Famous Chinese visitors to Nalanda → Xuanzang and Yijing
☛ Period of establishment of Nalanda → 5th century (c. 427 CE)
☛ Religion associated with Nalanda → Mahayana Buddhism

name: All Questions · Q1–14
sub: Ancient History - Sangam Age & South Indian Dynasties

q: The time period of the Chola Dynasty in South India was _______.
qs.e: The Chola Dynasty was one of the greatest dynasties of South India. Its prominent period is considered from the 9th century to the 13th century CE. This period, known as the 'Medieval Cholas', was founded by King Vijayalaya who captured Thanjavur in the 9th century. The Chola Empire reached its zenith under the reigns of Rajaraja Chola I and Rajendra Chola I. During this time, the Cholas extended their influence over South India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, and even Southeast Asia. The Chola period is renowned for its achievements in art, architecture, literature, and administration. The Brihadishwara Temple is an outstanding example of their architecture. The Chola Empire declined in the 13th century, giving way to the Pandyas and Hoysalas.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Chola dynasty? → Vijayalaya
☛ What was the capital of the Chola Empire? → Thanjavur (Tanjore)
☛ Which is the most famous temple of the Chola period? → Brihadishwara Temple
☛ Who was the last ruler of the Chola dynasty? → Rajendra Chola III
☛ Which religion was patronized by the Cholas? → Hinduism, especially Shaivism

q: Which of the following dynasties does NOT belong to the Sangam Period?
qs.e: The Sangam Period is the early historical period of South India, approximately from 300 BCE to 300 CE. During this period, three major dynasties - Chera, Chola, and Pandya - are mentioned in Sangam literature. These were ancient rulers of South India. The Gupta dynasty was a North Indian dynasty that ruled from approximately 320 CE to 550 CE and is not part of the Sangam Period. Hence, the Gupta dynasty does not belong to the Sangam Period.
qs.kf:
☛ Major dynasties of Sangam Period → Chera, Chola, Pandya
☛ Language of Sangam literature → Tamil
☛ Time of Gupta dynasty → Approximately 320-550 CE
☛ Time of Sangam Period → 300 BCE to 300 CE
☛ Rulers of Sangam Period → Chera, Chola, Pandya

q: Which of the following texts is considered the earliest Tamil grammar work?
qs.e: Tolkappiyam is considered the earliest Tamil grammar work. It was composed during the Sangam period (approximately 500 BCE to 300 CE). Its author is Tolkappiyar. This text provides a detailed description of Tamil phonology, word formation, sentence structure, and semantics. Tolkappiyam is divided into three books: Eluttadikaram (sounds), Soladikaram (words), and Poruladikaram (meaning/subject matter). It is the foundation of Tamil literature and served as a basis for all later Tamil grammar works. The text is highly revered in Tamil culture and is one of the oldest extant Indian linguistic works.
qs.kf:
☛ Who authored Tolkappiyam? → Tolkappiyar
☛ To which period does Tolkappiyam belong? → Sangam period
☛ How many books are in Tolkappiyam? → Three (Eluttadikaram, Soladikaram, Poruladikaram)
☛ What is the oldest extant Tamil grammar work? → Tolkappiyam
☛ What is the subject of Tolkappiyam? → Tamil grammar and poetics

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 2
q: What is the central theme of the first five anthologies (Kuruntokai, Narrinai, Akananuru, Ainkurunuru, and Kalittokai) of the Ettuttokai in the Sangam literature?
qs.e: In Sangam literature, the Ettuttokai (eight anthologies) is divided into two main categories: Akam (love/interior) and Puram (war/exterior). The first five anthologies mentioned—Kuruntokai, Narrinai, Akananuru, Ainkurunuru, and Kalittokai—all belong to the Akam category. These works focus on love, union, separation, and intimate human emotions, often using nature imagery to convey feelings. In contrast, Puram deals with war, heroism, and public life, which are covered in the remaining three anthologies (Purananuru, Patitupathu, and Patirruppattu). Therefore, the central theme of these five anthologies is Akam.
qs.kf:
☛ How many anthologies are in Ettuttokai? → 8
☛ What does Akam deal with? → Love (interior)
☛ What does Puram deal with? → War (exterior)
☛ Which category does Kuruntokai belong to? → Akam
☛ In which language was Sangam literature composed? → Tamil

q: Which states were ruled by the earlier Chera dynasty?
A. Tamil Nadu and Kerala
B. Bengal and Orissa
C. Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim
D. Maharashtra and Gujarat
qs.e: The ancient Chera dynasty ruled over the regions of present-day Tamil Nadu and Kerala in South India. It was one of the three major Sangam period kingdoms, with its capital at Vanji. The Cheras were known for their maritime trade, especially with the Romans and Greeks. Prominent rulers included Nedum Cheral Adan and Senguttuvan, who is credited with introducing the worship of Pattini Devi. The Cheras exported spices, pearls, and ivory. The dynasty declined around the 3rd century CE and was later overshadowed by the Pandyas and Cholas.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the capital of the Chera dynasty? → Vanji
☛ During which period did the Cheras flourish? → Sangam period
☛ What is Senguttuvan famous for? → Introducing Pattini worship
☛ Which empire did the Cheras trade with? → Roman Empire
☛ What was the emblem of the Chera dynasty? → Bow and arrow

q: Silappadikaram, a famous Tamil epic, was composed by:
qs.e: Silappadikaram is one of the five great epics of ancient Tamil literature. It was composed by Ilango Adigal, a prince of the Chera dynasty. The epic is divided into three parts: Puhar Kandam, Madurai Kandam, and Vanji Kandam. It narrates the story of the merchant Kovalan and his wife Kannagi. This work is a valuable source of Tamil culture, trade, and politics. Chathanar wrote Manimekalai, Thiruvalluvar wrote Thirukkural, and Kalidas was a Sanskrit poet.
qs.kf:
☛ Author of Silappadikaram → Ilango Adigal
☛ Main characters of Silappadikaram → Kovalan and Kannagi
☛ Author of Manimekalai → Chathanar
☛ Author of Thirukkural → Thiruvalluvar
☛ Tamil epic among five great epics → Silappadikaram

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following is not one of the Ettuttokai (Eight Anthologies) of the Sangam literature?
qs.e: The Eight Anthologies (Ettuttokai) of Sangam literature include Purananuru, Kuruntokai, Narrinai, Akananuru, Aingurunuru, Pathirruppattu, Paripadal, and Kalittokai. Tolkappiyam is a grammar text and not part of the Sangam anthologies. It is one of the oldest Tamil grammar works, authored by Tolkappiyar. Hence, Tolkappiyam is not one of the Ettuttokai.
qs.kf:
☛ Period of Sangam literature → 300 BCE to 300 CE
☛ Total anthologies in Ettuttokai → 8
☛ Author of Tolkappiyam → Tolkappiyar
☛ Theme of Purananuru → War and heroism
☛ Theme of Kuruntokai → Love (short poems)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which among the following contains a collection of eight poetic anthologies from ancient Tamil literature?
qs.e: In ancient Tamil literature, the collection of eight poetic anthologies is known as 'Ettuttokai', which literally means 'eight collections'. It is a key part of the Sangam literature, composed between 300 BCE and 300 CE. Ettuttokai includes anthologies such as Akananuru, Purananuru, Aingurunuru, Patirruppattu, Paripadal, Kalittokai, Kuruntogai, and Nattinai. These works cover themes of love, war, kings, and society. Among the other options, Tolkappiyam is a grammar text, Pattuppattu is a collection of ten idylls, and Silappatikaram is an epic.
qs.kf:
☛ Ettuttokai literally means → eight collections
☛ Ettuttokai belongs to → Sangam literature
☛ Period of Ettuttokai → 300 BCE to 300 CE
☛ Number of anthologies in Ettuttokai → eight
☛ Famous anthologies → Akananuru and Purananuru

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which aspect of life is explored under the theme of akam in Sangam literary works?
qs.e: Sangam literature is broadly divided into two themes: Akam (interior) and Puram (exterior). The Akam theme explores the personal and emotional aspects of human life, particularly love and romantic experiences. It describes various stages of love such as union, separation, and longing. This theme is expressed by Sangam poets through natural imagery and symbols. In contrast, the Puram theme deals with public life, including war, politics, and valor. Thus, Akam primarily focuses on love and personal relationships. The classification into Akam and Puram is a unique feature of Sangam poetics, reflecting the depth of Tamil literary tradition.
qs.kf:
☛ What are the two main themes of Sangam literature? → Akam and Puram
☛ What does Akam theme mean? → Inner or private life
☛ What does Puram theme relate to? → War, politics, valor
☛ In which language was Sangam literature composed? → Tamil
☛ What is the time period of Sangam age? → 300 BCE to 300 CE

q: What is the main focus of the Sangam anthologies, Purananuru and Patirruppattu, from the Ettuttokai collection?
o: Heroism and praises of kings and their deeds
qs.e: The Ettuttokai collection comprises eight anthologies, among which Purananuru and Patirruppattu primarily focus on heroism and praises of kings. Purananuru consists of 400 poems describing war, valor, and deeds of kings. Patirruppattu contains poems in praise of Chera kings. These works are part of Sangam literature and emphasize heroism and glorification of kings, rather than love, nature, or religion.
qs.kf:
☛ How many anthologies are in the Ettuttokai? → Eight
☛ How many poems are in Purananuru? → 400
☛ Which dynasty does Patirruppattu praise? → Chera
☛ What is the period of Sangam literature? → 300 BCE to 300 CE
☛ What is the main theme of Purananuru? → Heroism and deeds of kings

q: Who defeated Harshavardhana on the Narmada frontier?
qs.e: Harshavardhana (606-647 AD) was a powerful emperor who ruled over a large part of North India. He attempted to expand his empire southward but was defeated by the Chalukya king Pulakesin II (610-642 AD) on the banks of the Narmada river. This battle took place around 618-619 AD. After this defeat, Harsha did not attempt to expand further south, and the Narmada river became the boundary between the two empires. Pulakesin II was one of the greatest rulers of the Chalukya dynasty, ruling from their capital Vatapi (present-day Badami). His victory over Harsha is mentioned in the Aihole inscription, which praises his military achievements. This event highlights the strength of the Chalukya kingdom in the Deccan region during the early medieval period.
qs.kf:
☛ Which festival did Harsha celebrate at Kannauj? → Kumbh Mela (at Prayag)
☛ To which dynasty did Pulakesin II belong? → Chalukya dynasty
☛ Who was the court poet of Harshavardhana? → Banabhatta
☛ What was the capital of the Chalukyas? → Vatapi (Badami)
☛ What are the literary works of Harsha? → Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika

q: In which language was the Sangam literature of South India, composed between 300 BCE and 300 CE, primarily written?
qs.e: Sangam literature is the earliest known literature of South India, composed between approximately 300 BCE and 300 CE. It was primarily written in the Tamil language. The Sangam period is considered the golden age of Tamil society, culture, and politics. This literature consists of two main collections: Ettuthokai (Eight Anthologies) and Pattupattu (Ten Idylls). The poems cover themes such as love, war, governance, and nature. Sangam literature forms the foundation of Tamil language and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ In which language is Sangam literature written? → Tamil
☛ When was Sangam literature composed? → 300 BCE to 300 CE
☛ What are the two main collections of Sangam literature? → Ettuthokai and Pattupattu
☛ What themes are covered in Sangam literature? → Love, war, governance, nature
☛ Which period is considered the golden age of Tamil culture? → Sangam period

q: Which Sangam text, from the 2nd century CE, is an epic about a chaste wife’s devotion?
qs.e: Silappatikaram is a famous Tamil epic from the 2nd century CE, written by Ilango Adigal. It is an epic about a chaste wife's devotion and fidelity towards her husband. The protagonist, Kannagi, symbolizes unwavering love and sacrifice for her husband Kovalan. It is one of the five great epics of Tamil literature and is considered a masterpiece of moral and ethical values. Other options: Pattuppattu is a collection of Sangam poems, Tolkappiyam is a grammar text, and Manimekalai is a Buddhist epic. Silappatikaram emphasizes the ideals of dharma (righteousness) and conjugal fidelity.
qs.kf:

☛ Who is the heroine of Silappatikaram? → Kannagi
☛ What is the main theme of Silappatikaram? → Devotion and justice

☛ In which century was Silappatikaram composed? → 2nd century CE

q: The Tamil literary work Iraiyanar Ahapporul is dated to which century?
qs.e: The Tamil literary work Iraiyanar Ahapporul is dated to the 8th century CE. It is a treatise on poetics composed by the poet Iraiyanar and is considered one of the earliest works on Tamil rhetoric and poetics. The text deals with the themes of love and eroticism, and it represents the development of Tamil grammar and poetics after the Tolkappiyam.

q: Which Chinese traveller came and stayed in Nalanda both as a student and a teacher?
qs.e: Hiuen Tsang was a Chinese Buddhist monk and traveler who visited India in the 7th century. He stayed at Nalanda University first as a student and later as a teacher. He spent about 15 years in India and wrote the travelogue 'Si-Yu-Ki' (Records of the Western World), which provides detailed accounts of Nalanda and other regions. Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of Emperor Harshavardhana and was honored in his court. He carried 657 Sanskrit texts to China and had them translated. Other options: Fa-Hien (5th century), I-Tsing (late 7th century), and Kublai Khan (Mongol ruler) did not stay as both student and teacher at Nalanda.
qs.kf:

☛ Chinese traveler during Harshavardhana's reign → Hiuen Tsang

☛ Chinese traveler who was both student and teacher at Nalanda → Hiuen Tsang
☛ Chinese traveler who carried 657 Buddhist texts to China → Hiuen Tsang

q: Who wrote Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda?
qs.e: The three Sanskrit plays Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, and Nagananda were written by Emperor Harshavardhana (606-647 AD). Harsha was not only a great ruler but also a renowned literary figure. He personally composed these plays. Ratnavali is a love story, Priyadarshika deals with the romance between Princess Priyadarshika and King Udayana, and Nagananda is a play influenced by Buddhism. Harsha's court included scholars like Banabhatta, who wrote Harshacharita. Harsha made Kannauj his capital and organized the Kumbh Mela at Prayag.

q: The Vardhan dynasty, was also known by which of the following names?
qs.e: The Vardhan dynasty was also known as the Pushyabhuti dynasty. It was established in the late 6th century in northern India with its capital at Thanesar (present-day Haryana). The founder of this dynasty was Pushyabhuti, while the most famous ruler was Harshavardhana (Harsha), who ruled from 606 to 647 CE. Under Harsha's reign, the dynasty reached its zenith and he also made Kannauj his capital. The dynasty is mentioned in Harshacharita, written by Banabhatta. After Harsha's death, the dynasty declined.

☛ Capital of Vardhan dynasty → Thanesar (early)

☛ Chinese traveler during Harsha's period → Hiuen Tsang

q: Yagnavarman, Sardulavarman and Anantavarman were the kings of which of the following kingdoms?
qs.e: Yagnavarman, Sardulavarman and Anantavarman were prominent rulers of the Maukhari dynasty who ruled the region of Kanauj. The Maukharis played a significant role in 6th-7th century North India. Yagnavarman shifted their capital to Kanauj and established it as a major power. Sardulavarman expanded the kingdom and clashed with the Gupta rulers. Anantavarman was the last great Maukhari king, who was defeated by Harsha. The Maukhari kingdom emerged after the decline of the Guptas of Magadha and later merged into Harsha's empire.
qs.kf:

☛ To which dynasty did Harsha belong? → Pushyabhuti dynasty

q: Who came to India during the reign of Harshavardhana?
qs.e: During the reign of Harshavardhana (606-647 CE), the Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited India. He arrived in India in 630 CE and stayed for about 14 years. He documented his journey in the book 'Si-yu-ki' (Buddhist Records). Hiuen Tsang studied at Nalanda University and provided detailed accounts of the social, religious, and political conditions under Harshavardhana. Other travelers include Fa-hien (Gupta period, 401-410 CE), Itsing (late 7th century), and Alberuni (11th century with Mahmud Ghazni).

q: Which Chinese traveler mentions a Maitraka ruler named Shiladitya?
qs.e: Hiuen Tsang was a famous Chinese Buddhist monk and traveler who visited India in the 7th century. In his travelogue 'Si-Yu-Ki' (Great Records of the Western World), he mentions a Maitraka ruler named Shiladitya (II). This ruler was the king of Vallabhi (Gujarat), and Hiuen Tsang visited his kingdom during his reign. Shiladitya welcomed Hiuen Tsang and helped him in studying Buddhist teachings. q: The Harsha inscription of 554 CE mentions the rise of Yajnavarman from which place?
qs.e: The Harsha inscription of 554 CE, located at Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh, mentions the rise of Yajnavarman from Gaya. Yajnavarman was a ruler of the Maukhari dynasty. The Maukhari dynasty initially rose in the Magadha region, but Yajnavarman's specific association is with Gaya. Gaya is a historically significant city in Bihar, considered sacred in both Buddhist and Hindu traditions. The Harsha inscription records the rise of Yajnavarman from Gaya, indicating the extent of Maukhari influence. This inscription is an important source for early medieval Indian history.

q: Who was the court poet of King Harshavardhana?
qs.e: The court poet of King Harshavardhana (606-647 AD) was Banabhatta. Banabhatta was a great Sanskrit poet and writer. He composed the famous work "Harshacharita", which is a historical biography of Harshavardhana and is considered an important text in Sanskrit literature. Banabhatta also wrote the renowned prose poem "Kadambari". Harshavardhana himself wrote plays like "Nagananda", "Ratnavali", and "Priyadarshika". Banabhatta is regarded as one of the greatest prose writers in Sanskrit literature.

qs.e: The Chinese Buddhist monk and traveller Hiuen Tsang (also known as Xuanzang) visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana (606–647 CE), a prominent ruler of North India. Hiuen Tsang travelled to India between 630 and 645 CE and spent considerable time at Harsha's court. He described Harsha's administration, religious tolerance, and patronage of Buddhism in detail. Hiuen Tsang also visited and studied at the famous Nalanda University. His work 'Si-yu-ki' (Great Tang Records on the Western Regions) is a valuable source for Indian history and culture. q: Which Gupta emperor established his capital at Sakala?
qs.e: The Huna emperor Mihirakula established his capital at Sakala (modern Sialkot, Pakistan). Mihirakula belonged to the Huna dynasty, which emerged after the decline of the Gupta Empire. He is notorious for his cruelty and persecution of Buddhism. He ruled over Kashmir and Punjab regions. The Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang mentioned Mihirakula's atrocities. Sakala was an important trade and cultural center in ancient times. Mihirakula is also depicted in the famous play 'Mudrarakshasa'.

q: Who among the following was considered the first notable king of the Pushyabhuti dynasty, ruling from 580-605 CE?
qs.e: The first notable king of the Pushyabhuti dynasty was Prabhakaravardhana (580-605 CE), who transformed the dynasty into a powerful empire. He was the father of Harsha Vardhana and Rajyavardhana. Prabhakaravardhana ruled from Thaneshwar (present-day Haryana) as his capital after the decline of the Gupta Empire. He defeated the Huns, Malavas, and Gurjaras, expanding his territory. His achievements are recorded in the Harshacharita by Banabhatta. His reign laid the foundation for Harsha's empire.

q: The capital of Harshavardhana's empire was:
qs.e: Harshavardhana (606-647 AD) was a ruler of the Pushyabhuti dynasty. Initially, his capital was Thanesar (in present-day Haryana), but later he shifted his capital to Kannauj (in present-day Uttar Pradesh). Kannauj was also known as Kanyakubja. Harsha ascended the throne after the death of his brother Rajyavardhana in 612 AD and established a vast empire covering most of northern India. His reign is noted for administrative efficiency, cultural patronage, and support for Buddhism. The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang visited Harsha's court and described Kannauj as a prosperous city. Harsha organized the famous Maha Moksha Parishad (Great Assembly) at Kannauj.

q: Chinese traveler Hsuan Tsang was contemporary-
qs.e: The Chinese traveler Hsuan Tsang (also known as Xuanzang) visited India in the 7th century CE. He was a contemporary of Emperor Harsh Vardhan (606-647 CE), who ruled over northern India with his capital at Kannauj. Hsuan Tsang traveled in India from around 630 to 643 CE and studied at the famous Nalanda University. He wrote a detailed account of his travels in the book 'Si-yu-ki' or 'Records of the Buddhist Countries', which is a crucial source for Indian history. The information provided by Hsuan Tsang helps historians understand the political, social, and religious conditions of that time.

qs.e: The court poet Banabhatta of Harshavardhana composed the Harshacharita in Sanskrit, which is a historical biography detailing the life of Harshavardhana. q: Who wrote the famous book Kamasutra?
qs.e: The Kamasutra is an ancient Indian text on human sexuality and lifestyle. It was written by Vatsyayan (also known as Mallanaga Vatsyayana), who lived around the 3rd century BCE. The book is written in Sanskrit and consists of seven parts focusing on love, marriage, and sexual arts. The Kamasutra holds a significant place in world literature and is an integral part of Indian culture. Among the other options, Kalidas was a famous poet, Vasumitra was a Buddhist monk, and Mahakashyapa was also associated with Buddhism.

q: The compilation of Kabir's compositions is called _________.
qs.e: Kabir was a 15th-century mystic poet and saint. His compositions are compiled in a work known as Bijak, which means 'seed' or 'source'. The Bijak contains three sections: Sakhi (couplets), Pad (songs), and Ramaini (mixed prose and verse). Kabir's philosophy was based on nirguna bhakti (formless devotion), and he criticized religious orthodoxy, caste discrimination, and ritualism. He used a mixed dialect called Sadhukaddi, blending Hindi, Punjabi, Awadhi, and Braj. The Bijak is the most authentic collection of Kabir's teachings and is studied for its spiritual and social insights.
qs.kf:

☛ Three parts of Bijak → Sakhi, Pad, Ramaini
☛ Language of Kabir → Sadhukkaddi

q: What is called Shaivism in the Bhakti Movement?
qs.e: In the Bhakti Movement, the followers of Shaivism were called Nayanars. These saints flourished in South India between the 7th and 9th centuries and composed numerous hymns in praise of Shiva. There are traditionally 63 Nayanars, prominent among them being Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar, and Manikkavacakar. Their hymns are collectively known as Tevaram. In contrast, the devotees of Vishnu were called Alwars. The term Bodhisattva is used in Buddhism, while Wali refers to Islamic saints. Thus, Shaivite bhakti saints are correctly termed Nayanars.
qs.kf:
☛ What are Shaivite saints called? → Nayanars
☛ How many Nayanars are there? → 63
☛ What is the collection of Nayanar hymns called? → Tevaram
☛ Who are prominent Nayanars? → Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar, Manikkavacakar
☛ What are Vaishnavite saints called? → Alwars

q: Which of the following is called God of medicine?
qs.e: Dhanvantar is considered the god of medicine in Hindu mythology. He is an avatar of Lord Vishnu and is regarded as the father of Ayurveda. Dhanvantar emerged during the churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan) holding a pot of amrita (nectar of immortality). He propagated the science of medicine. The other options: Aryabhatta was a mathematician, Patanjali authored the Yoga Sutras, and Panini was a Sanskrit grammarian.
qs.kf:

☛ Who is the father of Ayurveda? → Dhanvantar (mythological belief)

☛ Who authored the Yoga Sutras? → Patanjali

q: As Tola is related to the village, similarly the metropolis is related to which of the following?
A. City
B. Urban
C. District
D. Place
qs.e: Tola is a small part of a village, just as a metropolis is a large and prominent part of a city. Tola is a subdivision of a rural settlement, while a metropolis is the center of a large urban area. This relationship is of part-whole. Therefore, a metropolis is related to a city. Other options like Urban (urban area), District (administrative unit), and Place (general term) are not correct. Hence, the correct answer is 'City'.
qs.kf:
☛ Tola is a part of which? → Village
☛ Metropolis is a larger form of which? → City
☛ What is the relationship between Tola and village? → Part-whole
☛ What is a synonym for Metropolis? → Metropolis

q: Ulat Bansi is a distinct contribution of which Bhakti poet?
qs.e: Ulat Bansi is a distinctive style of poetry used by the Bhakti poet Kabir, characterized by paradoxical and inverted statements to convey deep spiritual truths. In this style, Kabir uses phrases that appear contrary to common experience, such as 'fire in water' or 'netherworld in the sky', to break the logical mind and lead to self-realization. The purpose of Ulatbansi is to challenge conventional thinking and social norms, emphasizing the path of devotion and inner experience over rituals. This unique expression became a hallmark of Kabir's poetry and influenced later saint-poets. Kabir lived during the 15th century and was a disciple of Ramananda. His works are composed in Sadhukaddi language and are compiled in the Gurugranth Sahib and the Bijak.
qs.kf:
☛ Which poet's composition is known as 'Ulat Bansi'? → Kabir
☛ Kabir belonged to which period of Bhakti movement? → Medieval period
☛ Where was Kabir born? → Lahartara, Kashi
☛ Who was Kabir's guru? → Ramananda
☛ In which language did Kabir compose his works? → Sadhukaddi

q: The Constituent Assembly was formed in November 1946 under the scheme-
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly of India was formed in November 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. This mission was sent by the British government in 1946, consisting of three ministers: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander. The mission's objective was to devise a framework for the transfer of power in India. According to this plan, a federal structure with groupings of provinces was proposed, paving the way for the formation of the Constituent Assembly. Members of the Assembly were indirectly elected by the provincial legislatures. The Assembly held its first meeting on 9 December 1946.
qs.kf:
☛ Who were the members of the Cabinet Mission? → Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander
☛ When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly? → 9 December 1946
☛ Who was the permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ How many members were there in the Constituent Assembly initially? → 389 (later 299)
☛ In which year did the Cabinet Mission visit India? → 1946

q: Which of the following states is connected with Kalhana's Rajatarangini?
qs.e: Kalhana was a 12th-century Sanskrit poet and historian from Kashmir. He composed the Rajatarangini, which chronicles the history of the kings of Kashmir. It is the only extant ancient Indian historical text in Sanskrit. The word Rajatarangini means "River of Kings". The text describes the rulers of Kashmir from early times up to the 12th century. Kalhana used evidence and sources to make his work reliable. Thus, this text is connected to the state of Jammu and Kashmir.
qs.kf:
☛ Author of Rajatarangini → Kalhana
☛ Language of Rajatarangini → Sanskrit
☛ Subject of Rajatarangini → History of the kings of Kashmir
☛ Period of Rajatarangini → 12th century (1148-1149 CE)
☛ Literal meaning of Rajatarangini → River of Kings

q: Which foreign trade relation was badly affected when Byzantium learned silk production in the 6th century CE?
qs.e: In the 6th century CE, Byzantium (the Eastern Roman Empire) learned silk production, ending its dependence on silk imports from India. This severely affected Indo-Byzantine trade, as silk was a major commodity traded between India and the Byzantine Empire. The technique of silk production reached Byzantium from China, after which they began producing their own silk. This reduced the demand for Indian silk and weakened trade relations. The event impacted the Indo-Byzantine trade routes.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Byzantium learn silk production? → 6th century CE
☛ From where did the silk production technique reach Byzantium? → China
☛ Which trade was affected by Byzantine silk production? → Indo-Byzantine trade
☛ What was the main commodity in Indo-Byzantine trade? → Silk
☛ Byzantium was part of which empire? → Eastern Roman Empire

q: What is the ancient style of articles containing Egyptian symbols called?
A. Hieroglyphics
B. Cuneiform
C. Hitite
D. Zapotec
qs.e: The ancient writing style of Egypt is known as Hieroglyphics. This pictographic writing system developed around 3200 BCE and included over 700 symbols. Hieroglyphs were used on temples, monuments, and papyrus. The discovery of the Rosetta Stone (1799) helped decipher this script. Cuneiform is the script of Mesopotamia, Hittite from Anatolia, and Zapotec from Mesoamerica.
qs.kf:
☛ Ancient Egyptian writing style → Hieroglyphics
☛ Time of origin of Hieroglyphics → Around 3200 BCE
☛ Stone that helped decipher Hieroglyphics → Rosetta Stone
☛ Cuneiform belongs to which civilization → Mesopotamia
☛ Where was Hittite script found → Anatolia

q: Who is the chairperson of the RBI constituted committee on development of housing finance securitisation market?
qs.e: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has constituted a committee on development of housing finance securitisation market. The committee aims to promote securitisation of housing loans and enhance liquidity in the market. The chairperson of this committee is Harsh Vardhan, a senior banker. The committee will work on improving the securitisation framework, standardisation, and transparency. This will provide new funding sources for housing finance companies and make home loans more accessible for common citizens. RBI forms such committees periodically to strengthen the financial market.
qs.kf:
☛ Chairperson of RBI committee on housing finance securitisation → Harsh Vardhan
☛ Main objective of the committee → Promote securitisation of housing loans
☛ Benefit of securitisation → New funding sources for banks and HFCs
☛ RBI's role → Form committees for financial market development
☛ Housing finance securitisation → Converting home loans into securities

q: Match the following correctly. Set I Set II (a) Naathmuni
1. Sanak Sampradaya (b) Shankaracharya
2. Sri Vaisnav Sampradaya (c) Raamanuj
3. Advait (d) Nimbark
4. Vishishtadvait
qs.e: Naathmuni is associated with the Sanak Sampradaya (1), which was founded by the four Kumaras (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sanatkumara). Shankaracharya propounded the Advaita Vedanta (3), emphasizing the oneness of Brahman and the individual self. Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita (4), focusing on devotion to a personal God with attributes. Nimbark founded the Sri Vaisnav Sampradaya (2), which follows the Dvaitadvaita philosophy. Thus, the correct match is a-2, b-3, c-4, d-1.
qs.kf:
☛ Who propounded Advaita Vedanta? → Shankaracharya
☛ Which saint is associated with Vishishtadvaita? → Ramanuja
☛ What is another name for Nimbark Sampradaya? → Sri Vaisnav Sampradaya
☛ Who founded the Sanak Sampradaya? → Four Kumaras (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sanatkumara)
☛ Which sampradaya is Naathmuni associated with? → Sanak Sampradaya

q: The Abhinav Bharat Mandir (Young India Society) was founded by _________ and his brother as a secret organisation during the Indian War for Independence.
qs.e: The Abhinav Bharat Mandir (Young India Society) was founded by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar in 1904 as a secret organisation. This organisation was established to promote revolutionary activities during the Indian War for Independence. Its aim was to incite an armed rebellion against British rule. Through this society, Savarkar inspired young Indians to fight for freedom. Abhinav Bharat Mandir trained many revolutionaries and played a key role in the independence movement. Savarkar later wrote the famous book 'The Indian War of Independence 1857', which was banned by the British.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Abhinav Bharat Mandir founded? → 1904
☛ Who founded Abhinav Bharat Mandir? → Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and Ganesh Damodar Savarkar
☛ What was the aim of Abhinav Bharat Mandir? → Armed rebellion against British rule
☛ What is Savarkar popularly known as? → Veer Savarkar
☛ Which famous book did Savarkar write? → 'The Indian War of Independence 1857'

q: Who succeeded Dhruvasena?
qs.e: Dhruvasena was a ruler of the Maitraka dynasty, which ruled over the Vallabhi region in Gujarat. He was succeeded by his son Dharapatta, who ascended the throne after Dhruvasena's death. Dharapatta expanded the Vallabhi kingdom and continued the dynasty's legacy. The Maitraka dynasty was contemporary to the Gupta Empire and existed from the 6th to the 8th century CE. Under Dharapatta's rule, Vallabhi became a prominent center of learning and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Maitraka dynasty? → Bhattaraka
☛ Which dynasty had Vallabhi as its capital? → Maitraka dynasty
☛ Who was the son of Dhruvasena? → Dharapatta
☛ Who succeeded Dharapatta as the ruler? → Shiladitya
☛ Who was the last ruler of the Maitraka dynasty? → Shiladitya VII

q: Which of the following ancient Indian philosophers deliberated on the smallest particle of matter and named it 'Parmanu'?
qs.e: In ancient Indian philosophy, Sage Kanada first deliberated on the smallest particle of matter and named it Parmanu. He is the founder of the Vaisheshika school of philosophy. According to him, the entire universe is composed of atoms (parmanu), which are indivisible and eternal. The combination of these atoms forms all material substances. This concept aligns with the modern atomic theory. Varahamihira was an astronomer, Charak was an Ayurvedic physician, and Baudhayana was a mathematician.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Vaisheshika school of philosophy? → Kanada
☛ Who first used the term Parmanu in ancient India? → Kanada
☛ What was Kanada's original name? → Kanabhuj
☛ Vaisheshika philosophy belongs to which category? → Astika (orthodox)
☛ Who propounded the atomic theory in ancient India? → Kanada

q: The famous 'Trimurti' sculpture is present in which of the following caves?
qs.e: The famous 'Trimurti' sculpture is located in the Elephanta Caves on Elephanta Island, Maharashtra. This magnificent 7th-century sculpture, carved out of a single basalt rock, depicts the three forms of Lord Shiva – Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. The Elephanta Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage site and were built during the reign of the Rashtrakuta dynasty. This sculpture is a masterpiece of Indian art and iconography.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state are the Elephanta Caves located? → Maharashtra
☛ Which deity is depicted in the Trimurti sculpture? → Shiva
☛ Which dynasty built the Elephanta Caves? → Rashtrakuta

☛ In which century were the Elephanta Caves built? → 7th century

q: Who among the following issued the earliest land grant of the Maitraka family in 502 CE?
qs.e: The Maitraka dynasty was founded in the 5th century and ruled over Saurashtra (Gujarat). In 502 CE, King Dronasimha issued the earliest known land grant of the Maitraka family. This grant is inscribed on a copper plate and belongs to the Vallabhi era. Dronasimha was one of the early Maitraka rulers who consolidated power after the decline of the Kshatrapas. His reign lasted approximately from 500 to 520 CE. The land grant was given to Brahmins, reflecting the royal patronage of religious institutions. Subsequent rulers like Guhasena, Shiladitya, and Dharapatta came later. Thus, the earliest grant is attributed to Dronasimha.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Maitraka dynasty → Vallabhi
☛ Start of Vallabhi era → 319 CE
☛ Successor of Dronasimha → Dhruvasena I
☛ Founder of Maitraka dynasty → Bhattaraka
☛ Ancient name of Saurashtra → Surashtra

q: According to the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act 1958, any structure, sculpture, inscription, etc., which are in existence for no less than _______ years is termed as ancient.
qs.e: According to Section 2(a) of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act 1958, any structure, sculpture, inscription, cave, painting, or other object is termed 'ancient' if it has been in existence for no less than 100 years. This act is the primary legislation in India for the preservation of archaeological heritage. It provides protection to monuments and sites of historical, artistic, or archaeological significance. By setting a minimum age of 100 years, the act ensures that only genuinely ancient items receive legal protection. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) is the main body responsible for implementing this act.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Ancient Monuments Act passed? → 1958
☛ What is the minimum age for an item to be considered ancient under this act? → 100 years
☛ What is the objective of this act? → Preservation of ancient monuments and archaeological sites
☛ Which items are termed 'ancient' under the act? → Any structure, sculpture, inscription, etc., at least 100 years old
☛ Which is the main body for archaeological conservation in India? → Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)

q: Who is the author of the historical work 'Rajatarangini', which records the history of Kashmir?
qs.e: 'Rajatarangini' is a famous historical chronicle documenting the history of Kashmir. It was composed in the 12th century by the Kashmiri Brahmin poet and historian Kalhana. Written in Sanskrit, it consists of 7826 verses and is considered the first authentic work of Indian historiography due to its careful mention of events and dates. Kalhana wrote it to present the reign of Kashmiri kings in a chronological order. The work covers the mythical history of Kashmir up to the 12th century, including various dynasties and events. It is a valuable source for understanding the political and cultural history of Kashmir.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed Rajatarangini? → Kalhana
☛ In which language is Rajatarangini written? → Sanskrit
☛ How many verses are in Rajatarangini? → 7826
☛ Which region's history does Rajatarangini record? → Kashmir
☛ Kalhana belonged to which century? → 12th century

q: Who composed the famous book 'Kitab-ul-Hind'?
qs.e: The famous book 'Kitab-ul-Hind' was composed by Al-Biruni in the 11th century. This book provides a detailed account of Indian culture, religion, philosophy, science, and social life. Al-Biruni was a Persian scholar who came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni. He deeply studied Sanskrit and wrote this treatise in Arabic. 'Kitab-ul-Hind' is considered an authentic source on Indian history and culture. It covers topics like Indian astronomy, mathematics, medicine, and religious practices. Al-Biruni's objective and analytical approach made this work unique for its time.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous book of Al-Biruni → Kitab-ul-Hind
☛ Al-Biruni came to India during whose reign? → Mahmud of Ghazni
☛ Kitab-ul-Hind was written in which language? → Arabic
☛ Full name of Al-Biruni → Abu Rayhan Muhammad al-Biruni
☛ Alternative name of Kitab-ul-Hind → Tahqiq-e-Hind

q: Who among the following has plundered and destroyed Somnath Temple 17 times along with other temples in his attacks?
qs.e: Mahmoud Ghazni (971-1030 AD) was a Turkish ruler who conducted 17 invasions of India. He plundered and destroyed the Somnath Temple (Gujarat) in 1025-26 AD. This temple dedicated to Lord Shiva was renowned for its immense wealth. Mahmoud also looted other temples like Mathura, Kannauj, and Thanesar. His motives were to acquire wealth and spread Islam. He ruled from Ghazni (Afghanistan) and was granted the title of 'Sultan' by the Caliph. His invasions weakened Indian kingdoms and paved the way for future Islamic invasions.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of invasions on India by Mahmoud Ghazni → 17 times
☛ Year of Somnath Temple attack → 1025-26 AD
☛ Ruled from → Ghazni (Afghanistan)
☛ Court poet of Mahmoud Ghazni → Firdausi (Shahnameh)
☛ First Muslim invader called 'Sultan' → Mahmoud Ghazni

q: Which of the following was the founder of Pala Empire?
qs.e: The Pala Empire was founded by Gopala around 750 CE. He was the first democratically elected king in the Bengal region. He established the town of Gopalganj and founded the Odantapuri Vihara. The Pala dynasty is renowned for its patronage of Buddhism. Notable rulers of this dynasty include Dharmapala and Devapala. Gopala's successors expanded the empire, ruling over parts of Bengal, Bihar, and Assam.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Pala dynasty? → Gopala
☛ What was the main religion of the Pala dynasty? → Buddhism
☛ Who established the Odantapuri Vihara? → Gopala
☛ Who was the most powerful Pala ruler? → Dharmapala
☛ What was the time period of the Pala Empire? → 750 CE - 1161 CE

q: When was the second battle of Tarain fought?
qs.e: The second battle of Tarain was fought in 1192 AD between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan. In this battle, Ghori defeated Prithviraj and captured Delhi, laying the foundation of Muslim rule in India. The first battle was fought in 1191, where Prithviraj emerged victorious. Ghori's victory in the second battle established Turkish rule in northern India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first battle of Tarain fought? → 1191 AD
☛ Who won the second battle of Tarain? → Muhammad Ghori
☛ Between whom were the battles of Tarain fought? → Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad Ghori
☛ What was the outcome of the second battle of Tarain? → Establishment of Muslim rule in Delhi
☛ Which dynasty did Prithviraj Chauhan belong to? → Chauhan dynasty

q: When was the first battle of Panipat fought?
qs.e: The first Battle of Panipat was fought on 21 April 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. This battle laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India. Babur used artillery and advanced tactics to defeat Ibrahim Lodi. The battle ended the Lodi dynasty and marked the beginning of Mughal rule. The battles of Panipat hold a significant place in Indian history.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first Battle of Panipat fought? → 21 April 1526
☛ Who fought in the first Battle of Panipat? → Babur and Ibrahim Lodi
☛ Between whom was the first Battle of Panipat fought? → Babur and Ibrahim Lodi
☛ What was the result of the first Battle of Panipat? → Babur's victory and establishment of Mughal Empire
☛ When was the second Battle of Panipat fought? → 1556

q: Al- Biruni, the Persian scholar, accompanied which invader to Afghanistan and India?
qs.e: Al-Biruni was a renowned Persian scholar, mathematician, and historian. He accompanied Mahmud Ghazni to Afghanistan and India. Mahmud Ghazni led 17 invasions into India, and Al-Biruni studied Indian culture, religion, science, and philosophy in depth. His famous work "Tarikh-ul-Hind" (History of India) is a valuable source of Indian life and knowledge. Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and translated many Indian texts into Arabic.

q: Who was the founder of the Pala empire?
qs.e: The Pala Empire was founded by Gopal around 750 CE. He was the first ruler of the Pala dynasty and was elected through a democratic process. The empire extended over Bengal and Bihar regions and became a major center of Buddhism. Gopal established the Vikramashila University, which became an important center for Buddhist learning. The Pala dynasty ruled for about 400 years, and its famous rulers include Dharmapala and Devapala. The Palas promoted art, culture, and education, especially Buddhism.

q: When was Panipat's second war?
qs.e: The second battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556 between Akbar and Hemu. Hemu was a Hindu ruler who had captured Delhi and assumed the title of Vikramaditya. Akbar's army was led by Bairam Khan. Hemu was defeated and captured in this battle. This victory strengthened the foundation of the Mughal Empire.

q: Who fought the war of turmeric valley against the Mughals?
qs.e: The Battle of Haldighati was fought in 1576 between Maharana Pratap of Mewar and the Mughal army of Emperor Akbar. Maharana Pratap was a Sisodia Rajput ruler who refused to submit to Mughal authority. The battle took place near Gogunda in a narrow pass called Haldighati. The Mughal forces were led by Man Singh and Asaf Khan. Despite being outnumbered, Maharana Pratap fought valiantly and later continued guerrilla warfare from the hills. His loyal horse Chetak saved his life but was fatally wounded. Although the Mughals claimed victory, Maharana Pratap never accepted Mughal suzerainty, making this battle a symbol of Rajput resistance and honor.

☛ Who fought the Battle of Haldighati? → Maharana Pratap vs. Akbar's forces

q: Which dynasty built the famous Khajuraho temples in the 10th and 11th centuries?
qs.e: The Khajuraho temples were built by the Chandela dynasty between the 10th and 11th centuries. They are located in the Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh, India. The Chandela capital was Mahoba. These temples are famous for their Nagara style architecture and intricate erotic sculptures. The temple complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Chandela ruler Dhanga Deva constructed the largest number of temples. The most notable temple is the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva.

☛ Who is considered the most powerful Chandela ruler? → Vidyadhara

☛ Chandela dynasty is a branch of which dynasty? > Gahadavala
☛ What architectural style are Khajuraho temples built in? → Nagara style

q: When was the Third Battle of Panipat fought?
qs.e: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the Maratha Empire and the Afghan army led by Ahmad Shah Abdali. The Marathas were decisively defeated, halting their expansion in India and paving the way for the rise of the British East India Company. It was one of the largest battles of the 18th century, with approximately 100,000 soldiers killed. This battle weakened the Maratha Confederacy and led to the emergence of regional powers.

q: The famous Lakshmana temple found in Khajuraho was built by whom?
qs.e: The famous Lakshmana Temple in Khajuraho was built by the Chandela king Yashovarman (also known as Lakshmavarman) in the 10th century. It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and showcases the Nagara style of architecture. The Chandela rulers constructed about 85 temples in Khajuraho, of which only 25 survive today. The Lakshmana temple is part of a group of three temples that also includes the Vishwanath and Kandariya Mahadeva temples. It is renowned for its intricate carvings and erotic sculptures.

☛ In which state is Khajuraho located? → Madhya Pradesh

q: When was the Battle of Kanauj fought?
qs.e: The Battle of Kanauj was fought on 17 May 1540 between Sher Shah Suri and Humayun. In this battle, Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun, leading to the decline of the Mughal Empire and forcing Humayun to flee to Persia. After this victory, Sher Shah Suri established the Sur Empire and ruled over northern India. This battle is significant in Indian history as it temporarily ended Mughal rule.

☛ After which battle did Sher Shah Suri establish the Sur Empire? → Battle of Kanauj
☛ When did the Battle of Kanauj take place? → 1540 AD

q: Which Chandela ruler is credited with the construction of the Kandariya Mahadev Temple situated in Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh, India?
qs.e: The Kandariya Mahadev Temple, located in Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh, India, is a prominent Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. It was built around 1050 CE by the Chandela ruler Vidyadhara. This temple is renowned for its grandeur and intricate sculptures, and is the largest and most magnificent temple in the Khajuraho group of temples, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Vidyadhara's reign is considered the golden age of the Chandela dynasty. The temple's architecture is a masterpiece of Chandela art, with a height of about 31 meters. It reflects the zenith of temple building in central India during the medieval period.

q: Who among the following is the founder of the Pala dynasty?
qs.e: The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala around 750 CE. He was the first Buddhist king to rule the Bengal region. The Pala dynasty ruled for nearly 400 years and holds a significant place in Indian history. After Gopala, his son Dharmapala ascended the throne and founded the Vikramashila University. The Pala rulers made important contributions to the spread of Buddhism and education. Gopala was elected as king through a democratic process by the feudal lords of Bengal. Thus, Gopala is the founder of the Pala dynasty.

☛ Founder of Vikramashila University → Dharmapala
