q: In one of his famous works, Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi claims that the founder of _____ was a descendant of the Prophet.
qs.e: In his famous work 'Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi', Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi claims that the founder of the Sayyid Dynasty was a descendant of Prophet Muhammad. The Sayyid Dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1414 to 1451 CE. It was founded by Khizr Khan, who was initially appointed as governor by Timur and later declared independence. His successors claimed the title 'Sayyid' (descendant of the Prophet). The last ruler of this dynasty was Alam Shah, who was defeated by Bahlol Lodi, marking the beginning of the Lodi Dynasty. This claim is recorded in historical documents, though historians debate its authenticity.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Sayyid Dynasty? → Khizr Khan
☛ What was the reign period of the Sayyid Dynasty? → 1414-1451 CE
☛ Who wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi? → Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi
☛ Who was the last ruler of the Sayyid Dynasty? → Alam Shah
☛ What does the term 'Sayyid' mean? → Descendant of the Prophet

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Who among the following appointed a superintendent (Shahna-i-Mandi) for the effective implementation of market reforms?
qs.e: Alauddin Khilji appointed a superintendent called Shahna-i-Mandi for the effective implementation of his market reforms. These reforms aimed at controlling prices and managing supply of essential commodities. Alauddin fixed prices for food grains, cloth, and other goods. The Shahna-i-Mandi was responsible for supervising markets and enforcing price regulations, with strict punishments for violators. This system is considered a significant economic measure in the Delhi Sultanate history.
qs.kf:
☛ Market control officer of Alauddin Khilji → Shahna-i-Mandi
☛ Objective of Alauddin Khilji's market reforms → Price stability and supply control
☛ Duty of Shahna-i-Mandi → Market inspection and enforcement of price rules
☛ Most important reform under Alauddin Khilji → Economic reforms and market control
☛ Commodities whose prices were controlled by Alauddin Khilji → Food grains, cloth, and other essentials

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3
q: What was the name of the new department opened by Muhammad Tughlaq for the development of agriculture?
qs.e: Muhammad Tughlaq established a new department called Diwan-i-Kohi for the development of agriculture. Its main objective was to bring barren land under cultivation and increase agricultural production. The government provided seeds, tools, and loans to farmers. However, the scheme failed due to poor implementation and corruption. The term 'Diwan-i-Kohi' literally means 'Department of Hills'. Tughlaq also created Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi for agricultural reforms. This was an important initiative in medieval India to boost agriculture.
qs.kf:
☛ Agriculture department under Muhammad Tughlaq? → Diwan-i-Kohi
☛ Objective of Diwan-i-Kohi? → Cultivate barren land
☛ Literal meaning of Diwan-i-Kohi? → Department of Hills
☛ Why did Tughlaq's agricultural scheme fail? → Corruption and mismanagement
☛ Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi related to? → Agriculture

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 1
q: 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' in Ajmer was built in the period of which of the following dynasties?
qs.e: 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' in Ajmer was originally a Sanskrit college, later converted into a mosque by Qutub-ud-din Aibak of the Slave Dynasty in 1199 AD. The structure reflects a blend of Hindu and Islamic architecture. The name 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' is associated with a legend about its rapid construction, though it took more time. This mosque is one of the oldest in India and was commissioned by Qutub-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Slave Dynasty. It is a significant example of early Indo-Islamic architecture in the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra? → Qutub-ud-din Aibak
☛ During which dynasty was it built? → Slave Dynasty
☛ Where is it located? → Ajmer, Rajasthan
☛ What was its original purpose? → Sanskrit college
☛ Who converted it into a mosque? → Qutub-ud-din Aibak

q: Ibn Battuta, a famous traveler, was a native of________
qs.e: Ibn Battuta was a famous medieval traveler and geographer, born in 1304 in Tangier, Morocco. He is regarded as one of the greatest travelers of the Islamic world. He journeyed for nearly 30 years covering over 120,000 kilometers. His travels are documented in his book "Rihla" (The Travels of Ibn Battuta), where he described regions of Africa, Asia, and Europe. He also visited India and stayed in the Delhi Sultanate during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq. His accounts provide valuable insights into the social, cultural, and political life of the 14th century.
qs.kf:
☛ Ibn Battuta was a native of which country? → Morocco

q: Who founded the 'Slave Dynasty'?
qs.e: The 'Slave Dynasty' was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in India, founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206 AD. He was a slave of Muhammad Ghori but later became an independent ruler. The dynasty was named so because most of its rulers were slaves or descendants of slaves. Qutb-ud-din Aibak started the construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque and the Qutb Minar in Delhi. His reign lasted from 1206 to 1210 AD. After his death, Iltutmish succeeded him.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Slave Dynasty → Qutb-ud-din Aibak
☛ Last ruler of Slave Dynasty → Ghiyas-ud-din Balban
☛ First dynasty of Delhi Sultanate → Slave Dynasty
☛ Who started construction of Qutb Minar → Qutb-ud-din Aibak
☛ Builder of Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque → Qutb-ud-din Aibak

q: Sloped or battter walls are the main attributes of the architecture of which Sultanate?
qs.e: Sloped or batter walls are the main attributes of the architecture of the Tughlaq Sultanate. This style was initiated by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq and was based on military architecture. The walls of Tughlaq buildings are thick and sloping downwards, providing strength and stability. This design aimed to protect against enemy attacks. The Tughlaqabad Fort in Delhi is a prime example. In contrast, the Lodi dynasty focused on tombs and domes, while the Slave dynasty adopted Indo-Islamic styles with arches and minarets.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the main feature of Tughlaq architecture? → Sloping walls
☛ Who built the Tughlaqabad Fort? → Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq
☛ What is a key example of Lodi architecture? → Shish Gumbad
☛ What was special about Slave dynasty architecture? → Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque
☛ What was the rule period of the Tughlaq dynasty? → 1320-1414 AD

q: Who founded the famous city of Siri ?
qs.e: The city of Siri was founded by Allauddin Khilji in 1303 AD. He was the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. The purpose of establishing Siri as his capital was to create a fortified city for protection against Mongol invasions. The city was known for its massive walls and architectural grandeur. Allauddin expanded his conquests up to the Vijayanagara empire in South India and implemented economic reforms. Today, Siri is part of the Shahjahanabad area in Delhi and holds historical significance.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Siri city → Allauddin Khilji
☛ Year of establishment of Siri → 1303 AD
☛ Allauddin Khilji's dynasty → Khilji dynasty
☛ Successor of Allauddin Khilji → Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah
☛ Death year of Allauddin Khilji → 1316 AD

q: Who founded the Tughlaq Dynasty?
qs.e: The Tughlaq Dynasty was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320 AD. He came to power after the last ruler of the Khilji dynasty. His original name was Ghazi Malik. He established the city of Tughlaqabad and made it his capital. His reign lasted from 1320 to 1325 AD. He died in an accident when a wooden pavilion collapsed. After him, his son Muhammad bin Tughlaq became the ruler. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq implemented administrative reforms and strengthened the irrigation system.

☛ Who succeeded Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq? → Muhammad bin Tughlaq

q: Which Sultan of Delhi first started the construction of Qutub Minar?
qs.e: The construction of the Qutub Minar was started by Qutub ud-Din Aybak in 1199 AD. He was the founder of the Slave Dynasty in the Delhi Sultanate. He only built the first storey (basement). Later, Iltutmish added three more storeys. Firoz Shah Tughlaq added a dome and a fifth storey at the top in 1368 AD, and Sikander Lodi carried out repairs in 1505 AD. The Qutub Minar is a 73-meter tall minaret made of red sandstone and marble, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

☛ Which dynasty is Qutub Minar associated with? → Slave Dynasty

q: Which place did Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq decide to move his capital from Delhi?
qs.e: Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-1351 AD) decided to shift his capital from Delhi to Devagiri (later renamed Daulatabad). The main reason was to have better control over the southern parts of the empire and administrative convenience. Devagiri was considered a central location geographically. However, due to lack of water and distance from Delhi, the plan failed. He later ordered the capital to be moved back to Delhi. This decision is regarded as one of his unpopular policies.

☛ Founder of Tughlaq dynasty → Ghiyath al-Din Tughlaq

q: Who was the first woman ruler of Delhi?
qs.e: The first woman ruler of Delhi was Razia Sultana, who reigned as Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240 CE. She was the daughter of Iltutmish and belonged to the Slave Dynasty. Iltutmish had nominated her as his successor during his lifetime because she was more capable than his sons. However, the nobles first placed her brother Rukn ud din Firuz on the throne, but later Razia assumed power. She was an able administrator and military leader, who abandoned purdah and dressed like men to rule. She was eventually killed in 1240.

☛ Razia Sultana was the daughter of → Iltutmish
☛ Razia Sultana's reign period → 1236-1240 CE
☛ How did Razia Sultana die? → Killed

q: Under the Delhi Sultanate what was the name of the state laws that grew under the monarchy, even if they violated the Shari’at?
qs.e: Under the Delhi Sultanate, the state laws formulated by the monarchy, even if they violated the Shari'at, were called Zawabit. These laws were based on administrative necessity and gave the sultan flexibility beyond religious law. Farman referred to royal decrees, Iqta was a revenue assignment system, and Fatwas were legal opinions by Islamic jurists. Zawabit helped the sultanate maintain secular governance. Zawabit were distinct from Shari'at and allowed the state to impose taxes and punishments not permitted under Islamic law.
qs.kf:
☛ What were Zawabit related to? → Laws made by the monarchy
☛ What is Shari'at? → Islamic religious law
☛ What does Farman mean? → Royal decree
☛ What was the Iqta system? → Land revenue administration
☛ Who issued Fatwas? → Islamic scholars or muftis

q: During which dynasty did the Mongols, led by Qultlug Khwaja, besiege Delhi and inflict significant damage?
qs.e: During the reign of Alauddin Khalji of the Khalji Dynasty, the Mongol leader Qultlug Khwaja besieged Delhi in 1299 AD, causing significant damage. Alauddin Khalji successfully defended the city and forced the Mongols to retreat. This event is a notable instance of Mongol invasions in Indian history. The Khalji Dynasty ruled from 1290 to 1320 AD and is known for its military campaigns and administrative reforms.

q: Under the reign of Islamic rulers, which among the following used to be a private building?
qs.e: Under the reign of Islamic rulers, Diwan-i-khas was a private building. It was used for confidential meetings and discussions between the king and his special officials. This was distinct from public buildings like Diwan-i-aam, which was open to the public. Other options such as Sarai (rest house for travelers), Bridges (structures for transportation), and Katra (commercial or residential space) were for public or general use. The construction of Diwan-i-khas was a feature of Mughal architecture, emphasizing privacy and aesthetics.

q: In one of his famous works, Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi claims that the founder of the _____ was a descendant of the Prophet Muhammad
qs.e: Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi was a noted historian who authored the work 'Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi'. In this work, he claimed that the founder of the Sayyid Dynasty, Khizr Khan, was a descendant of the Prophet Muhammad. The Sayyid Dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1414 to 1451 CE. Khizr Khan was appointed as the ruler of Delhi after Timur's invasion. This dynasty is known for its claim of being descendants of the Prophet Muhammad, though modern historians have doubted this. The Sayyid rule was weak and was eventually ended by Bahlol Khan Lodi.

q: Which Delhi Sultanate ruler was associated with the expedition of Bhilsa (Vidisha) in AD 1292?
qs.e: In AD 1292, Alauddin Khilji (then known as Ulugh Khan) led the expedition of Bhilsa (present-day Vidisha) during the reign of his uncle Sultan Jalaluddin Khilji. The expedition was aimed at acquiring wealth and treasure. Alauddin plundered the rich temples of Bhilsa and amassed huge wealth, which boosted his military and financial power. Later, in 1296, he also attacked Devagiri. This expedition proved to be a turning point in Alauddin's career, as the wealth obtained helped him later to seize the throne of Delhi.

☛ What was the purpose of the Bhilsa expedition? → To acquire wealth and treasure

q: _______ introduced the famous Persian festival of 'Nauroz'.
qs.e: Ghiyasuddin Balban (r. 1266-1287 CE) was the ninth sultan of the Delhi Sultanate. He introduced the Persian festival of 'Nauroz' in India. Nauroz is the Persian New Year festival celebrated on the vernal equinox. Balban started it to legitimize his authority and promote Persian culture. He was a strict ruler who introduced the practices of 'sijda' (prostration) and 'paibos' (kissing the feet). Balban protected the empire from Mongol invasions and established a centralized administrative system.
qs.kf:
☛ Who introduced the Nauroz festival? → Ghiyasuddin Balban
☛ Nauroz is associated with which religion? → Zoroastrianism (Parsi religion)
☛ Which practices did Balban introduce? → Sijda and Paibos
☛ Balban belonged to which dynasty? → Slave Dynasty
☛ What was Balban's full name? → Ghiyasuddin Balban

q: The visitor, Ibn Batuta, from Morocco, came to India during the rule of ?
qs.e: The famous Moroccan traveler Ibn Batuta came to India in 1333 AD. He documented his journey in the book 'Rihla'. He stayed for about 8 years at the court of Muhammad bin Tughluq, the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. The Sultan appointed him as a Qazi and later sent him as an ambassador to China. Ibn Batuta provided detailed information about Indian society, administration, and culture. Muhammad bin Tughluq ruled from 1324 to 1351 AD. Ibn Batuta's writings give a glimpse of the economic and social life of that period.
qs.kf:

☛ What is the name of Ibn Batuta's travel account? → Rihla

☛ To which country was Ibn Batuta sent as an ambassador? → China

q: Who was the founder of Tughlaqabad city?
qs.e: The city of Tughlaqabad was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1321 AD. He was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, which ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320 to 1325. Tughlaqabad Fort is a historic fort located in Delhi, built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq as his capital. The city is known for its massive walls and strong architecture. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb is also situated in Tughlaqabad. During his reign, administrative reforms were implemented and the army was strengthened.

☛ Where is Tughlaqabad Fort located? → Delhi
☛ What was Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's reign period? → 1320-1325 AD
☛ Where is Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb? → Tughlaqabad

q: In Delhi Sultanate, the holder of an ‘iqta’, who also worked as the administrative head of his ‘iqta’, was designated as ________.
qs.e: During the Delhi Sultanate, the iqta system was a key administrative and revenue arrangement. Under this system, the state assigned land revenue rights to officials or soldiers in lieu of salary, and such land was called an iqta. The holder of the iqta was known as muqti or iqtadar. The muqti was responsible not only for collecting revenue from his iqta but also for maintaining law and order, administration, and military management within his territory. Qazi was a judicial officer, ariz was the head of the military department, and wazir was the prime minister in charge of finance and administration. Hence, the holder of an iqta who served as its administrative head was designated as muqti.
qs.kf:
☛ Who introduced the iqta system in India? → Iltutmish
☛ What was the main purpose of the iqta system? → Assigning land in lieu of salary
☛ What was the main function of a muqti? → Administration and revenue collection of iqta
☛ What was the role of wazir in the Delhi Sultanate? → Head of finance and administration
☛ Which department did the ariz head? → Military department

q: Qutbuddin Ebak was killed while playing the game?
qs.e: Qutbuddin Ebak was the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate and founder of the Slave Dynasty. He died in 1210 AD in Lahore while playing Chaugan (polo) after falling from his horse. Chaugan was a horseback sport where players hit a ball with a mallet. After his death, his successor Aram Shah ascended the throne but proved incompetent and was soon replaced by Iltutmish. This event is significant in Indian history as it highlighted the instability in the early Delhi Sultanate. Chaugan was a popular sport among the nobility during that period.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Slave Dynasty → Qutbuddin Ebak
☛ Cause of Qutbuddin Ebak's death → Falling from horse while playing Chaugan
☛ Another name for Chaugan → Polo
☛ Successor of Qutbuddin Ebak → Aram Shah
☛ First ruler of Delhi Sultanate → Qutbuddin Ebak

q: Who was called Dewan - i - Arz in Medieval India?
qs.e: Dewan-i-Arz was an important department during the Sultanate period in medieval India. It was established by Alauddin Khalji. This department dealt with military administration and its head was called Dewan-i-Arz. Its functions included recruitment of soldiers, training, salary distribution, and maintaining military discipline. The Dewan-i-Arz was a high-ranking officer who reported directly to the Sultan. This system continued later in the Mughal Empire as well.
qs.kf:
☛ Which department was headed by Dewan-i-Arz? → Military Department
☛ Which Sultan established Dewan-i-Arz? → Alauddin Khalji

☛ Dewan-i-Risalat was related to which matters? → Religious affairs
☛ Who headed the military department in the Mughal period? → Mir Bakhshi

q: Which Sultan of Delhi popularized 'Taka' and 'Jintal' coins?
qs.e: The Delhi Sultanate ruler Iltutmish (r. 1211-1236 AD) popularized the 'Taka' (silver coin) and 'Jintal' (copper coin). The Taka was a silver coin weighing 175 grains, which later evolved into the Mughal rupee. The Jintal was a copper coin used for small transactions. Iltutmish established an Islamic monetary system by inscribing Arabic script and the name of the Caliph on coins. Before him, various types of coins were in circulation. He standardized coinage by introducing the silver 'Taka' and copper 'Jintal', which became the foundation of the Delhi Sultanate's currency system.

☛ Who popularized the copper coin Jintal? → Iltutmish
☛ Which Caliph's name did Iltutmish put on coins? → Al-Mustansir
☛ What was the weight of the Taka coin? → 175 grains
☛ Who was the first Delhi Sultan to issue a pure silver coin? → Iltutmish

q: Who among the following Sultans of Delhi started a new department for the development of agriculture called Diwan-i Kohi?
qs.e: Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq started a new department called Diwan-i Kohi for the development of agriculture. Its aim was to bring barren land under cultivation and increase agricultural production. The Sultan planned to provide loans, seeds, and implements to farmers. However, the scheme failed due to high expenditure and mismanagement. Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq is known for his ambitious but impractical policies, such as the transfer of capital and token currency experiments.

☛ Why did Diwan-i Kohi fail? → Excessive expenditure and administrative inefficiency
☛ Which department promoted agriculture? → Diwan-i Kohi

q: Which term was used to denote poll tax on non-muslim subjects during the reign of the Mughal Empire?
qs.e: During the Mughal Empire, the poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects was called Jizyah. It is an Islamic tax imposed on non-Muslims (dhimmis) in exchange for protection and religious freedom. Mughal emperor Akbar abolished Jizyah in 1564, but Aurangzeb reimposed it in 1679. This tax was applicable only to adult males; women, children, the elderly, and the disabled were exempt. The rates varied according to income. Sharia refers to Islamic law, Shafi'i is a school of jurisprudence, and Jahiliyah denotes the pre-Islamic age of ignorance.
qs.kf:
☛ Mughal ruler who abolished Jizyah → Akbar (1564)
☛ Mughal ruler who reimposed Jizyah → Aurangzeb (1679)
☛ Who were exempt from Jizyah? → Women, children, elderly, disabled
☛ Jizyah is a tax on which category? → Non-Muslims (poll tax)
☛ Meaning of Dhimmi → Protected non-Muslim citizen

q: Who was the third ruler ruler of the Mamluk dynasty?
qs.e: The Mamluk dynasty was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206 AD. The second ruler was Aram Shah, Aibak's son. The third ruler was Iltutmish, who ascended the throne in 1211 AD and ruled until 1236 AD. Iltutmish is considered the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate. He established Delhi as the permanent capital, formed the Chalisa (Turkan-i-Chihalgani) military group, and standardized the coinage system. He successfully repelled Mongol invasions. Iltutmish appointed his daughter Razia Sultan as his successor, who later became the fourth ruler of the dynasty.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Mamluk dynasty? → Qutb-ud-din Aibak
☛ Which military group did Iltutmish form? → Chalisa (Turkan-i-Chihalgani)
☛ Who made Delhi the permanent capital of the Sultanate? → Iltutmish
☛ Who was the only female ruler of the Mamluk dynasty? → Razia Sultan
☛ What was the reign of Iltutmish? → 1211-1236 AD

q: Which Sultan of Delhi is known for taking bold decisions during his rule?
qs.e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-1351) is known for his bold and experimental decisions. He ordered the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad, causing mass migration. He introduced token currency based on copper coins, but the experiment failed due to widespread forgery. He increased taxes in the Doab region, leading to peasant revolts. He also planned invasions of Khorasan and China, which were unsuccessful. His bold decisions lacked practical foresight, weakening his rule. These experiments earned him the title of 'the contradictory Sultan'.
qs.kf:
☛ To which city did Muhammad bin Tughlaq shift the capital? → Daulatabad
☛ Which currency system did Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduce? → Token currency
☛ Which tax experiment of Muhammad bin Tughlaq failed? → Tax increase in Doab
☛ Which countries did Muhammad bin Tughlaq plan to invade? → Khorasan and China
☛ What epithet is used for Muhammad bin Tughlaq? → The contradictory Sultan

q: Arrange the following rulers of the Slave dynasty in the chronological order

qs.e: The Slave dynasty was founded by Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210). He was succeeded by Aram Shah (1210-1211) and then Iltutmish (1211-1236). qs.e: The Qutub Minar in Delhi is the tallest brick minaret in the world. Its foundation was laid by Qutb-ud-din-Aibak in 1192 AD, who was the founder of the Slave Dynasty. He built it to commemorate the victory of Muhammad Ghori and also in memory of the pillar built by Chandragupta. Later, the top two storeys were completed by Iltutmish. qs.e: Alai Darwaza is located in the Qutub complex in Delhi and was built by Allauddin Khilji in 1311 AD. It is the main gateway to the Qutub Minar complex and is made of red sandstone. ☛ When was Alai Darwaza built? → 1311 AD
☛ Where is Allauddin Khilji's tomb? → Delhi
☛ What material is Alai Darwaza made of? → Red sandstone

q: Who was the founder of the Khilji dynasty?
qs.e: The Khilji dynasty was the second ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. It was founded by Jalaluddin Khilji in 1290 AD. He murdered Muizuddin Qaiqabad, the last ruler of the Slave dynasty, and seized power. Jalaluddin Khilji was known as a benevolent and kind ruler, but his reign was short. His nephew and son-in-law Alauddin Khilji murdered him in 1296 AD and became the Sultan. The Khilji dynasty ruled from 1290 to 1320 AD. Major rulers of this dynasty include Jalaluddin Khilji, Alauddin Khilji, and Mubarak Shah Khilji. Malik Kafur was a general under Alauddin, not a ruler.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Khilji dynasty? → Jalaluddin Khilji
☛ Who was the last ruler of the Khilji dynasty? → Mubarak Shah Khilji
☛ When did Alauddin Khilji murder Jalaluddin? → 1296 AD
☛ How long did the Khilji dynasty rule? → 30 years (1290-1320 AD)
☛ Which Khilji ruler invaded South India? → Alauddin Khilji

q: The first ruler of Delhi Sultanate was:
qs.e: The Delhi Sultanate was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206 AD. He was a slave of Muhammad Ghori and after Ghori's death, he started ruling independently. Aibak ruled from Lahore and later made Delhi the capital. He was the founder of the Slave Dynasty. He began the construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and the incomplete Qutb Minar. His reign lasted from 1206 to 1210 AD. He is regarded as the one who laid the foundation of Islamic rule in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Delhi Sultanate? → Qutb-ud-din Aibak
☛ Who was the first ruler of the Slave Dynasty? → Qutb-ud-din Aibak
☛ Who started the construction of Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque? → Qutb-ud-din Aibak
☛ When was the Delhi Sultanate established? → 1206 AD
☛ Whose slave was Qutb-ud-din Aibak? → Muhammad Ghori

q: Who among the following is known as the first sovereign ruler of the Delhi sultanate?
qs.e: Shams al-Din Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236) is considered the first sovereign ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Although Qutb al-Din Aybak laid the foundation of the Sultanate, he remained a military general and did not assume the title of Sultan. Iltutmish, after succeeding Aybak, declared himself Sultan and sought recognition from the Caliph of Baghdad, which legitimized his sovereignty. He introduced the silver Tanka coin and strengthened the administration. Mahmud of Ghazni was an invader of India but not a ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Jalal al-Din Firuz Khalji was the first ruler of the Khalji dynasty, who came much later. Hence, Iltutmish is rightly regarded as the first sovereign ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is considered the first sovereign ruler of the Delhi Sultanate? → Shams al-Din Iltutmish
☛ From which Caliph did Iltutmish seek recognition? → Caliph of Baghdad
☛ Which silver coin was introduced by Iltutmish? → Tanka
☛ Who founded the Delhi Sultanate? → Qutb al-Din Aybak
☛ Iltutmish belonged to which dynasty? → Slave Dynasty

q: What is the dominant form of decoration employed in Sultanate buildings?
qs.e: The dominant form of decoration in Sultanate buildings is Arabesque. Arabesque is a distinctive feature of Islamic art, characterized by geometric and floral designs. Due to the prohibition of depicting humans and animals in Islam, Arabesque developed as an alternative. It consists of interlacing vines, leaves, and flowers, influenced by Turkish and Iranian styles. In Delhi Sultanate monuments like Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, Alai Darwaza, and Qutub Minar, Arabesque is extensively used. Other options like Toranas and Amalaka are associated with Indian temple architecture, while Kalasha is placed on the spire.
qs.kf:
☛ Arabesque is associated with which religion's art? → Islam
☛ Which Sultanate building prominently features Arabesque decoration? → Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque
☛ Why does Islamic art avoid human depiction? → Religious prohibition
☛ Arabesque is mainly based on which styles? → Turkish and Iranian
☛ Which Sultanate gateway has excellent Arabesque? → Alai Darwaza

q: Select the INCORRECT statement about the polices of Jalaluddin Khalji.
o: He avoided harsh punishments, even to those who revolted against him.
He put forward the view that the state should never be based on the willing support of the governed.
He not only forgave those who revolted against him but at times even rewarded them to win their support.
He tried to win the goodwill of the nobility by a policy of tolerance.
qs.e: Jalaluddin Khalji (r. 1290-1296 CE) was the first Khalji ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. He adopted a policy of conciliation and tolerance. He forgave rebels and even rewarded them to win their support. He believed that the state should be based on the willing support of the governed, not just force. Therefore, the statement that he opposed the state being based on the willing support of the governed is incorrect. His actual approach was to seek popular support.
qs.kf:
☛ Jalaluddin Khalji's reign → 1290-1296 CE
☛ Founder of Khalji dynasty → Jalaluddin Khalji
☛ Jalaluddin's policy → Tolerance and forgiveness
☛ His view → State based on support of governed
☛ Successor → Alauddin Khalji

q: Which of the following administrative innovations is attributed to Alauddin Khilji’s reign?
o: Regulation of market prices and rationing
Foundation of Diwan-i-Arz for military reforms
qs.e: Alauddin Khilji implemented a comprehensive market control system to support his extensive imperial policies and large army. He fixed prices of essential goods like grain, cloth, and other items in Delhi and appointed officials called Shahna-i-Mandi to supervise markets. Records of sales and purchases were maintained, and arrangements for storage and rationing of grain were made. Strict punishments were imposed to prevent black-marketing. This was a revolutionary administrative innovation. The other options: Diwan-i-Arz (military department) was established by Balban, Iqta system existed earlier in the Delhi Sultanate, and Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar.
qs.kf:
☛ Market control officer of Alauddin Khilji → Shahna-i-Mandi
☛ Main objective of Alauddin Khilji's market reforms → Ensure low prices and continuous supply of goods to support a large army
☛ How were grain prices regulated under Alauddin Khilji? → Fixed at predetermined rates
☛ Who established Diwan-i-Arz? → Balban
☛ Founder of Mansabdari system → Akbar

q: What was the Diwan-i-Riyasat under Alauddin Khilji?
qs.e: During his reign, Alauddin Khilji implemented a price control policy. Under this policy, prices of goods were fixed and strict control was maintained over the market. For this purpose, he created a separate department called Diwan-i-Riyasat, headed by Yana Malik. This department was responsible for monitoring the market and prices. Alauddin Khilji fixed the prices of grains, cloth, horses, etc. Shopkeepers were registered and severe punishments were given for violations. This was the first and most effective price control system of its kind in the Delhi Sultanate period.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the head of Diwan-i-Riyasat? → Yana Malik
☛ Name of the price control department of Alauddin Khilji? → Diwan-i-Riyasat
☛ Which market policy did Alauddin Khilji implement? → Price control policy
☛ Diwan-i-Riyasat was related to which department? → Department controlling markets and prices
☛ What was the function of Diwan-i-Riyasat? → Control over markets and prices of goods

q: Which of the following rulers built Tughlaqabad Fort in 1321?
qs.e: Tughlaqabad Fort was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1321. He was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty and ruled from 1320 to 1325. The fort is located in Delhi and its massive walls and structure are an excellent example of Tughlaq architecture. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq established his capital at Tughlaqabad. After him, Muhammad bin Tughlaq ruled, who shifted the capital to Devagiri. Firoz Shah Tughlaq built Firozabad and other structures. Alauddin Khalji was a ruler of the Khalji dynasty. Tughlaqabad Fort is one of the important forts of the Delhi Sultanate.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty? → Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq
☛ What was the reign of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq? → 1320-1325
☛ Where is Tughlaqabad Fort located? → Delhi
☛ Which ruler shifted the capital to Devagiri? → Muhammad bin Tughlaq
☛ Which city was built by Firoz Shah Tughlaq? → Firozabad

q: The Group of Forty who advised and assisted the Sultan in administering the Delhi Sultanate was established by which of the following rulers?
qs.e: The Group of Forty, known as Turkan-e-Chihalgani or Chalisa, was established by Iltutmish to advise and assist the Sultan in administering the Delhi Sultanate. This council of forty Turkic nobles was created to counterbalance the influence of powerful Turkish amirs and strengthen the Sultan's authority. Later, Balban dismantled this group to centralize power. Iltutmish reigned from 1211 to 1236 CE and is also known for introducing the silver coin Tanka and the copper coin Jital.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Turkan-e-Chihalgani? → Iltutmish
☛ Who abolished the Group of Forty? → Balban
☛ What was the reign period of Iltutmish? → 1211–1236 CE
☛ Which currency did Iltutmish introduce? → Tanka (silver) and Jital (copper)
☛ What title was given to Iltutmish? → Illustrious Sultan

q: Mughal miniature painting reached its peak during the rule of _____
qs.e: Mughal miniature painting reached its peak during the rule of Jahangir. Jahangir had a deep interest in art and painting. His court included famous painters like Ustad Mansur and Abul Hasan. During this period, paintings focused on realism, natural scenes, and wildlife. Jahangir incorporated European techniques like shading and perspective. In contrast, Akbar laid the foundation of Mughal painting, Shah Jahan emphasized architecture, and Aurangzeb neglected painting, leading to its decline.
qs.kf:
☛ Golden age of Mughal miniature painting → Jahangir
☛ Jahangir's court painters → Ustad Mansur, Abul Hasan
☛ Contribution of Akbar's painting → Illustration of Dastan-e-Amir Hamza
☛ Shah Jahan's main artistic focus → Architecture
☛ Aurangzeb's attitude towards painting → Neglect, lack of patronage

q: By what name was the famous ruler of Delhi named Farid?
qs.e: Farid, later known as Sher Shah Suri, was the founder of the Sur Empire. He defeated Humayun in 1540 and captured Delhi. Sher Shah introduced administrative reforms such as the silver rupee currency and built the Grand Trunk Road. He streamlined the land revenue system and strengthened the judiciary. Though his reign was short (1540-1545), it was highly impactful. Sher Shah is credited with laying the groundwork for the Mughal Empire.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the original name of Sher Shah? → Farid
☛ Which coin was introduced by Sher Shah? → Rupee
☛ Who built the Grand Trunk Road? → Sher Shah Suri
☛ What was Sher Shah's reign period? → 1540-1545 CE
☛ Which Mughal ruler did Sher Shah defeat? → Humayun

q: Which Mughal ruler had implemented the Manashbari system?
qs.e: The Mansabdari system was implemented by the Mughal emperor Akbar. It was an administrative and military system where officials were granted a mansab (rank) according to their merit and position. Mansabdars were classified based on Zat (personal rank) and Sawar (number of horsemen). This system was designed to enhance administrative efficiency and military organization. It was developed during Akbar's reign and continued by later Mughal rulers. The Mansabdari system strengthened the central control of the Mughal Empire.
qs.kf:
☛ Who implemented the Mansabdari system? → Akbar
☛ What does 'Zat' mean in the Mansabdari system? → Personal rank
☛ What does 'Sawar' mean in the Mansabdari system? → Number of horsemen
☛ In which century was the Mansabdari system introduced? → 16th century
☛ What was the main objective of the Mansabdari system? → To strengthen administrative and military organization

q: The battle of Khanwa was fought between ________.
qs.e: The Battle of Khanwa was fought on March 16, 1527, between Babur and Rana Sanga. This battle was a crucial turning point in Babur's establishment of power in India. Rana Sanga was the ruler of Mewar and had formed a large confederacy against Babur. Babur achieved victory through superior strategy and the effective use of artillery. This victory strengthened the foundation of the Mughal Empire in North India.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Battle of Khanwa → March 16, 1527
☛ What did Babur use in the battle → Artillery
☛ Rana Sanga was the ruler of which kingdom → Mewar
☛ First Battle of Panipat was fought between → Babur and Ibrahim Lodi
☛ Which title did Babur adopt → Ghazi

q: Which Mughal Emperor founded Fatehpur Sikri as his capital city?
qs.e: The Mughal Emperor Akbar founded Fatehpur Sikri as his capital in 1571 AD. This city is located about 40 km from Agra. Akbar built several architectural marvels here, including the Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, and Birbal's House. Fatehpur Sikri was constructed by Akbar in reverence to the Sufi saint Salim Chishti. Later, in 1585 AD, due to water scarcity, Akbar had to shift the capital to Lahore. Fatehpur Sikri was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986 AD.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded Fatehpur Sikri? → Akbar
☛ In which state is Fatehpur Sikri located? → Uttar Pradesh
☛ Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built to commemorate which victory? → Gujarat victory (1573 AD)
☛ When was the capital shifted from Fatehpur Sikri? → 1585 AD
☛ Whose tomb is located in Fatehpur Sikri? → Salim Chishti

q: In Indian history, who was also known as Alamgir?
qs.e: The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb (1658-1707) was also known by his title 'Alamgir' (Conqueror of the World). He was the sixth ruler of the Mughal Empire and ascended the throne after imprisoning his father Shah Jahan. His reign lasted about 50 years, making it one of the longest in Mughal history. Aurangzeb was an orthodox Muslim ruler who strictly enforced Islamic laws and reinstated the jizya tax on non-Muslims. He expanded the empire into the Deccan and fought against the Maratha ruler Shivaji. His policies eventually weakened the Mughal Empire and contributed to its decline.
qs.kf:
☛ Title of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb → Alamgir
☛ Reign period of Aurangzeb → 1658–1707 CE
☛ Tax re-imposed by Aurangzeb → Jizya
☛ Maratha ruler who opposed Aurangzeb → Shivaji
☛ Name of Aurangzeb's father → Shah Jahan

q: _______ was the 3rd Mughal Emperor of India. A. Humayun
B. Akbar C. Aurangzeb D. Jahangir
qs.e: The third Mughal Emperor of India was Akbar. The Mughal Empire was founded by Babur in 1526 after the First Battle of Panipat. He was succeeded by Humayun, the second emperor. After Humayun's death, Akbar ascended the throne in 1556. Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605 and strengthened the Mughal Empire. He abolished the jizya tax and implemented a policy of religious tolerance called Sulh-i-Kul. Akbar's reign is considered the golden age of the Mughal Empire. He was succeeded by Jahangir, Shah Jahan, and Aurangzeb. Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri and patronized the Navaratnas (nine gems) in his court.
qs.kf:
☛ First Battle of Panipat → Fought in 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi
☛ Son of Humayun → Akbar
☛ Akbar's coronation → Took place in 1556 at Kalanaur
☛ Akbar's capital cities → Agra and Fatehpur Sikri
☛ Court language of Akbar → Persian

q: In 1857, the last ruler of the Mughal dynasty _______ was overthrown by the British.
qs.e: After the Revolt of 1857, the British defeated the last Mughal ruler Bahadur Shah Zafar and exiled him to Rangoon (present-day Yangon, Myanmar). This marked the formal end of the Mughal Empire. Bahadur Shah Zafar was not only a ruler but also a renowned poet and a Sufi saint. Following the revolt, the British East India Company was dissolved, and the British Crown assumed direct control over India through the Government of India Act 1858. Bahadur Shah Zafar died in 1862 in Rangoon. The trial and exile of the last Mughal emperor symbolized the complete subjugation of India by the British.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the last ruler of the Mughal dynasty? → Bahadur Shah Zafar
☛ Where was Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled? → Rangoon
☛ After the Revolt of 1857, which body assumed direct rule over India? → The British Crown
☛ Which act of 1858 laid the foundation of British rule in India? → Government of India Act 1858
☛ When and where did Bahadur Shah Zafar die? → 1862, Rangoon

q: Shah Jahan's daughter _______ participated in many architectural project of the new capital of Shahjahanabad (Delhi).
qs.e: Shah Jahan's daughter Jahanara participated in many architectural projects of the new capital Shahjahanabad (Delhi). She was the eldest daughter of Shah Jahan and known for her intelligence and love for arts. Jahanara contributed to the construction of structures like Chandni Chowk market and sarai (inns) and played a significant role in the development of Shahjahanabad. During the Mughal Empire, she was highly influential and promoted architecture during her father's reign.
qs.kf:
☛ Shah Jahan's daughter who was involved in Shahjahanabad projects → Jahanara
☛ Chandni Chowk market was built by → Jahanara
☛ Shahjahanabad in Delhi was founded by → Shah Jahan
☛ Jahanara was the daughter of → Shah Jahan
☛ Capital during Mughal emperor Shah Jahan was → Shahjahanabad

q: When did Nadir Shah invade India and sack Delhi?
qs.e: Nadir Shah, the ruler of Persia, invaded India in 1739 CE. He defeated the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah at the Battle of Karnal (1739) and sacked Delhi. During this invasion, he plundered invaluable treasures like the Kohinoor diamond and the Peacock Throne. Nadir Shah's invasion weakened the Mughal Empire and caused political instability in India.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Nadir Shah invade India? → 1739
☛ Which Mughal emperor was defeated by Nadir Shah? → Muhammad Shah
☛ When was the Battle of Karnal fought? → 1739
☛ Famous diamond looted by Nadir Shah? → Kohinoor
☛ Nadir Shah was the ruler of which country? → Persia (Iran)

q: Who built the Buland Darwaza, which is located in Fatehpur Sikri?
qs.e: The Buland Darwaza was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1601 AD at Fatehpur Sikri to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. It is the highest gateway in the world, standing at about 54 meters (176 ft). The structure is made of red sandstone and white marble. An inscription inside the gate mentions Jesus Christ, reflecting Akbar's religious tolerance. It is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Buland Darwaza? → Akbar
☛ Where is Buland Darwaza located? → Fatehpur Sikri
☛ When was Buland Darwaza built? → 1601 AD
☛ Which victory is commemorated by Buland Darwaza? → Gujarat victory
☛ What is the height of Buland Darwaza? → Approximately 54 meters

q: 'Humayun Nama' provides a glimpse into the world of Mughals. Who wrote the book?
qs.e: 'Humayun Nama' is a historical text written by Gulbadan Begum, the daughter of Mughal emperor Babur and sister of Humayun. The book provides a vivid account of Humayun's reign and the Mughal court. It was written in Persian and is also known as 'Ahval-e-Humayun'. Gulbadan Begum is regarded as the first female historian of the Mughal Empire. This work is a crucial primary source for early Mughal history.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was Gulbadan Begum's father? → Babur
☛ What is another name for Humayun Nama? → Ahval-e-Humayun
☛ Who was Gulbadan Begum's brother? → Humayun
☛ Who was the first female historian of the Mughal Empire? → Gulbadan Begum
☛ In which language was Humayun Nama written? → Persian

q: To commemorate his victory over Gujarat, Akbar built 'Gate of Magnificence' the highest gateway of India at Fatehpur Sikri. What is another name for this gateway?
qs.e: Buland Darwaza, also known as the 'Gate of Magnificence', is the highest gateway in India, located at Fatehpur Sikri. It was built by Akbar in 1573 to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. This imposing structure stands at a height of 54 meters (171 feet) and is made of red sandstone and marble. Buland Darwaza is a magnificent example of Mughal architecture and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is considered one of the most iconic monuments in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Buland Darwaza? → Akbar
☛ Where is Buland Darwaza located? → Fatehpur Sikri
☛ Which victory does Buland Darwaza commemorate? → Victory over Gujarat
☛ What is the height of Buland Darwaza? → 54 meters (171 feet)
☛ What material is Buland Darwaza made of? → Red sandstone and marble

q: The Red Fort of Agra was founded by which Mughal Emperor?
qs.e: The Red Fort of Agra was founded by the Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1565. Located on the banks of the Yamuna River, this fort is built primarily with red sandstone. Akbar constructed it to serve as the main residence and defensive structure for his capital, Agra. Later, Emperor Shahjahan added several marble palaces inside the fort. The architecture of the fort reflects a blend of Mughal and Hindu styles. In 1983, the Agra Fort was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river's bank is the Agra Fort located? → Yamuna River
☛ When was the construction of Agra Fort started? → 1565
☛ Which Mughal emperor added marble palaces to the Agra Fort? → Shahjahan
☛ In which year did Agra Fort become a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1983
☛ Which architectural styles are blended in the Agra Fort? → Mughal and Hindu

q: Which Queen of Ahmednagar fought against Emperor Akbar?
qs.e: Chand Bibi, the queen of the Ahmednagar Sultanate, fought against Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1595-1596. She was the daughter of Sultan Hussain Nizam Shah I of Ahmednagar and the wife of Sultan Ali Adil Shah I of Bijapur. After her husband's death, she returned to Ahmednagar and became the regent for her nephew, Bahadur Nizam Shah. When Akbar attacked Ahmednagar, Chand Bibi led the defense of the fort and forced the Mughal army to retreat. A treaty was later signed, but Chand Bibi died in 1600. She is remembered for her bravery and diplomatic skills.
qs.kf:
☛ Which queen of Ahmednagar fought against Akbar? → Chand Bibi
☛ Against which Mughal emperor did Chand Bibi fight? → Akbar
☛ Who was the husband of Chand Bibi? → Ali Adil Shah I
☛ Who was the father of Chand Bibi? → Hussain Nizam Shah I
☛ When did Chand Bibi die? → 1600

q: The Shalimar Gardens located in Lahore and Kashmir are architectures of the ________.
qs.e: The Shalimar Gardens located in Lahore and Kashmir are prime examples of Mughal architecture. The Shalimar Gardens in Lahore were built in 1641 during the reign of Emperor Shah Jahan. The Shalimar Gardens in Kashmir were built in 1619 by Emperor Jahangir for his wife Nur Jahan. These gardens are designed in the Charbagh style, where the garden is divided into four parts. Mughal architecture showcases a blend of Persian and Indian styles. The Shalimar Gardens are recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Shalimar Gardens in Lahore? → Shah Jahan
☛ Who built the Shalimar Gardens in Kashmir? → Jahangir
☛ What is the style of Mughal gardens called? → Charbagh style
☛ What is a key feature of Mughal architecture? → Blend of Persian and Indian styles
☛ In which year were the Shalimar Gardens in Lahore built? → 1641

q: Panch Mahal built by Akbar is located in ________.
qs.e: Panch Mahal, built by Akbar, is located in Fatehpur Sikri. This structure is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture and was constructed between 1571 and 1585 CE. Panch Mahal is a five-storeyed palace, with each upper storey progressively smaller. It was primarily used for entertainment and audience purposes. Akbar made Fatehpur Sikri his capital in 1571, but it was later abandoned due to water scarcity. This site is different from Agra, Delhi, and Ajmer.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Panch Mahal? → Akbar
☛ Where is Panch Mahal located? → Fatehpur Sikri
☛ Who founded Fatehpur Sikri? → Akbar
☛ When was Fatehpur Sikri made capital? → 1571 CE
☛ Why was Fatehpur Sikri abandoned? → Due to water scarcity

q: Tuzuk-i-Baburi/Baburnama was originally written in:
qs.e: Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also known as Baburnama, is the autobiography of Mughal emperor Babur. It was originally written in Chagatai Turkic language, which was Babur's mother tongue. Chagatai is a Turkic language from Central Asia, prevalent in the Timurid and Mughal courts. Later, during the reign of Mughal emperor Akbar, it was translated into Persian. The work provides a detailed account of Babur's life, military campaigns, and cultural observations. It is a crucial source for the early history of the Mughal Empire.
qs.kf:
☛ Original author of Baburnama → Babur
☛ Persian translator of Baburnama → Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana
☛ Babur's mother tongue → Chaghatai Turkic
☛ Other name of Baburnama → Tuzuk-i-Baburi
☛ English translator of Baburnama → Annette Beveridge

q: In which city is Buland Darwaza located?
qs.e: Buland Darwaza is located in the city of Fatehpur Sikri in Uttar Pradesh, India. It was built by the Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1601 CE to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. It is the highest gateway in the world, with a height of about 54 meters. It is made of red sandstone and decorated with white marble. It is also known as the Gate of Victory and serves as the main entrance to the Jama Masjid.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Buland Darwaza? → Akbar
☛ When was Buland Darwaza built? → 1601 CE
☛ In whose memory was Buland Darwaza built? → Gujarat victory
☛ Which mosque's entrance is Buland Darwaza? → Jama Masjid
☛ Which stone is Buland Darwaza made of? → Red sandstone

q: Four word-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd one.
o: Sikhism : Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji
qs.e: Among the given word-pairs, three pairs represent a religion and its founder/chief propagator, while one pair represents a historical ruler and his dynasty. Jainism is founded by Mahavir, Sikhism is founded by Guru Nanak Dev Ji, and Buddhism is founded by Gautam Buddha. These three pairs are based on the religion-founder relationship. On the other hand, Humayun was a Mughal emperor, and Mughal is a dynasty. This pair indicates a ruler-dynasty relationship, which is different from the other three. Hence, Humayun : Mughal is the odd one out.
qs.kf:
☛ 24th Tirthankara of Jainism → Mahavir Swami
☛ First Guru of Sikhism → Guru Nanak Dev Ji
☛ Founder of Buddhism → Gautam Buddha
☛ Founder of Mughal dynasty → Babur
☛ Full name of Humayun → Nasir-ud-Din Muhammad Humayun

q: Who was also known as Rabia-ud-Daurani?
qs.e: Dilras Banu Begum was the wife of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and mother of Aurangzeb. She was given the title Rabia-ud-Daurani (Lady of the Age). Her original name was Dilras Banu Begum and she was a Safavid princess. Shah Jahan built the Tomb of Rabia-ud-Daurani in Agra in her honor, which is also known as Bibi ka Maqbara. This tomb is considered an inspiration for the Taj Mahal. Dilras Banu Begum died in 1657. Among other options, Asmat Begum was Jahangir's mother, Nur Jahan was Jahangir's wife, and Jagat Gosain was Jahangir's wife.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was given the title Rabia-ud-Daurani? → Dilras Banu Begum
☛ Who built Bibi ka Maqbara? → Shah Jahan
☛ Where is Bibi ka Maqbara located? → Agra
☛ Who was Dilras Banu Begum's husband? → Shah Jahan
☛ Who was Dilras Banu Begum's son? → Aurangzeb

q: Who among the following Mughal rulers of India gave permission to the British to establish their first factory in Surat?
qs.e: During the reign of Mughal Emperor Jahangir (1605-1627), the British were allowed to establish their first factory in India. In 1613, the East India Company sought permission to open a factory in Surat, which Jahangir granted. This permission was given upon the request of a British envoy, Thomas Roe, who visited Jahangir's court. This allowed the British to have a base for trade in India, gradually strengthening their influence. Jahangir provided trading facilities to the British, helping the East India Company consolidate its presence. Among the other options, Shahjahan, Bahadur Shah Zafar, and Aurangzeb were rulers during whose times the British factory was already established.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Mughal emperor allowed the British to establish a factory in Surat? → Jahangir
☛ Where was the first factory of the East India Company established in 1613? → Surat
☛ Who was the British envoy to Jahangir's court? → Thomas Roe
☛ In which year did Jahangir allow the British to set up a factory in Surat? → 1613
☛ What was the reign period of Mughal Emperor Jahangir? → 1605-1627

q: The battle in which Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi was the:
qs.e: The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. Babur's use of artillery and superior military tactics led to a decisive victory. Ibrahim Lodi was killed in the battle, marking the end of the Lodi dynasty and the Delhi Sultanate. This battle laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India. Babur then captured Delhi and Agra.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first battle of Panipat fought? → 1526
☛ Who did Babur defeat in the first battle of Panipat? → Ibrahim Lodi
☛ What war tactic did Babur use in the first battle of Panipat? → The Ottoman or Rumi tactic
☛ Which new weapon did Babur's army use in the first battle of Panipat? → Cannons
☛ Which cities did Babur capture after the first battle of Panipat? → Delhi and Agra

q: Peacock Throne (Frames Tauce) was built during whose reign?
qs.e: The Peacock Throne was built during the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. It was constructed in the mid-17th century and symbolized Mughal power and opulence. The throne was designed in the shape of a peacock, adorned with precious gems and gold. It was kept in the Red Fort of Delhi. In 1739, Nadir Shah invaded India and looted the throne, taking it to Iran. The French traveler François Bernier also described this magnificent throne in his writings.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Peacock Throne? → Shah Jahan
☛ Where was the Peacock Throne located? → Red Fort, Delhi
☛ Who looted the Peacock Throne? → Nadir Shah
☛ Famous monument built during Shah Jahan's reign? → Taj Mahal
☛ Shah Jahan's reign period? → 1628–1658

q: Which of the following ruler made Jama Masjid in Delhi?
qs.e: The famous Jama Masjid in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan. It is one of the largest mosques in India. Construction took place between 1650 and 1656 CE. Shah Jahan built this mosque in his capital Shahjahanabad (Old Delhi). The chief architect of the mosque was Ustad Khalil. It has three gates, two minarets, and a large courtyard that can accommodate about 25,000 worshippers. The mosque is built with red sandstone and white marble. During Shah Jahan's reign, other magnificent monuments like the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort were also constructed.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Jama Masjid in Delhi? → Shah Jahan
☛ When was the Jama Masjid construction completed? → 1656 CE
☛ Who was the chief architect of Jama Masjid? → Ustad Khalil
☛ What was the name of Shah Jahan's capital? → Shahjahanabad
☛ Other major monuments built by Shah Jahan? → Taj Mahal and Red Fort

q: Which of the following was a famous painter during the reign of Jahangir?
qs.e: During Jahangir's reign (1605-1627 AD), Mughal painting reached its zenith. Ustad Mansoor was a leading painter of that period, renowned for his realistic depictions of flora and fauna. Jahangir honored him with the title 'Nadir-ul-Asr' (Wonder of the Age). Other options: Nandalal Bose (modern Indian art), Raja Ravi Varma (19th century), and M. F. Hussain (20th century) do not belong to that era.
qs.kf:
☛ Court painter of Jahangir → Ustad Mansoor
☛ Title given to Ustad Mansoor → Nadir-ul-Asr
☛ Golden age of Mughal painting → Jahangir's reign
☛ Painter of 'Siberian Crane' → Ustad Mansoor
☛ Painter of Baburnama → Ustad Mansoor

q: Which of the following Mughal rulers laid the foundations of Dinapnah, but could not fulfill it?
qs.e: Humayun planned to build a new city called Dinapnah in Delhi, whose foundation was laid in 1533 AD. The purpose was to establish a new capital, but due to political instability and the invasion of Sher Shah Suri, he could not complete it. Later, Sher Shah built the fort Shergarh on the same site. Although Humayun later regained Delhi, the construction of Dinapnah remained unfinished. This project is considered an important attempt in Mughal architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Mughal ruler started building Dinapnah? → Humayun
☛ When was the foundation of Dinapnah laid? → 1533 AD
☛ Who completed Dinapnah? → None (remained incomplete)
☛ Which fort did Sher Shah build on the site of Dinapnah? → Shergarh
☛ What was Humayun's full name? → Nasiruddin Humayun

q: Humayun-Naama is composed by whom
qs.e: Humayun-Naama is a historical text based on the life of Mughal emperor Humayun. It was written by Gulbadan Begum, who was the daughter of Babar and sister of Humayun. This book was originally written in the Persian language and describes Humayun's reign, his exploits, and the conditions of the Mughal Empire. Gulbadan Begum wrote this work at the request of Akbar, which provides important information about Mughal history. This text is known for its authenticity and detailed narration.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the author of Humayun-Naama? → Gulbadan Begum
☛ Gulbadan Begum was the daughter of whom? → Babar
☛ In which language was Humayun-Naama written? → Persian
☛ At whose request was Humayun-Naama written? → Akbar
☛ What relation was Gulbadan Begum to Humayun? → Sister

q: During which of the following Mughal ,painting was at its peak?
qs.e: Mughal painting reached its peak during the reign of Jahangir. He had a deep knowledge of art and patronized painting. During his reign, realism and naturalism were incorporated into Mughal painting. Famous painters include Ustad Mansur, Abul Hasan, and Bishandas. Jahangir himself was a skilled art critic and understood the intricacies of paintings. During this period, depiction of animals, birds, and plants received special attention. Jahangir blended Persian and Indian styles to create a unique style.
qs.kf:
☛ Court painters of Jahangir → Ustad Mansur, Abul Hasan, Bishandas
☛ Painting style encouraged by Jahangir → Realistic and naturalistic
☛ Peak of realism in Mughal painting → Jahangir's reign
☛ Painter specialized in animal and bird depiction → Ustad Mansur
☛ Mention of painting in Jahangir's autobiography Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri → Yes

q: Which province was established by Nizam-ul-Mulk Asfajah in 1724?
qs.e: In 1724, Nizam-ul-Mulk Asfajah, a powerful noble of the Mughal Empire, established his independent authority in the Deccan and founded the Hyderabad state. He was the governor of the Deccan under Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah, but due to central weakness, he declared autonomy. This led to the creation of the Hyderabad state, which later remained a major princely state until the British period. Hyderabad was known for its rich culture and administrative system. The Nizam adopted Mughal administrative techniques and developed a strong army and tax system. This establishment is a key example of the disintegration of the Mughal Empire and the rise of regional powers in Indian history.
qs.kf:
☛ Who established the Hyderabad state? → Nizam-ul-Mulk Asfajah
☛ Year of establishment → 1724
☛ Original position of Nizam → Mughal governor of Deccan
☛ Related Mughal emperor → Muhammad Shah
☛ Which dynasty ruled Hyderabad? → Asaf Jahi dynasty

q: Who drew a new religion called Din-i-Elahi?
qs.e: Din-i-Elahi was a religious movement founded by the Mughal emperor Akbar in 1582 AD. Its aim was to synthesize the best elements of various religions and create a new faith that promoted religious tolerance and unity in Akbar's empire. Din-i-Elahi was mainly based on principles of Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, Christianity, and Jainism. It emphasized monotheism and regarded Akbar as the spiritual leader. However, it remained limited to a few select members of Akbar's court and became obsolete after his death. Abul Fazl, one of Akbar's Navratnas, supported Akbar's religious ideology. Din-i-Elahi never gained a large following.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Din-i-Elahi → Akbar
☛ Year of establishment of Din-i-Elahi → 1582 AD
☛ Akbar's religious advisor → Abul Fazl
☛ Religions included in Din-i-Elahi → Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, Christianity, Jainism
☛ Building built by Akbar for religious discussions → Ibadat Khana

q: Taj Mahal was constructed in memory of ___________.
qs.e: The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Her real name was Arjumand Banu Begum. This monument is located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of river Yamuna. The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered a masterpiece of Islamic architecture. Its construction started in 1632 and was completed in 1653, involving over 20,000 artisans. The main building material is white marble inlaid with precious stones.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Taj Mahal? → Shah Jahan
☛ Which river is the Taj Mahal located on? → Yamuna
☛ What is the architectural style of the Taj Mahal? → Islamic/Mughal
☛ What was Mumtaz Mahal's real name? → Arjumand Banu Begum
☛ When was the Taj Mahal declared a UNESCO World Heritage site? → 1983

q: Birbal was a member of which Mughal Emperor's court?
qs.e: Birbal, originally named Mahesh Das, was one of the Nine Gems (Navaratnas) in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar. He was renowned for his wit, wisdom, and administrative skills. During Akbar's reign (1556-1605), Birbal served as a close advisor and poet. The anecdotes between Akbar and Birbal remain popular in Indian folklore. He represented Hindu perspectives in the Mughal court and participated in religious discussions. Birbal died in 1586 during a military campaign in the Swat Valley. His legacy as a symbol of intellect and humor continues to be celebrated.
qs.kf:
☛ Who were the Navaratnas of Akbar? → Todar Mal, Birbal, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Tansen, Man Singh, Bhagwan Das, Mulla Do Piyaza, and Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana
☛ What was Birbal's real name? → Mahesh Das
☛ In which battle did Birbal die? → Swat Valley campaign (1586)
☛ Which religion did Akbar found? → Din-i-Ilahi
☛ What was Akbar's reign period? → 1556-1605

q: Who among the following emperors built the Taj Mahal?
qs.e: The Taj Mahal was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It is located in Agra, India, on the banks of the Yamuna River. Construction began in 1632 and was completed in 1653. Made of white marble, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered a symbol of love. The Taj Mahal is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is the Taj Mahal located on? → Yamuna River
☛ Who was the chief architect of the Taj Mahal? → Ustad Ahmad Lahauri
☛ How many years did it take to build the Taj Mahal? → 21 years (1632-1653)
☛ When was the Taj Mahal inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1983
☛ Where is Shah Jahan's tomb located? → Inside the Taj Mahal

q: Who was the founder of the Mughal dynasty?
qs.e: Babur founded the Mughal dynasty in 1526 AD after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat. He was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan. Babur was the ruler of Ferghana (present-day Uzbekistan) and later ruled Kabul before invading India. He won the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga, the Battle of Chanderi (1528) against Medini Rai, and the Battle of Ghaghra (1529) against the Afghans. Babur was a skilled general, writer, and nature lover. He wrote his autobiography Baburnama in Turkish, later translated into English as 'Memoirs of Babur'. He died in 1530 AD in Agra.
qs.kf:
☛ Babur's autobiography → Baburnama
☛ Language of Baburnama → Turkish
☛ Babur's tomb → Kabul
☛ Babur's ancestral kingdom → Ferghana
☛ First Mughal emperor → Babur

q: Who translated 'The Mahabharat' called 'Razmnama' into Persian language, during the Mughal Period?
qs.e: During the Mughal period, the translation of 'The Mahabharata' into Persian was titled 'Razmnama' (Book of War). This translation was commissioned under the rule of Akbar. Abul Fazl, one of the nine gems (Navratnas) of Akbar's court, oversaw this project. The aim was to promote interfaith understanding and make Hindu epics accessible to the Muslim community. Several scholars contributed, but Abul Fazl led the entire endeavor. 'Razmnama' was later adorned with miniature paintings, exemplifying Mughal artistry.
qs.kf:
☛ Who commissioned the translation of Razmnama? → Akbar
☛ Abul Fazl was a Navratna of which emperor? → Akbar
☛ What does 'Razmnama' mean in Persian? → Book of War
☛ What is the Persian translation of Mahabharata called? → Razmnama
☛ Which epic was translated during Akbar's reign? → Mahabharata

q: Who was Akbar’s revenue minister?
qs.e: During the reign of Akbar, the revenue minister was Raja Todar Mal. He streamlined the land revenue system and introduced the Dahshala system (also known as Todar Mal's settlement). Under this system, land measurement, crop classification, and revenue assessment were based on average yield. Todar Mal was born in 1524 AD in Sitapur (Uttar Pradesh). He standardized revenue collection across different regions of Akbar's empire and developed a simple tax system for farmers. He is considered one of the 'Navratnas' of Akbar, though some scholars debate his inclusion. His reforms brought stability to the empire's finances.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of the Dahshala system? → Raja Todar Mal
☛ Which minister of Akbar reformed the land revenue system? → Raja Todar Mal
☛ By what name is Todar Mal's settlement known? → Dahshala system
☛ From which place did Raja Todar Mal originate? → Sitapur (Uttar Pradesh)
☛ Who was the revenue minister during Akbar's reign? → Raja Todar Mal

q: Who among the following wrote Akbar Nama?
qs.e: The Akbar Nama is the official history of the reign of Mughal Emperor Akbar, written by Abul Fazl. It is divided into three volumes: the first describes Akbar's ancestors and his early life, the second gives a detailed account of Akbar's reign, and the third is the Ain-i-Akbari, focusing on the administration, society, and culture of the empire. Abul Fazl was one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court, and his work is considered a crucial historical source.
qs.kf:
☛ Autobiography written by Babur → Babur Nama (in Turkish)
☛ Autobiography written by Jahangir → Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri
☛ Book written by Abul Fazl → Akbar Nama and Ain-i-Akbari
☛ Book written by Barani → Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
☛ Association of the author of Akbar Nama → Abul Fazl was a historian and Navratna of Mughal court

q: The Mughals were descendants of which clan?
qs.e: The founder of the Mughal Empire, Babur, was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side. He belonged to the Chaghtai Turk Mongol clan. The term 'Mughal' is derived from Persian, meaning 'Mongol'. Babur's ancestor Timur (Timurid Empire) was from the Chaghtai lineage, which originated from Genghis Khan's son Chaghtai. The Mughals traced their genealogy to Timur and were raised in the Turko-Mongol tradition. Thus, they were neither pure Mongols nor full Turks, but from the mixed Chaghtai Turk-Mongol clan.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of the Mughal dynasty → Babur
☛ Name of Babur's father → Umar Sheikh Mirza
☛ Name of Babur's mother → Qutlugh Nigar Khanum
☛ Title used by Mughal rulers → 'Badshah' or 'Padshah'
☛ Name of Babur's grandfather → Abu Sa'id Mirza

q: The first volume of Akbarnama dealt with the history of _______.
qs.e: The Akbarnama is the official history of Mughal emperor Akbar, written by Abul Fazl in Persian. It is divided into three volumes. The first volume deals with the history of Akbar's ancestors, covering from Timur and Babur to Humayun. The second volume describes the events of Akbar's reign, and the third volume is the Ain-i-Akbari, which focuses on administration, army, and revenues. This work is a key source for Mughal history.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote Akbarnama? → Abul Fazl
☛ In which language was Akbarnama written? → Persian
☛ What is the name of the third volume of Akbarnama? → Ain-i-Akbari
☛ Whose reign is described in Akbarnama? → Akbar
☛ How many volumes are in Akbarnama? → Three

q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India?
qs.e: The Mughal Empire was founded by Babur. He was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan. In 1526, he defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat, laying the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India. In 1527, he won the Battle of Khanwa, weakening Rajput power. Babur ruled until his death in 1530. His autobiography, Baburnama, was written in Turkish.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Mughal dynasty? → Babur
☛ When was the First Battle of Panipat fought? → 1526
☛ Whom did Babur defeat in the Battle of Khanwa? → Rana Sanga
☛ In which language was Baburnama written? → Turkish
☛ Babur was a descendant of which dynasty? → Timur and Genghis Khan

q: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought between the forces of _______.
qs.e: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556 between the forces of Akbar and Hemu (Hemchandra Vikramaditya). Hemu was a Hindu ruler who had captured Delhi and assumed the title of Vikramaditya. The Mughal army was led by Bairam Khan on behalf of Akbar. In this battle, Hemu's forces were defeated and Hemu was captured and executed. This victory re-established the Mughal Empire in North India and strengthened Akbar's reign.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Second Battle of Panipat fought? → 1556
☛ Who led Akbar's army? → Bairam Khan
☛ What was Hemu's title? → Vikramaditya
☛ Which battle re-established the Mughal Empire? → Second Battle of Panipat
☛ What was Hemu's community? → Hindu (Mewati)

q: When did Akbar become the emperor of Delhi?
qs.e: Akbar was born in 1542. He became the emperor of Delhi in 1556 at the young age of 13, after the death of his father Humayun. He was the third ruler of the Mughal Empire and reigned for nearly 50 years. His reign is considered the golden age of the Mughal Empire. Akbar emphasized religious tolerance, centralized administration, and land revenue reforms. He built the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri and founded the Din-i-Ilahi religion. His Navratnas included scholars like Birbal, Todar Mal, and Abul Fazl.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Akbar born? → 1542
☛ What is Akbar's reign called? → Golden Age
☛ Which religion did Akbar found? → Din-i-Ilahi
☛ How many Navratnas were in Akbar's court? → 9
☛ Where did Akbar build the Ibadat Khana? → Fatehpur Sikri

q: Tuzuk-i-Baburi was written in which language?
qs.e: Tuzuk-i-Baburi is the autobiography of Babur, originally written in Chagatai Turkish. This language is an eastern dialect of Turkish, which was Babur's mother tongue. Later, it was translated into Persian by Abdurrahim Khan-i-Khanan. The book describes Babur's life, his military campaigns, and the early history of the Mughal Empire he founded. Babur wrote this book in a highly personal and candid style, sharing his experiences and observations. It is considered one of the earliest examples of autobiography in Islamic literature, offering valuable insights into the politics, culture, and society of the time.
qs.kf:
☛ Original language of Tuzuk-i-Baburi → Chagatai Turkish
☛ Who translated Tuzuk-i-Baburi into Persian → Abdurrahim Khan-i-Khanan
☛ Author of Tuzuk-i-Baburi → Babur
☛ Alternate name of Tuzuk-i-Baburi → Baburnama
☛ Style used in Tuzuk-i-Baburi → Autobiographical style

q: The Battle of Khanua was fought between _______.
qs.e: The Battle of Khanua was fought on March 17, 1527, between Babur and Rana Sanga. This battle was crucial for Babur to establish his rule in India. Rana Sanga was the ruler of Mewar and led a Rajput confederacy. Babur effectively used artillery and cannon formation, leading to the defeat of the Rajput army. This victory strengthened Babur's Mughal empire. Rana Sanga was severely wounded in the battle and later died.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Battle of Khanua fought? → 1527
☛ Who effectively used artillery in the Battle of Khanua? → Babur
☛ Rana Sanga was the ruler of which state? → Mewar
☛ Which military tactic did Babur use in the Battle of Khanua? → Artillery and cannon formation
☛ Who strengthened Mughal power after the Battle of Khanua? → Babur

q: During the rule of which of the following Mughal rulers did Sunnis and Shias meet in one mosque and Christians and Jews in one church to pray, thus following the principle of 'universal peace' (sulh-i kul)?
qs.e: Mughal emperor Akbar adopted a policy of religious tolerance in his empire known as sulh-i kul (universal peace). During his reign, he established the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri, where scholars of different religions discussed theological matters. According to the historian Abul Fazl, Akbar arranged a place where Sunnis and Shias could pray together in one mosque, and Christians and Jews in one church, in line with the principle of sulh-i kul. This reflected his commitment to interfaith harmony. Akbar also founded a syncretic religion called Din-i Ilahi, though it did not last long. His policies fostered communal harmony and strengthened the empire's unity.
qs.kf:
☛ Name of Akbar's religious policy → Sulh-i kul
☛ Location of Ibadat Khana → Fatehpur Sikri
☛ Religion founded by Akbar → Din-i Ilahi
☛ Work authored by Abul Fazl → Ain-i Akbari
☛ Akbar's reign period → 1556-1605

q: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was fought between Ahmad Shah Abdali and which Indian power?
qs.e: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was fought between Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas. It took place on January 14, 1761, and is considered one of the largest battles in India. The Maratha forces were led by Sadashivrao Bhau, while Abdali's army included Afghans and Rohillas. The Marathas lost due to internal divisions, lack of supplies, and Abdali's superior strategy. This battle significantly weakened the Maratha Empire and paved the way for the rise of British power in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat? → Sadashivrao Bhau
☛ When was the Third Battle of Panipat fought? → 14 January 1761
☛ Ahmad Shah Abdali was the ruler of which country? → Afghanistan
☛ What artillery technique was used in the Third Battle of Panipat? → Zainal artillery
☛ What was the outcome of the Third Battle of Panipat? → Weakening of Maratha Empire

q: The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526, replacing the Lodi Dynasty with Mughal rule in India. It was fought between Ibrahim Lodi and _____.
qs.e: The First Battle of Panipat was fought on April 21, 1526, between Ibrahim Lodi and Babar. Using superior strategy and artillery, Babar defeated Lodi's army, ending the Lodi Dynasty and establishing the Mughal Empire in India. Babar was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of First Battle of Panipat → 1526
☛ Key strategy used in the battle → Artillery and Tulughma tactics
☛ Dynasty established after the battle → Mughal Dynasty
☛ Babar's lineage → Descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan
☛ Ibrahim Lodi's dynasty → Lodi Dynasty

q: The Red Fort in Delhi was constructed during the reign of which of the following Mughal emperors?
qs.e: The Red Fort in Delhi was constructed during the reign of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. Its construction began in 1638 and was completed in 1648. Located on the banks of the Yamuna River, it is an excellent example of Mughal architecture. Shah Jahan shifted his capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad (Old Delhi), with this fort as its centerpiece. The Red Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and every year on Independence Day, the Prime Minister hoists the national flag here.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Red Fort? → Shah Jahan
☛ When did construction of Red Fort start? → 1638
☛ When was Red Fort completed? → 1648
☛ Which river is the Red Fort located on? → Yamuna
☛ In which year did Red Fort become a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 2007

q: During the Mughal period, the Ain-i-Dahsala system was introduced by _____.
qs.e: The Ain-i-Dahsala system was introduced by the Mughal emperor Akbar. It was a crucial part of the land revenue system developed under the guidance of Raja Todar Mal. Under this system, land was measured and assessed based on the average production over ten years, and the revenue was collected from farmers in cash at a fixed rate. This system was fairer and more transparent for the farmers and provided financial stability to the Mughal Empire. The Ain-i-Dahsala is considered a major reform in Mughal revenue administration.
qs.kf:
☛ During whose reign was the Ain-i-Dahsala system introduced? → Akbar
☛ What was the basis for revenue assessment under this system? → Average production of ten years
☛ Who was the key official associated with the Ain-i-Dahsala system? → Raja Todar Mal
☛ In which system was revenue collected in cash? → Ain-i-Dahsala
☛ What type of system was Ain-i-Dahsala? → Land revenue system

q: Who was declared the Emperor of India by the revolting sepoys during the 1857 uprising?
qs.e: During the 1857 uprising, the revolting sepoys declared Bahadur Shah II as the Emperor of India. He was the last ruler of the Mughal dynasty and led the rebellion. Also known as Bahadur Shah Zafar, he was proclaimed Emperor after the sepoys captured Delhi. The uprising, also called the First War of Independence, began in Meerut and spread across northern India. The British East India Company suppressed the revolt, deposed Bahadur Shah, and exiled him to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was declared the leader of the 1857 revolt? → Bahadur Shah II
☛ Bahadur Shah II belonged to which dynasty? → Mughal dynasty
☛ Where did the 1857 uprising start? → Meerut
☛ What was Bahadur Shah II's pen name? → Zafar
☛ Where was Bahadur Shah II exiled? → Rangoon

q: In which of the following sections of Akbarnama does Abul Fazal discuss Akbar's administration, household, army, revenue and geography of his empire?
o: in both the second and third sections
in both the first and second sections
qs.e: Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl in three volumes. The first volume deals with Akbar's ancestors and the early part of his reign. The second volume describes the events of Akbar's reign. The third volume, known as Ain-i-Akbari, discusses Akbar's administration, royal household, army, revenue system, and geography of the empire in detail. It is in Ain-i-Akbari that a systematic account of Akbar's policies, institutions, and various aspects of the empire is found. Hence, the third section focuses on administration, household, army, revenue, and geography.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote Akbarnama? → Abul Fazl
☛ Which volume is Ain-i-Akbari a part of? → Third volume
☛ How many volumes are in Akbarnama? → Three volumes
☛ What is not discussed in Ain-i-Akbari? → Akbar's biography
☛ What does the first volume of Akbarnama focus on? → Akbar's ancestors

q: Who among the following compiled the Mriga-Pasi-Shastra in the 13th century, which gave details of animals and birds of prey?
qs.e: In the 13th century, Hansdev compiled the Mriga-Pasi-Shastra, a text that provides detailed descriptions of animals and birds of prey used for hunting. The work covers various wild species, their habits, and hunting techniques. It is considered an important medieval Indian source on hunting art and falconry. While Akbar and Jahangir were Mughal rulers of the 16th-17th centuries, Mansoor was a renowned painter known for depicting wildlife in Mughal miniatures. Hence, the correct option is Hansdev.
qs.kf:
☛ Compiler of Mriga-Pasi-Shastra → Hansdev
☛ Content of Mriga-Pasi-Shastra → Details of animals and birds of prey
☛ Century of composition of Mriga-Pasi-Shastra → 13th century
☛ Mughal ruler who wrote on hunting → Jahangir (Tuzuk-e-Jahangiri)
☛ Mansoor's field → Mughal painting (wildlife depictions)

q: Under Akbar, who was responsible for revenue and financial supervision across the entire Mughal Empire?
qs.e: Under Akbar, Diwan-i-Kul was responsible for revenue and financial supervision across the entire Mughal Empire.
