The empire lasted for about 300 years and was a patron of Hindu culture and religion. Its zenith was under Krishnadevaraya, but he was not the founder.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Vijayanagar Empire? → Harihar and Bukka
☛ On which river is Vijayanagar located? → Tungabhadra River
☛ To which dynasty did Harihar and Bukka belong? → Sangama dynasty
☛ When was the Vijayanagar Empire founded? → 1336 AD
☛ What was the capital of Vijayanagar? → Hampi (Vijayanagar)

q: Krishnadevaraya was the ruler of _________ empire.
qs.e: Krishnadevaraya was the most famous ruler of the Vijayanagar Empire. He belonged to the Tuluva dynasty and reigned from 1509 to 1529 AD. His reign is considered the golden age of the Vijayanagar Empire. He promoted art, literature, and architecture. His court had eight scholars known as Ashtadiggajas. He defeated the Sultan of Bijapur in the Battle of Raichur (1520 AD). He also renovated the Tirupati temple. He wrote works like Amuktamalyada in Telugu and Madalasacharita in Sanskrit. Under his rule, the empire extended across much of South India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Vijayanagar Empire? → Harihara and Bukka
☛ Krishnadevaraya belonged to which dynasty? → Tuluva dynasty
☛ Who was the court poet of Krishnadevaraya? → Tenali Rama
☛ What was the capital of the Vijayanagar Empire? → Vijayanagar (modern Hampi)
☛ Whom did Krishnadevaraya defeat? → Bijapur Sultan

q: The famous Golconda Fort is situated in the state of:
qs.e: The Golconda Fort is located near Hyderabad, the capital of Telangana state. Built by the Qutb Shahi dynasty in the 16th century, it is renowned for its architecture and acoustic system. Golconda Fort is one of India's prominent historical forts and is on the tentative list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The fort's name is derived from the Telugu word "Golla Konda" (shepherd's hill). It served as the capital of the Golconda Sultanate and was a major center for diamond trade; the famous Kohinoor diamond was mined here.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Golconda Fort? → Qutb Shahi dynasty (originally Kakatiya dynasty built a mud fort, later expanded by Qutb Shahi)
☛ Which river is near Golconda Fort? → Musi River
☛ What is the famous feature of Golconda Fort? → Acoustic system (clap sound could be heard at the top)
☛ What was the ancient name of Golconda Fort? → Golla Konda (shepherd's hill)
☛ Which famous diamond was found from Golconda Fort? → Kohinoor diamond

q: Tirumala Raya was the founder of which of the following dynasties in ancient India?
qs.e: Tirumala Raya was the founder of the Aravidu dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire. This was the fourth and last dynasty of the empire. He established the dynasty after the Battle of Talikota in 1565 CE. He ruled from the capital Penukonda. The Aravidu dynasty reigned from 1570 to 1646 CE. The last ruler of this dynasty was Sriranga III, during whose rule the empire declined. Other options: The Tuluva dynasty was founded by Veeranarasimha; the Saluva dynasty was founded by Saluva Narasimha; the Sangama dynasty was founded by Harihara and Bukka.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Aravidu dynasty? → Tirumala Raya
☛ When was the Battle of Talikota fought? → 1565 CE
☛ What was the capital of the Aravidu dynasty? → Penukonda
☛ Which was the last dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire? → Aravidu
☛ Who was the last ruler of the Aravidu dynasty? → Sriranga III

q: Which of the following statements about the Charminar in Hyderabad is INCORRECT?
o: It is built upon four grand arches facing North, South, East and West.
It was built by Mohammed Quli Qutb Shah, in 1591.
It marked the end of plague in the city.
The arches support four floors of rooms and a gallery of archways.
qs.e: Charminar is a historic monument in Hyderabad built by Mohammed Quli Qutb Shah in 1591. It marks the end of plague in the city. It is built on four grand arches facing North, South, East, and West. The arches support two floors of rooms and a gallery, not four floors. Thus, the fourth statement is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Charminar? → Mohammed Quli Qutb Shah
☛ Year of construction of Charminar? → 1591
☛ In which city is Charminar located? → Hyderabad
☛ How many floors do the arches of Charminar support? → Two floors
☛ Which disease's end does Charminar symbolize? → Plague

q: Hampi was the capital of the __________ Kingdom.
qs.e: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagar Empire. The Vijayanagar Empire (1336-1646) was founded by Harihara and Bukka. It was a prominent Hindu empire in South India. Hampi, located in present-day Karnataka, was renowned for its grand architecture and culture. The city was situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River. The glory of Hampi was destroyed after the Battle of Talikota in 1565. Today, Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the capital of the Vijayanagar Empire? → Hampi
☛ Who founded the Vijayanagar Empire? → Harihara and Bukka
☛ On which river is Hampi located? → Tungabhadra
☛ When was the Battle of Talikota fought? → 1565
☛ In which year was Hampi declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1986

q: There were constant conflicts between Vijayanagar and ________ over the control of the Raichur doab, which was the land between the rivers Krishna and Tungabhadra.
qs.e: There were constant conflicts between the Vijayanagar Empire and the Bahmani Sultanate over the control of the Raichur Doab, the fertile land between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers. This region was strategically and economically important, leading to numerous wars. The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 CE by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah. Vijayanagar rulers like Devaraya II and Krishnadevaraya fought the Bahmani sultans for this doab. The rivalry continued until the 16th century. The Raichur Doab was a major cause of conflict between the two powers.
qs.kf:
☛ Between which rivers is the Raichur Doab located? → Krishna and Tungabhadra
☛ Who founded the Bahmani Sultanate? → Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah
☛ When was the Bahmani Sultanate founded? → 1347 CE
☛ Which Vijayanagar rulers fought for the Raichur Doab? → Devaraya II and Krishnadevaraya
☛ What was the strategic importance of Raichur Doab? → Fertile land and control over trade routes

q: The present-day ________ used to be the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
A. Hampi
B. Mysore
C. Belur
D. Srirangapattanam
qs.e: The capital of the Vijayanagara Empire was Hampi, which is located in present-day Karnataka. The empire existed from 1336 to 1646 CE and was founded by Harihara and Bukka. Hampi was also known as Vijayanagara. It was situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River. After the Battle of Talikota in 1565, the city was destroyed. Today, Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is famous for its grand temples, palaces and ruins. Other options like Mysore, Belur and Srirangapattanam were not capitals of the Vijayanagara Empire.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire? → Hampi
☛ Which river flows near Hampi? → Tungabhadra
☛ Who founded the Vijayanagara Empire? → Harihara and Bukka
☛ What is the other name of Hampi? → Vijayanagara
☛ In which present-day state is Hampi located? → Karnataka

q: Which of the following dynasties is associated with the Thousand Pillars Temple at Warangal built in the 12th century?
qs.e: The Thousand Pillars Temple is located in Warangal, Telangana, and was built in the 12th century during the reign of the Kakatiya dynasty. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva, Vishnu, and Surya. It features over a thousand intricately carved pillars, showcasing exquisite architecture. The Kakatiya dynasty ruled southern India from the 12th to the 14th century, with Warangal as their capital. Prominent rulers included Ganapati Deva and Rudrama Devi. The temple is a proposed UNESCO World Heritage Site.
qs.kf:
☛ Which dynasty is associated with the Thousand Pillars Temple? → Kakatiya dynasty
☛ Where is the temple located? → Warangal, Telangana
☛ What was the capital of the Kakatiya dynasty? → Warangal
☛ Which famous queen belonged to the Kakatiya dynasty? → Rudrama Devi
☛ Who was the last ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty? → Prataparudra II

q: During the second quarter of the 14th century, three independent kingdoms were established in South India. Which of the following was NOT part of it?
qs.e: During the second quarter of the 14th century (approximately 1325-1350), three independent kingdoms were established in South India: the Vijayanagara Empire, the Bahmani Sultanate, and the Ma'bar Sultanate. Vijayanagara was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka. The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah. The Ma'bar Sultanate (Madurai Sultanate) was established in 1335 by Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah. Daulatabad (Devagiri) was the capital of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Delhi Sultanate and was not part of these three independent South Indian kingdoms. Therefore, Daulatabad was NOT part of this group.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Vijayanagara Empire established? → 1336
☛ Who founded the Bahmani Sultanate? → Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah
☛ What is the other name of Ma'bar Sultanate? → Madurai Sultanate
☛ Daulatabad was the capital of which dynasty? → Tughlaq dynasty
☛ Which ruler shifted his capital to Daulatabad? → Muhammad bin Tughlaq

q: Which of the following turned the Sikhs into a military sect?
qs.e: Guru Gobind Singh (1666–1708) was the tenth Guru of the Sikhs. In 1699, he founded the Khalsa Panth at Anandpur Sahib, which transformed the Sikhs into a military sect. The Khalsa means 'pure' and was established to fight for religious freedom and against tyranny. Guru Gobind Singh introduced the Five K's: Kesh, Kara, Kirpan, Kanga, and Kachera. He made the Sikhs physically and spiritually strong, and led wars against Mughal oppression. Guru Teg Bahadur sacrificed his life, Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth, and Banda Bahadur was a Sikh military commander, but the credit for turning the Sikhs into a military sect goes to Guru Gobind Singh.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Khalsa Panth? → Guru Gobind Singh
☛ Who introduced the Five K's? → Guru Gobind Singh
☛ When was Guru Gobind Singh born? → 1666
☛ When did Guru Gobind Singh establish the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib? → 1699
☛ Who was the father of Guru Gobind Singh? → Guru Teg Bahadur

q: Who defeated the Marathas in the third battle of Panipat?
qs.e: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the Maratha Empire and the Afghan forces led by Ahmed Shah Abdali. The Marathas suffered a devastating defeat. The Maratha army was commanded by Sadashivrao Bhau. This battle weakened the Maratha power significantly and increased Abdali's influence in northern India. It was a decisive conflict for control over North India after the decline of the Mughal Empire.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Third Battle of Panipat fought? → 1761
☛ Who led the Marathas in this battle? → Sadashivrao Bhau
☛ Ahmed Shah Abdali was the ruler of which region? → Afghanistan
☛ Which community did not support the Marathas in this battle? → Sikhs
☛ What was the outcome of the Third Battle of Panipat? → Maratha defeat and Abdali's victory

q: At which Sikh Guru's invitation did the Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir lay the foundation stone of Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar?
qs.e: The foundation stone of the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar was laid in 1588 CE by the Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir at the invitation of the fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan Dev ji. Guru Arjan Dev ji not only supervised the construction of the temple but also compiled the Guru Granth Sahib. This event symbolizes religious tolerance and interfaith respect in Sikhism. Mian Mir was a revered Sufi saint from Lahore and a close friend of Guru Arjan Dev ji.
qs.kf:
☛ Who laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple? → Hazrat Mian Mir
☛ Which Sikh Guru built the Golden Temple? → Guru Arjan Dev ji
☛ Who compiled the Guru Granth Sahib? → Guru Arjan Dev ji
☛ To which order did Hazrat Mian Mir belong? → Sufi
☛ Where is the Golden Temple located? → Amritsar, Punjab

q: Shree Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born in Rai Bhoi Ki Talwandi (present day Nankana Sahib) in:
qs.e: Shree Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, was born on 15 April 1469 in Rai Bhoi Ki Talwandi (present day Nankana Sahib, Pakistan). He is the first of the ten Sikh Gurus. He preached the message of 'Ek Onkar' (One God) and equality. His teachings are compiled in the Guru Granth Sahib. He died in 1539 at Kartarpur.
qs.kf:
☛ Birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev Ji → Rai Bhoi Ki Talwandi (Nankana Sahib)
☛ Father of Guru Nanak Dev Ji → Kalu Chand (Mehta Kalu)
☛ Mother of Guru Nanak Dev Ji → Tripta Devi
☛ Wife of Guru Nanak Dev Ji → Sulakhani (Mata Sulakhni)
☛ Major composition by him → Japuji Sahib

q: Which community has the Adi Granth as their Holy Book?
qs.e: Adi Granth, also known as Guru Granth Sahib, is the holy scripture of Sikhism. It was compiled by the fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan Dev Ji, in 1604. The text includes hymns of Sikh Gurus, Hindu saints, and Muslim Sufis. It is considered the living Guru of the Sikhs and elaborates on core Sikh principles such as one God, equality, and service. The holy book of Buddhists is Tripitaka, of Jains is Agam, and of Jews is Tanakh.
qs.kf:
☛ Compiler of Adi Granth → Guru Arjan Dev Ji
☛ Year of compilation of Adi Granth → 1604 CE
☛ Holy book of Sikhs → Guru Granth Sahib (Adi Granth)
☛ Languages in Adi Granth → Punjabi, Sanskrit, Braj, Arabic, Persian
☛ Holy book of Buddhists → Tripitaka

q: Which of the following kings was sent by Aurangzeb against Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj?
qs.e: Aurangzeb sent Raja Jai Singh (the Kachhwaha Rajput ruler of Amber) as the commander of the Mughal expedition to the Deccan in 1665 to subdue Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Jai Singh defeated Shivaji in the Battle of Purandar (1665), resulting in the Treaty of Purandar. Under this treaty, Shivaji surrendered 23 forts to the Mughals and agreed to attend the Mughal court. Later, Jai Singh arranged Shivaji's journey to Agra to meet Aurangzeb, where he was imprisoned. Jai Singh was a loyal Mughal general and played a key role in several campaigns against the Deccan sultanates.
qs.kf:
☛ Treaty of Purandar was signed between whom? → Shivaji and Jai Singh
☛ Jai Singh was the ruler of which state? → Amber (Jaipur)
☛ Who invited Shivaji to Agra? → Jai Singh
☛ Who was the commander of the Mughal Deccan expedition in 1665? → Jai Singh
☛ How many forts did Shivaji cede in the Treaty of Purandar? → 23 forts

q: Who was the last physical master (Guru in human form) of Sikh religion?
qs.e: The last human form master of Sikhism was Guru Gobind Singh (1666-1708), the tenth Guru. He founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699, transforming the Sikhs into a martial community. He declared the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru of the Sikhs, ending the line of human Gurus. Guru Gobind Singh fought against injustice and gave Sikhism a distinct identity. His father, Guru Tegh Bahadur, was the ninth Guru.
qs.kf:
☛ Tenth Guru of Sikhs → Guru Gobind Singh
☛ Year of Khalsa Panth foundation → 1699
☛ Eternal Guru of Sikhs → Guru Granth Sahib
☛ Ninth Guru → Guru Tegh Bahadur
☛ Death of Guru Gobind Singh → 1708

q: Who was the founder of Sikhism?
qs.e: Sikhism was founded by Guru Nanak (1469-1539). He was born in Talwandi (now in Pakistan). He preached the message of one God, equality, and selfless service. His three core principles are: Naam Japo (meditate on God's name), Kirat Karo (work honestly), and Vand Chakko (share with others). Guru Nanak established Sikhism as a distinct faith, and after him, the tradition of ten Gurus continued.
qs.kf:
☛ Birthplace of Guru Nanak → Talwandi (Pakistan)
☛ First of the ten Sikh Gurus → Guru Nanak
☛ Three principles of Guru Nanak → Naam Japo, Kirat Karo, Vand Chakko
☛ Compiler of Guru Granth Sahib → Guru Arjan Dev
☛ Holy scripture of Sikhism → Guru Granth Sahib

q: The famous Golden Temple in Amritsar was completed by which of the following Sikh Guru?
qs.e: The Golden Temple, also known as Shri Harmandir Sahib, is the holiest shrine of Sikhism located in Amritsar. Its construction was initiated in 1581 and completed in 1589 by the fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjun Dev. He also compiled the Adi Granth, the early version of Guru Granth Sahib. The foundation was laid by Guru Ramdas, but the structure was finished by Guru Arjun Dev. The temple is surrounded by the Amrit Sarovar (Pool of Nectar), from which Amritsar gets its name.
qs.kf:
☛ Who completed the construction of the Golden Temple? → Guru Arjun Dev
☛ Who was the fifth Sikh Guru? → Guru Arjun Dev
☛ Who compiled the Adi Granth? → Guru Arjun Dev
☛ What is the name of the pool surrounding the Golden Temple? → Amrit Sarovar
☛ Where is Shri Harmandir Sahib located? → Amritsar

q: Who was the 10th Sikh Guru among the following?
qs.e: Guru Gobind Singh (1666-1708) was the tenth and last human Guru of Sikhism. He founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699, a warrior community of Sikhs. He was a poet, philosopher, and warrior. He declared the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru of Sikhs. Guru Arjun Dev was the fifth Guru, Guru Nanak the first, and Guru Teg Bahadur the ninth Guru.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Khalsa Panth? → Guru Gobind Singh
☛ When was Guru Gobind Singh born? → 1666
☛ Who was the last human Guru of Sikhs? → Guru Gobind Singh
☛ Who declared Guru Granth Sahib as Guru? → Guru Gobind Singh
☛ Which Guru was Guru Teg Bahadur? → Ninth

q: 'Guru Granth Sahib' is the holy book of ______.
qs.e: Guru Granth Sahib is the holy book of Sikhism. It is also known as Adi Granth. It was compiled by Guru Arjan Dev in 1604 CE. Later, Guru Gobind Singh established it as Guru Granth Sahib in 1708 CE. It is written in Gurmukhi script. It contains the teachings of Sikh Gurus, Hindu bhaktas, and Muslim saints. Guru Granth Sahib is considered the living Guru of Sikhs.
qs.kf:
☛ Who compiled Guru Granth Sahib? → Guru Arjan Dev
☛ Who gave Guru status to Guru Granth Sahib? → Guru Gobind Singh
☛ What is the script of Guru Granth Sahib? → Gurmukhi
☛ How many Gurus' words are in Guru Granth Sahib? → 6 Gurus
☛ When was Guru Granth Sahib established? → 1708 CE

q: Which of the following Peshwas was known as Nana Saheb?
qs.e: Balaji Baji Rao (1721-1761) was the seventh Peshwa of the Maratha Empire, popularly known as Nana Saheb. He was the son of Bajirao I and served as Peshwa from 1740 to 1761. During his reign, the Maratha Empire reached its zenith, but he was defeated by Ahmad Shah Abdali in the Third Battle of Panipat (1761), which marked the decline of Maratha power. He implemented administrative reforms and strengthened the Maratha revenue system. He governed from his capital at Pune. The title Nana Saheb was a term of endearment reflecting his popularity among the people.
qs.kf:
☛ Balaji Baji Rao's nickname → Nana Saheb
☛ Year of Third Battle of Panipat → 1761
☛ Father of Balaji Baji Rao → Bajirao I
☛ Tenure as Peshwa → 1740-1761
☛ Capital of Maratha Empire → Pune

q: Who was the fourth Sikh Guru who laid the foundation of Sri Darbar Sahib at Amritsar (The Golden Temple) in 1577?
qs.e: In 1577, the fourth Sikh Guru, Guru Ram Das Ji, laid the foundation of Sri Darbar Sahib (The Golden Temple) at Amritsar. He succeeded Guru Amar Das Ji and founded the city of Amritsar as the central place for Sikhism. He also excavated the sacred tank (Amrit Sarovar) around which the temple was later built. The construction of the temple was later completed by Guru Arjan Dev Ji. The Golden Temple is the holiest shrine of Sikhism.
qs.kf:
☛ Who laid the foundation of the Golden Temple? → Guru Ram Das Ji
☛ Who founded Amritsar city? → Guru Ram Das Ji
☛ Who was the fourth Sikh Guru? → Guru Ram Das Ji
☛ Tenure of Guru Ram Das Ji? → 1574–1581
☛ Who excavated the Amrit Sarovar? → Guru Ram Das Ji

q: In 1706, the compilations of the holy scripture of the Sikhs, Guru Granth Sahib, was authenticated by whom of the following?
qs.e: The compilation of the holy scripture of Sikhs, Guru Granth Sahib, was authenticated by Guru Gobind Singh in 1706. The original compilation was done by Guru Arjan Dev in 1604, known as Adi Granth. Later, Guru Gobind Singh added the hymns of Guru Tegh Bahadur and finalized the scripture at Damdama Sahib in 1706. He named it Guru Granth Sahib and declared it as the eternal Guru of the Sikhs. This scripture is the central religious text of Sikhism and contains teachings of Sikh Gurus and saints.
qs.kf:
☛ Who first compiled the Guru Granth Sahib? → Guru Arjan Dev (1604)
☛ Who finalized the Guru Granth Sahib? → Guru Gobind Singh (1706)
☛ Who declared Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru? → Guru Gobind Singh
☛ Whose hymns were added by Guru Gobind Singh? → Guru Tegh Bahadur
☛ Where was the final compilation of Guru Granth Sahib done? → Damdama Sahib

q: Which of the following festivals of the Sikh community is celebrated on the full moon day of Kartik month as per the Hindu calendar?
qs.e: Guru Nanak Jayanti is a major Sikh festival celebrated on the full moon day of Kartik month as per the Hindu calendar. It marks the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism. He was born in 1469 CE in Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib in Pakistan). On this day, special prayers, kirtan (devotional hymns), and Akhand Path (continuous reading of Guru Granth Sahib) are held in gurdwaras. Processions called Nagar Kirtan are taken out and langar (community meal) is organized. Among the other options, Lohri is celebrated in January, Hola Mohalla in the month of Phalguna, and Baisakhi in the month of Vaisakha.
qs.kf:
☛ When is Guru Nanak Jayanti celebrated? → On Kartik Purnima
☛ Who is the founder of Sikhism? → Guru Nanak Dev Ji
☛ Birthplace of Guru Nanak? → Talwandi (Nankana Sahib)
☛ Birth year of Guru Nanak? → 1469 CE
☛ Other name for Kartik month? → Month of Diwali

q: On which of the following Sikh Guru's birth anniversary is the Prakash Parv celebrated?
qs.e: Prakash Parv is celebrated on the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the first Sikh Guru. This festival falls on the full moon day of Kartik (Kartik Purnima) and is also known as Guru Nanak Jayanti. Guru Nanak Dev was born in 1469 CE in Nankana Sahib, now in Pakistan. He founded Sikhism and preached the concept of 'Ek Onkar' (One God). His teachings are compiled in the Guru Granth Sahib. On this day, Sikhs perform special prayers, kirtan, and community meals (langar) at gurudwaras.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the founder of Sikhism? → Guru Nanak Dev
☛ Where was Guru Nanak Dev born? → Nankana Sahib (Pakistan)
☛ On which date is Guru Nanak's birth celebrated? → Kartik Purnima
☛ What was Guru Nanak's main message? → Worship of One God (Ek Onkar)
☛ Which is the holy scripture of Sikhism? → Guru Granth Sahib

q: Rohilla chief, Najib-ud-Daula, played a key role in the ____.
qs.e: Rohilla chief Najib-ud-Daula played a key role in the Third Battle of Panipat (1761). He was an ally of Ahmad Shah Abdali and a part of the coalition against the Marathas. Najib-ud-Daula invited Abdali to India and led the Rohilla contingent in the battle. The Maratha defeat weakened Mughal influence in North India and strengthened Afghan dominance. Najib-ud-Daula later became influential in the Mughal court.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat? → Sadashivrao Bhau
☛ When was the Third Battle of Panipat fought? → January 14, 1761
☛ What was Najib-ud-Daula's ethnicity? → Rohilla Pathan
☛ Ahmad Shah Abdali was the ruler of which empire? → Durrani Empire
☛ What was the outcome of the Third Battle of Panipat? → Maratha defeat

q: This freedom fighter proclaimed himself the Peshwa during the Revolt of 1857 and gathered armed forces and expelled the British garrison from the city. He was the adopted son of the late Peshwa Baji Rao. The leader in question is:
qs.e: Nana Saheb, originally named Dhondu Pant, was the adopted son of the late Peshwa Baji Rao II. During the Revolt of 1857, he proclaimed himself the Peshwa and expelled the British garrison from Kanpur. He gathered armed forces and fought against the British. Nana Saheb was one of the prominent leaders of the revolt. After the uprising, he mysteriously disappeared.
qs.kf:
☛ Real name of Nana Saheb → Dhondu Pant
☛ Nana Saheb was the adopted son of → Baji Rao II
☛ Where did Nana Saheb expel the British garrison in 1857 → Kanpur
☛ What title did Nana Saheb proclaim himself → Peshwa
☛ Nana Saheb is associated with which revolt → Revolt of 1857

q: Who were the signatories of the Tripartite Treaty signed in 1838 against Dost Muhammad Khan?
o: Lord Auckland, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shuja ud-Daula
Lord Ellenborough, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shuja ud-Daula
Lord Auckland, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shah Shuja
Charles Metcalfe, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shah Shuja
qs.e: The Tripartite Treaty of 1838 was signed between the British, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, and Shah Shuja to remove Dost Muhammad Khan from power in Afghanistan and restore Shah Shuja to the throne. The British Governor-General Lord Auckland signed on behalf of the British East India Company. This treaty led to the First Anglo-Afghan War (1839-1842). Under the treaty, the British agreed to support Shah Shuja, while Ranjit Singh provided passage and assistance through Punjab. The treaty was part of the British Forward Policy, aimed at countering Russian influence in Central Asia and securing the northwestern frontier of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Signatories of Tripartite Treaty (1838) → Lord Auckland, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Shah Shuja
☛ Objective of the treaty → Remove Dost Muhammad Khan and reinstate Shah Shuja in Afghanistan
☛ War caused by this treaty → First Anglo-Afghan War (1839-1842)
☛ Policy associated with Lord Auckland → Forward Policy
☛ Main British motive → Counter Russian influence in Central Asia

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Raigad Fort? (1) It is part of the 12 forts nominated for UNESCO World Heritage under the title “Maratha Military Landscapes of India” for 2024-25. (2) It was the capital of the most illustrious Maratha sovereign, nurtured by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. (3) Raigad, surrounded by valleys shaped by the Kal and Gandhari rivers, stands as an isolated massif without connections to neighbouring hills.
qs.e: Raigad Fort served as the capital of the Maratha Empire under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. It is among the 12 forts nominated for UNESCO World Heritage status for 2024-25 under the title 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India'. The fort is an isolated massif, surrounded by valleys formed by the Kal and Gandhari rivers, with no connections to neighbouring hills. Hence, all three statements are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Part of 12 nominated forts → Raigad Fort
☛ Capital of which empire → Maratha Empire under Shivaji Maharaj
☛ Geographical feature → Isolated massif surrounded by Kal and Gandhari river valleys
☛ UNESCO nomination 2024-25 → Under 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India'
☛ Key characteristic → No connections to neighbouring hills, separate hill fort

q: Which Sikh guru established the Khalsa Panth?
qs.e: The Khalsa Panth was established by the tenth Sikh Guru, Shri Guru Gobind Singh ji, in 1699 AD at Anandpur Sahib on the day of Baisakhi. He initiated five beloved ones (Panj Pyare) with Amrit, laying the foundation of the Khalsa Panth, which eliminated discrimination based on caste, religion, or social background. Guru Gobind Singh organized the Sikhs into a military and spiritual community that stood against injustice and oppression. The Khalsa Panth gave Sikhism a new identity, with the mandatory wearing of the Five Ks (Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kirpan, Kachera). Guru Gobind Singh's contribution is immensely significant in Sikh history.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Khalsa Panth established? → 1699 AD
☛ Where was the Khalsa Panth established? → Anandpur Sahib
☛ Who were the Panj Pyare? → Five Sikhs who first took Amrit
☛ Who is the tenth Sikh Guru? → Guru Gobind Singh ji
☛ What is the meaning of Khalsa? → Pure or devoted community

q: Banda Singh Bahadur, military commander of Khalsa army was executed in:
qs.e: Banda Singh Bahadur was executed in 1716. He was the military commander of the Khalsa army and known for leading a rebellion against the Mughal Empire. After the death of Guru Gobind Singh, he formed a powerful Khalsa army in Punjab. He defeated the Mughals at the Battle of Sirhind in 1710 and established Sikh rule. However, after the siege of Gurdaspur in 1715, he was captured. Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar had him tortured and executed in Delhi in 1716. His martyrdom is significant in Sikh history.
qs.kf:
☛ Banda Singh Bahadur's birth → 1670, Rajouri, Jammu
☛ Meeting with Guru Gobind Singh → 1708, Nanded
☛ Battle of Sirhind → 1710
☛ Date of execution → 9 June 1716, Delhi
☛ Mughal Emperor → Farrukhsiyar

q: Shri Guru Gobind Singh Ji founded the ‘Khalsa Panth’ in the year _______.
qs.e: Shri Guru Gobind Singh Ji founded the Khalsa Panth in the year 1699 on the day of Baisakhi at Anandpur Sahib. He initiated the Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) by giving them Amrit, establishing the Khalsa order. This event gave Sikhs a distinct identity and instilled a spirit of struggle against injustice. The purpose of founding the Khalsa Panth was to protect religious freedom and human rights. Guru Ji required Sikhs to wear the Five Ks: Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kirpan, and Kachera. This marked a significant turning point in Sikh history.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Khalsa Panth founded? → 1699
☛ Who founded Khalsa Panth? → Guru Gobind Singh Ji
☛ Name one of the Panj Pyare → Bhai Daya Singh
☛ Which is NOT among the Five Ks? → Sword
☛ Baisakhi is related to which religious event? → Foundation of Khalsa Panth

q: Which of the following is NOT in the list of five Sikh Takhts?
o: Sri Damdama Sahib, Talwandi Sabo, Bathinda
Shri Rakab Ganj Sahib, New Delhi
qs.e: The five Sikh Takhts (seats of authority) are major religious and historical centers for Sikhism. They include: Sri Akal Takht Sahib (Amritsar), Sri Keshgarh Sahib (Anandpur Sahib), Sri Damdama Sahib (Talwandi Sabo, Bathinda), Sri Patna Sahib (Patna), and Sri Hazur Sahib (Nanded). Shri Rakab Ganj Sahib in New Delhi is a famous Gurudwara but is not among the five Takhts. The Takhts are associated with the Sikh Gurus and the Khalsa Panth, serving as sacred places for spiritual and temporal decisions. This list is crucial for understanding Sikh history and governance.
qs.kf:
☛ Most important Sikh Takht → Sri Akal Takht Sahib (Amritsar)
☛ Place of Khalsa Panth foundation → Sri Keshgarh Sahib (Anandpur)
☛ Birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh → Sri Patna Sahib
☛ Final resting place of Guru Gobind Singh → Sri Hazur Sahib (Nanded)
☛ Place of Guru Granth Sahib editing → Sri Damdama Sahib (Talwandi Sabo)

q: Who among the following was the tenth Sikh Guru?
qs.e: The tenth Sikh Guru was Guru Gobind Singh. He was born in 1666 in Patna. He was the son of Guru Tegh Bahadur and became Guru at the age of 9 in 1675. In 1699, he founded the Khalsa Panth, a key institution in Sikhism. He instructed Sikhs to wear the Five Ks: Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kirpan, and Kachera. He was a great warrior and spiritual leader who fought against the Mughals. He declared the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal and final Guru. He died in 1708 in Nanded, Maharashtra.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of Sikhism? → Guru Nanak
☛ Who was the fifth Sikh Guru? → Guru Arjan Dev
☛ Who was the fourth Sikh Guru? → Guru Ram Das
☛ When was Khalsa Panth established? → 1699
☛ Who declared Guru Granth Sahib as the Guru? → Guru Gobind Singh

q: Who laid the foundation stone of the world-famous Swarna Mandir (Golden Temple)?
qs.e: The foundation stone of the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) was laid in 1588 (or 1589) AD by Hazrat Mian Mir ji, a Sufi saint and a friend of the fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan Dev ji. Guru Arjan Dev ji invited him to emphasize the temple as a symbol of peace and brotherhood. Located in Amritsar, it is the holiest shrine in Sikhism. Construction was completed in 1604 AD, and the Guru Granth Sahib was installed inside. The current golden exterior was done by Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the 19th century.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Golden Temple located? → Amritsar, Punjab
☛ Who built Harmandir Sahib? → Guru Arjan Dev ji
☛ Who gilded the Golden Temple? → Maharaja Ranjit Singh
☛ Which scripture is installed in the Golden Temple? → Guru Granth Sahib
☛ Hazrat Mian Mir ji was a saint of which order? → Sufi

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which princely ruler patronised the Sikh community and institutions?
qs.e: Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala (1891-1938) was a great patron of the Sikh community and institutions. He was a strong supporter of Sikhism and helped establish several gurdwaras and Sikh educational institutions in Patiala. During his reign, he emphasized the preservation of Sikh culture and religious scriptures. He was also one of the key patrons of the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee. He initiated various programs to promote Sikh history and traditions. Thus, he was a ruler who patronized the Sikh community not only politically but also culturally and religiously.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the last ruler of Patiala State? → Yadavindra Singh
☛ Which building was built by Bhupinder Singh? → Moti Bagh Palace
☛ Who founded the Patiala dynasty? → Baba Ala Singh
☛ Which sport was Bhupinder Singh interested in? → Cricket
☛ By what name is Patiala known? → British city of Punjab

q: Who established the Chishti sect in India?
qs.e: The Chishti sect in India was established by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in the 12th century. He settled in Ajmer (Rajasthan), where his shrine (dargah) is located. The Chishti order is a prominent Sufi tradition emphasizing love, service, and music. Moinuddin Chishti is also known as Garib Nawaz (favorer of the poor). His notable successors include Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki, Baba Farid, and Nizamuddin Auliya, who expanded the order across India.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Chishti sect → Moinuddin Chishti
☛ Dargah of Moinuddin Chishti → Ajmer, Rajasthan
☛ Core principle of Chishti order → Love and service
☛ Who is called 'Garib Nawaz' → Moinuddin Chishti
☛ Major saints of Chishti order → Nizamuddin Auliya, Baba Farid, Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki

q: The word 'Silsila' is related to which of the following?
qs.e: The word ‘Silsila’ is related to Sufi Sampraday. It is an Arabic word meaning ‘chain’ or ‘lineage’. In the Sufi tradition, ‘Silsila’ refers to the spiritual lineage through which Sufi teachings and spiritual knowledge are transmitted from a master to a disciple. Each Silsila follows the tradition of a specific Sufi saint, such as the Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, and Naqshbandi orders. This concept represents the spiritual continuity and the master-disciple tradition in Sufism. Among the other options, the Sikh tradition has a ‘Guru lineage’, an Imperial Decree is a royal order, and the Devotional Sect (Bhakti) does not have a similar chain.
qs.kf:
☛ Through which does spiritual knowledge pass in a Sufi Silsila? → Guru-disciple tradition
☛ What are the major Sufi Silsilas? → Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi
☛ From which language is the word Silsila derived? → Arabic
☛ What is the chain of Sufi orders called? → Silsila
☛ Which Sufi Silsila was established first in India? → Chishti Silsila

q: Which one of the following devotional saints have projected the philosophy of Shuddha advaita?
qs.e: Shuddha Advaita (pure non-dualism) is a prominent school of Vedanta, propagated by Vallabhacharya (1479-1531). According to this philosophy, Brahman (the Supreme Being) is the only reality, and the world is a real manifestation of Brahman, not an illusion. Vallabhacharya founded the Pushti Marg, emphasizing devotion to Lord Krishna. In contrast, Shankaracharya propounded Advaita, Madhavacharya Dvaita, and Ramananda Vishishtadvaita. Hence, Vallabhacharya is the correct exponent of Shuddha Advaita.
qs.kf:
☛ Who propounded the Shuddha Advaita philosophy? → Vallabhacharya
☛ What is the name of the devotional path founded by Vallabhacharya? → Pushti Marg
☛ What is Shankaracharya's philosophy? → Advaita (Kevaladvaita)
☛ What is Madhavacharya's philosophy? → Dvaita
☛ What is Ramananda's philosophy? → Vishishtadvaita

q: Ajmer is associated with the Sufi saint:
qs.e: Ajmer is famous for the dargah of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti, the founder of the Chishti order in India. He was one of the first major Sufi saints to arrive in India and established his center in Ajmer. He died in 1236 CE, and his shrine attracts millions of devotees annually. Other options: Khwaja Nizamuddin Auliya is associated with Delhi, Bandanawaz Gisudaraz with Gulbarga, and Baba Farid with Pakpattan.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Chishti order in India → Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti
☛ Dargah of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti is located in → Ajmer, Rajasthan
☛ Tomb of Khwaja Nizamuddin Auliya is located in → Delhi
☛ Baba Farid belonged to which Sufi order → Chishti
☛ Bandanawaz Gisudaraz is associated with which city → Gulbarga

q: Where is the dargah of sufi mystic Sheikh Fariduddin Ganjshaker located?
qs.e: Sheikh Fariduddin Ganjshaker, also known as Baba Farid, was a prominent Sufi saint of the Chishti order. He was born in 1173 CE and taught in Pakpattan, a city in Punjab province of present-day Pakistan. His disciples included Khwaja Nizamuddin Auliya, a major figure in the Chishti order. The dargah of Baba Farid is located in Pakpattan, which remains an important pilgrimage site for Sufi followers. Thousands of devotees visit every year to pay homage. The shrine complex also includes a mosque and a langar (community kitchen).
qs.kf:
☛ Which Sufi order was Sheikh Fariduddin Ganjshaker associated with? → Chishti order
☛ When was Baba Farid born? → 1173 CE
☛ Who was the chief disciple of Sheikh Fariduddin? → Khwaja Nizamuddin Auliya
☛ In which present-day country is Pakpattan located? → Pakistan (Punjab province)
☛ Where is the dargah of Sheikh Fariduddin Ganjshaker? → Pakpattan

q: Under which branch of devotion is the formless form of God envisaged?
qs.e: The Bhakti movement is mainly divided into two branches - Saguna and Nirguna. Saguna devotion worships the formless with attributes, while Nirguna devotion envisions God as formless (without any shape) and without qualities. The prominent saints of the Nirguna stream include Kabir, Guru Nanak, Raidas, and Dadu Dayal. They opposed idol worship and believed in a formless God. Nirguna bhakti emphasized internal devotion and love over external rituals.
qs.kf:
☛ Major Nirguna saints → Kabir, Guru Nanak, Raidas, Dadu Dayal
☛ Major Saguna saints → Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai
☛ Nature of God in Nirguna bhakti → formless and attributeless
☛ Nature of God in Saguna bhakti → with form and attributes
☛ Kabir's language → Sadhukkari mixed language

name: Set 1 · Q1–44
sub: Medieval History - Medieval Art, Architecture & Literature

q: Who among these was a famous traveler from Venice?
qs.e: Marco Polo (1254-1324) was a famous Venetian traveler who spent 24 years traveling across Asia. He reached the court of Kublai Khan and documented regions including China, India, and Persia. His book 'The Travels of Marco Polo' became a crucial source for Europeans about Asian culture and trade. François Bernier was a French physician and traveler who visited India during the Mughal period. Duarte Barbosa was a Portuguese explorer. Nikitin was a Russian merchant. Hence, Marco Polo is the traveler from Venice.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous Venetian traveler → Marco Polo
☛ Book written by Marco Polo → 'The Travels of Marco Polo'
☛ Marco Polo visited the court of → Kublai Khan
☛ French traveler who visited Mughal India → François Bernier
☛ Portuguese explorer who described India → Duarte Barbosa

q: The famous Borobudur Temple is dedicated to _______.
qs.e: Borobudur Temple is a famous Mahayana Buddhist monument located in Central Java, Indonesia. It was built during the 9th century under the Shailendra dynasty. This temple is dedicated to Buddha and is considered the largest Buddhist temple in the world. Borobudur was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991. Its structure is divided into three levels: Kamadhatu, Rupadhatu, and Arupadhatu, representing the Buddhist cosmology. The temple walls feature 2,672 relief panels depicting the life and teachings of Buddha.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country is Borobudur Temple located in? → Indonesia
☛ Which dynasty built Borobudur Temple? → Shailendra dynasty
☛ When was Borobudur declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1991
☛ Which religion is Borobudur Temple associated with? → Mahayana Buddhism
☛ How many relief panels are there in Borobudur? → 2,672

q: What was the Royal emblem of the Rashtrakutas?
qs.e: The royal emblem of the Rashtrakuta dynasty (c. 753-982 CE) was the Golden Eagle (Garuda). This symbol represented their military strength and divine authority. The Rashtrakutas built the Kailashnath Temple at Ellora and were patrons of art and literature. Their capital was Manyakheta (modern Malkhed, Karnataka). Garuda is considered the mount of Vishnu in Vaishnavism, indicating the Rashtrakutas' connection to Vaishnava traditions. Their coins and inscriptions also feature the Garuda emblem.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Rashtrakutas → Manyakheta
☛ Founder of Rashtrakuta dynasty → Dantidurga
☛ Most famous Rashtrakuta ruler → Amoghavarsha I
☛ Title used by Rashtrakuta kings → Prithvivallabha
☛ Temple built by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I → Kailashnath Temple at Ellora

q: Which of the following Monuments is not built by Shah Jahan?
qs.e: Panch Mahal was not built by Shah Jahan; it was constructed by Akbar in Fatehpur Sikri. Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal (in memory of Mumtaz Mahal), the Red Fort (in Delhi), and the Peacock Throne (a jewel-studded throne later looted by Nadir Shah). Shah Jahan's reign is considered the golden age of Mughal architecture. Thus, all the given monuments except Panch Mahal are associated with Shah Jahan.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Panch Mahal? → Akbar
☛ Who built Taj Mahal? → Shah Jahan
☛ Who built Red Fort? → Shah Jahan
☛ Who built Peacock Throne? → Shah Jahan
☛ Who founded Fatehpur Sikri? → Akbar

q: "Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuran one of the "UNESCO World Heritage Site" founded by the Pallava kings is in _______ district of _______.
A. Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu
B. Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu
C. Sivagangai, Tamil Nadu
D. Siligiris, Tamil Nadu
qs.e: The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram is located in the Kancheepuram district of Tamil Nadu. This UNESCO World Heritage Site was built by the Pallava kings during the 7th and 8th centuries. It includes Rathas (chariot temples), Mandapas (cave temples), and giant rock-cut reliefs like Arjuna's Penance. This site is a masterpiece of Pallava architecture and showcases ancient Indian craftsmanship.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the ancient name of Mahabalipuram? → Mamallapuram
☛ Which dynasty built the monuments at Mahabalipuram? → Pallava
☛ Which Pallava king built Mahabalipuram? → Narasimhavarman I
☛ Which river flows near Mahabalipuram? → Palar River
☛ What type of rock are the temples at Mahabalipuram made of? → Granite

q: ______________ is one of India’s largest palaces, which is also known as ‘Amba Villa’ and it was the residence of the Wodeyar monarch. A. Mysore Palace B. Leh Palace C. Mattancherry Palace
D. Hampi
qs.e: Mysore Palace, also known as 'Amba Villa', is one of the largest and most famous palaces in India. Located in Mysore, Karnataka, it was the official residence of the Wodeyar dynasty. The current palace was completed in 1912 after the original wooden structure was destroyed by fire in 1897. Designed by British architect Henry Irwin, it showcases Indo-Saracenic architecture, blending Hindu, Muslim, Rajput, and Gothic styles. The palace is renowned for its grandeur, intricate carvings, and the spectacular Dussehra celebrations. It remains a major tourist attraction and a symbol of India's rich cultural heritage.
qs.kf:
☛ Alternate name of Mysore Palace → Amba Villa
☛ Ruling dynasty of Mysore Palace → Wodeyar dynasty
☛ Year of completion of Mysore Palace → 1912
☛ Architect of Mysore Palace → Henry Irwin
☛ Architectural style of Mysore Palace → Indo-Saracenic

q: Which mosque, believed to be the first one to be built in Delhi, is situated near Qutub Minar?
qs.e: Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is considered the first mosque built in Delhi. It was constructed in 1193 CE by Qutb-ud-din Aibak. The mosque is located near Qutub Minar and is an important monument of the Delhi Sultanate. Its construction used debris from 27 Hindu and Jain temples. The name 'Quwwat-ul-Islam' means 'Might of Islam'. This mosque is an early example of Islamic architecture in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Builder of Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque → Qutb-ud-din Aibak
☛ Year of construction → 1193 CE
☛ Construction material → Debris from 27 Hindu and Jain temples
☛ Meaning of name → Might of Islam
☛ Location → Near Qutub Minar, Delhi

q: Which traveller from Uzbekistan visited India in the 11th Century?
qs.e: Alberuni (973-1048 AD) was a polymath scholar from the Khwarezm region of Uzbekistan. He had deep knowledge of mathematics, astronomy, history, and geography. He was brought to India by Mahmud of Ghazni, where he extensively studied Indian philosophy, religion, science, and culture. His famous work "Tarik-ul-Hind" (also known as Kitab-ul-Hind) provides an invaluable account of the social, religious, and scientific conditions of India in the 11th century. This travelogue is a key source for understanding India's history during that period.
qs.kf:
☛ Alberuni's original country → Uzbekistan (Khwarezm)
☛ Alberuni's major work → Kitab-ul-Hind (Tarik-ul-Hind)
☛ Who brought Alberuni to India → Mahmud of Ghazni
☛ Century of Alberuni's visit to India → 11th century
☛ Fields of expertise of Alberuni → Mathematics, Astronomy, History

q: Which of the following foreign travelers called the Telugu language "Italian of the East"?
qs.e: The Italian traveler Nicolò Conti visited India in the 15th century. He called the Telugu language the 'Italian of the East' because Telugu words end with vowels, similar to the Italian language. This reflects the sweetness and musicality of Telugu. Nicolò Conti was a Venetian merchant and explorer who traveled to many parts of Asia. His travel accounts provide important information about Indian languages and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who called Telugu 'Italian of the East'? → Nicolò Conti
☛ Nicolò Conti was a traveler from which country? → Italy
☛ Telugu language belongs to which language family? → Dravidian
☛ In which century did Nicolò Conti visit India? → 15th
☛ What is the literal meaning of Telugu? → Sweet language

q: Which of the following dynasty was credited with the construction of Pancha Rathas in Mahabalipuram?
qs.e: The Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram were constructed during the reign of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I (also known as Mahamalla) in the 7th century AD. These five monolithic temples are carved out of a single granite rock and are named after the five Pandava brothers from the Mahabharata—Dharmaraja, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva. This unique style of Pallava art represents an early example of Dravidian architecture, which later influenced the Chola and Vijayanagara styles. The Pallava dynasty was founded by Simhavishnu and remained powerful in South India from around the 6th to the 9th century. The Pancha Rathas are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a testament to the mastery of Pallava rock-cut architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram? → Narasimhavarman I (Pallava)
☛ What was the capital of the Pallava dynasty? → Kanchipuram
☛ Which Pallava king was known as Mahamalla? → Narasimhavarman I
☛ Which dynasty succeeded the Pallavas in South India? → Cholas
☛ What material are the Pancha Rathas made of? → Granite rock (monolithic)

q: Where was the first Tamil Sangam organized?
qs.e: The first Tamil Sangam was organized in Madurai. This marked the beginning of the Sangam period, which witnessed the flourishing of Tamil literature, poetry, and grammar. The Sangam age lasted from around 300 BCE to 300 CE and included three major assemblies (Sangams). The first Sangam was held in Madurai, the second in Kapadapuram, and the third again in Madurai. These assemblies were attended by poets, scholars, and kings, contributing to the enrichment of the Tamil language. The first Sangam was chaired by the sage Agastya. It included 549 poets. The Sangam literature is a rich source of ancient Tamil history and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ First Tamil Sangam location → Madurai
☛ Second Tamil Sangam location → Kapadapuram
☛ Third Tamil Sangam location → Madurai
☛ Chairperson of first Sangam → Agastya
☛ Sangam period time frame → 300 BCE to 300 CE

q: In the Udaagiri caves, the Hathigumpha inscription gives information about the military expeditions of which ruler?
qs.e: The Hathigumpha inscription is located in the Udaagiri caves in Odisha. It was inscribed by King Kharaweel, a prominent ruler of the Kalinga dynasty. This inscription is written in Prakrit language and Brahmi script. It provides detailed information about Kharaweel's military expeditions, cultural achievements, and administrative works. Kharaweel waged wars against Magadha, Pandya, Greek rulers, etc. The inscription was engraved in the fifth year of his reign. It is a crucial source for understanding the Kalinga empire and its expansion in Indian history.
qs.kf:
☛ In which script is the Hathigumpha inscription written? → Brahmi
☛ In which language is the Hathigumpha inscription written? → Prakrit
☛ Which dynasty does the Hathigumpha inscription belong to? → Kalinga dynasty
☛ King Kharaweel was a ruler of which region? → Kalinga (present-day Odisha)
☛ To which century does the Hathigumpha inscription belong? → 2nd century BCE

q: Who built the famous beach at Mahabalipuram?
qs.e: The famous Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) was built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (also known as Rajasimhavarman). This temple is an outstanding example of South Indian architecture and was constructed in the 8th century CE. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Mahabalipuram. Narasimhavarman II was a great ruler of the Pallava dynasty, renowned for his patronage of art and architecture. He was also known by the title Rajasimha. The temple is unique as it is located on the seashore and was carved out of rocks, showcasing the skill of Pallava artisans.
qs.kf:
☛ Builder of the Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram → Narasimhavarman II
☛ Last great ruler of the Pallava dynasty → Narasimhavarman II
☛ Architectural style of the Shore Temple → Dravidian architecture
☛ Title of Narasimhavarman II → Rajasimha
☛ Ancient name of Mahabalipuram → Mamallapuram

q: Which of the following dynasties introduced the Vesarean style temple architecture?
qs.e: The Chalukya dynasty introduced the Vesarean style of temple architecture. This style developed in the Karnataka region of South India. It features a tall, pyramidal shikhara over the sanctum. The Chalukya rulers promoted this style, with examples found at Pattadakal and Badami. The Chola style is different, with a more towering vimana. The Kakatiya style has star-shaped ceilings. The Gupta style is North Indian. Vesarean style is a blend of Nagara and Dravida styles, developed by the Chalukyas. It is also known as the Chalukyan style.
qs.kf:
☛ Major temples of Vesarean style → Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal and Cave Temples at Badami
☛ Capital of Chalukya dynasty → Badami (Vatapi)
☛ Famous Chalukya ruler → Pulakeshin II
☛ River on which Pattadakal is located → Malaprabha River
☛ Material used in Chalukya architecture → Sandstone

q: Which of the following is the epic of Tamil literature?
qs.e: Silappadikaram is one of the five great epics of Tamil literature, composed by Ilango Adigal. It is a moral story centered around the merchant Kovalan, his wife Kannagi, and the dancer Madhavi. The epic depicts Tamil culture, trade, and the sense of justice. Among the options, Naladiyar is a didactic work, Tolakappiyam is a grammar text, and Attoogai is not a major work.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote Silappadikaram? → Ilango Adigal
☛ What are the five great epics of Tamil? → Silappadikaram, Manimekalai, Jivaka Chintamani, Kundalakesi, Valayapathi
☛ Who is the heroine of Silappadikaram? → Kannagi
☛ Who are the main characters of Silappadikaram? → Kovalan, Kannagi, Madhavi
☛ In which style is Silappadikaram written? → Sangam literature style

q: Where was the Second Tamil Sangam organized?
qs.e: The second Tamil Sangam was organized at Kapatapuram. The Tamil Sangams were ancient literary assemblies crucial for the development of Tamil language. There were three Sangams: the first at South Madurai, the second at Kapatapuram, and the third at Madurai. The Sangam literature period is approximately from 300 BCE to 300 CE. These assemblies gathered poets and scholars to compile literary works. The second Sangam was held at Kapatapuram, now considered part of the Pudukkottai district.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the first Tamil Sangam held? → South Madurai
☛ Where was the third Tamil Sangam held? → Madurai
☛ What is the period of Sangam literature? → 300 BCE to 300 CE
☛ Who were the patrons of the Sangams? → Pandya kings
☛ Where is Kapatapuram located today? → Pudukkottai, Tamil Nadu

q: Natraj's famous bronze statue is related to which of the following empires?
qs.e: The famous bronze statue of Nataraja belongs to the Chola Empire. This statue depicts Lord Shiva in his dancing form and is a masterpiece of Chola art (9th-13th century). The Chola rulers patronized art and culture, especially bronze sculpture. In the Nataraja statue, Shiva is shown standing on one leg, with the other leg crushing the demon Apasmara. This statue is found in temples like Thanjavur and Chidambaram. It represents the union of art and religion and is a heritage of Indian culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Chola Empire → Thanjavur
☛ Major art of Chola period → Bronze sculpture
☛ Meaning of Nataraja → King of Dance (Shiva)
☛ Founder of Chola dynasty → Vijayalaya Chola
☛ Famous Chola temple → Brihadeeswarar Temple (Thanjavur)

q: Who was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
qs.e: The Rashtrakuta dynasty was founded by Dantidurg in the 8th century. He was a ruler of Manyakheta (modern-day Karnataka) and established his empire by defeating the Chalukyas of Badami. Dantidurg assumed the title 'Khadgavaloka' and during his reign, the Rashtrakuta empire expanded. His successor Krishna I further strengthened the empire. The Rashtrakuta period is considered a golden age in South Indian history, with significant developments in art, architecture, and literature. The Kailash Temple at Ellora was built by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty? → Dantidurg
☛ What was the capital of the Rashtrakutas? → Manyakheta
☛ Who built the Kailash Temple at Ellora? → Krishna I
☛ Who was the last ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty? → Karka II
☛ Which book did Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I write? → Kavirajamarga

q: Where did the second Tamil Sangam meet take place?
qs.e: The second Tamil Sangam was held at Kapasapuram (also known as Kaviripoompattinam or Poompuhar). It was one of the three Sangam assemblies during the Sangam period. The first Sangam was held at South Madurai, the second at Kapasapuram, and the third at Madurai. These assemblies were instrumental in compiling and preserving Tamil literature. The Sangam period is considered the golden age of Tamil literature.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the first Tamil Sangam held? → South Madurai
☛ Where was the third Tamil Sangam held? → Madurai
☛ What is another name for Kapasapuram? → Kaviripoompattinam or Poompuhar
☛ Who were the patrons of the Tamil Sangam? → Pandya kings
☛ During which period was Sangam literature composed? → 300 BCE to 300 CE

q: The author of the Sanskrit book 'Jambavati Kalyanam' was ?
qs.e: 'Jambavati Kalyanam' is a Sanskrit play written by the great Vijayanagara emperor Krishna Dev Rai. This work is based on the story of Lord Krishna's marriage to Jambavati. Krishna Dev Rai was himself a scholar and poet, composing in both Telugu and Sanskrit. His court was adorned by the Ashtadiggajas, eight eminent poets, including Tenali Ram and Peddana. Another famous Sanskrit work by Krishna Dev Rai is 'Amuktamalyada'. This fact is significant as it highlights that he was not only a ruler but also a literary figure of high stature.
qs.kf:
☛ Author of Jambavati Kalyanam → Krishna Dev Rai
☛ Sanskrit work by Krishna Dev Rai → Amuktamalyada
☛ Ashtadiggajas of Vijayanagara → 8 famous poets
☛ Language of poets in Krishna Dev Rai's court → Telugu
☛ Name of Krishna Dev Rai's empire → Vijayanagara Empire

q: Which of the following literature is related to grammar and poetry?
qs.e: Tolkā ppiyam is an ancient Tamil literary work that deals with grammar and poetry. It is considered the oldest Tamil grammar text. It was authored by Tolkā ppiyar. The text is divided into three parts: Ezhuttadikaram (on letters and phonology), Soladikaram (on words), and Poruladikaram (on meaning and poetry). It provides rules for grammar and also covers aspects of poetry such as meter, figures of speech, and emotions. Other options like Manimekalai and Silappadikaram are epics based on stories, while Jivaka Chintamani is a Jain text. Thus, only Tolkā ppiyam is related to grammar and poetry.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the author of Tolkā ppiyam? → Tolkā ppiyar
☛ Which is the oldest Tamil grammar text? → Tolkā ppiyam
☛ How many parts does Tolkā ppiyam have? → Three parts
☛ What is the third part of Tolkā ppiyam called? → Poruladikaram
☛ In which language is Silappadikaram composed? → Tamil

q: Who is the founder of the Pallava Dynasty?
qs.e: The founder of the Pallava dynasty was Simha Vishnu, who established the Pallava kingdom in the 6th century CE. He was a great warrior and made Kanchipuram his capital. Simha Vishnu defeated the Kalabhras and restored Pallava power. His son Mahendravarman I expanded the Pallava empire. The Pallava dynasty was one of the major ruling dynasties in South India, lasting until about the 9th century. They are known for promoting art, architecture, and literature, especially the rock-cut temples and rathas (chariot temples) at Mahabalipuram.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Pallava dynasty? → Simha Vishnu
☛ What was the Pallava capital? → Kanchipuram
☛ Who was the son of Simha Vishnu? → Mahendravarman I
☛ What art form are the Pallavas famous for? → Rock-cut and ratha temples
☛ Whom did the Pallavas defeat to rise to power? → Kalabhras

q: Who was the last emperor of the Pallava dynasty?
qs.e: The last major ruler of the Pallava dynasty was Aparajitavarman, who reigned from around 882 to 898 CE. He was the son of Nandivarman III. During his reign, the Pallava kingdom weakened, and the Chola king Aditya I defeated him, ending Pallava dominance. This defeat marked the decline of the Pallava dynasty. The Pallavas are renowned for their contributions to architecture, especially the Ratha temples at Mamallapuram and the temples in Kanchipuram.
qs.kf:
☛ Last ruler of Pallava dynasty → Aparajitavarman
☛ Capital of Pallavas → Kanchipuram
☛ Founder of Pallava dynasty → Simhavishnu
☛ Famous Pallava king who built Mamallapuram → Narasimhavarman I
☛ Chola king who defeated the Pallavas → Aditya I

q: Who built the rock temple of Kailasa at Ellora?
qs.e: The Kailasa temple at Ellora is a famous rock-cut temple located in Aurangabad district, Maharashtra. It was built by Krishna I (756-773 CE), a ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is carved out of a single rock. Its architecture features a large courtyard, pillars, and intricate carvings. It is said that the construction took over seven centuries, but the main structure was completed during Krishna I's reign. The temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and an excellent example of Indian architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Kailasa temple? → Krishna I (Rashtrakuta)
☛ Where is the Kailasa temple located? → Ellora, Aurangabad, Maharashtra
☛ Which deity is the Kailasa temple dedicated to? → Lord Shiva
☛ Which dynasty is associated with Ellora caves? → Rashtrakuta, Yadava, Chalukya
☛ Who was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty? → Dantidurga

q: To whom among the following is the invention of the Sitar commonly credited?
qs.e: The invention of the Sitar is commonly credited to the 13th-century Sufi poet and musician Amir Khusrau. He was associated with the courts of several rulers of the Delhi Sultanate and made significant contributions to Indian classical music. It is believed that Khusrau developed the sitar by combining elements of the veena and the tanpura. Although historians debate this origin, the tradition attributes it to him. Khusrau is also credited with inventing the khayal gayaki and the tabla.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is considered the father of the Sitar? → Amir Khusrau
☛ Which sultanate was Amir Khusrau associated with? → Delhi Sultanate
☛ Who was Amir Khusrau's spiritual mentor? → Nizamuddin Auliya
☛ Which musical instrument did Amir Khusrau invent? → Sitar
☛ When was Amir Khusrau born? → 1253 CE

q: Which of the following is considered as the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent?
qs.e: Humayun's Tomb is considered the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent. It was commissioned by the Mughal emperor Akbar in 1572 in memory of his father Humayun. The tomb was designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas. It is built in the Charbagh style, which features a quadrilateral garden divided into four parts with the main structure at the center. This tomb is a significant example of Mughal architecture and inspired later structures like the Taj Mahal. In 1993, UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site. It is located in Delhi.
qs.kf:
☛ First garden-tomb in India → Humayun's Tomb
☛ Who built Humayun's Tomb → Akbar
☛ Architect of Humayun's Tomb → Mirak Mirza Ghiyas
☛ Garden style of Humayun's Tomb → Charbagh
☛ Year Humayun's Tomb declared UNESCO World Heritage → 1993

q: Alai Darwaja is a part of which of the following monuments of Mughal architecture?
qs.e: Alai Darwaja is a grand gateway located in the Qutub Minar complex in Delhi. It was built in 1311 CE by Alauddin Khilji. It is part of the Qutub Minar complex, not the Red Fort or Taj Mahal. Alai Darwaja is made of red sandstone and is considered the first example of Turkish architecture in India. It also uses marble and Arabic-Persian inscriptions. Its domed entrance features pointed arches and lattice windows. This structure is an important specimen of Indo-Islamic architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Alai Darwaja? → Alauddin Khilji
☛ In which year was Alai Darwaja built? → 1311 CE
☛ What material is Alai Darwaja made of? → Red sandstone and marble
☛ Which architectural style does Alai Darwaja represent? → Turkish architecture
☛ Which complex is Alai Darwaja part of? → Qutub Minar complex

q: Which of the following literary works of Sangam period has been considered as a collection of the oldest surviving Tamil Poetry?
qs.e: Patinenmelkanakku (The Eighteen Great Works) is the oldest surviving collection of Tamil poetry from the Sangam period. It comprises 18 works, some dating back to the 3rd century BCE. It is more ancient than Ettuthokai (Eight Anthologies) and Pattuppattu (Ten Songs), which are later compositions. Manimekhlai is a Buddhist epic from a later period. Patinenmelkanakku covers themes of love, war, and praise of kings. It is one of the earliest literary treasures of Tamil. It is also called 'Eighteen Lower Compositions'.
qs.kf:
☛ Meaning of Patinenmelkanakku → Eighteen Great Works
☛ Ettuthokai consists of → Eight Anthologies
☛ Number of songs in Pattuppattu → Ten Songs
☛ Religion of Manimekhlai → Buddhist epic
☛ Language of Sangam literature → Tamil

q: Name the classical language in which the ancient grammar book Tolkappiyam was written.
qs.e: Tolkappiyam is an ancient grammar text written in the Tamil language. It is considered the earliest extant literary work in Tamil literature. The composition of this text dates back to the Sangam period (around 3rd century BCE to 3rd century CE). Tolkappiyam provides a detailed description of phonetics, word formation, syntax, and semantics. This text is extremely important for understanding the development and structure of the Tamil language. Tolkappiyam is regarded as the foundational pillar of Tamil grammar and its author is Tolkappiyar.
qs.kf:
☛ In which language is the grammar book Tolkappiyam written? → Tamil
☛ Who is the author of Tolkappiyam? → Tolkappiyar
☛ During which period was Tolkappiyam composed? → Sangam period
☛ To which language family does Tamil belong? → Dravidian language family
☛ What does Tolkappiyam describe? → Phonetics, word formation, syntax, and semantics

q: Name the author who wrote the book Tajul-Ma'asir, considered as the first official history of the Delhi Sultanate.
qs.e: Tajul-Ma'asir is considered the first official history of the Delhi Sultanate, authored by Hasan Nizami. Written in Persian, it chronicles the reigns of Qutb-ud-din Aibak and Iltutmish. Hasan Nizami was the court historian of Iltutmish. The book begins with the history of Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni and covers events up to Iltutmish's rule. Other options: Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan traveler, Abdur Razzaq was a Persian historian, and Abul Fazl was a court historian of Akbar.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote Tajul-Ma'asir? → Hasan Nizami
☛ In which language is it written? → Persian
☛ Which rulers does it describe? → Qutb-ud-din Aibak and Iltutmish
☛ Whose court historian was Hasan Nizami? → Iltutmish
☛ Which is the first official history of the Delhi Sultanate? → Tajul-Ma'asir

q: In July 2024, India's first sunken museum was inaugurated at which location?
qs.e: In July 2024, India's first sunken museum was inaugurated at Humayun's Tomb Complex in Delhi. This museum has been developed by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture in collaboration with the Archaeological Survey of India. It is built inside an ancient stepwell located in the center of the complex, which remains filled with water. Visitors walk on a glass bridge above the water to view the museum below. The museum displays over 300 artifacts from the Mughal period, making it a unique blend of technology and heritage.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first sunken museum → Humayun's Tomb Complex, Delhi
☛ Year of inauguration → July 2024
☛ Collaborating organizations → Aga Khan Trust for Culture and Archaeological Survey of India
☛ Location of museum → Inside an ancient stepwell
☛ Items displayed → Over 300 Mughal-era artifacts

q: The term 'Sangam' refers to which of the following?
o: A literary assembly of Tamil scholars
qs.e: The term 'Sangam' in ancient Tamil literature refers to a literary assembly of Tamil scholars. These assemblies were held in three periods (Sangam period) from approximately 300 BCE to 300 CE. The first Sangam was held in Madurai, the second in Kapā ṭapuram, and the third again in Madurai. During these assemblies, poets and scholars composed Tamil poems and texts, which were later compiled. The early part of Tamil literature is called Sangam literature, which includes collections like Ettuthokai and Pattupattu. These assemblies were crucial for preserving Tamil culture and language, and they acted as academies for literary criticism and patronage. The Sangam period is considered the golden age of Tamil literature, with works like Tolkā ppiyam (grammar) and Silappadikaram (epic) originating from this tradition.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the first Sangam assembly held? → Madurai
☛ How many major collections are in Sangam literature? → Two: Ettuthokai and Pattupattu
☛ What was the time span of the Sangam period? → 300 BCE to 300 CE
☛ What was the main function of Tamil Sangam? → Evaluation and preservation of literary works
☛ When and where was the third Sangam held? → 3rd century CE in Madurai

q: From the 11th through the 18th centuries, what type of literature was the most prominent in medieval India?
qs.e: During medieval India (11th to 18th centuries), the Bhakti movement flourished, and devotional poetry became the most prominent literary form. Saints like Kabir, Tulsidas, Mirabai, Surdas, Nanak, and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu composed verses expressing love and devotion to God in local languages. This literature was simple and accessible to common people, challenging social norms and caste hierarchies. Devotional poetry not only fostered religious awakening but also contributed to the development of regional languages such as Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, and Bengali. While other forms like theatrical performances and philosophical discussions existed, none matched the widespread appeal and impact of devotional poetry, which remains a significant cultural heritage of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who were the major poets of the Bhakti movement? → Kabir, Tulsidas, Mirabai, Surdas
☛ What language did medieval devotional poetry use? → Regional vernaculars (Hindi, Marathi, Bengali)
☛ Who wrote Ramcharitmanas? → Tulsidas (16th century)
☛ What is the collection of Guru Nanak's compositions? → Guru Granth Sahib
☛ What is the central theme of devotional poetry? → Love and devotion to God

q: During which of the following dynasties was the Kailasa Temple at Ellora built?
qs.e: The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) at Ellora was built during the Rashtrakuta dynasty under the patronage of King Krishna I (c. 756– 773 CE). This temple is the world's largest monolithic structure, carved out of a single rock, and is an exquisite example of Dravidian architecture. It was constructed in the 8th century and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple is about 32 meters high and symbolizes Mount Kailash. The Rashtrakutas ruled parts of South and Central India from the 6th to the 10th centuries. The Kailasa Temple is a part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site at Ellora, which comprises 34 caves featuring Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments.
qs.kf:
☛ Builder of Kailash Temple → Krishna I
☛ Total caves at Ellora → 34
☛ Religions associated with Ellora caves → Hindu, Buddhist, Jain
☛ Ellora is a UNESCO World Heritage Site → Yes
☛ Ajanta caves are famous for → Buddhist paintings and sculptures

q: The famous Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal was built in the 8th century by?
qs.e: The Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal, located in Karnataka, was built in the 8th century by the Chalukya ruler Vikramaditya II. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, this temple is a masterpiece of architecture that blends the Dravidian and Nagara styles. Pattadakal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and among its ten temples, the Virupaksha Temple is the largest and most famous. The name 'Virupaksha' refers to a form of Shiva. The Chalukyas constructed numerous temples at Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal, showcasing their patronage of art and architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Virupaksha Temple located? → Pattadakal, Karnataka
☛ Which deity is the Virupaksha Temple dedicated to? → Shiva
☛ Which ruler built the Virupaksha Temple? → Vikramaditya II (Chalukya)
☛ What recognition does Pattadakal hold? → UNESCO World Heritage Site
☛ Which architectural styles does the Virupaksha Temple represent? → Mix of Dravidian and Nagara styles

q: Manimekali, a notable work within early Tamil literature, is categorised as which type of literary composition?
qs.e: Manimekalai is a famous epic in early Tamil literature, considered among the five great epics of Tamil. It was composed by Madurai Kulavanikan Seethalai Sattanar. The story revolves around Manimekalai, the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi, who chooses to become a Buddhist nun instead of a dancer. The epic emphasizes Buddhist philosophy, penance, and non-violence. It is a post-Sangam work and is seen as a sequel to the epic Silappadikaram. Manimekalai also contains elements of fantasy and supernatural events, reflecting the religious and cultural values of ancient Tamil society.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote Manimekalai? → Madurai Kulavanikan Seethalai Sattanar
☛ What are the five great Tamil epics? → Silappadikaram, Manimekalai, Jivaka Chintamani, Valayapati, Kundalakesi
☛ Which religion is associated with Manimekalai? → Buddhism
☛ Who wrote Silappadikaram? → Ilango Adigal
☛ Who is the protagonist of Manimekalai? → Manimekalai

q: Amir Khusrau is known for contributing to which two languages?
qs.e: Amir Khusrau (1253–1325) was a great scholar, poet, and musician of the Delhi Sultanate. He made significant contributions to Persian and Hindavi (early Hindi). In Persian, he was a renowned poet and authored many literary works. In Hindavi, he composed folk songs, riddles, and couplets, including famous ones like 'Chhap tilak sab chheen re' and 'Aaj shanichar ko man bhayo'. He is also regarded as the father of Qawwali and invented musical instruments like Tabla and Sitar. His works often blended Persian and Hindavi in a unique style. Amir Khusrau was a court poet of several Delhi Sultans and his writings reflect the cultural synthesis of medieval India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which sultan's court was Amir Khusrau associated with? → Jalaluddin Khalji, Alauddin Khalji, and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq
☛ In which book did Amir Khusrau describe India? → Tughlaqnama
☛ What title was given to Amir Khusrau? → Tuti-e-Hind
☛ Which music style did Amir Khusrau develop? → Qawwali and Tarana
☛ Which book contains Amir Khusrau's Hindavi poetry? → Halat-e-Hind

q: Which among the following South Indian kingdoms is known for the conquest that crossed the river Ganga in the north?
qs.e: The Chola king Rajendra Chola I is known for his northern campaign in which he crossed the Ganges river and founded the city of 'Gangaikonda Cholapuram'. This conquest demonstrated the military might of the Chola empire. The Chola dynasty was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in South India, with its capital at Thanjavur. Rajendra Chola I also led expeditions to Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and Southeast Asia. The Chola period saw significant advances in art, literature, and administration.
qs.kf:
☛ Chola king who crossed the Ganges → Rajendra Chola I
☛ City founded by Rajendra Chola I → Gangaikonda Cholapuram
☛ Capital of the Chola empire → Thanjavur
☛ Chief deity of the Cholas → Shiva
☛ Famous Chola temple → Brihadeeswarar Temple

q: During the Chola rule, which of the following was the land donated to Jaina institutions?
qs.e: During the Chola rule, land was classified into various categories. Pallichchhandam was the land donated to Jaina institutions. The term is derived from 'palli' (Jain temple) and 'chhandam' (gift). Among other options, Tirunamattukkani was land donated to temples, Shalabhoga was land for the maintenance of schools, and Vellanvagai was land given to peasants. Thus, the Chola administration had an elaborate classification of land grants, catering to the needs of various religious and social institutions.
qs.kf:
☛ Land donated to Jain institutions by Cholas → Pallichchhandam
☛ Land donated to temples by Cholas → Tirunamattukkani
☛ Land for schools under Cholas → Shalabhoga
☛ Land given to peasants under Cholas → Vellanvagai
☛ Chola land tax term → Kadamai

q: The Pallava kings adopted which title to reflect that their rule was guided by the principles of the Dharmashastras?
qs.e: The Pallava kings adopted the title 'Dharma-Maharaja' to signify that their rule was guided by the principles of the Dharmashastras. This title reflected their commitment to justice and righteousness in administration. The Pallava dynasty ruled over South India from the 3rd to the 9th century CE, with their capital at Kanchipuram. While Pallava rulers also used titles like 'Maharajadhiraja' and 'Chakravarti', it was the title 'Dharma-Maharaja' that specifically indicated rule by Dharmashastras. This title underscores their adherence to religious tolerance and Vedic traditions. The Pallavas are also known for their patronage of Dravidian architecture, as seen in the temples of Mahabalipuram.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the capital of the Pallava kings? → Kanchipuram
☛ What was the period of Pallava rule? → 3rd to 9th century CE
☛ Which Pallava king built the ratha temples at Mamallapuram? → Narasimhavarman I
☛ Which architectural style developed under Pallava rule? → Dravidian architecture
☛ What was another popular title used by the Pallavas? → Maharajadhiraja

q: Who among the following constructed the Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchi?
qs.e: The Kailasanatha Temple, located in Kanchi (present-day Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu), is an ancient Hindu temple built by Narasimhavarman II (also known as Rajasimhavarman). He was a great ruler of the Pallava dynasty, and his reign (c. 700-728 CE) is considered the golden age of Pallava art. The temple is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is carved out of stone and features numerous sculptures and inscriptions.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Kailasanatha Temple located? → Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu
☛ Who built it? → Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimhavarman)
☛ Dedicated to which deity? → Shiva
☛ Architectural style? → Dravidian
☛ Dynasty associated? → Pallava

q: What was the capital of Hoyasala’s Kingdom?
qs.e: Hoysala dynasty was a prominent South Indian kingdom that ruled from the 10th to 14th century. Its capital was Dvarasamudra (modern Halebidu, Karnataka). The Hoysala rulers patronized art and architecture, especially temple construction. The Hoysaleswara Temple at Dvarasamudra is an exquisite example of their architectural style. Other options are incorrect: Mysore was the capital of the Wodeyar dynasty, Devagiri of the Yadavas, and Kalyani of the Chalukyas. The Hoysala kingdom declined in the 14th century with the rise of the Vijayanagara Empire.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Hoysala dynasty → Nripa Kama (1006 CE)
☛ Most famous Hoysala ruler → Vishnuvardhana
☛ Best example of Hoysala architecture → Hoysaleswara Temple (Halebidu)
☛ Primary language of Hoysalas → Kannada
☛ Hoysala kingdom ended by → Vijayanagara Empire

q: The noted traveller and writer Muhammad Ibn Battuta, who travelled to many countries including India in the 14th century, belonged to which of the following countries?
qs.e: Muhammad Ibn Battuta was born in 1304 CE in Tangier, Morocco, and is renowned as one of history's greatest travelers and writers. In the 14th century, he traveled over 1,20,000 kilometers, covering most of the Islamic world and beyond. He visited India in 1333 CE during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq of the Delhi Sultanate, where he served as a judge (Qazi). His travelogue, known as Rihla or My Travels, provides detailed accounts of India, China, the Maldives, and Africa. Ibn Battuta's writings are invaluable to historians for understanding medieval societies. He is widely regarded as the greatest medieval traveler.
qs.kf:
☛ Ibn Battuta's birthplace → Tangier, Morocco
☛ His famous book → Rihla
☛ Year of arrival in India → 1333 CE
☛ His employer in India → Muhammad bin Tughlaq
☛ Approx. distance traveled → 1,20,000 km

q: Which world heritage site was built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty?
qs.e: King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty built the famous Sun Temple at Konark, Odisha, in the 13th century. Dedicated to the Sun God, it is also known as the Konark Sun Temple. The temple is designed as a massive chariot with 12 pairs of wheels and seven horses, showcasing the Kalinga architecture. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984. Hampi is associated with the Vijayanagara Empire, Sarnath with Buddhism, and Lepakshi with the Vijayanagara period, making them incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Konark Sun Temple? → King Narasimhadeva I (Eastern Ganga dynasty)
☛ Which deity is the Konark Temple dedicated to? → Sun God
☛ In which state is the Konark Sun Temple located? → Odisha
☛ Which architectural style is the Konark Temple built in? → Kalinga style
☛ When did the Konark Temple become a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1984

name: Set 2 · Q45–87
