☛ What was Swami Vivekananda's original name? → Narendranath Datta
☛ Who was Swami Vivekananda's guru? → Ramakrishna Paramahamsa

q: The Indian Home Rule League at Madras was founded by ______.
qs.e: Annie Besant founded the Indian Home Rule League at Madras (now Chennai) in September 1916. Its aim was to secure self-government (Home Rule) for India within the British Empire. Bal Gangadhar Tilak had started a separate Home Rule League in Maharashtra in April 1916. Both leagues worked through public meetings, propaganda, and petitions to energize the independence movement. Annie Besant was a prominent social reformer and later became the president of the Indian National Congress.
qs.kf:
☛ Home Rule League founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak → April 1916 in Maharashtra
☛ Home Rule League founded by Annie Besant → September 1916 in Madras
☛ Main objective of Home Rule Movement → To achieve self-government (Dominion Status) within the British Empire
☛ Annie Besant's first achievement → Became president of Indian National Congress in 1917
☛ Propaganda media of Home Rule Leagues → Newspaper 'New India' (Annie Besant) and 'Maratha' (Tilak)

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding the Poona Pact of 1932?
o: Seats reserved for depressed classes increased in the legislatures.
Ambedkar refused to sign the pact.
It was accepted by the government.
It dropped the idea of separate electorates for depressed classes.
qs.e: The Poona Pact was signed in 1932 between Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi. It was reached after Gandhi's fast unto death against the Communal Award. Ambedkar did sign the pact, which dropped the idea of separate electorates for depressed classes and increased reserved seats in legislatures. The government accepted it. Hence, statement 2 is false.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Poona Pact signed? → 1932
☛ Who were the main signatories of the Poona Pact? → Dr. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Which award did the Poona Pact modify? → Communal Award
☛ What concept was abandoned in the Poona Pact? → Separate electorates for depressed classes
☛ Which movement was the Poona Pact associated with? → Gandhi's hunger strike

q: Which reformer attempted to synthesize Indian and Western religious thought in the 19th century?
qs.e: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1772-1833) was a prominent 19th-century reformer who attempted to synthesize Indian and Western religious thought. He founded the Brahmo Samaj, a monotheistic reform movement. He integrated Western rationalism with Indian Vedantic philosophy to create a syncretic religious outlook. He opposed social evils like sati, child marriage, and caste system. He translated the Vedanta and Upanishads into English, introducing Indian philosophy to the Western world. He is considered the pioneer of the Indian Renaissance. His efforts laid the foundation for modern Indian reform movements.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Brahmo Samaj? → Raja Ram Mohan Roy
☛ Which reformer played a key role in abolition of Sati? → Raja Ram Mohan Roy
☛ Who translated Vedanta into English? → Raja Ram Mohan Roy
☛ Who is called the father of Indian Renaissance? → Raja Ram Mohan Roy
☛ Which reformer synthesized Western rationalism and Indian Vedanta? → Raja Ram Mohan Roy

q: Who was known as the "Mother of Indian Feminism" for her pioneering work in women’s education and rights?
qs.e: Savitribai Phule is known as the 'Mother of Indian Feminism' for her pioneering work in women's education and rights. She was India's first female teacher and opened the first school for girls in Pune in 1848. Along with her husband Jyotirao Phule, she contributed to social reforms and fought against untouchability, caste discrimination, and oppression of women. She promoted widow remarriage and opposed child marriage. Her work laid the foundation of the Indian feminist movement.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Savitribai Phule born? → 3 January 1831
☛ Where did Savitribai Phule open the first girls' school? → In Pune in 1848
☛ Who was Savitribai Phule's husband? → Jyotirao Phule
☛ What title is Savitribai Phule honored with? → Mother of Indian Feminism
☛ Which newspaper did Savitribai Phule edit? → 'Deenbandhu'

q: Which of the following social reformers established the ‘Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha’ in 1924?
qs.e: B R Ambedkar established the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in 1924. This organization aimed to work for the social, economic, and educational upliftment of Dalits. Ambedkar himself came from a Dalit family and dedicated his entire life to the rights of untouchables. This Sabha was the first major institution established by him, which later laid the foundation for his contribution to the framing of the Indian Constitution. Besides this, he also started newspapers like Mook Nayak and led the Mahad Satyagraha.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha established? → 1924
☛ Where was B R Ambedkar born? → Mhow, Madhya Pradesh
☛ What was the name of B R Ambedkar's wife? → Ramabai
☛ Which newspaper did B R Ambedkar start? → Mook Nayak
☛ In which year did the Mahad Satyagraha occur? → 1927

q: Which of the following freedom fighters led the Mahad Satyagraha in 1927?
qs.e: The Mahad Satyagraha was led by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar on 20 March 1927 in Mahad, Maharashtra. The protest aimed to secure the right of Dalits (then called untouchables) to use public water sources, specifically the Chawdar Tank. Ambedkar mobilized about 2,500 followers and marched to the tank, where they drank water, challenging the social discrimination based on caste. This event became a landmark in the Dalit movement for social equality. Later in 1927, Ambedkar also led the public burning of the Manusmriti, a text that justified caste hierarchy. The Mahad Satyagraha is considered a pivotal moment in India's social reform history, highlighting Ambedkar's role as a champion of Dalit rights and his strategy of non-violent protest.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Mahad Satyagraha? → B. R. Ambedkar
☛ Which water tank is associated with Mahad Satyagraha? → Chawdar Tank
☛ In which year did the Mahad Satyagraha take place? → 1927
☛ Which text was burned by Ambedkar in 1927? → Manusmriti
☛ What was the main aim of the Mahad Satyagraha? → To secure Dalits' right to use public water sources

q: Which of the following social reformers founded the Arya Mahila Samaj to serve the cause of women?
qs.e: Pandita Ramabai (1858-1922) was a prominent social reformer, scholar, and advocate for women's rights. She founded the Arya Mahila Samaj in 1882, dedicated to the education and empowerment of women. She was one of the first Indian women to advocate for higher education for women. Later, she established Sharada Sadan (1889) in Pune and Mukti Mission (1898) in Mumbai, providing shelter for widows and destitute women. Her work was pioneering in women's education and social reform.
qs.kf:
☛ Organization founded by Pandita Ramabai → Arya Mahila Samaj (1882)
☛ Famous work of Pandita Ramabai → Women's education and widow remarriage
☛ 'Sharada Sadan' established by → Pandita Ramabai in 1889 in Pune
☛ Autobiography of Pandita Ramabai → 'The High-Caste Indian Woman' (1887)
☛ Title conferred on Pandita Ramabai → 'Pandita' (as a Sanskrit scholar)

q: Behramji Merwanji Malabari, a Parsi social reformer, is credited for his efforts with the legislative enactment related to which of the following social evils?
qs.e: Behramji Merwanji Malabari was a prominent Parsi social reformer who campaigned against social evils like child marriage and widow remarriage in 19th-century India. His efforts led to the enactment of the Age of Consent Act of 1891, which raised the minimum age of marriage for girls to 12 years. This was a significant legislative step to curb child marriage. Malabari used his journal, 'The Indian Social Reformer', and published books to spread awareness. He is most credited for his work related to child marriage legislation. Other reforms like abolition of sati were championed by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, while female infanticide was addressed by later laws. Thus, Malabari's legacy is strongly tied to the fight against child marriage.
qs.kf:
☛ First act to restrict child marriage? → Age of Consent Act, 1891
☛ Act that completely prohibits child marriage? → Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
☛ Minimum age for marriage for a girl? → 18 years
☛ Minimum age for marriage for a boy? → 21 years
☛ Another reformer who campaigned against child marriage? → Keshab Chandra Sen

q: Keshab Chandra Sen was a prominent leader of which of the following reform movements in India?
qs.e: Keshab Chandra Sen (1838-1884) was a prominent leader of the Brahmo Samaj, founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828. He joined the Brahmo Samaj in 1857 and later founded the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866. Sen emphasized social reforms, especially women's education, widow remarriage, and abolition of caste system. He incorporated elements from Christianity and other religions into the Brahmo Samaj.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Brahmo Samaj? → Raja Ram Mohan Roy
☛ Who founded the Brahmo Samaj of India? → Keshab Chandra Sen
☛ Who founded the Adi Brahmo Samaj? → Debendranath Tagore
☛ What was the main aim of Brahmo Samaj? → Monotheism and social reform
☛ Which movement did Keshab Chandra Sen establish? → Brahmo Samaj of India

q: In which of the following present-day places did Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873?
qs.e: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 in Pune. The society aimed to eliminate caste discrimination, untouchability, and social inequality. Phule emphasized education for women and Dalits. He opened the first girls' school in Pune with his wife Savitribai Phule. The Satyashodhak Samaj promoted the search for truth and social reform. It opposed Brahmanical ideology and worked for the upliftment of Shudras and Ati-Shudras.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Satyashodhak Samaj? → Jyotiba Phule
☛ When was Satyashodhak Samaj founded? → 1873
☛ Where was Satyashodhak Samaj founded? → Pune
☛ What was the main objective of Satyashodhak Samaj? → Social equality and end of caste discrimination
☛ Name of Jyotiba Phule's wife? → Savitribai Phule

q: Who among the following was a Sanskrit scholar and helped in opening about 35 girls’ schools in Bengal?
qs.e: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a renowned Sanskrit scholar, social reformer, and educator. He played a crucial role in promoting female education in Bengal by helping establish about 35 girls' schools. He served as the principal of Sanskrit College, Kolkata, and was instrumental in passing the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856. He is considered a key figure of the Bengal Renaissance.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar born? → 1820
☛ Which Act did he help pass? → Widow Remarriage Act, 1856
☛ Which college's principal was he? → Sanskrit College, Kolkata
☛ How many girls' schools did he help open? → Approximately 35
☛ Which era is Vidyasagar associated with? → Bengal Renaissance

q: Who among the following is credited with establishing the 'Servants of India Society' to promote education and social reforms during the Indian National Movement?
qs.e: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society on June 12, 1905. Its aim was to promote education and social reforms in India. Gokhale was a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress and the political mentor of Mahatma Gandhi. Through the Society, he worked for rural development and against caste discrimination. The organization is still active today in social work. Bipin Chandra Pal, Dadabhai Naoroji, and Lala Lajpat Rai were other prominent nationalist leaders, but the Servants of India Society was established by Gokhale.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Servants of India Society? → Gopal Krishna Gokhale
☛ When was the Society established? → 1905
☛ What is Gokhale known as? → Founder of Servants of India Society
☛ Which party was Gokhale associated with? → Indian National Congress
☛ What was Gokhale's relationship with Gandhi? → Political mentor

q: Which of the following leader is associated with the founding of the Brahmo Samaj and its emphasis on monotheism and social reform?
qs.e: The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 in Kolkata. It was a religious and social reform movement that emphasized monotheism and opposed idol worship, caste system, sati, child marriage, and other social evils. Raja Ram Mohan Roy is regarded as the father of the Indian Renaissance and propagated monotheism based on Vedic and Upanishadic principles. The Brahmo Samaj promoted women's education, widow remarriage, and social equality.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Brahmo Samaj → Raja Ram Mohan Roy
☛ Year of establishment of Brahmo Samaj → 1828
☛ Main objective of Brahmo Samaj → Monotheism and social reform
☛ Raja Ram Mohan Roy is known as → Father of Indian Renaissance
☛ Sati practice was abolished due to efforts of → Raja Ram Mohan Roy

q: Which of the following is correct with respect to the theme of Yamuna Paryatam, the first novel in Marathi?
o: Focused on Political life of Yamuna region
qs.e: The first novel in Marathi language, 'Yamuna Paryatam', was written by Baba Padmanji. It was published in 1857. The theme of this novel is a critique of the miserable condition of Hindu widows and the prevalent social customs related to them. The author highlighted the hardships and injustices faced by widows. This novel was a significant step towards social reform in Maharashtra.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the first Marathi novel? → Yamuna Paryatam
☛ Who wrote Yamuna Paryatam? → Baba Padmanji
☛ When was Yamuna Paryatam published? → 1857
☛ What is the theme of Yamuna Paryatam? → Criticism of Hindu widows' condition

q: How did Mahatma Gandhi’s views on untouchability shape the priorities of the Indian National Congress during the Gandhian phase?
o: Endorsing separate political electorates for communities
Making abolition of untouchability a central objective
Shifting primary focus toward agrarian economic reforms
Concentrating on political integration of princely states
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi considered untouchability the greatest curse of Indian society and launched the 'Harijan' movement for its removal. During the Gandhian phase (1920-1947), the Indian National Congress prioritized social reforms, with the abolition of untouchability at the core. Gandhi emphasized temple entry, access to public places, and education for the untouchables. He opposed separate electorates as they would further divide society. The Congress, at its 1931 Karachi session, included the abolition of untouchability in its Fundamental Rights declaration. Thus, Gandhi's views shifted Congress priorities toward social equality, making untouchability eradication a central objective rather than focusing solely on political or economic issues.
qs.kf:
☛ What name did Gandhi give to untouchables? → Harijan (people of God)
☛ With whom did Gandhi oppose separate electorates? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Poona Pact, 1932)
☛ Which Congress session declared abolition of untouchability a fundamental right? → 1931 Karachi session
☛ When did Gandhi start his anti-untouchability movement? → 1932 (Harijan Sevak Sangh founded)
☛ Which community demanded separate electorates? → Dalit leaders, rejected by Gandhi

q: Who among the following is NOT directly associated with the Prarthana Samaj?
qs.e: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang in Mumbai. It was influenced by the Brahmo Samaj but focused more on social reforms. Mahadev Govind Ranade and R.C. Bhandarkar were prominent members, working on issues like widow remarriage and women's education. In contrast, Debendranath Tagore was a key figure in the Brahmo Samaj, founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828. Debendranath Tagore was the spiritual leader of the Brahmo Samaj and had no direct association with the Prarthana Samaj. Thus, he is the one not directly linked to the Prarthana Samaj.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Prarthana Samaj? → Atmaram Pandurang
☛ When was the Prarthana Samaj established? → 1867
☛ Key reformers associated with Prarthana Samaj? → Mahadev Govind Ranade and R.C. Bhandarkar
☛ Who founded the Brahmo Samaj? → Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1828)
☛ Which society was Debendranath Tagore associated with? → Brahmo Samaj

q: Which of the following best describes the Mahar Movement in Maharashtra?
o: A tribal uprising against British forest laws
A peasant movement against zamindari exploitation
A religious reform movement aimed at purifying Hindu rituals
A socio-political movement for Dalit rights and social equality
qs.e: The Mahar Movement in Maharashtra was a significant socio-political movement led by the Dalit community, particularly the Mahar caste, under the leadership of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. It aimed at securing social equality, educational opportunities, and political rights for Dalits. The movement strongly opposed caste-based discrimination and demanded rights such as temple entry, access to public spaces, and education. It emerged during the British colonial period and played a crucial role in awakening Dalit consciousness. After independence, it laid the foundation for constitutional safeguards for Scheduled Castes. The Mahar Movement was not a tribal uprising against forest laws, a peasant movement against zamindari, or a religious reform movement; it was specifically focused on Dalit empowerment and social justice.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Mahar Movement? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ What was the main objective of the Mahar Movement? → Social equality and rights for Dalits
☛ In which state did the Mahar Movement take place? → Maharashtra
☛ Which caste was the Mahar community part of? → Untouchable (Scheduled Caste)
☛ Which later movement was inspired by the Mahar Movement? → Dalit Panther Movement

q: Who gave the slogan 'Freedom is my birth right and I Shall have it'?
qs.e: Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave the slogan 'Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it' in 1907 during the Surat session of the Indian National Congress. He was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement and was widely known as 'Lokmanya'. This slogan ignited nationalist sentiments among the masses and became a rallying cry for freedom. Tilak criticized British rule through his newspapers 'Kesari' and 'Maratha' and turned the demand for Swaraj into a mass movement. He was a key leader of the Garam Dal (Extremist faction) and played a crucial role in founding the Home Rule League in 1916.
qs.kf:
☛ Birth of Bal Gangadhar Tilak → 23 July 1856, Ratnagiri, Maharashtra
☛ Who said 'Swaraj is my birthright'? → Bal Gangadhar Tilak
☛ Who gave Tilak the title 'Lokmanya'? → The public
☛ Which newspapers did Tilak start? → Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English)
☛ When did Tilak establish the Home Rule League? → 1916

q: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was made between-
o: Indian National Congress and All India Muslim League
British Government and All India Muslim League
Indian National Congress and British Government
qs.e: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was made between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League. It was a key event in the Indian independence movement, where both parties agreed on electoral reforms to promote communal unity. The pact was signed at the Congress session in Lucknow, presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar. Under this pact, the Muslim League supported Congress's demand for Home Rule, while Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims. This agreement paved the way for the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919. The Lucknow Pact is considered a high point of Hindu-Muslim unity.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of Lucknow Pact → 1916
☛ Parties involved in Lucknow Pact → Congress and Muslim League
☛ President of Lucknow session → Ambica Charan Mazumdar
☛ Muslim League supported which movement → Home Rule Movement
☛ Congress accepted what in the pact → Separate electorates for Muslims

q: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, along with Sir Ratanji Jamsetji Tata, opened a shop of indigenous goods in the year 1905, what was the name of that shop? A. Bharat Swadeshi Co-Op Shop Co. Ltd.
B. Jai Hind Co-Op Shop Ltd. C. Hindustan Swadeshi Co-Op Shop Co. Ltd. D. Bombay Swadeshi Co-Op Stores Co. Ltd.
qs.e: In 1905, Bal Gangadhar Tilak along with Sir Ratanji Jamsetji Tata established the Bombay Swadeshi Co-Op Stores Co. Ltd. This was part of the Swadeshi Movement, which began as a protest against the Partition of Bengal in 1905. The store aimed to promote indigenous goods and boycott foreign products. Tilak was a prominent leader of the Swadeshi Movement, encouraging people to use domestically produced items. The store was opened in Bombay (now Mumbai) and played a significant role in popularizing swadeshi products. Sir Ratanji Tata, a philanthropist, supported this initiative to foster economic nationalism.
qs.kf:
☛ Bal Gangadhar Tilak was given the title 'Lokmanya'.
☛ Swadeshi Movement began in 1905 against the Partition of Bengal.
☛ Sir Ratanji Jamsetji Tata was the son of Tata Group founder Jamsetji Tata.
☛ Bombay Swadeshi Co-Op Stores Co. Ltd. was established to promote indigenous goods.
☛ In 1905, the Indian National Congress passed the Swadeshi resolution at its Banaras session.

q: The lady who played an important role in the awakening of Indian women to fight for independence and who is also known as Nightingale of India is –
A. Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit
B. Durga Bai Deshmukh
C. Sarojini Naidu
D. Madam Bhikaiji Cama
qs.e: Sarojini Naidu is known as the 'Nightingale of India'. She was a renowned poetess and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the awakening of Indian women. She presided over the Indian National Congress session in 1925 and actively participated in the independence movement. Her poems inspired nationalism and women empowerment. She also became the first Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Sarojini Naidu born? → 13 February 1879
☛ Who called Sarojini Naidu 'Bharat Kokila'? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ In which year did Sarojini Naidu become President of INC? → 1925
☛ When did Sarojini Naidu die? → 2 March 1949
☛ What is a famous poem by Sarojini Naidu? → 'In the Bazaars of Hyderabad'

q: . In order to help in the freedom struggle, which newspaper was started by Lokmanya Tilak?
A. Kesari
B. Amrit Bazar Patrika
C. Ghadar
D. Harijan
qs.e: Lokmanya Tilak started two newspapers in 1881: Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English). Through Kesari, he spread public awareness for the freedom struggle. It became a key platform for promoting Indian nationalism and criticizing British rule. Tilak was charged with sedition for articles in Kesari and was exiled to Mandalay jail. Kesari is still published today and symbolizes Tilak's legacy. Other options: Amrit Bazar Patrika (associated with Sister Nivedita/Harish Chandra Mukherjee), Ghadar (Ghadar Party), Harijan (Mahatma Gandhi).

☛ Where was Tilak imprisoned for sedition? → Mandalay
☛ Who started the newspaper Harijan? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Who started Amrit Bazar Patrika? → Harish Chandra Mukherjee and Sister Nivedita

q: Who among the following advocated a moderate, gradual and persuasive approach to colonial rule through the Swadeshi movement?
qs.e: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a moderate leader of the Indian National Congress. He participated in the Swadeshi movement but advocated a moderate, gradual, and persuasive approach to colonial rule. He was associated with the Prarthana Samaj and founded the Servants of India Society. Gokhale opposed violent or revolutionary methods and believed in constitutional reforms. His approach distinguished him from extremist leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He is also regarded as Mahatma Gandhi's political mentor.
qs.kf:
☛ Birth year of Gopal Krishna Gokhale → 1866
☛ Institution founded by Gokhale → Servants of India Society (1905)
☛ Which society was Gokhale associated with → Prarthana Samaj
☛ Who considered Gokhale his political guru → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Which faction did Gokhale belong to → Moderates

q: Who among the following did NOT advocate militant opposition to colonial rule through the Swadeshi movement?
qs.e: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a moderate leader of the Indian National Congress and did not advocate militant opposition to colonial rule through the Swadeshi movement. He favored constitutional methods and gradual reforms. In contrast, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal were extremists who supported Swadeshi, boycott, and national education as tools of resistance. The Swadeshi movement was launched in 1905 in protest of the Partition of Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Swadeshi movement start? → 1905
☛ Who ordered the Partition of Bengal? → Lord Curzon
☛ Who were the three main extremist leaders? → Lal-Bal-Pal

☛ Which newspaper did Bal Gangadhar Tilak start? → Kesari

q: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 provided a joint political platform for the moderates, radicals of the Indian national Congress and the ________.
qs.e: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was a historic agreement between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League. It provided a joint political platform for the moderates and extremists within the Congress along with the Muslim League. The pact included demands for self-government (Home Rule) and separate electorates for Muslims. This agreement marked a significant step towards Hindu-Muslim unity in the Indian national movement. It was signed at the Congress session in Lucknow, where leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Muhammad Ali Jinnah played key roles. The pact strengthened the Home Rule Movement and later contributed to the Khilafat Movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Between whom was the Lucknow Pact signed? → Indian National Congress and Muslim League
☛ What was the main aim of the Lucknow Pact? → Hindu-Muslim unity and demand for self-government
☛ What was agreed upon in the Lucknow Pact regarding Muslims? → Separate electorates
☛ In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed? → 1916
☛ What was the outcome of the Lucknow Pact? → Boost to the Home Rule Movement

q: _________ was the first president of Indian National Congress.
qs.e: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume. Its first session was held in Bombay, and its first president was Womesh Chandra Banerjee. He was a distinguished lawyer and social reformer. Later, he also served as a member of the Public Service Commission of India. Other options: Annie Besant (a British social reformer who later became Congress president), J.B. Kriplani, and Jawaharlal Nehru were later presidents. Hence, the correct answer is Womesh Chandra Banerjee.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Indian National Congress founded? → 1885
☛ Who founded the Congress? → A.O. Hume
☛ Where was the first session held? → Bombay

q: In Lucknow Session of Congress in 1916, both the Moderates and Extremist leaders were united. It was presided over by ________.
qs.e: The 1916 Lucknow Session of the Indian National Congress was historic as it reunited the Moderates and Extremists. The session was presided over by Ambika Charan Majumdar, a prominent leader from Bengal and former secretary of the Indian Association. This unity was facilitated by the Lucknow Pact (1916) between the Congress and the Muslim League, which agreed on separate electorates and political reforms. Key figures like Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Gopal Krishna Gokhale played instrumental roles in reconciling the two factions. The session symbolized a renewed collective strength in India's freedom struggle and set the stage for future mass movements.
qs.kf:
☛ President of Lucknow Session (1916) → Ambika Charan Majumdar
☛ Lucknow Pact was signed between → Congress and Muslim League (1916)
☛ When did Bal Gangadhar Tilak rejoin Congress → 1916 Lucknow Session

q: What was the actual reason considered to be behind the Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon?
o: Bengal has emerged as an education center.
All freedom fighters were from Bengal.
Bengalis were opposing English dress and food.
Divide and Rule Policy of the British.
qs.e: Lord Curzon ordered the Partition of Bengal in 1905, officially citing administrative efficiency, but the actual motive was to implement the Divide and Rule Policy by creating a rift between Bengali Hindus and Muslims. Bengal was then a stronghold of Indian nationalism, and the British wanted to weaken this growing nationalist sentiment. At the time of partition, Bengal had a population of about 8 crores, which was divided into East Bengal and Assam (Muslim-majority) and West Bengal (Hindu-majority). This decision ignited the Swadeshi Movement and a surge in nationalism, eventually forcing the British to annul the partition in 1911.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the declared reason for the Partition of Bengal? → Administrative convenience
☛ When did the Partition of Bengal take place? → 1905
☛ Who was the prominent leader opposing the partition? → Surendranath Banerjee
☛ Who became the Lieutenant Governor of East Bengal and Assam after partition? → Bamfield Fuller
☛ When was the partition of Bengal annulled? → 1911

q: Who was the founding President of the Indian National Congress?
qs.e: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in 1885 in Bombay. It was founded by A.O. Hume. Womesh Chandra Bannerjee was elected as the first President of the Congress. He was a prominent lawyer from Bengal and later became a judge of the Calcutta High Court. Early Congress presidents included Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, and Ananda Mohan Bose.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Indian National Congress → A.O. Hume
☛ First session → 1885, Bombay
☛ First President → Womesh Chandra Bannerjee
☛ First woman President → Annie Besant (1917)

q: Where did Mahatma Gandhi preside over the annual session of the Indian National Congress for the first and the last time?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the annual session of the Indian National Congress only once, in 1924 at Belgaum (now in Karnataka). This was his first and last time as president. After returning to India in 1915, Gandhi played an active role in the Congress but avoided holding organizational posts. The Belgaum session, often called the "Gandhi Session," focused on post-Non-Cooperation movement strategies and promoted civil disobedience. Gandhi chose not to preside again, as he preferred to remain a guiding force rather than a formal leader. Notably, the 1924 session was significant for bridging the gap between moderates and extremists under Gandhi's leadership.
qs.kf:
☛ Gandhi served as Congress president? → Only once, in 1924 at Belgaum
☛ 1924 Congress session venue? → Belgaum, Karnataka
☛ Belgaum session is also known as? → Gandhi Session
☛ Why did Gandhi not preside again? → He preferred staying away from formal posts
☛ First Congress session after Non-Cooperation? → 1924 Belgaum

q: Which Viceroy ordered the partition of Bengal in 1905?
qs.e: The partition of Bengal in 1905 was ordered by Viceroy Lord Curzon. The official reason was administrative efficiency, but the actual motive was to divide and rule the politically conscious Bengal. The partition created East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal. This sparked widespread Swadeshi Movement and protests. The partition was later annulled in 1911 during the tenure of Viceroy Lord Hardinge.
qs.kf:
☛ Who ordered the Partition of Bengal? → Lord Curzon
☛ When did the Partition of Bengal happen? → 1905
☛ When was the partition revoked? → 1911
☛ Which Viceroy revoked the partition? → Lord Hardinge
☛ Which movement opposed the partition? → Swadeshi Movement

q: Banaras Hindu University was established in ________.
qs.e: Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was established in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya. It is one of the most prestigious universities in India, located in Varanasi. The aim of its establishment was to promote Indian culture, arts, and sciences. BHU is known for its residential nature and vast campus. The first Vice-Chancellor of BHU was Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. This university plays a vital role in education, research, and nation-building.
qs.kf:

q: When was the Muslim League founded?
qs.e: The Muslim League was founded in 1906 in Dhaka under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah Khan. Its aim was to protect the political rights of Indian Muslims. The League remained loyal to British rule and opposed the Indian National Congress. In 1940, the League passed the Lahore Resolution demanding a separate nation for Muslims, leading to the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

☛ Where was the Muslim League founded? → Dhaka
☛ Who founded the Muslim League? → Nawab Salimullah Khan

q: Who was the first Indian woman president of the Indian National Congress?
qs.e: Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman president of the Indian National Congress. She presided over the 1925 session held in Kanpur. She was a renowned poet and freedom fighter, known as the 'Nightingale of India'. Earlier, in 1917, Annie Besant became the first woman president of the Congress, but she was of British origin. Sarojini Naidu later served as a member of the Constituent Assembly and became the first governor of Uttar Pradesh. Indira Gandhi assumed the Congress presidency in 1959, while Vijay Laxmi Pandit was the first woman president of the United Nations General Assembly.
qs.kf:
☛ First woman president of Indian National Congress → Annie Besant (1917)
☛ First Indian woman president → Sarojini Naidu (1925)

☛ Achievement of Vijay Laxmi Pandit → First woman president of UN General Assembly

q: Who is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
qs.e: Dadabhai Naoroji is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'. He was a prominent Indian politician, economist, and educator. He was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress and served as its president in 1886, 1893, and 1906. He was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament. In his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', he propounded the theory of drainage of wealth from India. He is also revered as the 'Father of Indian Economics'. His contributions laid the foundation for India's freedom struggle.

q: Who among the following is called the 'Father of Local Self Government' in India?
qs.e: Lord Ripon (1880-1884) is known as the 'Father of Local Self Government' in India. He passed a famous resolution on Indian local self-government in 1882, which established rural and urban local bodies. Under this resolution, elected members were included in local boards and given the power to levy taxes and manage local affairs. The aim was to provide Indians with administrative experience and promote democratic processes at the local level. This effort of Lord Ripon is considered the foundation of local self-government in India.
qs.kf:

q: The first session of Indian National Congress was held in 1885. In which city of India was it held?
qs.e: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in 1885 in Bombay. It was presided over by Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee. The session took place at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College. The Congress was founded by A.O. Hume, a retired British civil servant. A total of 72 delegates attended this session. This event is considered an important milestone in the beginning of the Indian freedom struggle.

q: In 1866, who organised the East India Association in London to discuss the Indian question and to influence British public officials to promote Indian welfare?
qs.e: In 1866, Dadabhai Naoroji organised the East India Association in London with the aim of discussing Indian questions and influencing British public officials to promote Indian welfare. This association played a crucial role in the early phase of the Indian national movement. Naoroji later became the president of the Indian National Congress. He highlighted India's poverty in his famous book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'. He was also the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament.

q: Who among following was known as the 'extremist leader' during the Freedom Movement of India?
qs.e: The prominent extremist leader during the Indian freedom movement was Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright' and used Ganesh Chaturthi and Shivaji festivals for mass mobilization. Tilak launched the Home Rule Movement in 1916 and spread revolutionary ideas through newspapers Kesari and Maratha. He opposed the moderates' approach and advocated assertive methods. His radical stance marked a shift in the nationalist movement.

q: Where was the Muslim League founded?
qs.e: The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka (now Bangladesh) in 1906. Its primary objective was to protect the political rights of Indian Muslims and promote their interests. The All India Muslim League was established by Nawab Salimullah Khan, Aga Khan, and other leaders. This organization later became the main platform for the Pakistan Movement. The formation of the League created a significant communal divide in Indian politics, which eventually played a role in the partition of India. The first session of the Muslim League was held in Dhaka, and it elected Aga Khan as its first president.

q: In which year did the Indian National Congress split into two groups on the banks of River Tapti at The Surat Session?
qs.e: The Indian National Congress session at Surat in 1907 on the banks of the River Tapti witnessed a split into two groups: the Moderates (led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Ferozeshah Mehta) and the Extremists (led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal). The split occurred due to differences over the program of Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, and National Education. The Moderates favored constitutional methods, while the Extremists advocated a more aggressive approach. The split lasted until the Lucknow Session of 1916, when the two groups reunited.

☛ On which river bank was the Surat Session held? → River Tapti

q: The Indian League was established in 1875 in Calcutta (now Kolkata) by______.
qs.e: The Indian League was established in 1875 in Calcutta by Sisir Kumar Ghosh. It was a political organization aimed at fostering political awareness and nationalism among Indians. Sisir Kumar Ghosh was a prominent journalist and freedom fighter who also founded the 'Amrita Bazar Patrika'. The Indian League voiced opposition to British rule and paved the way for the formation of the Indian National Congress. This organization was a significant step in the development of Indian politics.

q: The newspaper "Kesari" was published by whom?
qs.e: Kesari was a Marathi-language newspaper founded in 1881 by Bal Gangadhar Tilak. It played a crucial role in spreading nationalist ideas during the Indian freedom struggle. Through Kesari, Tilak criticized British policies and mobilized public opinion. In 1897, he was charged with sedition and exiled to Mandalay jail. The newspaper also promoted the Swadeshi Movement and the Home Rule Movement, making it a key tool in India's fight for independence.

q: Where was the only convention of Indian National Congress held under the chairmanship of Mahatma Gandhi?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi chaired only one session of the Indian National Congress, held in 1924 at Belgaum (now in Karnataka). In this session, Gandhi reviewed the Non-Cooperation Movement and emphasized constructive programs like khadi and swadeshi. The Congress recognized Gandhi as the sole leader and shaped strategies accordingly. This session is notable for Gandhi's focus on village industries and self-reliance. The Belgaum session symbolizes Gandhi's leadership and the Congress's connection with rural masses, marking a shift towards mass mobilization.

q: In which year did Viceroy Curzon announce the partition of Bengal?
qs.e: Viceroy Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal in 1905, which took effect on 16 October 1905. The province was divided into Eastern Bengal and Assam (Muslim-majority) and Western Bengal (Hindu-majority). Curzon cited administrative convenience, but the real motive was to weaken the growing nationalist movement in Bengal. The partition sparked massive opposition, leading to the Swadeshi Movement and the Bang-Bhang Andolan, which became a major force in India's freedom struggle. The partition was annulled in 1911 by Lord Hardinge.

qs.e: Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress. She presided over the 1925 session in Kanpur. She was a renowned poetess and freedom fighter, often called the 'Nightingale of India'. Annie Besant, though the first woman president of Congress in 1917, was British, not Indian. Bina Das and Kalpana Dutt were freedom fighters but never Congress presidents. Sarojini Naidu later became the first woman governor of Uttar Pradesh.

q: When was the All India Muslim League formed in Dhaka?
qs.e: The All India Muslim League was formed in 1906 in Dhaka (now Bangladesh). It was established under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah Khan and included prominent leaders like Aga Khan and Muhammad Ali Jinnah. This party later spearheaded the Pakistan Movement. Before its formation, the Indian National Congress was founded in 1885. q: On whose advice, Gandhi spent a year travelling around British India to know the land and its people?
qs.e: On the advice of Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Gandhi spent a year travelling around British India to know the land and its people. Gokhale was considered Gandhi's political mentor. This journey took place after Gandhi returned from South Africa in 1915. Gokhale advised Gandhi to travel across the country to understand the real situation of India. During this trip, Gandhi visited rural areas and various communities, closely observing India's problems. This experience later shaped his ideas of Swaraj and Satyagraha. Gokhale guided Gandhi in political activities and inspired him to join Indian politics. Gokhale was a moderate leader of the Indian National Congress and a prominent social reformer. His mentorship played a crucial role in Gandhi's evolution as a leader.

q: Who said 'Home Rule is my birthright and I shall have it'?
qs.e: This famous quote was given by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, who founded the Home Rule League in 1916. Tilak was a prominent Indian nationalist, social reformer, and freedom fighter. He coined the slogan 'Home Rule is my birthright and I shall have it' to awaken the Indian masses towards the goal of self-rule. Tilak led the Garam Dal (Extremist faction) of the Indian National Congress and was honored with the title Lokmanya by the people. qs.e: The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was founded on 31 October 1920. It is the oldest trade union federation in India. Its first president was Lala Lajpat Rai, while the first general secretary was N. M. Joshi. The aim of AITUC was to protect workers' rights and promote their interests. Lala Lajpat Rai was a prominent freedom fighter and one of the founders of Punjab National Bank. He played an active role in the labor movement. q: National Planning Committee was established by the Indian National Congress in which year ?
qs.e: The National Planning Committee was established in 1938 by the Indian National Congress under the chairmanship of Subhas Chandra Bose, who was the Congress President at that time. Its purpose was to prepare a comprehensive plan for the economic development of India. The committee included prominent leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru, who later played a key role in setting up the Planning Commission in 1950. q: In 1907, where was the Annual Convention of the Indian National Congress held?
qs.e: The annual convention of the Indian National Congress in 1907 was held at Surat. This session was a turning point in the Indian freedom movement as it witnessed a clear split between the Moderates and the Extremists (Garam Dal). The session was presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh, but Bal Gangadhar Tilak and his supporters demanded Lala Lajpat Rai as the president. When this demand was rejected, the Extremists left the session and held their own separate convention. This event highlighted the ideological divide within the Congress: one faction believed in constitutional methods, while the other was more radical and aggressive in its nationalism. The Surat session marked the rise of extremism in Indian politics.

The Belgaum session was a significant milestone in the Indian freedom struggle, where Gandhi strongly articulated his views. Subsequently, the Congress laid the groundwork for the Civil Disobedience Movement. Thus, this session holds historical importance for Gandhi's leadership and Congress strategy.

qs.e: The agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League in 1916 at Lucknow is known as the Lucknow Pact. The split was primarily due to differences over the programme of Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, and National Education. The Extremist faction was led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal, while the Moderates were led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Ferozeshah Mehta. q: When the Indian National Congress (INC) had officially demanded an assembly to build the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The Indian National Congress officially demanded an assembly to frame the Constitution of India for the first time in 1935. This demand was made in opposition to the Government of India Act 1935, as the Congress believed that Indians should have the right to draft their own constitution. Later, the demand was reiterated during the Cripps Mission in 1942. Ultimately, the Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan, which adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949. The 1935 demand marks a significant milestone in the Indian freedom movement and constitutional development.

q: Who was the Viceroy of British India when the Elbert Bill was introduced?
qs.e: The Ilbert Bill was introduced in 1883 during the tenure of Viceroy Lord Ripon. This bill aimed to reform the Indian judicial system by removing racial discrimination in the judiciary, allowing European offenders to be tried by Indian magistrates. Lord Ripon (1880-1884) was a liberal viceroy known for his contributions to local self-government, educational reforms, and press freedom. The Ilbert Bill faced strong opposition from the European community in India, leading to a compromise that diluted its provisions. Despite the setback, Lord Ripon's administration is considered a milestone in the growth of Indian nationalism and civil rights. The bill was eventually passed in a modified form, but it sparked widespread debate about racial equality in British India.

☛ Which act restored press freedom under Lord Ripon? → Press Act of 1882

q: Whom did Gandhiji consider as his political guru?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi considered Gopal Krishna Gokhale as his political guru. Gokhale was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a social reformer. After returning from South Africa, Gandhi entered Indian politics under Gokhale's guidance. Gokhale introduced Gandhi to the intricacies of Indian society and politics. Gandhi greatly admired Gokhale's humility, spirit of service, and political acumen. After Gokhale's death, Gandhi paid tribute to him, stating that he was a true patriot and an ideal statesman.
qs.kf:
☛ Whom did Gandhi consider his political guru? → Gopal Krishna Gokhale
☛ Which organization was Gokhale associated with? → Indian National Congress
☛ Where was Gokhale born? → Kolhapur, Maharashtra
☛ Name the institution founded by Gokhale. → Servants of India Society
☛ What did Gandhi call Gokhale in his autobiography? → Political guru

q: Who among the following repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1881?
qs.e: Lord Ripon (1880-1884) repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1881. This act was passed in 1878 by Lord Lytton to curb the freedom of Indian language newspapers. Lord Ripon, known for his liberal policies, removed this repressive law, thereby promoting press freedom. He was a liberal Viceroy who made significant contributions in areas like local self-government, educational reforms, and press freedom. His tenure is considered important for the growth of Indian nationalism.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Vernacular Press Act enacted? → 1878
☛ Who enacted the Vernacular Press Act? → Lord Lytton
☛ What was the purpose of the Vernacular Press Act? → To control Indian language newspapers
☛ Who repealed the Vernacular Press Act? → Lord Ripon
☛ What was Lord Ripon's tenure? → 1880-1884

q: Where was the Indian National Congress session held in 1929?
qs.e: The 1929 session of the Indian National Congress was held in Lahore. This session was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. It is historically significant because the Purna Swaraj (complete independence) resolution was passed, and it was decided to observe 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day. This session also laid the groundwork for the Civil Disobedience Movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Who presided over the 1929 Congress session? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ What resolution was passed at the 1929 session? → Purna Swaraj
☛ When was the first Independence Day observed? → 26 January 1930
☛ Which movement followed the Lahore session? → Civil Disobedience Movement
☛ Where was the 1929 Congress session held? → Lahore

q: 'Pune Sarvajanik Sabha' was established at which of the following places?
qs.e: The 'Pune Sarvajanik Sabha' was first established in Pune in the year 1870. It was a prominent political organization during the Indian national awakening, founded by leaders like Mahadev Govind Ranade, Ganesh Vasudev Joshi, and Shivrao Holkar. The sabha aimed to raise public issues and seek redressal from the government. It later played a significant role in the formation of the Indian National Congress in 1885.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of establishment of Pune Sarvajanik Sabha → 1870
☛ Key founders → Mahadev Govind Ranade, Ganesh Vasudev Joshi
☛ Initial focus → Addressing grievances of peasants and workers
☛ Later contribution → Paved way for Indian National Congress
☛ Located in → Pune, Maharashtra

q: In which state did the Kisan Sabha movement start?
qs.e: The Kisan Sabha movement started in the state of Bihar. It was founded in 1929 under the leadership of Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, who is known as the 'Messiah of Bihar's peasants'. The main objective was to liberate farmers from the exploitation of zamindars and the British. This movement ignited peasant consciousness in Bihar and later strengthened the Congress as well as leftist parties. It is considered the precursor of the Indian peasant movement. Besides Bihar, Kisan Sabhas were also formed in Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, but the first organized Kisan Sabha began in Bihar.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is known as the father of the Kisan Sabha movement? → Swami Sahajanand Saraswati
☛ When was the Kisan Sabha founded in Bihar? → 1929
☛ What was the main objective of the Kisan Sabha? → Struggle against zamindari exploitation
☛ Who was the prominent leader of Bihar Kisan Sabha? → Swami Sahajanand Saraswati
☛ Into which organization did the Kisan Sabha later merge? → All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS)

q: Who became the fourth President of the Indian National Congress in 1888?
qs.e: In 1888, the fourth session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by George Yulee, a British industrialist. He became the second Englishman to hold the post of Congress president (after A.O. Hume). The session was held in Allahabad. Yulee's presidency was significant in the early years of Congress, when the organization was consolidating its foundation.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the first INC session held? → Bombay (1885)
☛ Who was the first President of INC? → Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee
☛ Where was the second INC session held? → Calcutta (1886)
☛ Who was the second President of INC? → Dadabhai Naoroji
☛ Who was the third President of INC? → Badruddin Tyabji

q: When was the Zamindar Sabha established?
qs.e: The Zamindar Sabha was established in 1838 in Calcutta. It was an organization of zamindars (landlords) loyal to the British government. Its founders included prominent zamindars like Raja Radhakanta Deb and Dwarkanath Tagore. The Sabha aimed to protect the interests of zamindars and cooperate with the government. It played a role in the early phase of Indian political awakening, although its influence declined later.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Zamindar Sabha established? → 1838
☛ Who were the founders of the Zamindar Sabha? → Raja Radhakanta Deb and Dwarkanath Tagore
☛ What was the main objective of the Zamindar Sabha? → Protecting zamindars' interests
☛ Where was the Zamindar Sabha established? → Calcutta
☛ To whom was the Zamindar Sabha loyal? → British government

q: Which extremist leader is known as 'Lokmanya'?
qs.e: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was honored with the title 'Lokmanya' (accepted by the people). He was a prominent leader of the extremist faction in the Indian freedom struggle. He gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' and used Ganpati and Shivaji festivals to mobilize the masses. Tilak published two newspapers: 'Maratha' in English and 'Kesari' in Marathi. He was one of the founders of the Home Rule League movement. He served as the president of the Indian National Congress three times. His ideas and actions gave a new direction to the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is known as 'Lokmanya'? → Bal Gangadhar Tilak
☛ Which newspapers did Tilak publish? → Maratha (English) and Kesari (Marathi)
☛ What was Tilak's famous slogan? → Swaraj is my birthright
☛ Which festivals did Tilak popularize? → Ganesh festival and Shivaji festival
☛ How many times was Tilak Congress president? → Three times

q: Which event intensified the Extremists' disillusionment with the British?
o: The arrival of the Simon Commission
qs.e: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 by Lord Curzon deepened the Extremists' disillusionment with the British government. This partition was implemented under the policy of 'Divide and Rule' to create a rift between Hindu and Muslim communities. In protest, the Swadeshi Movement and Boycott Movement were launched. Extremist leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal viewed it as a betrayal and adopted a stringent stance against the British. The event intensified the Extremists' distrust, pushing them toward demanding complete Swaraj.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Partition of Bengal? → 1905
☛ Who was the Viceroy during the Partition of Bengal? → Lord Curzon
☛ Which movement started against the Partition of Bengal? → Swadeshi Movement
☛ Who were the three extremist leaders (Lal-Bal-Pal)? → Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal
☛ What was the main objective of the Partition of Bengal? → Divide and Rule

q: Which extremist leader later adopted a spiritual path and was associated with Pondicherry (Puducherry)?
qs.e: Aurobindo Ghosh was a prominent extremist nationalist leader who later adopted a spiritual path and settled in Pondicherry (now Puducherry). He was involved in the Alipur Bomb Case (1908) during the Indian freedom movement and was tried for sedition. While in jail, he had spiritual experiences and later moved to Pondicherry, where he established the Sri Aurobindo Ashram. He became a propagator of Yoga and spirituality and wrote epic works like Savitri. His journal Arya is also well-known.
qs.kf:
☛ Which movement was Aurobindo Ghosh associated with? → Anti-Partition of Bengal movement
☛ Where is Aurobindo Ghosh's ashram? → Pondicherry (Puducherry)
☛ When did the Alipur Bomb Case occur? → 1908
☛ What is Aurobindo Ghosh's epic work? → Savitri
☛ Which journal did Aurobindo Ghosh publish? → Arya

q: Who was the Viceroy of India in 1905?
qs.e: The Viceroy of India in 1905 was Lord Curzon. He served as Viceroy from 1899 to 1905. During his tenure, the Partition of Bengal took place in 1905, which sparked the Swadeshi movement. He also implemented reforms in education, police, and railways. Robert Clive was in the 18th century, Lord Mountbatten in 1947, and Warren Hastings in the 18th century.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Viceroy did the Partition of Bengal happen? → Lord Curzon
☛ What was the tenure of Lord Curzon as Viceroy? → 1899-1905
☛ Which event initiated the Swadeshi movement? → Partition of Bengal
☛ Who was the last Viceroy of India? → Lord Mountbatten
☛ What is Robert Clive famous for? → Battle of Plassey

q: Which group criticised the moderates for their 'mendicancy'?
qs.e: In the Indian freedom movement, the Extremist faction criticised the Moderates for their policy of mendicancy. The Moderates sought reforms through prayers, petitions, and representation to the British government, which the Extremists viewed as weak and demeaning. Leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal advocated for direct struggle and self-reliance. This ideological divide culminated in the Surat session of 1907, leading to a split in the Indian National Congress. The Extremists believed in mass mobilization, boycotts, and Swadeshi as means to achieve Purna Swaraj (complete independence).
qs.kf:
☛ Group that criticised Moderates for 'mendicancy' → Extremists
☛ Key leaders of Extremist group → Lal-Bal-Pal
☛ Year of Congress split → 1907 at Surat session
☛ Method used by Moderates → Prayer, petition, and protest
☛ Main goal of Extremists → Complete independence (Purna Swaraj)

q: Which festival did Tilak introduce in 1893 to promote a sense of unity and nationalism?
qs.e: In 1893, Bal Gangadhar Tilak introduced the Ganpati Utsav (Ganesh Festival) to foster a sense of unity and nationalism among Indians during British rule. This public festival brought together people from different castes and classes, serving as a platform for cultural and political gatherings. Tilak used it to spread nationalist ideas and mobilize the masses, strengthening the freedom movement. The festival remains widely celebrated today, especially in Maharashtra, and symbolizes Indian cultural heritage. It played a crucial role in transforming the independence struggle into a mass movement by creating a collective identity.
qs.kf:
☛ Who started the Ganpati festival? → Bal Gangadhar Tilak
☛ When was the Ganpati festival started? → 1893
☛ What was the main aim of the Ganpati festival? → Promote unity and nationalism
☛ Which other festival did Tilak start? → Shivaji Festival
☛ In which state is Ganpati festival especially celebrated? → Maharashtra

q: In which year was the 1905 partition of Bengal reversed?
qs.e: The partition of Bengal in 1905 was carried out by Viceroy Lord Curzon. It led to widespread protests and the Swadeshi Movement. In 1911, during the Delhi Durbar, King George V announced the reversal of the partition. Bengal was reunified, and the new province of Bihar and Orissa was created. The capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi. This decision marked a significant change in British policy.
qs.kf:
☛ Who partitioned Bengal in 1905? → Lord Curzon
☛ Main reason for partition? → Administrative convenience
☛ Movement against partition? → Swadeshi Movement
☛ Year of reversal? → 1911
☛ Who announced the reversal? → King George V

q: Which slogan was associated with the extremist phase of the Indian National Movement?
o: Freedom is My Birthright and I Shall Have It
Sarfaroshi ki Tamanna, Ab Humare Dil Me Hai
Give me Blood, and I Shall Give Your Freedom
qs.e: During the extremist phase of the Indian National Movement, Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave this slogan. Tilak, known as Lokmanya, propagated the demand for Swaraj among the masses. This slogan gained prominence during the Swadeshi Movement after the Partition of Bengal in 1905. Tilak led the Garam Dal (extremist faction) and inspired people to fight against British rule. The slogan instilled a sense of self-determination and energized the freedom struggle. Tilak's efforts laid the foundation for mass mobilization in the subsequent years.
qs.kf:
☛ Slogan given by Bal Gangadhar Tilak → Freedom is My Birthright and I Shall Have It
☛ Tilak's title → Lokmanya
☛ Extremist phase period → 1905-1919
☛ Year of Bengal Partition → 1905
☛ Leaders of Garam Dal → Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal

q: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
qs.e: The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume. Its first session was held in Bombay (now Mumbai) at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College from 28-31 December 1885. The first President was Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee, a prominent lawyer from the Calcutta High Court. There were 72 delegates in this session. Initially, the Congress aimed to demand reforms from the British government, not to achieve independence. Later, it became the leading force of the Indian freedom movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first President of INC? → Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee
☛ When was INC founded? → 1885
☛ Who founded INC? → A.O. Hume
☛ Where was the first session held? → Bombay
☛ How many delegates attended the first session? → 72

q: The trio of extremist leaders, Lal-Bal-Pal, became prominent after:
qs.e: The trio Lal-Bal-Pal consisted of Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal. These extremist leaders rose to prominence after the Partition of Bengal in 1905. They led the Swadeshi and Boycott movements in protest against the partition. Tilak promoted Swadeshi in Maharashtra, Lajpat Rai in Punjab, and Pal in Bengal. Their efforts gave a militant turn to Indian nationalism.
qs.kf:
☛ Which movement is associated with Lal-Bal-Pal? → Swadeshi Movement
☛ When was the Partition of Bengal? → 1905
☛ Which newspapers were associated with Bal Gangadhar Tilak? → Kesari and Maratha
☛ What is Lala Lajpat Rai known as? → Punjab Kesari
☛ Which newspaper did Bipin Chandra Pal start? → Bengali

q: Who among the following was NOT associated with the 'moderate' phase of Indian National Congress?
qs.e: The early phase of the Indian National Congress (1885-1905) is known as the 'Moderate' or 'Liberal' phase. The prominent leaders of this phase were Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Surendranath Banerjee, Ferozeshah Mehta, and Anandamohan Bose. These moderates were loyal to British rule and sought reforms through constitutional means and prayers. In contrast, Bipin Chandra Pal was a key leader of the 'Extremist' or 'Assertive' phase. He was one of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio, who advocated radical methods like Swadeshi, Boycott, and Swaraj. Thus, Bipin Chandra Pal was not associated with the moderate phase of the Indian National Congress.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first president of the Indian National Congress? → Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee
☛ In which year did the moderate phase end? → 1905 (Partition of Bengal)
☛ Which organization was founded by Gopal Krishna Gokhale? → Servants of India Society
☛ What is Dadabhai Naoroji popularly known as? → Grand Old Man of India
☛ Which phase was Bal Gangadhar Tilak associated with? → Extremist phase

q: The Moderate leaders demanded simultaneous ICS examinations in __________________.
o: India and United States of America
qs.e: The Moderate leaders demanded simultaneous ICS (Indian Civil Service) examinations in India and England so that Indian candidates could avoid traveling to England. This demand was raised in the late 19th and early 20th centuries by the Moderate faction of the Indian National Congress. They argued that holding exams only in England disadvantaged Indian aspirants. However, the British government rejected this demand. Later, in 1922, following the Lee Commission's recommendations, exam centers were established in India as well. Thus, the Moderate leaders demanded simultaneous ICS examinations in India and England.
qs.kf:
☛ ICS exam started → in 1853.
☛ First Indian ICS officer → Satyendranath Tagore (1863).
☛ Moderate leaders → included Dadabhai Naoroji, Ferozeshah Mehta, Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
☛ Civil service exam conducted by → Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).
☛ ICS exam center in India → established in 1922.

q: During which of the following movements did the extremists call for the boycott of British goods as a form of protest?
qs.e: The Swadeshi Movement (1905-1908) was launched in protest against the partition of Bengal. Extremists like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal called for the boycott of British goods and promotion of indigenous products. The boycott aimed to exert economic pressure on the British government to reverse its policies. This movement marked a significant shift in the Indian freedom struggle as it involved mass participation and emphasized self-reliance. The Swadeshi Movement also promoted national education and cultural revival, making it a comprehensive protest against colonial rule.
qs.kf:
☛ Slogan of Swadeshi Movement → Vande Mataram
☛ Date of Partition of Bengal → 16 October 1905
☛ Extremist leader of Swadeshi Movement → Bal Gangadhar Tilak
☛ Main objective of boycott → Economic pressure
☛ Outcome of the movement → Promotion of indigenous goods

q: What slogan did Lokmanya Tilak popularise regarding Swaraj?
o: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."
qs.e: Lokmanya Tilak popularised the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it', which energised the Indian freedom struggle. Tilak believed that Swaraj was not a gift or achieved through sacrifice, but was a birthright. This slogan is associated with the Home Rule Movement launched by Tilak and Annie Besant in 1916. Through this slogan, Tilak instilled a sense of self-respect and freedom among Indians. He was honored with the title 'Lokmanya' and started newspapers 'Kesari' in Marathi and 'Maratha' in English.
qs.kf:
☛ What did Tilak call Swaraj? → Birthright
☛ When was Home Rule Movement launched? → 1916
☛ Which newspaper did Tilak start? → Kesari (Marathi)
☛ What title was Tilak given? → Lokmanya
☛ What was the aim of Home Rule Movement? → Achieving self-government

q: What ideology did the extremists strongly oppose within the Indian National Congress?
qs.e: The extremists within the Indian National Congress strongly opposed the policy of Gradualism (also known as the 'Slow and Steady' approach). The moderate leadership advocated for attaining self-governance through prayers, petitions, and gradual constitutional reforms. In contrast, the extremists demanded immediate complete Swaraj and considered the gradual approach ineffective. Led by leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal, they adopted aggressive methods including Swadeshi, boycott, and national education. The extremists believed that revolutionary steps were necessary to achieve freedom from British rule, rather than a slow process. Thus, gradualism was the primary ideology opposed by the extremists.
qs.kf:
☛ Main cause of split in Congress → Moderates vs. Extremists
☛ Three prominent extremist leaders → Lal-Bal-Pal
☛ What happened at Surat Session 1907 → Partition of Congress
☛ Two movements supported by extremists → Swadeshi and Boycott
☛ Main weapon of Moderates → Prayers and Petitions

q: The Indian National Congress session of 1905 took place in _____.
qs.e: The Indian National Congress session of 1905 was held in Banaras (Varanasi). It was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale. This was the same year as the Partition of Bengal (1905), which triggered the Swadeshi and Boycott movements. The Banaras session endorsed the Swadeshi movement and passed a resolution for the boycott of foreign goods. This session is significant in the history of the Indian National Congress as it gave a new direction to the nationalist movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the president of the 1905 Congress session? → Gopal Krishna Gokhale
☛ In which year did the Partition of Bengal occur? → 1905
☛ When did the Swadeshi movement begin? → 1905
☛ Which movement was supported at the Banaras session? → Swadeshi movement
☛ Where was the 1905 Congress session held? → Banaras

q: The Moderates' demand for 'No taxation without representation' was inspired by which historical movement?
qs.e: The Moderates of the Indian National Congress, such as Dadabhai Naoroji, Ferozeshah Mehta, and Gopal Krishna Gokhale, were inspired by the American War of Independence when they raised the demand of 'No taxation without representation'. This slogan was originally used by American colonists in 1765 to protest against the Stamp Act imposed by the British Parliament. The Moderates wanted Indians to have representation in the British Parliament so that taxes could not be levied without their consent. Their approach was constitutional and based on appeals to British justice and gradual reforms. The American struggle for representation against arbitrary taxation served as a historical precedent for their demand.
qs.kf:
☛ Who gave the slogan 'No taxation without representation'? → American colonists
☛ Which act prompted this slogan? → Stamp Act 1765
☛ Who were the key Moderate leaders in India? → Dadabhai Naoroji, Ferozeshah Mehta, Gopal Krishna Gokhale
☛ When did the American War of Independence occur? → 1775-1783
☛ What was the period of the Moderate phase in India? → 1885 to 1905

q: Who allied with Annie Besant for the Home Rule Movement?
qs.e: The Home Rule Movement aimed at achieving self-government for India within the British Empire. Annie Besant launched the All India Home Rule League in Lucknow in 1916, while Bal Gangadhar Tilak established the Indian Home Rule League in Pune. Both leaders worked in tandem to energize the movement and unite Indians. Tilak's famous slogan "Swaraj is my birthright" became the movement's rallying cry. Although Tilak withdrew from the movement in 1918 to focus on other activities, his collaboration with Besant was crucial in spreading the demand for self-rule across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Home Rule Movement start? → 1916
☛ Where was Annie Besant's Home Rule League established? → Lucknow
☛ Where was Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Home Rule League centered? → Pune
☛ What was the main objective of the Home Rule Movement? → To attain self-government
☛ What was Tilak's famous slogan? → Swaraj is my birthright

q: Which leader(s) represented the Bengal group of Extremists?
qs.e: The Bengal group of Extremists in the Indian National Congress was led by Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh. Both were prominent leaders of the extremist faction. Bipin Chandra Pal played a key role in the Swadeshi Movement and the anti-Partition of Bengal agitation. Aurobindo Ghosh established the National Council of Education and promoted revolutionary ideology. Other extremist leaders included Bal Gangadhar Tilak from Maharashtra and Lala Lajpat Rai from Punjab, but they represented their regional groups, not Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Bengal extremist group? → Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh
☛ B.C. Pal was associated with which movement? → Swadeshi Movement
☛ Which institution did Aurobindo establish? → National Council of Education
☛ Other extremist leaders? → Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai
☛ When was Bengal partitioned? → 1905

q: At which of the following places was the 'Servants of India Society' founded by Gopal Krishna Gokhale in 1905?
qs.e: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune on June 12, 1905. This society was established to work for social service and national awakening in India. Its objective was to unite people of different castes, religions, and classes, and to promote social reforms. Gokhale served as its first president. During the freedom struggle, the society worked in the fields of education, health, and other social areas. Later, it expanded to various parts of the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Servants of India Society → Gopal Krishna Gokhale
☛ Year of establishment → 1905
☛ Place of establishment → Pune
☛ Gokhale is known as → Political guru of India

q: Who among the following leaders strongly supported the idea of self-reliance and was an extremist?
qs.e: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement who strongly supported the idea of self-reliance (Swadeshi) and was an extremist. He was known as 'Lokmanya' and gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'. Tilak promoted the Swadeshi movement and emphasized the boycott of foreign goods. He propagated nationalist ideas through the newspapers 'Kesari' and 'Maratha'. He was the main leader of the Garam Dal (Hot Faction) and his ideology gave a militant edge to the freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Bal Gangadhar Tilak born? → 23 July 1856
☛ Which newspapers did Tilak start? → Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English)

☛ What is Tilak's famous slogan? → Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
☛ Which faction did Tilak belong to? → Garam Dal

q: All of the following were extremist leaders, EXCEPT _____.
qs.e: Surendranath Banerjee was a prominent leader of the moderate faction in the Indian national movement. He advocated for reforms through petitions and prayers against the British rule. In contrast, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Aurobindo Ghosh, and Bipin Chandra Pal were extremist leaders who emphasized Swaraj and direct action. Tilak gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.' Aurobindo Ghosh promoted revolutionary activities. Bipin Chandra Pal led the Swadeshi and boycott movement. Thus, Surendranath Banerjee was not an extremist but a moderate leader.
qs.kf:
