q: Which movement marked Mahatma Gandhi’s entry into all-India politics?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi led local movements like Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Kheda Satyagraha (1918), and Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918). However, the Non-Cooperation Movement launched in 1920, which was merged with the Khilafat Movement, was his first all-India political movement. It mobilized mass support against British rule and established Gandhi as a national leader. The movement included return of titles, boycott of schools and courts, and burning of foreign cloth. It was withdrawn after the Chauri Chaura incident in 1922. This movement marked Gandhi’s entry into national politics and set the stage for future struggles.
qs.kf:
☛ Gandhi’s first all-India movement → Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)
☛ Leaders of Khilafat Movement → Maulana Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali
☛ Year of Chauri Chaura incident → 1922
☛ Slogan of Non-Cooperation Movement → Swaraj is my birthright
☛ Who called Gandhi ‘Father of the Nation’ → Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose

q: To resolve peace following the riots that followed the Partition, the ‘Delhi Pact’ was signed between the Indian Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, and the Pakistan Prime Minister, __________.
qs.e: The Delhi Pact (1950) was signed between India and Pakistan to restore peace after the riots following the Partition. This pact was signed by Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistan's Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan. Its main objective was to ensure the safety of minorities and reduce tensions between the two countries. Under the pact, both nations pledged to grant equal rights to minorities and protect their property. Liaquat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, serving from 1947 to 1951.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Delhi Pact signed? → 1950
☛ Who was the Indian signatory of the Delhi Pact? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Who was the Pakistani signatory of the Delhi Pact? → Liaquat Ali Khan
☛ Which number Prime Minister of Pakistan was Liaquat Ali Khan? → First
☛ What was the main purpose of the Delhi Pact? → Protection of minorities and peace establishment

q: Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu was led by_________
qs.e: The Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu was led by C. Rajagopalachari, who later became the first Governor-General of India. This movement began in April 1930, following Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March. Rajagopalachari broke the salt law in Tamil Nadu (then Madras Presidency) along with many volunteers, protesting against British rule. This satyagraha strengthened Tamil Nadu's participation in the Indian freedom struggle. While K. Kamaraj, Potti Sriramulu, and C. Subramaniam were also significant leaders, the Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu was led by Rajagopalachari.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Salt Satyagraha start? → 12 March 1930
☛ Who led the Salt Satyagraha? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Where did the Dandi March start? → Sabarmati Ashram
☛ Who led the Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu? → C. Rajagopalachari
☛ What is C. Rajagopalachari's nickname? → C. Rajaji

q: On which date did Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
qs.e: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13th April 1919 in Amritsar, Punjab. It was a brutal act of firing on unarmed civilians by British troops under the command of Brigadier General Reginald Dyer. The firing was ordered at a gathering in Jallianwala Bagh without any warning, resulting in hundreds of deaths. This day also coincided with the festival of Baisakhi. The massacre led to widespread outrage and became a turning point in India's freedom movement. Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Jallianwala Bagh massacre → 13th April 1919
☛ Who ordered the firing → Brigadier General Reginald Dyer
☛ Festival on which it occurred → Baisakhi
☛ Who returned his knighthood in protest → Rabindranath Tagore
☛ Place where it happened → Amritsar, Punjab

q: Who has written the narrative history 'India after Gandhi’?
qs.e: Ramachandra Guha wrote the book 'India after Gandhi', which provides a detailed account of India's political history after 1947. The book focuses on the development of Indian democracy, major events, and leaders. Ramachandra Guha is a renowned historian, writer, and columnist who has authored several books on Indian history and the environment. His other notable works include 'Gandhi before India', 'A Corner of a Foreign Field', and 'The Unquiet Woods'.
qs.kf:
☛ Author of 'India after Gandhi' → Ramachandra Guha
☛ Birthplace of Ramachandra Guha → Dehradun
☛ Author of 'Gandhi: The Years That Changed the World' → Ramachandra Guha
☛ Publication year of 'India after Gandhi' → 2007
☛ Major award received by Ramachandra Guha → Sahitya Akademi Award

q: How many demands did Mahatma Gandhi make in his letter to Lord Irwin some of which were agreed to and came to be known as Gandhi-lrwin Pact?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi made a total of 11 demands in his letter to Lord Irwin dated March 2, 1930. These demands primarily included the abolition of salt tax, reduction of land revenue, prohibition of liquor, and release of political prisoners. Later, under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 5, 1931), only some demands were agreed upon, such as the withdrawal of the Civil Disobedience Movement, permission to make salt, and release of political prisoners. This pact paved the way for Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed? → 1931
☛ What is the other name of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact? → Delhi Pact
☛ Which movement was withdrawn under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact? → Civil Disobedience Movement
☛ Which Round Table Conference is related to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact? → Second Round Table Conference
☛ Who was Lord Irwin in India? → 29th Viceroy

q: Who led the non-cooperation movement in 1920-22?
qs.e: The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22) was led by Mahatma Gandhi. It was the first mass movement in India's freedom struggle, based on the principle of non-violence. The movement aimed at peaceful resistance against British rule, where people boycotted government posts, foreign goods, and educational institutions. Gandhi launched this movement after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Khilafat movement. In February 1922, following the Chauri Chaura incident, Gandhi called off the movement due to violence.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement start? → 1920
☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement end? → 1922
☛ When did the Chauri Chaura incident occur? → 5 February 1922
☛ Who was the leader of the Khilafat Movement? → Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar
☛ What was the main slogan of the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Swaraj

q: The Rowlatt Act was passed in ______.
qs.e: The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919 by the British Indian government. This act gave the British government the power to arrest and detain any person without trial. It was introduced under the pretext of suppressing anarchy and revolutionary crimes. In protest, Mahatma Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919. In response, the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on April 13, 1919. The Rowlatt Act was a significant event in the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Rowlatt Act passed? → 1919
☛ Which movement was started against the Rowlatt Act? → Rowlatt Satyagraha
☛ When did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occur? → April 13, 1919
☛ Who was the chairman of the Rowlatt Committee? → Sir Sydney Rowlatt
☛ What was the Rowlatt Act also known as? → Black Act

q: The Khilafat Movement was led by:
qs.e: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1922) was led by Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali. It was launched in protest against the British government's treatment of the Ottoman Caliphate, the Islamic religious leadership in Turkey. Indian Muslims supported the Turkish Caliph to protect his rights. Mahatma Gandhi linked it with the Non-Cooperation Movement to promote Hindu-Muslim unity. The movement ended after the Chauri Chaura incident in 1922.
qs.kf:
☛ Who were the main leaders of the Khilafat Movement? → Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali
☛ In which year did the Khilafat Movement start? → 1919
☛ What was the main objective of the Khilafat Movement? → To protect the rights of the Turkish Caliph
☛ Who linked the Khilafat Movement with the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Which event led to the end of the Khilafat Movement? → Chauri Chaura incident (1922)

q: Which one of the following was a measure taken under the Rowlatt Act?
qs.e: The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919 by the British government. Under this act, any person could be arrested and imprisoned without trial. It also ended the freedom of the press and allowed speedy trials for sedition cases. The act faced widespread opposition across India, especially in Punjab, where the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred. The Rowlatt Act intensified the national movement, and Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement against it.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Rowlatt Act passed? → 1919
☛ What was the main provision of the Rowlatt Act? → Imprisonment without trial
☛ Which movement was started against the Rowlatt Act? → Non-Cooperation Movement
☛ Which massacre occurred in protest of the Rowlatt Act? → Jallianwala Bagh massacre
☛ Which right was violated under the Rowlatt Act? → Right to judicial hearing

q: Which other movement was combined with the non-cooperation movement in 1920?
qs.e: In 1920, Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement, which was combined with the Khilafat Movement. The Khilafat Movement was a protest by Indian Muslims against the British government's disrespect of the Turkish Caliph. Gandhi saw this as an opportunity for Hindu-Muslim unity and merged it with the Non-Cooperation Movement. The combined movement aimed for non-violent resistance against British rule and the attainment of Swaraj. The Non-Cooperation Movement boycotted schools, courts, and foreign goods, while the Khilafat focused on religious issues. The movement was withdrawn in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year did the Non-Cooperation Movement start? → 1920
☛ Who led the Khilafat Movement? → Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali
☛ After which event was the Non-Cooperation Movement withdrawn? → Chauri Chaura incident (1922)
☛ The Khilafat Movement was related to which country? → Turkey
☛ Which movement did Gandhi use as a means for Hindu-Muslim unity? → Non-Cooperation Movement

q: In 1931, who among the following was the President of the Indian National Congress?
qs.e: In 1931, Vallabhbhai J Patel was the President of the Indian National Congress. He was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement and later became the first Home Minister of India. He presided over the Karachi session of 1931, where the Congress passed resolutions on fundamental rights and national economic policy. This session took place after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Vallabhbhai Patel is also known as Sardar Patel and played a crucial role in the integration of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Congress President in 1931 → Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Year of Karachi Session → 1931
☛ Year of Gandhi-Irwin Pact → 1931
☛ Who got the title 'Sardar' → Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ First Home Minister of India → Vallabhbhai Patel

q: Arrange the following in the correct chronological order as they occurred during the freedom struggle.
A. Jallianwala Bagh massacre;
B. Quit India movement;
C. Flag Satyagraha;
D. Non-cooperative movement
qs.e: The correct chronological order is: Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919) → Non-cooperative movement (1920-1922) → Flag Satyagraha (1923) → Quit India movement (1942). After the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, the national movement gained momentum, and in 1920, the Congress launched the Non-cooperative movement. Subsequently, in 1923, the Flag Satyagraha took place in Nagpur, demanding the right to hoist the Indian flag. Finally, in 1942, the Quit India movement was launched.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Jallianwala Bagh massacre → 13 April 1919
☛ Leader of Non-cooperative movement → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Location of Flag Satyagraha → Nagpur (1923)
☛ Slogan of Quit India movement → 'Do or Die'
☛ Duration of Non-cooperative movement → 1920-1922

q: Which of the following movements is related to forceful cultivation of Indigo?
qs.e: The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was the first civil disobedience movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in India. It was against the forceful cultivation of indigo by British planters in the Champaran district of Bihar. Farmers were forced to grow indigo on a portion of their land and sell it to the planters at low prices. Gandhi intervened and led a successful protest, resulting in the Champaran Agricultural Act, which ended the exploitation. This movement marked a significant turning point in India's freedom struggle and established Gandhi's leadership.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year did the Champaran movement take place? → 1917
☛ In which state did the Champaran movement occur? → Bihar
☛ What was the main issue of the Champaran movement? → Forced cultivation of indigo
☛ Who led the Champaran movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Which act was passed as a result of the Champaran Satyagraha? → Champaran Agricultural Act

q: When was the Gandhi - Irwin pact carried out?
qs.e: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and the then Viceroy Lord Irwin. This pact was signed before the Second Round Table Conference, in which Gandhi participated. Under this pact, the Civil Disobedience Movement was suspended and political prisoners were released. However, the pact failed as Indian demands were not accepted at the Round Table Conference. This pact was a significant phase in the Indian freedom struggle.

q: Who was the British Prime Minister during the first round table conference in London?
qs.e: The first Round Table Conference was held in London in 1930. At that time, the British Prime Minister was Ramsay MacDonald. The conference was convened to discuss constitutional reforms in India. MacDonald belonged to the Labour Party and served as Prime Minister from 1929 to 1935. The Indian National Congress did not participate in the first Round Table Conference, while it participated in the second and third conferences. The conference was chaired by the British Prime Minister himself.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first Round Table Conference held? → 1930
☛ Where was the first Round Table Conference held? → London
☛ Who was the Congress representative in the second Round Table Conference? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ What was the purpose of the Round Table Conferences? → Constitutional reforms for India
☛ When was the third Round Table Conference held? → 1932

q: When did the British Cabinet Mission arrive in India in order to examine the Muslim League's demand, and to suggest a suitable political framework for a free India?
qs.e: The British Cabinet Mission arrived in India in March 1946. Its purpose was to examine the Muslim League's demand for Pakistan and to suggest a suitable political framework for a free India. The mission consisted of three members: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A. V. Alexander. The mission presented its plan on 16 May 1946, proposing a federal union for India with provinces grouped into sections. It also recommended the formation of an interim government. However, due to differences between the Congress and the Muslim League, the plan failed.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Cabinet Mission arrive in India? → March 1946
☛ Who were the members of the mission? → Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, A. V. Alexander
☛ When was the plan presented? → 16 May 1946
☛ What was the main objective of the mission? → Examine Muslim League's demand and suggest political framework
☛ Why did the plan fail? → Differences between Congress and Muslim League

q: Prior to which of the following events was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
qs.e: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931. As per the pact, the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn, political prisoners were released, and salt tax was discussed. After the pact, Mahatma Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference (September-December 1931, London) as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress. The conference failed due to disagreements on minority issues. The First Round Table Conference (1930-31) was held without Congress participation, and the Third Round Table Conference (1932) was held in Gandhi's absence. The Lucknow Session of Congress (1916) was before the pact but is not the correct answer as it is not a Round Table Conference. Thus, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed prior to the Second Round Table Conference.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed? → 5 March 1931
☛ Which Round Table Conference did Gandhi attend? → Second Round Table Conference
☛ When was the First Round Table Conference held? → November 1930 to January 1931
☛ Which movement was withdrawn under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact? → Civil Disobedience Movement
☛ What pact was signed at the Lucknow Session (1916) between Congress and Muslim League? → Lucknow Pact

q: Who once remarked, "Nehru is a patriot, while Jinnah is a politician"?
qs.e: Mohammed Iqbal once remarked, 'Nehru is a patriot, while Jinnah is a politician.' He made this comment in the context of Indian politics. Iqbal was a renowned poet, philosopher, and politician who is credited with conceiving the idea of Pakistan. He is also known as Allama Iqbal. His poems, such as 'Sare Jahan se Achha', played a significant role in the Indian independence movement. He considered Nehru a loyal patriot and Jinnah a skilled politician. This statement reflects the political views of that era.
qs.kf:
☛ Who proposed the idea of Pakistan? → Allama Iqbal
☛ Which is the famous poem by Mohammed Iqbal? → Sare Jahan se Achha
☛ What did Iqbal say about Nehru and Jinnah? → Nehru is a patriot, Jinnah is a politician
☛ By what other name is Iqbal known? → Allama Iqbal
☛ In which fields was Mohammed Iqbal famous? → Poetry and philosophy

q: In which of following satyagraha's did Vallabh Bhai Patel get the title “Sardar”?
qs.e: In 1928, the Bardoli Satyagraha took place in the Bardoli region of Gujarat, led by Vallabhbhai Patel. The movement was against a 30% increase in land revenue imposed by the British government. Patel united the farmers and successfully led the non-violent protest based on the principles of swaraj. As a result, the government was forced to withdraw the revenue hike. Due to his exceptional leadership and organizational skills during this satyagraha, the women of Bardoli honored him with the title 'Sardar', which later became widely recognized across the nation.
qs.kf:
☛ Leader of Kheda Satyagraha (1918) → Gandhi and Sardar Patel
☛ Main objective of Bardoli Satyagraha → Opposition to revenue increase
☛ Who gave Sardar Patel the title 'Sardar' → Women of Bardoli
☛ Year of Bardoli Satyagraha → 1928
☛ Satyagraha where Sardar Patel got title 'Sardar' → Bardoli

q: In which annual session did the Indian National Congress proclaim commitment to ‘Purna Swaraj’ (complete independence)?
qs.e: The Indian National Congress, in its Lahore session in December 1929, passed the historic resolution demanding Purna Swaraj (complete independence). The session was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. On 26 January 1930, the first Independence Day was observed. This resolution marked a shift from the demand for dominion status to full independence. Earlier, the 1927 Madras session had focused on boycott and Swadeshi. The 1931 Karachi session is known for adopting the Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy resolution.
qs.kf:
☛ Who presided over the Lahore session of 1929? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ When was the Purna Swaraj resolution passed? → December 1929
☛ When was the first Independence Day celebrated? → 26 January 1930
☛ What was the slogan of the 1927 Madras session? → Preparation for Purna Swaraj
☛ What was adopted in the Karachi session (1931)? → Fundamental Rights and Economic Programme

q: Which Indian lady went to the 2nd Round Table Conference with Gandhiji?
qs.e: The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in 1931. Mahatma Gandhi attended as the representative of the Indian National Congress, and he was accompanied by Sarojini Naidu. She was a renowned poet and freedom fighter, known as the 'Nightingale of India'. She was the first Indian woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress (1925). At the conference, she advocated for women's rights and political representation. Sarojini Naidu was a close associate of Gandhi and participated in many movements like the Salt Satyagraha and Quit India Movement. Her role in the conference highlighted the contribution of Indian women in the freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Title of Sarojini Naidu → Nightingale of India
☛ First Indian woman Congress President → Sarojini Naidu (1925, Kanpur session)
☛ Year of Second Round Table Conference → 1931
☛ Woman who accompanied Gandhi to 2nd RTC → Sarojini Naidu
☛ Sarojini Naidu's political role → Freedom struggle, Salt Satyagraha, Quit India Movement

q: Which of the following is the correct chronology for these events?
A. Non Cooperation Movement
B. Chauri Chaura Incident
C. Quit India Movement
D. Civil Disobedience Movement
qs.e: The correct chronology is: Non Cooperation Movement (1920-22), Chauri Chaura Incident (Feb 1922), Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-34), and Quit India Movement (1942-45). The Non Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi but was withdrawn after the Chauri Chaura violence. Subsequently, the Civil Disobedience Movement began with the Salt Satyagraha. Finally, the Quit India Movement was launched with the slogan 'Do or Die'. This sequence represents the major events of India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Non Cooperation Movement started? → 1920
☛ When did Chauri Chaura incident occur? → February 1922
☛ What was the main event of Civil Disobedience Movement? → Salt Satyagraha (1930)
☛ What was the slogan of Quit India Movement? → Do or Die
☛ When was Quit India Movement launched? → 1942

q: Arrange the following events in their chronological order.
A. Jallianwala Bagh massacre B. Non-Cooperation Movement and Khilafat Movement C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact D. Quit India Movement E. Champaran Movement
qs.e: The correct chronological order is: Champaran Movement (1917), Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919), Non-Cooperation Movement and Khilafat Movement (1920-22), Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931), Quit India Movement (8 August 1942). Champaran was Gandhi's first successful satyagraha in India. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre led to the Non-Cooperation Movement against the Rowlatt Act. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact preceded the Second Round Table Conference. The Quit India Movement was the last major mass movement for Indian independence.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of Champaran Movement → 1917
☛ Date of Jallianwala Bagh massacre → 13 April 1919
☛ Duration of Non-Cooperation Movement → 1920-1922
☛ Date of Gandhi-Irwin Pact → 5 March 1931
☛ Date of Quit India Movement → 8 August 1942

q: Who gave M. K. Gandhi a title of Mahatma?
qs.e: The title 'Mahatma' was given to M. K. Gandhi by Rabindranath Tagore. Tagore, impressed by Gandhi's Satyagraha movement in South Africa, addressed him as 'Mahatma', meaning 'Great Soul'. This title symbolizes his spiritual greatness. Gandhi later led major movements in India like the Non-Cooperation Movement, Dandi March, and Quit India Movement. Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet, writer, and the first Asian Nobel laureate. He praised Gandhi's simplicity and sacrifice by calling him 'Mahatma' instead of just 'Gandhi'.
qs.kf:
☛ Rabindranath Tagore's notable work → Gitanjali
☛ Tagore's Nobel Prize year → 1913
☛ Year Gandhi was called Mahatma → 1915
☛ Gandhi's movement in South Africa → Satyagraha
☛ Gandhi's autobiography → The Story of My Experiments with Truth

q: Who among the following organized the “Red Shirts” movement?
qs.e: Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan, also known as 'Frontier Gandhi', organized the 'Red Shirts' movement in the North-West Frontier Province (now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa). This movement, also called 'Khudai Khidmatgar' (Servants of God), involved members wearing red shirts. It was a non-violent independence movement that emphasized non-violence and civil disobedience against British rule. Gaffar Khan was a staunch follower of Mahatma Gandhi and taught the Pathans the principles of non-violence. He was a member of the Indian National Congress, and the movement gained significant prominence in the 1930s.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Khudai Khidmatgar? → Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan
☛ In which province did the Red Shirts movement take place? → North-West Frontier Province (NWFP)
☛ By which nickname is Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan known? → Frontier Gandhi
☛ What is the literal meaning of Khudai Khidmatgar? → Servants of God
☛ To which political party did Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan belong? → Indian National Congress

q: Which movement is called India's first Civil Disobedience Movement?
qs.e: The Champaran Movement (1917) is regarded as India's first Civil Disobedience Movement. It was led by Mahatma Gandhi in the Champaran district of Bihar against the forced indigo cultivation system (Tinkathia system). This movement was an early example of non-violent resistance and civil disobedience. Gandhi raised his voice against the exploitation of local farmers and compelled the government to revise the regulations. This movement gave Gandhi national recognition and laid the foundation of civil disobedience in the Indian freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first Civil Disobedience Movement → Champaran Movement (1917)
☛ Leadership → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Cause → Against forced indigo cultivation (Tinkathia system)
☛ Location → Champaran district, Bihar
☛ Result → Formation of Indigo Commission and end of exploitation

q: The Cabinet Mission sent to India in 1946 by the British Government comprised of ________ members.
qs.e: The Cabinet Mission sent to India in 1946 by the British Government comprised of three members. The mission was led by Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade), and A.V. Alexander (First Lord of the Admiralty). Its objective was to negotiate with Indian leaders for the formation of a Constituent Assembly and a plan for power transfer. On 16 May 1946, the mission proposed a plan dividing provinces into three groups and forming a federal government. This mission was a crucial step towards Indian independence.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the chairman of the Cabinet Mission? → Lord Pethick-Lawrence
☛ When did the Cabinet Mission arrive? → 1946
☛ What was the purpose of the Cabinet Mission? → To discuss the formation of the Indian Constituent Assembly
☛ When did the Cabinet Mission present its plan? → 16 May 1946
☛ Which of the following was not a member of the Cabinet Mission? → Lord Wavell (Viceroy, not a member)

q: August Kranti is also known as the _______ Movement.
qs.e: August Kranti is also known as the Quit India Movement. This movement was launched on 8 August 1942 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. Its objective was to end British rule in India. Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' during this movement. The movement was started during World War II when Britain was engaged in the war. It was passed at the All India Congress Committee session in Mumbai. During the movement, many leaders were arrested and nationwide protests took place.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Quit India Movement start? → 8 August 1942
☛ What was the slogan of the Quit India Movement? → Do or Die
☛ Where was the Quit India Movement resolution passed? → Mumbai session
☛ Who led the Quit India Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ What is the other name of the Quit India Movement? → August Kranti

q: When did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi went to South Africa in 1893, where he led the Satyagraha movement for the rights of Indians. He stayed in South Africa for nearly 21 years and left in 1914, arriving at Mumbai port on January 9, 1915. This day is celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas (Non-Resident Indian Day). After his return, Gopal Krishna Gokhale guided him and introduced him to Indian politics. Gandhi's return was significant as he soon led movements like the Champaran Satyagraha (1917) and Kheda Satyagraha (1918), which marked his entry into India's freedom struggle. His time in South Africa had shaped his philosophy of non-violence and civil disobedience, which he later applied in India.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Gandhi go to South Africa? → 1893
☛ When did Gandhi start his first Satyagraha in South Africa? → 1906
☛ How many years did Gandhi spend in South Africa? → About 21 years
☛ When is Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas celebrated in India? → January 9
☛ Where did Gandhi start his first Satyagraha in India? → Champaran (Bihar)

q: Who was the second person who joined individual satyagraha movement in 1940?
qs.e: The Individual Satyagraha movement started by Mahatma Gandhi in 1940 aimed at individual protests against the war. The first satyagrahi was Vinoba Bhave, chosen by Gandhi. The second satyagrahi was Jawahar Lal Nehru, who gave anti-war speeches across villages on 7 November 1940 and was arrested. This movement was a significant phase of nonviolent resistance, allowing individuals to protest separately. It increased public awareness against British rule and strengthened the Indian freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Individual Satyagraha start? → 1940
☛ Who was the first individual satyagrahi? → Vinoba Bhave
☛ Who was the second individual satyagrahi? → Jawahar Lal Nehru
☛ Who started Individual Satyagraha? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ What was the main aim of Individual Satyagraha? → Opposing World War II

q: The demand for Pakistan was made in ______ at Lahore Session of the Muslim League.
qs.e: The Lahore Session of the All India Muslim League was held on 23 March 1940, where the formal demand for Pakistan was made. The session was presided over by Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The Lahore Resolution passed at this session proposed the creation of an independent state for Muslims in the north-western and eastern regions of India. Later, this resolution came to be known as the Pakistan Resolution. This event marked a turning point in the Indian independence movement and laid the foundation for the partition of India and the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Lahore Resolution passed? → 1940
☛ Who presided over the Lahore Session? → Muhammad Ali Jinnah
☛ What is the other name for the Pakistan Resolution? → Lahore Resolution
☛ Where was the Lahore Session held? → Lahore, at Minto Park (now Iqbal Park)
☛ What did the Lahore Resolution demand? → Independent state for Muslim-majority areas

name: Set 5 · Q197–245
sub: Modern History - Gandhian Era (Non-Cooperation to Quit India)

q: Who led the march to raid the Dharasana salt works after Gandhiji was arrested?
qs.e: After Gandhiji's arrest, Abbas Tyabji led the march to raid the Dharasana salt works, continuing the salt satyagraha. This event took place on 21 May 1930. Abbas Tyabji was a prominent freedom fighter and a close associate of Gandhiji. The march included notable figures like Sarojini Naidu and Manilal Gandhi. The Dharasana raid was a crucial phase of the civil disobedience movement, symbolizing defiance against the British salt laws. The brutal lathi charge on the peaceful protesters garnered international attention to the Indian independence struggle. This act of nonviolent resistance highlighted the determination of Indian nationalists.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Dharasana salt works raid march? → Abbas Tyabji
☛ When did the Dharasana raid take place? → 21 May 1930
☛ Which woman participated in the Dharasana march? → Sarojini Naidu
☛ When was Gandhiji arrested during the salt satyagraha? → 5 May 1930
☛ Which city was Abbas Tyabji associated with? → Vadodara

q: The Chauri Chaura incident resulted in the abrupt closure of the:
qs.e: The Chauri Chaura incident occurred on February 4, 1922, in the Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh, where protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. Deeply disturbed by this violence, Mahatma Gandhi abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement on February 12, 1922. The movement had begun in September 1920 with the aim of peacefully resisting British rule through boycotting government institutions. The violence at Chauri Chaura violated Gandhi's principle of non-violence, leading to the withdrawal of the movement. This incident marked a significant turning point in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Chauri Chaura incident occur? → February 4, 1922
☛ How many policemen were killed in the incident? → 22
☛ Which movement was withdrawn due to this incident? → Non-Cooperation Movement
☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement start? → September 1920
☛ Who was the leader of the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi

q: Chronologically, which of the following events in course of the Indian freedom struggle, happened first?
qs.e: The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre occurred on April 13, 1919, while the Non-Cooperation Movement started in 1920, the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930, and the Quit India Movement in 1942. This event highlighted the oppressive nature of British rule and accelerated the national movement. General Dyer ordered firing on unarmed civilians, killing hundreds. The massacre sparked nationwide outrage and led Gandhiji to launch the Non-Cooperation Movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Jallianwala Bagh Massacre → 13 April 1919
☛ General Dyer associated with → Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
☛ First Non-Cooperation Movement started → 1920
☛ Year of Civil Disobedience Movement → 1930
☛ Quit India Movement launched → 1942

q: In which year was the satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act called by Mahatma Gandhi?
qs.e: The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919, which gave the government the power to arrest any person without trial. Mahatma Gandhi called for a nationwide strike against this act. This movement is known as the Rowlatt Satyagraha. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919, which is a significant event linked to this satyagraha. Gandhi ji observed a nationwide protest day on 6 April 1919. This satyagraha gave a new direction to the Indian freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Rowlatt Act passed? → 1919
☛ Which tragic event occurred during the Rowlatt Satyagraha? → Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919)
☛ Who was the main leader opposing the Rowlatt Act? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Which movement started after the Rowlatt Satyagraha? → Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)
☛ What was the full name of the Rowlatt Act? → Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919

q: In 1930, at which place did Gandhi ji break the salt law?
qs.e: In 1930, Mahatma Gandhi broke the salt law at Dandi as part of the Salt Satyagraha. He started the march from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March and reached Dandi on 6 April, where he picked up natural salt, defying the British monopoly. This act sparked a wave of civil disobedience across India, mobilizing millions against colonial rule. The Dandi March was a pivotal event in India's freedom struggle, symbolizing peaceful resistance against unjust laws. It inspired nationwide participation and put pressure on the British government.
qs.kf:
☛ Leader of Salt Satyagraha → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Starting point → Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad
☛ End point → Dandi, Gujarat
☛ Date of breaking salt law → 6 April 1930
☛ Movement's purpose → Break salt law and launch civil disobedience

q: Who was the first President of the Swaraj Party in 1922-23?
qs.e: The Swaraj Party was founded on January 1, 1923, by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru. Its formation was a result of the differences between the Pro-changers and No-changers within the Indian National Congress after the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement. The party aimed to enter the legislative councils and challenge the government from within. Chittaranjan Das was the first President of the Swaraj Party, while Motilal Nehru served as its Secretary. The party achieved significant success in the 1923 elections, emerging as the largest party in the Central Legislative Assembly. This party is considered one of the earliest experiments in parliamentary politics in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Founders of Swaraj Party → Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru
☛ Date of formation of Swaraj Party → January 1, 1923
☛ Main objective of Swaraj Party → Enter legislatures and oppose the government
☛ First Secretary of Swaraj Party → Motilal Nehru
☛ Result of Swaraj Party → Became the largest party in 1923 elections

q: Who asked Gandhi to pay attention to the problems of farmers in Champaran?
qs.e: The Champaran Satyagraha was a landmark event in India's freedom struggle. In 1917, a peasant named Rajkumar Shukla (also known as Prince Shukla) met Mahatma Gandhi and apprised him of the miserable condition of farmers cultivating indigo in Champaran. Gandhi agreed to his request and arrived in Champaran, where he studied the farmers' problems and led the satyagraha against the British. This was Gandhi's first successful satyagraha movement in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Leader of Champaran Satyagraha → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Problem of farmers in Champaran → Tinkathia system of indigo cultivation
☛ Year of Champaran Satyagraha → 1917
☛ Person who invited Gandhi → Rajkumar Shukla (Prince Shukla)
☛ Outcome of Champaran Satyagraha → Formation of Indigo Commission and relief to farmers

q: When was the Gandhi-Irwin pact carried out?
qs.e: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin. Under this pact, the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn, and Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference. The pact included the release of political prisoners, relaxation of salt laws, and return of confiscated property. However, the pact proved short-lived as the British government did not fulfill its promises. This agreement was a significant phase in the Indian freedom movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Gandhi-Irwin Pact → 5 March 1931
☛ Key points of the pact → Withdrawal of Civil Disobedience, release of political prisoners
☛ Which conference did Gandhi attend due to this pact → Second Round Table Conference
☛ Other name of Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Delhi Pact
☛ Viceroy at the time of pact → Lord Irwin

q: Who was invited by Lord Wavell to form the interim Government in India in 1946?
qs.e: In 1946, Lord Wavell invited Jawaharlal Nehru to form the interim Government in India. This decision was taken under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. The Cabinet Mission recommended the formation of a Constituent Assembly and an interim government. Lord Wavell invited Nehru, as the leader of the Congress, to become the Prime Minister of the interim government. Nehru formed the interim government on 2 September 1946. This government included prominent leaders of the Congress. The Muslim League initially refused to join but later joined in October 1946. The interim government functioned until India's independence in August 1947.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the Prime Minister of the interim government? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ When was the interim government formed? → 2 September 1946
☛ When did the Cabinet Mission come to India? → 1946
☛ When did the Muslim League join the interim government? → October 1946
☛ What was Lord Wavell's tenure? → 1943-1947

q: Which day was observed as 'Swaraj Day' in Indian history?
qs.e: In Indian history, January 26, 1930 was observed as 'Swaraj Day'. On this day, the Indian National Congress declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) from British rule. This followed the Lahore Session of 1929, where the resolution for complete independence was passed. The first hoisting of the tricolor flag took place on this day across India. Later, this date was chosen for the enactment of the Constitution on Republic Day (January 26, 1950). August 14, 1947 is Pakistan's Independence Day, and August 15, 1947 is India's Independence Day. January 26, 1950 marks the adoption of the Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Swaraj Day observed? → January 26, 1930
☛ Which session passed the Purna Swaraj resolution? → Lahore Session (1929)
☛ When was the tricolor first hoisted? → January 26, 1930
☛ When is India's Republic Day? → January 26, 1950
☛ What is India's Independence Day? → August 15, 1947

q: In which of the following years was the first round table conference held?
qs.e: The first Round Table Conference was held from 12 November 1930 to 19 January 1931 in London. Its purpose was to discuss constitutional reforms in India. The conference was chaired by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. The Indian National Congress did not participate as its leaders were in jail. Three Round Table Conferences were held: first in 1930-31, second in 1931, and third in 1932. The first conference included participants from the Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha, and other parties. It paved the way for the Gandhi-Irwin Pact later.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first Round Table Conference held? → 1930
☛ Where were the Round Table Conferences held? → London
☛ Who chaired the first Round Table Conference? → Ramsay MacDonald
☛ Which organization boycotted the first Round Table Conference? → Indian National Congress
☛ How many Round Table Conferences were held? → Three

q: The signatories of the Poona Pact were the Mahatma Gandhi Group and the _________.
qs.e: The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. This agreement was reached after Gandhi's fast unto death against the Communal Award (1932). Under the pact, separate electorates for the depressed classes were replaced by reserved seats. It provided increased representation for the depressed classes in the provincial legislatures and also reserved seats in the central legislature. The Poona Pact was a significant milestone in Indian politics, bridging the differences between Gandhi and Ambedkar's approaches to the welfare of the depressed classes.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Poona Pact → 24 September 1932
☛ Signatories of the Pact → Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Outcome of the Pact → Reserved seats for depressed classes, no separate electorates
☛ Gandhi's fast → At Yerwada Jail against the Communal Award
☛ Impact of the Pact → Increased representation for depressed classes in provincial assemblies

q: The Khilafat Movement (Group) was launched to protest against which of the following?
qs.e: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was launched by Indian Muslims to protest the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire and the weakening of the Caliphate's position after World War I. It was led by Maulana Muhammad Ali, Shaukat Ali, and Abul Kalam Azad. Mahatma Gandhi linked it with the Non-Cooperation Movement to strengthen Hindu-Muslim unity. The movement ended in 1924 when Mustafa Kemal Pasha abolished the Caliphate in Turkey.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Khilafat Movement? → Maulana Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali
☛ Which movement was linked to Khilafat by Gandhi? → Non-Cooperation Movement
☛ Which treaty partitioned the Ottoman Empire? → Treaty of Sevres (1920)
☛ When did the Khilafat Movement end? → 1924
☛ Who abolished the Caliphate in Turkey? → Mustafa Kemal Pasha

q: The first parallel government, following the Quit India Movement, was established in which city?
qs.e: During the Quit India Movement in 1942, the first parallel government was established in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh. This government, led by Chittu Pandey, lasted for about a week. Subsequently, in 1943, a parallel government was formed in Satara, Maharashtra, which lasted much longer. Talchar in Odisha also saw a temporary parallel government. These parallel governments symbolized the people's resistance against British rule. The Ballia government is also referred to as 'Ballia Raj'.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the first parallel government established after Quit India Movement? → Ballia
☛ Who led the Ballia parallel government? → Chittu Pandey
☛ When was the parallel government established in Satara? → 1943
☛ Who led the Satara parallel government? → Nana Patil
☛ How long did the Ballia parallel government last? → About one week

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which leader collaborated with Mahatma Gandhi during the Kheda Satyagraha in 1918?
qs.e: In 1918, due to crop failure in the Kheda district of Gujarat, the British refused to grant remission of land revenue. Mahatma Gandhi, along with Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, led a satyagraha against this injustice. This was Gandhi's first major satyagraha where he used nonviolent tax resistance. Patel organized the peasants and ensured the movement's success. Eventually, the government had to provide relief. This satyagraha laid the foundation for the long partnership between Gandhi and Patel in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Main objective of Kheda Satyagraha → To obtain remission of land revenue
☛ Year of Kheda Satyagraha → 1918
☛ Sardar Patel's role in Kheda movement → Organizing the peasants
☛ Gandhi's first satyagraha was → Champaran Satyagraha (1917)
☛ Which tax was protested in Kheda Satyagraha? → Land revenue

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Who signed the Poona Pact of 1932 on behalf of Mahatma Gandhi, as he was imprisoned at the time?
qs.e: In 1932, Mahatma Gandhi was imprisoned in Yerwada Jail, so Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya signed the Poona Pact on his behalf. This pact was an agreement between Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and the Congress, providing for reserved seats for the depressed classes instead of separate electorates. It modified the Communal Award announced by the British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. Malviya ji was the founder of Banaras Hindu University and a prominent nationalist leader. The Poona Pact was concluded on 24 September 1932 and ensured political representation for the Dalits without separate electorates.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Poona Pact signed? → 24 September 1932
☛ Who were the main signatories? → Dr. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi (represented by Malviya)
☛ What was provided for the depressed classes? → Reserved seats, not separate electorates
☛ Who gave the Communal Award? → British PM Ramsay MacDonald
☛ After which event did the Poona Pact happen? → Second Round Table Conference

q: Which prominent Indian leader led the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928, a major civil disobedience movement against increased land taxes?
qs.e: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was a major civil disobedience movement against increased land taxes imposed by the British government. It was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who organized the peasants to refuse tax payment. The movement forced the government to withdraw the tax hike, and Patel earned the title 'Sardar' for his leadership. This satyagraha was inspired by Gandhi's non-cooperation movement. Prior to this, Patel had also led the mill workers' strike in Ahmedabad. The success of Bardoli established civil disobedience as an effective tool in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Bardoli Satyagraha? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ When did Bardoli Satyagraha take place? → 1928
☛ What was Bardoli Satyagraha against? → Increased land taxes
☛ What title did Patel earn after Bardoli? → 'Sardar'
☛ Which movement inspired Bardoli Satyagraha? → Non-cooperation movement

q: The aim of the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1929 was
o: Complete disobedience of the orders of the British Government.
Partial disobedience of the orders of the British Government.
To ensure all civil rights of the citizens are granted by the Government.
qs.e: At the 1929 Lahore Congress session, the goal of 'Purna Swaraj' was declared. Consequently, on 12 March 1930, Gandhi started the Dandi March, marking the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Its objective was complete non-cooperation with British rule and deliberate defiance of laws, aiming to force the British to leave India. The Chauri Chaura incident occurred in 1922, after which the Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn. Civil Disobedience demanded complete, not partial, disobedience of British orders. The movement was not merely about civil rights but about complete independence.
qs.kf:
☛ 1929 Lahore Congress Session → Passed resolution for Purna Swaraj
☛ Slogan of Civil Disobedience Movement → 'Simon Commission Go Back'
☛ Date of Dandi March → 12 March 1930
☛ Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Signed on 5 March 1931
☛ Second Round Table Conference → Held in London in 1931

q: Mahatma Gandhi started the famous ‘Salt March’ from Sabarmati to Dandi. In which district of Gujarat is Dandi?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi started the famous Salt March from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi on March 12, 1930, as a protest against the British salt monopoly. Dandi is a coastal village located in the Navsari district of Gujarat. The march lasted 24 days, covering 240 miles, and ended on April 6, 1930, when Gandhi broke the salt law by making salt at Dandi. This event was a pivotal moment in the Indian independence movement, inspiring widespread civil disobedience. Navsari district is situated in southern Gujarat and its headquarters is Navsari city.
qs.kf:
☛ Salt March start date → March 12, 1930 from Sabarmati
☛ Dandi district → Navsari, Gujarat
☛ Purpose of Salt March → Protest against British salt tax
☛ Gandhi broke salt law at Dandi → April 6, 1930
☛ Navsari district headquarters → Navsari city

q: What is correct about the Khilafat Movement in India?
o: It was a movement in demand of Pakistan
It was a movement in support of the Turkish Sultan
It was a movement to restore the Mughal Royal family in India
It was a movement against the massacre of Jallianwala Bagh
qs.e: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) in India was launched in support of the Caliph (Sultan) of Turkey, who was losing his position after the defeat in World War I. Indian Muslims considered the Caliph as a symbol of Islamic unity and mobilized to protect him. Key leaders were Maulana Mohammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali (the Ali brothers). Mahatma Gandhi linked it to the Non-Cooperation Movement, but after Mustafa Kemal Pasha abolished the Caliphate in 1924, the movement faded. This movement was not related to the demand for Pakistan, restoration of the Mughal Empire, or the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the main objective of the Khilafat Movement? → To protect the Caliph of Turkey
☛ Who were the prominent leaders of the Khilafat Movement? → Maulana Mohammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali
☛ Which movement did Gandhi link to the Khilafat Movement? → Non-Cooperation Movement
☛ When did the Khilafat Movement end? → In 1924 after Turkey abolished the Caliphate
☛ Which event played a decisive role in the Khilafat Movement? → Abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Pasha

q: Who represented the Congress in the second round table conference held in London?
qs.e: The second Round Table Conference was held in London in 1931. The Indian National Congress decided to participate and sent Mahatma Gandhi as its sole representative. Gandhi raised issues like untouchability and communal representation. He was the only Congress delegate at the conference. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar represented the depressed classes. Gandhi strongly opposed the Communal Award, which later led to the Poona Pact. The second Round Table Conference failed because no agreement could be reached between Gandhi and the British government on key issues.
qs.kf:
☛ Who represented Congress in the second Round Table Conference? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Did Congress participate in the first Round Table Conference? → No
☛ Who represented the depressed classes in the second Round Table Conference? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ When was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed? → 1931
☛ When was the Poona Pact signed? → 1932

q: Which of the following freedom fighters was a co-founder of Swaraj Party along with Motilal Nehru?
qs.e: The Swaraj Party was founded in 1923 by Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das. It emerged as a faction within the Indian National Congress that believed in working inside the legislature to oppose British rule. The party aimed to enter provincial and central assemblies to obstruct the British government. Chittaranjan Das was a prominent lawyer and nationalist leader who led revolutionary activities in Bengal. The Swaraj Party performed well in the 1923 elections and played a significant role within the Congress.
qs.kf:
☛ Who were the founders of Swaraj Party? → Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das
☛ When was Swaraj Party founded? → 1923
☛ What was the main aim of Swaraj Party? → To oppose British rule from within the legislature
☛ Which region was Chittaranjan Das associated with? → Bengal
☛ After which movement was Swaraj Party formed? → After the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement

q: AICC (All India Congress Committee) passed the Quit India Resolution on:
qs.e: The All India Congress Committee (AICC) passed the historic Quit India Resolution on August 8, 1942, at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay. The resolution demanded an immediate end to British rule in India and gave the call 'Do or Die'. Led by Mahatma Gandhi, this movement witnessed massive participation from the masses. The British promptly arrested Gandhi and other leaders, but the movement continued. This was a crucial turning point in the Indian freedom struggle, marking a shift from constitutional methods to mass civil disobedience.
qs.kf:
☛ In which session was the Quit India Resolution passed? → Bombay session (1942)
☛ What was the slogan of the Quit India Movement? → Do or Die
☛ Who moved the Quit India Resolution? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Who was the Viceroy during the Quit India Movement? → Lord Linlithgow
☛ When did the Quit India Movement begin? → August 9, 1942

q: During which of the following movements did Mahatma Gandhi give the slogan 'Do or Die'?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' on August 8, 1942 at Gwalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai. This slogan marked the beginning of the Quit India Movement, also known as the August Revolution. The movement demanded an immediate end to British rule. Gandhi urged Indians to engage in a non-violent but decisive struggle. The movement was launched after the failure of the Cripps Mission. As a result, Gandhi and many other leaders were arrested. This was the largest mass movement in the Indian freedom struggle.

☛ Other name of the movement → August Revolution

☛ Slogan given by Gandhi during the movement → Do or Die

q: The Satyagraha Sabha was founded in February 1919 by:
qs.e: The Satyagraha Sabha was founded in February 1919 by Mahatma Gandhi to protest against the Rowlatt Act. This act gave the British government the power to arrest any Indian without trial, which Gandhi considered unjust and oppressive. The main objective of the Satyagraha Sabha was to organize non-violent resistance and civil disobedience against this law. The movement marked a significant turning point in the Indian freedom struggle. The Satyagraha Sabha later laid the foundation for the Non-Cooperation Movement. Through this organization, Gandhi mobilized the masses and united them against British rule.
qs.kf:

q: The slogan 'Aaram Haraam Hai' was given by______________.
qs.e: The slogan 'Aaram Haraam Hai' was given by Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India. It means 'rest is forbidden' and conveys a message of hard work and discipline. Nehru used this slogan to inspire citizens to avoid laziness and contribute to nation-building. It was frequently mentioned in his speeches and remains motivational even today.

q: Who founded Natal Indian Congress to fight against racial discrimination?
qs.e: The Natal Indian Congress was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1894 in South Africa. Its aim was to fight against racial discrimination and unjust laws targeting the Indian community. Gandhi, who was working as a lawyer in South Africa, adopted the path of satyagraha and non-violent protest to protect the rights of Indians. This organization later became a foundation for the Indian independence movement.

q: Against which Act did Gandhiji decide to fight and start a Satyagraha?
qs.e: Gandhiji decided to start a Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act passed in 1919. This act gave the British government the power to arrest and detain any Indian without trial, making it a repressive law. Gandhiji saw it as an attack on civil liberties and launched the Non-Cooperation Movement. The act's opposition led to the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre on April 13, 1919. The Rowlatt Satyagraha marked a turning point in India's freedom struggle, spreading awareness nationwide.

q: What did the Champaran movement protest against?
o: Financial atrocities by the British government
Extra taxation by the land lords
qs.e: The Champaran movement in 1917 was led by Mahatma Gandhi in the Champaran district of Bihar. It was a protest against the forced cultivation of indigo, where British landlords compelled farmers to grow indigo and paid them very low prices. Witnessing the plight of the farmers, Gandhi launched a satyagraha, which eventually forced the government to abolish the compulsory cultivation of indigo. This was Gandhi's first successful civil disobedience movement in India.

q: Who among the following was the Viceroy of India when Gandhiji led the Dandi March?
qs.e: The Dandi March, also known as the 'Salt Satyagraha', began on 12 March 1930 and ended on 6 April 1930. At that time, the Viceroy of India was Lord Irwin. Lord Irwin served as Viceroy from 1926 to 1931. Gandhi led a 241-mile march from Ahmedabad to Dandi to break the British salt law. Following this, Lord Irwin signed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact with Gandhi in 1931, which included agreement to participate in the Second Round Table Conference. q: Where was Mahatma Gandhi during independence day celebration on 15th August 1947?
qs.e: On 15th August 1947, during the independence day celebrations, Mahatma Gandhi was not in Delhi but in Kolkata (formerly Calcutta). He was staying at a Muslim family's house in the Beliaghata area. Gandhi was focused on curbing the violence caused by the Partition and Hindu-Muslim riots. He did not give any speech on independence day but instead held prayer meetings for peace and communal harmony. He was engaged in peace efforts following the Noakhali riots. Gandhi observed the day with fasting and prayers.
qs.kf:

☛ When did Noakhali riots occur? → 1946
☛ Purpose of Gandhi's 1947 Kolkata visit? → Restore communal harmony

q: Which of the following facts about the 'Dandi March' is NOT true?
o: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi.
The volunteers used to travel 25 miles per day.
qs.e: The Dandi March started from Sabarmati Ashram on March 12, 1930, and ended on April 6, 1930, at Dandi, lasting 24 days. It was led by Mahatma Gandhi and began with 78 volunteers. However, the volunteers traveled approximately 10-12 miles per day, not 25 miles. The march was organized as a protest against the British salt tax and was a pivotal event in the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the total distance of the Dandi March? → 241 miles (388 km)
☛ Which tax was the Dandi March opposing? → Salt tax
☛ Who led the Dandi March? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ How many volunteers started the Dandi March? → 78
☛ When did the Dandi March start and end? → March 12, 1930 to April 6, 1930

q: On whose death, Jawaharlal Nehru said "The light went away from our lives"?
qs.e: After the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi on 30 January 1948, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru addressed the nation on All India Radio, saying, "The light has gone out of our lives and darkness is all around." This speech reflects Nehru's deep reverence for Gandhi and the profound grief caused by his death. Gandhi was the preeminent leader of the Indian independence movement and a champion of non-violence. His principles influenced not only India but the entire world. Nehru's words highlighted the significance of Gandhi's guidance and the void created by his absence. The phrase remains iconic, symbolizing the nation's collective loss and the enduring legacy of Mahatma Gandhi.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Mahatma Gandhi assassinated? → 30 January 1948
☛ Who called Gandhi 'Father of the Nation'? → Subhash Chandra Bose
☛ Gandhi's birthday is celebrated as? → International Day of Non-Violence
☛ Who assassinated Mahatma Gandhi? → Nathuram Godse
☛ Where did Nehru give the speech on Gandhi's death? → All India Radio

q: Mahatma Gandhi started his famous 'Salt march' accompanied by _________ of his trusted volunteers.
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi started the Dandi March (Salt March) from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 accompanied by 78 trusted volunteers. The march lasted 24 days and covered 240 miles, ending at Dandi on 6 April 1930, where Gandhi broke the salt law. This act was a key part of the Civil Disobedience Movement against British rule. The march united people across India and gave a new direction to the freedom struggle. The volunteers included people from different castes and communities, symbolizing national unity.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Salt March start? → 12 March 1930
☛ Where did the Salt March end? → Dandi
☛ Which movement was the Salt March part of? → Civil Disobedience Movement
☛ When did Gandhi break the salt law? → 6 April 1930
☛ How many volunteers accompanied Gandhi in the Salt March? → 78

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 1
q: What was the main reason for the protest against the Simon Commission in 1928?
qs.e: The Simon Commission was sent to India in 1928 to review constitutional reforms. However, it faced widespread protests because the commission had no Indian members. Indians saw this as a violation of their right to self-determination and an insult to their nationality. The slogan 'Simon Go Back' became popular. During a protest in Lahore, Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured in a police lathi charge. This protest marked a significant phase in the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the chairman of the Simon Commission? → Sir John Simon
☛ When did the Simon Commission arrive in India? → 1928
☛ What was the slogan against the Simon Commission? → Simon Go Back
☛ Which leader died during the Simon Commission protest? → Lala Lajpat Rai
☛ What was the main reason for protesting the Simon Commission? → No Indian members

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1
q: What were ‘privy purses’?
o: Pensions paid to the princes after integration
qs.e: 'Privy purses' were annual pensions paid to the rulers of princely states after their integration into India. This arrangement, made after independence in 1947, allowed the rulers to retain their titles and certain privileges. The privy purses were abolished in 1971 by the 26th Constitutional Amendment, which also ended the special status of the princely states. This move was led by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. The amendment removed Articles 291 and 362 from the Constitution, which had granted these privileges.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was given privy purses? → Rulers of princely states
☛ When were privy purses abolished? → In 1971 by the 26th Amendment
☛ Which PM abolished privy purses? → Indira Gandhi
☛ Which articles were related to privy purses? → Articles 291 and 362
☛ Who was the architect of integration of princely states? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Why did Mahatma Gandhi travel to Noakhali in 1946?
o: To support the Bengal famine victims
To organise the Quit India Movement
To lead a protest against British rule
To promote communal harmony after religious violence
qs.e: In 1946, after Hindu-Muslim riots broke out in Noakhali (present-day Bangladesh), Mahatma Gandhi traveled there to restore communal harmony. He walked through villages, visiting affected areas and urging people to embrace peace. This journey occurred just before India's partition, when communal tensions were at their peak. Gandhi emphasized non-violence and brotherhood throughout his campaign. The Noakhali visit symbolizes his deep commitment to communal unity. During this time, he also undertook fasts to encourage people to adopt peace. This event is considered a significant chapter in Gandhi's life, showcasing his efforts to heal religious divides through personal sacrifice and dialogue.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Noakhali riots occur? → 1946
☛ Why did Gandhi travel to Noakhali? → After communal violence
☛ What method did Gandhi use in Noakhali? → Non-violent resistance
☛ In which country is Noakhali located today? → Bangladesh
☛ How long did Gandhi stay in Noakhali? → About 4 months

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after the violent incident at Chauri Chaura. In which present-day state is Chauri Chaura located?
qs.e: Chauri Chaura is located in the Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh. The incident occurred on 4 February 1922, when during the Non-Cooperation Movement, protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. After this violent event, Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement, emphasizing the principle of non-violence. The Chauri Chaura incident was a turning point in the Indian freedom struggle, strengthening Gandhi's leadership and the strategy of non-violent resistance. It demonstrated the challenges of maintaining non-violence in mass movements and led to a shift in tactics for the independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Chauri Chaura incident occur? → 4 February 1922
☛ In which district is Chauri Chaura located? → Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh
☛ When was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched? → 1920
☛ What was the main reason for the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Jallianwala Bagh massacre and Rowlatt Act
☛ When did Gandhi call off the Non-Cooperation Movement? → After the Chauri Chaura incident (1922)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Who was honoured with the title 'Assam Kesari' for his courageous role in the Indian freedom movement?
qs.e: Ambikagiri Raichoudhury was honoured with the title 'Assam Kesari' (Lion of Assam) for his courageous role in the Indian freedom movement. He was a prominent freedom fighter, poet, writer, and musician from Assam. He played a vital role in the renaissance of Assamese literature and culture. He was associated with organizations like the Assam Association and the Assam Student Conference. He published the magazine 'Chetana' and actively participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement. His works inspired national consciousness among the Assamese people.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is called Assam Kesari? → Ambikagiri Raichoudhury
☛ Who gave the title Assam Kesari? → The people of Assam
☛ Famous magazine of Ambikagiri Raichoudhury? → Chetana
☛ Father of Assamese literature renaissance? → Ambikagiri Raichoudhury
☛ Prominent leader of Quit India Movement in Assam? → Ambikagiri Raichoudhury

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Hunger strike as a weapon was used for the first time by Mahatma Gandhi during which struggle?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi used hunger strike as a weapon for the first time in 1918 during the Ahmedabad mill workers' struggle. The struggle was for a wage increase and reduction in working hours. Gandhi mediated between the workers and mill owners, and when the mill owners refused to agree, he began a fast. After three days of hunger strike, the mill owners agreed to the demands. This was Gandhi's first hunger strike, and he later used it as a non-violent weapon in the freedom movement. The purpose of the hunger strike was to create peaceful pressure and achieve justice.
qs.kf:
☛ When and where did Mahatma Gandhi undertake his first hunger strike? → 1918, Ahmedabad Mill Workers' Struggle
☛ What was the main issue of the Ahmedabad Mill Workers' Struggle? → Wage increase and reduction in work hours
☛ What type of weapon is a hunger strike? → Non-violent protest
☛ When did Gandhi start the Champaran Satyagraha? → 1917
☛ In which year did the Kheda Satyagraha occur? → 1918

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Rowlatt Act, which was introduced by the British government to curb political dissent in India?
o: Arrest of political leaders without warrants
qs.e: The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919 by the British government to curb political dissent in India. Its provisions included arrest without warrant, detention without trial, and censorship of the press. However, restrictions on freedom of expression were not a specific provision of this Act; such restrictions were imposed through other ordinances or laws. The Act gave extensive powers to the police, but it did not directly target freedom of speech. The Rowlatt Act faced widespread opposition from Indian leaders, leading to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and eventually the Non-Cooperation Movement.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Rowlatt Act passed? → 1919
☛ What was the main purpose of the Rowlatt Act? → To curb political dissent
☛ Who led the movement against the Rowlatt Act? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ When did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occur? → 13 April 1919
☛ Which movement started due to the Rowlatt Act? → Non-Cooperation Movement

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the Round Table Conferences held from 1930 to 1932? (a) The Round Table Conferences were held to discuss Constitutional Reforms and India's future government under British rule. (b) Mahatma Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference in 1931.
qs.e: The Round Table Conferences were held in London between 1930 and 1932 to discuss constitutional reforms and the future government of India under British rule. The first conference (1930) was boycotted by the Indian National Congress. The second conference (1931) was attended by Mahatma Gandhi as the sole representative of Congress. However, due to disagreements over minority issues, Gandhi returned without any outcome. The third conference (1932) was again boycotted by Congress. Thus, both statements (a) and (b) are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the First Round Table Conference held? → 1930
☛ Who attended the Second Round Table Conference? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Which conference did Gandhi not attend? → First and Third
☛ What was the purpose of the Round Table Conferences? → Discuss constitutional reforms
☛ The Gandhi-Irwin Pact is related to which conference? → Second Round Table Conference

q: What title did the British confer Gandhi with, which was relinquished by him?
qs.e: The British government conferred the title of Kaiser-e-Hind (meaning 'Emperor of India') upon Mahatma Gandhi in 1915 for his medical services and public work during World War I. Gandhi renounced this title in 1920 during the Non-Cooperation Movement to protest the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Rowlatt Act. This act was a moral symbol of his defiance against British rule. Among other options, Rai Bahadur and Rai Sahib were titles given to Indians, while Hind Kesari was used for freedom fighter Madan Mohan Malaviya.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Kaiser-e-Hind title conferred? → 1915
☛ During which movement did Gandhi return this title? → Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)
☛ What was the reason for returning the title? → Protest against Jallianwala Bagh massacre and Rowlatt Act
☛ What does Kaiser-e-Hind mean? → Emperor of India
☛ Who was called Hind Kesari? → Madan Mohan Malaviya

q: Which eminent person is associated with Bardoli?
qs.e: Bardoli is a town in Gujarat, famous for the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928, led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The British government had increased land revenue by 30%, causing hardship to farmers. Patel united the farmers and launched a non-violent resistance, forcing the British to withdraw the tax hike. After this success, Patel was honored with the title 'Sardar'. The Bardoli Satyagraha is a significant event in India's freedom struggle and showcases Patel's leadership. Other options like Mahavir, Guru Nanak, and Aurobindo Ghosh have no specific association with Bardoli.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Bardoli Satyagraha? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ In which year did the Bardoli Satyagraha occur? → 1928
☛ What was the cause of the Bardoli Satyagraha? → Opposition to tax hike
☛ After which movement did Patel gain the title 'Sardar'? → Bardoli Satyagraha
☛ In which state is Bardoli located? → Gujarat

q: The Cabinet Mission came to India in the year_____
qs.e: The Cabinet Mission came to India in 1946. It was a mission sent by the British government to plan the transfer of power and to discuss constitution-making with Indian leaders. The mission consisted of three members: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander. It proposed a plan on 16 May 1946, which suggested grouping of provinces and a federal government. Both the Congress and the Muslim League initially accepted the recommendations, but later disagreements led to the failure of the plan.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Cabinet Mission come to India? → 1946
☛ Who were the members of the mission? → Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps, Alexander
☛ When was the plan presented? → 16 May 1946
☛ What was the objective of the Cabinet Mission? → Plan transfer of power
☛ What happened to the mission's recommendations? → Failed due to disagreements

q: Who among the following freedom fighters of India is known as 'Frontier Gandhi'?
qs.e: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan is known as 'Frontier Gandhi'. He was a Pashtun independence activist who followed the principle of non-violence. He founded the 'Khudai Khidmatgar' organization, which was based on Gandhian ideals. This organization was also known as the 'Red Shirts' due to their red uniforms. He opposed the partition of India and advocated for a united India. For his contributions, he was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 1987.
qs.kf:
☛ Organization founded by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan → Khudai Khidmatgar
☛ Color of the uniform of Khudai Khidmatgar members → Red
☛ Year Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan received the Bharat Ratna → 1987
☛ Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was from which province → North-West Frontier Province (now in Pakistan)
☛ Nickname of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan → Frontier Gandhi

q: When was Purna Swaraj i.e. complete freedom from the British Raj declared by the Indian National Congress?
qs.e: The Indian National Congress passed the 'Purna Swaraj' resolution at its Lahore session on 19th December 1929 and declared complete independence from British rule. The first Independence Day was celebrated on 26th January 1930, when the tricolor was hoisted and the pledge of complete freedom was taken under the presidentship of Jawaharlal Nehru. This declaration marked a significant shift in the Indian freedom struggle, moving from the demand for dominion status to complete independence. Later, 26th January was chosen as Republic Day in 1950 to honor this historic declaration.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Purna Swaraj resolution passed? → 19th December 1929
☛ When was the first Independence Day celebrated? → 26th January 1930
☛ Who presided over the Lahore session of INC in 1929? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Which movement was launched after the Purna Swaraj declaration? → Civil Disobedience Movement
☛ When did India become a Republic? → 26th January 1950

q: Which action did the Civil Disobedience Movement start?
o: Arrest of Jawaharlal Nehru and Abdul Ghaffar Khan
qs.e: The Civil Disobedience Movement began with Mahatma Gandhi's famous Dandi March on 12 March 1930. The march started from Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad and ended on 6 April 1930 at Dandi, a coastal village in Gujarat. The purpose of this march was to defy the British government's Salt Law, which imposed a tax on salt and was considered unjust. Gandhi broke the law by making salt from seawater, sparking a nationwide civil disobedience movement. This movement was a crucial phase in India's struggle for independence, involving millions of Indians in non-violent protests against British rule.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Dandi March start? → 12 March 1930
☛ Where did the Dandi March end? → Dandi (Gujarat)
☛ What was the main objective of the Dandi March? → To break the Salt Law
☛ Who was the leader of the Civil Disobedience Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ In which year was the Salt Law enacted? → 1882

q: Which honour did Gandhiji return in protest of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
qs.e: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on April 13, 1919 in Amritsar. In protest of this brutal incident, Mahatma Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal in 1920. This honour was conferred upon him by the British government for his ambulance services during the Boer War (1899-1902). At the time of the massacre, the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab was Michael O'Dwyer, who had implemented the Rowlatt Act. General Dyer ordered the firing on an unarmed crowd. Gandhi's return of the medal became a symbol of the start of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Jallianwala Bagh massacre → April 13, 1919
☛ When did Gandhi return Kaiser-i-Hind? → 1920
☛ Kaiser-i-Hind was given for which war? → Boer War (1899-1902)
☛ Who ordered the Jallianwala Bagh firing? → General Dyer
☛ Who was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab then? → Michael O'Dwyer

name: Set 6 · Q246–294
sub: Modern History - Gandhian Era (Non-Cooperation to Quit India)

q: In which session of the Congress did Mahatma Gandhi convince other leaders to start a non-cooperation movement in support of Khilafat as well as swaraj?
qs.e: In September 1920, the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress was held under the presidency of Lala Lajpat Rai. In this session, Mahatma Gandhi proposed the Non-Cooperation Movement in support of the Khilafat Movement and Swaraj. Although some leaders opposed, Gandhi convinced them to agree. The movement was based on non-violence and non-cooperation, including boycott of government posts, schools, courts, and foreign goods. The resolution was passed at Calcutta, and later fully ratified at the Nagpur session in December 1920. This marked a turning point in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Who presided over the 1920 Calcutta session of Congress? → Lala Lajpat Rai
☛ In which session was the Non-Cooperation Movement proposed? → Calcutta session
