☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement officially start? → 1 August 1920
☛ Which session gave final approval to the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Nagpur session (1920)

q: In which city was Gandhiji informed about the problems in Champaran and invited to visit the place?
qs.e: Gandhiji was informed about the problems in Champaran and invited to visit the place in the city of Lucknow. In 1917, Gandhi attended a meeting in Lucknow where he met Rajkumar Shukla, a peasant leader. Shukla told him about the oppression of farmers under the indigo cultivation system in Champaran and urged him to come and help the peasants. This led to Gandhi's visit to Champaran, where he successfully resolved the farmers' issues through his method of Satyagraha. This event is considered Gandhi's first successful Satyagraha movement in India and marked a significant turning point in the Indian freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Who invited Gandhiji to Champaran? → Rajkumar Shukla
☛ In which year did the Champaran Satyagraha take place? → 1917
☛ Which crop was the main issue in Champaran? → Indigo
☛ What was Gandhi's first successful Satyagraha in India? → Champaran Satyagraha
☛ When did Gandhiji reach Champaran? → April 1917

q: Which of the following statements with reference to the Indian Freedom Struggle is INCORRECT?
o: The Mutiny of 1857 is regarded as the First War of Independence.
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman played an important role in the freedom struggle of India.
The Simon Commission arrived in Bombay in 1928.
Bhagat Singh, Sukh Dev and Rajguru were executed in March 1931.
qs.e: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was the founding leader of Bangladesh and a key figure in East Pakistan's independence movement, having no association with the Indian freedom struggle. The Mutiny of 1857 is regarded as the First War of Independence. The Simon Commission arrived in Bombay in 1928, facing widespread protests and 'Simon Go Back' slogans. Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were executed on March 23, 1931, in the Lahore Conspiracy Case. Hence, option 2 is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the 1857 Revolt occur? → 1857
☛ When did the Simon Commission arrive in India? → 1928
☛ When were Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru executed? → March 23, 1931
☛ Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was the leader of which country? → Bangladesh
☛ What is considered the First War of Independence in India? → The 1857 Revolt

q: Which of the following statements with respect to the Jallianwala Bagh incident is INCORRECT?
o: The Jallianwala Bagh was a result of the Rowlatt Act of March 1919, which authorised the government to imprison without a trial.
The incident took place on 13 April 1919, when the publlic gathered at Jallianwala Bagh with an agenda.
The Jallianwala Bagh incident was followed by the Chauri Chaura incident, where a large group of protesters clashed with the police.
Brigadier-General Dyer opened fire at the people gathered, without giving any notice.
qs.e: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919, when Brigadier-General Dyer opened fire on unarmed civilians without warning. It was a result of the Rowlatt Act (March 1919), which authorised the government to imprison without trial. The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4 February 1922 during the Non-Cooperation Movement, when protesters set fire to a police station. Thus, Jallianwala Bagh preceded Chauri Chaura, not the other way around. All other statements are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Jallianwala Bagh massacre → 13 April 1919
☛ Who ordered the firing → Brigadier-General Dyer
☛ Act that triggered the incident → Rowlatt Act (1919)
☛ Date of Chauri Chaura incident → 4 February 1922
☛ Movement withdrawn after Chauri Chaura → Non-Cooperation Movement

q: Who killed General Dyer, who was responsible for Jallianwala Bagh Massacre?
qs.e: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar, where General Dyer ordered firing on unarmed Indians. To avenge this brutality, Sardar Udham Singh assassinated General Dyer on 13 March 1940 at Caxton Hall in London. Udham Singh was a revolutionary who planned the revenge for 21 years. He was hanged on 31 July 1940. This event symbolises retaliation in the Indian freedom struggle. Other options like Chandrasekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, and Surya Sen were also great revolutionaries but had no direct connection with Dyer.
qs.kf:

☛ Who ordered firing at Jallianwala Bagh → General Dyer
☛ Which organisation was Udham Singh associated with → Ghadar Party

q: The Khilafat committee was formed in Bombay, to defend temporal powers of Khalifa, in _________.
qs.e: The Khilafat committee was formed in March 1919 in Bombay to defend the temporal powers of the Turkish Khalifa, which were threatened after World War I. Indian Muslims considered the Khalifa their religious leader and opposed any injustice against him. The movement was led by Maulana Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali. Later, Mahatma Gandhi linked it with the Non-Cooperation Movement, promoting Hindu-Muslim unity. This committee became a significant milestone in India's freedom struggle, fostering communal harmony and mass mobilization.

☛ Where was the Khilafat committee formed? → Bombay

qs.e: The 1929 Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress was historic as it passed the resolution for Purna Swaraj (complete independence). q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Dandi March of 1930? (a)The march started from Sabarmati Ashram and ended at Dandi, covering a distance of 240 miles. (b) The Dandi March led to the signing of the Poona Pact
qs.e: The Dandi March started on March 12, 1930, from Sabarmati Ashram and ended at Dandi on April 6, 1930, covering a distance of 240 miles. q: Who was known as Badshah Khan?
qs.e: Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan was known as 'Badshah Khan' and 'Frontier Gandhi'. He was a prominent independence activist and Pashtun leader who adhered to non-violence and Gandhian ideology. He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Red Shirt) movement, which played a significant role in the Indian freedom struggle. He opposed Mohammed Ali Jinnah's creation of Pakistan and chose to stay in India. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1987.

B. Vallabh Bhai Patel

qs.e: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was a major peasant movement in the Bardoli region of Gujarat. It was launched in protest against the British government's increase in land revenue. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel led the movement, organizing peasants in non-violent resistance. The satyagraha succeeded, forcing the government to withdraw the revenue hike. This victory earned Patel the title 'Sardar'. The movement highlights the role of peasants in India's freedom struggle.

q: Which of the following leaders signed the Tashkent Agreement?
o: Lal Bahadur Shastri and Ayub Khan
qs.e: The Tashkent Agreement was signed on 10 January 1966 between Lal Bahadur Shastri, the Prime Minister of India, and Ayub Khan, the President of Pakistan. This agreement was reached after the 1965 India-Pakistan War in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, mediated by the Soviet Union (Premier Kosygin). Under the agreement, both countries agreed to withdraw their forces to pre-war positions and restore diplomatic and economic relations. Unfortunately, Lal Bahadur Shastri died the next day in Tashkent, making this agreement a significant event in Indian history.
qs.kf:
☛ Who mediated the Tashkent Agreement? → Soviet Union (Kosygin)
☛ When was the Tashkent Agreement signed? → 10 January 1966
☛ Which Indian Prime Minister died in Tashkent? → Lal Bahadur Shastri
☛ Who was the Prime Minister of India during the 1965 war? → Lal Bahadur Shastri
☛ Who signed on behalf of Pakistan in the Tashkent Agreement? → Ayub Khan

q: Dandi March, the non-violent protest organised by Mahatma Gandhi against the British salt monopoly, culminated on:
qs.e: The Dandi March, led by Mahatma Gandhi, began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram to protest the British salt monopoly. It lasted 24 days and culminated on 6 April 1930 at Dandi village (now in Navsari, Gujarat). Gandhi ji picked up salt from the seashore, breaking the salt law, which marked the start of the Civil Disobedience Movement. The march initially had about 80 followers, but many joined along the way. It is a significant chapter in the Indian freedom struggle, showcasing the power of nonviolent resistance.
qs.kf:
☛ Dandi March Start Date → 12 March 1930
☛ Dandi March End Date → 6 April 1930
☛ Place of breaking salt law → Dandi, Gujarat
☛ Name of the movement → Civil Disobedience Movement
☛ Distance of the march → About 390 km

q: Who said the following words: 'Indian nationalism is an elite phenomenon, a creation of lawyers and doctors and landlords'.
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi described Indian nationalism as an elite phenomenon, a creation of lawyers, doctors, and landlords. He made this statement in the 1920s during a session of the All India Congress Committee. Gandhi believed that the Indian freedom movement required mass participation and that nationalism should not be confined to the educated class. He emphasized grassroots involvement through constructive programs and the civil disobedience movement. This remark reflects Gandhi's vision of inclusive politics and social justice, advocating for the integration of rural and lower-caste populations into the national movement. His critique was aimed at broadening the base of Indian nationalism beyond the urban elite.
qs.kf:
☛ Who called Indian nationalism an elite phenomenon? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Gandhi's 'Constructive Programme' focused on? → Involving masses in freedom struggle
☛ In which year did Gandhi launch the Civil Disobedience Movement? → 1930
☛ According to Gandhi, who should be included in nationalism? → Common people
☛ Who wrote 'Hind Swaraj'? → Mahatma Gandhi

q: In which of the following years did the Quit India Movement start?
qs.e: The Quit India Movement started on August 8, 1942. It was launched by Mahatma Gandhi at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai. The movement demanded an immediate end to British rule. It was a major milestone in India's freedom struggle. People across the country participated in civil disobedience, strikes, and protests. The British government responded with mass arrests. Gandhi was arrested and imprisoned at the Aga Khan Palace. The movement strengthened India's resolve for independence.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Quit India Movement start? → 1942
☛ Who launched the Quit India Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ What was the slogan of Quit India Movement? → Do or Die
☛ Where was Gandhi detained during Quit India Movement? → Aga Khan Palace
☛ Who ran an underground radio during Quit India Movement? → Usha Mehta

q: The Quit India Movement was important in the freedom struggle of India. Which of the following event followed the movement?
o: Labour Government in Britain sent the Cabinet Mission to India
All India Muslim League was established in British India
qs.e: The Quit India Movement started in 1942 and continued till 1944. After the movement, several significant events occurred. In 1945, the Labour Government came to power in Britain and sent the Cabinet Mission (1946) to India for constitutional reforms. Other options: Rowlatt Bill (1919), Dandi March (1930), and Muslim League foundation (1906) all predate the Quit India Movement. Therefore, the correct answer is the Cabinet Mission.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Quit India Movement start? → 8 August 1942
☛ Who gave the slogan of Quit India Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ When did Cabinet Mission arrive in India? → 1946
☛ What was the purpose of Cabinet Mission? → To assist in framing Indian constitution
☛ Who was the chairman of Cabinet Mission? → Lord Pethick-Lawrence

q: Identify the option in which the given events are in the correct chronological order. Ⅰ. Non-cooperation Movement Ⅱ. The Salt (Dandi) March Ⅲ. The Quit India Movement Ⅳ. Mahatma Gandhi's return from South Africa
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi returned from South Africa to India in 1915. The Non-cooperation Movement was launched in 1920. The Salt (Dandi) March took place in 1930. The Quit India Movement started in 1942. Therefore, the correct chronological order is: Gandhi's return (1915), Non-cooperation Movement (1920), Dandi March (1930), Quit India Movement (1942).
qs.kf:
☛ When did Gandhi return from South Africa? → 1915
☛ When was Non-cooperation Movement launched? → 1920
☛ When did Dandi March occur? → 1930
☛ When was Quit India Movement launched? → 1942
☛ When did Champaran Satyagraha happen? → 1917

q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Non-cooperation Movement?
o: Surrender of titles that government awarded
qs.e: The Non-cooperation Movement (1920-22) included features like surrender of titles, boycott of civil services, and boycott of foreign goods. It was led by Mahatma Gandhi as a non-violent protest against British rule. The Salt March (1930) was part of the Civil Disobedience Movement, where Gandhi broke the salt law to challenge British monopoly. Hence, the Salt March is not a feature of the Non-cooperation Movement.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Non-cooperation Movement start? → 1920
☛ Who led the Non-cooperation Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Which incident led to the withdrawal of the Non-cooperation Movement? → Chauri Chaura incident (1922)
☛ Which movement was the Salt March part of? → Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)
☛ What was the main objective of the Non-cooperation Movement? → Attainment of Swaraj

q: When did the second Round Table Conference be held?
qs.e: The second Round Table Conference was held from September to December 1931 in London. It was the second of three conferences organized by the British government to discuss constitutional reforms in India. The first conference was held in 1930 and the third in 1932. Mahatma Gandhi attended the second conference as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress. Key discussions revolved around communal representation and minority rights. Gandhi strongly opposed the demand for separate electorates for the Depressed Classes. The conference failed to reach a consensus, leading to the imposition of the Communal Award in 1932.
qs.kf:
☛ First Round Table Conference → 1930
☛ Third Round Table Conference → 1932
☛ Congress representative in second RTC → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Venue of second RTC → London
☛ Gandhi-Irwin Pact → 1931

q: 'Do or Die', who gave this slogan?
qs.e: The slogan 'Do or Die' was given by Mahatma Gandhi on August 8, 1942, at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai during the Quit India Movement. This movement was against British rule and India's participation in World War II. Gandhi said that either India would get freedom or we would die. This slogan created a sense of awakening and rebellion across the country. During this movement, Congress leaders were arrested and the movement was suppressed, but it gave a new direction to the freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Quit India Movement start? → August 8, 1942
☛ What was the slogan of the Quit India Movement? → Do or Die
☛ Who started the Quit India Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Where was the Quit India Movement resolution passed? → Mumbai
☛ Which emergency power was used during the Quit India Movement? → Defence of India Rules

q: Who among the following persuaded Gandhiji not to restrict the protest of salt march to men alone?
qs.e: During the Salt March in 1930, Gandhiji initially decided to restrict the protest to men only. Kamladevi Chattopadhyay persuaded him to include women in the movement. Gandhiji agreed, and women actively participated in breaking the salt laws. Kamladevi Chattopadhyay was a prominent freedom fighter and social reformer. She was a member of the Indian National Congress and worked for women's rights. This incident marked a significant turning point in the active participation of women in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Salt March take place? → 1930
☛ Who led the Salt March? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Where did the Salt March start from? → Sabarmati Ashram
☛ What was the destination of the Salt March? → Dandi
☛ Which organization was Kamladevi Chattopadhyay associated with? → Indian National Congress

q: When did the Simon Commission arrive in India?
qs.e: The Simon Commission was appointed by the British government to review constitutional reforms in India. It arrived in India in 1928. All members of the commission were British, which led to widespread protests with the slogan "Simon Go Back". Lala Lajpat Rai was injured in a lathi charge during a protest in Lahore and later died. The Nehru Report was also prepared in this context.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the chairman of the Simon Commission? → Sir John Simon
☛ Who raised the slogan "Simon Go Back"? → Yusuf Meherally
☛ Which leader died due to lathi charge during the Simon Commission protest? → Lala Lajpat Rai
☛ Which report was prepared after the Simon Commission? → Nehru Report (1928)
☛ In which year did the Simon Commission arrive in India? → 1928

q: Which of the following places served as a prison for Mahatma Gandhi and Sarojini Naidu between 1942-44?
qs.e: Between 1942-44, Mahatma Gandhi and Sarojini Naidu were imprisoned at Aga Khan Palace in Pune, Maharashtra. After the launch of the Quit India Movement, Gandhi was arrested on 9 August 1942 and detained there for nearly two years. During this period, his wife Kasturba Gandhi died on 22 February 1944, and his secretary Mahadev Desai died on 6 November 1944.
qs.kf:
☛ Aga Khan Palace is located in → Pune, Maharashtra
☛ Quit India Movement started on → 8 August 1942
☛ Mahatma Gandhi was arrested on → 9 August 1942
☛ Kasturba Gandhi died on → 22 February 1944
☛ Mahadev Desai died on → 6 November 1944

q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was pitched in under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi from:
qs.e: The Non-Cooperation Movement, led by Mahatma Gandhi, lasted from 1920 to 1922. It was launched in response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Khilafat movement. Gandhi advocated non-violent resistance against British rule through non-cooperation, which included boycotting government jobs, schools, courts, and foreign goods. The movement gained massive support but was called off in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident, where a mob killed police officers. The movement was a major landmark in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement start? → 1920
☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement end? → 1922
☛ When did the Chauri Chaura incident occur? → 1922
☛ Who was the main leader of the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Who led the Khilafat movement? → Gandhi and the Ali brothers

q: Dandi March was a journey of _______ miles (approximately) on foot to the salt mines in Gujarat.
qs.e: The Dandi March, led by Mahatma Gandhi, started on March 12, 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram. It was a journey of approximately 240 miles (about 390 km) to the coastal village of Dandi in Gujarat, ending on April 6, 1930. During this march, Gandhi defied the British salt laws by making salt from seawater, initiating the Civil Disobedience Movement. This event was a pivotal moment in India's struggle for independence, mobilizing mass participation against colonial rule.
qs.kf:
☛ Total distance of Dandi March? → 240 miles (approx 390 km)
☛ When did Dandi March start? → 12 March 1930
☛ When did Dandi March end? → 6 April 1930
☛ Who led the Dandi March? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Which movement was associated with Dandi March? → Civil Disobedience Movement

q: The Quit India Movement was launched at the Bombay session of the All-India Congress Committee by Mahatma Gandhi in ____ 1942.
qs.e: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on August 8, 1942, at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee. This movement was a pivotal phase in the Indian freedom struggle, during which Gandhi gave the call of 'Do or Die' ('Karo Ya Maro'). Immediately after the launch, Gandhi and other Congress leaders were arrested. The movement witnessed widespread protests, strikes, and civil disobedience across the country. It continued until 1945 and significantly weakened British rule, ultimately leading to India's independence in 1947. The Quit India Movement is also known as the August Movement and is a key topic in Indian history for competitive exams.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Quit India Movement launched? → August 8, 1942
☛ What was the slogan of the Quit India Movement? → Do or Die (Karo Ya Maro)
☛ Where was the Quit India Movement launched? → Bombay (Mumbai) at AICC session
☛ Who was arrested during the Quit India Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi and other Congress leaders
☛ What was the outcome of the Quit India Movement? → Weakened British rule, leading to India's independence in 1947

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 2
q: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the resolution for Poorna Swaraj (complete independence) passed?
qs.e: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress was held in December 1929 under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru. At this session, the historic resolution for Poorna Swaraj (complete independence) was passed. The Congress also decided to observe 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day. This resolution rejected the demand for Dominion Status and instead demanded full independence. The Lahore Session also paved the way for the launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Session that passed Poorna Swaraj resolution → Lahore Session, 1929
☛ President of Lahore Session → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Date of first Independence Day celebration → 26 January 1930
☛ Demand before Poorna Swaraj → Dominion Status
☛ Movement launched after Lahore Session → Civil Disobedience Movement

q: 'Garibi hatao' was the slogan of which political leader?
qs.e: The slogan 'Garibi Hatao' was given by Indira Gandhi, the then Prime Minister of India, during the 1971 Lok Sabha elections. This slogan focused on poverty alleviation and social justice, which garnered her widespread public support. Under this slogan, several schemes were launched for those living below the poverty line, including the 20-Point Programme and nationalisation of banks. This historic slogan brought the issue of poverty to the forefront of Indian politics.
qs.kf:
☛ Who gave the slogan 'Garibi Hatao'? → Indira Gandhi
☛ What was Indira Gandhi's slogan in the 1971 Lok Sabha elections? → Garibi Hatao
☛ In which year was the 'Garibi Hatao' slogan given? → 1971
☛ When was Indira Gandhi's 20-Point Programme for poverty alleviation launched? → 1975
☛ When did Indira Gandhi nationalize banks? → 1969

q: Who led the Khilafat movement?
qs.e: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was led by the Ali Brothers (Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali). This movement was launched by Indian Muslims to protect the status of the Caliph of Turkey after World War I. Mahatma Gandhi supported it and linked it with the Non-Cooperation Movement. Muhammad Ali Jinnah did not participate. The Khilafat Movement promoted Hindu-Muslim unity but ended after Kemal Ataturk abolished the caliphate in Turkey.
qs.kf:
☛ Leader of Khilafat Movement → Ali Brothers (Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali)
☛ Supporter of Khilafat Movement → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Year of Khilafat Movement → 1919-1924
☛ Main objective of Khilafat Movement → To protect the Caliph of Turkey
☛ Khilafat Movement linked with → Non-Cooperation Movement

q: Which of the following did Rowlatt Act 1919 entail?
o: Indefinite detention without trial and censorship of the press
Open fire and lathi-charge on Indians
qs.e: The Rowlatt Act 1919 provided for indefinite detention without trial and censorship of the press. Under this act, any person could be arrested and detained without a trial. Its aim was to suppress the nationalist movement. This act sparked widespread protests, leading Mahatma Gandhi to call for the Rowlatt Satyagraha. The act caused outrage among Indians and contributed to events like the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. The act was passed on the recommendations of the Rowlatt Committee headed by Sir Sydney Rowlatt.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Rowlatt Act passed? → 1919
☛ Who opposed the Rowlatt Act? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ When did Rowlatt Satyagraha begin? → 6 April 1919
☛ Which incident followed the Rowlatt Act? → Jallianwala Bagh massacre
☛ Who chaired the committee that recommended the Rowlatt Act? → Sir Sydney Rowlatt

q: Who among the following was one of the defense attorneys of the famous 'Sehgal-Dhillon-Shah Nawaz' trials?
qs.e: The 'Sehgal-Dhillon-Shah Nawaz' trials (1945) were court-martials conducted by the British government against Indian National Army (INA) officers. Among the defense attorneys were Jawaharlal Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai, and Tej Bahadur Sapru. Nehru, a prominent lawyer and political leader, represented the INA officers to uphold their nationalist cause. The trial took place at the Red Fort in Delhi and significantly boosted the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Where were the INA trials held? → Red Fort, Delhi
☛ Who were the main accused? → Sehgal, Dhillon, Shah Nawaz
☛ Other defense attorneys? → Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru
☛ Who founded INA? → Subhash Chandra Bose
☛ Full name of INA? → Azad Hind Fauj

q: The Non-cooperation Movement was adopted at the Congress session in December 1920 at:
qs.e: The annual Congress session in December 1920 was held in Nagpur. At this session, the Non-cooperation Movement was formally adopted, which had been announced by Gandhi earlier in August 1920. The session was presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar. The movement aimed at nonviolent resistance against British rule, including boycotting government jobs, titles, foreign goods, and educational institutions. It was later withdrawn in 1922 following the Chauri Chaura incident.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the 1920 Congress session held? → Nagpur
☛ When was the Non-cooperation Movement adopted? → December 1920
☛ Who was the president of the Nagpur session? → C. Vijayaraghavachariar
☛ When did the Non-cooperation Movement start? → August 1920
☛ When was the Non-cooperation Movement withdrawn? → 1922 (Chauri Chaura incident)

q: What was the name of the movement started in 1927 in Maharashtra, led by Dr. BR Ambedkar to access public resources such as water bodies, temples and schools?
qs.e: Dr. BR Ambedkar led the Mahad Satyagraha in 1927 in Maharashtra to secure access to public resources like water bodies, temples, and schools for Dalits. The movement began for the right to drink water from the Chavdar Tank in Mahad. On 20 March 1927, Ambedkar, along with thousands of followers, entered the tank. Later, on 25 December 1927, he publicly burned the Manusmriti. This satyagraha was a landmark event against the caste system, strengthening the struggle for social justice and equality.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the main issue of Mahad Satyagraha? → Dalits' access to public water sources
☛ Where is Chavdar Tank located? → Mahad, Maharashtra
☛ Who led the Mahad Satyagraha? → Dr. BR Ambedkar
☛ In which year did Mahad Satyagraha take place? → 1927
☛ When did Ambedkar burn Manusmriti? → 25 December 1927

q: Who said the following when laying the foundation stone ceremony of Banaras Hindu University, "There is no salvation for India unless you strip yourself of this jewellery and hold it in trust for your countrymen in India."?
qs.e: The foundation stone of Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was laid in 1916. During the ceremony, Mahatma Gandhi said, "There is no salvation for India unless you strip yourself of this jewellery and hold it in trust for your countrymen." This statement reflects Gandhi's ideals of sacrifice and service. He emphasized that the university should be a center for national regeneration. Gandhi urged people to donate their wealth for the welfare of the nation. BHU was founded by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Banaras Hindu University → Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya
☛ Year of BHU establishment → 1916
☛ Gandhi's speech at BHU linked to which movement → Background of Non-Cooperation Movement
☛ Gandhi's path for India's salvation → Sacrifice and service
☛ What did Gandhi urge to give up at BHU ceremony → Jewellery and luxury

q: Which of the following is/are correct about Tej Bahadur Sapru?
I. He helped Annie Besant to build up the Central Hindu College at Banaras.
II. He entered politics during the Home Rule movement.
III. He participated in the Round Table Conferences held between 1930 and 1932 in London.
qs.e: Tej Bahadur Sapru was a prominent Indian lawyer, politician, and liberal leader. He helped Annie Besant establish the Central Hindu College at Banaras (later Banaras Hindu University). He entered politics during the Home Rule movement (1916) and emerged as a leader of Indian liberals. Sapru participated in all three Round Table Conferences held in London between 1930 and 1932 as an Indian delegate. He advocated constitutional reforms and communal harmony. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Which college did Sapru help Annie Besant establish? → Central Hindu College
☛ When did Sapru enter politics? → During the Home Rule movement
☛ Where were the Round Table Conferences held? → London
☛ In which years were the Round Table Conferences held? → 1930, 1931, and 1932
☛ Which ideology did Sapru follow? → Liberalism

q: Which individuals actively supported Mahatma Gandhi during the Kheda Satyagraha movement?
o: Raj Kumar Shukla and Rajendra Prasad
qs.e: The 1918 Kheda Satyagraha was a peasant movement in Gujarat for revenue remission. Led by Mahatma Gandhi, it was actively supported by Vallabhbhai Patel and Indulal Yajnik. Patel organized the peasants while Yajnik mobilized public opinion. The movement strengthened Gandhi and Patel's political careers.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the Kheda Satyagraha? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ When did Kheda Satyagraha occur? → 1918
☛ Role of Vallabhbhai Patel in Kheda Satyagraha? → Organizing peasants
☛ Which movement is Indulal Yajnik associated with? → Kheda Satyagraha
☛ Objective of Kheda Satyagraha? → Revenue remission

q: ______ was Mahatma Gandhi's first successful satyagraha in India.
A. Kheda
B. Bardoli
C. Champaran
D. Salt march
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi's first successful satyagraha in India was the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917. It was launched in the Champaran district of Bihar against the exploitation of indigo farmers by British planters under the Tinkathia system, which forced farmers to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land. The protest led to the abolition of the oppressive system and marked the beginning of non-violent resistance in India's freedom struggle. This success established Gandhi's leadership and the effectiveness of satyagraha as a tool for social and political change.
qs.kf:
☛ Gandhi's first satyagraha in India → Champaran (1917)
☛ Main cause of Champaran Satyagraha → Tinkathia system of indigo cultivation
☛ Kheda Satyagraha → 1918, against tax hike
☛ Bardoli Satyagraha → 1928, led by Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Salt March → 1930, part of Civil Disobedience Movement

q: Which of the following does NOT match?
qs.e: Ved Samaj was founded in 1864 by K. Sridharalu Naidu in Chennai, not by Gharalu Naidu. The society was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and emphasized rational religion and social reforms. Gharalu Naidu was a political leader. Other options are correctly matched: Swaraj Dal was founded in 1923 by Motilal Nehru and C. R. Das; Scientific Society was founded in 1864 by Syed Ahmed Khan in Aligarh; Bhoodan movement was started in 1951 by Vinoba Bhave.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Ved Samaj → K. Sridharalu Naidu
☛ Founders of Swaraj Dal → Motilal Nehru and C. R. Das
☛ Year of establishment of Scientific Society → 1864
☛ Leader of Bhoodan movement → Vinoba Bhave
☛ Location of Scientific Society → Aligarh

q: Which of the following nationalists co-founded and became the president of the Congress-Khilafat Swarajya Party, after a fall off with the Indian National Congress?
qs.e: After a fallout with the Indian National Congress, Chittaranjan Das along with Motilal Nehru co-founded the Congress-Khilafat Swarajya Party on January 1, 1923, and Chittaranjan Das became its first president. The party was formed to continue the struggle against British rule by entering legislative councils and opposing the government from within. The split occurred due to differences with Gandhi's decision to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement and boycott of councils. Chittaranjan Das was a prominent lawyer, freedom fighter, and leader from Bengal, popularly known as 'Deshbandhu'.
qs.kf:
☛ Founders of Congress-Khilafat Swarajya Party → Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru
☛ First president of Swaraj Party → Chittaranjan Das
☛ Year of formation of Swaraj Party → 1923
☛ Main objective of Swaraj Party → Enter legislatures and oppose the government
☛ Nickname of Chittaranjan Das → Deshbandhu

q: The weekly journal Young India was associated with whom among the following?
qs.e: Young India was an English weekly journal launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1919. Gandhi used it as a platform to propagate his ideas of non-cooperation and civil disobedience against British rule. The journal played a key role in spreading nationalist thought and mobilizing masses for the freedom struggle. Gandhi also edited other journals like Harijan (1933), Indian Opinion (in South Africa, 1903), and Navajivan (Gujarati). Young India was instrumental in shaping public opinion during the 1920s and promoting the concept of Swaraj. It was banned several times by the British government due to its anti-establishment content.
qs.kf:
☛ Young India was associated with → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Journal started by Gandhi in 1919 → Young India
☛ Gandhi's newspaper in South Africa → Indian Opinion
☛ Gandhi's Hindi weekly → Harijan (started 1933)
☛ Gandhi's Gujarati newspaper → Navajivan

q: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi break the Salt Act at Dandi?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi broke the Salt Act on April 6, 1930, after marching from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi from March 12 to April 5, 1930. This act of civil disobedience against the British salt monopoly sparked a nationwide protest and marked a turning point in India's freedom struggle. The Dandi March, also known as the Salt Satyagraha, mobilized millions and weakened British authority.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Salt Satyagraha begin? → 1930
☛ Where did the Dandi March start from? → Sabarmati Ashram
☛ How many days did the Dandi March last? → 24 days
☛ What was the main goal of breaking the Salt Act? → Opposition to salt tax
☛ Who led the Salt Satyagraha? → Mahatma Gandhi

q: Which major mass movement did the Indian National Congress agree to withdraw, under the Gandhi–Irwin Pact of March 1931?
qs.e: The Gandhi–Irwin Pact was signed in March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin. Under this agreement, the Indian National Congress agreed to withdraw the Civil Disobedience Movement. This movement had started in 1930 with the Dandi March and breaking of salt laws. The pact involved Congress calling off the movement, while the government agreed to release political prisoners and allow salt collection in coastal areas. However, the agreement did not fully succeed, and the movement was later resumed after the failure of the Second Round Table Conference.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Gandhi–Irwin Pact → 5 March 1931
☛ Main outcome of the pact → End of Civil Disobedience Movement
☛ Salt tax concession → Permission to make salt in coastal areas
☛ Release of political prisoners → Non-violent offenders were freed
☛ Second Round Table Conference → Congress participated

q: Which of the following incidents led to the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
qs.e: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in 1920 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. On February 5, 1922, in the village of Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. This violent incident deeply disturbed Gandhi, and he called off the Non-Cooperation Movement on February 12, 1922. He believed the nation was not yet ready for non-violent struggle. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) was a cause of the movement, the Dandi March (1930) was part of the Salt Satyagraha, and the Simon Commission (1928) led to the demand for Purna Swaraj.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Chauri Chaura incident occur? → February 5, 1922
☛ Number of policemen killed in Chauri Chaura? → 22
☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement start? → 1920
☛ Who was the leader of the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ In which state is Chauri Chaura located? → Uttar Pradesh

q: What key difference set the Kheda Satyagraha apart from the Ahmedabad Mill Strike during the phase of heightened nationalist activity?
o: Emphasis on constitutional and legislative demands
Mobilisation of rural peasants versus organisation of urban workers
Reliance on petitions and appeals to colonial authorities
Common leadership under the same nationalist figures
qs.e: Both the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) and the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) were led by Mahatma Gandhi, but the key difference was in the basis of struggle and the target group. In the Kheda Satyagraha, rural peasants protested against the collection of land revenue despite crop failure. It was a peasant movement involving non-violent resistance and tax non-cooperation. In contrast, the Ahmedabad Mill Strike was a labour movement where urban workers fought for bonus payments and better working conditions, using strikes and arbitration. Thus, Kheda Satyagraha mobilised rural peasants while the mill strike organised urban workers.
qs.kf:
☛ Main aim of Kheda Satyagraha (1918) → Demand for land revenue remission due to crop failure
☛ Main cause of Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) → Dispute over bonus payment to mill workers
☛ Leadership of both movements → Led simultaneously by Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Non-violent method used in Kheda → Tax non-cooperation and petition
☛ Outcome of Ahmedabad Mill Strike → Workers got bonus after Gandhi's fast

q: Which of the following prominent leaders led the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)?
qs.e: The Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. This movement was launched by farmers in the Bardoli taluka of Gujarat against a 30% increase in land revenue by the British government. The farmers decided to withhold tax payment under Patel's leadership, who organized them into a united front using non-violent resistance. The government eventually had to roll back the revenue hike. This success earned Patel the title 'Sardar'. The Bardoli Satyagraha was a significant milestone in India's freedom struggle, showcasing the power of peaceful civil disobedience.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year did the Bardoli Satyagraha take place? → 1928
☛ What was the main cause of the Bardoli Satyagraha? → Revenue hike
☛ After which movement did Sardar Patel get the title 'Sardar'? → Bardoli Satyagraha
☛ What type of resistance did farmers adopt in Bardoli Satyagraha? → Non-payment of taxes (non-violent)
☛ What was the outcome of the Bardoli Satyagraha? → Government withdrew the revenue increase

q: Which leader was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and carried out a salt protest in the Madras Presidency during the Civil Disobedience Movement?
qs.e: C. Rajagopalachari was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and led the salt protest in the Madras Presidency during the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930. He later became the first Indian Governor-General of India. He was also a member of the Swaraj Party.
qs.kf:
☛ The salt protest of 1930 was part of which movement? → Civil Disobedience Movement
☛ Who led the Dandi March? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ C. Rajagopalachari was the Chief Minister of which state? → Madras
☛ Who was the last Governor-General of India? → C. Rajagopalachari
☛ What was the main issue of the Civil Disobedience Movement? → Salt tax

q: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
qs.e: The Gandhi–Irwin Pact was signed in 1931, not 1929. This agreement was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin on March 5, 1931. It ended the Civil Disobedience Movement and agreed to participate in the Round Table Conference. The other pairs are correct: Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was led by Vallabhbhai Patel; Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was for revenue relief; Champaran Satyagraha (1917) opposed indigo cultivation. Thus, 1929–Gandhi–Irwin Pact is incorrectly matched.
qs.kf:
☛ Gandhi–Irwin Pact → Signed in 1931
☛ Bardoli Satyagraha → 1928, led by Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Kheda Satyagraha → 1918, for land revenue relief
☛ Champaran Satyagraha → 1917, against indigo cultivation
☛ Dandi March → 1930, Salt Satyagraha

q: Which of the following incidents prompted Mahatma Gandhi to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement?
qs.e: On February 5, 1922, in Chauri-Chaura, Uttar Pradesh, protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. Disturbed by this violence, Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement. Gandhi believed in non-violence and considered violence detrimental to the movement. This incident showed that the masses were straying from the path of non-violence, so on February 12, 1922, he decided to suspend the movement. The Congress Working Committee also supported this decision. The movement was a significant phase in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Chauri-Chaura incident occur? → February 5, 1922
☛ In which state is Chauri-Chaura located? → Uttar Pradesh
☛ What was the aim of the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Non-violent resistance against British rule
☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement start? → August 1, 1920
☛ What was Mahatma Gandhi's main principle? → Non-violence and Satyagraha

q: Who among the following muslim leaders first propounded the theory of 'Two nations'?
qs.e: The theory of 'Two Nations' was first propounded by Mohammad Iqbal in his 1930 Allahabad address. He argued that Hindus and Muslims in India are two distinct nations with separate cultures, religions, and traditions. This theory later became the ideological basis for the creation of Pakistan. Rahmat Ali Chaudhary coined the term 'Pakistan' in 1933, while Muhammad Ali Jinnah politically implemented the two-nation theory. Liaqat Ali was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan but did not propound the two-nation theory.
qs.kf:
☛ Who first propounded the two-nation theory? → Mohammad Iqbal
☛ When and where did Iqbal propose it? → 1930, Allahabad
☛ Who coined the term 'Pakistan'? → Rahmat Ali Chaudhary (1933)
☛ Who politically implemented the two-nation theory? → Muhammad Ali Jinnah
☛ Liaqat Ali was the first Prime Minister of which country? → Pakistan

q: In which year did the Non-Cooperation Movement begin in India?
qs.e: The Non-Cooperation Movement in India began in 1920 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. It was the first major mass movement of nonviolent resistance against British rule. The movement was launched in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Rowlatt Act. Gandhi announced the movement on August 1, 1920. People boycotted government jobs, schools, courts, and foreign goods. The movement was called off after the Chauri Chaura incident (1922). This movement was a significant milestone in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Leader of Non-Cooperation Movement → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Main cause of the movement → Jallianwala Bagh massacre & Rowlatt Act
☛ Date of launch → August 1, 1920
☛ Reason for withdrawal → Chauri Chaura incident (1922)
☛ Congress session where movement was approved → Calcutta session (1920)

name: Set 1 · Q1–38
sub: Modern History - Revolutionaries & Indian National Army

q: Who gave the slogan 'Delhi chalo'?
qs.e: Subhas Chandra Bose, while leading the Indian National Army (INA), gave the slogan 'Delhi Chalo' (Let's go to Delhi). The slogan aimed to march to Delhi to overthrow British rule. It was used to inspire patriotism and a spirit of freedom among INA soldiers and the Indian public. Netaji formed the INA in 1943 in Southeast Asia and also gave the famous slogan 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom'. The 'Delhi Chalo' slogan became a significant symbol in the Indian freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Slogan related to INA and freedom fighter → Delhi Chalo
☛ Famous slogan by Netaji → Give me blood, and I will give you freedom
☛ Year of INA formation → 1943
☛ First leader of INA → Mohan Singh (1942)
☛ Who gave the title 'Netaji' to Subhas Chandra Bose → INA soldiers

q: Who gave the slogan 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom'?
qs.e: This slogan was given by Subhash Chandra Bose. He gave this slogan to inspire the soldiers of the Indian National Army (INA). Through this slogan, Bose called for sacrifice for freedom. He was popularly known as Netaji and formed the Azad Hind Fauj. He believed that without shedding blood, freedom could not be achieved. This slogan was highly inspirational in the Indian freedom struggle. Subhash Chandra Bose was a revolutionary leader who fought for independence through armed struggle. His slogan continues to evoke patriotic feelings even today.
qs.kf:
☛ Known as Netaji → Subhash Chandra Bose
☛ Founder of Azad Hind Fauj → Subhash Chandra Bose
☛ Who gave the slogan 'Dilli Chalo' → Subhash Chandra Bose
☛ Birth of Subhash Chandra Bose → 23 January 1897, Cuttack
☛ Subhash Chandra Bose resigned from Congress presidency → In 1939

q: In which province did the famous Agartala movement "Tebhaga" occur?
qs.e: The Tebhaga movement (1946-47) was a peasant uprising that took place in the province of Bengal. The name 'Tebhaga' (three shares) comes from the demand of the peasants to retain two-thirds of the crop for themselves, while giving only one-third to the landlords. The movement was primarily led by the Communist Party of India and involved peasants fighting against the zamindari system. The movement was centered in North Bengal districts like Dinajpur, Rangpur, and Jalpaiguri. It was a significant part of the peasant movements during the Indian independence struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the main leader of the Tebhaga movement? → Harekrishna Konar
☛ Which political party played a role in the Tebhaga movement? → Communist Party of India (CPI)
☛ What was the main objective of the Tebhaga movement? → Peasants' right to two-thirds of the crop
☛ In which year did the Tebhaga movement occur? → 1946-47
☛ Which community was associated with the Tebhaga movement? → Peasants

q: Which of the following parties was founded by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose?
A. Indian National Congress
B. All India Forward Block
C. Socialist Party of India
D. Social Reformist Party of India
qs.e: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose founded the All India Forward Bloc in 1939. This party emerged as a left-wing faction within the Indian National Congress, advocating for complete independence and socialist policies. Bose resigned from the Congress presidency in 1939 due to ideological differences with the Congress leadership and formed the Forward Bloc. Its aim was to intensify the Indian freedom struggle and create a united front against British rule. The other options are incorrect: the Indian National Congress was founded in 1885, the Socialist Party of India was formed later, and the Social Reformist Party of India has no major historical relevance.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Forward Bloc founded? → 1939
☛ What was the main objective of the Forward Bloc? → Complete independence and socialist policies
☛ From which party did Netaji resign to form the Forward Bloc? → Indian National Congress
☛ Who founded the Indian National Congress? → A.O. Hume
☛ Who founded the Socialist Party of India? → Jayaprakash Narayan and Acharya Narendra Dev

q: Kakori train robbery was organized by the _______ in 1925.
A. Swaraj Party B. Indian National Congress C. Anushilan Samiti
D. Hindustan Republican Association
qs.e: The Kakori train robbery of 1925 was organized by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), a revolutionary organization led by prominent figures like Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and Chandrashekhar Azad. The HRA aimed to acquire funds for revolutionary activities against British rule. The robbery was executed on August 9, 1925, at Kakori near Lucknow. The HRA was founded in 1924 and later evolved into the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). This event significantly boosted the revolutionary movement in India's struggle for independence.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year did the Kakori train robbery occur? → 1925
☛ Who led the Kakori train robbery? → Ram Prasad Bismil
☛ When was the Hindustan Republican Association founded? → 1924
☛ Which revolutionaries were hanged after the Kakori case? → Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and Roshan Singh
☛ What was the HRA renamed after the Kakori case? → Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)

q: Who along with Bhagat Singh, was the main accused in Assembly Bomb Case? A, Ram Prasad Bismil B. Ashafaqulla C. Surya Sen D. Batukeshwar Dutta
qs.e: On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi. The aim was to draw attention to revolutionary activities, and no one was killed. Both surrendered to the court to propagate their ideas. In this case, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta were the main accused. Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqulla were associated with the Kakori Conspiracy, while Surya Sen led the Chittagong Armoury Raid. The Assembly Bomb Case brought fame to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta throw the bomb? → April 8, 1929
☛ Location of the bomb case? → Central Legislative Assembly, Delhi
☛ Birthplace of Batukeshwar Dutta? → Bardhaman, Bengal
☛ Organization linked to Assembly Bomb Case? → Hindustan Socialist Republican Association
☛ Companions of Bhagat Singh who were hanged? → Sukhdev and Rajguru

q: Indian National Army formed by _______
qs.e: The Indian National Army (INA) was first formed in 1942 by Mohan Singh, an Indian army officer. With Japanese support, he organized Indian prisoners of war in Malaya and Singapore to establish the Azad Hind Fauj. Later in 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose took over its leadership and reorganized it. Mohan Singh's contribution was crucial in the initial formation of the INA.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first commander of INA? → Mohan Singh
☛ Who was the second commander of INA? → Subhash Chandra Bose
☛ In which year was INA formed? → 1942
☛ When was INA reorganized? → 1943
☛ What rank did Mohan Singh hold in the Indian Army? → Captain

q: To take revenge for the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, who killed General O’Dwyer in London?
qs.e: To take revenge for the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, Sardar Udham Singh killed General O'Dwyer in London on 13 March 1940. This act occurred 21 years after the massacre, where on 13 April 1919, unarmed Indians were fired upon in Amritsar. Udham Singh lived in London under the alias 'Ram Mohammed Singh' and shot O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall. He was later hanged. This deed made him a prominent revolutionary in the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Jallianwala Bagh Massacre → 13 April 1919
☛ Birthplace of Udham Singh → Sunam, Punjab
☛ Venue where Udham Singh killed O'Dwyer → Caxton Hall, London
☛ Date of Udham Singh's execution → 31 July 1940
☛ Alias used by Udham Singh in London → Ram Mohammed Singh

q: Who among the following freedom fighters was NOT involved in the Kakori Train Robbery?
qs.e: The Kakori Train Robbery took place on 9 August 1925. This incident involved Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Chandrashekhar Azad and other revolutionaries. Bhagat Singh was not involved in this event as he was in Kanpur at that time and joined revolutionary activities only later in 1926. The aim of the robbery was to loot money from the British government to fund revolutionary activities. For this, Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan and Thakur Roshan Singh were hanged.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of Kakori Train Robbery → 9 August 1925
☛ Key revolutionaries involved → Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Chandrashekhar Azad
☛ When did Bhagat Singh join revolutionary movement → 1926
☛ Kakori revolutionaries who were hanged → Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Thakur Roshan Singh
☛ Reason for Kakori Train Robbery → To loot money from British government

q: Ram Prasad Bismil was hanged for ______.
qs.e: Ram Prasad Bismil was a prominent Indian revolutionary and a member of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA). On 9 August 1925, he participated in the Kakori train heist, which aimed to loot government funds to finance revolutionary activities. The revolutionaries stopped a train at Kakori station carrying the government treasury and stole 8,000 rupees. Later, they were arrested and tried in the Kakori conspiracy case. Bismil was sentenced to death and executed by hanging on 19 December 1927 at Gorakhpur Jail. This event is considered significant in the Indian independence movement. Other options: Chatgaon Armoury raid is associated with Surya Sen, Meerut Conspiracy with communists, and Lahore Conspiracy with Bhagat Singh.
qs.kf:
☛ How much money was looted in the Kakori train heist? → 8,000 rupees
☛ When did the Kakori train heist take place? → 9 August 1925
☛ Which organization did Ram Prasad Bismil belong to? → Hindustan Republican Association (HRA)
☛ Where was Ram Prasad Bismil hanged? → Gorakhpur Jail
☛ When was Ram Prasad Bismil hanged? → 19 December 1927

q: Who started publication of Al Hilal, a newspaper for propagating nationalism?
qs.e: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad started the Urdu newspaper Al Hilal in 1912 to propagate nationalism and the spirit of freedom. It gained immense popularity during the Khilafat Movement, but the British government banned it in 1914. Later, Azad launched other newspapers like Paigham and Al Balagh. He was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement and became the first Minister of Education of independent India.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Al Hilal → Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
☛ Year of Al Hilal publication → 1912
☛ Language of Al Hilal → Urdu
☛ Year of Al Hilal ban → 1914
☛ Other newspapers started by Maulana Azad → Paigham and Al Balagh

q: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw smoke bombs at Delhi Central Legislative Assembly. What were they protesting against?
o: Trade Disputes Bill and Public Safety Bill
qs.e: On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw smoke bombs at the Delhi Central Legislative Assembly. The act was intended not to cause harm but to protest against repressive laws. They were opposing the Trade Disputes Bill and Public Safety Bill, which curbed workers' right to strike and gave arbitrary powers to the police. After the incident, they shouted the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'. This protest was against the British government's anti-labour policies.
qs.kf:
☛ Where did Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt throw bombs? → Delhi Central Legislative Assembly
☛ What is the date of the bomb throwing? → 8 April 1929
☛ Which bills were they protesting against? → Trade Disputes Bill and Public Safety Bill
☛ What slogan did they raise? → Inquilab Zindabad
☛ What was the purpose of the bomb throwing? → To protest repressive laws

q: Which two freedom fighters threw smoke bombs at the Delhi Central Legislative Assembly in 1929?
o: Bhagat Singh and Subhash Chandra Bose
qs.e: In 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw smoke bombs in the Delhi Central Legislative Assembly. Their aim was to draw attention to the unjust treatment of political prisoners and to protest against the repressive policies of the British government. After the incident, both were arrested and tried. During the trial, Bhagat Singh declared that they were not terrorists but revolutionaries fighting for India's freedom. This event became a symbol of resistance and inspired many young Indians to join the freedom struggle.

☛ In which assembly did Bhagat Singh throw smoke bombs? → Delhi Central Legislative Assembly
☛ Who was with Bhagat Singh during the smoke bomb incident? → Batukeshwar Dutt
☛ In which year did the smoke bomb incident take place? → 1929
☛ What punishment did Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt receive? → Life imprisonment
☛ What was Bhagat Singh's famous slogan? → Inquilab Zindabad

q: What is the incident of 'Komagata Maru' related to?
qs.e: The Komagata Maru was a Japanese ship that arrived in Canada in 1914 carrying 376 Indian passengers, mostly Sikhs, Muslims, and Hindus, seeking better opportunities. The Canadian government denied them entry, sparking protests and linking the incident to the Indian freedom struggle. This event fueled anti-British sentiments among Indians and strengthened revolutionary groups like the Ghadar Party. It became a significant chapter in India's national movement, highlighting racial discrimination and colonial oppression. The incident is remembered as a symbol of resistance against injustice and contributed to India's fight for independence.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Komagata Maru incident occur? → 1914
☛ From where did the ship depart? → Hong Kong
☛ Which country denied entry? → Canada
☛ Which movement was influenced by this incident? → Ghadar Movement
☛ Who was the leader of Komagata Maru? → Gurdit Singh Sandhu

q: Where did Subhash Chandra Bose form the "Provisional Government of Free India"?
qs.e: Subhash Chandra Bose formed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind Government) on 21 October 1943 in Singapore. This government was established during World War II to fight against British rule and achieve India's independence. Bose proclaimed its formation at the Superintendent Cinema in Singapore. The Azad Hind Government was recognized by several countries including Japan, Germany, and Italy. It formed the Indian National Army (INA) to fight for India's freedom and hoisted its flag over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
qs.kf:
☛ Head of the Provisional Government of Free India → Subhash Chandra Bose
☛ Date of formation of Azad Hind Government → 21 October 1943
☛ Capital of Azad Hind Government → Singapore (provisional)
☛ Who formed the Indian National Army → Subhash Chandra Bose under Azad Hind Government
☛ Countries that recognized Azad Hind Government → Japan, Germany, Italy

q: Which freedom fighter started the newspaper Al-Hilal?
qs.e: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was a prominent freedom fighter and India's first Minister of Education. He started the Urdu weekly newspaper Al-Hilal in 1912. The newspaper criticized British rule and played a key role in bringing Indian Muslims into the national movement. Al-Hilal promoted communal harmony and supported India's independence. Due to its radical views, it was banned in 1914. Azad later started another newspaper named Paigham.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Al-Hilal → Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
☛ Year of Al-Hilal's launch → 1912
☛ Language of Al-Hilal → Urdu
☛ Year of Al-Hilal's ban → 1914
☛ Position held by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad → First Education Minister of India

q: Who among the following was NOT associated with the revolutionary organization 'Anushilan Samiti'?
qs.e: Anushilan Samiti was a prominent revolutionary organization established in 1902 in Kolkata. Its key members included Barindrakumar Ghosh, Bhupendra Nath Dutta, and Jatindra Nath Bannerji. Barindrakumar Ghosh was the younger brother of Sri Aurobindo and planned armed rebellion through the Samiti. Bhupendra Nath Dutta propagated revolutionary ideas via the journal 'Yugantar'. Jatindra Nath Bannerji led revolutionary activities in Bengal. Rajendra Lahiri was associated with the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) and participated in the Kakori Conspiracy (1925). He was not a member of Anushilan Samiti. Hence, the correct answer is Rajendra Lahiri.
qs.kf:
☛ When and who founded Anushilan Samiti? → 1902, Pramatha Nath Mitra and Barindrakumar Ghosh
☛ Major event linked to Anushilan Samiti? → Alipore Bomb Case (1908)
☛ Which conspiracy was Rajendra Lahiri involved in? → Kakori Conspiracy (1925)
☛ Which journal did Bhupendra Nath Dutta publish? → Yugantar
☛ Alias of Jatindra Nath Bannerji? → Nirmal Sen

q: Which of the following revolutionary journals was NOT published abroad?
qs.e: Yugantar was a revolutionary journal published in India, not abroad. It was started in 1906 in Bengal and edited by Bhupendranath Dutt and Barindra Ghosh. The other journals were published abroad: Talvar from Germany, Free Hindustan from Canada, and Indian Sociologist from London. All these played a significant role in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was Yugantar published? → India (Bengal)
☛ Where was Talvar published? → Germany
☛ Where was Free Hindustan published? → Canada
☛ Where was Indian Sociologist published? → London
☛ Who were the editors of Yugantar? → Bhupendranath Dutt and Barindra Ghosh

q: Who proclaimed the formation of a provisional government of the Azad Hind on October 21, 1943?
qs.e: On October 21, 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose proclaimed the formation of the provisional government of Azad Hind in Singapore. This government was recognized by Japan, Germany, Italy, and other countries. Bose named it 'Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind'. It fought for India's independence and established control over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Bose had arrived in Singapore on July 4, 1943, and took command of the Indian National Army (INA). The government aimed to liberate India from British rule.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Azad Hind government → Port Blair (Andaman)
☛ Founder of INA → Mohan Singh (1942) with Japanese help
☛ Title given to Subhash Chandra Bose → Netaji
☛ Main objective of Azad Hind government → Free India from British rule
☛ Slogan of Subhash Chandra Bose → Dilli Chalo

q: Who among the following was involved in Alipore Bomb Case?
qs.e: The Alipore Bomb Case (1908) was a significant political trial in British India, where Sri Aurobindo was charged with sedition and anti-government activities. The case was conducted in the Alipore district of Calcutta. Sri Aurobindo was accused of being associated with the revolutionary organization 'Yugantar' and being involved in the Muzaffarpur Bomb Case (1908) carried out by Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki. However, his lawyer C. R. Das successfully defended him, and he was acquitted. This case gave a new direction to the Indian freedom movement.
qs.kf:

☛ Who carried out the Muzaffarpur Bomb Case? → Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki
☛ Who was Sri Aurobindo's lawyer? → C. R. Das
☛ Who founded the Yugantar Party? → Barindra Ghosh
☛ How many accused were in the Alipore Bomb Case? → 49

q: Who among the following freedom fighters was involved in the assassination of British officer John Saunders in 1928?
qs.e: Bhagat Singh, along with Rajguru and Sukhdev, assassinated British police officer John Saunders in Lahore on December 17, 1928. This was in retaliation for the lathi charge that led to the death of Lala Lajpat Rai. The case is known as the Lahore Conspiracy Case. Bhagat Singh was a prominent revolutionary who played a key role in the founding of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). He is revered for his sacrifice in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the main accused in the Lahore Conspiracy Case? → Bhagat Singh
☛ When was John Saunders assassinated? → December 17, 1928
☛ When did Lala Lajpat Rai die? → November 17, 1928
☛ Which organization did Bhagat Singh found? → Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)
☛ When was Bhagat Singh executed? → March 23, 1931

q: Which of the following was included in the Kakori conspiracy of 1925?
qs.e: The Kakori Conspiracy of 1925 was carried out by members of the Hindustan Republican Association, including Ashfaq Ulla Khan, Ram Prasad Bismil, and Chandrashekhar Azad. They looted a train carrying government treasury at Kakori station near Lucknow. Ashfaq Ulla Khan was hanged in 1927 for his role in the conspiracy. Dadabhai Navroji and Jyotiba Phule were social reformers, while Behramji Merwanji Malabari was a Parsi journalist; none of them were involved in the Kakori conspiracy.
qs.kf:

☛ Who founded the Hindustan Republican Association? → Ram Prasad Bismil and associates

q: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were accused in the __________ conspiracy case.
qs.e: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were accused in the Lahore conspiracy case. This case was related to the murder of John Saunders in 1928, which was an act of revenge for the death of Lala Lajpat Rai. These three revolutionaries were members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). After a trial, they were sentenced to death on October 7, 1930. Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on March 23, 1931.
qs.kf:

☛ Which newspaper did Bhagat Singh write articles for? → Daur e Mukhtar
☛ What was the full name of HSRA? → Hindustan Socialist Republican Association
☛ When was Bhagat Singh arrested? → April 8, 1929
☛ What was the date of execution in the Lahore conspiracy case? → March 23, 1931

q: Who among the following is known as 'Bagha Jatin'?
qs.e: Jatindranath Mukherjee (1879-1915) is famously known as 'Bagha Jatin'. He was a prominent revolutionary who fought against British rule through the Anushilan Samiti. Inspired by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, he organized youth and adopted the path of armed revolution. He earned the title 'Bagha' (tiger) because he once killed a tiger with a dagger, showcasing his extraordinary bravery. He was martyred in 1915 in a police encounter near Balasore, Odisha. His legacy inspires Indian nationalists.
qs.kf:
☛ Real name of Bagha Jatin → Jatindranath Mukherjee
☛ Year of his death → 1915
☛ Organization he was associated with → Anushilan Samiti
☛ Reason for 'Bagha' title → Killed a tiger
☛ Place of martyrdom → Balasore, Odisha

q: In 1912, the 'Al-Hilal' newspaper was launched by whom?
qs.e: In 1912, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad launched the Urdu weekly newspaper 'Al-Hilal' from Calcutta. It became a powerful medium to spread political awareness among Indian Muslims against British rule. Azad was a prominent freedom fighter and served as the President of the Indian National Congress. In 1914, the British banned the newspaper, after which he started another newspaper named 'Paigham' in 1915. 'Al-Hilal' played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Al-Hilal → Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
☛ Year of publication of Al-Hilal → 1912
☛ Language of Al-Hilal → Urdu
☛ Place of publication of Al-Hilal → Calcutta
☛ Year of ban on Al-Hilal → 1914

q: The name of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) was changed to HSRA in 1928, in what exactly is the letter 'S' in it?
qs.e: In 1928, the name of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) was changed to Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). The letter 'S' stands for Socialist, reflecting the socialist ideology adopted by revolutionaries like Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad. The change was influenced by the Russian Revolution and the need for a broader egalitarian society. HSRA aimed at overthrowing British rule through armed struggle and establishing a socialist republic. The association was formed in Lahore and became famous for acts like the Central Assembly Bombing (1929).

q: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar, and Shivaram Rajguru were hanged for their role in -
qs.e: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar, and Shivaram Rajguru were hanged for their role in the Lahore Conspiracy Case. q: Who among the following chose the path of forming the army 'Azad Hind Fauj' to liberate India from the clutches of the British?
qs.e: Subhas Chandra Bose chose the path of forming the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) to liberate India from British rule. This army was primarily composed of Indian prisoners of war and civilians from Southeast Asia. Bose, with the help of Rash Behari Bose, reorganized the army and formally announced its formation in Singapore. Popularly known as Netaji, he established the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind Government) in 1943 and, with Japanese support, attempted to invade India. The slogan of the Azad Hind Fauj was “Chalo Delhi”, which inspired thousands. Bose believed that armed struggle was the only way to end British rule in India.

qs.e: Bhagat Singh was a prominent Indian revolutionary who fought against British rule. He was arrested in 1929 for throwing a bomb in the Central Assembly in Delhi. q: In which year did Ram Prasad Bismil and his comrades, including Ashfaqullah Khan, carry out the Kakori Train Action?
qs.e: The Kakori Train Action was carried out on August 9, 1925, at Kakori, Uttar Pradesh, by Ram Prasad Bismil and his comrades, including Ashfaqullah Khan. q: Which revolutionary along with Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Assembly in 1929?

q: This freedom fighter did not share Gandhi’s ideal of ‘ahimsa’ and ‘satyagraha’. In 1941, he left his Calcutta home to Singapore via Germany and raised the Indian National Army. The leader in question is:
qs.e: Subhash Chandra Bose did not share Mahatma Gandhi's ideals of ahimsa (non-violence) and satyagraha (passive resistance). He believed in armed struggle and formed the Indian National Army (INA). In 1941, he escaped from his Calcutta home and traveled to Singapore via Germany, where with Japanese assistance, he established the INA. His famous slogan 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom' inspired many. Bose also founded the Forward Bloc within the Indian National Congress. q: Which famous revolutionary set up base near Satar river in Jhansi in the 1920’s using the alias, Pandit Harishankar Brahmachari?
qs.e: Chandrashekhar Azad was a prominent revolutionary in the Indian independence movement. Azad was an active member of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) and later the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). He was involved in events like the Kakori Conspiracy, the Lahore Conspiracy Case, and the 1929 bombing of the Central Legislative Assembly. Born in 1906, he was martyred in 1931 at Alfred Park, Allahabad, in a police encounter. His real name was Chandrashekhar Tiwari, and he had taken a vow to never be captured alive by the British, adopting the surname 'Azad' meaning free.
