q: Which law has been called 'the highest law of the country' in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution itself is called the 'highest law of the country'. It is the supreme law of the land, under which all laws are made. According to Article 13(2) of the Constitution, any law that violates the provisions of the Constitution is void. In India, constitutional law is supreme, and it must be followed by the government, judiciary, and citizens alike. The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. It is the longest written constitution in the world. Constitutional law is the fundamental law of the country, which determines the validity of all other laws.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions 'supreme law'? → Article 13
☛ When did the Indian Constitution come into effect? → 26 January 1950
☛ When was the Indian Constitution adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ Which country has the longest written constitution? → India
☛ What does Article 13(2) of the Constitution state? → Laws against the Constitution are void

q: Who has called the preamble "essence" of the constitution
qs.e: The scholar who called the Preamble the 'essence' of the constitution is Sir Ernest Barker. In his book, he described the Preamble as the soul and core element of the constitution. The Preamble reflects the objectives and philosophy of the constitution. The Indian constitution's Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India' establishing the supremacy of the people. It enshrines the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. K.M. Munshi called the Preamble a 'political yardstick'. B.R. Ambedkar called it the 'keynote' of the constitution. Jawaharlal Nehru called it a 'solemn pledge'.
qs.kf:
☛ Who called the Preamble an 'identity card'? → N.A. Palkhivala
☛ Who called the Preamble a 'political yardstick'? → K.M. Munshi
☛ Who called the Preamble the 'keynote' of the constitution? → B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Who called the Preamble a 'solemn pledge'? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Which amendment added 'Socialist' to the Preamble? → 42nd Amendment, 1976

q: Who is the first President of Independent India?
qs.e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of independent India. He assumed office on 26 January 1950, when India became a republic. He was a prominent freedom fighter and a senior leader of the Indian National Congress. He also served as the President of the Constituent Assembly, playing a key role in drafting the Constitution. Dr. Prasad served as President for 12 years, making him the longest-serving President of India. He was born on 3 December 1884 and was actively involved in the Indian independence movement. He was also a skilled lawyer and academic. His tenure was marked by his dedication to national unity and development.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first President of India? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who was the first woman President of India? → Pratibha Devisingh Patil
☛ Who served as President for the longest term? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad (12 years)
☛ Who is the current President of India? → Droupadi Murmu (as of 2025)
☛ When did the first President assume office? → 26 January 1950

q: How many parts are there in the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The Constitution of India is the world's longest written constitution. It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. Originally, the Constitution had 22 parts, but after amendments, it currently has 25 parts. These parts cover various subjects such as Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and Centre-State relations. For example, Part III deals with Fundamental Rights, while Part IV covers Directive Principles. The Constitution also includes 12 schedules and over 470 articles.
qs.kf:
☛ Total parts in Indian Constitution → 25
☛ Original parts in Constitution → 22
☛ Total articles (original) → 395
☛ Current articles → Around 470
☛ Number of schedules → 12

q: From where in the preamble of our constitution, the ideals of freedom, equality and fraternity have been taken?
qs.e: The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution are derived from the French Revolution of 1789. The motto of the French Revolution was 'Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité'. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar advocated for the inclusion of these ideals in the Preamble. These principles are reflected in Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (Directive Principles) of the Constitution. The French Revolution inspired concepts of democracy, secularism, and social justice worldwide. The Indian Constitution guarantees liberty (of thought, expression, belief), equality (before law), and fraternity (dignity of individual) as fundamental rights.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the slogan of the French Revolution? → Liberty, Equality, Fraternity
☛ When was the Preamble of Indian Constitution adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ Fraternity in the Preamble is linked to which Article? → Article 51A (Fundamental Duties)
☛ Equality in the Preamble is mentioned in which Article? → Article 14
☛ Liberty in the Preamble begins from which Article? → Article 19

q: Indian socialism is a mixture of ________
qs.e: Indian socialism is a unique blend of Marxism and Gandhism. It rejects the extremes of capitalism and communism. From Marxism, it adopts the goal of economic equality and a classless society, while from Gandhism, it incorporates non-violence, sarvodaya (welfare of all), and decentralization. The term 'socialist' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment. Indian socialism does not abolish private property completely but emphasizes economic planning and social justice. This mixture suits India's diverse socio-economic conditions and aims to reduce inequality through peaceful means.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added 'socialist' to the Indian Constitution's Preamble? → 42nd Amendment
☛ What is the main principle of Gandhism? → Non-violence and sarvodaya
☛ What is the main goal of Marxism? → Classless society
☛ Indian socialism is a mixture of which two ideologies? → Marxism and Gandhism
☛ Who propounded the term 'sarvodaya'? → Mahatma Gandhi

q: The provision of judicial review in the Constitution of India was taken from _____
qs.e: The provision of judicial review in the Constitution of India was taken from the American Constitution. Judicial review empowers the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of laws passed by the legislature or executive. In the US, this power was established in the landmark case of Marbury v. Madison (1803). In India, the Supreme Court and High Courts have the power of judicial review under Articles 13, 32, and 226. This system ensures the supremacy of the Constitution and protects fundamental rights. The judiciary also uses judicial review to safeguard the basic structure of the Constitution, as established in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).
qs.kf:
☛ From which constitution is judicial review borrowed? → American
☛ Which case established judicial review in the US? → Marbury v. Madison (1803)
☛ Which articles in the Indian Constitution relate to judicial review? → Articles 13, 32, 226
☛ What is the scope of judicial review in India? → Subject to basic structure doctrine
☛ What is the purpose of judicial review? → To examine the constitutionality of laws

q: Who solemnly resolved the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with 'We, the People of India', signifying that the authority of the Constitution is derived from the citizens of India. The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, but the solemn resolution to enact it was made by the people of India themselves. This reflects the fundamental spirit of democracy where sovereignty lies with the people. The phrase 'We, the People of India' in the Preamble clearly declares that the Constitution is a gift of the people to themselves, embodying their collective will and determination.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Constitution adopted by the Constituent Assembly? → 26 November 1949
☛ What does 'We, the People of India' signify in the Preamble? → Sovereignty rests with the people
☛ When was the Indian Constitution enforced? → 26 January 1950
☛ What are the key words in the Preamble? → Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic
☛ Who was the permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad

q: Which term was replaced instead of "Unity of the Nation" in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
o: Unity and Integrity of the Nation
qs.e: In the original Preamble of the Indian Constitution, the phrase 'Unity of the Nation' was used. The 42nd Amendment (1976) replaced it with 'Unity and Integrity of the Nation' to emphasize both national unity and territorial integrity. This amendment, enacted during the Emergency, also added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. The change aimed to strengthen the country's sovereignty and territorial cohesion. The Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) had earlier upheld the Preamble as part of the Constitution but amendable. The inclusion of 'Integrity' highlights the indivisibility of the nation against separatist tendencies.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added 'Integrity' to the Preamble? → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ How many new words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment? → Three: Socialist, Secular, Integrity
☛ In which year was the 42nd Amendment enacted? → 1976
☛ What word was added before 'Unity' in the Preamble? → Integrity
☛ Which case declared the Preamble as part of the Constitution? → Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)

q: How many important committees were there in the Indian Constituent Assembly?
qs.e: The Indian Constituent Assembly had eight major committees that worked on different aspects of the constitution. The most important among them was the Drafting Committee headed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. The other committees included the Central Power Committee, Provincial Constitution Committee, Fundamental Rights Committee, Union Power Committee, Union Constitution Committee, Rules of Procedure Committee, and Steering Committee. These committees played a crucial role in framing various parts of the constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ Major committees of Constituent Assembly → 8
☛ Chairman of Drafting Committee → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Chairman of Fundamental Rights Committee → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Chairman of Union Power Committee → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Chairman of Rules of Procedure Committee → Rajendra Prasad

q: Which of the following government act permits the establishment of All India Federation in British India?
qs.e: The Government of India Act, 1935 was the first British legislation to propose the establishment of an All India Federation, comprising both British Indian provinces and princely states. Although the federation never fully materialized, this act laid the groundwork for a federal structure in India. Key features included provincial autonomy, a bicameral legislature, and a federal court. Other options: Government of India Act, 1919 introduced dyarchy; Indian Councils Act, 1892 expanded legislative councils; and Act for the Strong Government, 1858 transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown, ending company rule.
qs.kf:
☛ Name of the federation proposed in the Government of India Act, 1935 → All India Federation
☛ Key provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935 → Provincial autonomy and federal court
☛ Main feature of the Government of India Act, 1919 → Dyarchy
☛ Purpose of the Indian Councils Act, 1892 → Increase members of legislative councils
☛ Effect of the Act for the Strong Government, 1858 → Transfer of Indian governance to British Crown

q: Which was the First Constitution to begin with a preamble?
qs.e: The American Constitution (1787) is the first constitution in the world to begin with a preamble. Its preamble starts with the words "We the People", reflecting democracy and popular sovereignty. The preamble outlines the objectives and philosophy of the constitution, such as justice, liberty, and peace. Later, many countries, including India (1950), included a preamble in their constitutions. The Irish Constitution (1937) also has a preamble, but it came after the American Constitution. The British Constitution is unwritten and has no formal preamble.
qs.kf:
☛ Which was the first written constitution? → American Constitution
☛ When was the American Constitution adopted? → 1787
☛ Who inspired the Preamble of the Indian Constitution? → American Constitution
☛ What is the nature of the British Constitution? → Unwritten and uncodified
☛ Which constitution's preamble has 'We the People'? → American Constitution

q: The format of the parliamentary system of government described in the Indian Constitution was drafted on the basis of which constitution?
qs.e: The parliamentary system in India is based on the British Westminster system. In this system, the executive is responsible to the legislature. The President is the constitutional head, while the Prime Minister is the real executive head. This system is inspired by the unwritten conventions and practices of the British Constitution. The framers of the Indian Constitution adopted it because it ensures stable government and democratic accountability. In a parliamentary system, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Parliament. The main reason for adopting this system in India was prior experience under British rule.
qs.kf:
☛ From which country is India's parliamentary system borrowed? → Britain
☛ Who is the real executive head in India? → Prime Minister
☛ Who is the constitutional head of India? → President
☛ What is the British parliamentary system also known as? → Westminster system
☛ Under which articles is the parliamentary system described in the Indian Constitution? → Articles 74 and 75

q: When was the Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir adopted?
qs.e: The Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir was adopted on November 17, 1956. It came into effect on January 26, 1957. It was drafted by the Jammu and Kashmir Constituent Assembly. This constitution defined the special status of the state of Jammu and Kashmir under the Constitution of India. The state had special autonomy under Article 370. On August 5, 2019, Article 370 was abrogated and Jammu and Kashmir was reorganized into two union territories.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Jammu and Kashmir Constitution come into effect? → January 26, 1957
☛ Who was the chairman of the Jammu and Kashmir Constituent Assembly? → Maulana Mohammad Saeed Masoodi
☛ Who was the last Governor of Jammu and Kashmir? → Satya Pal Malik
☛ When was the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act passed? → August 5, 2019
☛ What special status did Article 370 grant to Jammu and Kashmir? → Temporary and special autonomy

q: When did the implementation of the Indian Constitution formally came into effect ?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949, but was formally implemented on 26 January 1950. This date was chosen to commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj by the Indian National Congress in 1930. With its implementation, India became a sovereign democratic republic. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was appointed as the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution. Fundamental Rights are listed in Part III of the Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Constitution adopted by the Constituent Assembly? → 26 November 1949
☛ What is the date of implementation of the Constitution? → 26 January 1950
☛ Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
☛ In which year was Purna Swaraj declared? → 1930
☛ Who is known as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution? → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

q: The idea of constitution of India's Constituent Assembly was first presented by whom?
qs.e: The idea of constituting a Constituent Assembly for India was first proposed by Manabendra Nath Roy in 1934. He was an Indian revolutionary, philosopher, and political theorist. He suggested to the Indian National Congress that a Constituent Assembly should be formed to draft India's constitution. This idea was later officially adopted by the Congress in 1935. The Constituent Assembly was eventually formed in 1946 and adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949. Roy's contribution was significant as he was the first to conceptualize this idea, which played a crucial role in India's constitutional development.
qs.kf:
☛ Who proposed the idea of Constituent Assembly in 1934? → Manabendra Nath Roy
☛ When was the Constituent Assembly formed? → 1946
☛ When was the Indian Constitution adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ Which movement was Manabendra Nath Roy associated with? → Revolutionary movement
☛ Who was the first President of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad

q: Which of the following states does not have a provision in the Sixth Schedule of Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions for the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. It provides for the formation of autonomous councils to govern these regions. Sikkim was integrated into India in 1975 and its special provisions are covered under Article 371F, not under the Sixth Schedule. Hence, Sikkim does not have any provision in the Sixth Schedule. Among the options, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Assam are included in the Sixth Schedule, while Sikkim is not.
qs.kf:
☛ Which states are covered under the Sixth Schedule? → Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
☛ Which article provides special provisions for Sikkim? → Article 371F
☛ What does the Sixth Schedule deal with? → Administration of tribal areas
☛ When was Sikkim merged with India? → 1975
☛ Which Schedule contains provisions for tribal areas? → Sixth Schedule

q: Which of the following model is based on the Indian federal system?
qs.e: The Indian federal system is based on the Canadian model. India has a federal structure where powers are divided between the centre and states as per the constitution. Like Canada, India has a strong centre with more powers vested in the central government. Article 1 of the Indian Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States' and not a 'Federal State'. The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution divides powers through the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. Thus, the foundation of Indian federalism is the Canadian model.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country's model is the basis of Indian federal system? → Canada
☛ In which schedule is the division of powers in India? → Seventh Schedule
☛ Under which Article is India called a 'Union of States'? → Article 1
☛ Which model inspired a strong centre in India? → Canadian model
☛ How many subjects are in the Union List of Indian Constitution? → 100 (originally 97)

q: What was the total expenditure in the construction of Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The total expenditure incurred in the formation of the Indian Constitution was 6.4 million rupees (approximately 64 lakh rupees). This amount was spent on the formation of the Constituent Assembly, meetings of various committees, appointment of experts, printing, and other administrative tasks. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946, and the last meeting on 26 November 1949. The drafting of the Constitution took a total of 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days, with 165 days of sessions. Initially, the Constituent Assembly had 389 members, which reduced to 299 after partition. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly? → 9 December 1946
☛ How much time was taken to frame the Constitution? → 2 years, 11 months, 18 days
☛ How many members initially in the Constituent Assembly? → 389
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ When did the Constitution come into effect? → 26 January 1950

q: Who was the temporary president of the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly held on December 09, 1946?
qs.e: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946. Being the eldest member, Sachchidanand Sinha was elected as the temporary president to preside over the meeting. He served until Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent president on 11 December 1946. Sachchidanand Sinha was a senior leader from Bihar and a member of the Indian National Congress. His role as interim chairman was crucial in the initial proceedings of the Assembly.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of first Constituent Assembly meeting → 9 December 1946
☛ Temporary president of Constituent Assembly → Sachchidanand Sinha
☛ Permanent president of Constituent Assembly → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Constituent Assembly formed under → Cabinet Mission Plan 1946
☛ Total members of Constituent Assembly → 389 (later reduced to 299)

q: The provision of 'amendment in Indian constitution' was taken from which country's constitution?
qs.e: India's constitutional amendment process is borrowed from the Constitution of South Africa. The amendment procedure in Article 368 (Part XX) requires a special majority in Parliament and, in some cases, ratification by states. This model of flexible yet rigid amendment was inspired by South Africa's constitution. In contrast, the Weimar Constitution of Germany influenced emergency provisions, the American Constitution provided fundamental rights, and the USSR Constitution contributed fundamental duties. The borrowing of the amendment provision reflects India's adaptability in framing its supreme law.
qs.kf:
☛ From which constitution is India's amendment procedure taken? → South Africa
☛ Which article deals with constitutional amendment? → Article 368
☛ Which part of Indian Constitution covers amendments? → Part XX
☛ What other feature is borrowed from South Africa? → Election of Rajya Sabha members
☛ Which provision is taken from Weimar Constitution? → Emergency powers

q: The principle of Directive Principle of State Policy was taken from which the constitution of which country?
qs.e: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution (Part IV, Articles 36-51) were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. The Irish Constitution of 1937 incorporated principles of social and economic justice. The Indian Constituent Assembly adopted these principles to guide the state in policy-making. These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, but they are fundamental in governance. Other options: Fundamental Rights from the USA, Parliamentary system from the UK, and Socialist ideology from the USSR.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Irish Constitution enacted? → 1937
☛ Which part of Indian Constitution contains DPSPs? → Part IV
☛ Are Directive Principles enforceable in court? → No
☛ Which article deals with organisation of village panchayats? → Article 40
☛ Which article deals with equal justice and free legal aid? → Article 39A

q: When the Indian Constitution came into effect in 1949, how many Articles were there in it?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. At the time of its enforcement, the Constitution had 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. It was drafted by the Constituent Assembly over 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Over time, amendments have increased the number of Articles, but originally there were 395. Options 200 and 947 are incorrect; 1000 is also not correct. This is a common fact asked in competitive exams.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of Parts at commencement → 22
☛ Number of Schedules at commencement → 8
☛ Chairman of Drafting Committee → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ First meeting of Constituent Assembly → 9 December 1946
☛ Time taken to frame the Constitution → 2 years 11 months 18 days

q: In respect of the control and administration of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Tribes in any state, what are the provisions of the Indian Constitution given?
qs.e: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Tribes in any state except Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. It provides for the declaration of Scheduled Areas, their administration, and the establishment of Tribes Advisory Councils. The President has the power to make regulations for the governance of these areas. The Sixth Schedule is for tribal areas in northeastern states, the Eighth Schedule deals with languages, and the Fifteenth Schedule relates to municipalities. Thus, the correct answer is the Fifth Schedule.
qs.kf:
☛ Which states are excluded from the Fifth Schedule? → Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
☛ Who can declare an area as Scheduled Area under Fifth Schedule? → President
☛ Which schedule provides for Tribes Advisory Council? → Fifth Schedule
☛ Which schedule is for tribal areas in northeastern states? → Sixth Schedule
☛ How many languages are in the Eighth Schedule? → 22

q: According to Indian Constitution, India is-
qs.e: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution declares India as a Secular State. This means the state does not adopt any particular religion as the official religion. Articles 25 to 28 of the Constitution provide the right to freedom of religion. All citizens have the equal right to practice, profess, and propagate their religion. The state remains neutral in religious matters and treats all religions equally. This principle helps in maintaining the cultural diversity of India. The term 'secular' was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. India follows a model of positive secularism, where the state respects all religions and does not interfere in their affairs.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added 'secular' to the Preamble? → 42nd Amendment (1976).
☛ Article 25 deals with? → Freedom of conscience and religion.
☛ Which article prohibits religious taxes? → Article 27.
☛ Article 28 restricts what? → Religious instruction in educational institutions.
☛ Which model of secularism does India follow? → Positive secularism (equal respect for all religions).

q: In which of the following countries was the provision of 'single citizenship' in the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The provision of single citizenship in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the British Constitution. In Britain, there is a system of single citizenship where all citizens enjoy equal rights. In contrast, the Russian Constitution and the Constitution of Germany allow dual citizenship, while the Irish Constitution also provides for dual citizenship. Single citizenship in India means that there is only one citizenship for the entire country, not separate citizenships for states. This provision strengthens unity in diversity and grants equal rights to citizens across the nation.
qs.kf:
☛ From which country did India borrow single citizenship? → Britain
☛ Which countries allow dual citizenship? → Russia and Germany
☛ Which part of Indian Constitution deals with citizenship? → Part 2 (Articles 5-11)
☛ Which act governs citizenship in India? → Citizenship Act, 1955
☛ What is the advantage of single citizenship? → Equal rights and duties across the country

q: When the Indian Constitution was adopted in 1949, how many schedule were there in the Constitution?
qs.e: When the Indian Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949, it contained only 8 Schedules. Over time, through various amendments, the number of schedules has increased. Currently, the Constitution has a total of 12 Schedules. Schedules are an integral part of the Constitution, providing detailed administrative and legal provisions. The original Constitution had 22 Parts and 395 Articles. The primary function of schedules is to clarify constitutional provisions and assist in their implementation.
qs.kf:
☛ How many schedules are there in the Indian Constitution currently? → 12
☛ How many articles were in the original Constitution? → 395
☛ How many parts were in the original Constitution? → 22
☛ What is described in the First Schedule? → Details of states and union territories
☛ What is in the Second Schedule? → Salaries and allowances of President, Governors, etc.

q: In the Indian Constitution, the provision for suspending the fundamental rights during the Emergency has been taken from _____.
o: Constitution of the Soviet Socialist Republic (USSR) Association
qs.e: The provision in the Indian Constitution for suspending fundamental rights during an Emergency is borrowed from the Weimar Constitution of Germany. This provision is covered under Article 359, which empowers the President to suspend the enforcement of fundamental rights during an Emergency. However, Articles 20 and 21 (right to life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended. This provision is a crucial part of India's Emergency powers, outlined in Part XVIII of the Constitution. India adapted this concept from Germany's Weimar Constitution to suit its own needs, ensuring a balance between national security and individual rights.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article of the Indian Constitution suspends the enforcement of fundamental rights during an Emergency? → Article 359
☛ Which fundamental rights cannot be suspended during an Emergency? → Articles 20 and 21
☛ Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with Emergency provisions? → Part XVIII
☛ From which country did India borrow the idea of suspending fundamental rights during an Emergency? → Germany (Weimar Constitution)
☛ Under which Article is a National Emergency proclaimed? → Article 352

q: Who called the Preamble 'the identity card' of Indian Constitution?
qs.e: N. A. Palkhivala (1910-1994) was a renowned Indian jurist and economist. He called the Preamble of the Indian Constitution 'the identity card' because it reflects the soul and core principles of the Constitution. The Preamble declares India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic and outlines the objectives of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. Palkhivala considered the Preamble as the key document of the Constitution, summarizing the guiding principles of governance. He compared it to an identity card that defines the nation's identity and aspirations. Palkhivala also argued in favor of the basic structure doctrine in the landmark Keshavananda Bharati case (1974). The Preamble holds a central place in constitutional interpretation and is often referred to as the soul of the Constitution. It encapsulates the philosophy and vision of the framers, serving as a beacon for the nation's journey.
qs.kf:
☛ Who called the Preamble 'the identity card' of the Constitution? → N. A. Palkhivala
☛ Which three words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment (1976)? → Socialist, Secular, Integrity
☛ How many objectives are mentioned in the Preamble? → Four: Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity
☛ What is the opening phrase of the Preamble? → We, the People of India
☛ What was the language of the original Preamble? → English; Hindi translation was adopted in 1955

q: What does the secular state mean?
qs.e: A secular state means that the state does not adopt any religion as official and remains neutral towards all religions. It grants religious freedom to citizens and does not discriminate on the basis of religion. The Indian Constitution ensures secularism through fundamental rights (Articles 25-28). It directs the state to refrain from interfering in religious matters and to provide equal protection to all religions. The goal of secularism is to promote social harmony and unity. India follows positive secularism, which respects all religions equally rather than being irreligious.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is secularism defined in the Indian Constitution? → In the Preamble
☛ When was the word 'secular' added to the Constitution? → By the 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ What does Article 25 provide? → Right to freedom of religion
☛ What is the main principle of a secular state? → Equal treatment of all religions
☛ What type of secular state is India? → Positive secularism (respects all religions)

q: Which part of the Indian Constitution is called the 'identity card' of the Constitution?
qs.e: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution is called the 'identity card' or 'soul' of the Constitution. It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. The Preamble declares India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic. It outlines the objectives of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'. The Preamble serves as a guiding principle and shows that the power of the Constitution is derived from the people of India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Preamble adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ How many words are in the Preamble? → Approximately 80 words
☛ Which three words were added by the 42nd Amendment? → Socialist, Secular, Integrity
☛ What is the language of the Preamble? → English
☛ Who drafted the Preamble? → Jawaharlal Nehru (Objective Resolution)

q: What was the first constitution of the world to start with the introduction?
qs.e: The American Constitution (1787) is the first written constitution in the world to begin with an introduction or Preamble. Its Preamble starts with "We the People," symbolizing popular sovereignty. Before this, no constitution had a Preamble. Britain's constitution is unwritten, while African and Russian constitutions came later. The American Constitution used the Preamble to state its objectives and philosophy, which later became a model for other countries.
qs.kf:
☛ First constitution with a Preamble → American Constitution (1787)
☛ Opening words of American Preamble → "We the People"
☛ World's first written constitution → American Constitution
☛ Which country has an unwritten constitution? → Britain
☛ American Constitution came into effect → 1789

q: Which of the following is not contribute to the larger size of the Indian Constitution?
o: One Constitution for Central and States
qs.e: The Indian Constitution is the world's largest written constitution. Key factors contributing to its large size include Historical Factors, such as provisions borrowed from the Government of India Act 1935, Geographic and social diversity requiring detailed policies, and One Constitution for both Centre and States. Health factors do not contribute to the size of the Constitution; health policies are mentioned in the Directive Principles but do not affect its length.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Indian Constitution adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ How many Articles are in the Indian Constitution? → 448 Articles
☛ How many Schedules are in the Indian Constitution? → 12 Schedules

q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution includes the terms 'Justice', 'Liberty', and 'Equality', which reflect its core objectives. It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and later amended by the 42nd Amendment (1976) to add 'Secular' and 'Socialist'. The Preamble declares India as a 'Sovereign', 'Democratic', 'Republic'. The word 'Provision' is not a part of the Preamble; it appears elsewhere in the Constitution. Hence, option 4 is correct because it is not part of the Preamble.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Preamble adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ Which two words were added by the 42nd Amendment? → Socialist and Secular
☛ How many types of Justice are mentioned in the Preamble? → Social, Economic, and Political
☛ How many dimensions of Liberty are in the Preamble? → Five: thought, expression, belief, worship, and association
☛ What type of Equality is mentioned in the Preamble? → Equality of opportunity and dignity

q: Who was the Chairman of Finance and Staff Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly set up various committees to manage its work. The Finance and Staff Committee was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who later became the first President of India. This committee oversaw the budget and staff matters of the Assembly. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was also the President of the Constituent Assembly. Among the other options, H.C. Mukherjee was a member of the Drafting Committee; J.B. Kripalani was a politician; and K.M. Munshi was a member of the Constituent Assembly.
qs.kf:
☛ Chairman of Finance and Staff Committee → Rajendra Prasad
☛ President of Constituent Assembly → Rajendra Prasad
☛ Chairman of Drafting Committee → B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Chairman of Provincial Constitution Committee → C. Rajagopalachari
☛ Chairman of Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee → J.B. Kripalani

q: When did the Constitution of India come into force?
qs.e: The Constitution of India came into force on January 26, 1950. This day is celebrated as Republic Day. With its enforcement, India became a sovereign republic. The Constituent Assembly had adopted the Constitution on November 26, 1949, but it was fully enforced on January 26, 1950. This date was chosen to commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj in 1930. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the chairman of the Drafting Committee. At the time of enforcement, C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General of India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Constitution adopted by the Constituent Assembly? → November 26, 1949
☛ When did the Constitution of India come into force? → January 26, 1950
☛ Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ When was the Purna Swaraj declaration made? → January 26, 1930
☛ Who was the Governor-General when the Constitution was enforced? → C. Rajagopalachari

q: Which special date was selected for the implementation of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution was implemented on January 26, 1950. This date was chosen because on this day in 1930, the Indian National Congress had declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence). The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on November 26, 1949, but it was enforced on January 26, 1950. This day is celebrated as Republic Day. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is regarded as the chief architect of the Constitution. With the enforcement of the Constitution, India became a sovereign, democratic republic.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of adoption of Constitution by Constituent Assembly? → November 26, 1949
☛ Chairman of the Drafting Committee of Indian Constitution? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ When was Purna Swaraj declared? → January 26, 1930
☛ When is Republic Day celebrated? → January 26
☛ When did the Indian Constitution come into effect? → January 26, 1950

q: Who demanded the Constituent Assembly to officially construct the Constitution?
qs.e: The Indian National Congress was the first to demand the formation of a Constituent Assembly. At its 1936 Lucknow session, the Congress resolved that the Constitution of India should be framed by a Constituent Assembly elected by the people. In 1946, under the Cabinet Mission Plan, the Constituent Assembly was established. Congress leader Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objective Resolution in 1946, which guided the constitution-making process. Other options like Extremists or Swaraj Party did not raise this demand in an organized manner.
qs.kf:
☛ Who first demanded a Constituent Assembly? → Indian National Congress in 1936
☛ Under which plan was the Constituent Assembly formed? → Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)
☛ Who moved the Objective Resolution? → Jawaharlal Nehru (1946)
☛ Who was the permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar

q: The concept of 'rule of law' is taken from which country's constitution?
qs.e: The concept of 'rule of law' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the British Constitution. This principle establishes that law is supreme and no individual is above the law. British constitutional expert A.V. Dicey clearly propounded this concept. Article 14 of the Indian Constitution, which guarantees the right to equality, is based on this principle. The rule of law ensures that the government cannot act arbitrarily and all citizens are treated equally. This concept is considered the cornerstone of a democratic system.
qs.kf:
☛ Who gave the concept of rule of law? → A.V. Dicey
☛ Under which Article is the rule of law mentioned in India? → Article 14
☛ What does rule of law mean? → No one is above the law
☛ From which constitution is the rule of law borrowed? → British Constitution
☛ Rule of law is related to which right? → Right to equality

q: Which of the following is not part of the preamble of the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution mentions Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity. These are the core objectives of the Constitution. The Indian Flag (Tricolor) is not part of the Preamble; it is a national symbol adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947. The Preamble was adopted on 26 November 1949 and reflects the philosophy and goals of the Constitution. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the words Socialist, Secular, and Integrity to the Preamble.
qs.kf:
☛ What words are mentioned in the Preamble? → Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity
☛ When was the Preamble adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ Which amendment added 'Secular' to the Preamble? → 42nd Amendment, 1976
☛ When was the Indian Flag adopted? → 22 July 1947
☛ What is the main purpose of the Preamble? → To state the philosophy and objectives of the Constitution

q: Under which schedule of the Constitution of India comes the names of states and their territorial jurisdiction?
qs.e: The First Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the names of states and union territories along with their territorial jurisdiction. It describes the boundaries and areas of the states. Other schedules deal with different subjects: the Second Schedule deals with salaries and allowances, the Third Schedule with oaths, the Fourth Schedule with allocation of Rajya Sabha seats, the Fifth Schedule with administration of Scheduled Tribes areas, and the Ninth Schedule with land reforms. The First Schedule is crucial for understanding the federal structure of the Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ First Schedule relates to → Names and territorial jurisdiction of states
☛ Second Schedule relates to → Salaries, allowances, and pensions
☛ Fourth Schedule relates to → Allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha
☛ Fifth Schedule relates to → Administration of Scheduled Tribes areas
☛ Ninth Schedule relates to → Land reforms and other laws

q: Who was the President of the Order of Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly formed various committees to conduct its business smoothly. Among them, the Order of Business Committee was responsible for determining the agenda and order of proceedings of the Assembly. The President (Chairman) of this committee was KM Munshi, a prominent Assembly member and jurist. His full name was Kanhaiyalal Maniklal Munshi. He hailed from Gujarat and made significant contributions to the framing of the Indian Constitution. Other leaders had different roles: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the Chairman of the Advisory Committee, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly, and Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was the Chairman of the Union Powers Committee. Thus, KM Munshi is the correct answer for the Order of Business Committee.
qs.kf:
☛ Chairman of the Drafting Committee → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
☛ Interim President of Constituent Assembly → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Permanent President of Constituent Assembly → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Chairman of Steering Committee → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Chairman of National Flag Committee → Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru

q: The suspension of fundamental rights has been taken from which Constitution?
qs.e: The concept of suspension of fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from Germany's Weimar Constitution of 1919. The Weimar Constitution had provisions to suspend certain fundamental rights during emergency. Under Article 359 of the Indian Constitution, the President can suspend the enforcement of fundamental rights (except those under Articles 20 and 21) during a national emergency (Article 352). This borrowing reflects the influence of the Weimar Constitution on India's emergency provisions. The Constitution of India adopted several features from the Weimar Constitution, including the suspension of rights during emergencies.
qs.kf:
☛ From which constitution is the suspension of fundamental rights borrowed? → Germany's Weimar Constitution
☛ Under which Article can fundamental rights be suspended in India? → Article 359
☛ Which Articles can never be suspended? → Articles 20 and 21
☛ Under which Article is national emergency described? → Article 352
☛ Which country's constitution was the Weimar Constitution? → Germany

q: Which constitution has been adopted in the constitution to amend the constitution and the election of members of the Rajya Sabha?
qs.e: India adopted the procedure for constitutional amendment and the method of electing Rajya Sabha members from the South African Constitution. The amendment process requires a special majority in both houses of Parliament and, in some cases, ratification by states. Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies using the single transferable vote system. These features were inspired by the South African model. Among other options, the Canadian Constitution provided the federal system, the American Constitution provided fundamental rights and judicial review, and the British Constitution provided the parliamentary system.
qs.kf:
☛ From which constitution did India borrow the amendment procedure? → South Africa
☛ From which constitution is the Rajya Sabha election method taken? → South Africa
☛ How are Rajya Sabha members elected? → Single transferable vote
☛ Feature taken from South African Constitution? → Amendment process & Rajya Sabha election
☛ Source of federal system in Indian Constitution? → Canada

q: Who was the Chairman of the Draft Committee?
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly of India, formed in 1946, drafted the Indian Constitution. It constituted several committees, among which the Drafting Committee was the most important. Formed on 29 August 1947, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was appointed as its Chairman. He is revered as the chief architect or 'Father' of the Indian Constitution. Other members of the Drafting Committee included K.M. Munshi, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The President of the Constituent Assembly was Rajendra Prasad, while Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ When was the Drafting Committee formed? → 29 August 1947
☛ Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who moved the Objectives Resolution? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ How many committees were there in the Constituent Assembly? → 13 committees

q: Who has presided over the Union Power Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly of India formed several committees to efficiently carry out its work. Among these, the Union Powers Committee was a key committee responsible for deliberating on the distribution of powers between the center and the states. Its chairman was Jawaharlal Nehru, who was also the Prime Minister of the interim government and advocated for a strong center. Among the other options, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee and the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee, B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, and K.M. Munshi was a member of the Constituent Assembly. This committee's recommendations significantly influenced the federal structure of the Indian Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Union Powers Committee? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Provincial Constitution Committee? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ How many main committees did the Constituent Assembly have? → 13 main committees

q: In which year was the Federal Court of India established?
qs.e: The Federal Court of India was established in 1937 under the Government of India Act 1935. It was located in Delhi and its primary function was to resolve disputes between provinces and the central government. The first Chief Justice of the Federal Court was Sir Maurice Gwyer. The Federal Court functioned from 1937 until 1950, when it was replaced by the Supreme Court of India. The Supreme Court came into existence on 26 January 1950 after the adoption of the Constitution of India. The Federal Court consisted of a maximum of six judges, including the Chief Justice.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which act was the Federal Court of India established? → Government of India Act 1935
☛ Where was the headquarters of the Federal Court? → Delhi
☛ Who was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court? → Sir Maurice Gwyer
☛ Which court replaced the Federal Court? → Supreme Court (1950)
☛ What was the maximum number of judges in the Federal Court? → Six

q: Under which of the following paragraphs was the provision of setting up of the National Scheduled Castes (ST) Commission?
qs.e: Article 338 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (SC). This commission monitors the constitutional safeguards for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Originally, it provided for a Special Officer for SCs only, but the 65th Amendment Act, 1990 replaced it with a multi-member commission. The 89th Amendment Act, 2003 divided the commission into two separate bodies: one for SCs and one for STs. The commission works to protect the rights and ensure the welfare of these communities. It submits its report to the President. The President appoints the chairperson and members.
qs.kf:
☛ Amendment that divided SC Commission → 89th Amendment, 2003
☛ Who appoints the chairperson of SC Commission → President
☛ Term of members of SC Commission → 3 years
☛ To whom does the SC Commission submit its report → President
☛ Article 338 deals with → National Commission for Scheduled Castes

q: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly took place on ______.
qs.e: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly of India took place on December 9, 1946. The meeting was held at the Constitution House (now Parliament House) in New Delhi. The session was chaired by Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, who served as the temporary President. A total of 211 members were present on that day. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was later elected as the permanent President on December 11, 1946. The Constituent Assembly was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan and adopted the Constitution on November 26, 1949.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of first meeting of Constituent Assembly → December 9, 1946
☛ Temporary President → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Permanent President elected on → December 11, 1946
☛ Constitution adopted on → November 26, 1949
☛ Constituent Assembly under which plan → Cabinet Mission Plan

q: The total number of members of the Constituent Assembly was ______.
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly of India was formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. Its total membership was 389, consisting of 292 members from the provinces of British India, 93 members from the princely states, and 4 members from the chief commissioner provinces. After the partition of India in 1947, its strength was reduced to 299. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946, and its last meeting on 24 January 1950. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was its permanent chairman. The Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to frame the Constitution of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Total members of Constituent Assembly → 389
☛ Members from British Indian provinces → 292
☛ Members from princely states → 93
☛ Members after partition → 299
☛ First meeting of Constituent Assembly → 9 December 1946

q: The word 'preamble' means ______.
qs.e: The preamble is the introductory part of the Constitution that states its purposes, ideals, and philosophy. It is called the soul of the Constitution. The Indian Constitution's preamble was adopted on 26 November 1949 and was amended once by the 42nd Amendment (1976), adding the words socialist, secular, and integrity. The preamble emphasizes justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. It serves as a guiding principle for the interpretation of the Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ How many times has the Preamble been amended? → Once (in 1976)
☛ Which three words were added to the Preamble? → Socialist, Secular, Integrity
☛ From which constitution is the Preamble borrowed? → USA
☛ When was the Indian Preamble adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ What is the Preamble called? → Soul/Guiding principle of the Constitution

q: The Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir came into force from ________.
qs.e: The Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir was adopted on 17 November 1956 and came into force on 26 January 1957. It provided special status to the state under Article 370 of the Indian Constitution, granting separate citizenship, flag, and penal code. The constitution was framed by a Constituent Assembly elected in 1951. After the abrogation of Article 370 on 5 August 2019, the Jammu and Kashmir Constitution became ineffective, and the state was reorganized into two Union Territories.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Jammu and Kashmir Constitution adopted? → 17 November 1956
☛ When did the Jammu and Kashmir Constitution come into force? → 26 January 1957
☛ When was Article 370 abrogated? → 5 August 2019
☛ Who was the President of the Jammu and Kashmir Constituent Assembly? → Sheikh Abdullah
☛ How many articles are in the Jammu and Kashmir Constitution? → 158

q: How many schedules are currently there in the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The Constitution of India currently has 12 Schedules. At the time of its adoption, there were only 8 Schedules. Later, amendments added more schedules. The Ninth Schedule was added by the First Amendment (1951), the Tenth Schedule by the 52nd Amendment (1985) (anti-defection law), the Eleventh Schedule by the 73rd Amendment (1992) (Panchayati Raj), and the Twelfth Schedule by the 74th Amendment (1992) (Municipalities). These schedules cover various subjects such as names of states, center-state relations, languages, land reforms, etc.
qs.kf:
☛ Schedule added by the First Amendment → Ninth Schedule
☛ Schedule added by the 52nd Amendment → Tenth Schedule (Anti-defection)
☛ Schedule added by the 73rd Amendment → Eleventh Schedule (Panchayats)
☛ Schedule added by the 74th Amendment → Twelfth Schedule (Municipalities)
☛ Number of Schedules at the time of adoption of Constitution → 8

q: Which of the following is CORRECT with respect to the Indian Constitution?
o: It is completely based on British Constitution
It is completely based on Constitution of Canada
It is made only on the basis of Government of India Act, 1935
It is a mixture of several Constitutions
qs.e: The Indian Constitution is inspired by various constitutions of the world, hence it is considered a mixture of several constitutions. It is not completely based on any single constitution or act. Features like parliamentary system from Britain, federal system from Canada, fundamental rights and judicial review from the USA, directive principles of state policy from Ireland, republic from France, and concurrent list from Australia were incorporated. While the Government of India Act, 1935 contributed many structural provisions, the constitution is not solely based on it. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described it as the essence of the best constitutions.
qs.kf:
☛ Main feature of Indian Constitution → Mixture of several constitutions
☛ Main source of Indian Constitution → Government of India Act, 1935
☛ Parliamentary system borrowed from → Britain
☛ Fundamental rights borrowed from → USA
☛ Directive principles borrowed from → Ireland

q: Who is considered as the architect of the Indian Constitution
qs.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is considered the architect of the Indian Constitution. He was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly. He played a crucial role in drafting the constitution. Ambedkar was a jurist, economist, and social reformer. He is also known as the Father of the Indian Constitution. He fought for the rights of Dalits and marginalized communities. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the temporary president of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Who was the permanent president of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ How many members were in the Drafting Committee? → 7
☛ When did the Indian Constitution come into effect? → 26 January 1950
☛ When was the Constituent Assembly formed? → 1946

q: India became a Sovereign Democratic Republic on -
qs.e: India became a Sovereign Democratic Republic on 26 January 1950. On this day, the Constitution of India came into effect, declaring India fully independent and democratic. India gained independence on 15 August 1947, but it remained a British Dominion. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949, but it was enforced on 26 January 1950. This date was chosen because on the same day in 1929, the Indian National Congress passed the Purna Swaraj declaration. Thus, 26 January 1950 is when India truly became a sovereign democratic republic.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Constitution of India come into effect? → 26 January 1950
☛ When was Purna Swaraj declared? → 26 January 1929
☛ Who was the first President of India? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ When was the Constitution adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ When was democracy established in India? → 26 January 1950

q: ______ presided over the first meeting of the Indian Constitue
qs.e: The first meeting of the Indian Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946. It was presided over by Sachchidananda Sinha as the temporary chairman, because the permanent chairman had not yet been elected. He was the oldest member of the Assembly, and according to procedure, the senior-most member acted as the provisional president. Later, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent chairman. The meeting took place at the Constitution House (formerly Council House) in New Delhi. A total of 211 members attended the first session. Sachchidananda Sinha was a prominent lawyer and leader from Bihar, and played a key role in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first meeting of the Indian Constituent Assembly held? → 9 December 1946
☛ Who was the permanent chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ How many members attended the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly? → 211
☛ Where was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly held? → Constitution House, New Delhi
☛ Which state did Sachchidananda Sinha belong to? → Bihar

q: From which Constitution did the Constitution of India borrow the scheme of Federation?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution adopted the scheme of federation from the Canadian Constitution. From Canada, India borrowed the federal structure, residual powers with the centre, and the system of appointment of governors. India is a quasi-federal state with a strong central government. This model is based on the Canadian system where residual powers lie with the federal government. Additionally, emergency provisions and the concept of single citizenship were also taken from Canada. The Constituent Assembly selected the best features from various constitutions to frame the Indian Constitution. The Canadian federal model was found suitable for India as it promotes unity in diversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Federal scheme borrowed from? → Canada
☛ Residual powers with centre from? → Canada
☛ Appointment of governors from? → Canada
☛ Emergency provisions from? → Canada
☛ Single citizenship from? → Canada

q: In India, the concept-of single citizenship is adopted from-
qs.e: The concept of single citizenship in India is adopted from the United Kingdom. It means that there is one uniform citizenship for the entire country, regardless of the state of residence. Despite being a federal system, India provides for single citizenship to promote national unity. The provisions related to citizenship are enshrined in Articles 5 to 11 of the Indian Constitution. In contrast, countries like the United States have dual citizenship (state and federal). Single citizenship ensures that all citizens enjoy equal rights and duties, strengthening the unity and integrity of the nation.
qs.kf:
☛ From which country is single citizenship adopted? → United Kingdom
☛ Which articles deal with citizenship in India? → Articles 5 to 11
☛ Which country has dual citizenship (state and federal)? → United States (USA)
☛ What is the purpose of single citizenship? → To promote national unity and integrity
☛ In which part of the Indian Constitution is citizenship mentioned? → Part II

q: Fundamental Duties of Indian Constitution were taken from -
qs.e: The Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976). These duties were inspired from the constitution of the former Soviet Union (Russia). India has 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution. The concept of fundamental duties was borrowed from socialist countries, which emphasize both rights and duties of citizens. This feature reminds citizens of their obligations towards the nation. The duties were incorporated based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'Mini-Constitution' due to its wide-ranging changes.
qs.kf:
☛ From which country were the Fundamental Duties taken? → Russia (former Soviet Union)
☛ When were Fundamental Duties added in India? → 1976 via 42nd Amendment
☛ Under which Article are Fundamental Duties listed? → Article 51A
☛ How many Fundamental Duties are there? → 11
☛ In which Part are Fundamental Duties mentioned? → Part IV-A

q: Where was the first session of the Constituent Assembly held?
qs.e: The first session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held on 9 December 1946 at the Constitution Hall in New Delhi (now the old Parliament House). The session was presided over by Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the temporary chairman of the Assembly. The Constituent Assembly was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 to draft the Constitution of India. A total of 211 members attended the first session. On 11 December 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent chairman. The Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, and it was implemented on 26 January 1950.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly held? → New Delhi
☛ Who was the interim chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Who was the permanent chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Rajendra Prasad
☛ Under which plan was the Constituent Assembly formed? → Cabinet Mission Plan 1946
☛ How many members were in the Constituent Assembly initially? → 389 (later 299)

q: Parliamentary system of Indian Constitution was taken from-
qs.e: The parliamentary system of the Indian Constitution was taken from Britain. The British parliamentary system evolved with the executive being responsible to the legislature. India adopted this system where the President is the constitutional head and the Prime Minister is the real executive head. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Like Britain, India also has a bicameral legislature (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Among other options, the federal system was taken from Canada, fundamental duties from Russia, and judicial review from the United States.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Indian parliamentary system → Britain
☛ Real executive head in India → Prime Minister
☛ Constitutional head in India → President
☛ Two houses of Indian Parliament → Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
☛ Key feature taken from Canada → Federal system

q: Who was made the acting Prime Minister of India immediately after the death of Jawaharlal Nehru?
qs.e: Jawaharlal Nehru died on 27 May 1964. After his death, the country needed an interim leader. The senior cabinet minister Gulzarilal Nanda was made the Acting Prime Minister. He was the Home Minister and served as Acting PM twice (1964 and 1966). He held the position until the Congress Parliamentary Party elected a new leader. After Nehru, Lal Bahadur Shastri became the Prime Minister. Nanda was a socialist leader associated with the labour movement.
qs.kf:
☛ How many times was Gulzarilal Nanda made Acting Prime Minister? → Twice (1964 and 1966)
☛ Which ministry was Gulzarilal Nanda in charge of? → Home Ministry
☛ Who became Prime Minister after Nehru's death? → Lal Bahadur Shastri
☛ Where was Gulzarilal Nanda born? → Punjab (now in Pakistan)
☛ Which movement was Gulzarilal Nanda associated with? → Labour movement

q: When did the Constitution of India come into force?
qs.e: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949, but it came into force on 26 January 1950. This date was chosen to commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) by the Indian National Congress in 1930. With the enforcement of the Constitution, India became a republic, and Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the first President of India. The original Constitution had 395 articles, 8 schedules, and 22 parts. Currently, there are 12 schedules. 26 January is celebrated as Republic Day in India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the final draft adopted by the Constituent Assembly? → 26 November, 1949
☛ How long did it take to frame the Constitution of India? → 2 years 11 months 18 days
☛ Who was the permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ How many members were there in the Constituent Assembly initially? → 389
☛ Who is known as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar

q: Who among the following served as President for two consecutive terms?
qs.e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India and the only one to serve two consecutive terms (1950-1962). He assumed office after the adoption of the Indian Constitution in 1950 and was re-elected in 1957. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (1962-1967) and V.V. Giri (1969-1974) served only one term each. A P J Abdul Kalam (2002-2007) also served a single term. Dr. Prasad played a key role in the Indian independence movement and the Constituent Assembly.
qs.kf:
☛ First President of India → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Only President to serve two consecutive terms → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Tenure of Dr. Rajendra Prasad → 1950-1962
☛ Tenure of Dr. S. Radhakrishnan → 1962-1967
☛ Tenure of V.V. Giri → 1969-1974

q: Who among the following had the longest tenure as President of India?
qs.e: India's first President, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, served the longest tenure. He held office from January 26, 1950 to May 13, 1962, for nearly 12 years. He was re-elected in 1957, making him the only person to serve two terms as President. His tenure lasted 12 years and 107 days. Among the other options, F. A. Ahmed served only 2.5 years (1974-77), V.V. Giri served about 5 years (1969-74), and N. Sanjiva Reddy served about 5 years (1977-82). Dr. Rajendra Prasad played a crucial role in strengthening the Indian Constitution and the Republic.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first President of India? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who had the longest tenure as President? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad (12 years 107 days)
☛ Who is the only person elected President twice? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ What is the term of the President of India? → 5 years
☛ When did Dr. Rajendra Prasad's tenure end? → May 13, 1962

q: How many schedules are there at present in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution currently has 12 schedules. Originally, there were 8 schedules, increased through amendments. The First Schedule lists states and union territories; the Second deals with salaries of President, Governors, etc. The Third contains oaths and affirmations. The Fourth allocates Rajya Sabha seats. Fifth and Sixth relate to administration of Scheduled Tribes. The Seventh has Union, State, and Concurrent lists. Eighth includes languages. Ninth covers land reform laws. Tenth is the anti-defection law. Eleventh deals with Panchayati Raj, and Twelfth with municipalities. These schedules provide detailed structures for governance and rights.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of Schedules in original Constitution → 8
☛ Schedule 11 is related to → Panchayati Raj
☛ Subject of Schedule 12 → Municipalities
☛ Schedule 9 added by which amendment → First Amendment, 1951
☛ Name of Schedule 10 → Anti-defection Law

q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution outlines the allocation of seats in the Council of States?
qs.e: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) to the states and union territories. It is associated with Article 4(1) and Article 80(2). Currently, the Rajya Sabha has a total of 245 members, out of which 233 represent the states and union territories, while 12 members are nominated by the President. The Fourth Schedule lists the number of seats allocated to each state. This schedule has been in existence since the commencement of the Constitution and has been amended from time to time to reflect changes in state boundaries or reorganizations.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats? → Fourth Schedule
☛ How many members are nominated by the President in Rajya Sabha? → 12
☛ What is the total strength of Rajya Sabha? → 245
☛ How many members represent states in Rajya Sabha? → 233
☛ Under which Article is Rajya Sabha constituted? → Article 80

q: Which of the following Acts provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation consisting of provinces and princely states as units?
qs.e: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation consisting of provinces and princely states as units. This Act aimed to introduce a federal system in India, granting autonomy to provinces and proposing the inclusion of princely states. However, the federation never came into effect because the princely states did not join. The Act included three lists: Federal List, Provincial List, and Concurrent List. It abolished dyarchy at the provincial level and introduced provincial autonomy. At the centre, dyarchy was introduced. It came into force in 1937 and served as the constitutional framework until 1947.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Act proposed an All-India Federation? → Government of India Act, 1935
☛ How many lists were under the Government of India Act, 1935? → Three – Federal, Provincial, Concurrent
☛ Which Act granted provincial autonomy? → Government of India Act, 1935
☛ Which system was at the centre in the Government of India Act, 1935? → Dyarchy
☛ When did the Government of India Act, 1935 come into effect? → 1937

q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution was added to prevent defection of elected members?
qs.e: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, also known as the 'Anti-defection Law', was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985. Its purpose is to prevent elected members from switching parties. If a member voluntarily gives up party membership or votes against the party whip, they can be disqualified from the House. The schedule applies to both Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. It was further strengthened by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003. The presiding officer (Speaker/Chairman) is the authority to decide disqualification cases. This law has enhanced political stability and party discipline in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Tenth Schedule is related to? → Anti-defection
☛ Which amendment added Tenth Schedule? → 52nd Amendment
☛ When was the anti-defection law amended? → 2003 (91st Amendment)
☛ Who decides disqualification under Tenth Schedule? → Presiding officer
☛ Which houses are covered by Tenth Schedule? → Lok Sabha and assemblies

q: Which Act abolished the dyarchy in provinces and introduced provincial autonomy during the British rule?
qs.e: The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished the dyarchy in provinces and introduced provincial autonomy. It divided provinces into separate entities and granted them the power of self-government. This Act expanded the powers of provincial legislatures and reduced the role of the Governor. It was a significant step towards establishing a federal structure in British India. Before this, the Government of India Act, 1919 had introduced the dyarchy system, where subjects were divided into reserved and transferred categories. The 1935 Act ended this division and gave full responsibility to provinces, though the federal system at the centre could not be implemented.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Act introduced dyarchy? → Government of India Act, 1919
☛ Which Act introduced provincial autonomy? → Government of India Act, 1935
☛ How many provinces were there in the Government of India Act, 1935? → 11 provinces
☛ What type of government did the Government of India Act, 1935 propose at the centre? → Federal government
☛ When did the Government of India Act, 1935 come into effect? → 1937

q: The Regulating Act of 1773 was enacted to regulate which organization’s activities in India?
qs.e: The Regulating Act of 1773 was passed by the British Parliament to regulate the activities of the East India Company in India. The Company was engaged in both trade and administration, and the Act aimed to bring transparency and establish parliamentary control over its affairs. It was the first major step by the British government to assert authority over the Company's territorial acquisitions and governance in India. The Act also provided for the appointment of a Governor-General of Bengal and a Supreme Court in Calcutta.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Regulating Act passed? → 1773
☛ Which post was created under this Act? → Governor-General of Bengal
☛ Who became the first Governor-General? → Warren Hastings
☛ Whose powers were limited by this Act? → Board of Directors of the East India Company
☛ What was the main objective of this Act? → To bring British control over Company's activities

q: The printed records of the Constituent Assembly discussions were compiled into how many volumes?
qs.e: The printed records of the Constituent Assembly discussions were compiled into 12 volumes. These records provide a detailed account of the debates, discussions, and amendments that took place during the framing of the Indian Constitution. The Constituent Assembly held a total of 11 sessions from 9 December 1946 to 26 November 1949, with the final session adopting the Constitution. Subsequently, the records of these discussions were published in 12 volumes, which serve as a crucial source for understanding constitutional history. Each volume covers deliberations on various topics such as fundamental rights, directive principles, and the federal structure.
qs.kf:
☛ How many volumes contain the printed records of Constituent Assembly discussions? → 12 volumes
☛ How many sessions did the Constituent Assembly hold? → 11 sessions
☛ When was the first session of the Constituent Assembly? → 9 December 1946
☛ When was the Constitution adopted? → 26 November 1949
☛ Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad

q: Under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution are the provisions for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes provided?
qs.e: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It applies to states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Key provisions include the declaration of Scheduled Areas, establishment of Tribal Advisory Councils, and the President's power to make regulations. The Governor has the authority to modify or exempt laws in these areas. This schedule is crucial for the welfare and protection of Scheduled Tribes, ensuring their distinct identity and rights are preserved while integrating them into the mainstream.
qs.kf:
☛ Sixth Schedule → Administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram
☛ Seventh Schedule → Division of powers between Union and States
☛ Eighth Schedule → List of official languages
☛ Fourth Schedule → Allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha
☛ Fifth Schedule → Administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribes

q: Who was elected the first President of the country after independence on 26 January 1950?
qs.e: On 26 January 1950, India became a republic and Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the first President of the country. He also served as the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly and held the presidential office from 1950 to 1962. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was actively involved in the Indian independence movement and studied law at the University of Patna. He is the longest-serving President of India. During his tenure, India strengthened its democratic system.
qs.kf:
☛ First President of India → Rajendra Prasad
☛ First Prime Minister of India → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Chairman of the Constituent Assembly → Rajendra Prasad
☛ Chairman of the Drafting Committee → B. R. Ambedkar
☛ First Vice President of India → Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan

q: Who among the following headed the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas under Constituent Assembly?
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly set up an Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas. This committee was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. It played a crucial role in drafting the constitution, dealing with issues like fundamental rights, protection of minorities, and reservation for scheduled castes and tribes. Based on its recommendations, provisions related to fundamental rights, minority rights, and tribal areas were included in the Constitution. Under Patel's leadership, the committee successfully built consensus among different communities, ensuring the protection of diverse interests while maintaining national unity.
qs.kf:
☛ Who headed the Advisory Committee? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Who headed the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee? → J.B. Kripalani
☛ Who headed the Minorities Sub-Committee? → H.C. Mookerjee
☛ Who headed the Tribal and Excluded Areas Sub-Committee? → A.V. Thakkar
☛ How many members were in the Advisory Committee? → 54 members

q: Which Schedule of the Constitution of India deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to states and union territories?
qs.e: The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution of India deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to states and union territories. It specifies the number of seats each state and union territory is entitled to, based on their population. The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of Parliament, with a maximum strength of 250 members. Currently, it has 245 members, out of which 233 represent states and union territories, and 12 are nominated by the President. The allocation of seats in the Fourth Schedule ensures proportional representation of states based on population, thereby maintaining balance in the federal structure.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Schedule deals with Rajya Sabha seat allocation? → Fourth Schedule
☛ What is the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha? → 250
☛ What is the current strength of Rajya Sabha? → 245
☛ How many members are nominated in Rajya Sabha? → 12
☛ On what basis are Rajya Sabha seats allocated? → Population proportion
