Under Nehru's chairmanship, the committee included experts from various fields and formulated a comprehensive development strategy. The recommendations of this committee later formed the basis for the Five-Year Plans.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the National Planning Committee established? → 1938
☛ Who was the chairman of the National Planning Committee? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Under which organization was the National Planning Committee formed? → Indian National Congress
☛ When was the Planning Commission formed? → 1950
☛ When did the first Five-Year Plan start? → 1951

q: Who was the temporary president of the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly?
qs.e: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on December 9, 1946. The temporary president of this meeting was Sachchidanand Sinha, as he was the oldest member. Later, on December 11, 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent president. Sachchidanand Sinha belonged to Bihar and was a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress. He presided over the inaugural session and played a key role in the early proceedings of the Assembly.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of first Constituent Assembly meeting → December 9, 1946
☛ Permanent president of Constituent Assembly → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Name of temporary president → Sachchidanand Sinha
☛ State of Sachchidanand Sinha → Bihar
☛ Last meeting of Constituent Assembly → January 24, 1950

q: Which of the following is related to the administration and control of the scheduled areas of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It falls under Article 244(1) and applies to states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram (which have the Sixth Schedule). The Fifth Schedule provides for the declaration of Scheduled Areas, their administration, the establishment of Tribes Advisory Councils, and special powers of the Governor. The objective is to protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes and ensure their socio-economic development. It also empowers the Governor to make regulations for peace and good government in these areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Schedule V → Relates to administration of Scheduled Areas
☛ Schedule VI → Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
☛ Article 244(1) → Basis of Fifth Schedule
☛ Article 244(2) → Basis of Sixth Schedule
☛ Tribes Advisory Council → Formed under Fifth Schedule

q: Who among the following was the President of the Constituent Assembly of India?
qs.e: The President of the Constituent Assembly of India was Dr. Rajendra Prasad. He was elected as the permanent President on 11 December 1946. The Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan and held its first meeting on 9 December 1946. In that meeting, Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected as the temporary President. Later, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was chosen as the permanent President. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution in the Assembly. The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949 and it came into effect on 26 January 1950.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Who moved the Objectives Resolution? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly? → 9 December 1946
☛ Who was the first President of India? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad

q: Who among the following is the longest serving Prime Minister of India?
qs.e: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and served continuously for 16 years and 286 days from 15 August 1947 to 27 May 1964. He is India's longest-serving Prime Minister. Indira Gandhi served two non-consecutive terms totaling about 15 years, Morarji Desai served for about 2 years, and Dr. Manmohan Singh served for 10 years. Nehru's leadership laid the foundation for India's economic and industrial development, and his policies significantly shaped modern India.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest serving Prime Minister → Jawaharlal Nehru (16 years, 286 days)
☛ Second longest serving → Indira Gandhi (total 15 years)
☛ Third longest serving → Dr. Manmohan Singh (10 years)
☛ Nehru's tenure → 1947 to 1964
☛ Nehru is known as → Architect of modern India

q: Who among the following was the President of the Constituent Assembly?
qs.e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946. He later became the first President of India. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946, with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as its temporary chairman. Subsequently, Rajendra Prasad was chosen as the permanent chairman. Jawaharlal Nehru moved the 'Objectives Resolution' in the Assembly. B.R. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General of India. Rajendra Prasad served as President from 1947 to 1962.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the temporary chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Who moved the Objectives Resolution? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Who was the first President of India? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who was the last Governor-General of India? → C. Rajagopalachari

q: When was the first session of the Constituent Assembly held?
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly of India was formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. Its first session was held on 9 December 1946 at the Constitution Hall (now Parliament House) in New Delhi. The session was chaired by Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the temporary president of the Assembly. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent president on 11 December 1946. A total of 205 members attended the first session. The Constituent Assembly drafted the Constitution of India, which came into effect on 26 January 1950. This Assembly reflected India's sovereignty.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the temporary president of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Who was the permanent president of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ In which year was the Cabinet Mission Plan introduced? → 1946
☛ Under which plan was the Constituent Assembly formed? → Cabinet Mission Plan
☛ How many members attended the first session? → 205

q: Before the constitution of India, an “Objectives Resolution” was proposed by ______ in 1946.
qs.e: In 1946, the 'Objectives Resolution' was proposed by Jawaharlal Nehru before the Constituent Assembly of India, and it was unanimously adopted on 22 January 1947. This resolution laid the foundation for the framing of the Indian Constitution and later formed the basis of the Preamble. It declared India to be a sovereign, democratic republic. While B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly, and Vallabhbhai Patel was a prominent leader, the resolution was moved by Nehru.
qs.kf:
☛ Who proposed the Objectives Resolution? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ When was the Objectives Resolution adopted? → 22 January 1947
☛ What did the Objectives Resolution form the basis of? → Preamble of the Indian Constitution
☛ Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly? → Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → B. R. Ambedkar

q: Which of the following statements about the cardinal features of the political system in India are correct?
1. It is a democratic republic.
2. It has a Parliamentary form of government.
3. The Supreme Power draws its power from the people of India.
4. It provides for a unified authority.
qs.e: The cardinal features of the Indian political system include: it is a democratic republic, where the people elect the government and the President is the head of state. India has a Parliamentary form of government, where the executive is responsible to the legislature. The supreme power is derived from the people of India, as mentioned in the Preamble. Statement 4 is incorrect because India does not provide for a unified authority; instead, it has a separation of powers and a federal structure, with the center and states functioning in their respective domains.
qs.kf:
☛ Political form of India → Democratic republic
☛ Type of government → Parliamentary
☛ Source of power → People of India
☛ Nature of authority → Not unified, federal
☛ Feature of Indian political system → Sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic

q: The members of the constituent assembly were elected by ___________.
o: the eminent leaders of congress party
qs.e: The members of the Indian Constituent Assembly were elected in 1946 by the members of the provincial legislatures. This was an indirect election where members of each provincial assembly voted. The process was based on the Cabinet Mission Plan, which proposed the formation of the Constituent Assembly. There were 389 members in total, with 292 from provincial legislatures, 93 from princely states, and 4 from chief commissioner provinces. The election was not based on universal franchise. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946.
qs.kf:
☛ Who elected the members of the Constituent Assembly? → Provincial legislatures
☛ Total members in the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan? → 389
☛ When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly? → 9 December 1946
☛ Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ On what basis were the elections by provincial legislatures conducted? → Cabinet Mission Plan

q: What is the term of office of the Chairmen and Members of the National Commission of Scheduled Tribes?
qs.e: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) is a constitutional body established under Article 338A of the Constitution of India. The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and members of the NCST hold office for a term of three years from the date of their appointment, as determined by the President. The Commission is responsible for safeguarding the interests and welfare of Scheduled Tribes, monitoring the implementation of constitutional safeguards, and making recommendations to the government. The tenure of three years ensures continuity in overseeing tribal affairs. Members are appointed by the President of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of office of Chairperson of NCST → 3 years
☛ Term of office of Chairperson of National Commission for Scheduled Castes → 3 years
☛ Article under which NCST is formed → Article 338A
☛ Article under which NCSC is formed → Article 338
☛ First Chairperson of NCST → E. M. Sudarsana Natchiappan

q: Who among the following was the chairman of the Constituent Assembly of India?
qs.e: The chairman of the Constituent Assembly of India was Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who later became the first President of India. The Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946, and its first meeting was held on 9 December 1946. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha served as the temporary chairman, while Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent chairman on 11 December 1946. The Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949 and it came into effect on 26 January 1950. Dr. B R Ambedkar was the chairman of the Drafting Committee, not the Constituent Assembly. The other options, Gopal Das Ambaidas Desai and K M Munshi, were members of the Assembly but not the chairman.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the temporary chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly held? → 9 December 1946
☛ Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B R Ambedkar
☛ When was the Constitution adopted by the Constituent Assembly? → 26 November 1949
☛ When did the Constitution of India come into effect? → 26 January 1950

q: Indian political activist and advocate for women’s rights, ____________, had unfurled the first version of the Indian national flag at the International Socialist Congress held at Stuttgart, Germany
qs.e: Bhikaji Cama was a prominent Indian political activist and advocate for women's rights. She unfurled the first version of the Indian national flag at the International Socialist Congress held in Stuttgart, Germany in 1907. The flag had three stripes of green, yellow, and red, with eight lotuses on the green stripe, 'Vande Mataram' on the yellow stripe, and a sun and moon on the red stripe. Bhikaji Cama worked with the Indian community in London to support the Indian freedom movement and played a crucial role in overseas Indian nationalism. She is often referred to as the 'Mother of the Indian Revolution.'
qs.kf:
☛ Where did Bhikaji Cama unfurl the flag at the International Socialist Congress? → Stuttgart, Germany
☛ What is Bhikaji Cama's famous nickname? → 'Mother of the Indian Revolution'
☛ How many stripes were on the flag unfurled by Bhikaji Cama? → Three (green, yellow, red)
☛ What was written on the flag unfurled by Bhikaji Cama? → 'Vande Mataram'
☛ In which year did Bhikaji Cama unfurl the flag? → 1907

q: In a federal country, disputes regarding federal matters are resolved by which of the following?
qs.e: In a federal country, disputes regarding federal matters are resolved by the Supreme Court. It acts as the guardian and final interpreter of the constitution. In a federal system, powers are divided between the center and states, and the Supreme Court has the authority to resolve disputes arising from this division. In India, under Article 131, the Supreme Court has original jurisdiction to hear disputes between the Union and states or between states. This court ensures the supremacy of the constitution and protects the federal structure.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which article does the Supreme Court hear federal disputes in India? → Article 131
☛ Which jurisdiction of the Supreme Court deals with federal disputes? → Original jurisdiction
☛ Who is the guardian of the constitution in a federal country? → Supreme Court
☛ Who gives the final decision in center-state disputes? → Supreme Court
☛ On what basis is the division of powers in a federal system? → Constitution

q: Who among the following referred to the Directive Principles as the 'life-giving provisions' of the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The Directive Principles were referred to as the 'life-giving provisions' of the Constitution of India by LM Singhvi. He was a prominent constitutional expert and senior advocate. The Directive Principles are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution. These principles are non-justiciable but are considered fundamental in the governance of the country. Their aim is to establish social and economic justice. Singhvi called them 'life-giving' because they give meaning to fundamental rights. Among other options, Dr. BR Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly, Ivor Jennings was a British legal scholar, and HM Seervai was also a constitutional expert, but none of them used this specific phrase.
qs.kf:
☛ Who described Directive Principles as 'life-giving provisions'? → LM Singhvi
☛ Which part of Indian Constitution contains Directive Principles? → Part IV
☛ How many Articles in Directive Principles? → Articles 36-51
☛ Which country's constitution inspired the Directive Principles? → Ireland
☛ Who first called Directive Principles 'life-giving'? → LM Singhvi

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following acts provided a regular code of all regulations that could be enacted for the internal Government of British India?
qs.e: The Pitt's India Act 1784, also known as the East India Company Act 1784, provided a regular code of all regulations that could be enacted for the internal government of British India. This act separated the political and commercial functions of the Company. A Board of Control was established to oversee civil, military, and revenue affairs in India. The Court of Directors was restricted to commercial matters. The act strengthened the powers of the Governor-General and gave him control over the Bombay and Madras Presidencies. It was passed by the British Parliament to regulate the Company's rule in India. The act aimed to address the shortcomings of the Regulating Act 1773 and establish a more centralized administration.
qs.kf:
☛ Purpose of Pitt's India Act → Separate political and commercial functions of East India Company
☛ Board of Control members → 6 members appointed by British government
☛ Governor-General's powers → Control over Bombay and Madras Presidencies
☛ Under this act → Court of Directors limited to commercial affairs
☛ Other name of Pitt's India Act → East India Company Act 1784

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which Article of the Constitution of India states about a directive to states for the settlement of international disputes by arbitration?
qs.e: Article 51 of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). It deals with the promotion of international peace and security. It has four clauses: (a) promote international peace and security, (b) maintain just and honourable relations between nations, (c) foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and (d) encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration. Clause (d) specifically directs the State to settle international disputes through arbitration. Being a directive principle, it is not enforceable by any court, but it is fundamental in the governance of the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 51 → Part of Directive Principles of State Policy
☛ Main focus of Article 51 → International peace and security
☛ Article 51d → Settlement of disputes by arbitration
☛ Article 51c → Respect for international law and treaties
☛ Nature of DPSP → Non-justiciable but fundamental in governance

q: Among, the democratic countries of the world, which country’s constitution is the longest written constitution and most detailed?
qs.e: India's Constitution is the longest written constitution among all democratic countries in the world. It contains 448 articles, 12 schedules, and more than 100 amendments. The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. It was drafted by the Constituent Assembly under the chairmanship of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. It is the most detailed constitution because it incorporates the best provisions from various countries' constitutions. The UK has an unwritten constitution, Japan has a short constitution, and South Africa's constitution is also shorter than India's. Hence, India's constitution is the longest and most detailed.
qs.kf:
☛ Adoption of Indian Constitution → 26 November 1949
☛ Chief architect of Indian Constitution → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Total articles in Indian Constitution → 448
☛ Total schedules in Indian Constitution → 12
☛ Indian Constitution came into effect → 26 January 1950

q: Who is Known as the ‘Father of Indian Constitution’?
qs.e: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar is known as the 'Father of Indian Constitution' because he was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly. He played a pivotal role in drafting the Constitution which was adopted on 26 November 1949. Ambedkar was a renowned jurist, economist and social reformer. He fought against untouchability and worked for the upliftment of the Dalit classes. In the Constituent Assembly, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was its President, while Dr. K. M. Munshi and Shri Sachchidanand Sinha were also members, but they were not given the title of 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Indian Constitution come into effect? → 26 January 1950
☛ Who was the permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar
☛ How many articles are there in the Indian Constitution? → 448 (originally 395)
☛ Where is the term 'Indian Constitution' used? → In the Preamble of the Constitution

q: The total number of articles that were present originally in the Indian Constitution during its implementation is:
qs.e: The Indian Constitution was finalized on 26 November 1949 and implemented on 26 January 1950. Originally, at the time of its implementation, the Constitution contained 395 articles divided into 22 parts and included 8 schedules. The Constituent Assembly took about 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to draft it. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. It is the world's longest written constitution. Over time, amendments have increased the number of articles to approximately 448.
qs.kf:
☛ Total articles in original Constitution → 395
☛ Total parts in original Constitution → 22
☛ Total schedules in original Constitution → 8
☛ President of Constituent Assembly → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Chairman of Drafting Committee → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

q: What was the Government of India Act 1935 based on?
o: The principle of a federation and parliamentary system
The acceptance of the idea of a constituent assembly to draft a constitution
The principle of session of the British India provinces
The acceptance of the independence of India
qs.e: The Government of India Act 1935 was a landmark act passed by the British Parliament. It was primarily based on the principle of a federation and parliamentary system. The act introduced provincial autonomy and ended dyarchy in the provinces. However, the federal part was never implemented. The act granted special powers to the Governor. It also served as the foundation for the Indian Constitution, as many provisions of the Indian Constitution were borrowed from this act. Hence, the correct answer is 'The principle of a federation and parliamentary system'.
qs.kf:
☛ Basis of Government of India Act 1935 → Federation and parliamentary system
☛ System introduced by this act → Provincial autonomy
☛ Dyarchy ended in which provinces by this act → All provinces
☛ When was the federal part of this act implemented → Never
☛ Part of Indian Constitution influenced by this act → Federal system

q: Which country has the longest written constitution in the world?
qs.e: The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution in the world. It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. Originally, it had 395 articles and 8 schedules, but currently it has around 470 articles and 12 schedules. It serves as the foundation of the world's largest democracy. The President of the Constituent Assembly was Dr. Rajendra Prasad, while the Chairman of the Drafting Committee was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. The Indian Constitution is inspired by various constitutions, including those of Britain, the USA, and Ireland.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of adoption of Indian Constitution → 26 November 1949
☛ President of Constituent Assembly → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Chairman of Drafting Committee → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Date of enforcement → 26 January 1950
☛ Original number of articles → 395

q: When was the Indian Constitution adopted?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 by the Constituent Assembly. This day is celebrated as Constitution Day or National Law Day. The Constituent Assembly began its work on 9 December 1946 and finalized the Constitution on 26 November 1949. However, it came into effect on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day. The President of the Constituent Assembly was Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and the Chairman of the Drafting Committee was Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Indian Constitution enforced? → 26 January 1950
☛ When was the Constituent Assembly formed? → 9 December 1946
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
☛ When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly? → 9 December 1946
☛ How long did it take to frame the Constitution? → 2 years 11 months 18 days

q: Who was the president of the first meeting of the constituent assembly which was held on December 9, 1946?
qs.e: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on December 9, 1946. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, being the eldest member, was elected as the interim president to preside over this initial session. He served as the temporary chairman until the permanent president was elected. Later, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent president of the Constituent Assembly. Dr. Sinha was a prominent lawyer and leader from Bihar. He played a key role in the early proceedings of the Assembly. This historic meeting took place at the Constitution Hall (now Parliament House) in New Delhi.
qs.kf:
☛ Interim President of the first Constituent Assembly meeting → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Permanent President of the Constituent Assembly → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Formation of the Constituent Assembly → December 6, 1946
☛ Date of the first Constituent Assembly meeting → December 9, 1946
☛ Total number of members in the Constituent Assembly → 389

q: In the Constitution of India, principles of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity were borrowed from:
qs.e: The principles of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the French Constitution. These ideals, originating from the French Revolution (1789), are enshrined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. They reflect the commitment to a just and egalitarian society, influencing Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy. The framers adopted these principles to promote individual freedoms, social equality, and national unity.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country's constitution provided the ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity to India? → France
☛ When did the French Revolution take place? → 1789
☛ Which part of the Indian Constitution mentions these principles? → Preamble
☛ Who called the Preamble the 'soul of the Constitution'? → Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Which document in France first proclaimed these ideals? → Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen

q: When is the Constitution Day celebrated in India?
qs.e: In India, Constitution Day is celebrated annually on 26 November. On this day in 1949, the Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Constitution. However, the Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day. The observance of Constitution Day began in 2015, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced it on the occasion of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's birth anniversary. This day honors the contribution of Dr. Ambedkar in drafting the Constitution. The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Constitution Day → 26 November
☛ Date of adoption of Constitution → 26 November 1949
☛ Date of enactment of Constitution → 26 January 1950
☛ Constitution Day started → 2015
☛ Dr. B.R. Ambedkar birth anniversary → 14 April

q: Which of the following is not one of the features of the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The Constitution of India is the lengthiest written constitution in the world. It provides for an independent judiciary with the power of judicial review. The three-tier government refers to government at the central, state, and local levels, which is part of the federal structure. India follows a parliamentary form of government, not a presidential one. In a presidential system, the executive and legislature are separate, whereas in India, the executive is responsible to the legislature. Hence, the presidential form of government is not a feature of the Indian Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ Form of government in India → Parliamentary
☛ Lengthiest written constitution → Indian Constitution
☛ Provision of judicial review → Independent judiciary
☛ Three-tier government → Centre, State, Local
☛ Presidential form of government → In USA

q: The provision of appointment of state governors by the national government has been taken from the constitution of which country?
qs.e: The provision for appointment of state governors by the national government in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Canadian Constitution. In Canada, the Lieutenant Governors of provinces are appointed by the federal government. This system was adopted in India to maintain coordination between the centre and states. The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts as a representative of the centre. The Indian Constitution has taken provisions from many countries, like the parliamentary system from Britain and the Directive Principles of State Policy from Ireland.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Governor appointment → Canadian Constitution
☛ Source of Parliamentary system → Britain
☛ Source of Directive Principles → Ireland
☛ Source of Preamble ideas → USA
☛ Inspiration for Directive Principles → Ireland

q: How is India defined by Article 1 of Indian Constitution?
qs.e: Article 1 of the Indian Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States'. The term 'Union' signifies the indestructible unity of India, rather than a federal structure based on a treaty. The Constituent Assembly deliberately chose 'Union' over 'Federation' because it does not grant states the right to secede. Article 1 states that 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'. This provision is part of Part I of the Constitution, which deals with the Union and its territory. India is an indestructible Union where states have no constitutional right to alter their boundaries or existence. The phrase 'Union of States' emphasizes the permanent and indissoluble nature of the Indian federation.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 1 defines India as what? → A Union of States
☛ Which part of the Constitution deals with the Union and its territory? → Part I
☛ Which Article contains 'Union of States'? → Article 1
☛ What type of Union is India? → Indestructible
☛ Do states have the right to secede? → No

q: In the schedule of the Indian Constitution, the provision of distribution of powers between the Center and the states has been done?
qs.e: The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the distribution of powers between the Centre and states. It contains three lists: Union List (100 subjects for Centre), State List (61 subjects for states), and Concurrent List (52 subjects for both). This forms the basis of the federal structure. The Fifth Schedule deals with scheduled areas, the Sixth Schedule with tribal areas, and the 10th Schedule with anti-defection laws.
qs.kf:
☛ Which part of the Constitution mentions the Union List? → Part XI (Articles 245-255)
☛ Total subjects in the Seventh Schedule? → 213 (Union: 100, State: 61, Concurrent: 52)
☛ Some subjects in the Concurrent List? → Education, Forests, Labour Welfare
☛ Which Schedule is related to defection? → 10th Schedule
☛ What does the Fifth Schedule deal with? → Administration of Scheduled Areas

q: The details of relations between the Center and the states are given in which part of the constitution?
qs.e: Part 11 of the Indian Constitution (Articles 245-263) deals with relations between the Centre and the states. It covers three types of relations: legislative, administrative, and financial. Articles 245-255 cover legislative relations, Articles 256-263 cover administrative relations, and Articles 264-293 cover financial relations. This part clarifies the federal structure and divides powers between the Centre and states. Under Article 246, there are three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. Article 256 directs states to comply with central laws, while Article 263 mentions the Inter-State Council. The Union List has 100 subjects, State List 61, and Concurrent List 52 subjects as of now.
qs.kf:
☛ Which part of Indian Constitution deals with Centre-State relations? → Part 11
☛ How many articles are in Part 11? → 19 (Articles 245-263)
☛ How many subjects in Union List? → 100
☛ How many subjects in State List? → 61
☛ How many subjects in Concurrent List? → 52

q: The Constitution of Fundamental Rights of Indian Constitution has been taken from which Constitution?
qs.e: The Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Constitution of the United States. The US Constitution includes the Bill of Rights and civil liberties, which were adapted as Fundamental Rights in India. India also adopted the concept of judicial review from the US model. Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution and are justiciable and enforceable. Among the other options, the Constitution of England is unwritten and a source of the parliamentary system; the Constitution of South Africa emphasizes equality and dignity; and the Constitution of France influenced republican and secular ideals in India.
qs.kf:
☛ From which country did India adopt Fundamental Rights? → United States
☛ Which part of the US Constitution is the source of Fundamental Rights? → Bill of Rights
☛ In which part of the Indian Constitution are Fundamental Rights mentioned? → Part III
☛ From which country did India adopt judicial review? → United States
☛ What type of constitution does England have? → Unwritten and based on parliamentary system

q: When did the Indian Constituent Assembly recognize the national anthem?
qs.e: The Indian Constituent Assembly recognized the national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' on 24 January 1950. It was composed by Rabindranath Tagore and first sung in 1911. The Assembly officially adopted it, and it became effective with the enforcement of the Constitution on 26 January 1950. The duration of the national anthem is approximately 52 seconds. On the same day, the Constituent Assembly also recognized the national song 'Vande Mataram' composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
qs.kf:
☛ Composer of national anthem → Rabindranath Tagore
☛ Composer of national song → Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
☛ Prescribed duration of national anthem → 52 seconds
☛ Date of adoption by Constituent Assembly → 24 January 1950
☛ Year when national anthem was first sung → 1911

q: The Indian Constitution has been divided into _______ parts at the time of commencement.
qs.e: The Indian Constitution was drafted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. At the time of commencement, it had 22 parts, 395 articles, and 8 schedules. These 22 parts covered various topics such as relations between the Union and States, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and amendment procedures. Due to subsequent amendments, the number of parts has now increased to 25, but initially it was 22.
qs.kf:
☛ Total parts in Constitution (at commencement) → 22
☛ Total articles at commencement → 395
☛ Total schedules at commencement → 8
☛ Current number of parts → 25
☛ Current number of articles → approximately 470

q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with languages?
qs.e: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with languages. Initially, it included 14 languages, which have been increased to 22 through various amendments. These are the official languages recognized by the Constitution for use in the Official Language Commission, Sahitya Akademi, etc. The list is periodically revised by Parliament. Currently, the Eighth Schedule includes Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kashmiri, Kannada, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santhali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu. The Eighth Schedule languages are used for official communication and cultural representation.
qs.kf:
☛ How many languages are in the Eighth Schedule? → 22
☛ Which languages were added in the 71st Amendment (1992)? → Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali
☛ Basis of Eighth Schedule? → Official Language Commission (1956)
☛ Which amendment added Santhali, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili? → 92nd Amendment (2003)
☛ Which language is NOT in the Eighth Schedule? → English

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2
q: How many functional items are listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution for Panchayats?
qs.e: The Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists 29 functional items for Panchayats. This schedule was added by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions. The items include subjects like agriculture, education, health, poverty alleviation, small industries, roads, drinking water, and social forestry. It empowers state legislatures to transfer these items to Panchayats. Note that the Eleventh Schedule has 29 items, while the Twelfth Schedule has 18 functional items for Municipalities.
qs.kf:
☛ How many functional items are in the Eleventh Schedule? → 29
☛ Which amendment added the Eleventh Schedule? → 73rd Amendment, 1992
☛ When did Panchayati Raj get constitutional status? → 1992
☛ How many items are in the Twelfth Schedule? → 18
☛ What subjects are included in the Eleventh Schedule? → Agriculture, education, health, roads, etc.

q: On which date is the Constitution Day of India celebrated?
qs.e: In India, Constitution Day is celebrated annually on 26th November. On this day in 1949, the Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Indian Constitution. It is also known as National Law Day. The Constitution came into effect on 26th January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day. Constitution Day has been observed at the government level since 2015. The purpose of this day is to spread awareness about the values and ideals of the Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Indian Constitution adopted? → 26th November 1949
☛ When did the Indian Constitution come into effect? → 26th January 1950
☛ Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ When was the Constituent Assembly formed? → 1946
☛ Since when has Constitution Day been celebrated? → 2015

q: Government of India Act, 1935 introduced:
qs.e: The Government of India Act 1935 was a significant act passed by the British Parliament. It introduced provincial autonomy, granting provincial governments extensive powers over internal affairs in their regions. The act ended dyarchy in provinces and gave more authority to provincial legislatures. It also envisaged a federal structure, though the federal part never came into effect. This act provided autonomy to provincial governments, leading to provincial elections in 1937, in which the Congress and other parties formed governments. The act marked a major step in India's constitutional development.
qs.kf:
☛ Which system was abolished by the Government of India Act 1935 in provinces? → Dyarchy
☛ How many provinces were there under the Government of India Act 1935? → 11 provinces
☛ When were provincial elections held under the Government of India Act 1935? → In 1937
☛ What type of government system did the Government of India Act 1935 propose? → Federal system
☛ At which level was a bicameral legislature proposed in the Government of India Act 1935? → Central level

q: Which is the most important feature of federal government adopted by India?
o: The state government has more power than the union government.
The jurisdiction of all governments is the same.
The relationship between the state and the center should be based on cooperation.
The center is financially dependent on states.
qs.e: The most important feature of federal government adopted by India is cooperative federalism, where the center and states work together. The Indian Constitution, inspired by the Canadian model, divides powers with a strong center. However, in practice, a cooperative relationship between center and states is crucial. India's federal structure is indestructible, and states cannot secede. This cooperative approach ensures national unity and effective governance. Other options are incorrect because states do not have more powers than the union, jurisdictions are not identical, and the center is not financially dependent on states. The essence of Indian federalism lies in cooperation, not confrontation.
qs.kf:
☛ From which country's constitution did India adopt cooperative federalism? → Canada
☛ What is the basis of federal system in India? → Division of powers in the Constitution
☛ Which feature of Indian federal system allows center to alter state boundaries? → Without state consent
☛ When did India's federal system come into effect? → 26 January 1950
☛ Where do residual powers lie in Indian federal system? → With the center

q: India's constitutional provision of ‘Indirect election of Rajya Sabha members’ was adopted from which country?
qs.e: The provision of indirect election of Rajya Sabha members in the Indian Constitution was adopted from South Africa. In South Africa, the Senate members were also elected indirectly. In India, Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies, making it an indirect election system. This system strengthens the federal structure and gives representation to states at the center. Among other options, the USA contributed fundamental rights and judicial review, England contributed parliamentary system, and Germany contributed emergency provisions.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of indirect election of Rajya Sabha → South Africa
☛ Source of Fundamental Rights → USA
☛ Source of Parliamentary System → England
☛ Source of Emergency Provisions → Germany
☛ Term of Rajya Sabha members → 6 years

q: When were the words " Socialist, Secular and Democratic Republic' added in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The words Socialist, Secular and Democratic Republic were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution through the 42nd Amendment in 1976. This amendment is often called the Mini Constitution. It was enacted during the Indira Gandhi government and also introduced the Fundamental Duties of citizens. The amendment aimed to emphasize the socialist and secular nature of the Indian state. The 44th Amendment (1978) later modified some provisions of the 42nd Amendment but did not alter the Preamble. The words Unity and Integrity of the Nation were also added by the same amendment.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of the 42nd Amendment → 1976
☛ Words added to the Preamble → Socialist, Secular, Integrity
☛ Fundamental Duties added by which amendment → 42nd Amendment
☛ Mini Constitution refers to → 42nd Amendment
☛ Year of the 44th Amendment → 1978

q: Which of the following schedules of the Indian Constitution enumerates the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states or union territories?
qs.e: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to states and union territories. Under Article 80(2), the representation of states in the Rajya Sabha is based on their population. The Fourth Schedule explicitly lists the number of seats allotted to each state and union territory. For instance, Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of seats at 31. The First Schedule lists the territories of states and union territories, the Tenth Schedule pertains to anti-defection laws, and the Sixth Schedule deals with the administration of tribal areas. Therefore, the Fourth Schedule is the correct answer for Rajya Sabha seat allocation.
qs.kf:
☛ Rajya Sabha seats for states → Fourth Schedule
☛ Article related to Rajya Sabha → Article 80
☛ State with most Rajya Sabha seats → Uttar Pradesh (31 seats)
☛ Territorial description of states → First Schedule
☛ Anti-defection law → Tenth Schedule

q: As per Articles 344(1) and 351 of the Constitution of India, the eighth schedule includes the recognition of ____ languages.
qs.e: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution currently recognizes 22 languages under Articles 344(1) and 351, which deal with the formation of the Official Language Commission and the development of Hindi. Initially, the Constitution listed 14 languages, but through amendments, the number increased. The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi; the 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali; and the 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali, bringing the total to 22. These languages represent India's linguistic diversity and cultural heritage. The Eighth Schedule provides for the use of these languages in official purposes and promotes their development.
qs.kf:
☛ Current number of languages in the Eighth Schedule → 22
☛ Most recently added languages → Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali (2003)
☛ Language added in 1967 → Sindhi
☛ Article 344(1) relates to → Official Language Commission
☛ Article 351 relates to → Development of Hindi language

q: Which of the following statements is not about Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose?
o: He participated in the Non-cooperation Movement, 1921
He was member of the Constitution Drafting Committee.
He founded the Indian National Army (INA).
qs.e: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was a prominent leader of the Indian freedom movement. He participated in the Non-cooperation Movement of 1921 and founded the Indian National Army (INA). The British government deported him to Mandalay (Myanmar) due to his political activities. However, he was never a member of the Constituent Assembly Drafting Committee, as the Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946, while Bose had mysteriously disappeared in 1945. Therefore, this statement is not about him.
qs.kf:
☛ Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's birth → 23 January 1897, Cuttack, Odisha
☛ INA's slogan → “Dilli Chalo”
☛ Title given to Netaji → “Pearl of Asia”
☛ When was he deported to Mandalay → 1925
☛ Party founded by Subhas Bose → Forward Bloc (1939)

q: Who had presided over the Constituent Assembly?
qs.e: The Constituent Assembly of India was formed in 1946. Its temporary chairman was Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, while Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President on 11 December 1946. He presided over the Assembly and later became the first President of India. The Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to draft the Constitution. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, while Sardar Patel and K. M. Munshi were prominent members of the Assembly.
qs.kf:
☛ Who presided over the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
☛ Who was the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee? → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
☛ When was the Constituent Assembly formed? → 1946
☛ When did the Indian Constitution come into force? → 26 January 1950

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which schedule allows for the creation of village councils or courts for tribal cases?
qs.e: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides special provisions for the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. This schedule allows for the creation of village councils (local village assemblies) and courts (district and appellate courts) for tribal matters. These courts decide civil and criminal cases according to tribal customs and laws. The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas, the Seventh Schedule contains the Union, State, and Concurrent lists, and the Tenth Schedule deals with the anti-defection law.
qs.kf:
☛ Which states does the Sixth Schedule apply to? → Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram
☛ What does the Fifth Schedule deal with? → Administration and control of Scheduled Areas
☛ What is the Tenth Schedule related to? → Anti-defection law
☛ What lists are in the Seventh Schedule? → Union, State, and Concurrent lists
☛ Which schedule allows village councils? → Sixth Schedule

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Under the Fifth Schedule, the Governor's regulations in Scheduled Areas can prohibit or restrict which of the following?
qs.e: Under the Fifth Schedule, the Governor can make regulations to prohibit or restrict land transfers in Scheduled Areas. This is to protect the land rights of tribal communities and prevent exploitation by outsiders. The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It empowers the Governor to make regulations for the peace and good government of these areas. Specifically, regulations can cover land transfers, money lending, and other matters to safeguard tribal interests. Taxation, freedom of speech, and water usage are not directly restricted under these regulations. This provision helps maintain the socio-economic balance of tribal regions.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas? → Fifth Schedule
☛ Who has the power to regulate land transfers in Scheduled Areas? → Governor
☛ Under which Article does the Fifth Schedule apply? → Article 244
☛ What is the purpose of the Fifth Schedule? → To protect tribal rights and administer Scheduled Areas
☛ Can the Governor restrict land transfers in Scheduled Areas? → Yes, by making regulations

q: In the Indian Constitution, from which country were the concepts of liberty, equality and fraternity adopted?
qs.e: The concepts of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Indian Constitution were adopted from the French Constitution. These ideals originated from the French Revolution of 1789 and were incorporated into the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar proposed their inclusion in the Constituent Assembly. Liberty refers to individual freedom, equality ensures equal opportunities for all citizens, and fraternity promotes national unity and brotherhood. France’s constitution is based on these principles, while Japan, USSR, and Britain have different constitutional systems. The Indian Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950. The Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946, and the Drafting Committee was chaired by Dr. Ambedkar.
qs.kf:
☛ From which country did India adopt the ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity? → France
☛ Which revolution is associated with the slogan 'Liberty, Equality and Fraternity'? → French Revolution (1789)
☛ When was the Constituent Assembly formed in India? → 1946
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ When did the Indian Constitution come into force? → 26 January 1950

q: ________ describe(s) India as a secular state.
qs.e: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution describes India as a secular state. It declares India as a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic'. The term 'secular' was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Secularism means that the state does not have an official religion and treats all religions equally. The Preamble is part of the basic structure of the Constitution. Other options like Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV), Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code), and Article 475 (which does not exist) do not describe India as a secular state like the Preamble does.
qs.kf:
☛ Which part describes India as secular? → Preamble
☛ Which amendment added 'secular'? → 42nd Amendment
☛ How many adjectives are in Preamble? → 6 (Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic, after 42nd Amendment)
☛ Source of Preamble is? → US Constitution
☛ Meaning of secularism? → State not aligned to any religion

q: Which of the following is INCORRECT in relation to the Indian political system?
qs.e: India follows a parliamentary system of government where the President is the constitutional head and the Prime Minister is the real executive head. A presidential system, like that of the USA, has the President as both the head of state and government, separate from the legislature. India is a secular state, meaning no official religion and equal treatment for all religions. India is described as a quasi-federal system because it combines federal and unitary features, such as a single constitution, single citizenship, and central dominance. Thus, the presidential system is not part of the Indian political system.
qs.kf:
☛ India's government system → Parliamentary
☛ Real executive head in India → Prime Minister
☛ Constitutional head in India → President
☛ Example of presidential system → USA
☛ India's federal nature → Quasi-federal

q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with power, authority and responsibility of municipalities?
qs.e: The Twelfth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the powers, authorities, and responsibilities of municipalities. It was added by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992. This schedule contains 18 subjects including urban planning, roads, water supply, public health, sanitation, fire services, urban forestry, education, and cultural activities. It provides a legal framework for local self-governance in urban areas. Other options: Seventh Schedule deals with Centre-State relations, Eighth Schedule lists official languages, and Tenth Schedule deals with anti-defection law.
qs.kf:
☛ Schedule related to municipalities → Twelfth Schedule
☛ 74th Amendment relates to → Municipalities
☛ Number of subjects in Twelfth Schedule → 18
☛ 73rd Amendment relates to → Panchayati Raj
☛ Number of languages in Eighth Schedule → 22

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1
q: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of tribal areas in which region?
qs.e: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of tribal areas in North-East India. It provides special provisions for the tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Under this schedule, District Councils and Regional Councils are formed, which have the power to make laws on land, forests, agriculture, social customs, etc. This schedule ensures the protection of tribal culture and rights while promoting development. It is connected with Article 244(2) and Article 275(1) of the Constitution. In non-North-Eastern regions, tribal administration comes under the Fifth Schedule.
qs.kf:
☛ Which states are covered under the Sixth Schedule? → Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
☛ Bodies formed under the Sixth Schedule? → District Councils and Regional Councils
☛ Which areas are covered under the Fifth Schedule? → Tribal areas except North-East
☛ Constitutional basis of the Sixth Schedule? → Article 244(2) and 275(1)
☛ Which amendment introduced Sixth Schedule in Mizoram and Tripura? → 49th Amendment, 1984

q: Which foreign constitution is the source of 'The idea of the Rule of Law' of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The idea of 'Rule of Law' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the UK constitution. This principle was propounded by British jurist A.V. Dicey. 'Rule of Law' means that no person is above the law and all actions must be in accordance with the law. In the Indian Constitution, this principle is embodied in Articles 14, 21, and 32. It is a fundamental principle of democratic governance.
qs.kf:
☛ From which constitution is the 'Rule of Law' borrowed? → UK
☛ Who propounded the 'Rule of Law' principle? → A.V. Dicey
☛ Which Articles of Indian Constitution embody 'Rule of Law'? → Articles 14, 21, and 32
☛ What does 'Rule of Law' mean? → No one is above the law
☛ How many foreign sources influenced the Indian Constitution? → Many countries

q: Provision of 'First Past the Post' in Indian Constitution has been adopted from the constitution of:
qs.e: The 'First Past the Post' (FPTP) system in the Indian Constitution has been adopted from Britain's parliamentary system. It is a plurality voting system where the candidate with the most votes wins. India has borrowed many provisions from Britain, such as parliamentary government, cabinet system, and legislative procedures. The FPTP system is used for Lok Sabha and state assembly elections. India adopted this system from Britain, where it is called 'First Past the Post'. This system is simple and provides quick results, but sometimes does not proportionally represent the majority.
qs.kf:
☛ From which country did India adopt the FPTP system? → Britain
☛ From which country was the parliamentary government borrowed? → Britain
☛ How many votes are needed to win in FPTP? → Most votes
☛ In which elections is FPTP used in India? → Lok Sabha and state assemblies
☛ Another provision borrowed from Britain? → Cabinet system

q: The first Foreign Minister of independent India was:
qs.e: India's first Prime Minister Jawahar Lal Nehru also served as the first Foreign Minister. He was appointed as the External Affairs Minister in the interim government on 2 September 1946 and continued after independence in 1947. Nehru laid the foundation of the Non-Aligned Movement and shaped India's foreign policy. He emphasized the Panchsheel principles. Other options: V.V. Giri (President of India), Baldev Singh (Defence Minister), Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (Vice President) were not Foreign Ministers.
qs.kf:
☛ First Foreign Minister of independent India → Jawahar Lal Nehru
☛ Nehru's tenure → 1946-1964
☛ Panchsheel principles → 1954 India-China agreement
☛ Founders of Non-Aligned Movement → Nehru, Tito, Nasser
☛ Core of Nehru's foreign policy → Non-alignment and peaceful coexistence

q: The idea of Justice (Social, Economic and Political) in the Preamble of Indian Constitution has been taken from the Constitution of ________.
qs.e: The idea of Justice (Social, Economic and Political) in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution has been taken from the Constitution of Russia (1918). This concept emerged after the Socialist Revolution in Russia, which emphasized social and economic equality. The Indian Constitution adopted this to establish a just society. The Preamble includes three dimensions of justice: Social Justice (equal opportunities), Economic Justice (fair distribution of resources), and Political Justice (equal participation in power). This idea is part of the basic structure of the Indian Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ From which constitution was the idea of Socialism taken? → Russia
☛ From which constitution was Liberty, Equality and Fraternity taken? → France (French Revolution)
☛ From which constitution was the idea of Republic taken? → America (USA)
☛ When was the Preamble adopted by the Constituent Assembly? → 26 November 1949
☛ How many ideals are there in the Preamble? → Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity

q: The first Amendment to the constitution of India was made on _______.
qs.e: The first amendment to the Constitution of India was made in 1951. It is known as the First Amendment Act, 1951. Through this amendment, Article 19 was amended to impose reasonable restrictions on the freedom of speech and expression. Additionally, Articles 31A and 31B were inserted to protect land reform laws, and the Ninth Schedule was added to shield certain laws from judicial review. The amendment was introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and received presidential assent on 18 June 1951.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first amendment to the Indian Constitution made? → 1951
☛ Which Article was amended by the first amendment? → Article 19
☛ Which new schedule was added by the first amendment? → Ninth Schedule
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during the first amendment? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ In which year was the first amendment passed? → 1951

q: The concept of the procedure established by law is taken from which constitution?
qs.e: The concept of 'Procedure Established by Law' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of Japan. In contrast, the US Constitution provides for 'Due Process of Law', which was not adopted by India. 'Procedure Established by Law' means that a law enacted by the state must be followed, regardless of its fairness. This principle is enshrined in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution. The purpose of adopting this concept from Japan was to give more power to the legislature, preventing the judiciary from reviewing the reasonableness of laws. This ensures that the law made by the Parliament is supreme, subject to constitutional limitations.
qs.kf:
☛ 'Procedure Established by Law' borrowed from? → Constitution of Japan
☛ Article 21 deals with? → Right to life and personal liberty
☛ 'Due Process of Law' is in which constitution? → US Constitution
☛ Meaning of 'Procedure Established by Law' in India? → Law made by the Parliament
☛ Landmark case for Article 21? → Kesavananda Bharati and Maneka Gandhi cases

q: The provision of the election of members of the Rajya Sabha was taken from the constitution of which country?
o: From the Government of India Act, 1935
qs.e: The framers of the Indian Constitution borrowed several provisions from various constitutions worldwide. The provision for indirect election of members of the Rajya Sabha was taken from the South African Constitution. In South Africa, members of the upper house (Senate) were also indirectly elected. In India, Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and its members are indirectly elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies. This system ensures representation of states in the federal structure. Other options: Government of India Act, 1935 contributed the office of President and federal system; American Constitution provided Fundamental Rights and judicial review; Australian Constitution inspired the Concurrent List idea.
qs.kf:
☛ From which constitution was the provision for Rajya Sabha election borrowed? → South Africa
☛ Fundamental Rights in Indian Constitution are taken from? → USA
☛ Provision of Presidential election borrowed from? → Government of India Act, 1935
☛ Amendment procedure of Indian Constitution is based on? → South Africa
☛ Concept of Concurrent List borrowed from? → Australia

q: Constitution of India came into effect -
qs.e: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 but came into effect on 26 January 1950. This date was chosen to commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj in 1930. With its enforcement, India became a sovereign, democratic republic. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the chairman of the Drafting Committee. The Constitution established a parliamentary form of government and defined centre-state relations. It is the world's longest written constitution. This day is celebrated as Republic Day.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of adoption of Indian Constitution → 26 November 1949
☛ Formation of Constituent Assembly → 9 December 1946
☛ Chairman of Drafting Committee → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ First Republic Day celebrated in India → 26 January 1950
☛ Chief architect of the Constitution → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which Schedule and Article contain the names and extent of states and union territories?
qs.e: The First Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the names and extent of states and union territories. Article 1 defines India as a Union of States, while Article 4 empowers Parliament to enact laws altering names, boundaries, or areas of states. The First Schedule lists 28 states and 8 union territories. This schedule is fundamental in defining India's territorial structure. Article 2 deals with admission or establishment of new states, whereas Article 3 concerns formation of new states and alteration of boundaries of existing states.
qs.kf:
☛ Which articles are linked to the First Schedule? → Articles 1 and 4
☛ What does Article 2 deal with? → Admission or establishment of new states
☛ What does Article 3 deal with? → Formation of new states and boundary changes
☛ Which articles are linked to the Second Schedule? → Articles 5, 59, 65, 75, 97, 125, 148, 158, 164, 186, and 221
☛ Which articles are linked to the Fourth Schedule? → Articles 4 and 80

q: Which article empowers the Indian parliament to include in or exclude caste, race, tribes from the list of Schedule castes?
qs.e: Article 341 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to specify the list of Scheduled Castes, but the power to include or exclude any caste, race or tribe from this list lies solely with the Parliament. This provision is part of Part XVI of the Constitution dealing with Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. According to Article 341, the President issues a public notification to determine the list of Scheduled Castes. However, any amendment to this list can only be made by the Parliament through a law. Article 341 ensures that the central authority maintains uniformity in the classification of Scheduled Castes across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Article for specifying Scheduled Castes → Article 341
☛ Article for specifying Scheduled Tribes → Article 342
☛ Power to amend the list of Scheduled Castes → Parliament
☛ Who issues notification under Article 341 → President
☛ How can the list of Scheduled Castes be changed → By law of Parliament

q: In which year did C Rajagopalachari voice the demand for a constituent assembly based on adult franchise?
qs.e: C Rajagopalachari voiced the demand for a constituent assembly based on adult franchise in the year 1939. This demand aligned with the Indian National Congress's proposal for a constituent assembly that emphasized universal adult suffrage. Rajagopalachari was a prominent leader from Tamil Nadu and later became the first and last Indian Governor-General of India. The year 1939 marked the beginning of World War II and significant political developments in India. His demand was a crucial step toward the framing of the Indian Constitution, which later came into effect on 26 January 1950, enshrining adult franchise as a fundamental right.
qs.kf:
☛ What is C Rajagopalachari known for? → He was the last Governor-General of India.
☛ Who demanded a constituent assembly based on adult franchise and when? → C Rajagopalachari in 1939.
☛ When was the Constituent Assembly of India formed? → 1946.
☛ When did the Indian Constitution come into effect? → 26 January 1950.
☛ Who was the first Governor-General of independent India? → Lord Mountbatten.

q: When was Jana Gana Mana officially adopted by the Constituent Assembly as the Indian National Anthem?
qs.e: The Indian National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was officially adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950. It was originally composed by Rabindranath Tagore in Bengali. The song was first sung on 27 December 1911 at the Indian National Congress session. The adoption took place just two days before India became a republic on 26 January 1950. The duration of the anthem is approximately 52 seconds.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed the Indian National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'? → Rabindranath Tagore
☛ When was the Anthem first sung? → 27 December 1911
☛ When was the Anthem adopted by the Constituent Assembly? → 24 January 1950
☛ When did India become a republic? → 26 January 1950
☛ What is the duration of the National Anthem? → 52 seconds

q: Which of the following parts/provisions of the Constitution of India CANNOT be amended?
qs.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Supreme Court established the basic structure doctrine, declaring that certain features of the Constitution cannot be amended. Judicial review, which allows courts to examine laws' constitutionality under Articles 13 and 32, is a part of this basic structure. The Preamble has been amended (42nd Amendment added socialist, secular). Fundamental Rights (Articles 14-35) and Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51) can be amended as long as they do not violate the basic structure. Thus, judicial review cannot be abolished even by Parliament.
qs.kf:
☛ Which articles embody judicial review? → Articles 13 and 32
☛ Which case established the basic structure doctrine? → Kesavananda Bharati (1973)
☛ Which amendment added words to the Preamble? → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ What limits amendments to Fundamental Rights? → Must not violate basic structure
☛ What is the source of Directive Principles? → Irish Constitution

q: The provision of 'Impeachment of President' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of _____.
qs.e: The provision of impeachment of the President in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the United States of America. It is detailed in Article 61, which lays down the procedure for removing the President for violation of the Constitution. The impeachment process can be initiated in either House of Parliament and requires a special majority. In the US Constitution, this process applies to the President, Vice President, and other federal officers, whereas in India it applies only to the President. This provision is not subject to judicial review, similar to the US system. The Indian Constitution has borrowed many features from various countries, and this procedure from the US is a significant one.
qs.kf:
☛ Article related to impeachment → 61
☛ Grounds for removal of President → Violation of Constitution
☛ House that initiates impeachment → Any House of Parliament
☛ House that investigates charges → The other House
☛ In India, impeachment applies to → Only President

q: The Twelfth Schedule of the Indian Constitution defines how many new tasks in the functional domain of the Urban Local Bodies as of March 2025?
qs.e: The Twelfth Schedule of the Indian Constitution was added by the 74th Amendment Act of 1992. This schedule lists the functions of urban local bodies (municipalities). As of March 2025, it defines a total of 18 tasks. These tasks include urban planning, land use, building construction, water supply, public health, fire services, urban forestry, education, cultural activities, and more. The schedule empowers state legislatures to assign these functions to municipalities. The 74th Amendment granted constitutional status to urban local self-government. The Twelfth Schedule is part of Part IX-A of the Constitution, which deals with municipalities.
qs.kf:
☛ How many tasks are in the Twelfth Schedule? → 18
☛ Which amendment added the Twelfth Schedule? → 74th Amendment, 1992
☛ What does the Twelfth Schedule relate to? → Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities)
☛ Which part was added by the 74th Amendment? → Part IX-A (Articles 243P-243ZG)
☛ What is the first task listed in the Twelfth Schedule? → Urban planning

q: Consider the following statements regarding the 74th Amendment Act of 1992.
1. It has added a new Part IX-A to the Constitution of India.
2. The Act has also added a new 10th Schedule to the Constitution.
3. The Act provides for the constitution of three types of municipalities in every state.
4. It consists of provisions from Articles 243-P to 243-ZG. Which of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: The 74th Amendment Act of 1992 added provisions related to municipalities in the Indian Constitution. It introduced Part IX-A (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG) and the Twelfth Schedule, not the Tenth. The Tenth Schedule is related to anti-defection law, added by the 52nd Amendment. The Act provides for the constitution of three types of municipalities in every state: Municipal Corporation (larger urban areas), Municipal Council (smaller urban areas), and Nagar Panchayat (transitional areas from rural to urban). Statement 2 is incorrect because a new 10th Schedule was not added; instead, the 12th Schedule was added. Hence, statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Which part was added by the 74th Amendment Act? → Part IX-A
☛ Which articles relate to municipalities? → 243-P to 243-ZG
☛ Which schedule was added by the 74th Amendment? → 12th Schedule
☛ What are the three types of municipalities? → Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Nagar Panchayat
☛ Which amendment added the Tenth Schedule? → 52nd Amendment

q: Oaths and affirmations for various constitutional posts are provided in which Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Third Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the forms of oaths and affirmations for various constitutional positions such as the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, Members of Parliament, Judges, etc. This schedule is part of Part XIX of the Constitution under Article 324. The Third Schedule includes a total of 9 types of oath forms, which are taken before assuming office. The First Schedule lists states and union territories, while the Ninth Schedule contains land reform and other laws. The Eleventh Schedule deals with Panchayati Raj.
qs.kf:
☛ Which schedule contains oaths and affirmations? → Third Schedule
☛ How many oath forms are in the Third Schedule? → 9
☛ Where is the President's oath given? → Third Schedule
☛ Which part of the Constitution relates to the Third Schedule? → Part XIX
☛ What does the First Schedule contain? → States and Union Territories

q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to States and Union Territories?
qs.e: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to States and Union Territories. This schedule is governed by Articles 4(1) and 80(2), which define the composition and seat distribution of the Rajya Sabha. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house with a maximum strength of 250 members, of which 238 represent States and Union Territories, and 12 are nominated by the President. The Fourth Schedule specifies the number of seats for each State and Union Territory, ensuring equitable representation in the federal structure. It plays a crucial role in maintaining the balance of power between the Centre and states.
qs.kf:
☛ Maximum strength of Rajya Sabha → 250
☛ Nominated members in Rajya Sabha → 12
☛ Articles related to Fourth Schedule → 4(1) and 80(2)
☛ State representation in Rajya Sabha → 238 seats
☛ Total number of Schedules in Constitution → 12

q: Which Article empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Castes in various states and union territories?
qs.e: Article 341 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to specify which castes shall be deemed as Scheduled Castes for the purposes of the Constitution in relation to a state or union territory. This provision falls under Part XVI of the Constitution, which deals with special provisions relating to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other backward classes. The President issues an order by public notification for this purpose. Parliament may by law modify or amend the list of Scheduled Castes. Article 330 deals with reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in the Lok Sabha, Article 342 deals with the specification of Scheduled Tribes, and Article 344 relates to the Commission on Official Language.
qs.kf:
☛ Main purpose of Article 341 → To specify Scheduled Castes
☛ Part containing Article 341 → Part XVI
☛ Who can modify the list of Scheduled Castes → Parliament by law
☛ What Article 330 deals with → Reservation of seats in Lok Sabha
☛ What Article 342 deals with → Specification of Scheduled Tribes

q: Which Articles in the Constitution of India deal with citizenship at the time of its commencement?
qs.e: In the Constitution of India, Part II (Articles 5 to 11) deals with citizenship at the time of its commencement. Article 5 defines citizenship conditions for those domiciled in India at commencement. Article 6 grants citizenship to migrants from Pakistan. Article 7 addresses citizenship for those who migrated to Pakistan. Article 8 provides citizenship for persons of Indian origin residing abroad. Article 9 terminates citizenship if a person voluntarily acquires foreign citizenship. Article 10 ensures continuity of citizenship rights. Article 11 empowers Parliament to legislate on citizenship matters. These articles were crucial for determining who became Indian citizens on January 26, 1950. Later, the Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted under Article 11 to provide for acquisition and termination of citizenship after commencement.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Articles deal with citizenship? → Articles 5-11
☛ What does Article 5 state? → Citizenship at commencement based on domicile
☛ Migrants from Pakistan covered under? → Articles 6 and 7
☛ What happens if one acquires foreign citizenship? → Article 9 terminates Indian citizenship
☛ Which Article empowers Parliament for citizenship law? → Article 11

q: What is the total number of languages listed under the 8th Schedule of the Constitution of India, as on 30 June 2024?
qs.e: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, under Articles 344(1) and 351, lists the official languages. As of 30 June 2024, there are 22 languages in this schedule. Originally, the Constitution included 14 languages, which were later increased through amendments. Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment (1967); Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment (1992); and Maithili, Dogri, Santali, and Bodo were added by the 92nd Amendment (2003). These languages represent the diverse regional languages of India, and the government promotes their preservation and development.
qs.kf:
☛ Total languages in 8th Schedule → 22
☛ Languages in original Constitution → 14
☛ Which amendment added Sindhi? → 21st Amendment (1967)
☛ Which amendment added Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali? → 71st Amendment (1992)
☛ Which amendment added Maithili, Dogri, Santali, Bodo? → 92nd Amendment (2003)

q: Provincial autonomy in provinces in place of dyarchy was introduced by which of the following British Indian government legislations?
qs.e: The Government of India Act of 1935 was a landmark British legislation that abolished dyarchy in provinces and introduced provincial autonomy. Under this act, provincial governments gained full control over their subjects, and the governor's powers were limited. Provincial legislatures were expanded, and the council of ministers became responsible to the provincial legislature. This act also laid the foundation for a federal structure in India, though the federal part was never implemented. It marked a significant shift towards self-governance by allowing elected representatives to manage provincial affairs.
qs.kf:
☛ Which act introduced provincial autonomy? → Government of India Act of 1935
☛ Which act introduced dyarchy? → Government of India Act of 1919
☛ How many provincial subjects in 1935 Act? → 54 subjects
☛ Role of provincial Governor in 1935 Act? → Constitutional head with some discretionary powers
☛ Did 1935 Act provide for a Federal Court? → Yes

q: Division of legislative subjects into union, state and concurrent List is contained in which of the following schedules of the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the division of legislative subjects into three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. The Union List originally had 97 subjects, now 100, on which only Parliament can legislate. The State List originally 66, now 61 subjects, on which state legislatures can legislate. The Concurrent List originally 47, now 52 subjects, on which both can legislate, but in case of conflict, central law prevails. This division is outlined under Article 246. The Eleventh Schedule deals with Panchayats, the Ninth Schedule with land reforms, and the Fifth Schedule with scheduled areas.
qs.kf:
☛ How many subjects in Union List? → 100
☛ How many subjects in State List? → 61
☛ How many subjects in Concurrent List? → 52
☛ Which Article relates to Seventh Schedule? → Article 246
☛ Eleventh Schedule relates to? → Panchayats

q: Allocation of seats to States and Union Territories in the Rajya Sabha is provided under which of the following Schedules of the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats to states and union territories in the Rajya Sabha. It specifies the number of seats each state and union territory is entitled to. Members of the Rajya Sabha are indirectly elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies. Seats for union territories are also mentioned in this schedule. Other schedules have different functions; for example, the Tenth Schedule deals with anti-defection law, the Sixth Schedule with administration of tribal areas, and the Eighth Schedule with official languages.
qs.kf:
☛ Schedule for Rajya Sabha seat allocation → Fourth Schedule
