qs.e: The President of India appoints several high-ranking officials including Governors of States, Chief Election Commissioner, and Comptroller and Auditor General. However, the Vice President is not appointed by the President but is elected by the members of both Houses of Parliament. As per Article 66 of the Constitution, the Vice President is elected through a system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote. Therefore, the Vice President is an elected position, not a presidential appointment. The other options are all appointed by the President.
qs.kf:
☛ Appointed by President → Governor of States
☛ Appointed by President → Chief Election Commissioner
☛ Appointed by President → Comptroller and Auditor General
☛ Election of Vice President → by members of Parliament
☛ Term of Vice President → 5 years

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Under what circumstance can the President of India dissolve the Lok Sabha before its normal term expires?
o: On the recommendation of the Prime Minister
Whenever the President wishes, without any conditions
After consulting a joint session of both Houses of Parliament
When the Supreme Court orders a dissolution
qs.e: According to Article 85(2)(b) of the Constitution of India, the President can dissolve the Lok Sabha before its normal term expires, but this power is exercised only on the recommendation of the Prime Minister. This is based on the advice of the Council of Ministers, which is binding on the President. The President cannot dissolve the Lok Sabha arbitrarily or on the order of the Supreme Court. Consultation with a joint session of Parliament is not mandatory. This provision is an integral part of the parliamentary system, where the President is the nominal head and real power rests with the Prime Minister. If the Prime Minister loses a vote of confidence and no alternative government is formed, dissolution occurs only upon recommendation.
qs.kf:
☛ Who has the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha? → President, on the advice of the Prime Minister
☛ Which Article of the Constitution deals with dissolution of Lok Sabha? → Article 85(2)(b)
☛ Can the President dissolve Lok Sabha at his own will? → No, only on the advice of the Council of Ministers
☛ Who is the head of the Council of Ministers? → Prime Minister
☛ What type of government system does India have? → Parliamentary system

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Who among the following appoints the Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission of India?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
qs.e: The Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India is appointed by the President of India. This appointment is made on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha. The NHRC was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act (1993). The Chairman holds office for a term of 5 years or until he attains the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier. The President also has the power to remove the Chairman from office.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the NHRC Chairman? → The President of India
☛ How many members are in the committee that recommends the NHRC Chairman? → 6 members
☛ Under which act was the NHRC established? → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ What is the term of the NHRC Chairman? → 5 years or until age 70
☛ Who has the power to remove the NHRC Chairman? → The President of India

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 2
q: How does the President of India exercise his/her executive functions with respect to decision-making?
o: The President considers the advice of the Prime Minister and the Union council of ministers.
The President can repeatedly ask for reconsideration of any ministerial decision until satisfied.
The President acts entirely on his own absolute discretion
The President acts independently of the Union Government for foreign affairs.
qs.e: The President of India is the constitutional head of the parliamentary system, but the real executive power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. According to Article 74, the President is bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers in the exercise of his/her functions. The President may ask for reconsideration of the advice once, but after reconsideration, he/she is bound to accept it. The President does not act on absolute discretion, nor independently in foreign affairs. This system makes the President a formal head, while the actual power rests with the Council of Ministers.
qs.kf:
☛ Who advises the President? → Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
☛ Can the President reject advice? → No, must accept after reconsideration
☛ Which article binds the President to advice? → Article 74
☛ Who exercises actual executive power? → Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
☛ What type of head is the President? → Constitutional and formal head

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following options best describes the principle of 'collective executive responsibility' as applicable to the Council of Ministers in India?
o: All ministers share full responsibility for government decisions.
Ministers can opt out of collective responsibility if they disagree publicly.
Only the Prime Minister is responsible for decision‑making.
Each minister is independent and is solely accountable for his/her actions.
qs.e: Under Article 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This means that all ministers bear joint responsibility for every government decision. If a minister disagrees with a decision, he or she can resign but cannot publicly dissent. Collective executive responsibility ensures unity and stability of the government. It is a key feature of the Westminster system where the Council of Ministers acts as a single entity accountable to the Parliament. This principle prevents internal conflicts from undermining the government's functioning.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article deals with collective responsibility? → Article 75
☛ To whom is the Council of Ministers responsible? → Lok Sabha
☛ What can a dissenting minister do? → Resign
☛ From which system is this principle derived? → Westminster system
☛ Can a minister publicly disagree? → No

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2
q: In its advisory capacity, the Union Cabinet’s advice to the President of India is considered:
o: overruled by the Speaker of the Lower House
qs.e: According to Article 74(1) of the Indian Constitution, there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President. This advice is considered binding on the President, as clarified by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976. However, the President can send the advice back for reconsideration, but after reconsideration, it becomes binding. This provision strengthens the parliamentary system of government, where real executive power lies with the Cabinet. The President acts as a constitutional head and follows the Cabinet's advice. This principle is derived from the British constitutional tradition. The binding nature ensures stability and collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers.
qs.kf:
☛ What does Article 74(1) primarily state? → The Council of Ministers advises the President, and the advice is binding.
☛ What did the 42nd Amendment 1976 clarify? → The advice of the Council of Ministers is binding on the President.
☛ How many times can the President send advice for reconsideration? → Only once.
☛ Who holds the real executive power? → The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
☛ Which country's constitutional tradition is this system based on? → Britain.

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which of the following accurately describes the Indian President's role in foreign affairs?
o: The President delegates all foreign affairs responsibilities to the Prime Minister.
The President appoints ambassadors and conducts diplomatic work in his/her name.
The President only receives foreign ambassadors but does not appoint them
The President is solely responsible for negotiating international treaties without any advisory input.
qs.e: According to Article 53 of the Indian Constitution, the President is the Supreme Commander and head of all executive powers. In foreign affairs, the President appoints ambassadors and other diplomatic representatives in his/her name. These appointments are made on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, but formally the President performs the appointment. Additionally, the President receives foreign ambassadors, signs international treaties, and declares war and peace. However, these powers are exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Thus, option 2 is correct because the President appoints ambassadors and conducts diplomatic work in his/her name.
qs.kf:
☛ President's role in foreign policy → Appoints ambassadors and signs international treaties.
☛ President's powers are exercised on whose advice → Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.
☛ President's foreign functions include → Appointment of ambassadors, treaty ratification, and war/peace declaration.
☛ Purpose of President's foreign visits → Strengthening bilateral relations.
☛ Constitutional provision for President → Article 53 vests executive power in the President.

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following statements best describes the Indian Union Cabinet’s role in legislation?
o: The Cabinet is the only law-making body in India.
The Cabinet gives final shape to government bills and prepares the legislative agenda.
The Cabinet enacts laws without any involvement of any house of the Indian Parliament.
The Cabinet has judicial authority over legislations surpassing the judiciary.
qs.e: The Indian Union Cabinet's legislative role involves giving final shape to government bills and preparing the legislative agenda for Parliament. The Cabinet does not enact laws itself; it discusses and approves bills before they are introduced in Parliament. It is a part of the executive branch, not the legislature. In India, legislative power rests with Parliament, which consists of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. The Cabinet guides the legislative process, but the final approval lies with Parliament. Judicial review of legislation is the domain of the judiciary, not the Cabinet. Thus, the Cabinet's role is limited to policy formulation and bill preparation.
qs.kf:
☛ Who holds legislative power in India? → Parliament (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha).
☛ What is the primary function of the Cabinet? → Formulating government policies and finalizing bills.
☛ Can the Cabinet enact laws? → No, only Parliament can enact laws.
☛ What power does the judiciary have? → Judicial review of laws.
☛ The Cabinet is part of which branch? → Executive, not the legislature.

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2
q: How many times may the President of India ask the Prime Minister to have an executive recommendation reconsidered by the Cabinet?
o: It is at the President's absolute discretion without limits.
qs.e: According to Article 74 of the Indian Constitution, the President can ask the Cabinet to reconsider an executive recommendation only once. This constitutional provision sets a limit. If the Cabinet reaffirms the same advice after reconsideration, the President is bound to accept it. This ensures the supremacy of the executive in the parliamentary system and keeps the President as a ceremonial head. This rule was clarified by the 42nd Amendment.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 74 → Aid and advice of Council of Ministers
☛ President → Can return for reconsideration only once
☛ After reconsideration → Cabinet advice is binding
☛ 42nd Amendment, 1976 → Clarified President's power
☛ Parliamentary system → Supremacy of Prime Minister and Cabinet

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 1
q: When appointing Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, the President of India acts on the advice of which body?
qs.e: The President of India appoints Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers. This provision is governed by Articles 155 and 156 of the Indian Constitution. The Governor acts as the representative of the President at the state level. Their appointment is made by the central government. The normal term of a Governor is five years, but they can be removed earlier by the President. The Union Council of Ministers advises the President on these appointments, and such advice is binding on the President. This ensures that the central executive has control over the appointment of constitutional heads of states.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Governor of a state? → President (on the advice of Union Council of Ministers)
☛ Who appoints the Lieutenant Governor of a UT? → President
☛ What is the term of a Governor? → Five years (during pleasure of President)
☛ Who does the Governor represent? → The President of India
☛ Which articles deal with Governor's appointment? → Articles 155 and 156

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Who administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Union Ministers under Article 75(4) of the Constitution of India?
qs.e: Under Article 75(4) of the Indian Constitution, the President of India administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Union Ministers. This oath is prescribed in the Third Schedule of the Constitution. The President is the head of the Union executive, and all ministers function in the President's name. The Council of Ministers is also appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. Only after taking the oath can a minister assume their duties. This process is a crucial step in the formation of the government, ensuring constitutional adherence and accountability.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 75(4) → Oath administered by President
☛ Oath format → Given in Third Schedule
☛ President's role → Head of Union executive
☛ Council of Ministers formation → President appoints on PM's advice
☛ Article 75(1) → President appoints Prime Minister

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of the selection committee for the Lokpal?
o: Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, Leader of the Opposition, Vice-President, and a Cabinet Minister
Prime Minister, Home Minister, Chief Justice of India, Attorney General, and Leader of the Opposition
President, Prime Minister, Chief Election Commissioner, Lok Sabha Speaker, and a Jurist
Prime Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of the Opposition, Chief Justice of India, and an eminent jurist nominated by the President
qs.e: The composition of the Lokpal selection committee is defined by the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. It consists of five members: the Prime Minister (Chairperson), Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of the Opposition, Chief Justice of India (or a judge nominated by him), and an eminent jurist nominated by the President. The committee recommends candidates for the appointment of the Lokpal Chairperson and members. This structure ensures participation of various constitutional authorities, making the appointment process independent and impartial.
qs.kf:
☛ How many members are in the Lokpal selection committee? → 5
☛ Who is the chairperson of the Lokpal selection committee? → Prime Minister
☛ In which year was the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act passed? → 2013
☛ Who appoints the Lokpal Chairperson? → President
☛ Who nominates the jurist in the selection committee? → President

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following groups is NOT considered a part of the Union Council of Ministers in India?
qs.e: According to Articles 74 and 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Union Council of Ministers consists of three categories: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State (including those with independent charge), and Deputy Ministers. Parliamentary Secretaries are not part of the Council of Ministers; they are appointed to assist ministers but are not constitutional posts. Cabinet Ministers head major departments, Ministers of State assist Cabinet Ministers, and Deputy Ministers provide assistance at a lower level. Parliamentary Secretaries are primarily appointed for assistance in parliamentary affairs, but they are not formally part of the Council of Ministers. Thus, the correct answer is Parliamentary Secretaries.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest category of Council of Ministers → Cabinet Minister
☛ Types of Ministers of State → Independent charge and non-independent charge
☛ Who decides the size of Council of Ministers → Prime Minister
☛ Constitutional provision → Article 75
☛ Lowest ministerial category → Deputy Minister

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following options correctly describes the Indian President’s power to summon the Parliament?
o: The President may summon the Parliament only once every calendar year.
The President may summon the Parliament at least twice a year.
The President can only summon the Parliament after consulting the Prime Minister.
The President may summon the Parliament at his/her discretion with no statutory minimum frequency.
qs.e: According to Article 85 of the Indian Constitution, the President must ensure that not more than six months elapse between two sessions of Parliament. This means the Parliament must be summoned at least twice a year. This provision ensures regular functioning of Parliament and upholds democratic processes. The President acts on the advice of the Prime Minister, but the minimum frequency is constitutionally mandated. Option 1 is incorrect because it allows only once a year, while the Constitution requires at least twice. Option 3 mentions consultation, but it is not the source of the power. Option 4 has no minimum frequency, which contradicts the constitutional requirement.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 85 → Maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament is six months.
☛ Summoning of Parliament → Done by the President.
☛ Minimum sessions → At least two per year mandatory.
☛ President's role → Summoning and proroguing Parliament.
☛ Prime Minister's advice → President acts on PM's recommendation.

q: The Prime Minister is the ex - officio President of
qs.e: The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio President of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR). CSIR is India's premier institution for scientific research and industrial development, established in 1942. It operates 38 laboratories and field centers across the country. As its President, the Prime Minister provides strategic direction and oversees policies. Among the options: CLRI (Central Leather Research Institute) is a constituent laboratory of CSIR, while ISRO and DRDO are independent organizations headed by the Secretary of Space and the Secretary of Defence Research and Development respectively.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of CSIR → New Delhi
☛ Year of establishment of CSIR → 1942
☛ Prime Minister is ex-officio President of → CSIR
☛ Number of CSIR laboratories → 38
☛ A constituent laboratory of CSIR → CLRI

q: If the posts of the President and Vice-president fall vacant, who will act as the President of India?
qs.e: If both the posts of President and Vice-President fall vacant, the Chief Justice of India acts as the President of India. This provision is mentioned in Article 65 of the Indian Constitution. According to Article 65, the Vice-President performs the duties of the President when the latter is unable to act. However, if the office of Vice-President is also vacant, then the Chief Justice of India becomes the acting President. This is a temporary arrangement during which the Chief Justice exercises all powers of the President. This process continues until a new President is elected. The provision ensures continuity in the highest office of the country and is a safeguard against a complete vacuum at the top.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 65 → Discharge of President's duties by Vice-President or Chief Justice
☛ Acting President → Chief Justice of India when both President and Vice-President are vacant
☛ President's absence → Vice-President acts as President
☛ Vacancy period → Election for new President must be held within six months
☛ Article 62 → Election process to fill vacancy in President's office

q: Which among the following is NOT a qualification to become a Vice President of India?
o: He or she must be qualified for election as a Member of the Rajya Sabha or the Council of States.
qs.e: The office of the Vice President of India is provided under Articles 63-67 of the Indian Constitution. The qualifications to become Vice President are mentioned in Article 66. According to this, the person must be a citizen of India, must have completed the age of 35 years, and must be qualified to be elected as a member of the Rajya Sabha. Membership of the Lok Sabha is not a qualification because the Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Thus, possessing Lok Sabha membership is not a requirement.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of Vice President → 5 years
☛ Election of Vice President → by single transferable vote
☛ Removal of Vice President → by resolution of Rajya Sabha
☛ Salary of Vice President → determined by Parliament
☛ Function of Vice President → as Chairman of Rajya Sabha

q: Name the minister who resigned during the India China war in 1962?
qs.e: During the India-China war of 1962, the then Defence Minister V. K. Krishna Menon resigned taking responsibility for India's defeat. He was serving in Jawaharlal Nehru's cabinet. The Indian Army suffered a major setback in the war, leading to widespread public and parliamentary outrage. Under this pressure, Krishna Menon stepped down from his post. This was a significant event in Indian politics, paving the way for subsequent reforms in defence strategy and policy.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the Defence Minister during the 1962 India-China war? → V. K. Krishna Menon
☛ From which post did V. K. Krishna Menon resign? → Defence Minister
☛ Who became Defence Minister after the 1962 war? → Yashwantrao Chavan
☛ In which year did the India-China war occur? → 1962
☛ Who was the Prime Minister of India at that time? → Jawaharlal Nehru

q: How many ministers can be included in the council of Ministers of the Union?
o: Ten to fifteen percent of the total number of members of the House of People
Fifty percent of the total number of members of the House of People
As many as wished by the Prime Minister of India
Fifteen percent of the total number of members of the House of People
qs.e: According to Article 75 of the Indian Constitution, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha (House of the People). This ceiling was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. The purpose is to limit the size of the Council of Ministers and enhance administrative efficiency. Based on the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha (550), the maximum number of ministers can be 82. This provision ensures a balanced and effective executive.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article limits the size of the Council of Ministers? → Article 75
☛ Which Constitutional Amendment introduced the 15% limit? → 91st Amendment, 2003
☛ What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha? → 550
☛ Is the Prime Minister included in the 15% limit? → Yes
☛ Can the Council of Ministers exceed 15% of Lok Sabha members? → No

q: Which Prime Minister was born after India gained independence?
qs.e: India gained independence on 15 August 1947. Among the given options, only Narendra Modi was born on 17 September 1950, after independence. Manmohan Singh was born on 26 September 1932, I.K. Gujral on 4 December 1919, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee on 25 December 1924, all before independence. Narendra Modi is the 14th Prime Minister of India and served from 2014 to 2024. He is a leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
qs.kf:
☛ First Prime Minister of India → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ First Prime Minister born after independence → Narendra Modi
☛ Longest serving Prime Minister → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ India's independence date → 15 August 1947
☛ Narendra Modi's birth year → 1950

q: Which President of India is known as the Missile Man?
qs.e: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam is known as the 'Missile Man' for his contribution to missile technology. He served as the 11th President of India from 2002 to 2007 and was a renowned scientist. He played a key role in developing SLV-III, Agni, and Prithvi missiles. He was also involved in the Pokhran-II nuclear tests. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1997. Born on 15 October 1931 in Dhanushkodi, Tamil Nadu, he is also called the 'People's President'.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the Missile Man of India? → Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam
☛ Which President was Dr. Kalam? → 11th President
☛ His famous book? → Wings of Fire
☛ Year he got Bharat Ratna? → 1997
☛ His birthplace? → Dhanushkodi, Tamil Nadu

q: Which of the following politicians has never been a leader of the House in the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: The Leader of the House in Lok Sabha is a member of Parliament who leads the government's business in the house. Shri Manmohan Singh was never a member of Lok Sabha; he served as a member of Rajya Sabha and became Prime Minister. Hence, he could not become the Leader of the House in Lok Sabha. In contrast, Atal Bihari Vajpayee served as Leader of the House from 1998 to 2004, Pranab Mukherjee held the position from 2004 to 2012, and Narendra Modi has been the Leader of the House since 2014. According to the Indian Constitution, the Leader of the House must be a member of Lok Sabha. Since Manmohan Singh was from Rajya Sabha, he was ineligible.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → The Prime Minister, if he is a Lok Sabha member.
☛ Which Prime Minister never became Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → Manmohan Singh (he was from Rajya Sabha).
☛ Who served the longest as Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → Pranab Mukherjee (2004-2012).
☛ Who is the current Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → Narendra Modi.
☛ Can a Rajya Sabha member become Leader of the House in Lok Sabha? → No, only Lok Sabha members.

q: Who has the power to give forgiveness to the person who has been awarded capital punishment?
o: Exclusive Committee of the Supreme Court
qs.e: Under Article 72 of the Indian Constitution, the President of India has the power to grant pardon to a person who has been awarded capital punishment. This power applies to cases where the punishment is under a union law or by a court martial. The President exercises this power on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Article 72 also includes the power to suspend, remit, or commute the death sentence. This constitutional provision introduces an element of mercy in the judicial process, allowing the President to act as the highest authority for clemency.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article deals with the President's power to pardon death sentence? → Article 72
☛ On whose advice does the President exercise pardoning power? → Council of Ministers
☛ Which article gives similar power to the Governor? → Article 161
☛ In which cases does the President's pardoning power apply? → Union laws and court martial
☛ Can the President completely pardon a death sentence? → Yes

q: How many ministers can be included in the Central Council of Ministers?
o: Fifty percent of the total members of the Lok Sabha
Fifteen percent of the total members of the Lok Sabha
Ten to fifteen percent of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
As desired by the Prime Minister of India
qs.e: According to Article 75(1) of the Indian Constitution, the total number of ministers in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total members of the Lok Sabha. This provision was added by the 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) to limit the size of the Council of Ministers and ensure efficiency. The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 (530 from states, 20 from union territories, and 2 nominated Anglo-Indians). Thus, the maximum number of ministers is about 83. This rule prevents the government from becoming too large and unwieldy.
qs.kf:
☛ Maximum size of Central Council of Ministers → 15% of Lok Sabha members
☛ Year of 91st Constitutional Amendment → 2003
☛ Article 75(1) relates to → Formation of Council of Ministers
☛ Maximum strength of Lok Sabha → 552
☛ Who fixed the size of Council of Ministers? → 91st Amendment

q: Who among the following was honoured with Bharat Ratna award before becoming the President of India?
qs.e: Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954, India's highest civilian award. He served as the President of India from 1962 to 1967. Before becoming President, he was the Vice President of India (1952-1962). He was a renowned philosopher and educator. Rajendra Prasad received the Bharat Ratna in 1962, but he had already served as President (1950-1962). V.V. Giri and Pranab Mukherjee received this award after their presidencies.
qs.kf:
☛ First President to receive Bharat Ratna → Rajendra Prasad
☛ Second President to receive Bharat Ratna → Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
☛ Received Bharat Ratna before becoming President → Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
☛ First Vice President of India → Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
☛ First recipient of Bharat Ratna → C. Rajagopalachari (1954)

q: Who among the following was the first attorney General of Independent India?
qs.e: Under Article 76 of the Indian Constitution, the Attorney General is appointed by the President. Motilal Chimanlal Setalvad was the first Attorney General of Independent India. He served from January 26, 1950, to March 1, 1963. He was a distinguished lawyer and jurist. During his tenure, many important constitutional cases were handled. Niren De succeeded him as the second Attorney General. Soli Sorabjee and SV Gupta held this position later. The Attorney General is the highest legal officer of the Government of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Attorney General of Independent India? → MC Setalvad
☛ Who appoints the Attorney General? → President
☛ Which Article deals with the Attorney General? → Article 76
☛ Tenure of MC Setalvad? → 1950-1963
☛ Who is the highest legal officer of India? → Attorney General

q: Which of the following is NOT an essential qualification for being elected as the President?
o: Qualified for election as a member of the House of the People
qs.e: Article 58 of the Indian Constitution lays down the qualifications for election as President. These include: (1) must be a citizen of India, (2) must have completed 35 years of age, and (3) must be qualified for election as a member of the House of the People (Lok Sabha). The Constitution does not prescribe any educational qualification for the President. Therefore, being 'highly educated' is not an essential requirement.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the minimum age for President? → 35 years
☛ Which citizenship is required for President? → Citizen of India
☛ Who administers the oath to the President? → Chief Justice of India
☛ What is the term of the President? → 5 years
☛ Under which Article can the President be impeached? → Article 61

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which criticism highlights the parliamentary system’s departure from the principle of separation of powers?
o: The President has absolute control over the Prime Minister.
The cabinet simultaneously leads the executive and legislature, creating fusion of powers.
The executive and legislature operate independently.
Ministers are appointed based on expertise rather than political affiliation.
qs.e: In a parliamentary system, there is a fusion of powers rather than a separation of powers. The cabinet leads both the executive (government) and the legislature (parliament), as ministers are themselves members of the legislature. This departure from the principle of separation of powers is criticized because it concentrates too much power and weakens checks and balances. Other options are incorrect: the President does not have absolute control over the Prime Minister; the executive and legislature are not independent; ministers are appointed based on political affiliation, not expertise.
qs.kf:
☛ Who propounded the theory of separation of powers? → Montesquieu
☛ Which form of government does India have? → Parliamentary system
☛ What is the feature of parliamentary system regarding powers? → Fusion of powers
☛ What is the feature of presidential system regarding powers? → Separation of powers
☛ To whom is the cabinet responsible? → Legislature (Parliament)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3
q: What power does the President of India hold regarding the Contingency Fund of India?
o: The President approves the annual disbursement of the fund.
The President controls the fund to advance money for unforeseen expenses.
The President can only advise on the use of the fund.
The President delegates the control of the fund to the Finance Commission.
qs.e: The Contingency Fund of India is maintained by the President of India under Article 267 of the Constitution. This fund is used to meet unforeseen expenses that cannot wait for parliamentary approval. The President has the power to advance money from this fund for such urgent expenditures, and subsequent approval is obtained from Parliament. The fund is separate from the Consolidated Fund of India and can only be utilized with the President's authorization. The Ministry of Finance assists the President in administering this fund. The Contingency Fund currently stands at ₹500 crore. This mechanism ensures that the government can respond quickly to emergencies without procedural delays.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which article is the Contingency Fund established? → Article 267
☛ Who controls the Contingency Fund? → President of India
☛ What is the purpose of the fund? → To meet unforeseen expenses
☛ Is prior parliamentary approval needed? → No, it is obtained later
☛ What is the corpus of the Contingency Fund? → ₹500 crore

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3
q: What must State legislators do under Article 188 of the Constitution of India before taking their seats for the first time in state assembly?
qs.e: Article 188 of the Indian Constitution mandates that every member of a State Legislature, before taking their seat, must take an oath or affirmation before the Governor or some person appointed by them. This oath is a pledge of allegiance to the Constitution of India and to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India. Without taking this oath, a member cannot participate in the proceedings of the legislature or claim salary and allowances. This procedure ensures constitutional fidelity and democratic accountability. Other options like declaring assets or background checks are not required under Article 188. The oath is a fundamental prerequisite for assuming office as a legislator.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 188 → Oath or affirmation for State Legislature members
☛ Administering authority → Governor or appointed person
☛ Part of Constitution → Part VI (The States)
☛ Parallel provision for Parliament → Article 99
☛ Consequence of not taking oath → Cannot participate in proceedings

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3
q: What happens if a no‑confidence motion is passed in the Indian Lok Sabha against the union government?
o: The Prime Minister is given a chance to reorganise the Cabinet.
The entire Council of Ministers must resign.
qs.e: A no-confidence motion is moved in the Lok Sabha against the government. If it is passed, it indicates that the government no longer enjoys the confidence of the majority. As a result, the entire Council of Ministers (including the Prime Minister) must resign. The President then either tries to form an alternate government or dissolves the Lok Sabha for fresh elections. This process reflects the principle of collective responsibility under Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, where the executive is accountable to the legislature.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is a no-confidence motion introduced? → Lok Sabha
☛ How many members are required to support a no-confidence motion? → 50 members
☛ Who resigns when a no-confidence motion is passed? → The entire Council of Ministers
☛ To whom is the Council of Ministers responsible? → Lok Sabha
☛ How much time is allowed for discussion on a no-confidence motion? → 10 days

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 3
q: The President of India possesses the power to remove or recall officials such as Governors and Ambassadors. This power is exercised based on the advice of:
o: a resolution passed by the Parliament
qs.e: The President of India has the power to remove or recall officials like Governors and Ambassadors, but this power is exercised only on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Article 74 of the Constitution makes it mandatory for the President to act on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. Governors are appointed by the President and hold office during the pleasure of the President, but the removal cannot be done without the advice of the Council of Ministers. Similarly, Ambassadors are recalled only on the advice of the Council of Ministers. This reflects the parliamentary system of government where the President is a constitutional head and the real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers. The provision ensures that the executive actions are controlled by the elected government.
qs.kf:
☛ On whose advice can the President remove a Governor? → Union Council of Ministers
☛ Which Article binds the President to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers? → Article 74
☛ Under which Article are Governors appointed and removed by the President? → Article 156
☛ Who makes the final decision to recall an Ambassador? → President on the advice of the Council of Ministers
☛ Which system of government makes the President a constitutional head? → Parliamentary System

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which position within the Union Council of Ministers of India is immediately below the Prime Minister in hierarchy?
qs.e: In the Union Council of Ministers of India, immediately below the Prime Minister in hierarchy is the position of Cabinet Minister. Cabinet Ministers are senior members who lead key departments and play a major role in policy making. The hierarchy then proceeds to Minister of State (Independent Charge), Minister of State, and Deputy Minister. The Parliamentary Secretary is not a part of the council of ministers. According to Articles 74 and 75 of the Indian Constitution, the council of ministers functions under the leadership of the Prime Minister.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest rank in the council of ministers → Prime Minister
☛ Second highest rank after Prime Minister → Cabinet Minister
☛ Difference between Cabinet Minister and Minister of State → Cabinet Ministers attend cabinet meetings
☛ Types of Ministers of State → Independent Charge and Attached
☛ Role of Deputy Minister → Assists senior ministers

q: ______ served twice as Acting Prime Minister of India. A. Charan Singh B. Vishwanath Pratap Singh C. Indra Kumar Gujral
D. Gulzarilal Nanda
qs.e: Gulzarilal Nanda served as Acting Prime Minister of India twice. The first time was from 27 May 1964 to 9 June 1964 after the death of Jawaharlal Nehru. The second time was from 11 January 1966 to 24 January 1966 after the death of Lal Bahadur Shastri. He was a senior leader and also served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission. He held important portfolios like Labour Minister and Home Minister.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first acting Prime Minister of India? → Gulzarilal Nanda
☛ After whose deaths did Gulzarilal Nanda become acting PM? → Nehru and Shastri
☛ Which commission was Gulzarilal Nanda the deputy chairman of? → Planning Commission
☛ Which state was Gulzarilal Nanda associated with? → Punjab
☛ What is the birth year of Gulzarilal Nanda? → 1898

q: When did an Indian chief minister hoist the national flag on Independence Day for the first time?
qs.e: The first Indian chief minister to hoist the national flag on Independence Day was M. Karunanidhi, the then Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. This historic event took place on 15th August 1974. From 1947 to 1974, the privilege of hoisting the flag on Independence Day was reserved only for the Prime Minister or central ministers. Karunanidhi broke this tradition by hoisting the flag in Chennai, setting a new precedent for state governments. Later, in 1977, the Janata Party government allowed all chief ministers to hoist the flag on Independence Day. This event was a significant step towards strengthening Indian federalism and state autonomy.
qs.kf:
☛ First CM to hoist flag on Independence Day → M. Karunanidhi (Tamil Nadu)
☛ Year → 15th August 1974
☛ Earlier flag hoisting right → Only Prime Minister
☛ Permission to all CMs → Granted in 1977 by Janata Party government
☛ Significance → Strengthened state autonomy and federalism

q: As per the Constitution of India, who does NOT form the Council of Ministers?
o: Ministers who are members of Cabinet
qs.e: According to Articles 74 and 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers consists of the Prime Minister, Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers. Ministers of local government (such as municipalities and panchayats) are not part of the constitutionally defined Council of Ministers, as they operate at the local level, not at the state or central government level. The Council of Ministers is formed by the Prime Minister, who is appointed by the President. The Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ Who leads the Council of Ministers? → Prime Minister
☛ To whom is the Council of Ministers responsible? → Lok Sabha
☛ Are Ministers of State part of the Council? → Yes
☛ Who appoints Deputy Ministers? → President on PM's advice
☛ Which article deals with local government? → Article 243

q: The ____ is the first citizen of India.
qs.e: The President of India is the first citizen of the country. This constitutional position is the head of the Indian Republic and the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces. The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both houses of Parliament and the legislative assemblies of states. The President's term is five years and he/she is eligible for re-election. India's first President was Dr. Rajendra Prasad. The President's role is largely ceremonial, while the Prime Minister is the head of government.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the first citizen of India? → President
☛ What is the term of the President? → 5 years
☛ Who was the first President of India? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad
☛ Who elects the President? → Electoral College
☛ Who is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces? → President

q: Who among the following is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
qs.e: According to Article 64 of the Indian Constitution, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. This means that the Vice-President automatically becomes the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha by virtue of holding that office. This provision is also described in Article 89 of the Constitution. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha conducts the proceedings of the House and controls the conduct of its members. When the Vice-President acts as the President, he cannot perform the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. In such a situation, the Deputy Chairman performs the duties of the Chairman. Currently, Shri Jagdeep Dhankhar is the Vice-President of India and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha? → Vice-President of India
☛ Which article of the Constitution deals with the Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Article 89
☛ When can the Vice-President not act as Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → When he is acting as President
☛ Who elects the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Members of Rajya Sabha
☛ Who is the current Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Jagdeep Dhankhar

q: Which of the following articles deal with the provisions regarding the election, qualification, and removal of the Vice-President of India?
qs.e: The Constitution of India deals with the Vice-President in Articles 63 to 71. Article 63 establishes the office of the Vice-President. Article 64 makes the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Article 66 describes the election process, which is done by the members of Parliament through single transferable vote. Article 67 provides for the term (5 years) and removal process, requiring a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha. Article 68 deals with election to fill a vacancy. Article 69 covers the oath, and Article 71 deals with disputes related to the election. Other options like Articles 224-245 pertain to the judiciary.
qs.kf:
☛ Which articles deal with the Vice-President? → Articles 63-71
☛ What is the term of the Vice-President? → 5 years
☛ Which article covers the removal of the Vice-President? → Article 67
☛ Which article describes the election of the Vice-President? → Article 66
☛ Which article makes the Vice-President the Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Article 64

q: Which of the following articles deals with the office of the special officer for Linguistic Minorities?
qs.e: Article 350-B of the Indian Constitution deals with the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. This officer is appointed by the President and is tasked with investigating all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution and reporting to the President. This provision was added after the States Reorganisation Act of 1956 to protect the rights of linguistic minorities. Article 350-A directs state governments to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue to children of linguistic minorities. The Special Officer ensures that these safeguards are implemented effectively, thereby promoting linguistic diversity and protecting minority rights.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities? → 350-B
☛ Which article provides for instruction in mother tongue for linguistic minorities? → 350-A
☛ Who appoints the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities? → President
☛ Article 350-B deals with? → Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
☛ To whom does the Special Officer under Article 350-B report? → President

q: Who among the following is the leader of the house in the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: The leader of the house in the Lok Sabha is the Prime Minister. According to the Constitution, the Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party and guides the proceedings of the house. This position is informal, but the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs may act as leader if the Prime Minister is a member of the Rajya Sabha. The Lok Sabha Speaker is the presiding officer, not the leader. The Leader of Opposition is the leader of the largest opposition party. The President of India is a part of Parliament but not the house leader. Hence, the Prime Minister is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the leader of the house in Lok Sabha? → Prime Minister
☛ What is the role of Lok Sabha Speaker? → Presiding officer
☛ Who is the Leader of Opposition? → Leader of largest opposition party
☛ What part of Parliament is the President? → Integral part
☛ When can Parliamentary Affairs Minister become leader of house? → When PM is a member of Rajya Sabha

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which two policy areas are explicitly managed by the Union Cabinet in India as part of its coordinating functions?
qs.e: In India, the Union Cabinet is primarily responsible for coordinating government policies. It directly manages critical areas like Foreign Relations and Defence due to their significance for national security and international affairs. Other options such as Agriculture, Labour, Tourism, Sports, Education, and Health are subjects in the Concurrent List or State List, meaning they are shared with state governments. In contrast, Foreign Relations and Defence are exclusively under the central government's jurisdiction as per the Union List of the Constitution. The Cabinet's coordinating role ensures that various ministries work cohesively, and these two areas require unified decision-making at the highest level to maintain sovereignty and diplomatic integrity.
qs.kf:
☛ Head of the Cabinet → Prime Minister
☛ Foreign policy determination → Union Cabinet
☛ Defence matters control → Central Government
☛ Coordination body → Union Cabinet
☛ Included in Union List → Foreign Affairs & Defence

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1
q: In some cases, the Prime Minister of India assigns an independent charge of a portfolio to a Minister of State. This implies that the Minister of State:
o: loses the title of Minister of State
serves jointly with a Cabinet Minister to share and perform responsibilities of the assigned portfolio
functions as if in Cabinet rank with full independent responsibility for that portfolio
qs.e: When the Prime Minister assigns independent charge of a portfolio to a Minister of State, that minister becomes the sole head of that department and functions akin to a Cabinet Minister. In such a role, the Minister of State does not work under any Cabinet Minister but reports directly to the Prime Minister. The minister exercises full powers and responsibilities of that portfolio independently, though the official title remains Minister of State. This arrangement allows the minister to operate with Cabinet rank status, including attending Cabinet meetings when invited, and having full decision-making authority for the assigned ministry.
qs.kf:
☛ What rank is given to a Minister of State with independent charge? → Cabinet rank
☛ To whom does a Minister of State with independent charge report? → Prime Minister
☛ Can a Minister of State with independent charge attend Cabinet meetings? → Yes, if invited
☛ How many types of ministers are there in the Union Council of Ministers? → Three: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State (Independent Charge), Ministers of State
☛ A Minister of State with independent charge enjoys powers equivalent to which minister? → Cabinet Minister

q: The Prime Minister's Climate Change Council consists of _______ members.
qs.e: The Prime Minister's Climate Change Council (PMCCC) was established in 2021. It consists of a total of 18 members. The council is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes ministers, secretaries, and experts from various ministries. Its main objective is to coordinate policies and strategies related to climate change. The council periodically reviews the climate action plan and approves new initiatives. It plays a crucial role in achieving India's climate goals. The council ensures that all departments work together to address climate challenges effectively.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMCCC established? → 2021
☛ What is the full form of PMCCC? → Prime Minister's Climate Change Council
☛ Who is the chairperson of PMCCC? → Prime Minister
☛ How many members are in PMCCC? → 18
☛ What is the main objective of PMCCC? → Coordination of climate policies

q: Which is the second highest constitutional office in India?
qs.e: In India, the Vice President is the second highest constitutional office. After the President, the Vice President holds the highest constitutional position. Article 63 provides for the Vice President. The Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. In the absence or death of the President, the Vice President assumes the duties of the President. The Prime Minister is the head of the executive, not a constitutional office. The Governor is the constitutional head at the state level.
qs.kf:
☛ Who elects the Vice President? → Members of both Houses of Parliament
☛ What is the term of the Vice President? → 5 years
☛ Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha? → Vice President
☛ Who settles disputes related to the election of the Vice President? → Supreme Court
☛ Where is the resolution to remove the Vice President introduced? → Rajya Sabha

q: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
qs.e: The first Deputy Prime Minister of India was Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He served in this role from 1947 to 1950. He was also the first Home Minister of India and played a crucial role in the integration of princely states into the Indian Union. Known as the 'Iron Man of India', Patel was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement and a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi. His efforts were instrumental in creating a unified India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Home Minister of India? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ When is Sardar Patel's birth anniversary celebrated? → 31 October
☛ Who was the first Prime Minister of India? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ What is Vallabhbhai Patel's birthplace? → Gujarat
☛ By which title is he known? → Iron Man of India

q: The word "Primus inter Pares" shows which of the following?
qs.e: The Latin phrase "Primus inter Pares" translates to "first among equals." It describes a person who is the leader or foremost among a group of peers, without possessing superior legal authority over them. In a parliamentary system, the Prime Minister is often considered the "first among equals" within the cabinet. The Prime Minister is a member of the cabinet like other ministers, but as the head of government, holds a preeminent position. According to this concept, the Prime Minister is the leading figure among equals, not a superior authority. Unlike a President or head of state, the Prime Minister's power is based on the collective responsibility of the cabinet. This term is used in political science to explain the nature of government where the leader is not above others but primus among them. It applies to many countries following the Westminster system, such as India and the United Kingdom.
qs.kf:
☛ What does Primus inter Pares mean? → First among equals
☛ Which language does this term originate from? → Latin
☛ For which position is this term used in India? → Prime Minister
☛ How does the Prime Minister relate to the cabinet in a parliamentary system? → As first among equals
☛ Which type of government system uses this concept? → Westminster system (e.g., India, UK)

q: The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by whom?
o: By the Prime Minister of India
qs.e: Under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, the President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and other Election Commissioners. The President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The Election Commission is an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India. The CEC holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier. This appointment is part of the President's executive powers and not subject to judicial or legislative approval, though removal requires impeachment by Parliament similar to a Supreme Court judge.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner? → President of India
☛ Which article deals with the Election Commission? → Article 324
☛ What is the term of the Chief Election Commissioner? → 6 years or age 65, whichever is earlier
☛ What type of body is the Election Commission? → Independent constitutional body
☛ Can the Chief Election Commissioner be removed? → Yes, through impeachment like a High Court judge

q: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
qs.e: The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India. This procedure is governed by Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. The President also appoints other Election Commissioners along with the CEC. The appointment is made on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister. The Chief Election Commissioner holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier. He/she can be removed from office only through impeachment by the Parliament, similar to the removal of a Supreme Court judge.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India? → President
☛ What is the term of office of the CEC? → 6 years or until age 65
☛ How can the CEC be removed? → Through impeachment
☛ Under which Article is the Election Commission established? → Article 324
☛ Who heads the Election Commission of India? → Chief Election Commissioner

q: What is the maximum number of Ministers allowed in the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, as per the 91st Amendment Act?
qs.e: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003, amended Articles 75 and 164 of the Indian Constitution. It stipulates that the total number of ministers in the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total membership of the Lok Sabha. This provision was made to limit the size of the cabinet and ensure efficient governance. For example, with the current Lok Sabha having 543 members, the maximum number of ministers would be 81 (15% of 543). This amendment is crucial for political stability and accountability. Similarly, in states, the number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, cannot exceed 15% of the total members of the Legislative Assembly, but must have a minimum of 12 ministers.
qs.kf:
☛ 91st Amendment Act → Enacted in 2003.
☛ Maximum size of Council of Ministers → 15% of Lok Sabha members.
☛ Maximum ministers in states → 15% of Legislative Assembly members (minimum 12).
☛ Article 75 → Deals with Union Council of Ministers.
☛ Article 164 → Deals with State Council of Ministers.

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following is NOT one of the factors that the Prime Minister should consider when selecting ministers for the Union Council of Ministers in India?
qs.e: In India, the Prime Minister appoints the Union Council of Ministers. While selecting ministers, the Prime Minister considers factors like individual capacity and capability, geographical representation (balance from different states), representation of backward classes, minorities, and women, as well as political experience. However, representation of foreign communities is not a valid factor because the Council of Ministers consists only of Indian citizens, and there is no constitutional provision for foreign communities. This factor is irrelevant and should not be considered. The Prime Minister ensures the cabinet reflects India's diversity and competence, but foreign representation is outside the scope of Indian polity.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints ministers in the Union Council of Ministers? → Prime Minister
☛ What is the basis of geographical representation? → Balance of different states and regions
☛ Can foreign citizens become ministers in India? → No, only Indian citizens
☛ Which groups' representation is important in minister selection? → Backward classes, minorities, women
☛ What is the primary consideration for minister selection? → Merit and experience

q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the extent of executive power of the Union?
qs.e: Article 73 of the Indian Constitution deals with the extent of executive power of the Union. It states that the executive power of the Union shall extend to all matters on which Parliament has the power to make laws, and to the exercise of powers arising from treaties or agreements. Article 73(2) clarifies that this power does not affect the executive power of the states. This article clarifies the distribution of powers in the federal structure. Article 70 deals with the discharge of the President's functions in his absence, Article 61 with the impeachment of the President, and Article 78 with the duties of the Prime Minister.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 73 → Extent of executive power of the Union
☛ Article 70 → Discharge of President's functions
☛ Article 61 → Impeachment of President
☛ Article 78 → Duties of Prime Minister
☛ Article 73(2) → No effect on state executive power

q: White one of the following articles of Indian Constitution deals with the tenure of the President?
qs.e: Article 56 of the Indian Constitution deals with the tenure of the President. It states that the President holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office. He may resign by writing under his hand addressed to the Vice-President. The process of removal of the President is described in Article 61. Article 55 relates to the method of election of the President, Article 53 deals with the executive power of the Union, and Article 54 deals with the Electoral College for the President's election.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the term of the President of India? → Five years
☛ Which article deals with the executive power of the President? → Article 53
☛ Which article mentions the Electoral College for President? → Article 54
☛ Which article describes the method of election of President? → Article 55
☛ Which article provides for the removal of the President? → Article 61

q: Which British Prime Minister sent the Cripps Mission to India?
qs.e: The Cripps Mission was sent to India in 1942 by the British Prime Minister Winston Churchill. It was led by Sir Stafford Cripps. The mission aimed to negotiate with Indian leaders for Indian cooperation during World War II. It proposed granting India Dominion status after the war. However, the proposal was rejected by both the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League. The Congress wanted immediate independence, while the Muslim League did not receive clear assurance regarding the demand for Pakistan. After the failure of the Cripps Mission, the Quit India Movement was launched.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the leader of the Cripps Mission? → Sir Stafford Cripps
☛ In which year did the Cripps Mission come to India? → 1942
☛ What was the objective of the Cripps Mission? → To secure Indian cooperation in World War II
☛ Which organizations rejected the Cripps Mission proposal? → Congress and Muslim League
☛ Which movement started after the failure of the Cripps Mission? → Quit India Movement

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 2
q: What happens if a minister is not a member of the Parliament for six consecutive months?
o: The minister ceases to hold office.
The minister must be re-elected within three months.
The minister can continue with special permission from the President.
The Prime Minister can grant an extension.
qs.e: According to Article 75(5) of the Indian Constitution, if a minister is not a member of Parliament for six consecutive months, they cease to be a minister. This provision ensures parliamentary accountability in a democracy. The minister must be a member of either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha to remain in office. If they fail to get elected or nominated within six months of appointment, they lose the post. This rule applies to all members of the Union Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister. It upholds the principle that ministers are responsible to the legislature.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 75(5) → Minister must be a member of Parliament for six consecutive months
☛ Membership requirement → Minister must be a member of either House of Parliament
☛ Appointment of PM → President appoints Prime Minister, who is the leader of Lok Sabha
☛ Council of Ministers → Appointed by President on PM's advice
☛ Tenure of Minister → Holds office during pleasure of President or until loss of Parliament membership

q: All other ministers, including the Prime Minister, are collectively responsible for __________.
qs.e: According to Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This means that all ministers, including the Prime Minister, are jointly accountable to the Lok Sabha. This is a fundamental principle of the parliamentary system of government where the executive is responsible to the legislature. If a no-confidence motion is passed against the Council of Ministers in the Lok Sabha, the entire council must resign. This system ensures the accountability of the government to the people's representatives.
qs.kf:
☛ To whom is the Council of Ministers collectively responsible? → Lok Sabha
☛ Which article deals with collective responsibility of ministers? → Article 75(3)
☛ In which house can a no-confidence motion be introduced? → Lok Sabha
☛ What type of government system does India have? → Parliamentary system
☛ Who appoints ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister? → President

q: In what way does the Union Cabinet differ from other government committees?
o: It functions independently of the Prime Minister
It serves as the supreme decision-making body of the executive branch
It is elected by the public
It includes members of the judiciary
qs.e: The Union Cabinet is the highest decision-making body in the executive branch of the Indian government, operating under Articles 74 and 75 of the Constitution. Unlike other government committees, the Cabinet is chaired by the Prime Minister and determines major policies. It is collectively responsible to the Parliament, and its members are appointed by the Prime Minister, not elected by the public. The Cabinet does not include judiciary members. Its meetings are confidential, and its decisions are binding on all ministers. This distinguishes it from other committees, which are often advisory or subordinate. The Cabinet exercises real executive power and coordinates government functions.
qs.kf:
☛ Who heads the Union Cabinet? → Prime Minister
☛ Whom are Cabinet decisions binding on? → All ministers
☛ To whom is the Cabinet responsible? → Parliament
☛ What is the nature of Cabinet meetings? → Confidential
☛ Who appoints the Cabinet members? → Prime Minister

q: An individual who is not a member of either House of Parliament may be appointed to the Council of Ministers; however, they must become a member of either House within a specified time frame of:
qs.e: According to Article 75(5) of the Indian Constitution, if a person who is not a member of either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) is appointed to the Council of Ministers, they must become a member of either House within 6 months from the date of appointment. This provision ensures that ministers remain accountable to the Parliament. If they fail to become a member within the specified period, their ministerial position is terminated. This rule upholds the democratic accountability of the parliamentary system, ensuring that only those who are answerable to the legislature can hold ministerial office.
qs.kf:
☛ Time limit for a non-member to become a member of Parliament after appointment as minister → 6 months
☛ Which Article deals with this provision? → Article 75(5)
☛ Can a non-MP become a minister? → Yes, but must become a member within 6 months
☛ Consequence of not becoming a member within 6 months → Ministerial post ends
☛ Principle behind this provision → Parliamentary accountability

q: Which of the following correctly represents the three-tier structure of the Council of Ministers?
o: Chief Ministers – State Ministers – Deputy Chief Ministers
Cabinet Ministers – Ministers of State – Deputy Ministers
Prime Minister – Ministers of State – Cabinet Ministers
qs.e: Under Articles 74 and 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers has a three-tier structure. At the top are Cabinet Ministers, who head important departments and make policy decisions. The second tier consists of Ministers of State (MoS), who may hold independent charge or work under Cabinet Ministers. The third tier comprises Deputy Ministers, who assist senior ministers. This structure ensures decentralization and efficiency in executive power. Cabinet Ministers form the highest decision-making body, while Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers work under their supervision. The hierarchy maintains order and specialization in governance.
qs.kf:
☛ What are the three tiers of the Council of Ministers in India? → Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, Deputy Ministers
☛ Which is the highest body of the Council of Ministers? → Cabinet Ministers
☛ Which article deals with the Council of Ministers? → Article 74
☛ What is a Minister of State also known as? → MoS (Minister of State)
☛ What is the main function of a Deputy Minister? → To assist senior ministers

q: Consider the following statements.
1. As per Article 167, it is the duty of the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers.
2. Article 165 states that the Governor administers the oaths of office and secrecy to ministers.
3. Article 163 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor, except in discretionary matters. Which of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: All three statements are correct. Article 167 imposes a duty on the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers, including proposed bills and administrative information. Article 165 states that the Governor administers the oaths of office and secrecy to ministers and appoints the Chief Minister. Article 163 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor, except in matters where the Governor is required to act in his discretion. These provisions are part of Part VI of the Indian Constitution concerning state executive.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 167 → Chief Minister's duty to inform Governor
☛ Article 165 → Governor administers oath to ministers
☛ Article 163 → Council of Ministers to aid Governor
☛ Article 164 → Appointment of Chief Minister and Council
☛ Article 166 → Conduct of state government business

q: Consider the following statements.
1. Before the Prime Minister enters upon his office, the President administers to him the oaths of office and secrecy.
2. The President can dismiss the Prime Minister at any time in an arbitrary way.
3. If the Prime Minister loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, he must resign or the President can dismiss him. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
qs.e: According to Article 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President. Before entering office, the President administers the oaths of office and secrecy to him, so statement 1 is correct. The President cannot dismiss the Prime Minister arbitrarily; this is possible only if the Prime Minister loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha or violates constitutional process, so statement 2 is incorrect. If the Prime Minister loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, he must resign or the President can dismiss him, which is the essence of the parliamentary system, so statement 3 is correct. Thus, only statements 1 and 3 are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Prime Minister? → President
☛ Who administers oath to the Prime Minister? → President
☛ To whom is the Prime Minister responsible? → Lok Sabha
☛ What is the basis for dismissal of the Prime Minister? → Loss of confidence of Lok Sabha
☛ What is the form of government in India? → Parliamentary system

q: Consider the following pairs. Article Provision
1. 63 The Vice-President of India
2. 64 The Vice-President to be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States
3. 65 The Vice-President to act as President during the absence of the President
4. 66 Election of Vice-President Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
qs.e: Article 63 of the Indian Constitution provides for the Vice-President of India. Article 64 states that the Vice-President shall be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). Article 65 deals with the Vice-President acting as President during a vacancy or absence of the President. Article 66 provides for the Election of the Vice-President. Since all four pairs are correctly matched, option 2 is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the term of office of the Vice-President of India? → 5 years
☛ Which house initiates the resolution for removal of the Vice-President? → Rajya Sabha
☛ What is the method of election for the Vice-President? → Single transferable vote
☛ What is the minimum age required to be the Vice-President? → 35 years
☛ For how long can the Vice-President act as President in case of vacancy? → 6 months

q: Which of the following statements is true about the role of Cabinet Ministers in India?
o: They head important ministries like Home, Defence, and Finance.
They only assist other ministers in their duties.
They do not attend Cabinet meetings.
They are not involved in policy decisions.
qs.e: In India, Cabinet Ministers are senior ministers who head important ministries such as Home, Defence, Finance, and External Affairs. They are members of the Cabinet, which is the highest decision-making body in the government. They attend Cabinet meetings and are involved in policy decisions. According to Article 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Cabinet consists of the Prime Minister and other ministers. Cabinet Ministers are superior to Ministers of State and follow the principle of collective responsibility. They are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article are Cabinet Ministers appointed? → Article 75
☛ Who heads the Cabinet? → Prime Minister
☛ Which ministries do Cabinet Ministers typically head? → Home, Defence, Finance, etc.
☛ Are Cabinet Ministers involved in policy decisions? → Yes
☛ What principle do Cabinet Ministers follow? → Collective responsibility

q: What is the main difference between a Cabinet Minister and a Minister of State with independent charge?
o: A Minister of State with independent charge does not exercise any significant powers.
A Minister of State with independent charge may head a ministry without being under a Cabinet Minister.
A Ministry of State is included in Cabinet meetings but does not exercise any significant powers.
A Minister of State with independent charge does not hold any specific responsibilities.
qs.e: In India, the Council of Ministers has three levels: Cabinet Minister, Minister of State, and Deputy Minister. A Cabinet Minister heads a major ministry and attends Cabinet meetings. In contrast, a Minister of State either works under a Cabinet Minister or can be given independent charge. A Minister of State with independent charge is not subordinate to any Cabinet Minister; instead, they independently lead a ministry and report directly to the Prime Minister. However, they do not attend Cabinet meetings unless specially invited. This distinction reflects the difference in powers and responsibilities, with independent charge ministers having autonomy but not full Cabinet rank.
qs.kf:
☛ Main difference between Cabinet Minister and Minister of State with independent charge → MoS with independent charge is not under any Cabinet Minister.
☛ Who does a Minister of State with independent charge report to → Directly to the Prime Minister.
☛ Does a Minister of State with independent charge attend Cabinet meetings → No, unless specially invited.
☛ Levels of Council of Ministers in India → Cabinet Minister, Minister of State, Deputy Minister.
☛ Status of Minister of State with independent charge → Not equivalent to Cabinet Minister, but autonomous leadership.

q: Who headed the Committee of Ministers on the Augmentation of Financial Resources of Urban Local Bodies, formed in India in 1963?
qs.e: In 1963, the Government of India formed a Committee of Ministers to examine measures for the augmentation of financial resources of urban local bodies. This committee was headed by Rafiq Zakaria, who was a central minister at the time. The committee is also known as the Zakaria Committee. It recommended increasing financial resources for urban bodies through improved taxation, higher grants from state governments, and better resource mobilization. This committee is considered significant in the field of urban administration and financial reforms.
qs.kf:
☛ Zakaria Committee → Formed in 1963 for augmentation of financial resources of urban local bodies.
☛ Chairman of the committee → Rafiq Zakaria.
☛ Rafiq Zakaria → Also served as India's first Minister of Education.
☛ Urban local bodies → Include municipal corporations, municipalities, and nagar panchayats.
☛ Augmentation of financial resources → Focus on increasing taxes, fees, and grants.

q: What is the correct sequence in which the oath of office binds a Union Minister?
o: Integrity → Constitution → Sovereignty → Duty → Impartiality (justice without fear or favour)
Allegiance to the → Constitution, → Sovereignty and integrity → Faithful discharge of duties→ Impartiality
Allegiance → Sovereignty → Duty and Impartiality→ Faithful discharge
qs.e: According to Article 75(4) of the Indian Constitution, a Union Minister takes an oath of office. The correct sequence is: first allegiance to the Constitution, then a vow to uphold sovereignty and integrity, followed by faithful discharge of duties, and finally a promise of impartiality (justice without fear or favour). This sequence is given in the third option. The format of the oath is prescribed in the Third Schedule of the Constitution. The oath emphasizes the paramount importance of India's sovereignty and integrity.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article does a Union Minister take oath? → Article 75(4)
☛ Where is the oath format prescribed? → Third Schedule
☛ What is the first vow of a Minister? → Allegiance to the Constitution
☛ To whom is impartiality promised? → Law and justice
☛ Which oath mentions India's sovereignty and integrity? → Minister's oath

q: Which of the following bodies is described as the "real executive" in the Indian political system?
qs.e: In the Indian political system, the Prime Minister is termed as the 'real executive'. According to the Constitution, the President is the constitutional head, but the actual executive power is vested in the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. The Prime Minister is the head of the government and runs the administration and policies. The Supreme Court is a judicial body, while the Council of Ministers acts collectively, but the Prime Minister holds primacy. He advises the President and plays a central role in the governance system.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is called the real executive? → Prime Minister of India
☛ Who is the constitutional head? → President
☛ Who is the leader of the Council of Ministers? → Prime Minister
☛ Who is the head of the government? → Prime Minister
☛ On whose advice does the President act? → Council of Ministers

q: Which of the following cabinet committees is NOT headed by the Prime Minister?
o: Cabinet committee on employment and skill development
Cabinet committee on investment and growth
qs.e: In India, cabinet committees are formed to streamline government functioning. The Prime Minister chairs most key committees such as the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, Cabinet Committee on Employment and Skill Development, and Cabinet Committee on Investment and Growth. However, the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs is chaired by the Home Minister, not the Prime Minister. This committee is responsible for advancing the government's legislative agenda in Parliament and ensuring cooperation in the house. Therefore, it is the committee that is NOT headed by the Prime Minister.
qs.kf:
☛ Who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs? → Prime Minister
