☛ Who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Employment and Skill Development? → Prime Minister
☛ Who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Investment and Growth? → Prime Minister
☛ Who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs? → Home Minister
☛ What is the main purpose of cabinet committees in India? → To ensure coordination and efficiency in policy decisions

q: Which Indian Prime Minister among the following was never the Chief Minister of any state of India?
qs.e: Chandrashekhar was the 8th Prime Minister of India. He never served as the Chief Minister of any state. In contrast, Morarji Desai was the Chief Minister of Bombay State, V.P. Singh was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, and P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh. Chandrashekhar lacked experience as the head of a state government before becoming Prime Minister. He was a member of both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha but never became a Chief Minister.
qs.kf:
☛ Indian PM who was never a Chief Minister? → Chandrashekhar
☛ Morarji Desai was CM of which state? → Bombay State
☛ V.P. Singh was CM of which state? → Uttar Pradesh
☛ P.V. Narasimha Rao was CM of which state? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Chandrashekhar's tenure as PM? → 1990-1991

q: Who among the following was the first Union Finance Minister of Independent India?
qs.e: RK Shanmukham Chetty was the first Union Finance Minister of independent India, serving from 1947 to 1949. He presented India's first budget (1947-48). Chetty was a member of the Indian Civil Service and later became Chief Minister of Madras state. His tenure laid the foundation for India's early economic policies.
qs.kf:
☛ First Union Finance Minister → RK Shanmukham Chetty
☛ First Budget Presenter → RK Shanmukham Chetty (1947-48)
☛ First Female Finance Minister → Indira Gandhi
☛ Longest Serving Finance Minister → P. Chidambaram
☛ Current Finance Minister → Nirmala Sitharaman

q: Which of the following articles in the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice?
qs.e: Article 74 of the Indian Constitution provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice. This article forms the bedrock of the parliamentary system of government in India, where the real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers while the President acts as the constitutional head. The 42nd Amendment (1976) made it binding on the President to follow the advice of the Council of Ministers. However, the Supreme Court later clarified that the President can send the advice back for reconsideration. Article 74 thus ensures the principle of collective responsibility and democratic governance in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 74 → Provisions for formation and functions of Council of Ministers
☛ Article 75 → Appointment of Prime Minister and other ministers
☛ Article 53 → Executive power of the Union vested in the President
☛ 42nd Amendment → Made the President bound by the advice of Council of Ministers
☛ Article 78 → Prime Minister's duty to furnish information to the President

q: Who amongst the following became the Acting Prime Minister of India twice?
qs.e: Gulzarilal Nanda became the Acting Prime Minister of India twice. First in 1964 after the death of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and second in 1966 after the death of Lal Bahadur Shastri. He was a freedom fighter and a leader of the Indian National Congress. Gulzarilal Nanda also served as the Minister of Labour and Employment and is known for his work in labour welfare.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Acting Prime Minister of India? → Gulzarilal Nanda
☛ How many times did Gulzarilal Nanda serve as Acting PM? → Two times
☛ Which party did Gulzarilal Nanda belong to? → Indian National Congress
☛ When was Gulzarilal Nanda's tenure? → 1964 and 1966
☛ Which ministry is Gulzarilal Nanda known for? → Ministry of Labour and Employment

q: The Attorney General of India is the highest law officer of the country appointed by whom?
o: The seniormost Judge of Supreme Court
qs.e: The Attorney General of India is the highest law officer of the country. According to Article 76, he/she is appointed by the President of India. The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President. The Attorney General advises the Government of India on legal matters and represents the government in the Supreme Court. He/She may participate in the proceedings of Parliament but cannot vote. The Attorney General must have the same qualifications as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article does the Attorney General of India come? → Article 76
☛ What is the removal process of the Attorney General? → At the pleasure of the President
☛ Which court does the Attorney General represent the government in? → Supreme Court
☛ What qualifications must the Attorney General have? → Same as a Judge of the Supreme Court
☛ Can the Attorney General vote in Parliament? → No

q: The impeachment of President due to violation of the the Constitution is preferred by _____________.
qs.e: According to Article 61 of the Indian Constitution, the impeachment of the President for violation of the Constitution can be initiated by either House of the Parliament. The process begins when at least one-fourth of the members of that House sign a notice of the charge. The House then investigates the charge through a committee. If the committee finds the charge valid, the resolution is sent to the other House. The other House also investigates, and if passed by a two-thirds majority, the President is removed from office. This procedure can be initiated at any time during the President's term.
qs.kf:
☛ Ground for Presidential impeachment → Violation of the Constitution
☛ House that can prefer the charge → Either House of Parliament
☛ Minimum signatories for the notice → One-fourth of total members of the House
☛ Majority required in the other House → Two-thirds of members present and voting
☛ Article governing impeachment → Article 61

q: The governor’s power to issue ordinances is mentioned in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: Article 213 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Governor to issue ordinances. This power is exercised when the state legislature is not in session and immediate action is required. An ordinance has the same force as a legislative act but ceases to operate six weeks after the legislature reassembles unless approved. This differs from Article 123, which grants similar powers to the President at the national level. The Governor's ordinance-making power is part of Part VI of the Constitution, dealing with state executive. It is a discretionary power but must follow constitutional limitations.
qs.kf:
☛ Article for Governor's ordinance power → 213
☛ Article for President's ordinance power → 123
☛ When can Governor issue ordinance? → When legislature not in session
☛ Maximum duration of ordinance → 6 weeks after session starts
☛ Ordinance has same effect as → an Act of legislature

q: Who appoints the members of the Union Public Service Commission in India?
qs.e: The members of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) are appointed by the President of India under Article 316 of the Constitution. The President appoints the Chairman and other members of the UPSC. The term of office for members is 6 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. UPSC is a constitutional body responsible for recruitment to civil services in India. The President also has the power to remove members, but only through the process of impeachment on grounds of misbehavior or incapacity. The President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers in making these appointments.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Chairman of UPSC? → President of India
☛ What is the term of UPSC members? → 6 years or age 65
☛ Under which article is UPSC established? → Article 315
☛ Who can dissolve UPSC? → Only Parliament
☛ How can a UPSC member be removed? → Impeachment by President

q: Who has the power to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship?
qs.e: According to Article 11 of the Indian Constitution, the power to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship lies with Parliament. This article empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship through legislation. The President, Prime Minister, or Cabinet do not have this authority. Exercising this power, Parliament enacted the Citizenship Act, 1955, which provides for acquisition of citizenship by birth, descent, registration, and naturalization. It also covers termination of citizenship through renunciation, termination, and deprivation. Thus, all matters concerning citizenship rules are under Parliament's jurisdiction.
qs.kf:
☛ Power over citizenship provisions → Parliament (Article 11)
☛ Main citizenship law → Citizenship Act, 1955
☛ Citizenship by birth → For those born in India on or after 26 Jan 1950
☛ Citizenship by descent → For those born abroad to Indian parents
☛ Citizenship by naturalization → For foreigners residing at least 11 years

q: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha will have to send his resignation letter to ________.
qs.e: According to Article 94 of the Indian Constitution, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha must submit his letter of resignation to the Deputy Speaker. This provision ensures the smooth functioning of the House even in the Speaker's absence. When the Speaker resigns, the Deputy Speaker assumes the responsibilities of the Speaker until a new Speaker is elected. The resignation cannot be sent to the Prime Minister, President, or Minister of Parliamentary Affairs as per the constitutional mandate. This rule is designed to maintain continuity and transparency in the parliamentary process.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 94 → Deals with resignation of Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha
☛ Resignation letter → Speaker sends to Deputy Speaker; Deputy Speaker sends to Speaker
☛ Article 90 → Corresponding provision for Rajya Sabha Chairman and Deputy Chairman
☛ Election of Speaker → Elected by members of Lok Sabha
☛ First Speaker → Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar

q: The tenure of the members of the Rajya Sabha is ________
qs.e: The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament. The tenure of its members is 6 years, while the tenure of Lok Sabha members is 5 years. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and one-third of its members retire every two years. Members of the Rajya Sabha are indirectly elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies. The President nominates 12 members for their expertise in art, literature, science, and social service. The total strength of the Rajya Sabha is 245 members, of which 233 are elected and 12 are nominated.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the tenure of Rajya Sabha members? → 6 years
☛ What is the tenure of Lok Sabha members? → 5 years
☛ What is the total strength of Rajya Sabha? → 245
☛ How many Rajya Sabha members are nominated by the President? → 12
☛ How many Rajya Sabha members are elected? → 233

q: The interval between the two consecutive parliament session is called
qs.e: In Indian Parliament, the interval between two consecutive sessions is called Recess (Relaxation). It is the gap between the end of one session and the beginning of the next. During this period, parliamentary proceedings are adjourned. Suspension means stopping the proceedings of a day for a few hours. House dissolution occurs when the Lok Sabha's term ends or is dissolved by the President. Indefinitely postponement means adjourning the session for an indefinite period, whereas recess is for a fixed duration. Thus, the interval between two consecutive sessions is called Recess.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the interval between two consecutive parliament sessions called? → Recess
☛ What does suspension mean in parliament? → Stopping proceedings of a day for a few hours
☛ How is Lok Sabha dissolved? → On completion of term or by President
☛ What is meant by indefinite adjournment? → Adjourning the session for an indefinite period
☛ Who summons the parliament session? → The President

q: When did the post of Lok Sabha Speaker and Deputy Speaker originate in India?
qs.e: The post of Lok Sabha Speaker and Deputy Speaker originated in 1921. These posts were created in the Central Legislative Assembly established under the Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms). The first Speaker was Sir Frederick Whyte and the first Deputy Speaker was Sachchidananda Sinha. After independence, the tradition continued in the newly formed Lok Sabha in 1952. The first Lok Sabha Speaker was Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar. The Speaker presides over the lower house of Parliament.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of Lok Sabha Speaker → Usually 5 years
☛ Who elects the Lok Sabha Speaker → Members of Lok Sabha
☛ First Lok Sabha Speaker → Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar (1952)
☛ Pro tem Speaker of Lok Sabha → Senior most member
☛ Article related to Lok Sabha Speaker → Article 93

q: Prime Minister is the leader of the ________
qs.e: In India, the Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha. According to Article 75 of the Constitution, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President and is usually the leader of the party that commands a majority in the Lok Sabha. Even if the Prime Minister is a member of the Rajya Sabha, he or she must have the confidence of the majority in the Lok Sabha. Majority in the Lok Sabha means the party has at least 272 seats out of a total of 543. The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers and is responsible to the Lok Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum age to become Prime Minister → 25 years
☛ Term of Prime Minister → 5 years
☛ Who appoints the Prime Minister → President
☛ Which house can a Prime Minister belong to → Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
☛ To whom is the Prime Minister responsible → Lok Sabha

q: Who was the ﬁrst Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
qs.e: Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was the first Vice President of India, who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Hence, he became the first Chairman (Presiding Officer) of the Rajya Sabha. He served from 13 May 1952 to 12 May 1962. Later, he became the second President of India. The Rajya Sabha was constituted in 1952 and its first session began on 13 May 1952. Dr. Radhakrishnan was a renowned philosopher and educationist.
qs.kf:
☛ First Chairman of Rajya Sabha → Dr. S. Radhakrishnan
☛ First Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha → S.V. Krishnamoorthy Rao
☛ First session of Rajya Sabha → 13 May 1952
☛ First woman Chairman of Rajya Sabha → Najma Heptulla
☛ Term of Chairman of Rajya Sabha → 5 years (as Vice President)

q: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by ___________
o: All Members of the Lok Sabha
qs.e: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by all members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves. This election is held in the first meeting after the formation of the Lok Sabha. The office of the Speaker is provided under Article 93 of the Indian Constitution. A resolution to remove the Speaker must be passed by a majority of all members of the Lok Sabha. The Speaker presides over the proceedings of the Lok Sabha and maintains the dignity of the House. This position is usually given to a member of the ruling party.
qs.kf:
☛ Who elects the Speaker of Lok Sabha? → All Members of Lok Sabha
☛ By what majority is a removal resolution passed? → Majority of all members of Lok Sabha
☛ Under which Article is the Speaker's office? → Article 93
☛ To whom does the Speaker report? → Lok Sabha
☛ In which type of voting can the Speaker participate? → Casting vote in case of a tie

q: The number of nominated members in the Lok Sabha by the President
qs.e: Under Article 331 of the Indian Constitution, the President can nominate a maximum of 2 members from the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha if they are not adequately represented. This provision was made to ensure representation for the community. Nominated members have all the rights of other members except they cannot become ministers. However, the 104th Constitutional Amendment (2020) abolished the reservation for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. Therefore, currently the President cannot nominate anyone to the Lok Sabha. But according to the older provision before the amendment, the number was 2, which is the answer to this question.
qs.kf:
☛ President → Could nominate up to 2 Anglo-Indian members in Lok Sabha.
☛ Article 331 → Provision for nomination of Anglo-Indian members in Lok Sabha by President.
☛ 104th Amendment (2020) → Ended Anglo-Indian reservation in Lok Sabha and state assemblies.
☛ Rajya Sabha → President nominates 12 members (art, literature, science, social service).
☛ Nominated members in Lok Sabha → Cannot become ministers but have voting rights.

q: The total number of members in Rajya Sabha can be ___________.
qs.e: Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament. According to Article 80 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250. Out of these, 238 members represent the states and union territories, while 12 members are nominated by the President for their expertise in fields like literature, art, science, and social service. Currently, the actual strength of Rajya Sabha is 245, but the constitutional provision allows up to 250. This house is permanent and cannot be dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years.
qs.kf:
☛ Maximum strength of Rajya Sabha → 250
☛ Current strength of Rajya Sabha → 245
☛ Number of nominated members → 12
☛ Constitutional provision for Rajya Sabha → Article 80
☛ Nature of Rajya Sabha → Permanent house

q: The provision of the joint sitting of the two houses of Parliament has been taken from which constitution?
qs.e: The provision of joint sitting of both houses of Parliament in the Indian Constitution is taken from the Australian Constitution. It aims to resolve a deadlock on a bill when there is disagreement between Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. The joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha, and members of both houses participate. This provision is mentioned in Article 108. So far, joint sittings have been held only three times: in 1961 on the Dowry Prohibition Bill, 1978 on the Banking Service Commission Bill, and 2002 on the Prevention of Terrorism Bill (POTA). This provision is inspired by the Australian Constitution, which also has a mechanism for joint sittings to resolve disagreements between the two houses.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article deals with joint sitting? → Article 108
☛ Who presides over the joint sitting? → Speaker of Lok Sabha
☛ How many joint sittings have been held so far? → Three
☛ What was the first joint sitting for? → Dowry Prohibition Bill, 1961
☛ From which constitution is the joint sitting provision borrowed? → Australian Constitution

q: Which is the supreme institution of law making in India?
qs.e: In India, the Parliament is the supreme law-making institution, consisting of the President, Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha. It has the authority to enact laws, amend the constitution, and discuss policies. According to Article 79 of the Constitution, the structure of Parliament is defined. It also controls the executive and passes the budget. Although the Supreme Court can review laws for constitutionality, the power to make laws rests solely with Parliament. The Prime Minister's Office is part of the executive, and the Election Commission handles election conduct, not legislation.
qs.kf:
☛ How many houses does the Indian Parliament have? → Two: Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
☛ Who is the supreme head of Parliament? → President
☛ What is the term of Lok Sabha? → 5 years
☛ What is the term of a Rajya Sabha member? → 6 years
☛ Who summons the Parliament session? → President

q: The Vice-President is a member of
o: neither Lok Sabha nor Rajya Sabha
qs.e: According to the Indian Constitution, the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha, but he is not a member of either Rajya Sabha or Lok Sabha. Article 64 states that the Vice-President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament. Although he presides over the proceedings of the Rajya Sabha, he does not have the right to vote except a casting vote in case of a tie. This provision ensures the impartiality of the office.
qs.kf:
☛ Which House of Parliament does the Vice-President belong to? → None
☛ What is the role of Vice-President in Rajya Sabha? → Ex-officio Chairman
☛ Does the Vice-President have voting rights in Rajya Sabha? → No, only casting vote
☛ Who elects the Vice-President? → Elected members of both Houses of Parliament
☛ What is the minimum age for Vice-President? → 35 years

q: Rajya Sabha is considered to be a Permanent House because
o: one-fourth of its members retire after every 3 years
qs.e: Rajya Sabha is called the Permanent House because it is never dissolved. Unlike Lok Sabha, which dissolves after 5 years or can be dissolved earlier, Rajya Sabha is a continuous chamber. One-third of its members retire every 2 years, allowing new members to enter, but the entire House is never dissolved. This permanence is important in the federal structure as it represents states and ensures continuity. Thus, it is known as the 'Permanent House'.
qs.kf:
☛ After how many years do one-third members of Rajya Sabha retire? → 2 years
☛ Which House is called the Permanent House? → Rajya Sabha
☛ What is the term of a Rajya Sabha member? → 6 years
☛ Who is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Vice President
☛ Who has the power to remove a member of Rajya Sabha? → President

q: Who among the following can preside over a joint sitting of the two Houses of the Indian Parliament?
o: Chief Minister of any one of the states
qs.e: According to Article 108 of the Indian Constitution, the joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides. The joint sitting is summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock over a bill that is passed by one House but rejected or amended by the other. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice President of India) cannot preside, as they are not a member of Rajya Sabha. Neither the Prime Minister nor a Chief Minister is authorized for this role. So far, three joint sittings have occurred: 1961 (Dowry Prohibition Bill), 1978 (MPs and Judicial Immunity), and 2002 (POTA).
qs.kf:
☛ Who presides over a joint sitting? → Speaker of Lok Sabha
☛ Who presides in the absence of the Speaker? → Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha
☛ Who summons the joint sitting? → The President
☛ Which article deals with joint sitting? → Article 108
☛ How many joint sittings have been held so far? → Three

q: The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for the period of
qs.e: Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament. The term of its members is six years. It is a permanent house, with one-third of its members retiring every two years. Members of Rajya Sabha are indirectly elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies. Article 83 of the Indian Constitution provides for the term of Rajya Sabha members. In contrast, Lok Sabha members have a term of five years. The six-year term ensures stability and continuity in the legislative process.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of Rajya Sabha member → 6 years
☛ How many members retire every 2 years in Rajya Sabha → 1/3 members
☛ Who elects Rajya Sabha members → Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
☛ Article related to Rajya Sabha → Article 80
☛ Article for term of Rajya Sabha members → Article 83

q: The lower house of the Indian Parliament is called
qs.e: The Indian Parliament is a bicameral legislature consisting of two houses - the Lok Sabha (lower house) and the Rajya Sabha (upper house). Members of Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people, while Rajya Sabha members are indirectly elected. According to the Constitution, the maximum strength of Lok Sabha is 552, with 530 members from states, 20 from union territories, and 2 nominated by the President. Lok Sabha has a term of 5 years, whereas Rajya Sabha is a permanent house. The presiding officer of Lok Sabha is called the Speaker. Money bills can only be introduced in Lok Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ Lower house of Indian Parliament → Lok Sabha
☛ Maximum strength of Lok Sabha → 552
☛ Term of Lok Sabha → 5 years
☛ Presiding officer of Lok Sabha → Speaker
☛ Where money bills are introduced → Lok Sabha

q: How many members of India's Lok Sabha were nominated by the president?
qs.e: Under the original provisions of the Indian Constitution, the President could nominate two members from the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha. This was provided under Article 331 to ensure representation for this minority community. However, the 104th Constitutional Amendment (2020) abolished this nomination system for both Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The amendment came into effect before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Thus, initially, the number of nominated members in Lok Sabha was two. Currently, there are no nominated members in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha still has 12 nominated members from fields like arts, literature, science, and social service.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 331 → Provision for nomination of 2 Anglo-Indian members to Lok Sabha
☛ 104th Constitutional Amendment → Ended Anglo-Indian reservation in Lok Sabha and state assemblies
☛ Nominated members in Rajya Sabha → 12 members nominated by President for expertise in various fields
☛ Anglo-Indian community → The only community in India that originally got representation via nomination
☛ Maximum strength of Lok Sabha → 552 (530 from states, 20 from UTs, 2 nominated)

q: When was the ﬁrst general election of the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: The first general election of the Lok Sabha in India was held in 1951-52. The election took place from 25 October 1951 to 21 February 1952. A total of 17.32 crore voters participated in this election. Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India, led the Indian National Congress to a landslide victory. Independent India's first general election was a historic event that laid the foundation of the democratic process. The voter turnout was about 45%. As a result of this election, the first Lok Sabha was constituted in 1952.
qs.kf:
☛ When was India's first general election held? → 1951-52
☛ How many voters participated in the first general election? → 17.32 crore
☛ Which party won the majority in the first general election? → Congress
☛ When was the first Lok Sabha formed? → 1952
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during the first general election? → Jawaharlal Nehru

q: What is the minimum age for becoming a member of the Rajya Sabha?
qs.e: As per Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the minimum age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years. This is different from the Lok Sabha, where the minimum age is 25 years. The Rajya Sabha being the upper house requires more maturity and experience. Additionally, the member must be a citizen of India and should not hold any office of profit under the government. This age limit was set by the framers of the Constitution to ensure that only experienced and serious individuals become part of the upper house.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum age for Rajya Sabha member → 30 years
☛ Minimum age for Lok Sabha member → 25 years
☛ Minimum age for President of India → 35 years
☛ Maximum strength of Rajya Sabha → 250
☛ Term of Rajya Sabha members → 6 years

q: Which committee is of semi-judicial nature?
qs.e: The Parliamentary Privileges Committee is of semi-judicial nature. It investigates breaches of members' privileges and recommends punishment, such as imprisonment or warning, when found guilty. Its proceedings resemble a judicial process, involving evidence and witnesses. Other committees like the Petition Committee, Ethics Committee, and Subordinate Legislative Committee perform administrative or legislative functions. The Privileges Committee has the power to summon and punish individuals for contempt, making it quasi-judicial.
qs.kf:
☛ Semi-judicial committee → Privileges Committee
☛ Chairperson of Privileges Committee → Lok Sabha Speaker (usually)
☛ Penalty for privilege breach → Warning or imprisonment
☛ Function of Petition Committee → Examine public petitions
☛ Function of Subordinate Legislation Committee → Review rules and orders

q: How much time can be banned by the Rajya Sabha on the money bill?
qs.e: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, not in the Rajya Sabha. The Rajya Sabha can delay a Money Bill for a maximum of 14 days. If the Rajya Sabha fails to return the bill with its recommendations within 14 days, the bill is deemed to have been passed by both houses. This provision is mentioned under Article 109 of the Indian Constitution. The Rajya Sabha has limited powers over Money Bills because they deal with taxation, expenditure, and public funds. This time limit ensures the supremacy of the Lok Sabha in financial matters.
qs.kf:
☛ Maximum delay period for Money Bill by Rajya Sabha → 14 days
☛ Constitutional article related to Money Bill procedure → 109
☛ House where Money Bill can be introduced → Only Lok Sabha
☛ Effect of Rajya Sabha's recommendation on Money Bill → Lok Sabha may accept or reject it
☛ Definition of Money Bill is given in which article → Article 110

q: The budget mentioned in the Constitution is called
qs.e: Under Article 112 of the Indian Constitution, the budget is termed as the 'Annual Financial Statement'. It is presented by the President before both Houses of Parliament. It contains details of estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year (April 1 to March 31). The budget must be passed by Parliament to authorize government spending. It reflects the government's financial planning and policy priorities.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 112 → Related to Annual Financial Statement
☛ Article 113 → Related to Appropriation Bill
☛ Article 114 → Related to Demands for Grants
☛ Article 115 → Related to Supplementary Grants
☛ Article 116 → Related to Vote on Account

q: Can the amendment of Money Bill be done by whom?
qs.e: A Money Bill is a special type of bill related to taxes, expenditure, loans, etc. According to Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and amendments can only be made by the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only delay it for up to 14 days. After that, the bill is deemed passed with the Lok Sabha's recommendations. The definition and procedure of Money Bills are clearly laid out in the Constitution, ensuring that the Lok Sabha retains control over financial matters.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article defines a Money Bill? → Article 110
☛ In which house is a Money Bill introduced? → Only Lok Sabha
☛ How long can the Rajya Sabha delay a Money Bill? → 14 days
☛ What is the power of the Rajya Sabha over a Money Bill? → Can only recommend
☛ Who decides whether to include Rajya Sabha's recommendations in a Money Bill? → Lok Sabha

q: Funds belonging to the Government of India are kept in-
qs.e: Funds belonging to the Government of India are kept in three main accounts: the Consolidated Fund of India, the Contingency Fund of India, and the Public Account of India. The Consolidated Fund receives all tax revenues, non-tax revenues, and loan receipts. The Contingency Fund is used for emergency expenditures, while the Public Account handles transactions like savings banks, provident funds, etc., that are not part of the government's own account. Together, they manage all government funds.
qs.kf:
☛ Consolidated Fund of India → Contains tax, non-tax revenue, and loan receipts
☛ Contingency Fund of India → Used for emergencies, corpus of ₹50 crore
☛ Public Account of India → Money can be withdrawn without Parliament approval
☛ Parliament approval → Required for withdrawal from Consolidated Fund
☛ Contingency Fund custodian → Finance Secretary, with President's prior approval

q: What should be the minimum age to get the Rajya Sabha membership?
qs.e: According to Article 84 of the Indian Constitution, the minimum age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years, while for the Lok Sabha it is 25 years. The Rajya Sabha being the upper house requires more experience and maturity, hence a higher age limit. Other conditions for Rajya Sabha membership include being a citizen of India and not holding any office of profit. The term of Rajya Sabha members is 6 years, with one-third of members retiring every two years. This age requirement ensures that members have sufficient life experience to contribute meaningfully to legislative debates and decision-making.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum age for Rajya Sabha membership → 30 years
☛ Minimum age for Lok Sabha membership → 25 years
☛ Term of Rajya Sabha members → 6 years
☛ Maximum strength of Rajya Sabha → 250
☛ Election of Rajya Sabha members → Indirect election (by state legislative assemblies)

q: Compensatory Afforestation Fund Bill was passed by Rajya Sabha of India in the year ________.
qs.e: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Bill was passed by the Indian Parliament in the year 2016. This bill establishes a fund for forest conservation and management, where compensatory amounts received for diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes are deposited. The objective is to promote afforestation, reforestation, and related activities. Both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha passed the bill, after which it received presidential assent. This legislation is considered crucial for forest rights and environmental sustainability.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of passing of Compensatory Afforestation Fund Bill → 2016
☛ Main objective of the bill → Management of forest conservation and afforestation fund
☛ Who introduced the bill → Union Environment Minister
☛ Use of fund under this bill → Afforestation and forest conservation
☛ When did the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act come into force → 2018

q: Which of the following is NOT a routine session of the Indian Parliament?
qs.e: The Indian Parliament has three routine sessions: Budget Session, Monsoon Session, and Winter Session. There is no official Summer Session. The Budget Session starts in January-February and continues till April, during which the Union Budget is presented. The Monsoon Session is held from July to August. The Winter Session is convened in November-December. Each session has designated days for government business, passing bills, and discussions. The term 'Summer Session' is not used in parliamentary calendar.
qs.kf:
☛ How many routine sessions does the Indian Parliament have? → Three
☛ When is the Budget Session held? → January-February to April
☛ Which months include the Monsoon Session? → July-August
☛ What is the timing of Winter Session? → November-December
☛ Which session is not a routine session? → Summer Session

q: What is the total number of members nominated by the President to the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
qs.e: According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the President can nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha. These members are persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields like literature, art, science, and social service. Additionally, under Article 331, the President can nominate 2 members from the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha if the community is not adequately represented. However, the 104th Constitutional Amendment (2020) abolished the reserved seats for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, but the President's power to nominate remains. Thus, the total nominated members are 12 (Rajya Sabha) + 2 (Lok Sabha) = 14.

q: Find out the odd in relation to the Indian Parliament.
A. Budget Session
B. Summer Session
C. Monsoon Session
D. Winter Session
qs.e: The Indian Parliament holds three sessions every year: Budget Session, Monsoon Session, and Winter Session. There is no separate official session called 'Summer Session'. Although the Budget Session is sometimes informally referred to as the Summer Session, it is not an official designation. The Budget Session is held in February-March, the Monsoon Session in July-September, and the Winter Session in November-December. Therefore, 'Summer Session' is the odd one out as it is not an officially recognized session of the Parliament.
qs.kf:
☛ Three official sessions of Parliament → Budget, Monsoon, Winter
☛ Budget Session duration → February to March
☛ Monsoon Session duration → July to September
☛ Winter Session duration → November to December
☛ Summer Session → Not an official session, only an informal name for Budget Session

q: Rajya Sabha is also known as
A. Legislative Council
B. Senior House
C. Upper House
D. Lower House
qs.e: Rajya Sabha is also known as the Upper House of the Indian Parliament. The Lok Sabha is called the Lower House. Rajya Sabha members are indirectly elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies. It is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved. A Legislative Council is the upper house at the state level, not at the national level. Rajya Sabha was constituted in 1952 and its members have a term of 6 years. The Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ What are the two houses of Indian Parliament? → Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
☛ What is the term of Rajya Sabha members? → 6 years
☛ How are Rajya Sabha members elected? → By elected members of state legislative assemblies
☛ Who is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Vice President
☛ What is the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha? → 250 (currently 245)

q: Who is the current supreme commander of Indian Defense forces?
A. Narendra Modi
B. Sumitra Mahajan C.Ram Nath Kovind D. Lt. Gen Dalbir Singh
qs.e: According to Article 53(1) of the Indian Constitution, the President is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Defense Forces. The current President is Ram Nath Kovind, who assumed office on 25 July 2017. The defense forces include the Army, Navy, and Air Force. The President's military powers include declaring war, making treaties, and appointing the Chiefs of Staff. The Prime Minister and Defense Minister play roles in implementing defense policies, but the supreme command rests with the President. Option A (Narendra Modi) is the Prime Minister, Option B (Sumitra Mahajan) was the Lok Sabha Speaker, and Option D (Lt. Gen Dalbir Singh) was the Army Chief, but none are the Supreme Commander.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the Supreme Commander of Indian Defense Forces? → President
☛ Under which Article does the President have defense powers? → Article 53
☛ Who is the current President of India? → Ram Nath Kovind
☛ Who is the Chief of the Indian Army? → General Manoj Mukund Naravane
☛ Who is the Chief of the Indian Navy? → Admiral Karambir Singh

q: The annual financial statement prepared under article 112 of the Indian Constitution is called ______ A. Public account
B. Consolidated account C. Budget D. Revenue account
qs.e: Article 112 of the Indian Constitution states that the President shall cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for each financial year, known as the 'annual financial statement', commonly called the Budget. The budget has two parts: Revenue Budget and Capital Budget. The Revenue Budget includes revenue receipts and revenue expenditure, while the Capital Budget includes capital receipts and capital expenditure. The annual financial statement must be passed by Parliament before the government can implement it. It is a key tool of the government's fiscal policy.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 112 → Deals with annual financial statement (Budget)
☛ Article 113 → Deals with appropriation bills in Parliament
☛ Article 114 → Deals with provisions of appropriation bills
☛ Parts of Budget → Revenue Budget and Capital Budget
☛ The term 'Budget' in Constitution → Not mentioned; only 'annual financial statement' is used

q: In the Parliament of India, who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha?
A. M.A Ayyangar
B. Ganesh Mavalankar
C. Sardar Hukam Singh
D. Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy
qs.e: Ganesh Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha in the Indian Parliament. He served from 15 May 1952 to 27 February 1956. He was popularly known as 'Dada' and was a freedom fighter and politician from Gujarat. The Lok Sabha was constituted for the first time after the general elections held in 1952. M.A. Ayyangar became the second Speaker, while Sardar Hukam Singh and Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy served as Speakers later.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Speaker of Lok Sabha? → Ganesh Mavalankar
☛ What was Ganesh Mavalankar's tenure? → 1952-1956
☛ Who was the second Speaker of Lok Sabha? → M.A. Ayyangar
☛ By what name was Ganesh Mavalankar known? → Dada
☛ In which year was Lok Sabha constituted? → 1952

q: The GST Bill introduced in parliament in 2015 is
A. A financial bill.
B. Not a money bill.
C. A constitutional amendment bill.
D. An ordinary bill.
qs.e: The GST Bill introduced in Parliament in 2015 was a Constitutional Amendment Bill because it required amendments to Article 246A and other provisions of the Constitution. It was passed as the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act. The bill was brought to implement the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India. It was neither a money bill, nor a financial bill, nor an ordinary bill. GST is an indirect tax that subsumes various taxes levied by central and state governments. After the constitutional amendment, the GST Council was formed.
qs.kf:
☛ When was GST implemented? → 1 July 2017
☛ What type of tax is GST? → Indirect tax
☛ Who is the Chairman of GST Council? → Union Finance Minister
☛ How many tax slabs are there under GST? → 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%
☛ First country to implement GST? → France

q: Who was the Speaker of 16th Lok Sabha?
qs.e: The Speaker of the 16th Lok Sabha (2014-2019) was Sumitra Mahajan, a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party. She was the second woman to hold the office of Lok Sabha Speaker. During her tenure, the Prime Minister was Narendra Modi. She represented the Indore parliamentary constituency of Madhya Pradesh. Several key legislations were passed during her speakership.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the Speaker of 17th Lok Sabha? → Om Birla
☛ Who was the first woman Speaker of Lok Sabha? → Meira Kumar
☛ From which state was Sumitra Mahajan an MP? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ What was the tenure of 16th Lok Sabha? → 2014 to 2019
☛ Which party did Sumitra Mahajan belong to? → Bharatiya Janata Party

q: In India, all the bills introduced and passed by both the houses (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha) can come into force only after they receive the assent of:
qs.e: According to Article 111 of the Indian Constitution, any bill passed by both Houses of Parliament cannot become law without the President's assent. The President has three options: he may give assent, withhold assent (pocket veto), or return the bill for reconsideration (except for Money Bills). This process ensures a separation of powers between the executive and legislature. Only after the President's assent does the bill become an Act and come into force in the country.
qs.kf:
☛ President's power on Money Bill → Can neither withhold nor return; only give or refuse assent.
☛ When can the President use pocket veto? → By not taking any decision on the bill indefinitely.
☛ Article 111 → Relates to President's assent to bills.
☛ Article 200 → Governor's assent to state bills.
☛ Role of Supreme Court → To review the constitutionality of a bill.

q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Indian Parliament?
qs.e: The Indian Parliament consists of three parts: the President, the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha. According to Article 79 of the Constitution, the Parliament is composed of these three entities. State Legislative Assemblies are part of the state-level legislature, not the central Parliament. State Legislative Assemblies make laws for their respective states, while Parliament makes laws for the entire country. Hence, State Legislative Assemblies are not a part of the Indian Parliament.
qs.kf:
☛ Which are the parts of the Indian Parliament? → President, Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha
☛ Which Article describes the Parliament? → Article 79
☛ Under which Article are State Legislative Assemblies constituted? → Article 170
☛ How are Lok Sabha members elected? → Direct election by adult suffrage
☛ Who elects Rajya Sabha members? → Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies

q: Into how many constituencies was India divided for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections?
qs.e: India was divided into 543 constituencies for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. This number is determined under Article 81 of the Indian Constitution, which provides for a maximum of 550 members in the Lok Sabha, with 530 from states and 20 from union territories. In 2019, elections were held for all 543 seats, while 2 seats (Anglo-Indian) are nominated. This division is based on population by the Delimitation Commission. In the 2019 elections, voting took place for a total of 543 seats, with the Bharatiya Janata Party winning 303 seats.
qs.kf:
☛ Total seats in current Lok Sabha → 543 (elected) + 2 (nominated) = 545
☛ Distribution of Lok Sabha seats in states → Uttar Pradesh has the highest 80 seats
☛ Formation of Delimitation Commission → Under the Delimitation Act, 2002
☛ Seats in first Lok Sabha (1952) → 489
☛ State with fewest seats → Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim (1 each)

q: The First elected Parliament of independent India came into existence in -
qs.e: The first elected Parliament of independent India came into existence in 1952. India's first general election was held in 1951-52, with about 173 million voters participating. After the election, the first Lok Sabha was formed in April 1952. This Parliament's term lasted from 1952 to 1957. This election is considered the foundation of Indian democracy because it implemented universal adult suffrage. The first Lok Sabha had a total of 489 seats. Its first session began on 13 May 1952. India became independent in 1947, but the Constitution came into effect only in 1950, so the first elected Parliament was formed in 1952.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first Lok Sabha formed? → 1952
☛ When was the first general election held? → 1951-52
☛ How many seats were in the first Lok Sabha? → 489
☛ What was the term of the first Lok Sabha? → 1952-1957
☛ When did the first session of the first Lok Sabha begin? → 13 May 1952

q: Who enjoys the power to summon, prorogue either house of Indian Parliament?
qs.e: According to Article 85 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to summon, prorogue either house of Parliament, and dissolve the Lok Sabha. The President determines the time and place of parliamentary sessions. Prorogation means ending a session, while dissolution means ending the term of the Lok Sabha before its scheduled expiration. The President exercises this power on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. The President is responsible for convening parliamentary sessions, and there must not be a gap of more than six months between two sessions. This power gives the President control over the functioning of Parliament.
qs.kf:
☛ Who has the power to summon Parliament sessions? → The President
☛ What is prorogation? → Ending a session
☛ Who can dissolve the Lok Sabha? → The President
☛ What is the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament? → Six months
☛ Which Article deals with sessions, prorogation, and dissolution? → Article 85

q: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by:
o: all the members of Lok Sabha
members of majority party in Lok Sabha
qs.e: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by all the members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves. This election is conducted by simple majority. According to Article 93 of the Constitution, the Lok Sabha elects a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker. The Speaker is not appointed by the President. The Speaker presides over the proceedings of the Lok Sabha and maintains discipline. A resolution to remove the Speaker can only be passed by the Lok Sabha itself.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article is the Speaker of Lok Sabha elected? → Article 93
☛ What is the tenure of the Speaker? → Until the dissolution of Lok Sabha
☛ By what majority is the Speaker removed? → Simple majority
☛ Who determines the salary of the Speaker? → Parliament
☛ Who appoints the Pro-tem Speaker? → President

q: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: The first Speaker of the Lok Sabha was G. V. Mavalankar. He served from 1952 to 1956. Mavalankar was a freedom fighter and a prominent politician from Gujarat. He also served as a member of the Constituent Assembly. The position of Lok Sabha Speaker is the highest office in the lower house of the Indian Parliament. Mavalankar played a vital role in managing parliamentary procedures. He was succeeded by Hukum Singh as the second Speaker. Note that the first Lok Sabha Speaker was Mavalankar, while Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India. Purushottam Tandon served as the President of the Indian National Congress.
qs.kf:
☛ First Speaker of Lok Sabha → G. V. Mavalankar
☛ First Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha → M. A. Ayyangar
☛ Chairman of Constituent Assembly → Rajendra Prasad
☛ First Prime Minister of India → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Formation of Lok Sabha → 17 April 1952

q: Which of the following states has more than one seat in the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: The Lok Sabha, the lower house of the Indian Parliament, allocates seats to states based on their population. Nagaland has 1 seat, Sikkim has 1 seat, Mizoram has 1 seat, while Meghalaya has 2 seats. The two Lok Sabha constituencies in Meghalaya are Shillong and Tura. This difference arises due to Meghalaya's relatively higher population compared to the other states listed. Therefore, among the given options, only Meghalaya has more than one seat in the Lok Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of Lok Sabha seats in Meghalaya → 2
☛ Number of Lok Sabha seats in Nagaland → 1
☛ Number of Lok Sabha seats in Sikkim → 1
☛ Number of Lok Sabha seats in Mizoram → 1
☛ Total Lok Sabha seats in India (including SC/ST reservations) → 543

q: With reference to the Rajya Sabha, which of the following statement is correct?
o: It is a directly elected body like Lok Sabha.
The term of Rajya Sabha is six years.
Rajya Sabha is the lower house of parliament.
The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved.
qs.e: The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of Parliament and is a permanent house, meaning it is never dissolved. One-third of its members retire every two years. The term of a Rajya Sabha member is six years, but this does not refer to the term of the house. The Rajya Sabha is indirectly elected, unlike the Lok Sabha which is directly elected. The Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved like the Lok Sabha; it continues indefinitely. According to Article 83, dissolution of the Rajya Sabha is not possible.
qs.kf:
☛ How many members of Rajya Sabha are nominated by the President? → 12
☛ What is the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha? → 250
☛ Who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Vice President
☛ On what basis are states represented in Rajya Sabha? → Population
☛ Where can a Money Bill be introduced? → Only in Lok Sabha

q: What is the total strength of elected members in the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's Parliament. According to the Constitution, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552, comprising 530 members elected from states, 20 from union territories, and 2 nominated by the President from the Anglo-Indian community. However, the nomination for Anglo-Indians has been abolished. Thus, the current total strength of elected members is 543. This is determined under Article 81 of the Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ Maximum strength of Lok Sabha → 552
☛ Elected members from states → 530
☛ Elected members from union territories → 20
☛ Current elected members (after Anglo-Indian abolition) → 543
☛ Article providing for Lok Sabha composition → Article 81

q: Which Act of the British Parliament provided for responsible government in the provinces?
qs.e: The Government of India Act 1935, passed by the British Parliament, introduced responsible government in the provinces. It granted provincial autonomy, making the council of ministers responsible to the provincial legislature. This act abolished diarchy in the provinces and established a parliamentary form of government. While the governor retained certain discretionary powers, day-to-day administration was placed in the hands of elected representatives. The Act of 1935 was a landmark in the development of India's constitution and served as a blueprint for the future Constitution of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which act provided for provincial autonomy in India? → Government of India Act 1935
☛ Under Act of 1935, who was responsible to the provincial legislature? → Council of Ministers
☛ Which system was abolished by the Act of 1935? → Diarchy
☛ Under Act of 1935, what special powers did the governor have? → Discretionary powers
☛ Act of 1935 was based on the recommendations of which commission? → Simon Commission

q: Which of the following Article of the Indian constitution defines the Money bill?
qs.e: Article 110 of the Indian Constitution defines a Money Bill. A Money Bill contains provisions related to the imposition, abolition, alteration, or regulation of taxes; borrowing of money; custody of the Consolidated Fund; appropriation of money; or expenditure from the Consolidated Fund. It can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and requires prior recommendation of the President. The Rajya Sabha cannot amend it, only recommend changes within 14 days, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject. Article 109 deals with the special procedure for Money Bills in Parliament, while Article 115 and 113 pertain to supplementary grants and the annual financial statement, respectively.
qs.kf:
☛ Article defining Money Bill → Article 110
☛ Power of Rajya Sabha over Money Bill → Only recommend, 14 days
☛ Where Money Bill is introduced → Lok Sabha
☛ Prior approval required for Money Bill → President
☛ Difference between Money Bill and Finance Bill → Article 110 and 117

q: Which article of the Indian Constitution empowers joint sitting of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha under certain circumstances?
qs.e: Article 108 of the Indian Constitution provides for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). It is convened by the President when a Bill passed by one House is rejected by the other House, or when the Houses disagree on amendments, or when more than six months elapse without the Bill being passed by the other House. In a joint sitting, members of both Houses deliberate together and decide by majority vote. Importantly, Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills are exempted from this provision. So far, joint sittings have been held only three times (in 1961, 1978 and 2002).
qs.kf:
☛ Who presides over a joint sitting? → Speaker of Lok Sabha
☛ Which Bills cannot be referred to joint sitting? → Money Bill and Constitution Amendment Bill
☛ Who can summon a joint sitting? → President
☛ How many joint sittings have been held so far? → Three (1961, 1978, 2002)
☛ Which Article provides for joint sitting? → Article 108

q: Which of the following Articles of the constitution refers to the Union Budget as the Annual Financial Statement?
qs.e: Article 112 of the Indian Constitution refers to the Union Budget as the 'Annual Financial Statement'. It is part of Part V (The Union). According to this article, the President causes to be laid before both Houses of Parliament a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for each financial year. This statement is called the Annual Financial Statement. Article 113 deals with voting on the budget and the Appropriation Bill, while Articles 101 and 102 relate to membership and disqualification of members of Parliament. Thus, the correct constitutional provision for the budget being called the Annual Financial Statement is Article 112.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article mentions Annual Financial Statement? → Article 112
☛ Which article deals with voting on budget? → Article 113
☛ Disqualification of MPs is under which article? → Article 102
☛ Qualification for membership of Parliament? → Article 101
☛ Article 112 is in which part? → Part V

q: The first Lokpal Bill was introduced in the Indian Parliament in:
qs.e: The concept of Lokpal in India was first recommended by the Administrative Reforms Commission in 1966. Subsequently, the first Lokpal Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in 1968 but failed to pass. Several attempts were made later, leading to the enactment of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. The Lokpal is an anti-corruption body that investigates allegations of corruption against public functionaries. The first bill was introduced during the tenure of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. The bill aimed to establish an independent authority to probe corruption.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Administrative Reforms Commission recommend Lokpal? → 1966
☛ When was the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act passed? → 2013
☛ Who appoints the chairperson of Lokpal? → President of India
☛ How many members are there in Lokpal? → 9 (including chairperson)
☛ Which committee first recommended Lokpal? → Santhanam Committee (1964)

q: Who among the following represents the full authority of the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: The Speaker represents the full authority of the Lok Sabha. According to the Constitution, the Speaker is the chief officer of the House and presides over its proceedings. The Speaker acts as the guardian of the dignity and independence of the House. The President, Vice President, and Prime Minister do not represent the full authority of the Lok Sabha. The President is the head of state, the Vice President is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha, and the Prime Minister is the head of the executive. The Speaker manages the membership, proceedings, and discipline of the House.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of Lok Sabha Speaker → Until dissolution of the House or as long as he holds office
☛ Who appoints Lok Sabha Speaker → Members of Lok Sabha elect among themselves
☛ Resolution to remove Lok Sabha Speaker → Must be passed by majority of members of Lok Sabha
☛ Vote of Lok Sabha Speaker → Casts a deciding vote in case of a tie
☛ Oath of Lok Sabha Speaker → Administered by the President

q: The first general election of Lok Sabha was held in the year:
qs.e: The first general election in India was held in 1951-52 for the 489 seats of the Lok Sabha. This election was conducted under the supervision of India's first Election Commission, headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sukumar Sen. A total of 17,32,12,000 voters participated. The election was held in multiple phases from October 1951 to February 1952. The Indian National Congress won 364 seats and formed the government, with Jawaharlal Nehru becoming the Prime Minister. This was the largest democratic election in the world at that time.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the Chief Election Commissioner of the first Lok Sabha election? → Sukumar Sen
☛ How many seats did Congress win in the first Lok Sabha election? → 364
☛ How many voters were there in the first Lok Sabha election? → 17.32 crore
☛ How many seats were there in the first Lok Sabha? → 489
☛ Who became the Prime Minister after the first general election? → Jawaharlal Nehru

q: Members of Rajya Sabha are elected for the duration of:
qs.e: Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament, and its members are elected for a term of 6 years. It is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every 2 years. Members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies using the system of proportional representation. The President nominates 12 members who have special knowledge in fields like art, literature, science, and social service. The minimum age for membership in Rajya Sabha is 30 years.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of Rajya Sabha members → 6 years
☛ Who elects Rajya Sabha members → Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
☛ Number of nominated members in Rajya Sabha → 12
☛ Minimum age for Rajya Sabha membership → 30 years
☛ How many Rajya Sabha members retire every 2 years → One-third

q: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha is:
qs.e: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha is the Speaker of Lok Sabha, who is the chief authority of the house. The Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha and conducts the proceedings of the house. The Speaker grants permission to speak, conducts voting, and maintains the dignity of the house. This position is provisioned under Article 93 of the Indian Constitution. In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker presides.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of Lok Sabha Speaker → Until dissolution of the house or until he remains in office
☛ Who elects the Lok Sabha Speaker → Members of Lok Sabha
☛ Constitutional provision for Lok Sabha Speaker → Article 93
☛ Power of Lok Sabha Speaker → To conduct proceedings of the house
☛ Who presides in absence of Lok Sabha Speaker → Deputy Speaker

q: Which House of the Indian Parliament is elected by the people directly?
qs.e: The Indian Parliament has two Houses - the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. Members of Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people, while Rajya Sabha members are indirectly elected. Lok Sabha is also called the Lower House or the First House. Its maximum strength is 552, with 530 members from states, 20 from union territories, and 2 nominated by the President. The term of Lok Sabha is 5 years.
qs.kf:
☛ By which system are Lok Sabha members elected? → Direct election system
☛ What is the maximum strength of Lok Sabha? → 552
☛ What is the term of Rajya Sabha members? → 6 years
☛ What is the term of Lok Sabha? → 5 years
☛ By whom are Rajya Sabha members elected? → State legislative assemblies

q: The Constitution of India refers to the budget as _____.
qs.e: According to Article 112 of the Constitution of India, the budget is referred to as the Annual Financial Statement. This document presents the estimated receipts and expenditures of the government for each financial year. It includes components like revenue receipts, capital receipts, revenue expenditure, and capital expenditure. The Annual Financial Statement is presented by the Finance Minister in Parliament and is the key document outlining the government's fiscal policy. Article 112 explicitly states that the President shall cause to be laid before Parliament the Annual Financial Statement for every financial year. This statement forms the basis of the government's financial management and is essential for understanding the allocation of resources.
qs.kf:
☛ Article related to Annual Financial Statement → Article 112
☛ When is Annual Financial Statement presented → Every financial year
☛ Main components of Annual Financial Statement → Revenue receipts and expenditure
☛ Who presents the Annual Financial Statement → Finance Minister
☛ Alternative name for Annual Financial Statement → Budget

q: Who was the chairperson of the first Parliament of Independent India as a legislative body?
qs.e: The first Parliament of Independent India, known as the First Lok Sabha, was constituted in 1952. Its Speaker (Chairperson) was Ganesh Vasudev Mavlankar, commonly known as G.V. Mavlankar. He served as the Speaker from 1952 to 1956. Mavlankar also served as the Vice-President of the Constituent Assembly and played a key role in establishing parliamentary procedures. Sardar Patel was the Home Minister, Mahatma Gandhi had passed away in 1948, and H.C. Mukherjee was the Vice-President. Hence, the correct answer is G.V. Mavlankar.
qs.kf:
☛ First Speaker of Lok Sabha → G.V. Mavlankar
☛ First Lok Sabha formed → 1952
☛ Vice-President of Constituent Assembly → G.V. Mavlankar
☛ First Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha → M.A. Ayyangar
☛ First Lok Sabha tenure → 1952-1957

q: In which year did the Indian Parliament adopt the industrial policy resolution?
qs.e: The Indian Parliament adopted the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956), often called the economic constitution of India. This policy aimed at establishing a socialist pattern of society and classified industries into three categories: Schedule A (exclusive state monopoly), Schedule B (state and private sector partnership), and Schedule C (private sector). It introduced the license raj and promoted import substitution. The IPR 1956 was linked to the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) and remained effective until the economic reforms of 1991.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the main objective of IPR 1956? → To establish a socialist pattern of society
☛ How many categories of industries were created under IPR 1956? → Three (A, B, C)
☛ Which Five-Year Plan was associated with IPR 1956? → Second Five-Year Plan
☛ What is IPR 1956 also known as? → Economic constitution of India
☛ Until which year was IPR 1956 in effect? → 1991

q: What is the maximum duration limit within which the Rajya Sabha can pass the Money Bill?
qs.e: According to Article 109 of the Indian Constitution, after a Money Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha and transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, the Rajya Sabha must return the bill within 14 days. If the Rajya Sabha fails to pass the bill within 14 days, or passes it with amendments, the bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses. This provision ensures the supremacy of the Lok Sabha in financial matters. A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations, not amendments. The 14-day limit restricts the Rajya Sabha's powers to prevent delays in financial legislation.
qs.kf:
☛ Who can introduce a Money Bill in the Lok Sabha? → Only a Minister
☛ What can Rajya Sabha do with a Money Bill? → Recommend, not amend
☛ Which Article deals with the special procedure for Money Bills? → Article 109
☛ What if Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill in 14 days? → Bill is deemed passed
☛ Money Bill requires prior recommendation of whom? → President

q: Which of the following determines whether a bill is a money bill or not?
qs.e: According to Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, the Speaker of Lok Sabha determines whether a bill is a money bill or not. A money bill deals with matters such as taxation, borrowing of money, or expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India. The Speaker's decision on this matter is final and cannot be challenged in any court of law or in Parliament. Money bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations on them, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject. This provision ensures financial control in the legislative process.
qs.kf:
☛ Article defining money bill → Article 110
☛ Speaker's decision on money bill → Final and binding
☛ House where money bill is introduced → Only Lok Sabha
☛ Role of Rajya Sabha on money bill → Only recommendations
☛ Time limit for Rajya Sabha on money bill → 14 days

q: The maximum number of members in the Rajya Sabha is-
qs.e: Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament. According to Article 80 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250 members. Out of these, 238 members represent the states and union territories, while 12 members are nominated by the President. These nominated members are individuals having special knowledge or practical experience in fields like literature, science, art, and social service. Currently, the total membership of Rajya Sabha is 245, comprising 233 elected and 12 nominated members. The term of office of a Rajya Sabha member is 6 years, and one-third of the members retire every two years. It is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved.
qs.kf:
☛ Maximum strength of Rajya Sabha → 250
☛ Number of elected members in Rajya Sabha → 238
☛ Number of nominated members in Rajya Sabha → 12
☛ Term of office of Rajya Sabha members → 6 years
☛ After how many years do one-third of Rajya Sabha members retire → 2 years

q: Which term is used for ending the session of Parliament for an indefinite period?
qs.e: Ending a session of Parliament for an indefinite period is called Adjournment sine die. This means the session is adjourned without fixing a date for reassembly. When proceedings are suspended for a specific period, it is called Adjournment. Prorogation is another process of ending a session, done by the President. Summoning is the process of starting a session.
qs.kf:
☛ Adjournment sine die → Termination of session for indefinite period
☛ Adjournment → Suspension for a specified period
☛ Prorogation → End of session by President
☛ Summoning → Calling a session
☛ Power to adjourn sine die → Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman)

q: Members of the Rajya Sabha are:
qs.e: Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament. Its members are indirectly elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of states and union territories. The election is conducted using the single transferable vote system of proportional representation. Rajya Sabha is a permanent house, with one-third of its members retiring every two years. Article 80 of the Indian Constitution provides for the composition of Rajya Sabha. The maximum strength of Rajya Sabha is 250, of which 238 members represent states and union territories, and 12 members are nominated by the President. The minimum age for membership in Rajya Sabha is 30 years.
qs.kf:
☛ Who elects the members of Rajya Sabha? → Members of State Legislative Assemblies
☛ What is the minimum age for Rajya Sabha membership? → 30 years
☛ What is the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha? → 250
☛ How many members are nominated to Rajya Sabha by the President? → 12
☛ What type of house is Rajya Sabha? → Permanent house

q: According to the Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956 passed by the Indian Parliament, into how many sections have industries been divided?
qs.e: The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956 was the foundation of India's industrial development strategy. It classified industries into three categories: Schedule A included industries exclusively under state control (like railways, defense, atomic energy); Schedule B comprised mixed sector industries where the state could gradually involve private sector; and Schedule C included the remaining industries open to private sector. This policy guided India's industrial framework from 1956 to 1991 and reinforced the socialist structure. The classification aimed to ensure the state's role in economic development and reduce regional disparities. The IPR 1956 was a key step in implementing the Mahalanobis model of heavy industrialization and laid the groundwork for the public sector's dominance in core industries.
qs.kf:
☛ How many categories were there in IPR 1956? → Three
☛ Schedule A industries were under? → Complete state control
☛ Schedule B industries belonged to? → Mixed sector
☛ Schedule C industries were open to? → Private sector
☛ IPR 1956 was in effect until? → 1991

q: The Lok Sabha and assembly elections of each state are per __________ year.
qs.e: According to the Constitution of India, the term of the Lok Sabha and each state legislative assembly is five years. This provision is mentioned in Article 83 for the Lok Sabha and Article 172 for the state assemblies. After the completion of five years, the Election Commission conducts fresh elections. However, the President (for Lok Sabha) or Governor (for state assembly) can extend this period during an emergency, but normally it remains five years. This system ensures democratic representation and accountability.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the term of the Lok Sabha? → Five years
☛ Under which article is the term of the state assembly given? → Article 172
☛ Who has the power to extend the term of the Lok Sabha? → President
☛ During an emergency, the Lok Sabha term can be extended for how long? → One year
☛ Which article deals with the term of the state legislative assembly? → Article 172

q: Who chairs the joint sitting of both the houses of the house?
qs.e: As per Article 108 of the Indian Constitution, the Speaker of Lok Sabha chairs the joint sitting of both houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Such a sitting is convened when a bill passed by one house is pending in the other house for more than six months, or the other house rejects it or proposes amendments. The President summons the joint sitting. If the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha presides. Decisions in a joint sitting are taken by a simple majority of the total members present. So far, three joint sittings have been held in India: the Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), the POTA Bill (1978), and the Women's Reservation Bill (2008).
qs.kf:
☛ Who has the power to summon a joint sitting? → President
☛ Who chairs the joint sitting? → Speaker of Lok Sabha
☛ When does the Deputy Speaker chair the joint sitting? → In absence of Speaker
☛ Which Article deals with joint sitting? → Article 108
☛ How many joint sittings have been held so far? → Three

q: According to the Indian Constitution, the maximum number of members of Rajya Sabha has been fixed______.
qs.e: According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum number of members of Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250. Out of these, 238 members represent states and union territories, elected indirectly, and 12 members are nominated by the President. These nominated members have special knowledge in fields like literature, science, art, and social service. Currently, the strength of Rajya Sabha is 245, as 5 seats out of 250 are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved, but one-third of its members retire every two years. This structure ensures continuity in the legislative process, with members serving a six-year term. The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the maximum membership of Rajya Sabha? → 250
☛ How many members are nominated by the President in Rajya Sabha? → 12
☛ Under which Article is Rajya Sabha membership determined? → Article 80
☛ How many members represent states and union territories in Rajya Sabha? → 238
☛ How many Rajya Sabha members retire every two years? → One-third

q: What is the "minimum number of required members in the House before editing any work" called?
qs.e: Quorum is the minimum number of members required to be present in a house or meeting before any business can be transacted. According to Article 100 of the Indian Constitution, at least one-tenth of the total membership must be present in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha to constitute a quorum. If the quorum is not met, the presiding officer can adjourn the house. The term 'quorum' is derived from Latin, meaning 'of whom'. It is a crucial aspect of legislative procedure ensuring adequate representation for decision-making. Decisions made in the absence of a quorum are considered invalid. Quorum guarantees that no law or resolution is passed without sufficient participation of members.
qs.kf:
☛ What is quorum? → Minimum number of members required for proceedings in a house
☛ Which Article of Indian Constitution deals with quorum? → Article 100
☛ How many members are needed for quorum in Lok Sabha? → One-tenth of total members (i.e., 55 members)
☛ Who can adjourn the house if quorum is not present? → Presiding officer (Speaker or Chairman)
☛ From which language is the term 'quorum' derived? → Latin

q: Who was the first president of the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar was elected as the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha in independent India's first Lok Sabha (1952-1957). He was a prominent freedom fighter and a member of the Constituent Assembly. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the proceedings of the house and is considered the highest authority in the chamber. Mavalankar played a key role in establishing parliamentary traditions. He is often called the 'Father of the Lok Sabha'. The second Speaker was M.A. Ayyangar. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy became Speaker later in 1977. Hukum Singh was the third Speaker. Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India.
qs.kf:
☛ First Speaker of Lok Sabha → Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar
☛ First Lok Sabha tenure → 1952-1957
☛ Second Speaker of Lok Sabha → M.A. Ayyangar
☛ First Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha → M.A. Ayyangar
☛ Election of Lok Sabha Speaker → Elected by the house from among its members

q: Which of the following article is related to the 'structure of the state council' in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: Article 80 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). It specifies that the Rajya Sabha shall consist of a maximum of 250 members, of which 12 are nominated by the President and the rest are representatives of states and union territories. The members are elected indirectly by the elected members of state legislative assemblies using the single transferable vote system. This article outlines the structure and formation of the upper house of the Indian Parliament. Article 60 deals with the oath of the President, Article 70 deals with the election of the President, and Article 3 deals with the reorganization of states.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha? → 250
☛ How many members are nominated to Rajya Sabha by the President? → 12
☛ Which electoral system is used for Rajya Sabha elections? → Single transferable vote
☛ What is the term of office for a Rajya Sabha member? → 6 years
☛ Who is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Vice President

q: The presence of _________ members is necessary for the meeting of the Lok Sabha in Parliament.
qs.e: According to the Indian Constitution, a quorum is required for the meeting of the Lok Sabha. Under Article 100(3), at least one-tenth of the total membership of the House must be present. The maximum strength of Lok Sabha is 550, so one-tenth is 55 members. If the quorum is not met during a session, the Speaker or Chairperson may adjourn the meeting. This rule ensures the validity of parliamentary proceedings and democratic participation. The requirement of 55 members is crucial for maintaining the legitimacy of legislative decisions in the Lok Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ Quorum for Lok Sabha → One-tenth of total members (55 members)
☛ Constitutional Article → Article 100(3) deals with quorum
☛ Quorum for Rajya Sabha → One-tenth of total members (current strength 245)
☛ Quorum decision → Taken by Speaker or Chairperson
☛ Quorum in State Assembly → One-tenth of total members (varies by state)

q: Who has the power to summon and prorogue any house of the Indian Parliament?
qs.e: According to Article 85 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to summon and prorogue both houses of Parliament. The President summons each house of Parliament from time to time and may prorogue them at his will. Additionally, the President also has the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha. This power is vested in the President as the head of the executive, but it is exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The sessions of Parliament begin and end only by the President's order.
qs.kf:
☛ Who summons Parliament → President (Article 85)
☛ Who prorogues Parliament → President
☛ Who dissolves Lok Sabha → President
☛ Maximum gap between sessions → 6 months (Article 85)
☛ President's address → First session of Parliament (Article 87)

q: The first Rajya Sabha (Council of States) of the Parliament was formed for the first time in the year _____.
qs.e: Under the Indian Constitution, the Parliament was formed on 26 January 1950, but the first Rajya Sabha was constituted on 3 April 1952.
