☛ What does a Point of order relate to? → Rules or procedure of the House
☛ What is the purpose of a Point of order? → To control the government and ensure rule compliance
☛ Who can raise a Point of order? → Any member of the House
☛ When can a Point of order be raised? → Immediately, without prior notice
☛ Who decides on a Point of order? → The Speaker

q: In what year was the Election Commission of India established?
qs.e: The Election Commission of India was established on January 25, 1950, a day before the Constitution came into effect. It is an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting and regulating elections in India. It derives its powers from Article 324 of the Constitution. The first Chief Election Commissioner was Sukumar Sen. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. The first general elections were held in 1952. The commission ensures free and fair elections.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of formation of Election Commission of India → 25 January 1950
☛ Constitutional Article related to Election Commission → Article 324
☛ First Chief Election Commissioner → Sukumar Sen
☛ Year of first general elections → 1952
☛ Headquarters of Election Commission → New Delhi

q: When was the first National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) constituted?
qs.e: The first National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) was constituted in March 2004. It was established under Article 338A of the Constitution. The main objective of this commission is to protect the rights and welfare of Scheduled Tribes. The commission was formed through the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. Earlier, there was a joint commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, which was later separated. The first chairman was Kunwar Singh. NCST has the authority to investigate matters related to Scheduled Tribes and make recommendations.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article is NCST established? → Article 338A
☛ Which constitutional amendment formed NCST? → 89th Amendment Act, 2003
☛ Who was the first chairman of NCST? → Kunwar Singh
☛ What is the full form of NCST? → National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
☛ When was NCST constituted? → March 2004

q: What is the full form of 'NITI' with respect to 'NITI Aayog'?
qs.e: The full form of NITI with respect to NITI Aayog is 'National Institution for Transforming India'. NITI Aayog was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission. It serves as a policy think tank of the Government of India, promoting cooperative federalism and sustainable development. The first Chairperson was Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and the first Vice-Chairperson was Arvind Panagariya. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. The acronym NITI stands for 'National Institution for Transforming India', reflecting its role in driving economic and social transformation.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog? → Arvind Panagariya
☛ Where is NITI Aayog headquartered? → New Delhi
☛ When was NITI Aayog established? → 1 January 2015
☛ What is the full form of NITI Aayog? → National Institution for Transforming India
☛ Which body was replaced by NITI Aayog? → Planning Commission

q: The term of office for the Chief Election Commissioner of India is:
o: 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
5 years or up to 70 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or up to 70 years of age, whichever is earlier
5 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
qs.e: The term of office for the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India is determined under Article 324 of the Constitution. The CEC serves for a term of 6 years or until reaching 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. This provision ensures the independence of the Election Commission. The CEC is appointed by the President and can only be removed through impeachment. This term limit ensures that the CEC remains in office for a maximum of six years or until age 65, providing opportunities for new talent and ensuring fair elections. The other options mentioning 5 years or 70 years are incorrect as the constitutional provision clearly specifies 6 years or 65 years.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of Chief Election Commissioner → 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
☛ Appointing authority of CEC → President
☛ Removal process of CEC → Impeachment (by Parliament)
☛ Constitutional article for Election Commission → Article 324
☛ Age limit for CEC → 65 years

q: According to the Constitution of India, who conducts the Election of the Vice-President of India?
o: The Legislature Councils of all States
The Legislative Assemblies of all States
qs.e: According to Article 66 of the Indian Constitution, the election of the Vice-President is conducted and controlled by the Election Commission of India. The election is held through the system of single transferable vote, where the electorate consists of members of both Houses of Parliament. The Election Commission issues the notification, receives nominations, ensures the process of voting and counting. The Vice-President holds office for a term of five years and serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Election Commission is an independent constitutional body that ensures free and fair elections.
qs.kf:
☛ Article related to Vice-President election → 66
☛ Term of Vice-President → 5 years
☛ Authority to decide disputes regarding Vice-President election → Supreme Court
☛ Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of → Rajya Sabha
☛ Electorate for Vice-President election → Members of both Houses of Parliament

q: Which of the following conducts the election of state legislatures?
o: State Election Commission of the concerned State
qs.e: According to Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, the Election Commission of India has the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections to Parliament, state legislatures, the President, and the Vice-President. It is an independent constitutional body. The State Election Commission only conducts elections for panchayats and municipalities. NITI Aayog and Parliament have no role in conducting elections. The Election Commission ensures free and fair elections.
qs.kf:
☛ Who conducts elections to state legislatures? → Election Commission of India
☛ Who conducts panchayat elections? → State Election Commission
☛ Who conducts the Presidential election? → Election Commission of India
☛ Under which article is the Election Commission formed? → Article 324
☛ What type of body is the Election Commission? → Constitutional body

q: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
qs.e: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution. It is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in the country. NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional body, created by an executive order. The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) are statutory bodies established by acts of Parliament. Therefore, only the Election Commission of India is a constitutional body directly set up by the Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article establishes the Election Commission? → Article 324
☛ NITI Aayog is which type of body? → Non-constitutional / executive body
☛ Which act created NHRC? → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ Examples of constitutional bodies → Election Commission, UPSC, CAG, Finance Commission
☛ Which body is not directly established by the Constitution? → NHRC (statutory body)

q: On which date in 1950 was the Election Commission established as per the Constitution?
qs.e: The Election Commission of India was established on 25th January 1950 under Article 324 of the Constitution. It is an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting elections in the country. This day is celebrated every year as 'National Voters' Day'. The first Chief Election Commissioner was Sukumar Sen. The Election Commission conducts elections, prepares voter lists, and enforces the Model Code of Conduct.
qs.kf:
☛ Establishment date of Election Commission → 25th January 1950
☛ Constitutional provision → Article 324
☛ First Chief Election Commissioner → Sukumar Sen
☛ National Voters' Day → 25th January
☛ Role of Election Commission → Conduct elections, voter list, code of conduct

q: The States Human Rights Commission is a/an:
qs.e: The State Human Rights Commission is a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It plays a crucial role in enforcing the right to life and personal liberty enshrined in Article 21 of the Constitution. The commission consists of a chairperson and four members, of which two are from a judicial background. Its main objective is to investigate human rights violations and make recommendations to the National Human Rights Commission. A statutory body is created by an act of parliament or state legislature, unlike a constitutional body which is established by the Constitution itself. It is not a non-profit organisation or an inter-state body.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which act is the State Human Rights Commission formed? → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ What is the maximum number of members in a State Human Rights Commission? → 5 (Chairperson + 4 members)
☛ Who appoints the chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission? → Governor
☛ Is the decision of the State Human Rights Commission subject to judicial review? → Yes
☛ What type of body is the State Human Rights Commission? → Statutory body

q: Which of the following is a constitutional body in India?
qs.e: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. It is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in the country. In contrast, NITI Aayog, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), and Central Information Commission (CIC) are statutory bodies, as they are created by acts of Parliament. NITI Aayog was formed in 2015 by an executive resolution, NHRC was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, and CIC under the Right to Information Act, 2005. Constitutional bodies derive their power and authority from the Constitution itself, while statutory bodies are created by laws passed by the legislature. Understanding this distinction is crucial for competitive exams.
qs.kf:
☛ Example of a constitutional body → Election Commission of India, UPSC, Finance Commission
☛ Article establishing Election Commission of India → Article 324
☛ NITI Aayog is a → Non-constitutional body (executive resolution)
☛ National Human Rights Commission established under → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ Central Information Commission established under → Right to Information Act, 2005

q: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
qs.e: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) is a statutory body, not a constitutional body. Constitutional bodies are those that are directly mentioned in the Constitution of India. The Election Commission of India (Article 324), the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (Article 148), and the Union Public Service Commission (Article 315) are constitutional bodies established by the Constitution. The NGT was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, an act of Parliament, not under the Constitution. It was created for the speedy disposal of environment-related cases.
qs.kf:
☛ Election Commission of India → Constitutional body under Article 324
☛ CAG of India → Constitutional post under Article 148
☛ UPSC → Constitutional body under Article 315
☛ National Green Tribunal → Statutory body, established by NGT Act, 2010
☛ Constitutional body → A body directly mentioned in the Constitution

q: According to the Indian Constitution, which of the following is NOT the function of the Union Public Service Commission?
o: To advise on the suitability of candidates for appointment, promotion and transfer
To advise on disciplinary matters affecting government servants
To advise on selection for the posts of high diplomatic nature
To advise on claims of legal proceedings instituted against a government servant
qs.e: Under Article 320 of the Indian Constitution, the functions of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) are defined. UPSC's primary role is to advise on the suitability of candidates for appointment, promotion, and transfer. It also advises on disciplinary matters affecting government servants, such as disciplinary proceedings. Additionally, UPSC advises on claims related to legal proceedings instituted against a government servant. However, advising on selection for posts of high diplomatic nature is not a function of UPSC. Such posts are selected directly by the President without consulting UPSC. Hence, this option is not part of UPSC's functions.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article defines UPSC functions? → Article 320
☛ When was UPSC established? → 26 January 1950
☛ Who appoints the Chairman of UPSC? → President
☛ Who constitutes the State Public Service Commission? → Governor
☛ Who selects for high diplomatic posts? → President

q: In the 1999 parliamentary elections, a coalition party government of _____ was formed, in which BJP was the largest member of the coalition.
qs.e: In the 1999 parliamentary elections, a coalition government of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) was formed, with BJP as its largest member. The NDA was first formed in 1998, but in 1999 elections it won a clear majority, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee became Prime Minister. The NDA included Shiv Sena, Janata Dal (United), Shiromani Akali Dal, Biju Janata Dal, and other parties. This coalition remained in power until 2004. The 1999 elections were held after the Kargil War, which boosted BJP's popularity. The NDA was formed with the aim of bringing non-Congress parties together on a common platform.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of NDA → National Democratic Alliance
☛ Leader of NDA in 1999 → Atal Bihari Vajpayee
☛ Major parties in NDA → BJP, Shiv Sena, JD(U), SAD, BJD
☛ Prime Minister after 1999 elections → Atal Bihari Vajpayee
☛ NDA's tenure → 1999-2004

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Both National Commission for Scheduled Castes and National Commission for Backward Classes are Constitutional bodies.
National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a Constitutional body, while National Commission for Backward Classes is a Non-Constitutional body.
National Commission for Backward Classes is a Constitutional body, while National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a Non-Constitutional body.
Both National Commission for Scheduled Castes and National Commission for Backward Classes are Non-Constitutional bodies.
qs.e: Under Article 338 of the Indian Constitution, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body. Similarly, the National Commission for Backward Classes was granted constitutional status through the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018, and operates under Article 338B. Both commissions come under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes ensures the protection and welfare of Scheduled Castes, while the National Commission for Backward Classes monitors reservations and schemes for backward classes. The objective of both constitutional bodies is to ensure the development and protection of disadvantaged groups.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article was the National Commission for Scheduled Castes formed? → Article 338
☛ Under which Article was the National Commission for Backward Classes formed? → Article 338B
☛ Which amendment granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes? → 102nd Constitutional Amendment, 2018
☛ Which ministry does the National Commission for Scheduled Castes come under? → Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
☛ Which ministry does the National Commission for Backward Classes come under? → Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

q: Who are eligible to vote in Lok Sabha elections?
o: Citizens aged 18 and above who are not disqualified under the Constitution or any law
Citizens who have paid income tax
Only citizens with a government job
qs.e: According to Article 326 of the Indian Constitution, every Indian citizen who is 18 years of age or older is entitled to vote in Lok Sabha and Assembly elections, unless disqualified under any law. The 61st Amendment (1988) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years. Payment of income tax or holding a government job is not a prerequisite for voting. Grounds for disqualification include bankruptcy, unsound mind, conviction for certain offenses, and corrupt practices. It is mandatory to have one's name in the electoral roll.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum voting age → 18 years
☛ Amendment that lowered voting age → 61st Amendment (1988)
☛ Constitutional provision → Article 326
☛ Grounds for disqualification → Bankruptcy, unsound mind, criminal conviction
☛ Name in electoral roll → Mandatory

q: Which of the following is NOT a provision to disqualify the members of a political party on the ground of defection mentioned in the tenth schedule of the Indian Constitution?
o: If a member votes against his party will
If a party merges with another party
If a nominated member joins another party after 6 months of his seat
If an elected member joins another party after election
qs.e: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, also known as the 'Anti-Defection Law', provides provisions for disqualifying members on grounds of defection. These include: a member voting against his party's whip, voluntarily giving up party membership, and an elected member joining another party after the election. Nominated members have a grace period of 6 months. However, if a party merges with another party, it is not considered defection, provided that at least two-thirds of the party's members agree to the merger. Hence, option 2 is NOT a provision for disqualification on the ground of defection.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Tenth Schedule added? → 1985 (via 52nd Amendment)
☛ What is the main objective of the Anti-Defection Law? → To prevent political instability
☛ What majority of members is required for a merger? → At least two-thirds
☛ Who decides the question of disqualification? → The Chairman or Speaker
☛ What is the grace period for nominated members? → 6 months

q: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is a constitutional body under which Article of the Indian Constitution, and what is its primary responsibility?
o: Article 325; Responsible for appointing Chief Ministers in states
Article 356; Responsible for appointing Governors in states
Article 310; Responsible for conducting state elections
Article 315; Responsible for recruitment and examinations for All India Services
qs.e: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is a constitutional body under Article 315 of the Indian Constitution. Its primary responsibility is to conduct recruitment and examinations for All India Services (IAS, IPS, IFS, etc.) and central services. UPSC is an independent institution ensuring merit-based selection. Its chairman and members are appointed by the President. Articles 315 to 323 contain provisions related to UPSC.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article is UPSC a constitutional body? → Article 315
☛ What is the primary function of UPSC? → Recruitment and exams for All India Services
☛ Who appoints the Chairman of UPSC? → President
☛ Which Articles cover UPSC provisions? → 315 to 323
☛ Which services are included in All India Services? → IAS, IPS, IFS

q: The political landscape in India fundamentally changed as a result of the fourth general election held in the year _____.
qs.e: The fourth general election in India was held in the year 1967. This election fundamentally changed the political landscape as the Congress party lost power in several states and secured a reduced majority at the centre. It was the first time the dominance of Congress was seriously challenged. Non-Congress coalition governments were formed in many states, marking the beginning of coalition politics and the rise of regional parties in India. The election further contributed to political fragmentation and diversity.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the fourth general election held in India? → 1967
☛ Which party faced a challenge in the fourth general election? → Congress
☛ What type of governments emerged after the 1967 election? → Coalition governments
☛ In which year did Congress first get a reduced majority at the centre? → 1967
☛ How many seats did Congress win in the fourth general election? → 283 (in Lok Sabha)

q: Which of the following Acts had provided the establishment of a public service commission for recruiting civil servants in British India?
qs.e: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the establishment of a Public Service Commission for recruiting civil servants in British India. This Act was based on the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms and introduced a system of diarchy at the provincial level. It also created a central Public Service Commission to oversee the recruitment of civil servants. Although the Act of 1919 laid the foundation, the actual commission was established in 1926, which later evolved into the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). The Act of 1935 further expanded and strengthened the commission's role. Thus, the 1919 Act was the first to envision a separate body for civil service recruitment.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Act established the Public Service Commission? → Government of India Act, 1919
☛ When was the first Public Service Commission established? → 1926
☛ Under which Act was UPSC formed? → Government of India Act, 1935
☛ Which Act introduced diarchy in provinces? → Government of India Act, 1919
☛ Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms are associated with which Act? → Government of India Act, 1919

q: What was a major focus of the 61st Constitutional Amendment?
o: Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years
Reservation of seats for women in Panchayats
Abolition of Privy Purses for former rulers
qs.e: The 61st Constitutional Amendment (1989) primarily focused on lowering the voting age. It amended Article 326 of the Indian Constitution, reducing the minimum voting age for Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly elections from 21 years to 18 years. The amendment aimed to involve the youth in the political process, as 18 is considered the age of adulthood. This increased youth participation and strengthened democracy. Other options, such as the Anti-Defection Law (52nd Amendment), reservation of seats for women in Panchayats (73rd Amendment), and abolition of Privy Purses (26th Amendment), are related to different amendments.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the 61st Constitutional Amendment passed? → 1989
☛ Which article was amended to reduce voting age? → Article 326
☛ What was the voting age before the 61st Amendment? → 21 years
☛ What is the voting age after the 61st Amendment? → 18 years
☛ Which government passed the 61st Amendment? → Rajiv Gandhi government

q: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
qs.e: The first Chief Election Commissioner of India was Sukumar Sen, who assumed office on 21 March 1950. He was responsible for conducting the first general elections in 1951-52. The Election Commission was formed under Article 324 of the Constitution. V. Narahari Rao was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, while H. K. Kripalani was a prominent freedom fighter. M. C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General of India. Sukumar Sen laid the foundation of the Election Commission and ensured free and fair elections.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India? → Sukumar Sen
☛ Who was the first RBI Governor of India? → V. Narahari Rao
☛ Who was the first Attorney General of India? → M. C. Setalvad
☛ Under which Article was the Election Commission formed? → Article 324
☛ When were the first general elections held? → 1951-52

q: Which body is entrusted with recruiting India’s civil servants on the basis of merit?
qs.e: The recruitment of India's civil servants on the basis of merit is entrusted to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). It is a constitutional body established under Articles 315 to 323 of the Constitution. UPSC conducts examinations like the Civil Services Examination, Engineering Services Examination, and Defence Services Examination. Its primary role is to ensure recruitment based on the principles of merit, impartiality, and transparency. The President's Secretariat, State Governments, and the Election Commission are not responsible for this recruitment. The independence of UPSC is constitutionally protected to maintain a fair recruitment process.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UPSC established? → 1 October 1926 (it got constitutional status after the Constitution)
☛ Who appoints the chairman of UPSC? → The President of India
☛ What is the tenure of UPSC members? → 6 years or until age 65, whichever is earlier
☛ Which articles mention UPSC? → Articles 315 to 323
☛ Which is the major examination conducted by UPSC? → Civil Services Examination (CSE)

q: Which of the following correctly describes the Planning Commission of India?
o: A constitutional body established by an Article of the Constitution.
A statutory body created by an Act of Parliament in 1950.
A constitutional commission chaired by the Chief Justice of India.
An extra-constitutional advisory body created by a government resolution in 1950.
qs.e: The Planning Commission of India (1950-2014) was an extra-constitutional body, meaning it was not established by the Constitution or an Act of Parliament. It was created on March 15, 1950, by a government resolution (executive order). It functioned as an advisory body and was chaired by the Prime Minister. Its main role was to formulate Five-Year Plans for economic development. In 2015, it was replaced by the NITI Aayog.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Planning Commission established? → 15 March 1950
☛ What was the nature of the Planning Commission? → Extra-constitutional and advisory
☛ Who chaired the Planning Commission? → The Prime Minister
☛ Which body replaced the Planning Commission? → NITI Aayog (2015)
☛ How was the Planning Commission created? → By a government resolution

q: Which act gave statutory status to the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)?
qs.e: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was established in 1964 by a government resolution, but it was granted statutory status through the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003. This act made CVC a statutory body responsible for advising and guiding central government agencies in corruption prevention. It was formed on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee on corruption. The CVC is an independent body whose chairman and members are appointed by the President. It has the power to direct the CBI in investigation of corruption cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
qs.kf:
☛ When was CVC established? → 1964 (by resolution)
☛ When did CVC get statutory status? → 2003
☛ Did Santhanam Committee recommend CVC? → Yes
☛ Who appoints CVC chairman? → President
☛ Which agency investigates under CVC? → CBI

q: What is the term period of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India?
qs.e: The term of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is 6 years or until he attains the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. This provision is laid down in Article 148 of the Indian Constitution. The CAG is appointed by the President and can be removed only in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court. The CAG acts as the guardian of the public financial system and audits all government accounts.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the CAG? → President
☛ Removal procedure of CAG is similar to which office? → Supreme Court judge
☛ What is the tenure of CAG? → 6 years
☛ What is the maximum age limit for CAG? → 65 years
☛ Which constitutional article deals with CAG? → Article 148

q: Which of the following central services holds the highest prestige, pay and emoluments among its peers?
qs.e: The Indian Foreign Service (IFS) is considered the most prestigious among central services due to its diplomatic role. IFS officers represent India abroad and handle international relations. They receive higher pay, allowances, and foreign postings compared to other services like Indian Defence Accounts Service, Indian Postal Service, or Indian Audit and Accounts Service. The service offers global exposure, faster promotions, and significant decision-making power in foreign policy. IFS is recruited through the UPSC Civil Services Examination and is a top choice for many candidates. Its officers work under the Ministry of External Affairs and are posted in Indian embassies and consulates worldwide.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Indian Foreign Service established? → 1946
☛ Who is the head of the IFS? → Foreign Secretary
☛ Under which ministry do IFS officers work? → Ministry of External Affairs
☛ What is the training institute for IFS? → Sushant Singh Rajput Lok Seva Training Institute
☛ Which is the oldest central service? → Indian Administrative Service (IAS)

q: What is the tenure of a member of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)?
o: 5 years or till attainment of 65 years of age
4 years or till attainment of 60 years of age
6 years or till attainment of the age of 65 years
qs.e: The tenure of a member of the UPSC is laid down in Article 316(2) of the Constitution. It is for a period of six years or until the member attains the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. This means that if a member turns 65 before completing six years, they must vacate the office. Similarly, if they complete six years before turning 65, their term ends. This provision ensures independence and efficiency of the Commission. UPSC is a constitutional body responsible for recruitment and disciplinary matters for civil services. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UPSC established? → 1 October 1926
☛ Who was the first Chairman of UPSC? → Sir Ross Barker
☛ What is the headquarters of UPSC? → New Delhi
☛ Under which Article was UPSC constituted? → Article 315
☛ Who has the power to remove members of UPSC? → President

q: Which authority is the appellate body under the RTI Act?
qs.e: Under the RTI Act, 2005, the Central Information Commission (CIC) is the appellate body. It deals with complaints and appeals related to the right to information. The CIC is an independent constitutional body comprising a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners. Its primary function is to ensure that public authorities provide timely and accurate information. If a person is dissatisfied with the first appeal decision, they can file a second appeal with the CIC. The commission's decision is final and binding. In contrast, the Chief Vigilance Commission handles anti-corruption matters, the National Human Rights Commission protects human rights, and the Lokpal addresses public grievances against officials. The CIC plays a crucial role in promoting transparency and accountability in government functioning.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the RTI Act enacted? → 2005
☛ What is the tenure of the CIC? → 5 years
☛ Who is the first appellate authority under RTI? → Senior officer of the concerned authority
☛ Is Right to Information a fundamental right? → It is a constitutional right but not under Article 19
☛ Who appoints the Information Commissioner? → The President of India

q: The All-India Services Act, 1951, allows which authority to frame rules for All-India service recruitment?
qs.e: The All-India Services Act, 1951, was enacted by the Parliament of India. This Act empowers the Central Government to frame rules regarding recruitment, service conditions, and other matters for All-India Services such as IAS, IPS, and IFS. Under Section 3, the Central Government can make rules after consulting the state governments. These rules are laid before Parliament. The President notifies the rules, but the authority to frame them lies with the Central Government. The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts the recruitment process but does not frame the rules.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the All-India Services Act enacted? → 1951
☛ Who has the authority to frame rules under this Act? → Central Government
☛ Which services are covered under All-India Services? → IAS, IPS, IFS
☛ Whose consultation is required for rule-making? → State Governments
☛ What is the role of UPSC? → Conducts recruitment process

q: How many seats did the BJP win in the February 2025 Delhi Assembly elections?
qs.e: In the February 2025 Delhi Assembly elections, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won 48 seats out of a total of 70 seats. This was a significant victory for the BJP, as it regained power in Delhi after losing three consecutive elections (2013, 2015, and 2020). The party saw a massive increase in its seat count compared to the 2020 elections, when it had won only 8 seats. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) secured 22 seats, while the Congress failed to win any seat. The BJP's victory was attributed to the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the party's development agenda. The voter turnout in this election was around 60%.
qs.kf:
☛ How many seats did BJP win in the Feb 2025 Delhi Assembly elections? → 48
☛ How many seats did AAP win in the same election? → 22
☛ How many seats did Congress win in the same election? → 0
☛ Total seats in Delhi Assembly? → 70
☛ How many more seats did BJP win in 2025 compared to 2020? → 40

q: Which of the following is an unstatutory and unconstitutional body?
qs.e: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is an unstatutory and unconstitutional body. It was established on 1 January 2015 through a cabinet resolution of the Government of India, replacing the Planning Commission. It was not created by any Act of Parliament or under any article of the Constitution but came into existence via an executive order. In contrast, the Attorney General of India (Article 76), the Central Information Commission (Right to Information Act 2005), and the National Human Rights Commission (Protection of Human Rights Act 1993) are either constitutional or statutory bodies.
qs.kf:
☛ First Chairman of NITI Aayog → Narendra Modi
☛ Headquarters of NITI Aayog → New Delhi
☛ NITI Aayog replaced → Planning Commission (2015)
☛ Full form of NITI → National Institution for Transforming India
☛ Basis of establishment of NITI Aayog → Executive resolution (non-statutory)

q: Which non-constitutional body investigates corruption complaints against public servants?
qs.e: Lokpal is a non-constitutional body established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 to investigate corruption complaints against public servants of the central government, including the Prime Minister, Ministers, and MPs. It is a statutory body created to combat corruption. In contrast, the Finance Commission, Election Commission, and Union Public Service Commission are constitutional bodies established under the Constitution of India. The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and up to eight members, with the Chairperson appointed through a process similar to that of the Chief Justice of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which act was the Lokpal established? → Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
☛ What is the scope of Lokpal's investigation? → Corruption complaints against central government public servants
☛ Which bodies are constitutional? → Election Commission, Finance Commission, Union Public Service Commission
☛ When was Lokpal formed? → 2013
☛ How is the Chairperson of Lokpal appointed? → Similar to the appointment of the Chief Justice of India

q: Which of the following is NOT a Central Armed Police Force?
qs.e: Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) include Indo-Tibetan Border Police, Border Security Force, and Central Reserve Police Force. The Criminal Investigation Department (CBI) is a central investigation agency, not an armed force. CAPFs are primarily responsible for border security and internal security, while CBI investigates specific crimes. There are seven CAPFs under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
qs.kf:
☛ Central Armed Police Forces → Work under Ministry of Home Affairs
☛ Number of CAPFs → 7
☛ Oldest CAPF → Assam Rifles (1835)
☛ Largest CAPF → Border Security Force
☛ CBI Headquarters → New Delhi

q: Which agency on 2025 authorised to share information with the Enforcement Directorate (ED) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act to combat cyber fraud?
qs.e: In 2025, the government authorised the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to share information with the Enforcement Directorate (ED) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) to combat cyber fraud. I4C, operating under the Ministry of Home Affairs, serves as a central nodal agency for preventing, investigating, and coordinating cyber crimes. This move was taken to address the growing nexus between money laundering and cyber fraud, strengthening financial investigations. I4C already plays a key role in reporting and analysing cyber fraud, and now it will provide critical data to the ED.
qs.kf:
☛ When was I4C established? → 2018
☛ Which ministry does I4C fall under? → Ministry of Home Affairs
☛ What is the full form of PMLA? → Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002
☛ Where is ED headquarters located? → New Delhi
☛ NCRP is associated with? → Cyber crime reporting

q: Select the correct statement regarding the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India.
o: It is a constitutional body formed by a Constitutional Amendment, with powers equal to the Supreme Court.
The NHRC has direct powers to prosecute and punish public officials for human rights abuses.
It was established in 1993 by an Act of Parliament to investigate and recommend on human rights violations.
The Chairperson of the NHRC is the Prime Minister of India.
qs.e: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India is a statutory body established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act passed by Parliament. It is not a constitutional body. The NHRC does not have direct powers to prosecute or punish; it only makes recommendations. Its chairperson is a former Chief Justice of India, not the Prime Minister. The NHRC investigates human rights violations and suggests measures to the government for their prevention.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NHRC established? → 1993
☛ Under which act was NHRC formed? → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ Who is the chairperson of NHRC? → Former Chief Justice of India
☛ What type of body is NHRC? → Statutory body
☛ What is the main power of NHRC? → Investigation and recommendations

q: To be eligible for membership of a State Legislature, a candidate must meet which of the following qualifications as laid down in the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Be an elector (voter) in any State assembly constituency
Pay income tax in the State
Have at least a graduate degree
Be a permanent resident of the State for 15 years
qs.e: For membership of a State Legislature, the Representation of the People Act, 1951 under Sections 4 and 5 mandates that a candidate must be an elector (voter) in any State assembly constituency. This ensures the candidate has a connection with the State. Other options such as paying income tax, having a graduate degree, or being a permanent resident for 15 years are not prescribed in the Act. Article 173 of the Indian Constitution sets the minimum age for State Legislature membership at 25 years.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum age for State Assembly member → 25 years
☛ Section 4 of RPA 1951 → Qualification for Assembly membership
☛ Minimum age for State Legislative Council member → 30 years
☛ Meaning of elector → Name in electoral roll of State assembly constituency
☛ Article 173 → Qualification for State Legislature membership

q: Who is responsible for implementing the RTI Act in public departments?
qs.e: Under the RTI Act, 2005, each public authority appoints a Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) or State Public Information Officer at the state level. These officers are responsible for processing information requests from citizens and providing the requested information within the stipulated time limit. The CPIO must provide information within 30 days of receiving the application. If the information is incorrect or incomplete, the CPIO is held accountable. Thus, the responsibility for implementing the RTI Act in public departments lies directly with the CPIO, not the Director General, District Magistrate, or Central Vigilance Officer.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the RTI Act enacted? → 2005
☛ What is the time limit to provide information? → 30 days
☛ Who is the first appellate authority? → Officer senior to CPIO
☛ What is the application fee for RTI? → ₹10
☛ Who constitutes the Central Information Commission? → Central Government

q: Who among the following is eligible to be appointed as the Chairperson of the Lokpal, as per the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: A retired Cabinet Secretary of India
A sitting judge of a High Court
A former Judge of the Supreme Court
qs.e: As per the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the eligibility criteria for the Chairperson of Lokpal are clearly defined. The Chairperson can be a former Chief Justice, a former Judge of the Supreme Court, or a former member of an All India Service. Option 4 'A former Judge of the Supreme Court' meets this condition. A retired Cabinet Secretary is eligible only for the post of member, not for Chairperson. A sitting judge of a High Court or a current Member of Parliament cannot be appointed. Thus, only a former Supreme Court Judge is eligible to be Chairperson of Lokpal.
qs.kf:
☛ Appointment of Lokpal Chairperson → Done by the President of India
☛ Number of members in Lokpal → Maximum 8 including Chairperson
☛ Committee recommending Lokpal → Includes PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of Opposition, and Chief Justice of India
☛ Tenure of Lokpal → 5 years or age of 70 years, whichever is earlier
☛ Jurisdiction of Lokpal → Covers PM, Ministers, MPs, and Group 'A' officers for corruption investigation

q: Which body is responsible for recruitment to All India Services like IAS and IPS?
qs.e: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is responsible for recruitment to All India Services like IAS and IPS. It is a constitutional body established under Article 315 of the Indian Constitution. UPSC selects suitable candidates through examinations like the Civil Services Examination. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. Other options such as Election Commission, Comptroller and Auditor General, and Finance Commission are not involved in recruitment.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which article was UPSC established? → Article 315
☛ Who appoints the Chairman of UPSC? → President
☛ Where is the headquarters of UPSC located? → New Delhi
☛ Which category do IAS and IPS belong to? → All India Services
☛ What is the term of UPSC members? → 6 years or until age 65

q: What does the Constitution of India stipulate regarding the composition of the Election Commission of India (ECI)?
o: It is constitutionally fixed as a single-member body headed by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) only.
It must always be a three-member body (one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners).
It must include one Election Commissioner from each major state to ensure federal balance
It may be single or multi-member; initially, there was only a Chief Election Commissioner until 1989.
qs.e: Article 324 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Election Commission of India (ECI). It does not specify whether the Commission will be single-member or multi-member; rather, it states that the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) shall be appointed by the President, and other Election Commissioners may also be appointed as needed. Initially, until 1989, the ECI consisted of only the CEC, making it a single-member body. In 1989, the government appointed two additional Election Commissioners, making it a three-member body. Thus, the Constitution does not fix the composition but allows flexibility; it may be single or multi-member. The CEC can be removed only through a process similar to that of a Supreme Court judge, while other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC.
qs.kf:
☛ Article related to Election Commission → Article 324
☛ Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner → President
☛ Provision for removal of Election Commissioners → On recommendation of CEC
☛ Term of office of CEC → 6 years or age 65, whichever is earlier
☛ Year when ECI became a three-member body → 1989

q: Who is described as the 'permanent executive'?
o: The permanent civil servants who manage daily administration
The heads of government and their ministers
qs.e: In the Indian political system, the executive is divided into two parts: political executive and permanent executive. The political executive includes elected ministers and heads of government, who are temporary and change with elections. The permanent executive consists of civil servants who permanently work in the government machinery and manage day-to-day administration. These civil servants remain in office for long periods and play a crucial role in implementing policies. They ensure continuity in administration even when the political executive changes. Therefore, the permanent executive is considered the backbone of the administration.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for permanent executive → Bureaucracy
☛ Head of civil services in India → Cabinet Secretary
☛ Tenure of political executive → Election-dependent (temporary)
☛ Main function of permanent executive → Implementation of policies
☛ Recruitment body for civil servants → UPSC

q: Under which article of the Constitution is the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India appointed?
qs.e: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is appointed under Article 148 of the Constitution. CAG is an independent authority under Part V (Chapter V) of the Indian Constitution pertaining to the Union. The CAG is appointed by the President and audits all accounts of the Government of India and state governments. Article 149 defines the duties and powers of the CAG, while Article 150 pertains to the form of accounts of the Union and states. The CAG holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. Other options: Article 324 relates to the Election Commission, Article 280 to the Finance Commission, and Article 76 to the Attorney General.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the CAG? → The President
☛ What is the term of CAG? → 6 years or 65 years (whichever is earlier)
☛ Under which article does the CAG take oath? → Article 148 read with Third Schedule
☛ Which article governs removal of CAG? → Article 148, similar to a Supreme Court judge
☛ Which article details the duties of CAG? → Article 149

q: What was the key electoral innovation introduced in the 1909 Act?
qs.e: The 1909 Act, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, was a significant constitutional reform in British India. Its key electoral innovation was the introduction of separate electorates for the Muslim community, creating distinct constituencies where only Muslim voters could elect Muslim candidates. The aim was to provide political representation to minorities, but it promoted communalism. This provision later continued in the 1935 Act and the Communal Award. Separate electorates deepened communal divisions in Indian politics and ultimately contributed to the partition of India. The system was a departure from the principle of joint electorates and had long-lasting effects on the subcontinent's political landscape.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year were the Morley-Minto Reforms introduced? → 1909
☛ For which community were separate electorates created? → Muslims
☛ What is the other name of the 1909 Act? → Indian Councils Act 1909
☛ What was the purpose of separate electorates? → Political representation for minorities
☛ What was the impact of separate electorates on India? → Increased communalism

q: When was K Sanjay Murthy sworn in as the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India by the president of India?
qs.e: K Sanjay Murthy was sworn in as the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India on 21 November 2024. President Droupadi Murmu administered the oath of office and secrecy at Rashtrapati Bhavan. He is the 15th CAG of India. Previously, he served as Secretary in the Department of Administrative Reforms. The CAG is the head of the supreme audit institution of India, ensuring public financial accountability. His appointment came after the tenure of Girish Chandra Murmu ended. The CAG holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the CAG of India? → President of India
☛ What is the term of office for the CAG? → 6 years or 65 years of age
☛ Under which article of the Constitution does the CAG function? → Article 148
☛ K Sanjay Murthy is the ___ CAG of India. → 15th
☛ Which department did K Sanjay Murthy serve as Secretary before becoming CAG? → Department of Administrative Reforms

q: Which constitutional body is empowered to adjudicate legal disputes between the Centre and one or more states in India?
qs.e: Under Article 131 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court of India is empowered with original jurisdiction to adjudicate legal disputes between the Centre and one or more states. This includes federal disputes such as boundary disagreements, water sharing, and constitutional interpretation. The Inter-State Council (Article 263) is only an advisory body, while the Election Commission and Finance Commission lack the authority to resolve such disputes. The Supreme Court's decision is final and binding, protecting the federal structure and ensuring legal uniformity.
qs.kf:
☛ Constitutional body for Centre-state disputes → Supreme Court
☛ Article granting original jurisdiction to Supreme Court → Article 131
☛ Primary function of Inter-State Council → Advising on Centre-state relations
☛ Article under which Finance Commission is formed → Article 280
☛ Nature of Supreme Court's decision → Final and binding

q: The first election for the provincial legislatures in British India was held in the year:
qs.e: The first election for the provincial legislatures in British India was held in 1937. These elections were conducted under the provisions of the Government of India Act 1935, which ended dyarchy and introduced provincial autonomy. The elections took place in February 1937, and the Indian National Congress formed governments in most provinces. This election marked a significant turning point in Indian politics as it gave Indians experience in governance at the provincial level. In 1936, electoral rolls were prepared, but the actual voting occurred in 1937. The Act of 1935 was passed earlier, but elections were held later. 1938 saw preparations for the next elections.
qs.kf:
☛ When were the provincial elections held under the Government of India Act 1935? → 1937
☛ Which act introduced provincial autonomy? → Government of India Act 1935
☛ Which party won most provinces in the 1937 elections? → Indian National Congress
☛ In which month were the 1937 provincial elections held? → February
☛ Approximately how many voters were there in the 1937 elections? → 30 million

q: As of October 2020, which of the following is NOT recognised as a national party?
qs.e: As of October 2020, India had eight national parties: Bharatiya Janata Party, Indian National Congress, Bahujan Samaj Party, Communist Party of India (Marxist), Communist Party of India, Nationalist Congress Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, and Trinamool Congress. The Samajwadi Party (SP) is a major regional party in Uttar Pradesh but does not hold national party status. To be recognized as a national party, a party must meet criteria set by the Election Commission, such as securing at least 6% of valid votes in Lok Sabha or assembly elections and winning at least 11 Lok Sabha seats. The SP has failed to meet these criteria, hence it is not a national party.
qs.kf:
☛ Vote percentage required for national party (Lok Sabha) → 6%
☛ Seats required for national party (Lok Sabha) → 11 seats
☛ Total national parties as of October 2020 → 8
☛ Main area of Samajwadi Party → Uttar Pradesh
☛ Body that grants national party status → Election Commission of India

q: As of Dec 2020, who is the Chairman of the National Commission for Backward Classes ?
qs.e: As of December 2020, the Chairman of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was Bhagwan Lal Sahni. This is a constitutional body that oversees matters related to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes. Sahni, a former Member of Parliament and social activist, held the position from 2017 to 2023. The commission aims to formulate policies for the welfare of disadvantaged communities and address their grievances.
qs.kf:
☛ NCBC Chairman (2020) → Bhagwan Lal Sahni
☛ NCBC Establishment Year → 1993
☛ NCBC Headquarters → New Delhi
☛ NCBC Constitutional Status → Granted in 2018
☛ NCBC Recommendations → Not binding

q: Against which act Mahatma Gandhi asked people to observe 6 April 1919 as a day of non- violence opposition?
qs.e: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 allowed the British government to imprison political prisoners without trial for up to two years. In protest against this repressive law, Mahatma Gandhi called for a nationwide hartal and non-violent opposition on April 6, 1919, known as the Rowlatt Satyagraha. This act later led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre on April 13, 1919. Gandhi described it as the 'Black Act' and mobilized mass protests across India. It was the first major pan-India movement led by Gandhi.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Rowlatt Act passed? → 1919
☛ When did the Rowlatt Satyagraha begin? → April 6, 1919
☛ When did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occur? → April 13, 1919
☛ What was the Rowlatt Act called? → Black Act
☛ Who chaired the Rowlatt Committee? → Sir Sydney Rowlatt

q: Who is appointed as new Chairman of National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) in February, 2021?
qs.e: In February 2021, Vijay Sampla was appointed as the new Chairman of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC). This commission is a constitutional body that works to protect the rights and promote the welfare of Scheduled Castes. Vijay Sampla hails from Punjab and has previously served as a Union Minister of State. Prior to his appointment, the position was held by Ramdas Athavale. This appointment is considered an important step by the government to strengthen representation and empowerment of the Scheduled Caste community.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NCSC established? → 2004 (Constitutional body)
☛ Who was the first Chairman of NCSC? → Surjit Singh Barnala
☛ Where is the headquarters of NCSC? → New Delhi
☛ What is the tenure of NCSC Chairman? → 3 years
☛ Vijay Sampla belongs to which state? → Punjab

q: When was the option of NOTA introduced as part of the Indian voting system?
qs.e: The option of NOTA (None of the Above) was introduced in India in September 2013 following a Supreme Court judgment. It allows voters to reject all candidates in an election. The Supreme Court ruled that NOTA provides a way for voters to express their dissent. NOTA was first used in the 2013 assembly elections in states like Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Delhi. The Election Commission of India ensured that NOTA was added as the last option on EVMs. NOTA maintains voter confidentiality and gives voters the right to record their choice without opting for any candidate.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NOTA introduced? → 2013
☛ Full form of NOTA? → None of the Above
☛ First election to use NOTA? → 2013 assembly elections
☛ Who implemented NOTA? → Election Commission of India
☛ Where is NOTA button on EVM? → Last option

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India examines the accounts of which of the following?
o: Neither state government nor central government
qs.e: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is an independent authority under Article 148 of the Constitution. CAG audits the accounts of the Government of India and all state governments. This includes revenue and expenditure of both the centre and states. CAG also audits accounts of public sector undertakings and other bodies when specified by law. CAG reports are submitted to the President and governors, who then place them before Parliament and state legislatures. This ensures transparency and accountability in the use of public funds. The CAG plays a crucial role in maintaining financial discipline and preventing misuse of public money.
qs.kf:
☛ Term of CAG → 6 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
☛ Who appoints CAG → President of India
☛ Oath of office administered by → President
☛ Article 148 → Provision for CAG
☛ Article 151 → CAG reports to be laid before Parliament

q: Who was the first President of the Union Public Service Commission in India?
qs.e: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) was established on 1 October 1926 under the Government of India Act 1919. Its first Chairman was Sir Ross Barker, who served from 1926 to 1932. The UPSC headquarters is located in New Delhi. Dr. A.R. Kidwai later became Chairman, while J.P. Gupta and Rajani Razdan also served as former Chairmen. UPSC conducts recruitment and examinations for civil services in India. It is an independent constitutional body established under Article 315.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UPSC established? → 1 October 1926
☛ Who was the first Indian Chairman? → Dr. A.R. Kidwai
☛ Who is the current Chairman? → Preeti Sudan (as of 2025)
☛ Where is UPSC headquarters? → New Delhi
☛ Under which act was UPSC created? → Government of India Act 1919

q: In which year was the first general election held in India?
qs.e: The first general election in India was held in 1951–52. This election took place after the adoption of the Constitution of India, which came into effect on 26 January 1950. The election was conducted for a total of 489 Lok Sabha seats and had around 173 million eligible voters. The voting process occurred in multiple phases, spanning from October 1951 to February 1952. The Indian National Congress won a majority, and Jawaharlal Nehru became the Prime Minister. This election was a landmark event that laid the foundation of democracy in independent India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first general election held in India? → 1951–52
☛ Total seats in the first election? → 489
☛ Total voters in the first election? → 173 million
☛ Prime Minister after the first election? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Duration of the first general election? → October 1951 to February 1952

q: In which of the following years did Mamata Banerjee found All India Trinamool Congress?
qs.e: Mamata Banerjee founded the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) in 1998. She was previously a member of the Indian National Congress but left due to ideological differences and formed her own party. TMC is primarily active in West Bengal and emerged as a challenge to the long-standing Left Front government. Mamata Banerjee has been the Chief Minister of West Bengal since 2011, and her party has formed the government multiple times in the state. This event is a significant example of the rise of regional parties in Indian politics.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of founding of TMC → 1998
☛ Founder → Mamata Banerjee
☛ Headquarters → Kolkata, West Bengal
☛ Election symbol → Double flowers (Jora Gaantha)
☛ Political ideology → Secularism, Social justice

q: Which of the following constitutional bodies is responsible for ensuring Free and Fair Elections?
qs.e: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body responsible for ensuring free and fair elections in the country. It was established on 25 January 1950 under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. The commission conducts elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, state legislative assemblies, and the offices of the President and Vice President. The Chief Election Commissioner and other commissioners are appointed by the President. The commission announces elections, enforces the Model Code of Conduct, and supervises the voting process. To ensure the Election Commission's independence, the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only through impeachment.
qs.kf:
☛ Constitutional provision for formation of Election Commission of India → Article 324
☛ Date of establishment of Election Commission of India → 25 January 1950
☛ Procedure to remove Chief Election Commissioner → Impeachment (by Parliament)
☛ Elections conducted by Election Commission of India → Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, Legislative Assemblies, President, Vice President
☛ Main function of Election Commission under Article 324 → Ensuring free and fair elections

q: In which of the following years was the National Commission for Women established?
qs.e: The National Commission for Women (NCW) in India was established on 31 January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990. It is a statutory body aimed at protecting and promoting the rights of women. The commission works to prevent discrimination and harassment against women and spreads awareness about their legal rights. It was constituted by a government order and reports to the central government. The first chairperson of NCW was Dr. Mohini Giri.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the National Commission for Women established? → 1992
☛ Under which act was NCW established? → National Commission for Women Act, 1990
☛ Where is the headquarters of NCW? → New Delhi
☛ Who was the first chairperson of NCW? → Dr. Mohini Giri
☛ What type of body is NCW? → Statutory body

q: The Constitution ensures the security of the tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. They are appointed for _______ years term or continue till the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
qs.e: According to Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners are appointed by the President. The Constitution ensures the security of their tenure by providing that they are appointed for a term of 6 years or continue till the age of 65, whichever is earlier. This provision is made to keep the Election Commission independent from executive pressure. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only through the same process as a judge of the Supreme Court, while other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
qs.kf:
☛ Chief Election Commissioner's tenure → 6 years or till age 65, whichever is earlier
☛ Election Commissioners' tenure → 6 years or till age 65, whichever is earlier
☛ Article 324 → Related to Election Commission
☛ Removal of Chief Election Commissioner → Same process as removal of Supreme Court judge
☛ Removal of Election Commissioners → Requires recommendation of Chief Election Commissioner

q: The Delimitation Commission is appointed by the _______________________ and works in collaboration with the Election Commission of India.
qs.e: The Delimitation Commission is a high-level body appointed by the President of India. Its primary function is to redraw the boundaries of Lok Sabha and state assembly constituencies to ensure equal representation based on population changes. The commission works in collaboration with the Election Commission of India. Typically, the Delimitation Commission consists of a retired Supreme Court judge as its chairperson, along with the Chief Election Commissioner and State Election Commissioners. It is not a permanent body and is constituted after each census. However, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976 froze the delimitation of constituencies until 2001 to encourage population control measures.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Delimitation Commission? → President of India
☛ Who chairs the Delimitation Commission? → Retired Supreme Court judge
☛ Which body does the Delimitation Commission work with? → Election Commission
☛ Is the Delimitation Commission a permanent body? → No, it is temporary
☛ On what basis is delimitation done? → Population

q: In which of the following years has Dinesh Goswami committee been formed for Electoral Reforms?
qs.e: The Dinesh Goswami Committee was formed in 1990 for Electoral Reforms. Its aim was to bring transparency and fairness to the election process. The committee made several key recommendations, including the introduction of voter identity cards and monitoring of election expenditure. It also suggested improvements in the registration of political parties and allocation of election symbols. The report of the Dinesh Goswami Committee laid the foundation for many changes in the Indian electoral system.
qs.kf:
☛ Formation year of Dinesh Goswami Committee → 1990
☛ Purpose of the committee → Electoral Reforms
☛ Key recommendation → Voter ID cards
☛ Another recommendation → Election expenditure monitoring
☛ Chairman of the committee → Dinesh Goswami

q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can a member of the Public Service Commission be removed by the President of India?
qs.e: Article 317 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to remove a member of the Public Service Commission. The removal process requires a recommendation from the Supreme Court judge. A member can be removed only on grounds of misbehaviour or incapacity. Article 318 deals with service conditions of members, Article 314 with salaries of constitutional posts, and Article 315 with establishment of Public Service Commissions. This procedure ensures the independence of the Commission.
qs.kf:
☛ Removal of Public Service Commission member → Article 317
☛ Whose recommendation is required for removal → Supreme Court judge
☛ Grounds for removal → Misbehaviour or incapacity
☛ Service conditions of Commission members → Article 318
☛ Establishment of Public Service Commission → Article 315

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for an independent Election Commission for the ‘superintendence, directions and control of the electoral roll and the conduct of the elections of India?
qs.e: Article 324 of the Indian Constitution provides for an independent Election Commission vested with the power of superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President. This article ensures free and fair elections in India. The Election Commission is a constitutional body. The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President and enjoys the same rank, power, and salary as a Judge of the Supreme Court. Article 324 guarantees the independence of the Election Commission and protects it from executive interference. It also allows the appointment of Regional Commissioners if necessary, with the President's approval.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Election Commission? → President
☛ How many members does the Election Commission have? → Chief Election Commissioner and other Commissioners
☛ Term of Chief Election Commissioner? → 6 years or 65 years, whichever is earlier
☛ Who appoints State Election Commissioner? → Governor
☛ Article 324 is in which Part? → Part XV (Elections)

q: In which of the following years did Kanshiram Found Bahujan Samaj Party?
qs.e: The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) was founded by Kanshiram in 1984. The party was established to uplift Dalits, Other Backward Classes, and minorities. Prior to this, Kanshiram had formed the Dalit Shoshit Samaj Sangharsh Samiti (DS-4) in 1981 and the Dalit Shoshit Samaj Nyay Manch in 1982. These organizations laid the groundwork for BSP as a political platform to fight for social justice and equality. In Uttar Pradesh, the party has formed governments multiple times, with Mayawati serving as Chief Minister four times.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of founding of BSP → 1984
☛ Founder of BSP → Kanshiram
☛ Headquarters of BSP → New Delhi
☛ Election symbol of BSP → Elephant
☛ Kanshiram's notable work → "The Chieftain"

q: Which of the following Parts of the Indian Constitution deals with the provision regarding composition, appointment and removal of members along with the independence, power and function of the UPSC?
qs.e: Part XIV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 315 to 323) deals with the Union and State Public Service Commissions. This part provides detailed provisions for the composition, appointment, removal, independence, powers, and functions of the UPSC. Article 315 establishes the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions. Article 316 deals with the appointment and term of members. Article 317 outlines the process for removal of members, which can only be done by the President after an inquiry by the Supreme Court. Articles 318 to 323 cover the independence, expenses, reports, and functions of the Commission. Part XIV contains 9 articles (315-323). It clarifies the role of UPSC in recruitment and disciplinary matters for public services. The Commission's independence is ensured by provisions like charging its expenses on the Consolidated Fund of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Constitutional Part dealing with UPSC → Part XIV
☛ Article 315 → Establishment of UPSC and SPSCs
☛ Article 317 → Removal of UPSC members
☛ Term of UPSC members → 6 years or until age 65
☛ Primary function of UPSC → Conduct recruitment exams for Union services

q: Subject to the provisions of Article ____, there shall be a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State.
qs.e: Article 315 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of Public Service Commissions for the Union and each state. It states that there shall be a Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for the Union and a State Public Service Commission (SPSC) for each state. This provision is part of Part XIV of the Constitution, which deals with services. Under Article 315, a joint Public Service Commission may also be created for two or more states if the state legislatures pass resolutions. The primary functions of these Commissions include recruitment to civil services and advising on disciplinary matters.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the chairman of UPSC? → President
☛ Who has the power to remove members of a State Public Service Commission? → President
☛ Article 320 deals with? → Functions of Public Service Commissions
☛ Article 317 deals with? → Removal of members of Public Service Commissions
☛ In which year was UPSC established? → 1926 (on the recommendation of the Lee Commission)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (20/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states about the formation of Union Public Service Commission of India?
qs.e: Article 315 of the Indian Constitution provides for the formation of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions. It states that there shall be a Public Service Commission for each state and a Union Public Service Commission for the centre. Article 316 deals with the appointment and term of members, Article 317 provides for the removal of members, and Article 318 deals with the service conditions of members and staff. Thus, the correct article for the formation of UPSC is Article 315.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article deals with formation of UPSC? → Article 315
☛ Which Article deals with appointment of UPSC members? → Article 316
☛ Which Article deals with removal of UPSC members? → Article 317
☛ Which Article deals with service conditions of UPSC members? → Article 318
☛ Who appoints the Chairman of UPSC? → President of India

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1
q: In the 2024 Jharkhand Assembly elections, how many seats were won by the winning party/coalition and what is the name of the party/coalition?
qs.e: In the 2024 Jharkhand Assembly elections, the JMM-led INDIA alliance won 56 seats out of 81, securing a majority. The alliance included JMM, Congress, RJD, and CPI(ML) Liberation. JMM alone won 34 seats, Congress 16, RJD 4, and CPI(ML) 2. The BJP-led NDA alliance won 24 seats. Hemant Soren of JMM took oath as Chief Minister. This was JMM's second consecutive victory under Hemant Soren's leadership.
qs.kf:
☛ Total seats in Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha → 81
☛ Seats won by JMM-led alliance in 2024 → 56
☛ Seats won by JMM alone → 34
☛ Seats won by BJP-led NDA → 24
☛ Chief Minister's name → Hemant Soren

q: What is the meaning of ‘Lokayukta’ in the Constitution of India?
o: A body operating at the state level to investigate an individual's complaint against public servants or any politician with respect to corruption
A body operating at the central level to investigate the civil servant or politician with respect to complaint made against them for corruption
A body created to look into the complaints made with respect to frauds in the financial sector
qs.e: In the Indian Constitution, Lokayukta is a state-level institution that investigates complaints against public servants or politicians regarding corruption. It is based on the principle of Ombudsman, which controls administrative corruption. The Lokayukta is appointed by the Governor of the state and functions as an independent body. This concept was adopted on the recommendation of the Administrative Reforms Commission in 1966. Maharashtra was the first state to establish a Lokayukta. The powers of Lokayukta are wide but subject to judicial review. It plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency and accountability in governance at the state level.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Lokayukta? → Governor
☛ Which was the first state to establish Lokayukta? → Maharashtra
☛ What is the other name for Lokayukta? → Ombudsman
☛ At which level does Lokayukta function? → State level
☛ Which commission suggested the concept of Lokayukta? → Administrative Reforms Commission (1966)

q: A political party can be recognised as a national party if it secures ___ of the valid votes in any four states in general or state assembly elections and in addition it wins 4 Lok Sabha seat from any state or states.
qs.e: According to the rules of the Election Commission of India, a political party must fulfill two conditions to be recognized as a National Party. First, it must secure at least 6% of the total valid votes polled in Lok Sabha or State Assembly elections in at least four states. Second, it must win at least 4 Lok Sabha seats from any state or states. This provision is designed to grant national-level recognition to larger parties. Currently, some recognized national parties include the Bharatiya Janata Party, Indian National Congress, and Bahujan Samaj Party. The 6% threshold is the minimum requirement for a party to be deemed a national party.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the minimum vote percentage required for a national party? → 6%
☛ In how many states must a party secure 6% votes for national party status? → At least 4 states
☛ Minimum Lok Sabha seats required for a national party? → 4 seats
☛ Who recognizes national parties in India? → Election Commission of India
☛ Which are the current major national parties? → BJP, Congress, BSP

q: Which political party was founded by Kanshi Ram?
qs.e: Kanshi Ram founded the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) on April 14, 1984. The party primarily aimed at uplifting Dalits, Adivasis, OBCs, and religious minorities socially and politically. Kanshi Ram is widely regarded as a symbol of social justice and equality. Before forming BSP, he established the Dalit Shoshit Samaj Sangharsh Samiti (DS4). He was a key leader of the Bahujan movement and later made Mayawati his political successor. The BSP has been a significant force in Indian politics, especially in Uttar Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ When was BSP founded? → April 14, 1984
☛ Birthplace of Kanshi Ram? → Khaspura, Ratan Garh, Punjab
☛ When did Kanshi Ram die? → October 9, 2006
☛ Election symbol of BSP? → Elephant
☛ Which organization did Kanshi Ram first form? → Dalit Shoshit Samaj Sangharsh Samiti

q: What is the right to delimitation of constituencies can be done by the majority?
qs.e: Under Articles 82 and 327 of the Indian Constitution, delimitation of constituencies is done by Parliament through legislation. It requires a general majority (simple majority) of members present and voting, not a special majority. Delimitation aims to readjust constituencies based on population changes. Since it is a legislative function, the Constitution does not mandate a specific majority. A general majority ensures that the law is passed by more than half of the members voting, making it a flexible process for periodic revisions.
qs.kf:
☛ Articles related to delimitation → 82 and 327
☛ Who constitutes the Delimitation Commission? → President
☛ Basis of delimitation → Population
☛ Meaning of general majority → 50%+1 of members present and voting
☛ Majority required for delimitation law → General majority

q: Who is known as the protector of public property?
qs.e: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is known as the protector of public property. The CAG is responsible for auditing the accounts of the central and state governments to ensure that public funds are used lawfully and efficiently. Mentioned in Article 148, the CAG acts as a watchdog of the public purse and submits reports to the President and Governors. Other options: Central Vigilance Commissioner deals with corruption prevention, Chief Information Commissioner with Right to Information, and Chief Election Commissioner with election processes.
qs.kf:
☛ First CAG of India → V. Narahari Rao
☛ Who appoints CAG → President
☛ Term of CAG → 6 years or up to age 65, whichever is earlier
☛ Removal process of CAG → Similar to a High Court judge
☛ Articles related to CAG → Articles 148-151

q: Which of the following articles deals with elections to the House of the People and to the legislative assemblies of state to be on the basis of adult suffrage?
qs.e: Article 326 of the Indian Constitution provides for elections to the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of states on the basis of adult suffrage. According to this article, every person who is a citizen of India and has completed the age of 18 years is entitled to vote, unless disqualified by law. This provision is crucial for strengthening democracy. Among the other options, Article 318 deals with Union Public Service Commission, Article 352 deals with National Emergency, and Article 340 deals with Commission for Backward Classes.
qs.kf:
☛ Article for adult suffrage → 326
☛ Minimum voting age → 18 years
☛ Article for National Emergency → 352
☛ Article for UPSC → 315–323
☛ Article for Backward Classes Commission → 340

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which institution has been established by the 74th Constitutional Amendment, 1992, to conduct municipal elections in each State?
qs.e: The 74th Constitutional Amendment, 1992 granted constitutional status to municipalities in India. Under Article 243K of this amendment, the State Election Commission was established in each state. This commission is responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of municipal elections. The State Election Commission is an independent constitutional body whose chairperson is appointed by the Governor. Its tenure and service conditions are determined by the state legislature. The establishment of this commission ensures that municipal elections are conducted freely and fairly, strengthening local self-governance. This amendment came into effect in 1993.
qs.kf:
☛ 74th Constitutional Amendment relates to → Municipalities
☛ Who appoints the chairperson of State Election Commission → Governor
☛ Article for State Election Commission → Article 243K
☛ Who conducts municipal elections in states → State Election Commission
☛ 74th Amendment came into effect in → 1993

q: Chief Election Commissioner of India can be removed from the office by _________.
