☛ Main purpose of ST seat reservation → Ensure political representation
☛ Body that revises reservation of seats in Lok Sabha → Delimitation Commission
☛ Current approximate number of ST reserved seats in Lok Sabha → Around 47 (depending on delimitation)

q: Basically, how many seats were reserved for Scheduled Castes in the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: Originally, 84 seats were reserved for Scheduled Castes (SC) in the Lok Sabha. This reservation was provided under Article 330 of the Indian Constitution, which mandates reservation of seats for SC and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in the Lok Sabha. The reservation was implemented in the original Constitution in 1950 with the aim of ensuring political representation for these communities. The number of reserved seats has been revised over time based on population changes. Currently, there are 84 seats reserved for SC and 47 seats for ST in the Lok Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article provides for SC reservation in Lok Sabha? → Article 330
☛ How many seats are currently reserved for ST in Lok Sabha? → 47
☛ How many seats were originally reserved for SC in Lok Sabha? → 84
☛ Which Article deals with reservation for women in Lok Sabha? → Article 334 (related to Women's Reservation Bill 2023)
☛ Is there reservation for SC/ST in Rajya Sabha? → No

q: National Human Rights Commission established in the year ______________.
qs.e: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It is a statutory body responsible for protecting and promoting human rights in India. Its headquarters is in New Delhi. The commission consists of a chairperson and four members. The first chairperson was Justice Ranganath Mishra. NHRC is in conformity with the Paris Principles of the United Nations.
qs.kf:
☛ NHRC headquarters → New Delhi
☛ First chairperson of NHRC → Justice Ranganath Mishra
☛ Act establishing NHRC → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ Total members in NHRC → 5 including chairperson
☛ Date of establishment of NHRC → 12 October 1993

q: Which one of the following is NOT an official State language in India?
qs.e: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution recognizes 22 languages, including Bodo, Punjabi, and Assamese. Khandeshi is a regional dialect spoken in the Khandesh region of Maharashtra, but it does not have official state language status. Hence, it is NOT an official state language of India. The other options (Bodo, Punjabi, Assamese) are listed in the Eighth Schedule and are state languages of Assam, Punjab, and Assam respectively.
qs.kf:
☛ How many languages are in the Eighth Schedule of India? → 22
☛ Which state has Bodo as an official language? → Assam
☛ Punjabi is the state language of which state? → Punjab
☛ Assamese is the official language of which state? → Assam
☛ Khandeshi is a dialect of which region? → Khandesh region of Maharashtra

q: Which Emergency does the term "Emergency Announcement" denotes?
qs.e: ✅ Correct Answer: (B) National Emergency

q: When did the Constituent Assembly adopt the national anthem?
qs.e: India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was originally written in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore. It was first sung on December 27, 1911, at the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress. The Constituent Assembly officially adopted it as the national anthem on January 24, 1950, just two days before the Constitution came into effect. The lyrics and music are both by Tagore, and the complete song lasts about 52 seconds. Rules regarding respect for the national anthem are outlined in the Indian Constitution and Supreme Court directives.
qs.kf:
☛ Writer of national anthem → Rabindranath Tagore
☛ Language of national anthem → Bengali (original), Hindi version also accepted
☛ Duration of national anthem → about 52 seconds
☛ First sung on → December 27, 1911
☛ Adopted by Constituent Assembly on → January 24, 1950

q: In which year was the 42nd Amendment came into force to the Constitution of India?
qs.e: The 42nd Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in 1976 during the Indira Gandhi government. It is often called the 'Mini-Constitution'. This amendment added Socialist, Secular, and Integrity to the Preamble. It also introduced Fundamental Duties (Part IV A) and established the supremacy of Parliament over the judiciary. The President was made bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers. The amendment strengthened the Centre in Centre-State relations.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the 42nd Amendment enacted? → 1976
☛ Which three words were added to the Preamble? → Socialist, Secular, Integrity
☛ Which amendment added Fundamental Duties? → 42nd Amendment
☛ Which government passed the 42nd Amendment? → Indira Gandhi government
☛ What is the 42nd Amendment also called? → Mini-Constitution

q: In the Indian Constitution, in the case of public employment, the provision for equality of opportunity has been done for whom?
o: For the citizens of the neighboring country
qs.e: Article 16 of the Indian Constitution provides equality of opportunity in matters of public employment for all citizens. It ensures that no citizen shall be disqualified or discriminated against solely on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, or residence. The state is also empowered under Article 16(4) to make reservations for backward classes. This right is restricted to Indian citizens and does not apply to foreigners or aliens. The provision aims to promote fairness and equal opportunity in the public sector, preventing arbitrary discrimination.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article deals with equality of opportunity in public employment? → Article 16
☛ Who is eligible for equality of opportunity under Article 16? → All Indian citizens
☛ What grounds are prohibited for discrimination in public employment? → Religion, caste, sex, etc.
☛ Can the state provide reservations for backward classes? → Yes, under Article 16(4)
☛ Which Part of the Constitution contains Article 16? → Part III (Fundamental Rights)

q: Which of the following languages in India is not the official language of any state?
qs.e: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution recognizes 22 languages, but Khasi is not among them and is not the official language of any state. Khasi is primarily spoken in Meghalaya, but the state's official language is English. In contrast, Punjabi is the official language of Punjab, Gujarati of Gujarat, and Oriya (now Odia) of Odisha. Thus, Khasi is the only option that is not the official language of any Indian state.
qs.kf:
☛ Which language is not recognized in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution? → Khasi
☛ What is the official language of Meghalaya? → English
☛ What is the official language of Punjab? → Punjabi
☛ What is the official language of Gujarat? → Gujarati
☛ What is the official language of Odisha? → Odia (Oriya)

q: Which emergency is called a constitutional emergency?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution provides for three types of emergencies. Among them, State Emergency (Article 356) is called a constitutional emergency because it is imposed when the constitutional machinery fails in a state. National Emergency (Article 352) is imposed due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. Financial Emergency (Article 360) is imposed during financial instability. State Emergency is also known as President's Rule. Under this, the state government is dismissed, and the administration comes under the control of the President. This emergency relates to the federal structure of the Constitution.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 352 → National Emergency
☛ Article 356 → State Emergency
☛ Article 360 → Financial Emergency
☛ Another name for State Emergency → President's Rule
☛ Grounds for National Emergency → War, external aggression, armed rebellion

q: The governor of a state can also act as the governor of another state. In this constitution, which provision was added by the Constitution Amendment Act?
qs.e: Article 153 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Governor for each state. The 7th Constitution Amendment Act, 1956 added a provision to Article 153 allowing a person to be appointed as Governor of more than one state. This amendment was introduced after the reorganization of states to provide flexibility in appointing Governors for smaller states. Thus, a Governor can also act as the Governor of another state. This provision was made to simplify the federal structure.
qs.kf:
☛ Who appoints the Governor? → President
☛ What is the term of the Governor? → 5 years (at the pleasure of President)
☛ Which Article deals with the Governor? → Article 153
☛ Which amendment allowed one person to be Governor of multiple states? → 7th Constitution Amendment (1956)
☛ Who administers the oath to the Governor? → Chief Justice of the High Court

q: When was the national anthem of India adopted?
qs.e: The national anthem of India, 'Jana Gana Mana', was officially adopted by the Constituent Assembly on January 24, 1950. It was originally written in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore, and later its Hindi version was adopted. On the same day, 'Vande Mataram' was given the status of the national song. This date is two days before India became a republic on January 26, 1950, when the Constitution came into effect. The prescribed duration for singing the national anthem is approximately 52 seconds.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the composer of the national anthem? → Rabindranath Tagore
☛ What is the original language of the national anthem? → Bengali
☛ What is the national song of India? → Vande Mataram
☛ What is the duration of the national anthem? → Approximately 52 seconds
☛ On which date was the national anthem adopted? → January 24, 1950

q: By which constitution amendment the word 'secular' was added in the preamble of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The word 'secular' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitution Amendment Act, 1976. This amendment is also known as the 'Mini-Constitution'. It added the words 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble. Before this, the Preamble only contained the words 'sovereign', 'democratic', 'republic'. The 42nd Amendment also added the Fundamental Duties and altered the powers of the judiciary. This amendment was passed during the Emergency period under the government of Indira Gandhi.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added the word 'socialist' to the Preamble? → 42nd Constitution Amendment
☛ What is the 42nd Amendment known as? → Mini-Constitution
☛ When was the word 'integrity' added to the Preamble? → 1976 by the 42nd Amendment
☛ Which amendment added Fundamental Duties? → 42nd Constitution Amendment
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during the 42nd Amendment? → Indira Gandhi

q: What amendment was made by the Panchayati Raj system?
qs.e: The 73rd Amendment (1992) to the Indian Constitution relates to the Panchayati Raj system. It added Part IX and Articles 243 to 243-O. This amendment gives constitutional status to Gram Panchayats, Block Panchayats, and District Panchayats. It provides for reservation for women and Scheduled Castes/Tribes. The 74th Amendment deals with urban local bodies (municipalities). The 73rd Amendment is the foundation of democratic decentralization in rural India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the 73rd Amendment enacted? → 24 April 1992
☛ What is the three-tier structure of Panchayati Raj? → Village, Block, District
☛ Percentage of reservation for women in Panchayats? → At least 33%
☛ Tenure of Panchayats? → 5 years
☛ Which schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment? → 11th Schedule

q: Part II of Indian Constitution is associated with ______.
qs.e: Part II of the Indian Constitution (Articles 5-11) deals with Citizenship. It defines citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution, rights of citizenship, and the rights of foreign citizens. Articles 5 to 8 grant citizenship to persons born in India, of Indian parentage, or those who migrated from Pakistan. Article 9 terminates Indian citizenship if a person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country. Article 10 ensures the continuation of citizenship rights, while Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law. This part forms the basis of the Citizenship Act, 1955, which further elaborates on the acquisition and termination of citizenship. The provisions ensure clarity on who is a citizen of India at the start and how future citizenship matters will be handled.
qs.kf:
☛ Constitutional part dealing with citizenship → Part II
☛ Articles related to citizenship → 5-11
☛ Citizenship Act enacted in which year → 1955
☛ Article 9 deals with → Voluntary renunciation of citizenship
☛ Article 11 empowers → Parliament to make citizenship laws

q: How many languages are there in the eighth schedule of our Constitution?
qs.e: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution originally listed 14 languages. Through amendments, Sindhi was added in 1967, Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali in 1992, and Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali in 2004. Currently, there are 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule. These languages are recognized for official purposes but do not replace Hindi as the official language of the Union. The schedule aims to preserve linguistic diversity and promote regional languages. It does not imply that all languages are official at the national level; instead, they are entitled to representation and promotion.
qs.kf:
☛ Which are the latest languages added to the Eighth Schedule? → Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali (2004)
☛ When was Sindhi added? → 1967 (21st Amendment)
☛ Which amendments added languages? → 21st, 71st, and 92nd Amendments
☛ Which schedule lists the languages? → Eighth Schedule
☛ How many languages were originally in the Eighth Schedule? → 14

q: Which of the following Articles of our Constitution relates to the proclamation to be issued by the President in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a state?
qs.e: Article 356 of the Indian Constitution deals with the proclamation issued by the President in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a state, also known as President's Rule or state emergency. Under this article, if the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution, he can assume control over the administration of the state. This is distinct from Article 352 (national emergency) and Article 360 (financial emergency). Article 312 relates to All India Services, while Article 249 empowers Parliament to legislate on subjects in the State List.
qs.kf:
☛ Article dealing with failure of constitutional machinery in a state → Article 356
☛ Article dealing with national emergency → Article 352
☛ Article dealing with financial emergency → Article 360
☛ Article dealing with All India Services → Article 312
☛ Article empowering Parliament to legislate on State List subjects → Article 249

q: Which of the following states does NOT have bicameral legislature?
qs.e: In India, states with bicameral legislature have a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) as the upper house. Currently, only 6 states have a bicameral system: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh. Tamilnadu abolished its Legislative Council in 1986 and has been unicameral since then. Therefore, Tamilnadu does NOT have a bicameral legislature. Karnataka, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh still have an active Legislative Council.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of states with bicameral legislature → 6
☛ Newest state to have Legislative Council → Andhra Pradesh (restored in 2007)
☛ State that abolished Legislative Council → Tamilnadu (1986)
☛ Union Territory with bicameral legislature → None
☛ Article in Constitution → Article 169 (creation and abolition of Legislative Council)

q: The word ''secular'' was inserted into Constitution of India by the _______ Amendment Act.
qs.e: The words 'secular' and 'socialist' were inserted into the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. This amendment was passed during the Emergency period (1975-77) under the government of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. It changed the description of India from 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' to 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic' and also replaced 'unity of the Nation' with 'unity and integrity of the Nation'. The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'Mini-Constitution' due to its extensive changes, which included alterations to Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and the powers of the judiciary and executive. It is one of the most significant amendments in Indian constitutional history.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the 42nd Amendment enacted? → 1976
☛ Which word was added along with 'secular' in the Preamble? → Socialist
☛ Under which Prime Minister was the 42nd Amendment passed? → Indira Gandhi
☛ What is the 42nd Amendment commonly called? → Mini-Constitution
☛ How many times has the Preamble been amended? → Once (by the 42nd Amendment)

q: With which of the following is Mandal Commission report associated?
qs.e: The Mandal Commission was established in 1979 by the Government of India, headed by B.P. Mandal. Its primary objective was to identify socially and educationally backward classes (OBC). The report was submitted in 1980, identifying 3,743 castes as backward and recommending 27% reservation in government jobs. The recommendations were implemented in 1990 by Prime Minister V.P. Singh. This commission is not related to economic reforms, Panchayati Raj, or human rights; it is specifically associated with the upliftment of backward classes.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Mandal Commission established? → 1979
☛ Which Prime Minister implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations? → V.P. Singh
☛ For which class did the Mandal Commission recommend reservation? → OBC (Other Backward Classes)
☛ What percentage of reservation did the Mandal Commission recommend in government jobs? → 27%
☛ Who was the chairman of the Mandal Commission? → B.P. Mandal

q: Through which Constitutional Amendment was the Nagarpalika Bill passed?
qs.e: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 grants constitutional status to municipalities in India. This amendment added Part IX-A (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG) to the Constitution. It was enacted to strengthen urban local self-government. The amendment provides for the constitution of Nagar Nigams (for metropolitan areas), Nagar Palikas (for smaller cities), and Nagar Panchayats (for transitional areas). The 74th Amendment sets rules for municipal elections, tenure, ward committees, and financial powers. In contrast, the 73rd Amendment relates to Panchayati Raj institutions. The 70th and 72nd Amendments deal with other subjects. Hence, the Nagarpalika Bill was passed through the 74th Amendment.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment relates to municipalities? → 74th Amendment
☛ Which amendment relates to Panchayati Raj? → 73rd Amendment
☛ What is the year of the 74th Amendment? → 1992
☛ Which part was added by the 74th Amendment? → Part IX-A (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG)
☛ Articles 243-P in 74th Amendment deal with? → Definitions and types of municipalities

q: The term "Fourth Estate" is used for -
qs.e: The term Fourth Estate is used for the press and newspaper. It signifies the independent and watchdog role of media in a democracy. In addition to the three traditional branches of government— Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary—the media is considered the fourth estate. Its function is to scrutinize government actions, inform the public, and shape public opinion. The media is regarded as the watchdog of democracy.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the Fourth Estate? → The press and newspaper
☛ What are the four pillars of democracy? → Executive, Legislature, Judiciary, and Press
☛ Where did the term Fourth Estate originate? → Western political thought
☛ What is the role of the press called? → Watchdog
☛ Which article guarantees press freedom in India? → Article 19(1) (a)

q: Who was the President of India at the time of proclamation of emergency in 1975?
qs.e: At the time of the proclamation of emergency in 1975, the President of India was Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed. He served as President from 1974 to 1977. On 25 June 1975, on the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, he signed the proclamation of emergency under Article 352 of the Constitution. This was the first and only national emergency in India's history. During this period, fundamental rights were suspended and press censorship was imposed. Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was the fifth President of India. He also served as the President of the Asian Football Confederation.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which article was emergency proclaimed in 1975? → Article 352
☛ Who was the Prime Minister at that time? → Indira Gandhi
☛ When did the emergency end? → 21 March 1977
☛ Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed's term as President? → 1974–1977
☛ Which number President was he? → Fifth

q: Can a person be a member of both Houses?
qs.e: According to Article 101 of the Indian Constitution, a person cannot be a member of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) simultaneously. If a person is elected to both Houses, they must resign from one. This provision ensures efficiency and accountability in the functioning of Parliament. This rule applies even during a national emergency or financial emergency, with no exceptions. The principle is also reflected in Articles 102 and 103, which deal with disqualification of membership. Thus, dual membership of both Houses is not permitted. The intention is to prevent conflicts of interest and maintain the integrity of the legislative process. Therefore, the correct answer is 'No'—a person cannot be a member of both Houses at the same time.
qs.kf:
☛ Can a person be a member of both Houses simultaneously? → No, Article 101 prohibits it.
☛ What must a person do if elected to both Houses? → Resign from one House.
☛ Article 101 deals with: → Vacation of seats in Parliament.
☛ Article 102 deals with: → Disqualifications for membership.
☛ Is dual membership allowed during an emergency? → No, no exceptions exist.

q: How long did the first national emergency declared in October 1962 last?
qs.e: The first national emergency in India was declared in October 1962 due to the India-China war. It was proclaimed by the President under Article 352 and continued until the security situation normalized. The emergency was finally revoked in January 1968, lasting about 5 years. During this period, the central government gained extensive powers, and fundamental rights were suspended. This emergency is a significant event in Indian history as it was the first time such a measure was invoked since independence. It also set precedents for the use of emergency powers in later years.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first national emergency declared? → October 1962
☛ Which war caused the first national emergency? → India-China war
☛ Under which article was the first national emergency imposed? → Article 352
☛ When was the first national emergency revoked? → January 1968
☛ Who was Prime Minister during the first national emergency? → Jawaharlal Nehru (initially)

q: The Indian constitution provides for _______.
qs.e: The Indian Constitution provides for single citizenship, meaning all citizens have a uniform citizenship across the entire country. This differs from federal countries like the USA, which have dual citizenship (state and national). The provisions for citizenship are covered in Part II (Articles 5-11) of the Indian Constitution. Single citizenship promotes national unity and prevents discrimination between states. It ensures that all citizens enjoy equal rights throughout the country. Unlike some federal nations, India does not have separate citizenship for states, thus strengthening the idea of one nation.
qs.kf:
☛ In which part of the Indian Constitution is citizenship described? → Part II (Articles 5-11)
☛ What type of citizenship does India have? → Single citizenship
☛ Which country has dual citizenship? → USA
☛ Under which article can Parliament make laws regarding citizenship? → Article 11
☛ When was the Citizenship Act of India passed? → 1955

q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the 9th Schedule to the Constitution?
qs.e: The 9th Schedule of the Indian Constitution was added by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951. This schedule included laws related to land reforms and farmer welfare to protect them from judicial review. The 1st Amendment amended the Right to Property under Article 31 and introduced Articles 31A and 31B. Laws in the 9th Schedule could not be challenged in courts initially. However, the Supreme Court later ruled that laws in the 9th Schedule are subject to judicial review if they violate fundamental rights, as established in the I.R. Coelho case (2007). This amendment was crucial soon after the Constitution's adoption to safeguard social and economic reforms.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the 1st Constitutional Amendment passed? → 1951
☛ What type of laws are included in the 9th Schedule? → Land reforms and farmer welfare laws
☛ Which articles were added by the 1st Amendment? → Articles 31A and 31B
☛ Which case allowed judicial review of 9th Schedule laws? → I.R. Coelho case (2007)
☛ Which schedule was added by the 1st Amendment? → 9th Schedule

q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the 10th Schedule to the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The 10th Schedule was added to the Indian Constitution by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985, also known as the 'Anti-Defection Law'. This Schedule lays down provisions for disqualification of members of Parliament and state legislatures on grounds of defection, i.e., voluntarily giving up party membership or disobeying the party whip. The amendment also modified Article 102 and Article 191 of the Constitution. Later, the 91st Amendment Act of 2003 further strengthened the anti-defection provisions. The 64th, 61st, and 48th Amendment Acts dealt with other issues.
qs.kf:
☛ Anti-Defection Law → Added by 52nd Amendment (1985)
☛ 10th Schedule deals with → Disqualification of MPs/MLAs
☛ 10th Schedule amended by → 91st Amendment (2003)
☛ Authority to decide defection → Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman)
☛ Prime Minister during 52nd Amendment → Rajiv Gandhi

q: Article 45 (concerning child education) was modified by which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts?
qs.e: Article 45 originally in the Directive Principles of State Policy directed the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children until the age of 14. The 86th Amendment (2002) made education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A for children aged 6-14. It modified Article 45 to focus on early childhood care and education for children below 6 years. Additionally, it added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k) for parents to provide education opportunities to their children. This amendment was a landmark step towards realizing the goal of universal elementary education in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article provides Right to Education? → Article 21A
☛ Which new Fundamental Duty was added by 86th Amendment? → Article 51A(k)
☛ Original Article 45 covered which age group? → 0-14 years
☛ After 86th Amendment, Article 45 covers which age group? → 0-6 years
☛ Which other Article is related to child education? → Article 21A

q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts had abolished the privy purse and privileges of the former rulers of the princely states?
qs.e: The 26th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, enacted in 1971, abolished the privy purse and privileges of the former rulers of princely states. It removed Articles 291 and 362 from the Constitution and amended Article 366 to delete the definition of 'princely state'. This amendment was a major step towards social justice and equality, ending the special status and payments given to former rulers. The Bill was introduced as the 31st Constitutional Amendment Bill. The privy purse was an annual sum paid to rulers as a condition for their integration into India.
qs.kf:
☛ Articles removed by 26th Amendment → Articles 291 and 362
☛ Year of abolition of privy purse → 1971
☛ Purpose of 26th Amendment → Ending privileges of former rulers
☛ Privy purse amount was determined by → The President
☛ Government that passed the 26th Amendment → Indira Gandhi's government

q: Which Constitutional Amendment allows the same person to be appointed as the Governor of two or more states?
qs.e: The 7th Amendment (1956) to the Indian Constitution is related to the reorganization of states. It amended Article 153 to allow the same person to be appointed as Governor of two or more states. This provision improved administrative efficiency and reduced the number of governors. The amendment was based on the recommendations of the States Reorganization Commission, which formed states on linguistic basis. This change helped in better coordination and utilization of resources.
qs.kf:
☛ Amendment allowing one person to be Governor of two states → 7th Amendment (1956)
☛ Article amended by 7th Amendment → Article 153
☛ Who appoints the Governor → President
☛ Term of Governor → 5 years (at pleasure of President)
☛ States Reorganization Commission formed in → 1953

q: Which Amendment introduced the Anti-Defection Law in the Indian Constitution, aiming to prevent elected members from switching parties?
qs.e: The Anti-Defection Law was introduced in the Indian Constitution by the 52nd Amendment in 1985. This law aims to prevent elected members from switching parties. Under this law, a member can be disqualified if they voluntarily give up party membership or vote against party directions. The decision is made by the Presiding Officer (Speaker or Chairman). The amendment added the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution, which contains disqualification provisions. The objective of this law is to maintain political stability and curb corrupt practices.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Anti-Defection Law enacted? → 1985
☛ Which Schedule was added by this Amendment? → Tenth Schedule
☛ Who decides the disqualification? → Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman)
☛ Which Amendment strengthened the Anti-Defection Law? → 91st Amendment (2003)
☛ What is the objective of the Anti-Defection Law? → To maintain political stability

q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts made Sikkim a full-fledged state of India?
qs.e: The 36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975 was enacted to make Sikkim a full-fledged state of India. Previously, Sikkim was a protectorate state under Indian suzerainty. This amendment inserted Article 371F into the Constitution, containing special provisions for the state of Sikkim. Sikkim became the 22nd state of India on 26 April 1975.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Sikkim incorporated into India? → 26 April 1975
☛ Which number state did Sikkim become? → 22nd state
☛ Which Article has special provisions for Sikkim? → Article 371F
☛ What was Sikkim's earlier status? → Protectorate state
☛ When was the 36th Amendment passed? → 1975

q: The 9th Amendment Act, 1960, made adjustments to the Indian territory due to an agreement with which country?
qs.e: The 9th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution was enacted in 1960 to implement an agreement between India and Pakistan regarding the exchange of certain territories. This agreement, often referred to as the Nehru-Noon Minto Agreement or the Pakistan Border Agreement, aimed to resolve border disputes along the western frontier. Under the pact, India ceded some territories to Pakistan in exchange for others, primarily concerning the Berubari region and Hussainiwala Headworks. The amendment made necessary changes to the First and Fourth Schedules of the Constitution to give effect to the territorial adjustments.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the 9th Amendment Act of India passed? → 1960
☛ With which country was the territorial adjustment made through the 9th Amendment? → Pakistan
☛ The Nehru-Noon Minto Agreement is related to which border? → India-Pakistan border
☛ Which region is associated with the 9th Amendment? → Berubari
☛ Which schedules were amended by the 9th Amendment? → First and Fourth Schedules

q: By which of the following Amendment Acts was Article 21(A) inserted in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: Article 21(A) was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002. This article provides free and compulsory education as a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years. The amendment added Article 21(A) after the original Article 21 and also modified Article 45 and inserted Article 51A(k). The Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 was enacted under this article to enforce it.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added Right to Education as a Fundamental Right? → 86th Amendment Act, 2002
☛ What is the age group for free education under Article 21A? → 6 to 14 years
☛ Which act implements the Right to Education in India? → RTE Act, 2009
☛ Which article was added by 86th Amendment regarding parental duty? → Article 51A(k)
☛ Before 86th Amendment, under which Directive Principle was education a right? → Article 45

q: The 95th Amendment Act of 2009 extended the reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for which categories of citizens?
qs.e: The 95th Amendment Act of 2009 extended the reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) for a further period of ten years, from 2010 to 2020. Originally, this reservation was intended for 70 years (1950-2020), but was earlier extended by the 79th Amendment in 1999. This constitutional amendment is governed by Article 330 (for Lok Sabha) and Article 332 (for State Assemblies). The purpose is to ensure adequate political representation for SC/ST communities. The 95th Amendment continued the reservation that was set to expire in 2010.
qs.kf:
☛ 95th Amendment Year → 2009
☛ Reservation Period → 2010 to 2020
☛ Applicable to → Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
☛ Related Articles → 330 and 332
☛ Previous Amendment → 79th (1999) and 23rd

q: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution states which of the following?
o: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats
Validation of certain Acts and Regulations
qs.e: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the official languages of India. It currently includes 22 languages: Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Sindhi, Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri. The Eighth Schedule provides official recognition and provisions for the development of these languages. Other options like powers of Panchayats (Eleventh Schedule), validation of certain Acts (Thirteenth Schedule), and forms of oaths or affirmations (Third Schedule) belong to different schedules.
qs.kf:
☛ How many languages are in the Eighth Schedule? → 22
☛ Latest added languages → Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri (2003)
☛ Main purpose of Eighth Schedule → Recognition of official languages
☛ What is in the Eleventh Schedule? → Powers of Panchayats
☛ What is in the Third Schedule? → Forms of oaths or affirmations

q: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with ____________.
o: administration and control of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes
qs.e: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It comes under Article 244(1) and empowers the Governor to modify or exempt laws in Scheduled Areas. The Sixth Schedule pertains to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Powers of Panchayats are covered by the 73rd Amendment (Article 243). Disqualification on ground of defection is in the Tenth Schedule. Provisions regarding languages are in the Eighth Schedule. The Fifth Schedule aims to protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes and ensure their welfare through special administrative measures.
qs.kf:
☛ Which states are under the Fifth Schedule? → Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, and Telangana.
☛ What is the main objective of the Fifth Schedule? → Protection of Scheduled Tribes' interests and administration of their areas.
☛ Who notifies Scheduled Areas? → The President of India.
☛ Under which article is the Tribal Advisory Council provided in the Fifth Schedule? → Article 244(1).
☛ What special power does the Governor have under the Fifth Schedule? → He can modify or exempt central or state laws in Scheduled Areas.

q: Which of the following Articles allows the State to make special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes?
qs.e: Article 15 of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. However, Article 15 (5) allows the State to make special provisions for Socio-Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC), including admission to educational institutions. This clause was inserted by the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005. It enables reservation in government and private educational institutions (excluding minority institutions). Article 14 deals with equality before law, Article 16 ensures equality of opportunity in public employment, and Article 17 abolishes untouchability.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added Article 15 (5)? → 93rd Constitutional Amendment (2005)
☛ For which classes does Article 15 (5) provide? → Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC)
☛ Which institutions are exempted from Article 15 (5)? → Minority educational institutions
☛ Article 15 (5) is related to? → Reservation in education
☛ Which article provides reservation in public employment? → Article 16 (4)

q: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi declared emergency on 25 June 1975, which lasted for _____ months.
qs.e: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi declared a state of emergency in India on 25 June 1975, which lasted for 21 months. The emergency was in effect from 25 June 1975 to 21 March 1977. It was imposed under Article 352 of the Constitution, which allows the President to declare emergency due to internal disturbance. During this period, civil liberties were suspended, press censorship was enforced, and opposition leaders were arrested. This period is considered one of the most controversial in Indian democratic history. The emergency ended after Indira Gandhi's government lost the 1977 general elections.
qs.kf:
☛ Emergency was imposed under which Article? → Article 352
☛ Who was the President during the Emergency? → Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed
☛ When were the first general elections held after the Emergency? → 1977
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during the Emergency? → Indira Gandhi
☛ How long did the Emergency last in months? → 21 months (approx. 639 days)

q: Which of the following Amendment Acts provided one-third reservation for women in municipalities?
qs.e: The Indian Constitution's 74th Amendment Act, 1992 deals with municipalities. It added Part IX‑A and Articles 243‑P to 243‑ZG to the Constitution. It provides for one-third (33%) reservation of seats for women in all municipalities, including seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The reservation also applies to the office of chairperson. The 73rd Amendment is related to Panchayati Raj institutions, while the 103rd Amendment provides reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). The 106th Amendment concerns women's reservation in Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. Hence, the amendment that provided one-third reservation for women in municipalities is the 74th Amendment Act.
qs.kf:
☛ Which part was added by the 74th Amendment? → Part IX‑A
☛ Which article provides women's reservation in municipalities? → Article 243‑T
☛ What does the 73rd Amendment relate to? → Panchayati Raj
☛ Which amendment provides reservation for EWS? → 103rd Amendment
☛ What does the 106th Amendment deal with? → Women's reservation in Lok Sabha and state assemblies

q: Which of the following Acts is also known as the Gagging Act?
qs.e: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 is also known as the 'Gagging Act'. It was enacted during the tenure of Lord Lytton. The purpose of this act was to impose restrictions on newspapers published in Indian languages to suppress criticism of the government. Under this act, the English press was exempted while Indian language publications faced severe curbs. It was a repressive law that curbed press freedom. Later, Lord Ripon repealed it in 1881.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name of Gagging Act → Vernacular Press Act, 1878
☛ Introduced by → Lord Lytton
☛ Applied to → Indian language newspapers
☛ Repealed by → Lord Ripon in 1881
☛ Objective → Suppress criticism of the government

q: Which of the following Articles was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976?
qs.e: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, also known as the 'Mini-Constitution', made several significant changes to the Indian Constitution. By this Act, Article 31D was added, which relates to judicial review. This article imposes restrictions on judicial review in cases concerning Public Service Commissions or members of Public Service Commissions. Regarding the other options, Article 101 deals with the vacation of seats in Parliament, Article 22 deals with preventive detention, and Article 31 deals with the right to property. None of these were added by the 42nd Amendment. Hence, the correct answer is Article 31D.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article was added by the 42nd Amendment 1976 → Article 31D
☛ What is the 42nd Amendment known as → Mini-Constitution
☛ Which article was added for Fundamental Duties by the 42nd Amendment → Article 51A
☛ Which words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment → Socialist, Secular
☛ Which article imposes restrictions on judicial review under the 42nd Amendment → Article 31D

q: Under which Act were Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs) established?
o: The Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act (RDB Act), 1993
qs.e: Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs) were established under the Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act (RDB Act), 1993. This act was enacted to expedite the recovery of debts due to banks and financial institutions. DRTs are constituted across India to adjudicate debt disputes involving amounts of ₹20 lakh or more. Later, in 2016, the act was amended and renamed as the 'Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act' after merging with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The SARFAESI Act, 2002, is a separate legislation dealing with securitization and reconstruction of financial assets.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Act are DRTs established? → RDB Act, 1993
☛ What is the minimum debt amount for DRT jurisdiction? → ₹20 lakh
☛ When was the RDB Act amended? → 2016
☛ When was the SARFAESI Act enacted? → 2002
☛ Who is responsible for establishing DRTs? → Central Government

q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts has NOT inserted any Directive Principles of State Policy?
qs.e: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions but did not introduce any new Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). In contrast, the 42nd Amendment (1976) added four new DPSPs: Article 39A (equal justice), 43A (participation in industry management), 46 (protection of SCs), and 48A (environment protection). The 44th Amendment (1978) amended Article 43. The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A (right to education), which is a fundamental right, but also amended Article 45 (child education), which is a DPSP. Thus, only the 73rd Amendment does not relate to DPSP.
qs.kf:
☛ DPSPs added by 42nd Amendment → Articles 39A, 43A, 46, 48A
☛ DPSP related to 86th Amendment → Article 45 (child education)
☛ DPSP affected by 44th Amendment → Article 43 (amended)
☛ Main objective of 73rd Amendment → Constitutionalization of Panchayati Raj
☛ Total number of DPSPs in India → 25 (Articles 36-51)

q: The 36th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, 1975, incorporated which of the following as a part of India?
qs.e: The 36th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, 1975, was enacted to make Sikkim a full-fledged state of India. This Act inserted Article 371F in the Constitution, which contains special provisions for Sikkim. Sikkim became the 22nd state of India on May 16, 1975. Earlier, Sikkim was a protectorate state, and after a referendum in 1975, it merged with India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the 36th Amendment related to? → Making Sikkim a full state of India
☛ Which number state did Sikkim become? → 22nd state
☛ When did Sikkim join India? → May 16, 1975
☛ In which year was the 36th Amendment passed? → 1975
☛ Which special Article was added for Sikkim? → Article 371F

q: In which year was the 42nd Amendment in the Indian Constitution passed?
qs.e: The 42nd Amendment to the Indian Constitution was passed in 1976 during the government of Indira Gandhi. It is known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because it brought numerous changes to the basic structure of the Constitution. This amendment added the words socialist, secular, and integrity to the Preamble. It also introduced Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A). It attempted to limit judicial review and enhanced the power of Parliament. The amendment was enacted during the Emergency period (1975-77).
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment is called the 'Mini-Constitution'? → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ Which amendment added 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble? → 42nd Amendment
☛ Which amendment introduced Fundamental Duties? → 42nd Amendment
☛ Under which Prime Minister was the 42nd Amendment passed? → Indira Gandhi
☛ Which amendment enhanced the power of Parliament? → 42nd Amendment

q: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is constituted under which Article?
qs.e: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) is constituted under Article 338 of the Indian Constitution. This constitutional body is established for the welfare and protection of the rights of Scheduled Castes. Its primary function is to monitor the constitutional and legal safeguards provided to Scheduled Castes and review their implementation. Article 338B pertains to the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes. Article 349 and 348A deal with other subjects. The commission is an independent body that submits annual reports to the Parliament.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article is NCSC constituted? → Article 338
☛ Under which Article is NCST constituted? → Article 338B
☛ Who appoints the chairperson of NCSC? → President
☛ To whom does NCSC submit reports? → Parliament
☛ How many members are in NCSC? → Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and five members

q: The Official Language Commission is governed by which Article of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Official Language Commission is constituted under Article 344 of the Indian Constitution. This article empowers the President to appoint a Commission on Official Language. The Commission's role is to make recommendations regarding the use of Hindi for official purposes, review the use of English, and suggest measures for the progressive use of Hindi. The composition and tenure of the Commission are determined by the President. This provision falls under Part 17 of the Constitution titled 'Official Language'. Article 345 deals with official languages of states but not the Commission. Thus, Article 344 is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Article is the Official Language Commission formed? → Article 344
☛ Who appoints the Official Language Commission? → President
☛ What is the main function of the Official Language Commission? → To make recommendations on official language
☛ In which Part of the Constitution is the Official Language Commission provision? → Part 17
☛ What does Article 344 pertain to? → Official Language Commission

q: Which part of the Indian Constitution, added by the 42nd Amendment, deals with tribunals?
qs.e: Part XIV-A of the Indian Constitution was added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. This part deals with Tribunals and contains two articles: Article 323A (Administrative Tribunals) and Article 323B (Tribunals for other matters). Article 323A empowers Parliament to establish Administrative Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes related to the recruitment and service conditions of central and state government employees. Article 323B allows state governments to establish tribunals for matters such as taxation, land reforms, industrial disputes, etc. This part was introduced to ensure speedy justice in government-related cases.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added Part XIV-A? → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ How many articles are in Part XIV-A? → 2 (Articles 323A and 323B)
☛ Which article deals with Administrative Tribunals? → Article 323A
☛ What does Article 323B deal with? → Tribunals for other matters
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during the 42nd Amendment? → Indira Gandhi

q: The Constitution (Jammu and Kashmir) Scheduled Tribes Order (Amendment) Bill, 2024, passed by the Parliament, aimed to include how many communities in the list of STs of the UT of Jammu and Kashmir?
qs.e: The Constitution (Jammu and Kashmir) Scheduled Tribes Order (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was passed by the Parliament. This bill aims to include 4 communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. These communities are Gaddi, Bakarwal, Sippi, and Pahari. Previously, these communities did not have Scheduled Tribe status. With the passage of this bill, these communities will benefit from reservations in government jobs, education, and other welfare schemes. This is a significant step towards the social and economic upliftment of the tribal communities in Jammu and Kashmir.
qs.kf:
☛ How many new communities were added to the ST list of Jammu and Kashmir? → 4
☛ What are the names of these 4 communities? → Gaddi, Bakarwal, Sippi, and Pahari
☛ In which year was this bill passed? → 2024
☛ Under which article was this amendment made? → Article 342
☛ How many ST communities existed earlier in Jammu and Kashmir? → 5

q: Right of parliament to regulate the citizenship by law is mentioned in which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: Article 11 of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law. This article grants Parliament the authority to legislate on the acquisition, termination, and other rules of citizenship. Article 10 deals with the continuance of the rights of citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution, while Article 9 provides for termination of citizenship upon voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign state. Article 11 is the final article of Part II (Citizenship) and enables Parliament to enact laws like the Citizenship Act, 1955. This article is significant as it ensures that citizenship rules are governed by parliamentary legislation rather than being solely based on constitutional provisions. It gives flexibility to the legislature to modify citizenship laws as per changing circumstances.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article gives Parliament the power to regulate citizenship by law? → Article 11
☛ What does Article 10 deal with? → Continuance of citizenship rights at the commencement of the Constitution
☛ What does Article 9 relate to? → Termination of citizenship on acquiring foreign citizenship
☛ How many articles are in Part II? → Articles 5 to 11
☛ When was the Citizenship Act enacted? → 1955

q: Which Amendment of the Indian Constitution introduced the concept of 'Panchayat Raj' in India?
qs.e: The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX (The Panchayats) to the Constitution of India, providing constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions. It introduced Articles 243 to 243O, establishing a three-tier system of rural local self-government: Gram Panchayat, Block Panchayat, and District Panchayat. The amendment mandates elections every five years and reserves seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women. It also includes the 11th Schedule with 29 subjects that can be transferred to local bodies. This amendment came into effect on 24 April 1993, marking a historic step towards decentralized democracy.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the 73rd Amendment come into force? → 24 April 1993
☛ How many tiers are in the Panchayati Raj system? → Three tiers (village, intermediate, district)
☛ What is the term of a Panchayat? → 5 years
☛ How many subjects are in the 11th Schedule? → 29 subjects
☛ Under which Article is Gram Sabha defined? → Article 243A

q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added Article 371A, granting special status to Nagaland?
qs.e: The 13th Amendment Act, 1962 added Article 371A to the Indian Constitution, granting special status to Nagaland. This amendment restricts the application of laws passed by Parliament in matters of religious or social practices, Naga customary law and procedure, and ownership and transfer of land and resources in Nagaland. It was enacted before Nagaland became a full-fledged state on 1 December 1963. The special provisions aim to preserve the cultural and social identity of the Naga tribes. Article 371A provides that no act of Parliament applies to Nagaland in these matters unless the state's Legislative Assembly decides by a resolution to adopt it.
qs.kf:
☛ Constitutional amendment that added Article 371A → 13th Amendment (1962)
☛ When did Nagaland achieve statehood → 1 December 1963
☛ Article 371A is for which state → Nagaland
☛ Areas protected under Article 371A → Religious practices, Naga customary law, land & resource ownership
☛ Year of 13th Amendment → 1962

q: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years in India?
qs.e: The Constitution (61st Amendment) Act, 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years. It amended Article 326, which determines the eligibility to vote in elections to the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies. The objective was to give the youth a voice in the political process. This amendment was passed during the tenure of Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and came into effect before the 9th Lok Sabha elections in 1989. The 61st Amendment was a significant change in India's democratic framework, expanding the electorate and increasing youth participation.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum voting age in India → 18 years
☛ Amendment that reduced voting age → 61st Amendment, 1988
☛ Purpose of reducing voting age → To give political participation to youth
☛ Article related to voting age reduction → Article 326
☛ Prime Minister during 61st Amendment → Rajiv Gandhi

q: ‘The state shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment’ is a Directive Principle of State Policy inserted by the _____ of the Indian Constitution.
qs.e: The phrase 'The state shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment' was inserted as Article 48-A into the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976. This Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) was added along with Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A), which includes the duty of every citizen to protect the environment. The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'Mini-Constitution' because it made extensive changes to the Constitution, including adding the words 'socialist', 'secular', and 'integrity' to the Preamble.
qs.kf:
☛ Article related to environmental protection → 48-A (State's duty)
☛ Environment in Fundamental Duties → Article 51-A(g)
☛ Year of 42nd Amendment → 1976
☛ Government that enacted 42nd Amendment → Indira Gandhi's government
☛ Words added by 42nd Amendment in Preamble → Socialist, Secular, Integrity

q: How many Fundamental Duties were inserted in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act?
qs.e: Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. Based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, a new Part IV-A and Article 51-A were inserted. Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties. Later, the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added one more duty (providing educational opportunities to children aged 6-14), making the total 11. However, the question asks about the number inserted by the 42nd Amendment, which was originally 10. These duties remind citizens of their obligations towards the nation and balance the Fundamental Rights.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added Fundamental Duties? → 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976
☛ Which Article contains Fundamental Duties? → Article 51-A
☛ Which duty was added by the 86th Amendment? → Opportunity for education to children aged 6-14
☛ Swaran Singh Committee gave its report in which year? → 1976
☛ How many Fundamental Duties are there now? → 11 (10 original + 1 added later)

q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts had added the Ninth Schedule to the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Indian Constitution by the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951. This schedule was created to protect land reform and other socio-economic laws from judicial review. Acts included in this schedule cannot be challenged in courts. The First Amendment also added Articles 31A and 31B, and amended Article 19(1)(g). It was passed under the leadership of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. Over time, many other laws have been added to the Ninth Schedule.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment added the Ninth Schedule? → First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951
☛ Which articles were added by the First Amendment? → Articles 31A and 31B
☛ What kind of laws are placed in the Ninth Schedule? → Land reform and agricultural laws
☛ What was the purpose of the Ninth Schedule? → Protection from judicial review
☛ When was the First Amendment passed? → 1951

q: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2024, aimed to make changes in the Scheduled Tribes of which state?
qs.e: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced to amend the list of Scheduled Tribes in the state of Andhra Pradesh. The aim was to add or modify certain communities in the Scheduled Tribes list of the state. This bill amends the Presidential orders issued under Article 342 of the Constitution, which defines the identification of Scheduled Tribes. The bill was significant for clarifying the status of various tribal communities in Andhra Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article deals with Scheduled Tribes identification? → Article 342
☛ Who issues the Scheduled Tribes Order? → President of India
☛ Which state does the 2024 Bill relate to? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Which bill amends the Scheduled Tribes list? → Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Amendment) Bill
☛ What is the capital of Andhra Pradesh? → Amaravati

q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts provides free legal aid as a Directive Principle of State Policy?
qs.e: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 brought several significant changes to the Indian Constitution. It added Article 39A to the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which directs the State to ensure that the legal system promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity and to provide free legal aid to ensure that no citizen is denied opportunities for securing justice due to economic or other disabilities. This amendment is also known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because it made extensive changes, including adding the words socialist, secular, and integrity to the Preamble. It also added the Fundamental Duties under Article 51A. The 42nd Amendment was enacted during the Emergency period and aimed at strengthening the central government.
qs.kf:
☛ Article related to free legal aid → 39A
☛ Words added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment → Socialist, Secular, Unity and Integrity
☛ Fundamental Duties added by the 42nd Amendment → Article 51A
☛ Year of the 42nd Amendment → 1976
☛ 42nd Amendment is also known as → Mini-Constitution

q: Which of the following Amendment Acts had the provision of establishing a common High Court for two or more states?
qs.e: The 7th Amendment Act, 1956 of the Indian Constitution was related to the reorganization of states and included a provision for establishing a common High Court for two or more states. This amendment was based on the recommendations of the States Reorganization Commission, which redrew state boundaries on a linguistic basis. It amended Articles 214 to 231, specifically adding Article 231 which allows for a common High Court for multiple states. Under this provision, a common High Court was established for Punjab and Haryana. This amendment aimed to enhance judicial efficiency and share resources. It was a significant step in the post-independence reorganization of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment facilitated the reorganization of states? → 7th Amendment
☛ Which Article provides for a common High Court for two or more states? → Article 231
☛ Example of a common High Court for two states? → For Punjab and Haryana
☛ When was the First Amendment Act passed? → 1950
☛ When was the 7th Amendment Act passed? → 1956

q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts has the land boundary agreement between India and Bangladesh?
qs.e: The 100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015 was enacted to implement the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh. This amendment modified the schedules of the Constitution to facilitate the exchange of border enclaves and territories, providing constitutional validity to the agreement. Under this agreement, India transferred 111 enclaves to Bangladesh and received 51 enclaves in return. This resolved the long-standing border dispute affecting over 50,000 stateless people and strengthened bilateral relations. The amendment was a historic step in India-Bangladesh relations.
qs.kf:
☛ Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) → Signed between India and Bangladesh in 1974
☛ 100th Amendment → Passed in 2015 to implement LBA
☛ Number of enclaves → India gave 111, received 51
☛ Beneficiaries → Over 50,000 border residents
☛ Constitutional changes → Amendments in Schedule 1 and 4

q: Which of the following communities may apply for Indian citizenship after just 6 years of residence, as per the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
qs.e: As per the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 (CAA), the residence requirement for Indian citizenship has been reduced from 11 years to 6 years for Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians facing religious persecution in Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh. The Act applies only to these three countries and six communities. Therefore, Sikhs from Pakistan are eligible to apply for citizenship after 6 years of residence. Other countries like Nepal, Sri Lanka, or Israel are not covered under this Act.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the residence period under CAA 2019? → 6 years
☛ Which countries are covered under CAA 2019? → Pakistan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh
☛ How many religious communities are covered under CAA 2019? → 6 (Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, Christians)
☛ What was the previous residence requirement before CAA 2019? → 11 years
☛ When was CAA 2019 passed? → 11 December 2019

q: For the development of cooperative societies, which part of the Constitution was amended through the 97th Amendment?
qs.e: The 97th Constitutional Amendment (2011) added Part IXB to the Constitution, dealing with cooperative societies. This amendment inserted Articles 243-ZH to 243-ZT, providing for the formation, operation, and management of cooperative societies. It also amended Article 19(1)(c) to include the right to form cooperative societies as a fundamental right. Part IXA relates to municipalities, and Part XI deals with center-state relations. This amendment gave constitutional protection to the cooperative sector, empowering states to legislate on cooperative societies and ensuring democratic functioning.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the 97th Amendment passed? → 2011
☛ How many articles are in Part IXB? → 243-ZH to 243-ZT
☛ Which article gives right to form cooperatives? → 19(1)(c)
☛ Part IXA relates to? → Municipalities
☛ Which entry in State List relates to cooperatives? → Entry 32

q: Which of the following Amendments clarified that the President must act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers?
qs.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) amended Article 74 of the Constitution to clarify that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers. Before this amendment, Article 74 stated that there shall be a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President, but it was not explicit whether the advice was binding. The 42nd Amendment made the advice binding. Later, the 44th Amendment (1978) allowed the President to send the advice back for reconsideration once, but after reconsideration, the advice is binding. The 24th Amendment (1971) dealt with the power to amend the Constitution, while the 74th Amendment (1992) is related to municipalities and urban local bodies.
qs.kf:
☛ Amendment that made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ Amendment that allowed the President to return advice for reconsideration → 44th Amendment (1978)
☛ Article 74 changed from 'aid and advise' to 'advise' by → 42nd Amendment
☛ Amendment that clarified the power to amend the Constitution → 24th Amendment (1971)
☛ Amendment that gave constitutional status to municipalities → 74th Amendment (1992)

q: How are the one-third reserved seats for women distributed across different categories in local bodies?
o: Only one-third of the general (unreserved) seats are reserved for women, excluding reserved-category seats.
One-third of all seats, including those reserved for SC/ST/OBC categories, are reserved for women, allowing a seat to be reserved simultaneously for a woman and for an SC/ST/OBC candidate.
One-third reservation applies only to leadership positions such as Sarpanch or Chairperson.
One-third reservation applies only to rural Panchayats and not to urban municipal bodies.
qs.e: Under the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, at least one-third of all seats in local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) are reserved for women. This includes seats already reserved for Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Other Backward Classes (OBC). Therefore, a single seat can be simultaneously reserved for a woman and a candidate from these categories. This reservation also extends to leadership positions like Sarpanch or Chairperson. The provision applies equally to rural and urban local bodies.
qs.kf:
☛ Constitutional basis for women's reservation → 73rd and 74th Amendments
☛ Scope of reservation → One-third of all seats (general + reserved)
☛ Example of simultaneous reservation → SC woman seat
☛ Reservation in leadership positions → At least one-third of Sarpanch/Chairperson posts for women
☛ Applicable areas → Both rural Panchayats and urban municipal bodies

q: According to the Citizenship Act, how many years must a person ordinarily reside in India to apply for citizenship by naturalisation under general conditions?
qs.e: According to Section 6 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, for citizenship by naturalisation under general conditions, a person must have ordinarily resided in India for at least 12 years. This includes 12 months immediately preceding the date of application and 11 years in the previous 14 years (total 12 years). This requirement applies to foreign nationals seeking Indian citizenship. Exceptions exist for persons of Indian origin (PIO), who need only 7 years. The 12-year period is a key condition in the naturalisation process, ensuring the applicant has sufficient connection to India.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum residence period for naturalisation → 12 years
☛ Section of Citizenship Act, 1955 → Section 6
☛ Residence period for persons of Indian origin → 7 years
☛ Condition for application → Continuous residence for 12 months before application
☛ First person to get citizenship by naturalisation → Sonia Gandhi (1983)

q: In February 2021, which of the following was amended, enabling the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to also look after the development of Ropeways and Alternate Mobility Solutions?
o: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1951
Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1981
Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1961
Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1971
qs.e: In February 2021, the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules 1961 were amended, enabling the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to also look after the development of ropeways and alternate mobility solutions. This amendment was approved by the Union Cabinet. Its objective was to promote alternative modes of transport in urban and inaccessible areas. Previously, ropeway development was under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Now, after this amendment, the Ministry of Road Transport is responsible for policy formulation, planning, and regulation of technologies like ropeways and cable cars.
qs.kf:
☛ When were the Allocation of Business Rules made? → 1961
☛ Which ministry was given the responsibility of ropeway development? → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
☛ What was the purpose of the amendment? → To promote alternate mobility solutions
☛ Which ministry earlier handled ropeways? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
☛ In which year was the amendment made? → 2021

q: Which of the following Articles deals with the citizenship of people of Indian origin residing outside India?
qs.e: Article 8 of the Indian Constitution deals with the citizenship of people of Indian origin residing outside India. It grants citizenship to persons who are living outside India but whose parents or grandparents were born in India. Such individuals can register as Indian citizens with the Indian consulate or embassy. Articles 5 to 11 cover citizenship provisions. Article 11 empowers Parliament to make laws regarding citizenship, while Article 7 relates to citizenship of displaced persons from Pakistan and Article 9 deals with termination of Indian citizenship upon voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship. Article 8 is a special provision to ensure that people of Indian origin abroad can retain a connection with India through citizenship.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 8 → Citizenship of Indian origin persons residing outside India
☛ Article 11 → Parliament's power to regulate citizenship by law
☛ Article 9 → Voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship terminates Indian citizenship
☛ Article 5 → Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
☛ Article 10 → Continuance of citizenship rights

q: Article 6 of the Constitution pertains to the citizenship of persons who migrated to India from which of the following territories?
qs.e: Article 6 of the Indian Constitution deals with the citizenship of persons who migrated to India from Pakistan. This article specifies the conditions under which individuals who moved from Pakistan to India during or after the partition (1947) could acquire Indian citizenship. It covers both those who migrated before January 1, 1947, and after, subject to certain registration and residency requirements. Article 6 is part of Part II of the Constitution, which outlines citizenship provisions. It was crucial in addressing the citizenship status of people displaced by the partition. The Citizenship Act, 1955, later supplemented these constitutional provisions. Article 6 ensures that migrants from Pakistan who fulfilled the criteria were granted Indian citizenship, thereby clarifying their legal status in the newly independent nation.
qs.kf:
☛ Article 6 deals with migrants from which country? → Pakistan
☛ Which part of the Constitution covers citizenship? → Part II
☛ What is the main citizenship law? → Citizenship Act, 1955
☛ Article 5 grants citizenship to whom? → Persons born or resident in India
☛ Article 7 deals with? → Citizenship of migrants to Pakistan

q: Which Amendment extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the legislatures for another 10 years till 2030?
qs.e: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2020 extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies for another 10 years till 2030. Earlier, the 95th Amendment (2009) had extended the reservation till 2020. This amendment amends Article 334 of the Constitution, which pertains to the reservation provisions. Additionally, the 104th Amendment also abolished the seats reserved for the Anglo-Indian community in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies. The amendment came into effect on 25 January 2020.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment extended SC/ST reservation till 2030? → 104th Amendment (2020)
☛ Which article was amended by the 104th Amendment? → Article 334
☛ What was the previous expiry date for SC/ST reservation? → 2020 (by 95th Amendment)
☛ Which community's reserved seats were abolished by the 104th Amendment? → Anglo-Indian
☛ When did the 104th Amendment come into effect? → 25 January 2020

q: Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) holders are:
o: Persons entitled to hold constitutional posts
Dual citizens of India and another country
qs.e: The Indian Constitution does not permit dual citizenship. OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) is a permanent residency visa that grants foreign nationals of Indian origin special privileges such as living and working in India, but they cannot vote or hold constitutional posts. OCI holders are not citizens of India; they are foreign nationals with special rights. They enjoy benefits like multiple-entry lifelong visa, economic and educational parity with Indian citizens, but are excluded from political rights. This status is distinct from Indian citizenship and is governed by the Citizenship Act, 1955.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country's citizens can apply for OCI? → Any country except Pakistan and Bangladesh
☛ Can OCI holders vote in India? → No
☛ Can OCI holders hold constitutional posts? → No
☛ What is the validity of an OCI card? → Lifetime
☛ Is dual citizenship allowed in India? → No

q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha?
qs.e: Article 330 of the Indian Constitution provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha. This reservation was originally for 10 years but has been extended periodically through amendments. Article 332 deals with reservation in state legislative assemblies, Article 331 provides for nomination of Anglo-Indian members by the President, and Article 334 relates to the expiration of reservation provisions. Thus, Article 330 is the core provision for SC/ST reservation in the Lok Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ Which article provides reservation for SC/ST in Lok Sabha? → Article 330
☛ Which article provides reservation for SC/ST in state assemblies? → Article 332
☛ Which article provides nomination of Anglo-Indians in Lok Sabha? → Article 331
☛ Which article deals with the expiration of reservation provisions? → Article 334
☛ Which communities are reserved seats in Lok Sabha? → Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes

q: Special provisions for certain states are covered under which Part of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e: Part XXI (Articles 369 to 392) of the Indian Constitution deals with special provisions for certain states. This part includes Article 370 (special status for Jammu & Kashmir, now abrogated), and Articles 371 to 371-J which provide special provisions for states like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, and Karnataka. These provisions are designed to address the specific needs of these states and ensure their development. Part XX deals with amendment of the Constitution, Part XIX covers miscellaneous topics, and Part XXII relates to title, commencement, etc. Therefore, Part XXI is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which Part was Article 370? → Part XXI
☛ Special provision for Andhra Pradesh is in which Article? → Article 371-D
☛ Special provision for Sikkim is in which Article? → Article 371-F
☛ Special provision for Nagaland is in which Article? → Article 371-A
☛ How many Articles are in Part XXI? → 24 (Articles 369 to 392)

q: The President of India is also the Supreme Commander of which force in India?
qs.e: As per Article 53(2) of the Indian Constitution, the President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, which includes the Army, Navy, and Air Force. This provision ensures civilian supremacy over the military. While the President holds the highest command authority, the actual administrative control is exercised by the Central Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The President can declare war or conclude peace, but only on the advice of the Council of Ministers. This system maintains democratic control and balance of military power. The President also appoints the chiefs of the three services. However, the President's role is largely ceremonial in this context, as real executive power lies with the elected government.
qs.kf:
☛ Article that makes President Supreme Commander of Armed Forces → 53(2)
☛ Three branches of Armed Forces under President → Army, Navy, Air Force
☛ President's military powers exercised on whose advice → Council of Ministers
☛ Administrative control of Armed Forces lies with → Central Council of Ministers
☛ President's war declaration subject to whose control → Parliament

q: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution is related to the:
o: distribution of seats in the Lok Sabha
qs.e: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, also known as the 'Anti-Defection Law', deals with the disqualification of members of Parliament and state legislatures on grounds of defection. It was added by the 52nd Amendment Act in 1985. The aim is to prevent political instability by discouraging elected representatives from switching parties. According to the Tenth Schedule, a member is disqualified if they voluntarily give up membership of their party or vote against party instructions. However, there are exceptions for party mergers. This schedule applies to both Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The presiding officer of the house (Speaker/Chairman) makes the final decision on disqualification, subject to judicial review.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Tenth Schedule added? → 1985
☛ Which amendment introduced the Tenth Schedule? → 52nd Amendment Act
☛ What is the objective of the Anti-Defection Law? → Prevent political instability
☛ Which houses does the Tenth Schedule apply to? → Lok Sabha and state assemblies
☛ Who decides disqualification under the Tenth Schedule? → Presiding officer of the house

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution was amended by the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act to provide for women’s reservation in the Legislative Assembly of Delhi?
qs.e: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act (2023) amended Article 239AA of the Indian Constitution to provide reservation for women in the Legislative Assembly of Delhi. Article 239AA deals with the administration of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. This amendment adds provisions for reserving seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women in the Delhi Legislative Assembly, ensuring 33% reservation for women. The other options: Article 330A and 332A relate to reservation in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies respectively (added by the 106th Amendment for women reservation in Parliament and state assemblies), while Article 243D deals with women reservation in Panchayats.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment provided women reservation in Delhi Assembly? → 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023
☛ What is the percentage of women reservation in Delhi Assembly? → 33%
☛ Which article was amended by the 106th Amendment for Delhi? → Article 239AA
☛ Which article gives special status to Delhi? → Article 239AA (inserted by 69th Amendment, 1991)
