qs.kf:
☛ Which pass is crossed by the Satluj river? → Shipki Pass
☛ Zozilla Pass is associated with which river? → Indus river
☛ Nathu Pass is located in which state? → Sikkim
☛ Where is Thang Pass situated? → Ladakh
☛ What is the altitude of Shipki Pass? → About 4,550 meters

q: Which of the following landforms are not produced by inflammatory water?
qs.e: Barkhan is a desert landform formed by wind (aeolian processes), not by inflammatory water. It is a crescent-shaped sand dune with its convex side facing the wind. Lake Gokur, Floodplain, and Delta are all landforms created by rivers. Lake Gokur is a oxbow lake formed when a river changes its course. Floodplain is formed by alluvial deposition during river floods. Delta is formed by sediment deposition at the river mouth. Thus, except for Barkhan, the other three landforms are produced by water.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of dune is a Barkhan? → Crescent-shaped sand dune
☛ What forms an oxbow lake? → River
☛ How is a floodplain formed? → Alluvial deposition
☛ Where does a delta form? → At the river mouth
☛ Which agent forms a Barkhan? → Wind

q: Which geographical features separate the the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
qs.e: The Ten Degree Channel is the geographical feature that separates the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It is located at 10° North latitude and is approximately 150 km wide. The Andaman Islands lie to the north of this channel, while the Nicobar Islands are situated to the south. This channel connects the Bay of Bengal with the Andaman Sea and is important for maritime traffic. It is the southernmost island group of India and the region is rich in biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Channel separating Andaman and Nicobar? → Ten Degree Channel
☛ Width of Ten Degree Channel? → Approximately 150 km
☛ Latitude of Ten Degree Channel? → 10° North
☛ Location of Andaman Islands? → North of Ten Degree Channel
☛ Location of Nicobar Islands? → South of Ten Degree Channel

q: The world's highest peak is?
qs.e: Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world, with an elevation of 8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 feet) above sea level. It is located in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and Tibet (China). It is also known as Sagarmatha (Nepali) and Chomolungma (Tibetan). The first successful ascent was made in 1953 by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay. Other options: Kanchanganga is the third highest, Kilimanjaro is the highest in Africa, while Salad Mountain is not a major peak.
qs.kf:
☛ World's highest peak → Mount Everest (8,848.86 m)
☛ Location of Mount Everest → Himalayas on Nepal-Tibet border
☛ Other names for Everest → Sagarmatha (Nepali), Chomolungma (Tibetan)
☛ First ascent → 1953 by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay
☛ Second highest peak → K2 (Godwin Austen, 8,611 m)

q: What is the southernmost point of the Indian Union where tsunami came?
qs.e: The southernmost point of the Indian Union is Indira Point, located on the Great Nicobar Island of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It was formerly known as Pygmalion Point and was renamed in 1985 in honor of Indira Gandhi. This point lies at 6°45'10" North latitude. The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami severely affected Indira Point, destroying the lighthouse there. Due to the tsunami, the area suffered extensive damage, and Indira Point was submerged. While Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India, Indira Point is the southernmost point of the entire Indian Union. Hence, Indira Point is the southernmost point where the tsunami struck.
qs.kf:
☛ Southernmost point of Indian Union → Indira Point (Great Nicobar)
☛ Southernmost point of Indian mainland → Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin)
☛ Former name of Indira Point → Pygmalion Point
☛ Cause of 2004 Tsunami → Earthquake in Indian Ocean
☛ Indian region affected by tsunami → Andaman and Nicobar Islands

q: Hispar Glacier is situated in which mountain range?
qs.e: Hispar Glacier is a major glacier located in the Karakoram Mountain Range. It is situated in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan and extends for about 49 km. It connects with the Biafo Glacier via the Hispar Pass, forming one of the longest glacier systems in the world. The glacier is part of the convergence zone of the Hindu Kush, Himalayas, and Karakoram ranges, but it lies specifically in the Karakoram range.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of Hispar Glacier → 49 km
☛ Country of Hispar Glacier → Pakistan
☛ Mountain range of Hispar Glacier → Karakoram
☛ Hispar Pass connects → Hispar and Biafo glaciers
☛ Biafo Glacier is located in → Karakoram Mountain Range

q: Which of the following is the longest mountain range in South America?
qs.e: The Andes mountain range is the longest mountain range in South America, stretching approximately 7,000 kilometers. It is also the longest continental mountain range in the world. The Andes run parallel to the Pacific coast, passing through seven countries: Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, and Argentina. Its highest peak is Mount Aconcagua (6,961 meters). The Andes were formed by the convergence of the Nazca Plate and the South American Plate. Among the options, the Alps are in Europe, the Himalayas in Asia, and the Rockies in North America.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of Andes → Approx 7,000 km
☛ Highest peak of Andes → Mount Aconcagua (6,961 m)
☛ Countries through which Andes passes → 7 countries (Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, Argentina)
☛ Formation of Andes → Convergence of Nazca and South American plates
☛ World's longest continental mountain range → Andes

q: What is the length of the Himalaya mountain range?
qs.e: The Himalaya mountain range extends for about 2400 km. It is the highest mountain range in the world, spanning across India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, and Pakistan. The Himalayas were formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates. Its width ranges from 150 to 400 km. The highest peak is Mount Everest (8848 m). The range is divided into three parts: Greater Himalaya, Lesser Himalaya, and Shivalik. It is the source of major Asian rivers like the Ganges, Indus, and Brahmaputra.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of Himalayas → 2400 km
☛ Width of Himalayas → 150-400 km
☛ Highest peak → Mount Everest (8848 m)
☛ Three divisions of Himalayas → Greater, Lesser, Shivalik
☛ Rivers originating from Himalayas → Ganga, Indus, Brahmaputra

q: Palghat Pass of Kerala connects Palakkad to ______.
qs.e: The Palghat Pass, also known as the Palakkad Gap, is a significant mountain pass located between the Palakkad district of Kerala and the city of Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu. It is a natural break in the Western Ghats that connects Kerala to Tamil Nadu. The pass is about 300 meters above sea level and is the widest pass in Kerala. Historically, it has been important for trade and transportation, providing a route between the Malabar Coast and the Coromandel Coast. Today, it is traversed by a national highway and a railway line. The pass plays a crucial role in the region's climate as well, allowing moisture-laden winds from the Arabian Sea to enter Tamil Nadu.
qs.kf:
☛ Which states does Palghat Pass connect? → Kerala and Tamil Nadu
☛ What is the altitude of Palghat Pass? → About 300 meters
☛ What is the other name of Palghat Pass? → Palakkad Gap
☛ In which mountain range is Palghat Pass located? → Western Ghats
☛ Which district of Kerala is Palghat Pass in? → Palakkad

q: The highest peak of Garo Hills-
qs.e: The Garo Hills are located in Meghalaya, part of Northeast India. The highest peak of these hills is Nokrek (1412 meters). Nokrek is also part of the Nokrek National Park, known for its biodiversity and wildlife like the Red Panda. Saramati is in Nagaland, Tiger Hills are also in Nagaland, and Eucalyptus is a tree species, not a peak—so none of these are peaks of Garo Hills. Nokrek peak also holds cultural significance for the Garo tribe.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Garo Hills → Nokrek (1412 m)
☛ Which national park is Nokrek part of? → Nokrek National Park
☛ Garo Hills are in which state? → Meghalaya
☛ Nokrek National Park is famous for? → Red Panda
☛ Other peaks of Garo Hills → Tura, Rangsakona

q: Which of the following hills is not the part of the Satpura ranges?
qs.e: The Satpura Range is a major mountain range in central India, running east-west. It consists of several hill ranges including Mahadev Hills, Hills of Rajpipla, and Meccal Hills. Mahadev Hills are located in Madhya Pradesh and are part of the Satpuras. Hills of Rajpipla in Gujarat form the westernmost part of the range. Meccal Hills in Madhya Pradesh constitute the eastern section. However, Nallamala Hills are located in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and are part of the Eastern Ghats, not the Satpuras. Therefore, Nallamala Hills are not a part of the Satpura range.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Satpura range → Dhupgarh (in Mahadev Hills)
☛ Source of Narmada river → Amarkantak (in Meccal Hills)
☛ Part of Eastern Ghats → Nallamala Hills
☛ Western limit of Satpura range → Hills of Rajpipla
☛ Location of Satpura range → North of Narmada river

q: Which of the following is the volcanic Island in the Bay of Bengal?
qs.e: Barren Island is the only active volcanic island in the Bay of Bengal. It is part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, a Union Territory of India. The island is located about 135 km northeast of Port Blair. The volcano on Barren Island first erupted in 1787 and has remained intermittently active since then. It is the only active volcano in South Asia. The island is uninhabited with no human settlements. Additionally, Narcondam Island in the Bay of Bengal is a dormant volcanic island.
qs.kf:
☛ Only active volcanic island in the Bay of Bengal → Barren Island
☛ Location of Barren Island → Andaman Sea
☛ First eruption of Barren Island volcano → 1787
☛ Only active volcano in South Asia → Barren Island
☛ Dormant volcanic island in Bay of Bengal → Narcondam Island

q: Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges are part of ______.
qs.e: The Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges are part of the Lower Himalayas (also known as the Himachal or Middle Himalaya). This zone lies between the Shivaliks and the Great Himalayas, with elevations ranging from 3,500 to 4,500 meters. The Pir Panjal range is primarily located in Jammu & Kashmir, while the Dhauladhar range extends across Himachal Pradesh. The Lower Himalayan region is characterized by lush forests, valleys, and important hill stations. In contrast, the Shivalik range forms the outer foothills, and the High Himalayas include the highest peaks like Mount Everest. Therefore, Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar are correctly classified under the Lower Himalayan region.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Pir Panjal range located? → Jammu & Kashmir
☛ Which state does the Dhauladhar range belong to? → Himachal Pradesh
☛ What is the elevation range of the Lower Himalayas? → 3,500 to 4,500 meters
☛ Which zone does the Shivalik range belong to? → Outer Himalayas
☛ Which states does the Lower Himalaya cover? → Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand

q: Sankotta Pass connects Madurai with _________.
qs.e: The Sankotta Pass is a significant mountain pass located between Kerala and Tamil Nadu. It connects Madurai in Tamil Nadu with Kottayam in Kerala. This pass is part of the Western Ghats and has historically been important for trade and transportation. Several major passes exist in South India, such as Palakkad Pass and Shenkotta Pass, but the Sankotta Pass is specifically known for the Madurai-Kottayam route.
qs.kf:
☛ Which cities does the Sankotta Pass connect? → Madurai and Kottayam
☛ In which mountain range is the Sankotta Pass located? → Western Ghats
☛ Which state is Kottayam in? → Kerala
☛ Which state is Madurai in? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which pass connects Kerala and Tamil Nadu through Palakkad? → Palakkad Pass

q: Mount Everest is located-
qs.e: Mount Everest is located in the Great Himalayan Range (also known as the Higher Himalayas or Inner Himalayas). It is the highest peak in the world with an elevation of 8,848.86 meters. The Himalayas are divided into three parallel ranges: the Shivaliks (Outer Himalayas), the Lesser Himalayas (Middle Himalayas), and the Great Himalayas (Inner Himalayas). The Great Himalayan range contains the highest peaks, including Everest, and forms the boundary between Nepal and Tibet. This region is characterized by rugged terrain, glaciers, and permanent snow.
qs.kf:
☛ Height of Mount Everest → 8,848.86 m
☛ Discoverer of Everest → Sir George Everest
☛ First climbers → Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary (1953)
☛ Three Himalayan ranges → Shivalik, Lesser Himalaya, Great Himalaya
☛ Feature of Great Himalaya → Highest and continuous range

q: Dhupgarh is the highest peak of -
qs.e: Dhupgarh is the highest peak of the Satpura Range, located in Madhya Pradesh, with an elevation of about 1,350 meters. The Satpura Range runs east-west across central India and acts as a watershed between the Godavari and Narmada rivers. Among the other options, the highest peak of the Aravalli Range is Gurushikhar, the Nilgiris' highest peak is Doddabetta, and the Garhjat Hills are in Odisha. Hence, Dhupgarh belongs to the Satpura Range.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Satpura Range → Dhupgarh
☛ Location of Dhupgarh → Madhya Pradesh (near Pachmarhi)
☛ Highest peak of Aravalli Range → Gurushikhar (1722 m)
☛ Highest peak of Nilgiris → Doddabetta (2637 m)
☛ Highest peak of Garhjat Hills → Malayagiri

q: A deep valley surrounded by steep and rocky walls is called _______.
qs.e: A deep valley with steep and rocky walls is called a narrow river valley or gorge. It is formed by river erosion cutting through hard rocks, resulting in nearly vertical slopes. These are commonly found in plateaus or mountainous regions, like the Grand Canyon. Glacial valleys are U-shaped, while narrow river valleys are V-shaped. The other options, shell and rock bend, are incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ What forms a narrow river valley? → River erosion
☛ What shape is a glacial valley? → U-shaped
☛ Which is the deepest gorge in the world? → Kali Gandaki Gorge, Nepal
☛ Example of a narrow river valley → Grand Canyon
☛ A valley with steep rocky walls is called? → Narrow river valley

q: In which of the following regions is the Karakoram Range located?
qs.e: The Karakoram Range is located in Northern India, specifically in the union territory of Ladakh. It is the second-highest mountain range in the world and includes K2 (Mount Godwin-Austen), the second-highest peak on Earth. The Karakoram is not part of the Himalayan range but is a separate mountain system. This range extends across the borders of India, Pakistan, and China. It contains some of the largest glaciers outside the polar regions, such as the Siachen Glacier. Northern India's region also includes the Zanskar and Ladakh ranges. The name 'Karakoram' means 'black gravel' in Turkish, referring to the dark-colored rocks found there.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the highest peak of the Karakoram range? → K2 (Godwin Austen)
☛ Which countries does the Karakoram range span? → India, Pakistan, China
☛ Which major glacier is located in the Karakoram range? → Siachen Glacier
☛ In which union territory is the Karakoram range located? → Ladakh
☛ Why is Karakoram called 'black gravel'? → 'Karakoram' means 'black gravel' in Turkish

q: Which of the following mountain passes connects India with China?
qs.e: Nathula Pass connects the Indian state of Sikkim with China's Tibet Autonomous Region. Located at an altitude of approximately 4,310 meters above sea level, it was a key part of the ancient Silk Route. After the 1962 India-China war, it was closed but was reopened in 2006 for border trade. It is one of the three functional trading routes between India and China. Thal Ghat is situated in Maharashtra, Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh, and Zoji La Pass in Ladakh, none of which connect to China.
qs.kf:
☛ Which states does Nathula Pass connect? → Sikkim (India) and Tibet (China)
☛ What is the altitude of Nathula Pass? → Approximately 4,310 meters
☛ When was Nathula Pass reopened? → In 2006
☛ In which state is Rohtang Pass located? → Himachal Pradesh
☛ Where is Zoji La Pass located? → Ladakh

q: The largest island in the Andaman and Nicobar group is:
qs.e: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a union territory of India comprising 572 islands. The largest island in this group is Middle Andaman. It is known for its dense rainforests, rich biodiversity, and pristine beaches. While North Andaman, South Andaman, and Great Nicobar are also large islands, Middle Andaman has the largest area. The island is a popular tourist destination and is home to several indigenous tribal communities. The capital of the territory is Port Blair, located on South Andaman.
qs.kf:
☛ Total islands in Andaman & Nicobar → 572
☛ Largest island → Middle Andaman
☛ Capital → Port Blair
☛ Highest point → Saddle Peak (North Andaman)
☛ Strait separating Andaman from Nicobar → Ten Degree Channel

q: What is ‘Northern Circar’ in India?
qs.e: Northern Circars is a name given to a coastal plain located on the eastern coast of India. This region extends across the coastal parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. During the British period, these areas were called 'Circars', and they were divided into five main regions: Ganjam, Visakhapatnam, Godavari, Krishna, and Guntur. The region lies along the Bay of Bengal and its economy is mainly based on agriculture and fishing. The term 'Northern Circars' is also found in ancient and medieval Indian history, referring to the fertile coastal belt that was ruled by various dynasties before the British.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Northern Circars located? → On the eastern coast of India
☛ Which states include Northern Circars? → Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
☛ How many regions was Northern Circars divided into? → Five
☛ Northern Circars is associated with which sea? → Bay of Bengal
☛ What is the main economic base of Northern Circars? → Agriculture and fishing

q: Which mountain range is a source of marble in India?
qs.e: The primary source of marble in India is the Aravalli Range. This mountain range is located in Rajasthan and is known for producing high-quality white marble. Makrana in Rajasthan is a famous marble-producing region, and its marble is world-renowned. The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, extending approximately 800 km from Gujarat to Delhi. Among the other options, the Vindhyas are known for sandstone and limestone, while the Himalayas are not a major source of marble. The Satpuras are mainly known for wildlife and minerals. The marble from the Aravallis has been used in iconic structures like the Taj Mahal.
qs.kf:
☛ Which mountain range is a major source of marble in India? → Aravallis
☛ Which region in Rajasthan is famous for marble production? → Makrana
☛ Which states does the Aravalli Range extend through? → Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi
☛ Which is the oldest mountain range in India? → Aravalli
☛ The Taj Mahal is built from which type of stone? → Marble (from Makrana)

q: Which of the following is a prominent feature of the Thar Desert?
qs.e: The Thar Desert, also known as the "Great Indian Desert," is located in the state of Rajasthan, India. Its most prominent feature is sand dunes, which are formed and constantly reshaped by wind action. The region has an extremely arid climate with very low rainfall. Unlike river valleys, rocky mountains, or dense forests, the Thar is dominated by sandy terrain. The sand dunes are the most recognizable geographical structure of this desert, making them the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for Thar Desert → Great Indian Desert
☛ State where Thar Desert is located → Rajasthan
☛ Climate of Thar Desert → Extremely arid
☛ Main landform in Thar Desert → Sand dunes
☛ Rainfall in Thar Desert → Very low

q: Which region in India has the highest annual rainfall?
qs.e: The highest annual rainfall in India is recorded in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, specifically at Mawsynram (and nearby Cherrapunji). Mawsynram receives an average annual rainfall of about 11,872 mm, making it the wettest place on Earth. This heavy rainfall is primarily due to the southwest monsoon winds that carry moisture from the Bay of Bengal and are forced to rise over the Khasi Hills, causing orographic precipitation. In contrast, Ladakh receives less than 100 mm annually, Western Rajasthan is arid, and the Northern Ganga plain experiences moderate rainfall.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest annual rainfall region in India? → Mawsynram (Meghalaya)
☛ Mawsynram is in which state? → Meghalaya
☛ Average annual rainfall at Mawsynram? → About 11,872 mm
☛ Main cause of rainfall in Meghalaya? → Orographic lifting of southwest monsoon winds
☛ Driest region in India? → Ladakh

q: Which plateau in India is known for its rich gold deposits?
qs.e: The Chota Nagpur Plateau in India is known for its rich gold deposits. Located primarily in Jharkhand, it is often called the mineral heartland of India. Besides gold, the plateau is abundant in coal, iron ore, mica, and limestone. Notable gold mining areas include Hatia and Kundarkochi. This plateau is part of the Gondwana landmass and has an average elevation of 600 to 900 meters. The Damodar River valley, which flows through the plateau, is a major coal-producing region. The Chota Nagpur Plateau is one of India's most important mineral-rich regions, contributing significantly to the country's economy.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Chota Nagpur Plateau located? → Jharkhand
☛ Which plateau is called the mineral heartland of India? → Chota Nagpur Plateau
☛ Which river flows through the Chota Nagpur Plateau? → Damodar
☛ Hatia and Kundarkochi are famous for which mineral? → Gold
☛ Which plateau is part of the Gondwana landmass? → Chota Nagpur Plateau

q: The Vindhyan range is bounded by which range on the south?
qs.e: The Vindhyan range is located in central India and extends in an east-west direction. Its southern boundary is bounded by the Satpura range, which runs parallel to the Vindhyas in the south. The Narmada River flows between the Vindhyas and the Satpuras, separating the two ranges. The Aravalli range lies to the west, the Kaimur range is a part of the eastern Vindhyas, and the Rajmahal hills are located in the east. Therefore, the Vindhyan range is bounded by the Satpura range on the south.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Vindhya range → Sad-bhaor (Sonmukh)
☛ River flowing between Vindhya and Satpura → Narmada
☛ Extent of Vindhya range → Gujarat to Bihar (approx 1200 km)
☛ Average height of Vindhya range → 300-600 meters
☛ Origin of Narmada river → Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)

q: The western coastal plains extend from __________ coastal region in the north to _____________ in the south.
qs.e: The western coastal plains are located along the west coast of India bordering the Arabian Sea. They extend from the coastal region of Gujarat in the north to Kerala in the south. These plains are divided into three sections: the northern part called the Gujarat coast, the central part called the Konkan coast (Maharashtra and Goa), and the southern part called the Malabar coast (Kerala and part of Karnataka). Konkan and Malabar are subdivisions of the western coastal plains, not the northern and southern boundaries. The Gujarat coast includes the Kutch and Kathiawar regions, while the Kerala coast is known for its backwaters and lagoons.
qs.kf:
☛ Northern limit of western coastal plains → Gujarat coast
☛ Southern limit of western coastal plains → Kerala coast
☛ Between which states is Konkan coast located? → Maharashtra and Goa
☛ In which state is Malabar coast located? → Kerala and Karnataka
☛ Which mountain range lies to the east of the western coastal plains? → Western Ghats

q: The Malabar Coast lies between:
qs.e: The Malabar Coast is the southern part of India's western coast, stretching from Mangalore (Karnataka) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu). It includes the coastal regions of Kerala and parts of Karnataka. To its north lie the Konkan Coast (Mumbai to Goa) and the Gujarat Coast. The Malabar Coast is famous for its Western Ghats, backwaters, and spice trade. Major ports include Kochi, Kozhikode, and Mangalore. Kanyakumari is the southernmost tip of India, where the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean meet.
qs.kf:
☛ Three divisions of India's western coast → Konkan, Kannad, and Malabar coasts
☛ Largest port on Malabar Coast → Kochi
☛ Northern limit of Malabar Coast → Mangalore
☛ Southern limit of Malabar Coast → Kanyakumari
☛ State with maximum extent of Malabar Coast → Kerala

q: Khardung La Pass, one of the highest motorable passes in the world, is located in which of the following States/Union Territories?
qs.e: Khardung La Pass is located in the Leh district of Ladakh. It is one of the highest motorable passes in the world, with an elevation of about 5,359 meters. The pass connects Leh to the Nubra Valley and provides access to the Shyok River valley and the Siachen Glacier. The name 'Khardung La' is derived from the Tibetan language, meaning 'small white house'. The pass is strategically important for the Indian Army. In 2021, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways officially named it 'Khardung La'.
qs.kf:
☛ Elevation of Khardung La Pass → Approximately 5,359 meters
☛ Khardung La connects which places → Leh and Nubra Valley
☛ Meaning of Khardung La → Small white house
☛ Language of origin of Khardung La name → Tibetan
☛ Strategic importance of Khardung La → Access to Siachen Glacier

q: Which of the following is a ‘Loo’ wind affected region of India?
qs.e: Loo is a hot and dry local wind that blows in the northwestern regions of India, especially the Thar Desert. It originates due to low-pressure areas during summer and is active in May-June. High temperatures in the Thar Desert cause the formation of Loo. It is lethal and can cause heatstroke. The Eastern Coast experiences humid winds, not Loo.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of wind is Loo? → Hot and dry local wind
☛ Which state has Thar Desert? → Rajasthan
☛ Hottest months in India? → May-June
☛ What is the color of Loo? → Red or yellow
☛ How to prevent Loo effects? → Drink enough water and stay in shade

q: Which is the highest peak of the Aravalli Range?
qs.e: The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges in India, extending across Rajasthan, Haryana, and Gujarat. The highest peak of this range is Guru Shikhar, located in the Mount Abu region of Rajasthan, with an elevation of approximately 1,722 meters. Guru Shikhar holds religious significance in Jainism and houses a famous Jain temple. Among the other options, Mount Abu is a hill station, Anamudi is the highest peak of the Western Ghats, and Doddabetta is the highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Aravalli Range → Guru Shikhar (1,722 m)
☛ Length of Aravalli Range → approx. 800 km
☛ Extent of Aravalli Range → Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat
☛ Location of Guru Shikhar → Mount Abu, Rajasthan
☛ Oldest fold mountain range in India → Aravalli

name: Set 3 · Q93–138
sub: Geography - Physical Features: Mountains, Plateaus & Plains

q: The Vindhyan range separates which two major physiographic regions?
o: The Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau
The Coastal Plains and the Peninsular Plateau
The Northern Plains and the Deccan Plateau
qs.e: The Vindhyan range is a major mountain range in central India, running in an east-west direction. It forms a geographical boundary between the Northern Plains (the Gangetic plains) and the Deccan Plateau. To the north of the Vindhyas lie the fertile alluvial plains, while to the south begins the plateau region of the Deccan. This range is located north of the Narmada River and is considered the northern edge of the Peninsular Plateau. Along with the Satpura range, the Vindhyas divide India into northern and southern physiographic regions.
qs.kf:
☛ Elevation range of Vindhya range → 300-900 meters
☛ Northwestern extent of Vindhyas → Gujarat to Bihar
☛ Highest peak of Vindhya range → Sadbhavana Peak (Gujarat)
☛ Major river flowing south of Vindhyas → Narmada
☛ Major river crossing the Vindhyas → Son (tributary of Ganga)

q: Which of the following tribes is primarily found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
qs.e: The Shompen tribe is primarily found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, specifically on Great Nicobar Island. They are a scheduled tribe and one of the smallest tribes in India. The Shompen people rely mainly on hunting and gathering. They speak a language belonging to the Nicobarese language family. The Indian government has notified special areas for their protection. The Siddi tribe is mainly found in Gujarat and Karnataka, the Kadar tribe in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, and the Irular tribe in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
qs.kf:
☛ Main tribe of Andaman & Nicobar → Shompen
☛ Shompen habitat → Great Nicobar Island
☛ Shompen language family → Nicobarese
☛ Siddi tribe region → Gujarat and Karnataka
☛ Kadar tribe region → Kerala and Tamil Nadu

q: Which of the following islands is known for having the only active volcano in India?
qs.e: India's only active volcano is located on Barren Island, which is part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. This volcano belongs to the Mediterranean Volcanic Belt and first erupted in 1787. Subsequent eruptions occurred in 1991, 1995, 2005-07, and 2010. Barren Island is situated in the Andaman Sea, about 135 km northeast of Port Blair. The island is uninhabited and is known for its volcanic activity, making it a significant geological site in India. The volcano is a stratovolcano and is closely monitored by scientists.
qs.kf:
☛ India's only active volcano island → Barren Island
☛ Barren Island is located in → Andaman and Nicobar Islands
☛ First eruption of Barren Island volcano → 1787
☛ Distance of Barren Island from Port Blair → 135 km northeast
☛ Barren Island volcano type → Stratovolcano

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct?
Statement I: Rain-bearing systems originating in the Bay of Bengal cause rainfall over the plains of North India.
Statement II: Arabian Sea rain-bearing systems bring rain to the west coast of India.
o: Statement II is correct, while statement I is incorrect.
Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct, while statement II is incorrect.
Neither statement I nor statement II is correct.
qs.e: India's monsoon rainfall is primarily driven by two branches: the Bay of Bengal branch and the Arabian Sea branch. The Bay of Bengal branch originates over the warm waters of the bay and moves northeastwards, causing heavy rainfall in the plains of North India including states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam. These systems interact with the Himalayas to produce widespread precipitation. On the other hand, the Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats leading to orographic rainfall along the west coast of India, including Mumbai, Goa, and Kerala. Thus, both statements are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Bay of Bengal branch → Causes rainfall over North Indian plains.
☛ Arabian Sea branch → Brings rain to the west coast of India.
☛ Western Ghats → Block Arabian Sea winds to cause rainfall.
☛ Himalayas → Block Bay of Bengal winds to cause rainfall.
☛ Monsoon → Main source of summer rainfall in India.

q: Which of the following islands lies in Lakshadweep?
qs.e: Pitti Island is a small uninhabited island in the Union Territory of Lakshadweep, located about 24 km northeast of Kavaratti. It is also known as 'Bird Island' because it serves as a crucial breeding ground for migratory birds. Spanning just 10 hectares, this island rises only 2 meters above sea level. Pitti Island is included in the tentative list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. In contrast, Purbasha and New Moore islands are located in the Sundarbans region of West Bengal, while Rameswaram is a town in Tamil Nadu. Pitti Island is one of the few islands in Lakshadweep that is protected as a bird sanctuary, sheltering species like the sooty tern.
qs.kf:
☛ Smallest uninhabited island in Lakshadweep → Pitti Island
☛ Other name of Pitti Island → Bird Island
☛ Area of Pitti Island → 10 hectares
☛ Total islands in Lakshadweep → 36 (10 inhabited, 26 uninhabited)
☛ Nearest main island to Pitti Island → Kavaratti

q: The Himalayan mountain system is geologically categorised as:
qs.e: The Himalayan mountain system is geologically categorized as folded mountains. It is formed when two tectonic plates collide with each other. The collision between the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate led to the formation of the Himalayas. During this process, the layers of rocks folded and rose upward, creating high mountain ranges. The Himalayas are the highest and youngest mountain range in the world, stretching about 2500 km. They extend across countries like India, Nepal, Bhutan, etc. Their formation took place in the Cenozoic Era.
qs.kf:
☛ Which plate collision formed the Himalayas? → Indian and Eurasian plates
☛ What type of mountain is the Himalayas? → Folded mountain
☛ What is the length of the Himalayas? → About 2500 km
☛ In which era were the Himalayas formed? → Cenozoic Era
☛ Why are the Himalayas called rejuvenated mountains? → Due to continuous rise in height

q: The Western Coastal Plains of India extend from:
qs.e: The Western Coastal Plains of India extend from Gujarat to Kanyakumari. These plains run parallel to the Arabian Sea and are divided into the Kathiawar coast in the north, the Konkan coast in the central region, and the Malabar coast in the south. The Konkan coast stretches from Maharashtra to Goa, while the Malabar coast covers Kerala and extends to Kanyakumari. The Western Coastal Plains are narrower than the Eastern Coastal Plains and are drained by short rivers originating from the Western Ghats. Due to the presence of the Western Ghats and the sea, this region receives heavy rainfall, leading to dense rainforests. Important ports like Mumbai, Mangalore, and Kochi are located along this coast.
qs.kf:
☛ Northern part of Western Coastal Plains → Kathiawar coast
☛ Konkan coast extends from → Maharashtra to Goa
☛ Malabar coast region → Kerala and Kanyakumari
☛ Major river draining Western Coastal Plains → Narmada
☛ Key feature of Western Coastal Plains → Narrow in width

q: What separates the North Andaman and South Andaman islands?
qs.e: Duncan Passage separates the North Andaman and South Andaman islands. It is a 48 km wide waterway. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a union territory of India, located in the Bay of Bengal. The Ten Degree Channel lies between the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, while the Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka. The Coco Channel lies between Myanmar and the Andaman Islands. Duncan Passage is named after a British naval officer named Duncan. This question is important for understanding the geography of Indian islands and their separating channels.
qs.kf:
☛ Which islands does Duncan Passage separate? → North Andaman and South Andaman
☛ Between which island groups is Ten Degree Channel? → Andaman and Nicobar Islands
☛ What does Palk Strait separate? → India and Sri Lanka
☛ Between which regions is Coco Channel? → Myanmar and Andaman Islands
☛ Width of Duncan Passage? → 48 km

q: Which mountain range acts as a natural boundary between the Northern Plains and the Deccan Plateau?
qs.e: The Vindhyachal mountain range acts as a natural boundary between the Northern Plains and the Deccan Plateau. It stretches approximately 1,100 km in an east-west direction. The average elevation of the Vindhyas is about 300-600 meters. This range passes through the states of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar. The Vindhyas have a mention in ancient Indian literature and are considered an important geographical divide of central India. The Satpura range lies to its south, the Aravallis to the northwest, and the Himalayas to the north.
qs.kf:
☛ Extent of Vindhyachal range → about 1,100 km
☛ Average elevation of Vindhyas → 300-600 meters
☛ Vindhyas in ancient texts → mentioned in Mahabharata and Puranas
☛ Rivers flowing through Vindhyas → Narmada (south side), Tons, Ken
☛ Region between Vindhyas and Satpuras → Narmada Valley

q: Which pass in the Himalayas connects Himachal Pradesh with Ladakh?
qs.e: Baralacha La (4,890 m) is a high mountain pass in the Himalayas, connecting Lahaul and Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh with Leh district of Ladakh. It lies on the Manali-Leh Highway and is used for vehicular movement. The name Baralacha La means 'pass with four peaks'. The Chandra and Bhaga rivers originate near this pass. Other options: Nathu La (Sikkim-China), Bum La (Arunachal-China), Zoji La (Kashmir-Ladakh).
qs.kf:
☛ Pass connecting Himachal Pradesh with Ladakh → Baralacha La
☛ Baralacha La is located on which highway → Manali-Leh Highway
☛ Height of Baralacha La → 4,890 meters
☛ Rivers originating from Baralacha La → Chandra and Bhaga
☛ Which pass connects Kashmir with Ladakh → Zoji La

q: Which of the following physiographic divisions of India is considered as ‘Tableland’?
qs.e: Among the physiographic divisions of India, the Peninsular Plateau is considered a 'Tableland' or plateau. It is the oldest landmass of India, formed from the ancient Gondwana Land. The plateau is bounded by the Vindhya and Satpura ranges in the north, and the Western and Eastern Ghats in the south. Its average elevation ranges from 600 to 900 meters. The Peninsular Plateau is divided into three parts: the Central Highlands, the Deccan Plateau, and the Northeastern Mountain Ranges. This region is rich in mineral resources and is drained by major rivers like Narmada, Tapti, Godavari, and Krishna.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest landmass of India → Peninsular Plateau
☛ Which river separates two plateaus? → Narmada separates Central Highlands and Deccan Plateau
☛ Rocks found in Peninsular Plateau → Crystalline and metamorphic rocks
☛ Highest peak of India is located in → Himalayas (Kanchenjunga)
☛ Average elevation of Peninsular Plateau → 600-900 meters

q: ‘Bhabar’ and ‘Khadar’ belts are part of which physiographic division of India?
qs.e: The Northern Plains of India are divided into regions based on the alluvial soil brought by rivers. 'Bhabar' is a narrow belt at the foothills of the Himalayas where rivers deposit large pebbles and stones. South of Bhabar lies the 'Terai' region with high water table and marshy conditions. Further south are 'Bangar' (old alluvium) and 'Khadar' (new alluvium) belts. Khadar is formed in floodplains where new soil is deposited every year, making it very fertile. Bhabar and Khadar are thus parts of the Northern Plains. The Northern Plains are formed by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems and their tributaries.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Bhabar belt located? → At the foothills of the Himalayas
☛ What type of soil is Khadar? → New alluvial soil
☛ What soil is found in Bangar region? → Old alluvial soil
☛ What is a characteristic of Terai region? → Marshy and high water table
☛ What formed the Northern Plains? → Alluvial soil brought by rivers

q: The Thar Desert experiences a significant temperature variation due to:
qs.e: The Thar Desert experiences significant temperature variation primarily due to dry conditions and sparse vegetation. In arid environments, low humidity causes extreme heating during the day and rapid cooling at night. Sparse vegetation contributes further because plants typically moderate temperature fluctuations. The lack of cloud cover and the presence of bare sand in the Thar enhance the temperature contrast. Distance from the sea, low rainfall, and flat terrain also amplify this effect. Therefore, the correct answer is dry conditions and sparse vegetation.
qs.kf:
☛ Extension of Thar Desert → Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, and Gujarat
☛ Largest part of Thar Desert → In Rajasthan
☛ Average rainfall in Thar → 100-500 mm per year
☛ River flowing in Thar → Luni (endorheic river)
☛ Major soil type in Thar → Desert soil

q: The Deccan Plateau is largely made up of which type of rock formation?
qs.e: The Deccan Plateau is predominantly composed of basalt, which is an igneous rock. It is a large lava plateau formed by volcanic eruptions at the end of the Cretaceous period. These solidified lava flows are known as the Deccan Traps. Since basalt is igneous, it does not contain fossils. Compared to sedimentary and metamorphic rocks, igneous rocks are hard and water-resistant, which is a characteristic of this region. The black soil (regur) found here is derived from the weathering of basalt. The Deccan Plateau covers parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat, and is one of the largest volcanic provinces in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ What rock type forms the Deccan Plateau? → Igneous rock (basalt)
☛ What is the main rock in Deccan Traps? → Basalt
☛ When was the Deccan Plateau formed? → End of Cretaceous period
☛ What type of soil is found on Deccan Plateau? → Black soil (regur)
☛ Why are fossils absent in igneous rocks? → Because they form from molten lava

q: The Great Indian Desert is also known as:
qs.e: The Great Indian Desert is also known as the Thar Desert. It is located in the state of Rajasthan, India, and is the 17th largest desert in the world. The Thar Desert covers an area of about 2,00,000 square kilometers. Its climate is extremely hot and dry, with annual rainfall less than 100 mm. The main rivers in this desert are Luni and Ghaggar. The people living in the desert rely on animal husbandry and agriculture for their livelihood.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Thar Desert located? → Rajasthan
☛ What is the area of the Thar Desert? → About 2,00,000 sq km
☛ Which is the major river flowing in the Thar Desert? → Luni River
☛ What is the annual rainfall in the Thar Desert? → Less than 100 mm
☛ What is the rank of the Thar Desert in the world by area? → 17th

q: Which pass is used to access Leh from Manali?
qs.e: The road from Manali to Leh passes through Baralacha La pass (4,890 m), located on the border of Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh. It is a part of the Leh-Manali Highway, which is 428 km long. Along this route, other passes like Rohtang Pass and Tanglang La also occur. Baralacha La is also called 'Bala Pass' and is the source of the Indus and Chenab rivers. This pass remains open only in summer and is closed in winter due to heavy snowfall.
qs.kf:
☛ Which pass is used to access Leh from Manali? → Baralacha La
☛ What is the height of Baralacha La pass? → 4,890 meters
☛ Which rivers originate at Baralacha La? → Indus and Chenab
☛ What is the total length of the Leh-Manali Highway? → 428 km
☛ Which two states/UTs does Baralacha La connect? → Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh

q: Which of the following are the Northernmost and Southernmost ranges of Himalayas, respectively?
qs.e: The Himalayas are divided into three parallel ranges: the Great Himalaya (Inner Himalaya), the Middle Himalaya (Lesser Himalaya), and the Shiwalik (Outer Himalaya). Among these, the Great Himalaya is the northernmost range, characterized by the highest peaks and permanent snow. In contrast, the Shiwalik is the southernmost range, consisting of low hills formed mainly from sedimentary rocks. The Middle Himalaya lies between them. According to the question's order (northernmost and southernmost), the correct answer is Great Himalaya and Shiwalik.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest range of Himalayas → Great Himalaya
☛ Southernmost range of Himalayas → Shiwalik
☛ Great Himalaya is also called → Himadri
☛ Shiwalik is also called → Outer Himalaya
☛ Middle Himalaya is also called → Lesser Himalaya

q: What is the geological origin of the Peninsular Plateau?
qs.e: The Peninsular Plateau is the oldest landmass of India, with its geological origin linked to Gondwana land. It was part of the ancient Gondwana supercontinent, which existed about 250 million years ago. When this supercontinent broke apart, the Indian plate drifted northward and collided with the Eurasian plate, forming the Himalayas. During this process, the Peninsular Plateau remained stable and stands today as an ancient craton. It consists of hard rocks such as granite, gneiss, and volcanic Deccan Traps. The Himalayan uplift, the Indo-Gangetic alluvium, and the Tethys Sea deposits are not related to its origin.
qs.kf:
☛ Ancient name of the Peninsular Plateau → Gondwana land
☛ Oldest landmass of India → Peninsular Plateau
☛ Period of Gondwana land breakup → Mesozoic Era
☛ Major rocks of the Peninsular Plateau → Granite, gneiss, Deccan Traps
☛ Extent of the Peninsular Plateau → From Aravalli to Eastern Ghats

q: Which of the following is the highest peak of the Himalayas located in India?
qs.e: The highest peak of the Himalayas is Mount Everest (8848 m) in Nepal, but the highest peak located in India is Kangchenjunga (8586 m). It lies on the border between Sikkim (India) and Nepal and is the world's third highest peak. Nanda Devi (7816 m) in Uttarakhand is India's second highest peak. Annapurna (8091 m) is in Nepal. Mount Everest is not in India because it is entirely within Nepal.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak in India → Kangchenjunga (8586 m)
☛ Highest peak in the world → Mount Everest (8848 m)
☛ Location of Kangchenjunga → Sikkim-Nepal border
☛ Second highest peak in India → Nanda Devi (7816 m)
☛ Annapurna is located in which country → Nepal

q: Which desert is known as the Great Indian Desert?
qs.e: The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is located in the state of Rajasthan, India, and the Sindh province of Pakistan. It is the world's 9th largest subtropical desert and the only desert in India, covering an area of about 2,00,000 square kilometers. The climate of the Thar Desert is extremely hot and dry, with very low rainfall. It features numerous sand dunes, some reaching heights of 150 meters. The desert is known for its diverse flora and fauna, including the camel (the state animal of Rajasthan) and the Great Indian Bustard (the state bird).
qs.kf:
☛ What is the area of the Thar Desert? → Approximately 2,00,000 sq km
☛ Which Indian states does the Thar Desert cover? → Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, and Gujarat
☛ What is the climate of the Thar Desert? → Extremely arid and hot
☛ Which animal is commonly found in the Thar Desert? → Camel
☛ What type of dunes are found in the Thar Desert? → Barchan and transverse dunes

q: The northernmost island of the Andaman group is:
qs.e: The Andaman group comprises over 300 islands. The northernmost island among them is Landfall Island, situated near the maritime boundary between India and Myanmar. It is part of North Andaman and holds strategic importance. South Andaman Island, Little Andaman Island, and Neil Island are located further south. Landfall Island is known for its natural beauty and biodiversity, and it is inhabited by indigenous tribes. Thus, the northernmost point of the Andaman group is indeed Landfall Island.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest island of Andaman → Middle Andaman
☛ Capital of Andaman → Port Blair
☛ Active volcano in Andaman → Barren Island
☛ Southernmost point of Andaman → Indira Point (Great Nicobar)
☛ Administrative language of Andaman & Nicobar → Hindi and English

q: The Thar Desert extends into which neighbouring country of India?
qs.e: The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is located in the northwestern part of India and extends into the neighbouring country Pakistan. It covers a large area in the Indian state of Rajasthan and spreads into the Sindh and Punjab provinces of Pakistan. The Thar Desert has an area of approximately 2,00,000 square kilometres, making it the 17th largest desert in the world. In India, it primarily lies in Rajasthan, while in Pakistan it extends into Sindh and Punjab. The desert is characterized by arid conditions, sand dunes, and a unique ecosystem.
qs.kf:
☛ What is another name for the Thar Desert? → Great Indian Desert
☛ Which Indian state mainly contains the Thar Desert? → Rajasthan
☛ What is the approximate area of the Thar Desert? → 200,000 sq km
☛ Into which Pakistani provinces does the Thar Desert extend? → Sindh and Punjab
☛ What is the rank of the Thar Desert in terms of size in the world? → 17th

q: What is the coastal zone located in the western part of India, along the Arabian Sea and south of Goa, known as?
qs.e: The western coastal region of India is divided into three parts: the Konkan coast (from Gujarat to Goa), the Malabar coast (south of Goa to Kanyakumari), and the Coromandel coast (eastern coast of Tamil Nadu). The area south of Goa along the Arabian Sea, as mentioned in the question, is the Malabar coast, which includes coastal parts of Kerala and Karnataka. This coast is famous for its coconut plantations, spices, and the slopes of the Western Ghats. The Sunderbans are the Ganges delta region in West Bengal. Thus, the coastal zone south of Goa is called the Malabar coast.
qs.kf:
☛ Western coastal part north of Goa → Konkan coast
☛ Major river of Malabar coast → Periyar
☛ Coromandel coast is located in which state? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Sunderban delta is formed by which river? → Ganges-Brahmaputra
☛ Southernmost point of western coast → Kanyakumari

q: Which coastal plain of India is predominantly rocky?
qs.e: The Western Coastal Plain of India is predominantly rocky. Stretching from Gujarat to Kerala, it has a rugged and uneven coastline due to the proximity of the Western Ghats. The plain is narrow and rocky, especially in the northern part known as the Konkan coast. In contrast, the Eastern Coastal Plain is wider and covered with alluvial soil brought by rivers. The Western Coastal Plain is divided into three sections: the Konkan coast (rocky), the Kannad plain, and the Malabar coast. The Malabar coast is relatively wider and has backwaters. Major natural harbors like Mumbai, Marmagao, and Kochi are located along this coast. The Coromandel Plain is part of the Eastern Coastal Plain and is not rocky. Understanding the distinct characteristics of India's coastal plains is important for geography exams.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the rocky coastal plain of India? → Western Coastal Plain
☛ What are the three sections of the Western Coastal Plain? → Konkan, Kannad, Malabar
☛ What is the Eastern Coastal Plain also known as? → Coromandel Coast (south) and Northern Circars (north)
☛ Which major natural harbor is on the Western Coast? → Mumbai
☛ Where are lagoons (backwaters) found in India? → Western Coast (Kerala)

q: Which is the highest peak of the Peninsular plateau of India?
qs.e: The highest peak of the Peninsular plateau of India is Anamudi (2,695 meters), located in the Western Ghats in Kerala. It lies in the Idukki district and is part of the Eravikulam National Park. The name Anamudi means 'elephant's head', and it is also the highest peak in South India. Doddabetta (2,637 meters) is the highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil Nadu, while Shevaroy Hills are in Tamil Nadu and Mahendragiri is in Odisha. The main mountain ranges of the Peninsular plateau are the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats. Anamudi is situated near the Palakkad Gap on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Peninsular Plateau → Anamudi
☛ Highest peak of Western Ghats → Anamudi
☛ Highest peak of South India → Anamudi
☛ Where is Doddabetta located? → Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu)
☛ Mahendragiri is in which state? → Odisha

q: The Luni River, flowing through the Thar Desert, eventually flows into:
qs.e: The Luni River originates from the Aravalli Range near Ajmer in Rajasthan and flows through the Thar Desert. It does not empty into the Arabian Sea or the Bay of Bengal; instead, it ends in the Rann of Kutch, a saline marshland in Gujarat. The total length of the Luni River is about 495 km. It is also known as the 'Lavani River' due to its saline water. It is the only significant river in the Thar Desert. In its final stretch, the water evaporates or seeps into the Rann. The river is seasonal and has no permanent flow to the sea.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Luni River → Aravalli Range (near Ajmer)
☛ Length of Luni River → Approximately 495 km
☛ Other name of Luni River → Lavani River (due to saline water)
☛ Luni River ends into → Rann of Kutch
☛ Major tributary of Luni River → Jojari River

q: Which physiographic division of India includes the Great Indian Plains?
qs.e: India's physiographic division consists of six major parts. Among them, the Northern Plains is the vast region located south of the Himalayas, formed by the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers. It is also known as the Himalayan Piedmont region and the Ganga Plain. This plain is fertile and considered the backbone of Indian agriculture. The Coastal Plains are located along the seashore, the Peninsular Plateau is the highland of southern India, and the Northern Mountains refer to the Himalayan range. Hence, the Great Indian Plains are included in the Northern Plains.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest physiographic division of India → Northern Plains
☛ Rivers forming the Northern Plains → Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra
☛ Number of subdivisions of Northern Plains → Three (Rajasthani, Ganga, Brahmaputra)
☛ Another name for Northern Plains → Himalayan Piedmont region
☛ Mountains between Peninsular Plateau and Northern Plains → Vindhya and Satpura

q: The Lakshadweep Islands lie close to the which coastal plain of India?
qs.e: The Lakshadweep Islands are located in the Arabian Sea off the southwestern coast of India. They lie close to the Malabar Coast, which is the coastal region of Kerala and Karnataka. The Malabar Coast lies between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea. Lakshadweep consists of 36 islands, of which 10 are inhabited. It is the smallest union territory of India. Its capital is Kavaratti. The name Lakshadweep means 'one hundred islands'. These islands are formed by coral reefs.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Lakshadweep → Kavaratti
☛ Total islands in Lakshadweep → 36
☛ Lakshadweep is located in which sea → Arabian Sea
☛ Largest island of Lakshadweep → Andrott
☛ Nearest state to Lakshadweep → Kerala

q: In the Thar Desert, inselbergs are:
o: sand dunes shaped by monsoon winds
flat desert plains formed by wind erosion
isolated rock hills rising sharply from the surrounding plain
qs.e: Inselbergs are isolated rock hills that rise abruptly from a flat plain. They are formed primarily by weathering and erosion, where softer surrounding rocks are worn away, leaving behind a resistant rock mass. In the Thar Desert, these landforms are remnants of ancient plateaus. Sand dunes, flat desert plains, and dry riverbeds do not qualify as inselbergs. Inselbergs are characteristic of arid and semi-arid regions.
qs.kf:
☛ How are inselbergs formed? → Weathering and erosion
☛ What are inselbergs in the Thar Desert remnants of? → Ancient plateaus
☛ Where are inselbergs commonly found? → Arid and semi-arid regions
☛ What type of rock forms inselbergs? → Hard, resistant rock
☛ Which landform rises abruptly from a flat plain? → Inselberg

q: Which of the following rivers is known for creating a rift valley in the Deccan Plateau and flows from Central India to the Arabian Sea?
qs.e: The Narmada River flows through a rift valley on the Deccan Plateau. It originates from the Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward into the Arabian Sea. It is the second longest peninsular river after the Godavari. The Narmada and the Tapti are the only major rivers in peninsular India that flow westward. A rift valley is formed by a crack in the Earth's crust, with steep cliffs on both sides. The total length of the Narmada is about 1312 kilometers. It forms the traditional boundary between North and South India. Its major tributaries include Banas, Tawa, and Barna. The river is known for the Dhuandhar Falls and supports several hydroelectric projects.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Narmada River → Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Narmada flows into which sea? → Arabian Sea
☛ Peninsular rivers flowing through rift valley → Narmada and Tapti
☛ Total length of Narmada → Approximately 1312 km
☛ Famous waterfall on Narmada → Dhuandhar Falls

q: Which of the following is a man-made island in India?
qs.e: India's only man-made island is Willingdon Island, constructed to improve the Cochin Port. It was built by dredging the channel between the natural islands of Venduruthy and Willingdon. The island is named after Lord Willingdon, who served as Viceroy of India from 1936 to 1943. It serves as a hub for maritime traffic and commercial activities. Other options: Minicoy is a natural island, Amwaj Islands are in Bahrain, and Jurong Island is in Singapore.
qs.kf:
☛ Only man-made island in India → Willingdon Island
☛ Where is Willingdon Island located → Kochi, Kerala
☛ When was Willingdon Island built → 1936
☛ Willingdon Island named after whom → Lord Willingdon
☛ Purpose of building Willingdon Island → Improvement of Cochin Port

q: The Eastern Ghats are part of which physical feature of the Indian Peninsular Plateau?
qs.e: The Eastern Ghats are part of the Indian Peninsular Plateau, a large plateau region. They are discontinuous and lower in elevation compared to the Western Ghats, with an average height of about 600 meters. The Eastern Ghats run parallel to the Bay of Bengal, extending through the states of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. They are intersected by major rivers like the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri. As part of the peninsular plateau, they are distinct from the coastal plains. The Eastern Ghats consist of various hill ranges such as the Nallamala, Palkonda, and Simhachalam hills. Their formation is ancient, dating back to the Precambrian era.
qs.kf:
☛ Which plateau includes the Eastern Ghats? → Peninsular Plateau
☛ What is the average height of the Eastern Ghats? → About 600 meters
☛ The Eastern Ghats are also known as? → Eastern Coastal Hills
☛ Which states do the Eastern Ghats cover? → Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu
☛ Which river divides the Eastern Ghats? → Godavari

q: The coastal strip between Daman and Goa is called the:
qs.e: The coastal strip between Daman and Goa is called the Konkan Coast. The Konkan Coast is located on the western coast of India and includes parts of Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka. This coast stretches along the Arabian Sea and is known for its natural beauty, beaches, and coconut groves. The northern part of the Konkan Coast starts from Daman and extends southwards up to Goa. Along this coast, many small rivers and creeks are found. The Konkan Coast is considered a part of the Western Coast, which is divided into three sections: Konkan Coast, Karnataka Coast, and Malabar Coast. Thus, the coastal strip between Daman and Goa is called the Konkan Coast.
qs.kf:
☛ What are the three parts of the Western Coast? → Konkan Coast, Karnataka Coast, Malabar Coast
☛ Which states does the Konkan Coast cover? → Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka
☛ What is the coastal strip between Daman and Goa called? → Konkan Coast
☛ Which sea is the Konkan Coast along? → Arabian Sea
☛ Where is the Karnataka Coast located? → South of Goa

q: The Deccan Plateau is mostly composed of:
qs.e: The Deccan Plateau is primarily composed of granite and basalt rocks. It was part of the ancient Gondwana landmass and later formed by volcanic activity that deposited basalt rocks. These basalt rocks are dark-colored and weather to form fertile black soil, suitable for cotton cultivation. Granite, an igneous rock, forms the underlying base of the plateau. The Deccan Plateau is a major geographical region covering parts of western and southern India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which activity formed the Deccan Plateau? → Volcanic activity
☛ Soil type found in Deccan Plateau? → Black soil (regur)
☛ States covered by Deccan Plateau? → Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana
☛ Highest peak of Deccan Plateau? → Anamudi
☛ Eastern part of Deccan Plateau is called? → Eastern Ghats

q: The sand dunes in the Thar desert are primarily formed by:
qs.e: The sand dunes in the Thar desert are primarily formed by wind action. This is an arid region with sparse vegetation and strong winds. Wind transports sand particles from one place to another, depositing them to form dunes of various shapes. The main types of sand dunes are barchans, seifs, and parabolic dunes. Barchans are crescent-shaped dunes. Wind direction and speed play a crucial role in dune formation in the Thar desert. Processes like river erosion, flash floods, and earthquakes are not the primary agents in the formation of desert dunes.
qs.kf:
☛ Extent of Thar desert → Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab (India) and Pakistan
☛ Largest sand dune type → Barchan
☛ Major river of Thar desert → Luni
☛ Climate of Thar desert → Arid and semi-arid
☛ Soil found in Thar → Regur and sandy soil

q: Which region of the Western Coastal Plains is known for its indented coastline with natural harbours?
qs.e: The Western Coastal Plains are divided into three sections: Konkan Coast, Karnataka Coast, and Malabar Coast. Among these, the Konkan Coast extends from Mumbai to Goa and is known for its indented coastline and natural harbours such as Mumbai, Marmagao, and Nhava Sheva. The coastline features numerous creeks, bays, and estuaries, making it ideal for port development. The Karnataka Coast is relatively less indented, while the Malabar Coast is long and straight. In the Konkan region, the Western Ghats approach close to the sea, resulting in short, swift rivers that create many rias and estuaries, further contributing to the rugged coastline. This unique topography provides excellent shelter for ships, making it a region rich in natural harbors.
qs.kf:
☛ Most indented coastline in India → Western coast (Konkan)
☛ North-south extent of Konkan Coast → Mumbai to Goa
☛ Major ports on Konkan Coast → Mumbai, Nhava Sheva, Marmagao
☛ Three divisions of Western Coastal Plains → Konkan, Karnataka, Malabar
☛ Reason for indented coastline → Proximity of Western Ghats to sea and active river erosion

q: Which geological event led to the formation of the Peninsular plateau?
o: Breaking and drifting of Gondwana land
qs.e: The Peninsular plateau of India was formed by the breaking and drifting of the Gondwana land. This geological event occurred during the Mesozoic era when the Gondwana supercontinent fragmented. The Indian plate drifted northwards from the Southern Hemisphere and collided with the Eurasian plate, leading to the formation of the Himalayas. The Peninsular plateau is composed of ancient igneous and metamorphic rocks, making it a stable and earthquake-resistant region. It is the oldest landmass of India and contains major mineral resources. The Eastern and Western Ghats run parallel to the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea, respectively.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Peninsular plateau → Anamudi (South India)
☛ Eastern boundary of Peninsular plateau → Eastern Ghats
☛ Western boundary of Peninsular plateau → Western Ghats
☛ Highest part of Peninsular plateau → Plateau region of Maharashtra and Karnataka
☛ Major river of Peninsular plateau → Godavari (largest river in Peninsular India)

q: In which of the following regions in India are Tropical Evergreen Forests found?
qs.e: Tropical Evergreen Forests in India are primarily found in regions with more than 200 cm of annual rainfall and temperatures between 22°C and 30°C. The Western Ghats, northeastern India, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are the main areas. The Western Ghats receive heavy rainfall from monsoon winds coming from the Arabian Sea, which is favorable for the growth of these forests. These forests are rich in biodiversity and have multi-layered vegetation. Punjab has dry forests, Sunderbans have mangrove forests, and Rajasthan has desert vegetation. Tropical Evergreen Forests are characterized by trees that remain green throughout the year, without shedding leaves. They are also known as rainforests.
qs.kf:
☛ Rainfall required for Tropical Evergreen Forests → More than 200 cm
☛ Major tree species found in Western Ghats → Rosewood, Mahogany, Ebony
☛ Area covered by Tropical Evergreen Forests in India → About 8%
☛ Where are Mangrove Forests found → Sunderbans, Ganga-Brahmaputra delta
☛ Characteristic of Tropical Evergreen Forests → Trees remain green throughout the year and do not shed leaves

q: Which of the following is the easternmost range of the Himalayas?
qs.e: The easternmost range of the Himalayas is the Purvanchal Range, located on the eastern border of India, which includes the Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, Mizo Hills, and others. This range extends up to Arakan Yoma and goes into Bangladesh and Myanmar. It forms the easternmost boundary of the Himalayas, whereas Zanskar, Dhauladhar, and Pir Panjal are ranges of the western and central Himalayas. The Purvanchal Range is part of the southern branch of the Himalayas and is also called the Eastern Hills.
qs.kf:
☛ Easternmost range of Himalayas → Purvanchal Range
☛ Extent of Purvanchal Range → From Assam to Myanmar
☛ Major hills in Purvanchal → Naga, Manipur, Mizo
☛ Other name of Purvanchal → Eastern Hills
☛ Countries associated with Purvanchal → India, Bangladesh, Myanmar

q: The Bhabar region lies in which part of the Great Plains?
o: Adjacent to the foothills of the Himalayas
qs.e: The Bhabar region is the northernmost part of the Great Plains of India, located adjacent to the foothills of the Himalayas. This region is formed by the deposition of pebbles, stones, and sand brought down by rivers from the Himalayas. It lies immediately north of the Terai region, not south. The width of the Bhabar is about 8-16 km. Rivers disappear underground here due to the highly permeable soil. Vegetation is sparse, and the area is less suitable for agriculture. The western part of the Indus plain and the Brahmaputra basin are different geographical units from the Bhabar.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the width of the Bhabar region? → About 8-16 km
☛ Why do rivers disappear in the Bhabar region? → Due to highly permeable soil
☛ What type of deposits form the Bhabar region? → Pebbles, stones, and sand
☛ In which direction is the Terai region located relative to Bhabar? → South
☛ What is the vegetation like in the Bhabar region? → Sparse

q: Which of the following Indian states has all three types of physical divisions – plateau, plains, and coastal plains?
qs.e: Tamil Nadu has all three types of physical divisions: plateau (eastern part of Deccan Plateau), plains (river plains of Kaveri, Palar, Vaigai), and coastal plains (southern part of Eastern Coastal Plains). Other states lack one division: Madhya Pradesh has plateau and plains but no coastal plains; Punjab is predominantly plains; Uttar Pradesh mainly consists of plains. This geographical diversity makes Tamil Nadu unique.
qs.kf:
☛ Major plateau in Tamil Nadu → Deccan Plateau
☛ Major river forming plains in Tamil Nadu → Kaveri
☛ Coastal plain of Tamil Nadu is called → Coromandel Coast
☛ Highest peak in Tamil Nadu → Doddabetta (Nilgiri Hills)
☛ Capital of Tamil Nadu → Chennai

q: Which geographical feature separates India from Sri Lanka?
o: Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar
qs.e: The maritime boundary between India and Sri Lanka is defined by the Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar. The Palk Strait is a narrow waterway located between the coast of Tamil Nadu (India) and the northern province of Sri Lanka, while the Gulf of Mannar extends south of it. This region is famous for marine life and pearl fishing. Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu), a chain of limestone shoals, separates the Palk Strait from the Gulf of Mannar. This geographical feature is crucial for navigation and trade between the two countries. Other options like the Strait of Hormuz (Persian Gulf), Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat), and Gulf of Aden (Yemen) are not related to the India-Sri Lanka separation.
qs.kf:
☛ Which features form the India-Sri Lanka maritime border? → Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar
☛ Between which regions is the Palk Strait located? → Tamil Nadu (India) and Sri Lanka
☛ What is the Gulf of Mannar known for? → Pearl fishing and marine biodiversity
☛ What does Adam's Bridge connect? → India and Sri Lanka
☛ Where is the Strait of Hormuz located? → Between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman

q: Which of the following statements about the Peninsular Plateau of India is NOT correct?
o: The Western Ghats are higher than the Eastern Ghats.
The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
The Peninsular plateau consists of three broad divisions, namely, the Northern Highlands, Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.
The Peninsular plateau is a tableland composed of the old crystalline, igneous and metamorphic rocks
qs.e: The Peninsular Plateau is divided into three broad divisions: the Central Highlands, the Deccan Plateau, and the Eastern and Western Ghats. The Northern Highlands are part of the Himalayan region, not the Peninsular Plateau. The Western Ghats are higher than the Eastern Ghats. The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass south of the Narmada River. The plateau is composed of old crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks. Therefore, the third statement is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ Three divisions of Peninsular Plateau → Central Highlands, Deccan Plateau, Eastern & Western Ghats
☛ Plateau south of Narmada → Deccan Plateau
☛ Highest peak in Western Ghats → Anamudi
☛ Rocks of Peninsular Plateau → Old crystalline, igneous, metamorphic
☛ Shape of Peninsular Plateau → Triangular tableland

q: What is the main reason behind the formation of lagoons along the Eastern Coastal Plains?
o: Sand deposition along the shallow coastlines
Tectonic activity and fault line shifts
Coral reef development and volcanic islands
Deposition by rivers and wave action along the coast
qs.e: The formation of lagoons along the Eastern Coastal Plains is primarily due to the depositional processes of rivers and sea waves. Rivers carry sediments and sand and deposit them along the coast, while waves redistribute this material to form sand bars parallel to the shoreline. Over time, these bars grow and isolate a portion of seawater, creating lagoons. This process is most effective on shallow and flat coastlines where the balance between tidal action and river deposition is maintained. Thus, lagoons result from combined fluvial and marine deposition.
qs.kf:
☛ Major lagoons on the Eastern Coast → Chilika Lake, Pulicat Lake
☛ Another name for lagoon → Brackish water lake
☛ Chilika Lake is located in → Odisha
☛ Pulicat Lake extends in which states → Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
☛ Eastern Coast is also known as → Coromandel Coast and Northern Circars Coast

q: Which natural formation in northwest India initiates a low pressure area during the summer months?
qs.e: The Thar Desert in northwest India heats up intensely during the summer months, creating a low pressure area. This low pressure zone plays a crucial role in attracting the southwest monsoon. At the onset of the monsoon, the low pressure over the Thar Desert draws moist winds from the Indian Ocean towards the Indian subcontinent. The high temperature and sandy soil of the Thar Desert cause rapid heating, making it a key factor in monsoon establishment. In contrast, the Ganges Basin, Aravalli Hills, and Satpura Mountains do not generate such a low pressure system.
qs.kf:
☛ What does the Thar Desert create in summer? → Low pressure area
☛ Which monsoon is influenced by Thar Desert's low pressure? → Southwest monsoon
☛ Maximum temperature of Thar Desert in summer? → About 50°C
☛ In which state is the Thar Desert located? → Rajasthan
☛ Other name for Thar Desert? → Great Indian Desert

q: Which island nation lies to the south of the Lakshadweep Islands?
qs.e: Lakshadweep is a union territory of India located in the Arabian Sea. To its south lies the island nation of Maldives, which is an archipelago of 26 coral atolls in the Indian Ocean. The Andaman Islands are in the Bay of Bengal to the east, Sri Lanka is to the southeast, and Mauritius is far to the south in the Indian Ocean. Hence, the correct answer is Maldives.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Lakshadweep → Kavaratti
☛ Total number of islands in Lakshadweep → 36
☛ Country to the south of Lakshadweep → Maldives
☛ Capital of Maldives → Male
☛ Official religion of Maldives → Islam

name: Set 4 · Q139–184
sub: Geography - Physical Features: Mountains, Plateaus & Plains

q: Which of the following is a feature of the Eastern Coastal Plain of India?
o: Wider and formed by alluvial deposits
Located between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea
qs.e: The Eastern Coastal Plain of India is wider compared to the Western Coastal Plain and is formed by alluvial deposits brought by major rivers like the Ganga, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri. It lies between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal, not between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea. It features numerous deltas rather than estuaries (estuaries are characteristic of the western coast). Hence, "Wider and formed by alluvial deposits" is the correct feature of the Eastern Coastal Plain.
qs.kf:
☛ Two divisions of Eastern Coastal Plain → Northern Circars and Coromandel Coast
☛ Famous lake on the eastern coast → Chilika Lake
☛ Major rivers on the eastern coast → Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri
☛ Northern part of eastern coast is called → Northern Circars
☛ Southern part of eastern coast is called → Coromandel Coast

q: The Gulf of Mannar lies between:
qs.e: The Gulf of Mannar is a shallow bay located between the southeastern coast of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka. It is part of the Indian Ocean and is separated from Sri Lanka in the south by the Palk Strait. The Gulf contains the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, known for its biodiversity and pearl cultivation. The region is also famous for the dugong (sea cow). The Gulf of Mannar has been declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. It defines the maritime boundary between India and Sri Lanka.
qs.kf:
☛ Between which two countries is the Gulf of Mannar located? → India and Sri Lanka
☛ Which ocean is the Gulf of Mannar part of? → Indian Ocean
☛ Which marine national park is located in the Gulf of Mannar? → Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
☛ Which animal is the Gulf of Mannar famous for? → Dugong (sea cow)
☛ What has the Gulf of Mannar been declared as? → UNESCO Biosphere Reserve

q: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Dweep is a part of which island?
qs.e: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Dweep, formerly known as Ross Island, is a part of the Andaman Islands. Located near Port Blair, it was renamed in 2018 by the Indian government in honor of Netaji. Similarly, Havelock Island was renamed Swaraj Dweep and Neil Island was renamed Shaheed Dweep. Netaji had temporarily hoisted the flag of the Azad Hind Government in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in 1943.
qs.kf:
☛ Former name of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Dweep → Ross Island
☛ New name of Havelock Island → Swaraj Dweep
☛ New name of Neil Island → Shaheed Dweep
☛ Capital of Andaman Islands → Port Blair
☛ Formation of Azad Hind Government → 21 October 1943, Singapore

q: The typical landform seen in the Thar Desert is:
qs.e: The Thar Desert is a tropical desert with very low rainfall (100-500 mm). Strong winds blow loose sand and deposit it to form various shapes of sand dunes, which are the typical landforms of this desert. These dunes are constantly shifting and dominate the landscape. Other options like glacial moraines are found in glaciated regions, river deltas form at river mouths, and alluvial plains are fertile plains formed by rivers, none of which are characteristic of the Thar Desert.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for Thar Desert → Great Indian Desert
☛ Highest sand dune in Thar Desert → Dhoomer Tila
☛ Major river of Thar Desert → Luni River
☛ Extent of Thar Desert → Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Gujarat
☛ Soil type in Thar Desert → Sandy soil

q: Which of the following belongs to the Lakshadweep group of islands?
qs.e: Lakshadweep is India's smallest Union Territory, comprising 36 islands. The Kannur Islands belong to the Lakshadweep group, whereas Kamorta Island and Chowra Island are part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Milo Island is not part of Lakshadweep. Major islands of Lakshadweep include Agatti, Kavaratti, Minicoy, and Kannur. The region is known for its coral reefs and marine biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the largest island of Lakshadweep? → Minicoy
☛ What is the capital of Lakshadweep? → Kavaratti
☛ How many islands are there in Lakshadweep? → 36
☛ Lakshadweep is located off the coast of which state? → Kerala
☛ What was the ancient name of Lakshadweep? → Laccadive Islands

q: The northern part of the plains along the Bay of Bengal is referred to as the Northern Circar, while the southern part is known as the ___________.
qs.e: The eastern coast of India is divided into two parts. The northern part is known as the Northern Circar and the southern part is called the Coromandel Coast. The Coromandel Coast extends from the southern part of Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu along the Bay of Bengal. The name 'Coromandel' is derived from the Tamil word 'Cholamandalam', meaning the realm of the Chola kings. This region is known for its historical ports and maritime trade. The plains here are fertile deltas formed by rivers like Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri. The Coromandel Coast has a tropical climate and receives heavy rainfall from the northeast monsoon.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the northern part of the eastern coast called? → Northern Circar
☛ Which state is the Coromandel Coast located in? → Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
☛ From which word is Coromandel Coast derived? → Cholamandalam
☛ Which river does NOT form a delta on the eastern coast? → Narmada (western coast)
☛ Utkal Plains are located in which state? → Odisha

q: Which of the following deserts is visible in the southern part of the world map?
qs.e: The Kalahari Desert is located in southern Africa, which appears in the southern part of the world map. It spans across Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa. The Gobi Desert is in Central Asia, the Thar Desert in India-Pakistan, and the Sonoran Desert in North America, all located in the northern hemisphere. Most of the Kalahari lies in the southern hemisphere, making it visible in the southern part of the world map.
qs.kf:
☛ Which continent is the Kalahari Desert in? → Africa
☛ Which countries does the Kalahari Desert cover? → Botswana, Namibia, South Africa
☛ What is the largest desert in the southern hemisphere? → Kalahari Desert
☛ Where is the Gobi Desert located? → Central Asia (Mongolia-China)
☛ Which country is the Thar Desert in? → India and Pakistan

q: In which of the following Indian regions is an alpine climate with snowy winters and cool summers predominant?
qs.e: An alpine climate is found in high mountainous regions with low temperatures and snowfall. In India, this climate is predominant in the Himalayan mountain range. Due to the high altitude of the Himalayas, winters are snowy and long, while summers are cool and short. In contrast, the Thar Desert experiences an arid climate, the Northern Plains have a subtropical climate, and the Western Ghats have a tropical monsoon climate. Thus, the Himalayas are the only region with an alpine climate.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is alpine climate found? → High mountainous regions
☛ What is the climate of the Himalayas? → Snowy winters and cool summers
☛ What is the climate of the Thar Desert? → Arid climate
☛ What is the climate of the Northern Plains? → Subtropical
☛ What is the climate of the Western Ghats? → Tropical monsoon

q: Which natural feature divides the Lakshadweep islands into two broad parts?
qs.e: The natural feature that divides the Lakshadweep islands into two broad parts is the Nine Degree Channel. This channel lies between the northern and southern groups of islands. The northern part includes Amindivi and some islands of Lakshadweep, while the southern part includes major islands like Minicoy and Kavaratti. The Nine Degree Channel is a significant waterway for maritime traffic and connects the Lakshadweep Sea with the Arabian Sea.
