q: How can rivers contribute to the formation of a coastal plain?
qs.e: Rivers carry large amounts of sediment (silt, sand, and clay) eroded from the land as they flow. When they approach the sea or ocean, their velocity decreases, causing them to deposit the transported sediments along the coast. This process of deposition, continuing over thousands to millions of years, gradually builds up flat, fertile land known as coastal plains. Famous examples include the Eastern Coastal Plain of India, formed by rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery depositing sediments into the Bay of Bengal. The Ganges-Brahmaputra delta also contributes to the coastal plain. Thus, rivers contribute to the formation of coastal plains primarily by depositing sediments over time.
qs.kf:
☛ Main process for coastal plain formation → Sediment deposition
☛ Largest coastal plain in India → Eastern Coastal Plain
☛ River depositing sediments in Bay of Bengal → Ganges
☛ Landform created by river deposition at coast → Delta
☛ Feature of coastal plains → Fertile soil and flat land

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 2
q: The Coromandel Coast is located along which part of India?
qs.e: The Coromandel Coast is located along the southern east coast of India. It lies along the Bay of Bengal and stretches across the states of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. The coast extends from the Krishna River delta in the north to Kanyakumari in the south. It belongs to the eastern part of peninsular India. Major cities on the Coromandel Coast include Chennai, Puducherry, and Cuddalore. This coast is known for its sand dunes and lagoons. It experiences heavy rainfall from the northeast monsoon.
qs.kf:
☛ Which bay does the Coromandel Coast border? → Bay of Bengal
☛ Major port on the Coromandel Coast? → Chennai
☛ Union territory on the Coromandel Coast? → Puducherry
☛ Which state lies in the northern part of the Coromandel Coast? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ What type of coast is the Coromandel Coast? → Sandy coast

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3
q: During summer, the Thar Desert becomes a low-pressure zone due to which of the following?
qs.e: During summer, the Thar Desert experiences intense solar heating, which causes the land to become extremely hot. This heats the air above, causing it to rise and create a low-pressure zone. This process forms a thermal low-pressure system that helps attract monsoon winds towards the Indian subcontinent. Western disturbances are effective during winter, while frontal cyclones are associated with mid-latitudes. Coastal humidity does not lead to low pressure. Thus, intense solar heating is the primary reason.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main cause of low pressure over the Thar Desert in summer? → Intense solar heating
☛ Where does the summer low-pressure zone form in India? → Thar Desert
☛ Which process creates the low pressure that attracts monsoons? → Intense solar heating
☛ When are western disturbances active? → Winter
☛ Frontal cyclones are associated with which latitudes? → Mid-latitudes

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following mountain ranges contains the 'Valley of Flowers' National Park?
qs.e: The 'Valley of Flowers' National Park is located in the state of Uttarakhand and is part of the Western Himalayas. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is known for its diverse alpine flora. The park is also a component of the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve. The Western Himalayas extend across Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Sikkim. Other options like Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal are ranges within Himachal Pradesh, while the Karakoram range lies in the Ladakh region.
qs.kf:
☛ Valley of Flowers National Park is located in which state? → Uttarakhand
☛ Which mountain range does Valley of Flowers belong to? → West Himalaya
☛ Valley of Flowers is part of which biosphere reserve? → Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve
☛ Which river flows through Valley of Flowers National Park? → Pushpawati River
☛ What is the altitude range of Valley of Flowers National Park? → 3,350 m to 6,700 m

q: Which of the following is the highest peak in India?
qs.e: The highest peak in India is Kanchanjunga (8,586 meters), located in Sikkim. It is the third highest peak in the world. Anamudi (2,695 meters) is the highest peak in Kerala, Kamet (7,756 meters) is in Uttarakhand, and Mount Everest (8,848.86 meters) is in Nepal, not India. The name Kanchanjunga is derived from Tibetan meaning 'Five Treasures of Snow'.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak in India → Kanchanjunga (8,586 m)
☛ Kanchanjunga is in which state? → Sikkim
☛ Highest peak in the world → Mount Everest (Nepal)
☛ Highest peak in Kerala → Anamudi
☛ Highest peak in Uttarakhand → Nanda Devi

q: Which of the following passes connects Srinagar and Leh?
qs.e: Zoji La is a mountain pass in Jammu and Kashmir, connecting Srinagar to Leh. It lies at an elevation of 3,528 meters in the Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas. This pass is crucial for linking the Kargil and Ladakh regions. Nathu La connects Sikkim to China, Bara-lacha-La is in Himachal Pradesh, and Jelep La is on the India-China border in Sikkim.
qs.kf:
☛ Pass connecting Srinagar and Leh → Zoji La
☛ Elevation of Zoji La → 3,528 meters
☛ Zoji La is located in → Pir Panjal range
☛ Zoji La is in which state → Jammu and Kashmir
☛ Nathu La connects → Sikkim and China

q: Which among the following hills has Indian desert to its western margin?
qs.e: The Aravali mountain range is located in the western part of India, and the Thar Desert (Indian desert) lies to its western margin. This range extends from Rajasthan to Gujarat and is one of the oldest fold mountains in the world. Due to the desert on its west, the region experiences arid and semi-arid climate. Among the given options, Kanchenjunga is in the eastern Himalayas, Palani hills are in South India, and Dhupgarh is part of the Mahadeo hills in Madhya Pradesh. Hence, only the Aravali range has the Indian desert on its western side.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest fold mountain in India → Aravali
☛ State where Thar Desert is located → Rajasthan
☛ Highest peak of Aravali range → Guru Shikhar
☛ Extent of Aravali range → Rajasthan to Gujarat
☛ Other name for Indian desert → Thar Desert

q: The highest point of Andaman and Nicobar islands is called___________.
qs.e: The highest point of the Andaman and Nicobar islands is Saddle Peak (732 meters), located in North Andaman. It is the highest elevation in the archipelago except for the active volcano on Barren Island. Saddle Peak gets its name from its saddle-like shape. The area is rich in biodiversity and hosts many rare birds and wildlife. Other options: Mount Pulag is in the Philippines, Semeru in Indonesia, and Teide in the Canary Islands.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest point of Andaman Islands → Saddle Peak
☛ Height of Saddle Peak → 732 meters
☛ Location of Saddle Peak → North Andaman
☛ Active volcano in Andaman → Barren Island
☛ Highest point of Nicobar Islands → Mount Thulier (642 meters)

q: The salt-water crocodile is found in:
qs.e: The salt-water crocodile (Crocodylus porosus) is the largest living reptile, found mainly in Southeast Asia, northern Australia, and in India specifically in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It inhabits mangrove swamps, river estuaries, and coastal areas. In India, its presence is largely restricted to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where special sanctuaries have been established for its conservation. This species is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List. Other options like Karnataka, Kerala, and Daman and Diu do not have natural populations of this crocodile.
qs.kf:
☛ Scientific name of salt-water crocodile → Crocodylus porosus
☛ Largest habitat area of salt-water crocodile → Northern Australia
☛ Main location of salt-water crocodile in India → Andaman and Nicobar Islands
☛ IUCN status of salt-water crocodile → Vulnerable
☛ Average size of salt-water crocodile → 4-5 meters long

q: Which two land masses does the Palk Strait separate?
o: Malay Peninsula and Indonesian island of Sumatra
qs.e: The Palk Strait is a narrow waterway located between the Tamil Nadu state of India and the Northern Province of Sri Lanka. It connects the Bay of Bengal to the Gulf of Mannar. Its width ranges from approximately 40 to 85 miles. The strait is not navigable for large ships due to its shallow waters and reefs. It is an important geographical feature in the southern part of the Asian continent.
qs.kf:
☛ Which two countries does the Palk Strait separate? → India and Sri Lanka
☛ Which water bodies does the Palk Strait connect? → Bay of Bengal and Gulf of Mannar
☛ What is the approximate width of the Palk Strait? → 40 to 85 miles
☛ Which Indian state does the Palk Strait border? → Tamil Nadu
☛ After whom is the Palk Strait named? → Robert Palk

q: Which of the following is situated at the mouth of the Gulf of Kutch?
qs.e: Kandla Port, located in Gujarat, is situated at the mouth of the Gulf of Kutch. It is a major seaport on the western coast of India and one of the busiest ports in the country. Kandla is a tidal port developed in the 1950s, emerging as an alternative to Karachi Port after the partition of India. It handles exports and imports of crude oil, grain, and chemicals. Porbandar is on the Arabian Sea, Mumbai in Maharashtra, and Mormugao in Goa. Thus, Kandla is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Kandla Port located? → Gujarat
☛ At the mouth of which gulf is Kandla Port situated? → Gulf of Kutch
☛ When was Kandla Port developed? → 1950s
☛ Which port was Kandla an alternative to? → Karachi Port
☛ What type of port is Kandla? → Tidal port

q: Dhoopgarh is the highest peak of the ________ mountain range.
qs.e: Dhoopgarh (1350 m) is the highest peak of the Satpura mountain range. Located in the Pachmarhi region of Madhya Pradesh, it is also known as the 'Pachmarhi summit'. The Satpura range runs east-west across central India, extending from Gujarat to Chhattisgarh. It was formed due to the breaking of the Gondwana landmass. Other major peaks include Mahendragiri (Eastern Ghats) and Gurushikhar (Aravalli).
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Satpura Range → Dhoopgarh (1350 m)
☛ Highest peak of Aravalli Range → Gurushikhar (1722 m)
☛ Highest peak of Vindhya Range → Kaimur Peak (700 m)
☛ Ajanta Hills → in Maharashtra, not an extension of Satpura
☛ Dhoopgarh is located in → Pachmarhi, Madhya Pradesh

q: The Dhauladhar range in the Himalayas is a part of ______.
qs.e: The Dhauladhar range is a prominent mountain range in the Himalayas, located in Himachal Pradesh. It is a part of the Middle Himalayas, also known as the Himachal Himalaya. The Middle Himalayas lie south of the Greater Himalayas and have an average elevation between 3,000 and 6,000 meters. Dhauladhar means 'White Mountain' and extends north of the Kangra Valley. This range is distinct from the Pir Panjal range and is famous for its snow-capped peaks. The Lower Himalayas and Shivaliks are to its south, while the Trans-Himalaya is to the north.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Dhauladhar range located? → Himachal Pradesh
☛ What is the average elevation of the Middle Himalayas? → 3,000-6,000 meters
☛ What is another name for the Middle Himalayas? → Himachal Himalaya
☛ What is the literal meaning of Dhauladhar? → White Mountain
☛ Which valley lies south of the Dhauladhar range? → Kangra Valley

q: What is the correct sequence of following mountain ranges of India from north to south?
1. Vindhya Range
2. Aravalli Range
3. Ajanta Range
4. Satpura Range
qs.e: The correct north-to-south sequence of the major mountain ranges of India is: Aravalli Range (2) is the northernmost, followed by Vindhya Range (1), then Satpura Range (4), and finally Ajanta Range (3) in the south. The Aravalli Range extends from Delhi to Gujarat and is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges in the world. The Vindhya Range runs east-west across central India, lying north of the Narmada River. The Satpura Range is located south of the Vindhyas and is also known as the Mahadeo Hills. The Ajanta Range is situated in Maharashtra and is famous for the Ajanta Caves. This order helps in understanding the physiographic divisions of the Peninsular Plateau of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Aravalli Range → Guru Shikhar
☛ Vindhya Range lies north of which river → Narmada
☛ Other name of Satpura Range → Mahadeo Hills
☛ Ajanta Range is located in which state → Maharashtra
☛ World's oldest mountain range → Aravalli

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following is not a surrounding feature of the Thar Desert?
qs.e: The Thar Desert is located in northwestern India. Its surrounding geographical features include the Aravalli Range to the northeast, the Rann of Kachchh to the south, and the Indus River Plain to the west. The Vindhya Hills are situated in central India, far from the Thar Desert, thus they are not a surrounding feature. The Thar Desert extends across Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana. It is the 17th largest desert in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Which feature borders the Thar Desert to the south? → Rann of Kachchh
☛ Which mountain range lies to the northeast of the Thar Desert? → Aravalli Range
☛ Which plain is to the west of the Thar Desert? → Indus River Plain
☛ In which state are the Vindhya Hills located? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Which states does the Thar Desert cover? → Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which zone of the Great Indian Plains has high humidity and marshy conditions?
qs.e: The Terai region is a part of the Great Northern Plains of India, located near the foothills of the Himalayas. It lies to the south of the Bhabar belt. This zone is characterized by high humidity and marshy conditions because the underground water comes close to the surface and many small streams reappear here. The Terai region has dense forests and rich biodiversity. In contrast, the Bhabar region is composed of gravel and pebbles, where water percolates rapidly. The Bhangar is an old alluvial plain, while the Delta forms at the river mouths. The Terai is fertile for agriculture, especially for sugarcane, wheat, and rice cultivation.
qs.kf:
☛ Which zone lies south of the Bhabar belt? → Terai
☛ What type of soil is found in the Terai? → Marshy and alluvial
☛ What is the main feature of the Bhabar belt? → Gravel and pebbles
☛ What is the Bhangar region? → Old alluvial plain
☛ Where does a delta form? → At the mouth of a river

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Most of the Thar Desert lies in which direction with respect to the Aravalli Hills?
qs.e: The Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert) is located to the north-west of the Aravalli Hills. The desert spreads across Rajasthan, lying in the north-western part of the Aravalli range. The Aravalli Hills run in a north-east to south-west direction, and the Thar Desert falls in the rain shadow region of these hills. As a result, the area receives very low rainfall and is characterized by sand dunes. The Thar Desert extends into parts of Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, but the major portion lies in Rajasthan, to the north-west of the Aravalli Hills.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Thar Desert mostly spread? → Rajasthan
☛ What is the highest peak of the Aravalli Range? → Guru Shikhar
☛ What is the Thar Desert also known as? → Great Indian Desert
☛ What type of mountain range is the Aravalli Hills? → Fold mountains
☛ Which is the major river flowing in the Thar Desert? → Luni

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which region in India is the least populated due to physical barriers and limited accessibility?
qs.e: The least populated region in India due to physical barriers and limited accessibility is the Northern Himalayas, specifically Ladakh. This area is characterized by high mountain ranges, difficult terrain, and extreme cold climate, which restrict movement and settlement. Located in Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh has a population density of about 4 persons per sq km. In contrast, the Ganga Basin is highly fertile, Eastern Rajasthan is relatively more populated, and Coastal Andhra Pradesh has higher density. The major town in Ladakh is Leh. The region is the source of the Indus River and is known for its Buddhist culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Least population density region in India → Ladakh
☛ Main town of Ladakh → Leh
☛ Major river in Ladakh → Indus
☛ Major language of Ladakh → Ladakhi
☛ Famous mountain pass in Ladakh → Khardung La

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 2
q: The Kalapani dispute is between India and which of these?
qs.e: The Kalapani dispute is a border dispute between India and Nepal over the Kalapani, Lipulekh, and Limpiyadhura areas in the Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand. This region is strategically important as it hosts the Kailash Mansarovar route. Nepal claims that according to the 1816 Sugauli Treaty, the area lies east of the Kali River, while India argues that the river's origin is different and the area belongs to India. The dispute escalated in 2020 after India opened the Lipulekh Pass on the China border. Nepal objected and amended its constitution to update the national map to include these areas. The dispute remains unresolved.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Kalapani region located? → Uttarakhand
☛ Which river is involved in the Kalapani dispute? → Kali River
☛ In which year was the Sugauli Treaty signed? → 1816
☛ Which pilgrimage route is associated with Kalapani? → Kailash Mansarovar route
☛ In which year did Nepal amend its map? → 2020

q: What is the approximate total length of coastline of India including the coastline of Lakshadweep islands and Andaman & Nicobar Islands?
qs.e: The total coastline of India, including the mainland and island groups, is approximately 7516.6 km. This includes the mainland coastline of 6100 km, the Andaman & Nicobar Islands' coastline of 1195 km, and the Lakshadweep Islands' coastline of 132 km. India has the 9th largest coastline in the world. The country's maritime boundary extends 12 nautical miles (22.2 km) into the sea. Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states (about 1600 km). The coastline touches the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of India's coastline (including islands) → 7517 km (approx)
☛ Length of mainland coastline of India → 6100 km
☛ Coastline of Andaman & Nicobar Islands → 1195 km
☛ Coastline of Lakshadweep Islands → 132 km
☛ Indian state with the longest coastline → Gujarat (approx 1600 km)

q: Which of the following is not one of the three business check posts between India and China?
qs.e: The three business check posts between India and China are Nathula Pass (Sikkim), Shipki La Pass (Himachal Pradesh), and Lipulekh Pass (Uttarakhand). These passes are open for trade along the India-China border. Khyber Pass is located between Afghanistan and Pakistan, not on the India-China border. Hence, Khyber Pass is not one of these three check posts.
qs.kf:
☛ Nathula Pass → Located in Sikkim, open for India-China trade
☛ Shipki La Pass → Located in Himachal Pradesh, India-China trade route
☛ Lipulekh Pass → Located in Uttarakhand, India-China trade check post
☛ Khyber Pass → Not on India-China border, between Afghanistan and Pakistan
☛ India-China business check posts → Nathula, Shipki La, Lipulekh

q: Which of the following countries shares some part of the Rann of Kutch with India?
qs.e: The Rann of Kutch, located in the Indian state of Gujarat, is a large salt marsh region. It extends along the border between India and Pakistan. A part of Pakistan's Sindh province falls in the western portion of the Rann of Kutch. The border dispute was resolved through the International Court of Justice after the 1965 India-Pakistan war. This area is of great geographical and strategic importance. It floods during the monsoon and dries up in summer. The region is also famous for its wildlife and migratory birds.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Rann of Kutch located? → Gujarat, India
☛ Which country shares the Rann of Kutch with India? → Pakistan
☛ After which war was the border dispute resolved? → 1965 war
☛ What type of terrain is the Rann of Kutch? → Salt marsh
☛ Which organization resolved the border dispute? → International Court of Justice

q: Which of the following areas have an uplifted region and saline sandy flats and swamps?
qs.e: The Rann of Kutch is a distinctive geographical region in western India characterized by an uplifted region, saline sandy flats, and swamps. Located mainly in Gujarat, its elevated part was once part of the ancient seabed that rose due to tectonic movements. The saline flats form after monsoon evaporation, while swamps appear when these salt plains get waterlogged. This area is ecologically important, hosting migratory birds like flamingos. Other options like the Ganga Brahmaputra Delta, Malabar Coast, and Konkan Coast lack such features. The Rann of Kutch is known for its unique landscape and biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Rann of Kutch located? → Gujarat
☛ What type of soil is found in the Rann of Kutch? → Saline soil
☛ Which national park is located in the Rann of Kutch? → Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary
☛ Which major festival is celebrated in the Rann of Kutch? → Rann Utsav
☛ What geological process formed the Rann of Kutch? → Tectonic uplift

q: Which of the following is an important mountain pass in the Western Ghats mountain range, in southwestern India that connects the Nilgiri Hills to the north and Anaimalai Hills to the south?
qs.e: The Palakkad Gap is a significant mountain pass in the Western Ghats, located in the state of Kerala. It connects the Nilgiri Hills to the north and the Anaimalai Hills to the south. This gap provides a natural corridor between the Eastern and Western Ghats and allows monsoon winds to penetrate into the interior regions of Tamil Nadu. The Palakkad Gap is about 30-40 kilometers wide and approximately 300 meters above sea level. It serves as a crucial geographical and economic link in South India, facilitating travel and trade between Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
qs.kf:
☛ State → Kerala
☛ Connects → Nilgiri and Anaimalai Hills
☛ Elevation → About 300 meters
☛ Width → 30-40 kilometers
☛ Significance → Natural corridor between Eastern and Western Ghats

q: The highest peak of Satpura is -
qs.e: The Satpura mountain range, located in central India, extends across Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat. Its highest peak is Dhoopgarh, with an elevation of approximately 1350 meters. Dhoopgarh is situated in the Pachmarhi region of Madhya Pradesh and is often called the 'Crown of Satpura'. This peak is a famous tourist destination known for its stunning views of sunrise and sunset. Guru Shikhar is the highest peak of the Aravalli range, Parasnath of the Chota Nagpur Plateau, and Mahendragiri is a peak of the Eastern Ghats.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Satpura → Dhoopgarh
☛ Height of Dhoopgarh → 1350 meters
☛ Location of Dhoopgarh → Pachmarhi, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Highest peak of Aravalli → Guru Shikhar
☛ Highest peak of Chota Nagpur Plateau → Parasnath

q: From which plateau does the Godavari River originate?
qs.e: The Godavari River originates from the Trimbak Plateau located in the Nashik district of Maharashtra. This plateau is part of the Western Ghats and lies at an elevation of about 1,067 meters above sea level. The Godavari is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South) and is the longest river in peninsular India, with a total length of approximately 1,465 km. It flows eastward and empties into the Bay of Bengal. The Trimbak Plateau is associated with the town of Trimbakeshwar, which houses one of the 12 Jyotirlingas.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Godavari River → Trimbak Plateau
☛ Total length of Godavari River → Approximately 1,465 km
☛ Godavari River is also known as → Dakshin Ganga
☛ Mouth of Godavari River → Bay of Bengal
☛ Major city on Godavari River → Nashik

q: Which of the following statements are correct with respect to Arunachal Himalaya? Statement 1: These extend from the east of the Bhutan Himalayas up to the Diphu pass in the east. Statement 2: The general direction of the mountain range is from southwest to northeast. Statement 3: Some of the important mountain peaks of the region are K2 and Annapurna.
Statement 4: These ranges are dissected by fast-flowing rivers from the north to the south, forming deep gorges.
qs.e: The Arunachal Himalayas extend from the east of the Bhutan Himalayas up to the Diphu pass in the east, making Statement 1 correct. The general direction of this mountain range is from southwest to northeast, which validates Statement 2. K2 and Annapurna are located in the Karakoram and Nepal Himalayas respectively, not in the Arunachal region, so Statement 3 is incorrect. These ranges are dissected by fast-flowing rivers from north to south, such as the Siang, Lohit, and Subansiri, forming deep gorges, making Statement 4 correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Extent of Arunachal Himalaya → From east of Bhutan Himalayas to Diphu pass
☛ Direction of Arunachal Himalaya → Southwest to northeast
☛ Rivers in Arunachal Himalaya → Siang, Lohit, Subansiri
☛ K2 is located in → Karakoram range
☛ Annapurna is located in → Nepal Himalayas

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which group of islands lies between 8° – 12° 13″ North latitude and 71° – 74° East longitude?
qs.e: Lakshadweep is the smallest Union Territory of India, located in the Arabian Sea between 8°–12°13' North latitude and 71°–74° East longitude. It consists of 36 islands, of which 11 are inhabited. Its capital is Kavaratti. This group of islands is made of coral reefs and shares a maritime border with the Maldives. Minicoy is the southernmost island. The name Lakshadweep means 'one lakh islands'. The main language is Malayalam, and the tribal language is Mahal. It is famous for tourism and rich in biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Lakshadweep → Kavaratti
☛ Total islands in Lakshadweep → 36
☛ Southernmost island of Lakshadweep → Minicoy
☛ Literal meaning of Lakshadweep → One lakh islands
☛ Largest island of Lakshadweep → Andrott

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which factor primarily contributed to the development of nucleated settlements in the Bundelkhand region of central India?
qs.e: The Bundelkhand region historically faced frequent invasions and insecurity, prompting people to settle in clustered or nucleated settlements for collective defense. These compact settlements facilitate mutual protection. Other factors like trade routes, fertile soil, or mineral resources were less influential in this region due to its dry and rocky terrain. Therefore, security concerns were the primary driver of nucleated settlement development in Bundelkhand.
qs.kf:
☛ Primary factor for settlements in Bundelkhand → Security concerns
☛ What is a nucleated settlement → A clustered or compact settlement
☛ Bundelkhand covers which states → Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
☛ Major rivers of Bundelkhand → Ken, Betwa
☛ Main crops in Bundelkhand → Sorghum, Pearl millet

q: To which archipelago does Diego Garcia island belong?
qs.e: Diego Garcia island is part of the Chagos Archipelago, located in the Indian Ocean. It is a territory of the British Indian Ocean Territory (BIOT). The island is strategically important and is leased to the United States for a military base by the United Kingdom. The Chagos Archipelago comprises about 60 islands. In 2019, the International Court of Justice ruled that the UK should end its administration of the archipelago. Mauritius claims sovereignty over the region.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Diego Garcia located? → Indian Ocean
☛ Which territory does Chagos Archipelago belong to? → British Indian Ocean Territory (BIOT)
☛ Which country has a military base on Diego Garcia? → United States
☛ Which country claims sovereignty over Chagos Archipelago? → Mauritius
☛ What was the former name of Diego Garcia? → Sometimes called 'Army'

q: Which one of the following channel separates Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
qs.e: The Ten Degrees Channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands. It is named so because it lies along the 10° north latitude. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a Union Territory of India located in the Bay of Bengal. The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives, while the Nine Degree Channel lies between Minicoy and the Lakshadweep archipelago. The Hindenberg Channel is located in Antarctica. Therefore, the correct answer is the Ten Degrees Channel.
qs.kf:
☛ Channel separating Andaman and Nicobar → Ten Degrees Channel
☛ Channel separating Minicoy and Maldives → Eight Degree Channel
☛ Channel between Minicoy and Lakshadweep → Nine Degree Channel
☛ Capital of Andaman and Nicobar Islands → Port Blair
☛ Southernmost point of India → Indira Point (Great Nicobar)

q: Of which of the following are iron and steel factories in the region?
qs.e: The Chota Nagpur Plateau is a major center of iron and steel industry in India. This region is rich in raw materials like iron ore, coal, limestone, and manganese. Major steel plants located here include Jamshedpur (Tata Steel), Bokaro (SAIL), Durgapur, and Rourkela. The establishment of these plants was facilitated by the water resources and coal fields of the Damodar River Valley. Among the options, the Hooghly River Basin is known for jute industry, the Malwa Plateau is primarily agricultural, and the Deccan Plateau is less conducive for steel production.
qs.kf:
☛ Major minerals found in the Chota Nagpur Plateau → Iron ore, coal, limestone, manganese
☛ Headquarters of Tata Steel → Jamshedpur, Jharkhand
☛ Ownership of Bokaro Steel Plant → Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)
☛ River on which Durgapur Steel Plant is located → Damodar River
☛ State where Rourkela Steel Plant is situated → Odisha

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which island was renamed as Swaraj Dweep?
qs.e: The Indian government decided to rename several islands in the Andaman and Nicobar archipelago to reflect Indian values. Havelock Island was renamed as Swaraj Dweep. This change was announced during President Ram Nath Kovind's visit in December 2018. In the same series, Ross Island was renamed as Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep, Neil Island as Shaheed Dweep, while Barren Island remained unchanged. This move aimed to remove colonial names and instill national pride. The islands are part of the Andaman district, and the renaming was widely appreciated as a step towards decolonization.

☛ New name of Neil Island → Shaheed Dweep

q: The Indian National Army reclaimed the Andaman and Nicobar Island from British rule and named them?
qs.e: The Indian National Army (INA), under the leadership of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, liberated the Andaman and Nicobar Islands from British rule in 1943 during World War II. The INA renamed them as 'Shaheed Island' (for North Andaman) and 'Swaraj Island' (for South Andaman). This was a significant event as it marked the first time the INA hoisted the Indian flag on Indian soil. However, the British forces recaptured the islands in 1945. This act showcased the INA's determination and contribution to India's freedom struggle, inspiring many Indians.
qs.kf:

☛ Who was the leader of INA? → Subhas Chandra Bose

q: Which of the following is NOT the Indian research station in Antarctica?
qs.e: India has three research stations in Antarctica: Dakshin Gangotri (established in 1983, first station), Maitri (1989, current main station), and Bharati (2012, newest station). These are all part of the Indian Antarctic Programme. Himalaya is not a research station; it is a mountain range. Therefore, Option 4 Himalaya is the correct answer. The other three options are actual Indian research stations in Antarctica.

q: On which island do the Mishing tribes live?
qs.e: The Mishing (also spelled Mising or Mishing) tribe resides on Majuli Island, located in the Brahmaputra River in the Indian state of Assam. Majuli is the world's largest river island and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (tentative list). The Mishing people speak the Mishing language, which belongs to the Tibeto-Burman language family, and they primarily practice agriculture, especially rice cultivation. This tribe is known for its rich cultural heritage, including traditional dances and festivals. Majuli faces environmental threats from floods and erosion, endangering the tribal communities living there. The other options—Minicoy, an island in Lakshadweep; Lakshadweep, a union territory; and Andaman Island—are incorrect as the Mishing tribe is exclusively found on Majuli Island.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Majuli Island located? → Brahmaputra River
☛ What language do the Mishing tribe speak? → Mishing language (Tibeto-Burman family)
☛ In which state is Majuli Island situated? → Assam
☛ Which is the world's largest river island? → Majuli Island
☛ What is the primary occupation of the Mishing tribe? → Agriculture (rice cultivation)

q: Which of the following animal species is special to the Western Ghats?
qs.e: The Nilgiri tahr is an endemic species of the Western Ghats, found only in the mountainous regions of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. It is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List and is primarily protected in Eravikulam National Park, Mukurthi National Park, and Periyar Tiger Reserve. The Nilgiri tahr is identified by its small size, short horns, and brownish-grey coat, with males having a white patch on the neck. This species inhabits the high-altitude grasslands and rocky slopes of the Western Ghats. While hornbills, elephants, and tigers also occur in the Western Ghats, only the Nilgiri tahr is endemic to this region, making it special. Its scientific name is Nilgiritragus hylocrius.
qs.kf:
☛ Scientific name of Nilgiri tahr → Nilgiritragus hylocrius
☛ IUCN status of Nilgiri tahr → Endangered
☛ Eravikulam National Park is famous for → Nilgiri tahr conservation
☛ Another endemic species of Western Ghats → Malabar civet
☛ Habitat of Nilgiri tahr → High-altitude grasslands of Western Ghats

q: What is the outermost range of the Himalayas called?
qs.e: The outermost range of the Himalayas is called the Shiwaliks. It is one of the three main ranges of the Himalayas. Its average height is between 900 to 1200 meters. The Shiwalik range lies between the Great Himalayas and the Gangetic plains. It is also known as the Outer Himalayas or the Sub-Himalayas. This range extends from Jammu and Kashmir to Assam. The Shiwaliks are composed of sediments brought down by rivers from the higher ranges. They are geologically the youngest part of the Himalayas.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest range of Himalayas → Himadri (Greater Himalayas)
☛ Middle range of Himalayas → Himachal (Lesser Himalayas)
☛ Other name for Shiwalik range → Outer Himalayas or Sub-Himalayas
☛ Three parallel ranges of Himalayas → Himadri, Himachal, Shiwaliks
☛ Average height of Shiwalik range → 900-1200 meters

q: What is the annual average rainfall in the Indian Desert?
qs.e: The Indian Desert, also known as the Thar Desert, is spread across Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana. This region has an extremely arid climate with very low annual average rainfall. The rainfall primarily comes from the southwest monsoon, but due to the parallel flow of the Aravalli range, precipitation is minimal. The average annual rainfall is less than 150 mm, making it the driest region in India. In some parts, the rainfall is even less than 100 mm. This low rainfall results in sparse vegetation and the presence of sand dunes. The Thar Desert covers about 2.3 lakh square kilometers and is one of the most populated deserts in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Area of Thar Desert → Approximately 2.3 lakh sq km
☛ Extent of Thar Desert → Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana
☛ Main source of rainfall → Southwest monsoon
☛ Highest rainfall location → Mount Abu (Rajasthan)
☛ Lowest rainfall area → Jaisalmer (Rajasthan)

q: The longitudinal valleys between the lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks are called:
qs.e: The Himalayas consist of three parallel ranges: the Himadri (Great Himalayas), the Lesser Himalayas (Middle Himalayas), and the Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas). The longitudinal valleys lying between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks are called Duns. These valleys are filled with gravel, sand, and soil brought by rivers. Famous Duns include Dehradun, Patiala Dun, and Kotli Dun. Doabs refer to land between two rivers, Meanders are river bends, and Khadars are the newer floodplain deposits.

q: Which of the following physiographic regions lies north of the Narmada River?
qs.e: The Narmada River flows from west to east in central India and divides the country into two major physiographic divisions. To the north of the Narmada lies the Central Highland region, of which the Malwa Plateau is a prominent part. This plateau is mainly spread across Madhya Pradesh and is formed of basaltic lava, giving rise to black soil (regur). The Deccan, Karnataka, and Telangana plateaus are all located south of the Narmada. Hence, among the given options, only the Malwa Plateau lies north of the Narmada River.

q: The Eastern Coastal Plains of India are best described as which type of coast?
qs.e: The Eastern Coastal Plains of India, comprising the Northern Circar coast and the Southern Coromandel coast, are examples of emergent coasts. These coasts are formed due to a relative fall in sea level or uplift of land. In contrast, the Western Coastal Plains are submerged coasts. On the eastern coast, deposition of sediments brought by rivers has created extensive deltas and flat plains. The coastline is linear and relatively straight, with few bays and peninsulas. Emergent coasts are characterized by shallow waters and the presence of marine terraces.
qs.kf:
☛ Which type of coast is the Western Coastal Plain of India? → Submerged coast
☛ Which major rivers form deltas on the eastern coast? → Ganga, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri

☛ In which state is the Coromandel Coast located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ What are the two divisions of the Eastern Coastal Plain? → Northern Circar Coast and Southern Coromandel Coast

q: Which physiographic feature lies parallel to the Shiwaliks and is about 8-16 km wide?
qs.e: The Bhabar is a narrow belt lying parallel to the Shiwalik hills, with a width ranging from 8 to 16 km. It constitutes the northernmost part of the Northern Plains of India. This region is characterized by the deposition of pebbles and boulders carried down by rivers as they descend from the mountains. The soil here is coarse and porous, leading to a deep water table, making it unsuitable for agriculture. The Bhabar belt is followed by the Terai region to its south, which is marshy and has a high water table.

q: Which of the following is the highest peak of the Maikal range?
qs.e: The Maikal range is located in Madhya Pradesh and is a part of the Satpura range. Its highest peak is Amarkantak, with an elevation of about 1,048 meters. Amarkantak is not only the highest point of the Maikal range but also holds religious significance as the source of the Narmada, Son, and Johila rivers. Other options: Kalsubai is the highest peak of Maharashtra, Guru Shikhar is the highest peak of the Aravali range, and Anamudi is the highest peak in South India. Therefore, the highest peak of the Maikal range is Amarkantak.

q: Which branch of Physical Geography is devoted to the study of landforms, their evolution and related processes?
qs.e: Geomorphology is the branch of Physical Geography that studies landforms, their origin, evolution, and the processes that shape them. It focuses on the scientific analysis of landforms such as valleys, mountains, plateaus, and plains, which are created by processes like erosion, weathering, mass wasting, and deposition. Unlike Climatology (study of climate), Soil Geography (study of soils), and Hydrology (study of water), geomorphology specifically deals with the Earth's surface features and the dynamic forces that modify them over time. Understanding these landforms is crucial for predicting future changes and assessing natural hazards.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of Geomorphology? → W.M. Davis
☛ Who proposed the cycle of erosion theory? → W.M. Davis
☛ Which theory did Penck propose? → Slope development theory
☛ Which scientific method is used in landform study? → Process-response system
☛ Which process breaks rocks to form landforms? → Weathering and erosion

q: Himalayas are divided into:
qs.e: The Himalayas are divided into three main ranges: Himadri (Greater Himalayas), Himachal (Lesser Himalayas), and Shivalik (Outer Himalayas). Himadri is the highest range, containing peaks like Everest and K2. Himachal is the middle range, including Kashmir valley and hill stations. Shivalik is the southernmost and newest range, formed by sediments brought by rivers. Other options include Satpura, Sahyadri (Western Ghats), and Vindhyas, which are not part of the Himalayas.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the highest Himalayan range? → Himadri (Greater Himalayas)

☛ Which is the southernmost part of the Himalayas? → Shivalik

q: The Thar Desert serves as a natural boundary between:
qs.e: The Thar Desert, also known as the 'Great Indian Desert', serves as a natural boundary between India and Pakistan. It covers parts of the Indian state of Rajasthan and the Pakistani provinces of Sindh and Punjab. The desert is located to the northwest of the Aravalli Range, which limits it on the east. The majority of the Thar Desert lies in India (approximately 85%), with the remaining portion in Pakistan. The region is known for its hot desert climate and low rainfall (150-500 mm). It not only acts as a geographical barrier but also forms a cultural and ecological boundary between the two countries.
qs.kf:
☛ Between which two countries does the Thar Desert form a natural boundary? → India and Pakistan
☛ Which Indian state contains the largest part of the Thar Desert? → Rajasthan
☛ Which mountain range limits the Thar Desert on the east? → Aravalli Range
☛ What is the Thar Desert also known as? → Great Indian Desert

q: What is the approximate area covered by the Thar Desert in India?
qs.e: The Thar Desert, also known as the 'Great Indian Desert', is located in the state of Rajasthan, India. Its total area is approximately 2,00,000 km2, out of which 1,70,000 km2 lies in India and 30,000 km2 in Pakistan. It is the world's 20th largest desert. The climate is extremely arid, with annual rainfall between 100-500 mm. The desert features sand dunes, salt flats, and thorny shrubs. Major rivers include Luni and Ghaggar.

q: Which of the following physiographic divisions is a part of the Peninsular Plateau?
qs.e: In the physiographic divisions of India, the Peninsular Plateau is divided into three main parts: the Central Highlands, the Deccan Plateau, and the Eastern and Western Ghats. The Central Highlands extend across central India in the north and include the Aravalli Range, Bundelkhand, and the Malwa Plateau. It forms the northern part of the Peninsular Plateau. The Himalayan Mountains and the Northern Plains are separate geographical units distinct from the Peninsular Plateau. The island groups are also not part of the Peninsular Plateau. Hence, the Central Highlands is the correct option.
qs.kf:

☛ Where is the Aravalli Range located → In Rajasthan, part of Central Highlands
☛ Which rivers surround the Malwa Plateau → Chambal, Sindh, Betwa
☛ Bundelkhand spans which states → Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
☛ Total area of the Peninsular Plateau → About 16 lakh sq km

q: The Bhabar and Terai regions of the Great Indian Plains differ primarily in:
o: Permeability of soil and groundwater availability
qs.e: The primary difference between the Bhabar and Terai regions lies in soil permeability and groundwater availability. Bhabar consists of coarse pebbles and gravel, making it highly permeable, causing rivers to disappear underground and resulting in deep groundwater levels. In contrast, Terai has fine silt and clay with lower permeability, allowing groundwater to come closer to the surface, creating swampy conditions. This makes Terai more fertile and suitable for agriculture. Options 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect because the distinction is fundamentally geological, not influenced by Himalayan rivers, rainfall patterns, or human settlements. Understanding this difference is crucial for questions related to India's physical geography.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the soil type in Bhabar? → Coarse pebbles and gravel
☛ Groundwater condition in Terai? → Shallow, leading to marshy areas
☛ Where do rivers vanish in Bhabar? → Underground
☛ Terai region is suitable for? → Agriculture
☛ Main reason for Bhabar-Terai difference? → Soil permeability

q: The Deccan Plateau is separated from the Chota Nagpur Plateau by which of the following?
qs.e: The Deccan Plateau and the Chota Nagpur Plateau are two major plateaus of India. They are separated by the Vindhya Range. The Vindhya Range runs east-west in central India and is located to the north of the Narmada River. This range separates the Gangetic plains from southern India. The Chota Nagpur Plateau is situated in Jharkhand, while the Deccan Plateau covers most of peninsular India. The Aravalli Hills are in Rajasthan, the Mahanadi Basin is in Odisha, and the Western Ghats run parallel to the western coast. Thus, the correct answer is the Vindhya Range.
qs.kf:
☛ Which mountain range separates the Deccan Plateau from the Chota Nagpur Plateau? → Vindhya Range
☛ The Vindhya Range is located north of which river? → Narmada River
☛ In which state is the Chota Nagpur Plateau located? → Jharkhand
☛ The Aravalli Hills are located in which state? → Rajasthan
☛ The Mahanadi Basin is located in which state? → Odisha

q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of alluvial soils in India?
o: Mainly consists of sand, silt and clay
Primarily found in the Deccan Plateau
qs.e: Alluvial soil is the most fertile soil in India, mainly found in the northern plains and river valleys. It is formed by the deposition of sand, silt and clay brought by rivers. It is rich in potash but deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus. This soil is highly fertile and ideal for crops like wheat, rice and sugarcane. The Deccan Plateau predominantly has black soil (regur), which is not alluvial. Therefore, the feature 'primarily found in the Deccan Plateau' is NOT a characteristic of alluvial soils.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for alluvial soil → River-deposited soil
☛ Where is alluvial soil mainly found? → Northern plains and coastal plains
☛ Which nutrients are deficient in alluvial soil? → Nitrogen and phosphorus
☛ Two types of alluvial soil → Khadar (new) and Bhangar (old)
☛ Most widespread soil in India → Alluvial soil

q: What lies between the sand dunes and the coast in the East Coastal Plains?
qs.e: In the East Coastal Plains, lagoons are located between the sand dunes and the coast. These are shallow water bodies separated from the sea by sand dunes or barriers. Major lagoons on the east coast of India include Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Pulicat Lake (Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border). These lagoons are biodiversity hotspots and important for fisheries and tourism. Deltas form at river mouths, while mountains are far from coastal plains. Beaches are on the seaward side of dunes; lagoons lie between dunes and the coast.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Chilika Lake located? → Odisha
☛ On which states' border is Pulicat Lake? → Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
☛ What lies between sand dunes and the coast? → Lagoons
☛ Which is the largest lagoon in India? → Chilika Lake
☛ How are lagoons formed? → By deposition of sand by sea waves and currents

q: Which peak marks the north-western end of the Great Himalaya?
qs.e: The north-western end of the Great Himalaya is marked by Nanga Parbat (8,126 m), located in Pakistan. It stands at the western extremity of the Himalayan range. In contrast, the eastern end is marked by Namcha Barwa (7,756 m) in Tibet. Mount Everest is the highest peak but not at the terminus. Kanchenjunga is the third highest peak on the Nepal-Sikkim border. Nanga Parbat is also known as the "Killer Mountain" due to its difficulty.

☛ North-western end of Great Himalaya → Nanga Parbat
☛ North-eastern end of Great Himalaya → Namcha Barwa
☛ Highest peak in the world → Mount Everest

q: What is the origin of the material that makes up the Bhabar belt?
o: Debris washed down from high ranges
qs.e: The Bhabar belt is a narrow strip at the base of the Himalayas, south of the Shivalik hills. It is formed by the deposition of pebbles, boulders, and coarse debris carried down by rivers from high mountain ranges. When rivers descend from the mountains to the plains, the steep slope causes them to deposit large amounts of coarse material, creating the Bhabar region. This debris is primarily fluvial deposits brought by Himalayan rivers fed by rainfall and snowmelt. The soil in Bhabar is porous, so most water seeps underground, leading to the emergence of several streams downstream. Thus, the Bhabar belt is made of debris washed down from high mountain ranges.
qs.kf:

☛ Characteristic of Bhabar soil → Coarse, porous, and infertile
☛ Rivers found in Bhabar → Ghaghara, Sharda, etc.
☛ Region after Bhabar → Terai (swampy marshy area)
☛ Depth of groundwater in Bhabar → About 200-300 feet below

q: Which of the following islands is the southernmost point of India?
qs.e: The southernmost point of India is Indira Point, located on Great Nicobar Island in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Formerly known as Pygmalion Point, it was renamed after Indira Gandhi in 1984. It lies at 6°45' North latitude. The 2004 tsunami significantly affected this area, submerging some land. Kavaratti is the capital of Lakshadweep. Little Andaman is part of southern Andaman, while Car Nicobar is the northernmost island of the Nicobar group.

☛ Former name of Indira Point → Pygmalion Point

q: Which of the following factors does NOT contribute to farming variety in India?
qs.e: Factors like soil types, irrigation availability, and climate significantly contribute to farming variety in India. Soil types (alluvial, black, red, laterite) support different crops. Irrigation availability determines crop choice and yield. Climate (temperature and rainfall) influences crop selection. Uniform landform implies no variation in landform, which does not contribute to farming variety. India's diverse landforms (mountains, plains, plateaus) enhance agricultural diversity.

q: As per the India Meteorological Department (IMD), what is the approximate total annual normal rainfall received in the Thar Desert, which has a coefficient of variation (CV) of about 38%?
qs.e: The Thar Desert is an arid region located in the western part of India. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the average annual rainfall in this region is approximately 250 mm. This rainfall is highly variable, with a coefficient of variation (CV) of about 38%, indicating high interannual variability. Due to low rainfall and high evaporation rates, the region falls under arid to semi-arid classification. Most of the precipitation occurs during the summer monsoon season.

q: Which of the following is an example of a minor industrial region of India?
qs.e: The Brahmaputra valley in Assam is an example of a minor industrial region of India. It is known for tea, petroleum, and timber industries. In contrast, the Gujarat region (Ahmedabad-Vadodara), Hugli region (Kolkata-Howrah), and Chota Nagpur region (Jharkhand) are major industrial regions. q: Approximately what percent of the area of India is occupied by plains?
qs.e: Approximately 43% of India's total geographical area is covered by plains. These plains mainly consist of the Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra plains in northern India, formed by fertile alluvial soil deposited by rivers. These are among the world's largest alluvial plains and are highly productive for agriculture due to the Green Revolution. Plains also include the coastal plains, such as the Eastern Coastal Plain and Western Coastal Plain. The remaining area comprises mountains (about 30%) and plateaus (about 27%).

q: Peninsular Plateau consists of which of the following two broad divisions?
o: Shevroy Hills and the Javadi Hills
qs.e: The Peninsular Plateau is a major physiographic division of India. It is broadly divided into two parts: the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau. The Central Highlands lie to the north of the Narmada River and include the Aravalli Range, Bundelkhand, and the Malwa Plateau. The Deccan Plateau is a large triangular plateau south of the Narmada, bounded by the Western Ghats in the west and the Eastern Ghats in the east. It was formed from the breakup of the ancient Gondwana landmass and is covered by extensive black basaltic soil. This division is geographically significant.

q: Who among the following established its factory in Petapuli on the North Coromandel Coast in 1606?
qs.e: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) established its factory at Petapuli (present-day Andhra Pradesh) on the North Coromandel Coast in 1606. This marks the early Dutch presence in India. The Dutch set up multiple factories in India to control the spice trade. The Petapuli factory was mainly used for textile and spice trading. The Dutch East India Company was founded in 1602 and was one of the most powerful trading companies in the 17th century.

q: Which of the following features distinguishes the Purvanchal hills from the rest of the Himalayan mountain system?
o: They stretch in a convex arc along the eastern frontier
They include the Aravalli and Satpura hill groups
They are snow-covered throughout the year
They form the highest peaks of the Zanskar range
qs.e: The Purvanchal hills are the eastern extension of the Himalayan mountain system, located along India's eastern frontier. They are distinguished from the rest of the Himalayas by their convex arc shape. Unlike the main Himalayan ranges, these hills are relatively low in altitude and are not snow-covered throughout the year. The Purvanchal includes hill groups like Patkai, Naga, Manipur, Mizo, Tripura, Mikir, and Garo-Khasi-Jaintia. In contrast, the Aravalli and Satpura ranges belong to the Peninsular India, and the Zanskar range is part of the Central Himalayas. This unique orientation and composition set the Purvanchal apart.
qs.kf:
☛ Key feature of Purvanchal hills → Convex arc along eastern frontier
☛ Major hill groups in Purvanchal → Patkai, Naga, Manipur, Mizo, Tripura, Mikir, Garo-Khasi-Jaintia
☛ Easternmost part of Himalayas → Purvanchal hills
☛ Highest peak of Purvanchal → Mount Saramati (Naga hills)
☛ Extent of Purvanchal → Arunachal Pradesh to Mizoram

q: The “Siachen Glacier,” the world’s highest battlefield, is located to the east of which mountain range?
qs.e: The Siachen Glacier, known as the world's highest battlefield, is located to the east of the Karakoram Range. Situated in the Ladakh region, this glacier is a disputed territory between India and Pakistan. The glacier is approximately 76 km long and sits at an elevation of 5,753 meters. In 1984, during Operation Meghdoot, the Indian Army gained control of the glacier. The Karakoram Range includes notable peaks like K2 (8,611 meters), the second highest in the world. This mountain range extends across Pakistan, India, and China. The Siachen Glacier is a significant strategic location due to its extreme altitude and harsh conditions.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the length of Siachen Glacier? → Approximately 76 km
☛ What is the elevation of Siachen Glacier? → 5,753 meters
☛ Under which operation did India gain control of Siachen? → Operation Meghdoot (1984)
☛ What is the highest peak in the Karakoram Range? → K2 (8,611 meters)
☛ In which Indian state/UT is Siachen Glacier located? → Ladakh

q: In which Indian state do the Western Ghats reach their maximum elevation, marked by the presence of Anaimudi, the highest peak of the range?
qs.e: The Western Ghats, also known as the Sahyadri mountain range, run parallel to the western coast of India. Their highest peak, Anaimudi (2,695 meters), is located in the state of Kerala. Anaimudi lies in the Idukki district of Kerala, within the Eravikulam National Park. This peak represents the maximum elevation of the Western Ghats and is also the highest peak in South India. The Western Ghats in Kerala are rich in biodiversity and have been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Other states like Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka also have portions of the Western Ghats, but the highest peak is situated exclusively in Kerala.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Anaimudi located? → Kerala
☛ Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats? → Anaimudi
☛ What is the height of Anaimudi? → 2,695 meters
☛ Anaimudi is part of which national park? → Eravikulam National Park
☛ The Western Ghats in Kerala are recognized as what? → UNESCO World Heritage Site

q: Which of the following is the highest peak of the Western Ghats mountain range?
qs.e: The highest peak of the Western Ghats is Anaimudi (2,695 m), located in the Idukki district of Kerala. It is part of the Anamalai Hills. The name Anaimudi means 'elephant's forehead' in Malayalam. Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills, while Mullayanagiri (1,930 m) is the highest peak in Karnataka. Mahabaleshwar is a hill station, not a peak. Anaimudi is also the highest peak in South India.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak of Western Ghats? → Anaimudi
☛ Anaimudi is part of which hills? → Anamalai Hills
☛ Highest peak in South India? → Anaimudi
☛ Doddabetta is part of which hills? → Nilgiri Hills
☛ Mullayanagiri is in which state? → Karnataka

q: With reference to fluvial geomorphic processes in the Indian subcontinent, the Indo-Gangetic Plains have been formed predominantly due to the long-term accumulation of which specific type of deposits?
o: Aeolian sand deposits formed under arid climatic conditions
Glacial till deposited directly by valley glaciers
Marine sediments laid down by repeated sea transgressions
Alluvial sediments deposited by Himalayan river systems
qs.e: The Indo-Gangetic Plains have been formed by the long-term accumulation of alluvial sediments brought down by Himalayan rivers such as the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra. These rivers erode the Himalayas and transport huge amounts of sediment, which is deposited on the plains during floods. This process is called alluvial deposition. Geologically, these plains are foredeep basins filled with sediments. The soil here is highly fertile. Aeolian sand, glacial till, or marine sediments are not the primary contributors to the formation of this region.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of deposits form the Indo-Gangetic Plains? → Alluvial deposits
☛ Which river systems are mainly responsible for these deposits? → Himalayan river systems
☛ What is a key characteristic of alluvial soil? → Highly fertile
☛ Geologically, what are these plains? → Foredeep basins
☛ Where do Himalayan rivers deposit their sediment load? → On the floodplains of the plains

q: Which physiographic region of the Northern Plains of India is characterised by a wet, marshy, and swampy surface and lies immediately south of the Bhabar belt due to the re-emergence of rivers?
qs.e: The Northern Plains of India consist of four physiographic regions: Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, and Khadar. The Terai belt lies immediately south of the Bhabar belt. In this region, the rivers re-emerge after disappearing in the Bhabar, leading to a wet, marshy, and swampy surface. The Terai is characterized by thick forests and wildlife. It is a fertile area and important for agriculture. Bhangar is the older alluvium, while Khadar is the newer alluvium. Karewas are lake sediments found in Jammu and Kashmir. Thus, the correct answer is Terai.
qs.kf:
☛ Which region lies south of the Bhabar belt? → Terai
☛ What is the characteristic feature of the Terai region? → Wet, marshy, swampy surface
☛ Why do rivers re-emerge in the Terai? → Groundwater level rises to the surface
☛ What is Bhangar? → Older alluvium
☛ What is Khadar? → Newer alluvium deposited by rivers

q: In which Indian region were ‘guls’ or ‘kuls’ traditionally constructed as diversion channels to carry water from mountain streams for agricultural irrigation?
qs.e: In the Western Himalayas, traditional irrigation channels called 'guls' or 'kuls' were constructed as diversion channels to carry water from mountain streams for agricultural irrigation. These channels are built along the slopes of the Himalayas, using gravity to direct water from streams and rivers to terraced fields. This indigenous technique has been practiced for centuries by local communities in states like Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand. The system is a fine example of sustainable water management in hilly terrain. The construction and maintenance of these channels are often community-driven, reflecting traditional knowledge of hydrology and agriculture.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the gul/kul system prevalent? → Western Himalayas
☛ What is the use of guls/kuls? → Agricultural irrigation
☛ What type of structure are guls/kuls? → Diversion channels
☛ Which states have this system? → Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand
☛ What principle do guls/kuls work on? → Gravity

q: Which mountain ranges traverse the Trans-Himalayan zone in India?
qs.e: The Trans-Himalayan zone consists of mountain ranges north of the Himalayas, forming part of Asia's major mountain systems. In India, these ranges are primarily located in Ladakh and Jammu & Kashmir. The key ranges are the Karakoram, Ladakh, and Zanskar ranges. The Karakoram range hosts the world's second-highest peak, K2 (8611 m). The Ladakh range forms the Ladakh Plateau, India's highest plateau. The Zanskar range lies between the Himalayas and the Ladakh range. These ranges are distinct from the Himalayan range and fall under the Trans-Himalayan region. Other options like Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, Satpura, Aravalli, and Vindhya are not part of the Trans-Himalayan zone. This geographical classification is important for exams.
qs.kf:
☛ What are Trans-Himalayan ranges? → Mountain ranges north of the Himalayas.
☛ Which range contains K2 peak? → Karakoram.
☛ What is India's highest plateau? → Ladakh Plateau.
☛ Where is Zanskar range located? → Between the Himalayas and Ladakh range.
☛ Which Indian states have Trans-Himalayan ranges? → Ladakh and Jammu & Kashmir.

q: Which glacier, located in the Karakoram range, is the longest in this range and the second longest in the world outside the polar regions?
qs.e: The Siachen Glacier is located in the Karakoram range and is the longest glacier in this range. It is the second longest glacier in the world outside the polar regions, with a length of about 76 km. Additionally, it is the largest glacier in Asia, situated on the Line of Control between India and Pakistan. This glacier is the source of the Nubra River and has an elevation of approximately 5,400 meters. The Siachen region also holds military significance as it hosts the highest battlefield in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest glacier in Karakoram range → Siachen
☛ Second longest glacier outside polar regions → Siachen
☛ Largest glacier in Asia → Siachen
☛ Length of Siachen Glacier → about 76 km
☛ Source river of Siachen Glacier → Nubra River

q: Which name is given to the southern stretch of the western coastal plain of India?
qs.e: The western coastal plain of India is divided into three parts: the northern part is called the Konkan coast, the middle part is the Kannad coast, and the southern part is the Malabar coast. The Malabar coast lies in the state of Kerala and is characterized by a narrow strip between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea. It is famous for its coconut plantations, spices, and backwaters. The Coromandel Coast is the southern part of the eastern coastal plain.
qs.kf:
☛ Northern part of western coastal plain → Konkan coast
☛ Middle part of western coastal plain → Kannad coast
☛ Southern part of western coastal plain → Malabar coast
☛ Malabar coast is located in which state? → Kerala
☛ Coromandel Coast is part of which coastal plain? → Eastern coastal plain

q: Which mountain range encompasses the Kashmir, Kangra, and Kullu valleys within the Himalayas?
qs.e: The Kashmir, Kangra, and Kullu valleys are situated within the Lesser Himalayas mountain range. The Lesser Himalayas, also known as the Himachal or Middle Himalayas, lie between the Great Himalayas and the Shivalik ranges. This range comprises mountains with elevations between 3,700 and 4,500 meters. It includes famous valleys like Kashmir, Kangra, and Kullu. The Lesser Himalayas include prominent ranges such as Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, and Mahabharat. This region is known for its natural beauty, lakes, and vegetation. Thus, these valleys are bounded by the Lesser Himalayas.
qs.kf:
☛ Average elevation of the Great Himalayas → Over 6,000 meters
☛ What is the Shivalik range also known as → Outer Himalayas
☛ Major range of the Lesser Himalayas → Pir Panjal
☛ Which river is Kangra valley situated on → Beas River
☛ Kashmir valley lies between which range and the Great Himalayas → Pir Panjal

q: Which Himalayan region has greater altitudinal variations?
qs.e: The Eastern Himalayan region has greater altitudinal variations. This is because the mountain ranges here are higher and steeper, and the valleys are deeper. This region contains high peaks like Kanchenjunga (8,586 meters) and deep river valleys. Heavy rainfall in the east leads to intense erosion, creating diverse landforms. The Eastern Himalayas include parts of Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, and northern West Bengal. This region is also rich in biodiversity. Altitudinal variation refers to changes in temperature, rainfall, and vegetation with elevation. The Eastern Himalayas experience a greater range of such changes compared to the Western Himalayas, making it the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest peak in Eastern Himalayas → Kanchenjunga (8,586 m)
☛ States included in Eastern Himalayas → Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, West Bengal
☛ Main cause of altitudinal variation → Climate change with elevation
☛ A major river in Eastern Himalayas → Teesta
☛ Compared to Western Himalayas, Eastern Himalayas have more → rainfall and biodiversity

q: Which plateau belt in India is notably rich in both iron ore and coal resources?
qs.e: The North-Eastern Plateau region of India, which includes the Chotanagpur Plateau (Jharkhand), parts of Odisha and West Bengal, is notably rich in both iron ore and coal resources. This area holds a significant portion of India's iron ore reserves and also contains the Gondwana coal fields, which contribute substantially to the country's coal production. Major iron ore mines like Noamundi, Gua and Kiriburu are located here, while coal fields such as Jharia, Bokaro and Raniganj are prominent. This region is also industrially important, hosting steel plants like Bokaro and Jamshedpur, which utilize these resources. The abundance of both iron ore and coal makes it a key belt for the mining and industrial sectors in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Major iron ore belt in North-Eastern Plateau → Singhbhum-Odisha belt
☛ Largest coal field in this region → Jharia coal field
☛ Steel plants located in North-Eastern Plateau → Bokaro and Jamshedpur
☛ Location of Gondwana coal fields → Eastern India
☛ Other key minerals in this plateau → Mica, copper, bauxite

q: Which of the following sectors of the western coastal plain extends between Mumbai and Goa?
qs.e: The western coastal plain is divided into three sections: the Konkan Coast (Mumbai to Goa) in the north, the Karnataka Coast (Goa to Mangalore) in the middle, and the Malabar Coast (Mangalore to Kanyakumari) in the south. The Konkan Coast stretches through the states of Maharashtra and Goa, as well as the northern part of Karnataka. It is a narrow strip with small creeks and rivers between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea. Major rivers include Ulhas, Vaitarna, Savitri, and Mandovi. The Coromandal Coast is part of the eastern coastal plain, located in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Extent of Konkan Coast → Mumbai to Goa
☛ Extent of Karnataka Coast → Goa to Mangalore
☛ Extent of Malabar Coast → Mangalore to Kanyakumari
☛ Southernmost part of western coastal plain → Malabar Coast
☛ Location of Coromandal Coast → Eastern coastal plain

q: Which coastal region of India is associated with the Vembanad Lagoon being separated from the Arabian Sea by narrow barrier islands?
qs.e: The Malabar Coast, situated on the western coast of India, extends over the state of Kerala. This region is associated with the Vembanad Lagoon, the longest lake in India, which is separated from the Arabian Sea by narrow barrier islands. The Malabar Coast is known for its backwaters and river deltas. In contrast, the Konkan Coast lies in Maharashtra-Goa, the Coromandel Coast is on the eastern coast, and the Northern Circars are coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest lagoon in India → Vembanad Lake (Kerala)
☛ Malabar Coast is located in which state → Kerala
☛ Islands separating Vembanad Lagoon from Arabian Sea → Barrier islands
☛ Subdivisions of western coast → Konkan, Kannad, Malabar
☛ Key feature of Malabar Coast → Backwaters and coconut plantations

q: Which of the following island groups in India is known to have an active volcano on Barren Island?
qs.e: Barren Island is India's only active volcano, located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands archipelago. The volcano lies at the convergence zone of the Indian Plate and the Burma Plate. It first erupted in 1991 and has remained active periodically since then. The island is situated in the Andaman Sea, about 140 km east of Port Blair. Barren Island is a stratovolcano, known for explosive eruptions.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is India's only active volcano located? → Barren Island, Andaman and Nicobar
☛ What type of volcano is Barren Island? → Stratovolcano
☛ When did Barren Island volcano first erupt? → 1991
☛ At which plate boundary is Barren Island located? → Indian and Burma Plates
☛ Which island group does Barren Island belong to? → Andaman and Nicobar

q: The Garo, Khasi, Jaintia, and Naga Hills, which run almost east–west, are connected to which hill chain that extends in a north–south direction?
qs.e: The Garo, Khasi, Jaintia, and Naga Hills run east-west and are connected to the Mizo Hills and Rakhine Hills (Arakan Yoma), which extend in a north-south direction. The Rakhine Hills are located in Myanmar and run parallel to India's eastern border. The Mizo Hills are in the state of Mizoram, and together these hill chains link the northeastern hills of India with the mountainous regions of Myanmar. This connection is crucial for understanding the geological structure of Northeast India and the region's biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state are the Garo Hills located in? → Meghalaya
☛ What is the old name of the Rakhine Hills? → Arakan Yoma
☛ Which state are the Mizo Hills located in? → Mizoram
☛ Which hill chain connects the east-west hills of Northeast India? → Mizo and Rakhine Hills
☛ Where are the Khasi and Jaintia Hills located? → Meghalaya

q: The Thar Desert is also referred to as:
qs.e: The Thar Desert is also known as the Great Indian Desert. It is located in the state of Rajasthan, India, and extends into the Sindh province of Pakistan. It is the 17th largest desert in the world. The climate is extremely arid with very low rainfall. The terrain is sandy with sand dunes. The Thar Desert is known for its biodiversity, including various species of plants and animals adapted to the harsh conditions.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Indian state is the Thar Desert located in? → Rajasthan
☛ What is the other name of the Thar Desert? → The Great Indian Desert
☛ What is the rank of the Thar Desert in terms of size in the world? → 17th
☛ Which country does the Thar Desert extend into? → Pakistan
☛ What type of climate does the Thar Desert have? → Arid

q: Which of the following processes is/are primarily responsible for the formation of fold mountains such as the Himalayas?
qs.e: The formation of fold mountains like the Himalayas is primarily due to plate tectonics, where the collision of two tectonic plates generates compressional forces on the Earth's crust. This compression folds sedimentary rocks, giving rise to high mountain ranges. The Himalayas were formed by the collision of the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate. Wind deposition (loess landforms) and river erosion (valley formation) shape mountains but do not create them. Volcanic eruptions form volcanic mountains, not fold mountains. Therefore, plate collision is the primary process for the formation of fold mountains such as the Himalayas.
qs.kf:
☛ What caused the formation of the Himalayas? → Collision of Indian and Eurasian Plates
☛ Main factor for fold mountain formation? → Plate tectonics (compressional forces)
☛ What type of mountain is the Himalayas? → Fold mountain
☛ Which collision formed the Andes? → Nazca and South American Plates
☛ Number of major tectonic plates? → About 7 major and several minor plates

q: Which landform is formed when a glacier erodes a pre-existing river valley by widening, deepening, and smoothing it?
qs.e: When a glacier moves through a pre-existing river valley, it carries ice and debris that widen, deepen, and smooth the valley. Rivers typically form V-shaped valleys, but the immense weight and movement of a glacier straightens the valley walls and broadens the floor, resulting in a U-shaped valley. This is a distinctive erosional landform created by glacial activity. U-shaped valleys are also referred to as glacial troughs. Examples include Yosemite Valley in the USA and many valleys in the Himalayas and Alps.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for U-shaped valley formed by glaciers → Glacial trough
☛ Valley shape formed by river erosion → V-shaped
☛ Valley shape formed by glacial erosion → U-shaped
☛ Main glacial erosion processes → Abrasion and plucking
☛ Example of a U-shaped valley → Yosemite Valley

q: Which of the following separates the Andaman from Nicobar Islands?
qs.e: The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands. This channel is located along the 10° north latitude line. To the north of the channel are the Andaman Islands, and to the south are the Nicobar Islands. The channel is approximately 150 km wide. In comparison, the Nine Degree Channel separates Lakshadweep from Minicoy, while the Six Degree Channel lies between Sumatra and the Nicobar Islands. The Palk Strait separates India from Sri Lanka.
qs.kf:
☛ Channel separating Andaman and Nicobar → Ten Degree Channel
☛ Nine Degree Channel separates → Lakshadweep and Minicoy
☛ Six Degree Channel is located → between Sumatra and Nicobar
☛ Palk Strait separates → India and Sri Lanka
☛ Width of Ten Degree Channel → approximately 150 km

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 1
q: The easternmost extension of the Himalayas does NOT include which of the following?
qs.e: The easternmost extension of the Himalayas is called the Purvanchal Hills, which includes the Naga Hills, Patkai Hills, Mizo Hills, Manipur Hills, and Arakan Yoma. These hills extend up to Myanmar and separate the Assam Valley from Myanmar. The Khasi Hills are not part of the eastern Himalayan extension; along with the Garo and Jaintia Hills, they form the Meghalaya Plateau, which is a part of the Peninsular Plateau. Thus, the Khasi Hills are a distinct geological entity and not part of the Himalayas.
qs.kf:
☛ Easternmost part of Himalayas → Purvanchal
☛ Mountain ranges included in Purvanchal → Naga, Patkai, Mizo, Manipur, Arakan Yoma
☛ Khasi Hills are part of → Meghalaya Plateau
☛ Meghalaya Plateau is part of → Peninsular Plateau
☛ Purvanchal extends up to which country → Myanmar

q: The ravines are generally found in which river basin of India?
qs.e: Ravines (badlands) are commonly found in the basin of the Chambal River. They are widespread across the Chambal region of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. Ravines are formed due to water erosion, where the river's flow creates deep gullies. The Chambal River, with its high silt load and strong current, causes extensive erosion in this area. The soil here is loamy and sandy, which erodes easily. Agriculture in ravine areas is difficult, and these regions have historically been associated with dacoit activity. The government has undertaken water conservation and afforestation measures to control erosion. Other rivers like Periyar, Kaveri, and Vaigai are in peninsular India and do not have ravines.
qs.kf:
☛ In which river basin are ravines found? → Chambal
☛ Where is the origin of Chambal River? → Mhow near Indore
☛ Chambal is a tributary of which river? → Yamuna
☛ The main cause of soil erosion in India? → Water erosion
☛ Which states does the Chambal valley cover? → Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh

q: Which of the following is formed when the river is at very low gradient?
qs.e: When a river flows at a very low gradient, it moves slowly in the plains and forms bends called meanders. Over time, erosion and deposition on the meander neck cause the river to cut through, forming a straight channel. The cut-off meander gets isolated and forms a crescent-shaped lake known as an oxbow lake. This is a result of fluvial erosion and deposition processes in the mature stage of a river. Peneplain is formed by long-term erosion in the lower course, while auxiliary river and river branch are not directly related to gradient. Thus, at very low gradient, an oxbow lake is formed.
qs.kf:
☛ From which meander does an oxbow lake form? → Cut-off meander
☛ In which part of the river does an oxbow lake form? → Lower course (plains)
☛ Where is a peneplain formed? → Lower course of the river
☛ What type of river velocity leads to meanders? → Low velocity
☛ Where are river branches commonly found? → Delta region

q: Which of these lakes is found in Ladakh?
qs.e: Tso Moriri is a high-altitude freshwater lake located in Ladakh, at an elevation of about 4,522 meters. It lies within the Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary and is a designated Ramsar site. The other options: Nainital Lake is in Uttarakhand, Pulicat Lake is on the Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border, and Bhimtal Lake is in Uttarakhand. Tso Moriri is known for its unique biodiversity and serves as a habitat for various migratory birds. It is one of the largest high-altitude lakes in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest lake in Ladakh → Pangong Tso
☛ Highest lake in India → Chola Lake (Sikkim)
☛ Ramsar lake in Ladakh → Tso Moriri
☛ Saltwater lake in Ladakh → Pangong Tso
☛ Lake in Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary → Tso Moriri

q: Which of the following rivers is the tributary of Ganges?
qs.e: The Gandak river is a major tributary of the Ganges. It originates in the Himalayan region of Nepal and joins the Ganges in Bihar. The Gandak is also known as the Narayani or Salgrami river. Manas and Subansiri are tributaries of the Brahmaputra, while Zanskar is a tributary of the Indus. Other important tributaries of the Ganges include Yamuna, Ghaghara, Kosi, and Son. The Gandak has a large catchment area and is known for causing floods.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest tributary of Ganges → Yamuna
☛ Tributary of Brahmaputra → Manas and Subansiri
☛ Tributary of Indus → Zanskar
☛ Other name of Gandak → Narayani or Salgrami
☛ Tributaries of Ganges → Gandak, Kosi, Ghaghara

q: National waterway number 2 has been established on which river?
qs.e: National Waterway Number 2 (NW-2) has been established on the Brahmaputra River in the northeastern states of India.
