It stretches from Dhubri to Sadiya in Assam, covering a distance of about 891 kilometers. The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet, flows through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, and enters Bangladesh. NW-2 is operated by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI). This waterway plays a crucial role in promoting transportation and trade in the region. Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, a total of 111 national waterways have been declared in the country.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is National Waterway Number 1 located? → Ganga
☛ On which river is National Waterway Number 3 located? → West Coast Canal (Kerala)
☛ Which rivers are connected by National Waterway Number 4? → Krishna and Godavari
☛ What is the full form of IWAI? → Inland Waterways Authority of India
☛ Which is the longest national waterway? → NW-1 (Ganga, 1620 km)

q: Which of the following rivers is the antecedent river?
qs.e: An antecedent river is one that existed before the uplift of a mountain range and maintained its course during the uplift. The Indus River is a classic example of an antecedent river in India, as it flowed before the Himalayan uplift and cut through the rising mountains to maintain its path. In contrast, Damodar is a subsequent river flowing through the Chotanagpur Plateau. Krishna and Luni are peninsular rivers that are not antecedent. Antecedent rivers are associated with deep gorges and are formed due to geological processes like orogeny.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the definition of an antecedent river? → A river that existed before mountain building and maintains its course.
☛ Which river is an example of an antecedent river in India? → Indus and Brahmaputra.
☛ Where does the Indus River originate? → Near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet.
☛ Which rivers cut through the Himalayas? → Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra.
☛ What is the opposite of an antecedent river? → Subsequent river (formed after the uplift).

q: Which of the following rivers is not an international river?
qs.e: An international river is a river that flows through or borders two or more countries. The Mahanadi River flows entirely within India, through the states of Chhattisgarh and Odisha, and empties into the Bay of Bengal. Therefore, it is not an international river. In contrast, the Indus River flows through Tibet (China), India, and Pakistan; the Ganga River flows through India and Bangladesh; and the Brahmaputra River flows through Tibet (China), India, and Bangladesh. All three are international rivers.
qs.kf:
☛ River flowing entirely within India → Mahanadi
☛ Origin of Indus River → Near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet
☛ Delta of Ganga River → Sundarbans Delta (in India and Bangladesh)
☛ Other name of Brahmaputra → Tsangpo in Tibet, Jamuna in Bangladesh
☛ Longest river in India → Ganga (2525 km)

q: The hotel Taj Lake Palace, built in the middle of Lake Pichola, is in which city?
qs.e: The Taj Lake Palace built in the middle of Lake Pichola is located in Udaipur, Rajasthan. This palace was originally constructed by Maharana Jagat Singh II in 1746 AD as Jag Niwas. It is famous for its architecture and location on an island in the lake. It was later converted into a luxury hotel. Udaipur is also known as the City of Lakes. The palace is made of marble and limestone and incorporates many Hindu architectural elements.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Lake Pichola located? → Udaipur
☛ Who built Jag Niwas? → Maharana Jagat Singh II
☛ What is the nickname of Udaipur? → City of Lakes
☛ Which palace is situated on Lake Pichola? → Taj Lake Palace
☛ What is the old name of Taj Lake Palace? → Jag Niwas

q: Through which of the following states does the Chambal river flow?
qs.e: The Chambal river originates near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh and flows through three states: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. It is a major tributary of the Yamuna river and originates from the Vindhyachal mountain range. Chambal is known for its ravines (deep gorges) and the Chambal Sanctuary. The river is approximately 960 km long and has major dams like Gandhi Sagar Dam, Rana Pratap Sagar Dam, and Jawahar Sagar Dam built on it.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin place of Chambal river → Near Mhow, Madhya Pradesh (Vindhyachal range)
☛ Total length of Chambal river → Approximately 960 km
☛ States through which Chambal flows → Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh
☛ Chambal is a tributary of which river → Yamuna river
☛ Major dams on Chambal river → Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar

q: Major purpose of most of the dams around the world is-
qs.e: Most dams around the world are multipurpose. Their major purpose includes irrigation, drinking water supply, and power generation among other functions. Dams are constructed for water resource management, aiding agriculture, domestic use, and energy production. Additionally, dams help in flood control. Hence, all options are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ World's tallest dam → Jinping-I Dam (China)
☛ India's tallest dam → Tehri Dam
☛ Longest dam → Hirakud Dam (India)
☛ Multipurpose river valley project → Bhakra Nangal Project
☛ Major purpose of dams → Irrigation, drinking water, power generation

q: Which Indian waterfall has four distinct falls namely Raja, Rani, Rocket and Roarer in it?
qs.e: Jog Falls, also known as Gerusoppa Falls, is located in Shivamogga district of Karnataka. It is the second-highest waterfall in India and the largest in Asia in terms of volume. The total height is 253 meters. It flows as four distinct falls: Raja (the tallest), Rani (picturesque), Rocket (falls rapidly), and Roarer (roaring). These falls are created by the Sharavathi River. Jog Falls is unique for being divided into four streams, making it a major tourist attraction. It was also designated as a Ramsar site in 2018.
qs.kf:
☛ Jog Falls is located on which river? → Sharavathi River
☛ What is the total height of Jog Falls? → 253 meters
☛ What are the four falls of Jog Falls? → Raja, Rani, Rocket, Roarer
☛ In which state is Jog Falls located? → Karnataka
☛ What is another name of Jog Falls? → Gerusoppa Falls

q: Vijayawada is located on the banks of the river _________.
qs.e: Vijayawada is a major city located in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh. The city is situated on the banks of the Krishna River, which is the second largest river in South India, originating from Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra. Vijayawada is also known as the 'Business City' and is home to the famous Kandaki Caves and the Prakasham Barrage. The Prakasham Barrage is built across the Krishna River and is crucial for irrigation and water supply. The Brahmaputra, Cauvery, and Tapti rivers are not associated with Vijayawada.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Prakasham Barrage built? → Krishna River
☛ In which state is Vijayawada located? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ What is the origin point of Krishna River? → Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra
☛ Into which bay does the Krishna River empty? → Bay of Bengal
☛ Which is the largest river in South India? → Godavari

q: Rajghat dam is situated on the river-
qs.e: The Rajghat dam is located on the Betwa river at the border of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. It is a multipurpose project aimed at irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control. The dam's foundation was laid in 1976 and it was completed in 1987. The Betwa river originates from the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh and merges into the Yamuna. The dam has a maximum height of 135 feet and a length of 4,350 feet. This project benefits millions of hectares of agricultural land.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Betwa river → Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Foundation year of Rajghat dam → 1976
☛ Betwa river merges into → Yamuna river
☛ Maximum height of Rajghat dam → 135 feet
☛ Length of Rajghat dam → 4,350 feet

q: Which of the following dams has been built on the river Krishna?
qs.e: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is built on the Krishna River. It is located on the border of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. It is about 124 meters high and 1.6 km long. The dam was constructed between 1967 and 1972. It is one of the largest masonry dams in the world. It provides water for irrigation and hydroelectric power. The reservoir is called Nagarjuna Sagar Lake.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Nagarjuna Sagar Dam built? → Krishna River
☛ On which river is Hirakud Dam built? → Mahanadi River
☛ On which river is Bhakra Nangal Dam built? → Sutlej River
☛ On which river is Narmada Sagar Dam built? → Narmada River
☛ Where is the origin of Krishna River? → Mahabaleshwar

q: On which of the following river banks is the city of Agra located?
qs.e: The city of Agra is located in Uttar Pradesh on the banks of the Yamuna River. This river originates from the Himalayas and meets the Ganga at Prayagraj. Agra is historically significant, especially during the Mughal Empire. It houses UNESCO World Heritage sites like the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri. Being on the Yamuna River provided irrigation and water supply, making Agra a major cultural and tourism center. Other options—Ganga, Tapti, and Sabarmati rivers—are associated with cities like Haridwar, Surat, and Ahmedabad respectively, not Agra.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Delhi located? → Yamuna
☛ On which river is the Taj Mahal situated? → Yamuna
☛ On which river is Agra Fort located? → Yamuna
☛ On which river is Ahmedabad located? → Sabarmati
☛ On which river is Surat located? → Tapti

q: Which of the following cities is located on the banks of the river Gomati?
qs.e: The Gomati River is an important river in Uttar Pradesh, a tributary of the Ganga. It originates from the middle Ganges plain in the Pilibhit district. Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh, is situated on the banks of the Gomati River. The river divides the city into two parts: old Lucknow and new Lucknow. Many historical monuments and ghats are located along the Gomati River, such as the Ghanta Ghar and Kukrail Ghat. Prayagraj is situated at the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers; Ghaziabad is near the Hindon River; and Kanpur is located on the banks of the Ganga River. Thus, Lucknow is the only city among the options located on the Gomati River.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Gomati River → Pilibhit district in the middle Ganges plain
☛ Gomati River is a tributary of which river → Ganga River
☛ Which city is on the banks of Gomati River → Lucknow
☛ Prayagraj is at the confluence of which rivers → Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati
☛ Length of Gomati River → Approximately 475 km

q: Ukai Dam was constructed across the river ________.
qs.e: Ukai Dam is a multipurpose dam built across the Tapti River in the state of Gujarat. It is also known as Vallabh Sagar Dam. Its construction was completed in 1972 and it is crucial for irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control. The Tapti River originates from the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh and flows through Gujarat before emptying into the Arabian Sea. The other options— Krishna, Godavari, and Narmada—are major rivers of South India, but Ukai Dam is specifically located on the Tapti River.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Ukai Dam built? → Tapti
☛ Alternative name of Ukai Dam? → Vallabh Sagar Dam
☛ In which state is Ukai Dam located? → Gujarat
☛ Origin of Tapti River? → Betul district, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Where does Tapti River drain? → Arabian Sea

q: Which is India's longest river that does not flow into the sea?
A. Ganga
B. Yamuna
C. Tapti
D. Kaveri
qs.e: Yamuna is the longest river in India that does not flow into the sea. It is a tributary of the Ganga and meets it at Prayagraj. Its total length is about 1376 km. The Yamuna originates from the Yamunotri glacier in the Himalayas. It flows through major cities like Delhi, Mathura, and Agra. Other options like Ganga, Tapti, and Kaveri all flow into the sea.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Yamuna → Yamunotri Glacier
☛ Length of Yamuna → Approximately 1376 km
☛ Yamuna is a tributary of → Ganga
☛ Confluence point of Yamuna → Prayagraj (Ganga-Yamuna Sangam)
☛ Major dam on Yamuna → Lakhwar Dam

q: Which river does not flow into the Arabian Sea?
A. Narmada
B. Tapi
C. Periyar
D. Mahanadi
qs.e: The Mahanadi river originates in the Eastern Ghats and flows into the Bay of Bengal, whereas Narmada, Tapi, and Periyar flow into the Arabian Sea. Narmada and Tapi rise in Madhya Pradesh and flow westward through Gujarat to meet the Arabian Sea. Periyar is a major river of Kerala that drains into the Arabian Sea. The Mahanadi is the largest river of Odisha and forms a delta at the coast of the Bay of Bengal. Hence, Mahanadi does not flow into the Arabian Sea.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Narmada → Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Source of Tapi → Multai (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Periyar river delta → Kuttanad region in Kerala
☛ Mahanadi delta → Odisha on Bay of Bengal
☛ West-flowing rivers of India → Narmada, Tapi, Mahi, Sabarmati

q: On which river is Hirakud Dam built?
A. Cauvery
B. Gandak
C. Mahanadi
D. Batarani
qs.e: Hirakud Dam is built across the Mahanadi river in Odisha. It is one of the longest dams in India, with a total length of about 4.8 km. Construction began in 1948 and was completed in 1957. The dam serves multiple purposes: flood control, irrigation, and hydroelectric power generation. It irrigates around 75,000 hectares of land and has a power generation capacity of 307.5 MW. Situated in the Mahanadi basin, the dam plays a vital role in Odisha's economy. Hirakud is a major multipurpose river valley project in India.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Hirakud Dam built? → Mahanadi
☛ In which state is Hirakud Dam located? → Odisha
☛ Type of Hirakud Dam? → Multipurpose
☛ Length of Hirakud Dam? → 4.8 km
☛ When was Hirakud Dam completed? → 1957

q: Which is the point of origin of river Narmada?
A. Amarkantak
B. Sahyadri Hills
C. Maikal Hills
D. Mahadeo Hills
qs.e: The river Narmada originates from the Amarkantak hill in the Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh. This location is part of the Maikal Hills. Narmada is one of the major west-flowing rivers of India and has a length of 1,312 km. It empties into the Gulf of Khambhat. Amarkantak is also known as 'Tirtharaj' as it is the source of three rivers: Narmada, Son, and Johila. The Narmada is mentioned in the Puranas and flows through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat. Several pilgrimage sites like Omkareshwar and Maheshwar are located on its banks. The river is known for the Sardar Sarovar Dam built on it.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the total length of the Narmada river? → 1,312 km
☛ Into which sea does Narmada fall? → Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea)
☛ What is the alternate name for the source of Narmada? → Amarkantak or Maikal Hills
☛ Which major dam is built on the Narmada? → Sardar Sarovar Dam
☛ Which famous Jyotirlinga is located on the banks of Narmada? → Omkareshwar

q: Which of the following powerhouses is /are associated with the Damodar Valley Project? I. Durgapur. II. Chandrapura.
III. Maithon. IV. Hampi. Choose the right option. A. Only I and II.
B. Only II and III. C. I, II, and III. D. I, II, III, and IV.
qs.e: The Damodar Valley Project (DVC) is India's first multipurpose river valley project, established in 1948. It includes the Durgapur, Chandrapura, and Maithon thermal power plants. Durgapur Thermal Power Station is located in West Bengal and is a major powerhouse of DVC. Chandrapura Thermal Power Station in Jharkhand is the largest thermal power plant under DVC. Maithon Hydel Power Station, built on the Barakar River, is also part of DVC. Hampi, situated in Karnataka, is associated with the Tungabhadra Dam project, not DVC. Hence, only I, II, and III are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of establishment of DVC → 1948
☛ Largest thermal power plant under DVC → Chandrapura
☛ Headquarters of DVC → Kolkata
☛ River on which Maithon Dam is built → Barakar River
☛ State where Durgapur Thermal Power Station is located → West Bengal

q: The second largest river in terms of length in India is
A. Narmada
B. Yamuna
C. Brahmaputra
D. Godavari
qs.e: The longest river in India is the Ganga, with a length of about 2525 km. The second longest river in terms of length is the Godavari, with a total length of about 1465 km. It is also known as the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South). The Godavari originates from the Trimbakeshwar hills in Nashik district of Maharashtra and flows into the Bay of Bengal. After Godavari, the third longest river is Yamuna (1376 km), followed by Narmada (1312 km) and Brahmaputra (916 km within India).
qs.kf:
☛ Longest river in India → Ganga
☛ Second longest river in India → Godavari
☛ Origin of Godavari → Trimbakeshwar, Nashik
☛ Other name of Godavari → Dakshin Ganga
☛ Mouth of Godavari → Bay of Bengal

q: The ________ region is responsible for 80% of Germany's total steel production.
qs.e: The Ruhr region is Germany's industrial heartland, responsible for about 80% of the country's total steel production. This area is famous for its coal and iron ore deposits, which played a crucial role in Germany's industrialization during the 19th century. Located along the Ruhr River, it includes cities like Essen, Dortmund, Duisburg, and Bochum, where large steel plants are situated. After World War II, the reconstruction of this region strengthened Germany's economy. Although the steel industry has declined in recent decades, the Ruhr remains the largest steel-producing region in Germany.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest industrial region of Germany → Ruhr
☛ River on which Ruhr region is located → Ruhr River
☛ Main city of Ruhr region → Essen
☛ Major coal region of Germany → Ruhr
☛ State where Ruhr region is located → North Rhine-Westphalia

q: ______ is the largest earthen dam in India and second largest in Asia. The dam is named after the son of Mahabali, who was the king of Kerala.
qs.e: Banasura Sagar Dam is the largest earthen dam in India and the second largest in Asia. It is located in the Wayanad district of Kerala. The dam is named after Banasura, the son of King Mahabali. It is built across the Kabini River and was constructed by the Kerala government in the 1970s for irrigation and hydroelectric power. The dam is about 39 meters high and 500 meters long. It is also a popular tourist destination. The other options include Krishna Raja Sagar Dam in Karnataka, Mettur Dam in Tamil Nadu, and Nagarjuna Sagar Dam in Andhra Pradesh, which are masonry or concrete dams.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest earthen dam in India → Banasura Sagar Dam
☛ Second largest earthen dam in Asia → Banasura Sagar Dam
☛ River on which Banasura Sagar Dam is built → Kabini River
☛ State where Banasura Sagar Dam is located → Kerala
☛ Named after which son of Mahabali → Banasura

q: On which river is Idukki Dam built?
qs.e: The Idukki Dam is built on the Periyar River in the state of Kerala, India. It is one of the highest arch dams in the world, with a height of about 168 meters. Construction of the dam started in 1969 and was completed in 1976. The dam is a part of the Idukki Hydroelectric Project, which supplies a significant portion of Kerala's total electricity generation. The Periyar River is the longest river in Kerala, originating in the Western Ghats and flowing into the Arabian Sea. The dam also serves as an important source of drinking water and irrigation for the state.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Idukki Dam located? → Kerala
☛ What type of dam is Idukki Dam? → Arch dam
☛ What is the height of Idukki Dam? → About 168 meters
☛ Which is the longest river in Kerala? → Periyar
☛ Which project is Idukki Dam part of? → Idukki Hydroelectric Project

q: Which of the following river's section was declared as National Waterway-2 in 1988?
qs.e: National Waterway-2 (NW-2) was declared in 1988 on the Brahmaputra River, covering a 891 km stretch from Sadia (Assam) to the Bangladesh border. This waterway is crucial for freight and passenger transport in northeastern India. India has a total of 111 National Waterways, with NW-1 on the Ganga, NW-3 on the West Coast Canal, and NW-4 on the Godavari and Krishna rivers. NW-2 was developed to boost the economic development of Assam and the northeastern states.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river hosts National Waterway-2? → Brahmaputra
☛ Length of NW-2? → 891 km
☛ Which river hosts NW-1? → Ganga (Haldia-Allahabad)
☛ Where is NW-3 located? → West Coast Canal in Kerala
☛ Which rivers are part of NW-4? → Godavari and Krishna

q: Name the drainage pattern where the river originates from a hill and flows in all directions.
qs.e: In a radial drainage pattern, rivers originate from a central high point (hill or dome) and flow outward in all directions, resembling spokes of a wheel. This pattern is typically found on isolated hills or volcanoes. Examples include rivers like the Narmada, Tapi, Mahanadi, and Godavari in South India, which originate from the Satpura range and flow in different directions. In the Himalayas, the Indus and its tributaries also exhibit a radial pattern. In contrast, a centripetal pattern has rivers flowing from the periphery toward a central basin. Trellis pattern features parallel main rivers with short tributaries, while dendritic pattern resembles tree branches with irregular branching in all directions.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river system shows a radial drainage pattern in India? → Narmada
☛ What is the main characteristic of a centripetal pattern? → Rivers flow from outside to center
☛ Where is trellis drainage pattern commonly found? → Folded mountains
☛ What does a dendritic pattern resemble? → Tree branches
☛ In radial pattern, rivers flow from? → Center to all directions

q: Which two rivers are linked by the Pattiseema Lift Irrigation Project?
qs.e: The Pattiseema Lift Irrigation Project is a major water resource project located in Andhra Pradesh, which links the Godavari and Krishna rivers. Under this project, water from the Godavari river is lifted and transferred to the Krishna river basin, aiding irrigation and water supply under the Polavaram Project. It is part of the river interlinking project aimed at balanced distribution of water resources. This project has enhanced irrigation facilities in the Krishna delta region of Andhra Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Pattiseema Project → Lift irrigation project linking Godavari and Krishna
☛ Pattiseema Project is in which state? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Polavaram Project is on which river? → Godavari
☛ India's first river interlinking project → Pattiseema
☛ Origin of Krishna river → Mahabaleshwar (Western Ghats)

q: In which city, on the ghats of the Shipra river, is the Kumbh Mela organised?
qs.e: The Kumbh Mela is held at four locations: Prayagraj (Ganga), Haridwar (Ganga), Nashik (Godavari), and Ujjain (Shipra). Ujjain hosts the Kumbh Mela on the banks of the Shipra river. Ujjain is a major religious city in Madhya Pradesh and houses the Mahakaleshwar Temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas. The Shipra river is considered sacred in Hinduism. The Ujjain Kumbh Mela occurs every 12 years.
qs.kf:
☛ On which rivers are Kumbh Melas held? → Ganga, Godavari, Shipra, and Sangam
☛ What is the famous temple in Ujjain? → Mahakaleshwar Temple
☛ In which state is Ujjain located? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Shipra river is a tributary of which river? → Chambal river
☛ How often is Kumbh Mela held? → Every 12 years

q: Tsangpo and Dihang are other names of which river?
qs.e: The Brahmaputra river is known as Tsangpo in Tibet and Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh. It originates from the Chemayungdung Glacier near the Kailash range in Tibet. Flowing eastward for about 1,100 km in Tibet, it enters Arunachal Pradesh where it is called Dihang. In Assam, it turns south and flows into Bangladesh, where it is known as Jamuna. After merging with the Ganga, it forms the Meghna before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. The Brahmaputra is the ninth largest river in the world by discharge and is known for its high volume of water flow. It is a major river for irrigation and transportation in Northeast India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is Brahmaputra called in Tibet? → Tsangpo
☛ What is Brahmaputra called in Arunachal Pradesh? → Dihang
☛ What is the source of Brahmaputra? → Chemayungdung Glacier
☛ What is Brahmaputra called in Bangladesh? → Jamuna
☛ What is the approximate length of Brahmaputra? → 2,900 km

q: On which of the following rivers was Independent India's first river dam constructed?
qs.e: Independent India's first river dam is the Tilaiya Dam built on the Damodar River. It was constructed in 1953 by the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC). DVC was established in 1948 as the first multipurpose river valley project in the country. The Tilaiya Dam aimed at flood control, irrigation, and hydroelectric power generation. This project later paved the way for the construction of many other dams.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the first dam of Independent India? → Tilaiya Dam (on Damodar River)
☛ When was Damodar Valley Corporation established? → 1948
☛ On which river is Tilaiya Dam located? → Damodar
☛ What is the origin of Damodar River? → Chota Nagpur Plateau
☛ By which name is Damodar River known? → Sorrow of Bengal

q: Jog falls, the highest waterfalls in India is also known as?
qs.e: Jog Falls is located on the Sharavathi River in Shimoga district of Karnataka. It is the highest waterfall in India with a height of 253 meters (830 feet). It is also known as Gersoppa Falls, named after the nearby village. The falls are divided into four cascades: Raja, Roarer, Rocket, and Rani. The waterfall is best viewed during the monsoon season. Jog Falls is a major tourist attraction and is also used for hydroelectric power generation.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Jog Falls located? → Sharavathi River
☛ What is the total height of Jog Falls? → 253 meters
☛ In which state is Jog Falls situated? → Karnataka
☛ By what other name is Jog Falls known? → Gersoppa Falls
☛ How many cascades does Jog Falls have? → Four (Raja, Roarer, Rocket, Rani)

q: Which of the following is NOT a 'grassland'?
qs.e: A fen is a type of wetland, not a grassland. Grasslands are areas dominated by grasses, such as savanna (tropical grassland), prairie (temperate grassland found in North America), and steppe (temperate grassland found in Eurasia). A fen is a peat-forming wetland that receives water from groundwater or surface water, supporting sedges, reeds, and other wetland plants rather than grasses. It typically has high water table and alkaline conditions. Therefore, fen is not classified as a grassland.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is a tropical grassland? → Savanna
☛ What is the grassland of North America called? → Prairie
☛ What is the grassland of Eurasia called? → Steppe
☛ What type of ecosystem is a fen? → Wetland
☛ What is the dominant vegetation in grasslands? → Grasses

q: Which of the following rivers of India flows from east to west?
qs.e: In India, most rivers flow from west to east, but the Narmada river is an exception. It originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows from east to west, emptying into the Gulf of Khambhat. The Narmada is the fifth largest river in India and is often called the 'lifeline of India'. In contrast, the Godavari, Tungabhadra, and Mahanadi rivers flow eastward and meet the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada originates from the Amarkantak plateau and flows for about 1312 km. The famous Dhuandhar Falls are located on this river.
qs.kf:
☛ River flowing westwards → Narmada
☛ Origin of Narmada → Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Mouth of Narmada → Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea)
☛ East-flowing peninsular rivers → Godavari, Mahanadi, Tungabhadra
☛ Famous waterfall on Narmada → Dhuandhar Falls

q: Which of the following is the largest delta in the world?
qs.e: The largest delta in the world is the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, also known as the Sundarban Delta. It spans across India and Bangladesh and covers an area of approximately 105,000 sq km. This delta is formed by the Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers. The Amazon Delta is the second largest, but smaller in size. The Nile Delta is located in Egypt and is much smaller. The Congo Delta is in Africa but not the largest. The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is famous for its fertility and biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest delta in the world → Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta (Sundarban)
☛ Countries of Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta → India and Bangladesh
☛ Second largest delta → Amazon Delta
☛ Location of Nile Delta → Egypt
☛ Approximate area of Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta → 105,000 sq km

q: Mechi river is a tributary of which river?
qs.e: The Mechi River is a major tributary of the Mahananda River. It originates from the Mahabharat Range in eastern Nepal and flows through the Indian states of Bihar and West Bengal. The Mahananda River itself is a tributary of the Ganga. The Mechi River is important for irrigation and drinking water in the region. It flows near the India-Nepal border and supports agriculture in the area.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is Mechi a tributary of? → Mahananda
☛ Which river is Mahananda a tributary of? → Ganga
☛ Origin of Mechi river? → Mahabharat Range, Nepal
☛ States through which Mechi flows? → Bihar and West Bengal
☛ Use of Mechi river? → Irrigation and drinking water

q: Bari Doab is the area between:
qs.e: Bari Doab is the fertile tract of land between the Beas and Ravi rivers in the Punjab region. 'Doab' refers to the area between two converging rivers. Punjab has five major rivers: Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum. The Bari Doab lies specifically between Beas and Ravi. Other Doabs include Bist Doab (Sutlej and Beas), Rechna Doab (Ravi and Chenab), Chaj Doab (Chenab and Jhelum), and Sindh Sagar Doab (Jhelum and Indus). This region is agriculturally rich, producing wheat, rice, and sugarcane. The name Bari derives from the combination of Beas and Ravi. Understanding these divisions is important for geographical and agricultural studies of the Indian subcontinent.
qs.kf:
☛ Bist Doab lies between which rivers? → Sutlej and Beas
☛ Rechna Doab lies between which rivers? → Ravi and Chenab
☛ Chaj Doab lies between which rivers? → Chenab and Jhelum
☛ Sindh Sagar Doab lies between which rivers? → Jhelum and Indus
☛ Which are the five rivers of Punjab? → Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, Jhelum

q: Which of the following canal systems is NOT in Haryana?
qs.e: Gandak canal is located in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, not in Haryana. It originates from the Gandak river in Nepal. In Haryana, the main canal systems are Western Yamuna Canal, Nangal canal, and Bhakra Canal System. Western Yamuna Canal draws water from Yamuna river. Nangal canal is part of Bhakra-Nangal project and takes water from Sutlej river. Bhakra Canal System originates from Bhakra dam. Gandak canal is associated with Gandak river project.
qs.kf:
☛ Major canal of Haryana → Western Yamuna Canal
☛ Nangal canal takes water from which river → Sutlej river
☛ Bhakra Canal System is in which states → Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan
☛ Gandak canal is in which state → Bihar
☛ Source of Western Yamuna Canal → Yamuna river

q: Which is the highest waterfall of the world on land?
qs.e: The highest waterfall on land in the world is the Angel Falls, located in Venezuela. It has a total height of approximately 979 meters (3212 feet), with a continuous drop of 807 meters. It was named after American pilot Jimmy Angel, who discovered it in 1933. The waterfall is situated in Canaima National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Angel Falls is about 15 times taller than Niagara Falls. Among the other options, Gavarnie (France), Jog (India), and Ribbon (USA) are notable but not the highest. Angel Falls remains the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ In which country is Angel Falls located? → Venezuela
☛ What is the height of Angel Falls? → 979 meters
☛ After whom is Angel Falls named? → Jimmy Angel
☛ Which national park contains Angel Falls? → Canaima National Park
☛ What is the second-highest waterfall in the world? → Tugela Falls (South Africa)

q: Which of the following lakes is the largest fresh water lake in north-east India?
qs.e: Loktak Lake, located in Manipur, is the largest fresh water lake in north-east India. It is famous for its floating islands called phumdis, which are heterogeneous masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter. The lake serves as the lifeline of Manipur and is home to the Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world. Loktak Lake is also recognized as a Ramsar site. It plays a vital role in the region's biodiversity and supports the livelihoods of local communities.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest fresh water lake in north-east India → Loktak Lake (Manipur)
☛ State where Loktak Lake is located → Manipur
☛ Special feature of Loktak Lake → Floating islands (phumdis)
☛ Keibul Lamjao National Park is located on → Loktak Lake
☛ International treaty protecting Loktak Lake → Ramsar Convention

q: Which of the following tributaries of Ganges meets Patna near Sonpur?
qs.e: The Gandak River is a major tributary of the Ganges, originating in the Himalayas of Nepal. It meets the Ganges near Sonpur in Patna, Bihar. The river is known as Narayani in Nepal and Gandak in India. It carries a large amount of silt, making the region highly fertile for agriculture. Important sites like the Gandak Barrage and Valmiki Tiger Reserve are located on this river. The Kosi River also joins the Ganges but near Kursela, not Patna. The Ghagghar River is a seasonal river in Rajasthan, and Ramganga flows in Uttarakhand. Thus, Gandak is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Gandak River → Himalayas of Nepal
☛ Other name of Gandak River → Narayani (in Nepal)
☛ Confluence of Gandak River → Sonpur, Patna (Bihar)
☛ Dam on Gandak River → Gandak Barrage (Bihar)
☛ Confluence of Kosi River → Kursela, Bihar

q: Tawa river, which is the tributary of River ________, is located on the Tawa reservoir
qs.e: Tawa river, an important river flowing in Madhya Pradesh, is a major tributary of the Narmada river. It is located on the Tawa reservoir, which is one of the dams built on the Narmada river. The Tawa river originates from the Satpura mountain range and merges into the Narmada river. The Narmada river flows through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat and is also known as the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh. The total length of the Tawa river is about 172 kilometers. This river is famous for its reservoir, which aids in irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.
qs.kf:
☛ Tawa river is a tributary of which river? → Narmada
☛ On which river is Tawa reservoir located? → Tawa river
☛ What is the origin of Narmada river? → Amarkantak
☛ What is the length of Tawa river? → Approximately 172 km
☛ Which states does Narmada river flow through? → Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat

q: Which river is known as Singi Khamban Lion's mouth in Tibet?
qs.e: In Tibet, the Indus River is known as 'Singi Khamban', which means Lion's mouth. The Indus originates near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet at Bokar Chu. It flows through Ladakh and Pakistan before emptying into the Arabian Sea. The name 'Singi Khamban' is derived from Tibetan, where 'Singi' means lion and 'Khamban' means mouth. The Indus has a total length of about 3180 km and is one of the most important rivers of the Indian subcontinent. It is the longest river in Pakistan and plays a vital role in agriculture and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Indus River → Tibet near Lake Mansarovar
☛ Total length of Indus River → Approximately 3180 km
☛ Indus River empties into → Arabian Sea
☛ Major tributaries of Indus → Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, Jhelum
☛ Indus River is known as in Tibet → Singi Khamban

q: Which of the following lake is also known as 'the only floating lake'?
qs.e: Loktak Lake is located in Manipur and is known as 'the only floating lake'. It is famous for its phumdis (floating islands), which are dense masses of vegetation and soil. The lake is recognized as a Ramsar site. The Keibul Lamjao National Park, situated on the lake, is the world's only floating national park and is famous for the Sangai (brow-antlered deer). This lake is the lifeline of the people of Manipur and plays a crucial role in the local ecosystem.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Loktak Lake located? → Manipur
☛ What are the floating islands called? → Phumdis
☛ Is Loktak Lake a Ramsar site? → Yes
☛ Keibul Lamjao National Park is famous for which animal? → Sangai deer
☛ What type of lake is Loktak? → Freshwater floating lake

q: Which of the following rivers is a tributary of the right bank of Yamuna (tributary)?
qs.e: The Yamuna River is a major tributary of the Ganga. The right bank tributaries of Yamuna include Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, and Ken. The Ken River originates from the Ahirgawan hills in Jabalpur district of Madhya Pradesh and joins the Yamuna near Banda, Uttar Pradesh. It is approximately 427 km long. Sanger, Rihand, and Hindon are also tributaries of Yamuna, but not of the right bank. Sanger joins the left bank, Rihand is a tributary of Ganga, and Hindon is a left bank tributary. Therefore, Ken is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Major right bank tributary of Yamuna → Chambal
☛ Major left bank tributary of Yamuna → Hindon
☛ Origin of Ken River → Ahirgawan hills (Jabalpur)
☛ Total length of Yamuna → 1376 km
☛ Origin of Yamuna → Yamunotri Glacier (Uttarakhand)

q: Which of the following rivers has the largest basin area in Peninsular India?
qs.e: The Godavari River has the largest basin area in Peninsular India, covering approximately 3,12,812 sq km. It is also known as the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganges of the South). The river originates from Tryambakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra and flows through Maharashtra, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. Its major tributaries include the Purna, Indravati, and Manjira. In comparison, the Kaveri basin covers 81,155 sq km, the Narmada basin covers 98,796 sq km, and the Mahi basin covers 34,842 sq km.
qs.kf:
☛ Alternative name of Godavari → Dakshin Ganga
☛ Source of Godavari → Tryambakeshwar, Nashik
☛ Longest tributary of Godavari → Manjira
☛ Second largest river basin in Peninsular India → Krishna
☛ Number of states in Godavari basin → 5 (Maharashtra, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh)

q: Jog Falls is situated on which river?
qs.e: Jog Falls is the second highest waterfall in India, located in Shimoga district of Karnataka. It is formed by the Sharavati River, which originates in the Western Ghats and flows into the Arabian Sea. The waterfall has a height of about 253 meters (829 feet) and is divided into four cascades: Raja, Rani, Roarer, and Rocket. It is also known as Gersoppa Falls. The Sharavati River also hosts the Linganamakki Dam and the Gersoppa Hydroelectric Project. The waterfall is a major tourist attraction in Karnataka.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest waterfall in India → Kunchikal (Shimoga, Karnataka)
☛ Largest river in Peninsular India → Godavari
☛ Largest river in Karnataka → Kaveri
☛ Origin of Sharavati River → Ambuthirtha (Western Ghats)
☛ Four cascades of Jog Falls → Raja, Rani, Roarer, Rocket

q: The Nagarjuna Sagar Project is constructed across the river
qs.e: The Nagarjuna Sagar Project is a major multipurpose river valley project located on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. It is constructed across the Krishna River and includes one of the largest masonry dams in the world. The dam has a height of about 124 meters and a total length of 1,450 meters. The project aims to provide irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and drinking water supply. Its construction was completed in 1969. The Krishna River is one of the major rivers in South India, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam built on? → Krishna River
☛ The Nagarjuna Sagar Project is located on the border of which states? → Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
☛ What type of dam is the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam? → Masonry dam
☛ When was the Nagarjuna Sagar Project completed? → 1969
☛ What is the reservoir of Nagarjuna Sagar called? → Nagarjuna Sagar Reservoir

q: Majuli Island is located in which river?
qs.e: Majuli Island is the world's largest river island, located on the Brahmaputra River in the state of Assam, India. It lies between the northern and southern channels of the Brahmaputra. Majuli was included in the tentative list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 2016. The island is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, especially the Vaishnavite tradition of saint Sankardev, and its biodiversity. It covers an area of approximately 1250 square kilometers.
qs.kf:
☛ World's largest river island → Majuli
☛ Majuli Island is located on → Brahmaputra River
☛ Majuli is in which state → Assam
☛ Year of UNESCO tentative listing → 2016
☛ Saint associated with Majuli → Sankardev

q: The place of the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Mandakini River is called _______________
qs.e: Rudraprayag is a famous confluence site in Uttarakhand where the Alaknanda River meets the Mandakini River. It is one of the Panch Prayag (five confluences), which include Vishnuprayag, Nandaprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, and Devprayag. Rudraprayag is associated with Lord Shiva, as 'Rudra' is a name of Shiva. This site is religiously significant and located on the route to Kedarnath and Badrinath. From here, the Alaknanda flows onward and joins the Bhagirathi at Devprayag to form the Ganga.
qs.kf:
☛ Confluence of Alaknanda and Bhagirathi → Devprayag
☛ Confluence of Alaknanda and Mandakini → Rudraprayag
☛ Confluence of Alaknanda and Pindar → Karnaprayag
☛ Confluence of Alaknanda and Dhauliganga → Vishnuprayag
☛ Confluence of Alaknanda and Nandakini → Nandaprayag

q: Which of the following river does not make a delta?
qs.e: The Mandvi river flows in the Kutch region of Gujarat and falls into the Arabian Sea. It does not form a delta but rather an estuary due to its fast flow and tidal influence. In contrast, the other options—Kaveri, Ganga, and Godavari—all form large deltas. The Ganga delta, known as Sundarbans, is the largest delta in the world. Kaveri creates a fertile delta in Tamil Nadu, while Godavari forms the second-largest delta in Andhra Pradesh. The Mandvi river is short and steep, preventing delta formation.
qs.kf:
☛ River not forming delta → Mandvi (Gujarat)
☛ Delta of Ganga → Sundarbans (world's largest delta)
☛ Godavari delta location → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Kaveri delta region → Tamil Nadu
☛ Rivers forming estuary → Narmada, Tapi, Mandvi

q: Mississippi river is located in which of these countries?
qs.e: The Mississippi River is located in North America and flows entirely within the United States. It originates from Lake Itasca in Minnesota and travels approximately 3,780 km before emptying into the Gulf of Mexico. The Mississippi is the fourth longest river in the world and its drainage basin covers 31 US states and 2 Canadian provinces. This river is extensively used for transportation, irrigation, and industry. The name 'Mississippi' is derived from a Native American word meaning 'great river'.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Mississippi River → Lake Itasca
☛ Length of Mississippi River → 3,780 km
☛ Mouth of Mississippi River → Gulf of Mexico
☛ Major tributary of Mississippi → Missouri River
☛ Importance of Mississippi → Transportation and irrigation

q: Which of the following rivers is not a tributary of Mahanadi?
qs.e: Mahanadi is a major river flowing through Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Its major tributaries include Shivnath, Mand, and Ib. The Shivnath river is the largest tributary of Mahanadi, flowing through Chhattisgarh. Mand and Ib are also important tributaries of Mahanadi. The Musi river is a river in Telangana, South India, which is a tributary of the Krishna river, not Mahanadi. Hence, Musi is not a tributary of Mahanadi.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Mahanadi → Sihawa hill region in Chhattisgarh
☛ Largest tributary of Mahanadi → Shivnath
☛ Musi river is a tributary of → Krishna river
☛ Mahanadi empties into → Bay of Bengal
☛ Length of Mahanadi → Approximately 858 km

q: Which of the following is the source of Teesta river?
qs.e: The Teesta River originates from the Jemu Glacier in Sikkim. It flows through the Indian states of Sikkim and West Bengal before entering Bangladesh, where it joins the Brahmaputra River. The Teesta River is approximately 315 km long. The Jemu Glacier is located in the Kanchenjunga region at an altitude of about 5,300 meters. The Siachen Glacier is in the Karakoram range, while the Balatora and Tolsthan glaciers are not sources of the Teesta. The river is vital for irrigation and hydropower in both India and Bangladesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Where does the Teesta River originate? → Jemu Glacier (Sikkim)
☛ What is the total length of the Teesta River? → Approximately 315 km
☛ Which states does the Teesta River flow through? → Sikkim and West Bengal
☛ Which river does the Teesta join in Bangladesh? → Brahmaputra River
☛ In which mountain region is the Jemu Glacier located? → Kanchenjunga region

q: The Hoover Dam is built on which river?
qs.e: The Hoover Dam is a massive concrete arch-gravity dam located on the border between the U.S. states of Nevada and Arizona, built on the Colorado River. Constructed between 1931 and 1936 near Boulder City, the dam serves multiple purposes including flood control, irrigation, drinking water supply, and hydroelectric power generation. The reservoir created by the dam is called Lake Mead, which is the largest man-made lake in the United States. The Hoover Dam stands 221 meters tall and was the tallest dam in the world at the time of its completion.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Hoover Dam located? → On the Nevada-Arizona border
☛ On which river is Hoover Dam built? → Colorado River
☛ When was Hoover Dam constructed? → 1931–1936
☛ What is the name of the lake formed by Hoover Dam? → Lake Mead
☛ What type of dam is Hoover Dam? → Arch-gravity dam

q: Which of the following rivers goes to the Arabian Sea?
qs.e: The Tapti River originates from Multai in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward to empty into the Gulf of Khambhat, which is part of the Arabian Sea. It is approximately 724 km long. The Tungabhadra and Krishna rivers flow into the Bay of Bengal, while Mahanadi also meets the Bay of Bengal. Tapti (also called Tapi) is one of the major west-flowing rivers in India. The city of Surat is located on its banks.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Tapti River → Multai, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Mouth of Tapti River → Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea)
☛ Length of Tapti River → 724 km
☛ West-flowing rivers of India → Narmada, Tapti, Mahi, Sabarmati
☛ Dam on Tapti River → Ukai Dam (Gujarat)

q: Which of the following is the mountainous river?
qs.e: The Ganga river is a major mountainous river originating from the Himalayas. Its source is the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand. Ganga is considered the holiest river in India and has a total length of about 2525 kilometers. The Krishna, Godavari, and Mahanadi are peninsular rivers that originate from the Western Ghats and flow into the Bay of Bengal. These rivers are monsoon-dependent and have seasonal water flow. Due to its Himalayan origin, the Ganga receives water from melting snow and remains perennial throughout the year. Therefore, Ganga is a mountainous river.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Ganga river → Gangotri Glacier (Uttarakhand)
☛ Tributaries of Ganga → Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi
☛ Plain region of Ganga → Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal
☛ Peninsular rivers → Krishna, Godavari, Mahanadi, Kaveri
☛ Characteristic of Himalayan rivers → Water from snowmelt, perennial flow

q: Which of the following rivers makes 'Bird Foot Delta'?
qs.e: The 'Bird Foot Delta' is a unique delta formed by the Mississippi River, which resembles the shape of a bird's foot. It is located in the Gulf of Mexico and is also known as the Mississippi Delta. Other rivers like the Amazon and Ganga form different types of deltas. The Amazon delta is large and tidal, while the Ganga delta is an arcuate or Sundarbans delta. The Nile River also forms an arcuate delta. The Mississippi delta is geographically significant due to its distinctive shape and distributary channels.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river forms the Bird Foot Delta? → Mississippi
☛ Where is the Mississippi Delta located? → Gulf of Mexico
☛ Which delta is known as the Sundarbans delta? → Ganga delta
☛ Which river has an arcuate delta? → Nile
☛ Which is the largest delta in the world? → Ganga-Brahmaputra delta

q: The area created by a single river system is known as _____.
qs.e: The area created by a single river system is called a drainage basin. A drainage basin, also known as a river basin or watershed, is the geographic region where all precipitation drains into a single river and its tributaries. It defines the drainage boundary of the river system. For example, the Ganga river basin covers a vast area in India. Other options: Valley is a low area between hills formed by a river, water dividing line is a ridge separating two basins, and floodplains are lands near rivers formed by floods.
qs.kf:
☛ Definition of Drainage Basin → Area where all water drains into a single river
☛ Other names for Drainage Basin → River Basin or Watershed
☛ What is Water Divide → High land separating two drainage basins
☛ Largest Drainage Basin in the world → Amazon River Basin
☛ Largest Drainage Basin in India → Ganga River Basin

q: Which of the following is not a type of coral reef?
qs.e: Coral reefs are important marine ecosystems. Their three main types are fringing reefs (attached to shore), barrier reefs (separated by a lagoon), and atolls (ring-shaped surrounding a lagoon). A lagoon is a water body, not a type of coral reef. This question tests basic geography concepts. Coral reefs are found in tropical regions and are vital for biodiversity. They face threats from climate change, pollution, and overfishing.
qs.kf:
☛ Where are fringing reefs found? → Near the coast
☛ Which is the world's longest barrier reef? → Great Barrier Reef
☛ How are atolls formed? → By subsidence of volcanic islands
☛ What surrounds a lagoon? → An atoll or barrier reef
☛ What is the main threat to coral reefs? → Climate change and pollution

q: Where is the origin of Narmada River?
qs.e: The Narmada River originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh. It flows westward and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat. The Narmada is one of the major west-flowing rivers of India and has a length of 1,312 km. It is considered the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Major projects like the Sardar Sarovar Dam and Indira Sagar Dam are built on this river. The Narmada has cultural significance since Vedic times and is also known as Reva.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Narmada River → Amarkantak Plateau (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Other name of Narmada → Reva
☛ Length of Narmada River → 1,312 km
☛ Largest dam on Narmada → Sardar Sarovar Dam (Gujarat)
☛ Narmada River falls into → Gulf of Khambhat

q: Amaravati School of Sculpture is built on the banks of which river?
qs.e: The Amaravati School of Sculpture, also known as the Amaravati style of art, developed in South India. This sculptural style is primarily associated with the Amaravati Stupa located on the banks of the Krishna River in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh. It was a significant center of Buddhism. The Amaravati sculptures used white marble and depicted scenes from the life of Buddha. This style flourished during the Satavahana period (approximately 200 BCE to 200 CE). The characteristic features of Amaravati sculptures include intricate carvings and elongated, graceful figures. The school is known for its narrative panels and delicate detailing.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Amaravati Stupa located? → Andhra Pradesh, Guntur district
☛ Which stone was used in Amaravati sculptures? → White marble
☛ During which period did the Amaravati style develop? → Satavahana period
☛ Which religion is the Amaravati School associated with? → Buddhism
☛ What is a key feature of Amaravati sculptures? → Intricate carvings and elongated figures

q: Which of the following is not included in the group of largest lakes?
qs.e: 'The Great Lakes' is a group of five large freshwater lakes located in North America. These include Lake Superior, Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, Lake Erie, and Lake Ontario. These lakes are situated on the border between the United States and Canada and are among the largest freshwater reserves in the world. Lake Athabasca is a large lake located in Canada, but it is not part of the Great Lakes system. It spans across the provinces of Saskatchewan and Alberta. Therefore, among the given options, Lake Athabasca is the one not included in the Great Lakes, while the other three lakes are part of this group.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest lake in the Great Lakes → Lake Superior
☛ Smallest lake in the Great Lakes → Lake Ontario
☛ Only Great Lake entirely in the USA → Lake Michigan
☛ Area of the Great Lakes → Approximately 2,44,000 sq km
☛ Water volume of the Great Lakes → Approximately 22,800 cubic km

q: Which of the following rivers flows from the Himalayan region of Nepal?
qs.e: The Kosi river originates from the Himalayan region of Nepal and flows into India. It is also known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent floods. The river originates from Gosainthan in Tibet and is called Saptakosi, comprising seven major tributaries. The Godavari, Son, and Yamuna rivers do not flow from the Himalayan region of Nepal.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Kosi river → Gosainthan, Tibet
☛ Kosi river is also known as → Saptakosi
☛ Nickname of Kosi river → Sorrow of Bihar
☛ Number of tributaries of Kosi → 7
☛ Kosi river flows in which Indian state's plains → Northern Bihar

q: Where is the origin of river Indus?
qs.e: The river Indus originates from Mount Kailash near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet, at a place called Senge Khabab. It flows through Tibet, enters India in the Ladakh region, and then continues into Pakistan. The total length of the Indus is about 3180 kilometers, and it empties into the Arabian Sea. Major tributaries include Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum. The Indus Valley Civilization developed along this river. The Indus Water Treaty signed in 1960 governs the sharing of its waters between India and Pakistan.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Indus River → Senge Khabab near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet
☛ Total length of Indus River → Approximately 3180 km
☛ Indus Water Treaty → Signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan
☛ Delta of Indus River → Located in Sindh province of Pakistan
☛ Longest tributary of Indus → Sutlej

q: The Koleru lake is found in the triangle of ________.
qs.e: Kolleru Lake is a freshwater lake located in Andhra Pradesh, situated in the delta region between the Godavari and Krishna rivers. It lies in the triangular area formed by these two rivers. The lake is an important habitat for birds and is recognized as a Ramsar site. It spreads across the Guntur and Krishna districts of Andhra Pradesh. The lake is also significant for fishing and agriculture.
qs.kf:
☛ Between which rivers is Kolleru Lake located? → Godavari and Krishna
☛ In which state is Kolleru Lake situated? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ What type of lake is Kolleru Lake? → Freshwater lake
☛ Under which international treaty is Kolleru Lake recognized? → Ramsar Convention
☛ Which districts does Kolleru Lake cover? → Guntur and Krishna

q: From which of these places does the river Narmada originate?
qs.e: The river Narmada originates from the Amarkantak hills in Madhya Pradesh. It flows westward and empties into the Gulf of Khambhat in the Arabian Sea. The Narmada is one of the major rivers of India and is often called the 'lifeline of Madhya Pradesh'. It is 1,312 km long and has several religious sites along its banks. Unlike most peninsular rivers, the Narmada flows into the Arabian Sea rather than the Bay of Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ Where does the Narmada River originate? → Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Which sea does the Narmada River drain into? → Arabian Sea (Gulf of Khambhat)
☛ What is the length of the Narmada River? → 1,312 km
☛ Which major city is located on the banks of the Narmada? → Jabalpur
☛ Which states does the Narmada River flow through? → Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat

q: On which river are the tallest waterfalls found in India?
qs.e: India's tallest waterfall is Jog Falls (also called Gerusoppa Falls), located on the Sharawati River in the state of Karnataka, in the Western Ghats region. Jog Falls has a height of approximately 253 meters (830 feet), making it the highest waterfall in India. The waterfall is divided into four distinct cascades: Raja, Rani, Roarer, and Rocket. The Sharawati River originates from the Ambuthirtha hills in the Western Ghats and flows into the Arabian Sea. This waterfall is a nationally significant natural site and a popular tourist destination.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the tallest waterfall in India? → Jog Falls (Sharawati River)
☛ In which state is Jog Falls located? → Karnataka
☛ Where does the Sharawati River empty? → Arabian Sea
☛ What is the height of Jog Falls? → 253 meters
☛ What is the other name of Jog Falls? → Gerusoppa Falls

q: Haridwar city is situated on the bank of river _______
qs.e: Haridwar city is situated on the bank of River Ganges in Uttarakhand and is a major pilgrimage site in Hinduism. The Ganges descends from the Himalayas and enters the plains at Haridwar. This city holds immense religious significance, hosting the Kumbh Mela every 12 years. The Ganges is the longest river in India, with a total length of about 2525 km. The name 'Haridwar' means 'Gateway to God Vishnu'.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of River Ganges → Gangotri (Gomukh)
☛ River entering plains at Haridwar → Ganges
☛ Festival held at Haridwar every 12 years → Kumbh Mela
☛ Length of River Ganges → 2525 km
☛ Meaning of Haridwar → Gateway of Lord Vishnu

q: Which of the following rivers is known as 'River of Sadness'?
qs.e: The Damodar river is known as the 'River of Sadness' because it frequently causes floods in Jharkhand and West Bengal. It originates from the Chota Nagpur plateau and joins the Hooghly river. The length of the Damodar river is about 592 km. Several dams like Tenughat, Konar, and Panchet have been built on it for flood control. Its water is important for irrigation and industries. The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) utilizes this river's water for power generation and other purposes.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is called 'River of Sadness'? → Damodar
☛ Where does Damodar river merge? → Hooghly river
☛ What is the length of Damodar river? → About 592 km
☛ When was Damodar Valley Corporation established? → 1948
☛ What is the origin of Damodar river? → Chota Nagpur plateau

q: The two parts of the two drainage basins are called separating parts?
qs.e: A water divide is a highland area that separates two drainage basins. It is a line or boundary that diverts rainwater to flow in two different directions. For example, in India, the Vindhya mountain range acts as a water divide between the Ganga and Narmada river basins. The water divide is also called a 'watershed divide' or 'drainage divide'. It plays a crucial role in determining the drainage pattern and the course of rivers. The concept is important in geography to understand how river systems develop and how water flows across different regions.
qs.kf:
☛ Definition of Water Divide → Highland separating two drainage basins
☛ Major water divide in India → Vindhya mountain range
☛ Other name → Drainage divide
☛ Function → Determines river flow direction
☛ Example → Between Ganga and Narmada basins

q: Jabalpur is situated on the banks of which river?
qs.e: Jabalpur is a major city in Madhya Pradesh, situated on the banks of the Narmada River. The Narmada is one of India's most important rivers, flowing through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. The city's significance is enhanced by its location along the Narmada, which is a religious and tourist hub. Key attractions like the Dhuandhar Falls and Marble Rocks are directly associated with the Narmada. Among the options, Bhima is a tributary of the Krishna River, Brahmaputra flows in Northeast India, and Mahanadi is in Odisha, making them incorrect for Jabalpur.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Jabalpur located? → Narmada
☛ Origin of Narmada River? → Amarkantak
☛ Dhuandhar Falls is on which river? → Narmada
☛ Where are the Marble Rocks located? → Jabalpur
☛ Through how many states does Narmada flow? → Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat

q: What is the name of a lake made from sand and a basal water separated by the sea by sandbars and spits?
qs.e: A lagoon is a lake made from sand and basal water, separated from the sea by sandbars or spits. It is a shallow water body located near coastal areas, formed when sea waves and currents deposit sand to create a barrier, trapping seawater behind it. Lagoons are important in coastal geography and climate studies. Examples include the Venice Lagoon in Italy and Mar Chiquita in Chile. They support diverse ecosystems like mangroves and aquatic life. Lagoons differ from estuaries, which are river mouths open to the sea. Understanding lagoons helps in coastal management and environmental conservation.
qs.kf:
☛ Definition of Lagoon → Shallow lake separated from sea by sand barriers.
☛ Example of Lagoon → Venice Lagoon, Italy.
☛ Formation of Lagoon → Sand deposition by waves and currents.
☛ Ecological Importance → Habitat for mangroves and aquatic species.
☛ Difference from Estuary → Lagoon is isolated, estuary is river mouth.

q: Which of the following is the longest river of Southern India?
qs.e: The longest river in Southern India is the Godavari, often called the 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Ganges of the South'. It originates from the Trimbakeshwar hills in Nashik, Maharashtra, and flows eastwards into the Bay of Bengal. Its total length is about 1,465 km, making it the longest river in peninsular India. After the Godavari, the Krishna river (1,400 km) and Kaveri (800 km) are next in length. The Narmada river, although sometimes considered, flows westward through central India and is not considered a river of Southern India. The Godavari has a drainage basin of about 3,12,812 sq km, the largest among all peninsular rivers.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Godavari river → Trimbakeshwar, Nashik (Maharashtra)
☛ Length of Godavari river → Approximately 1,465 km
☛ Drainage basin of Godavari → 3,12,812 sq km
☛ Tributaries of Godavari → Pranhita, Indravati, Manjira, Wardha
☛ Which river is called Dakshin Ganga → Godavari

q: Which of the following is the longest canal in India?
qs.e: The longest canal in India is the Indira Gandhi Canal (formerly known as Rajasthan Canal). Its total length is about 650 km. It originates from the Harike Barrage in Punjab and traverses through the Thar Desert in Rajasthan. Its construction started in 1958. This canal provides irrigation and drinking water to districts in Rajasthan such as Sriganganagar, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, and Barmer.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest canal in India → Indira Gandhi Canal (650 km)
☛ Source of Indira Gandhi Canal → Harike Barrage, Punjab
☛ Former name of Indira Gandhi Canal → Rajasthan Canal
☛ Longest canal in the world → Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal (China)
☛ Second longest canal in India → Yamuna Eastern Canal

q: Mettur Dam is built on which river?
qs.e: Mettur Dam is a significant dam located in the state of Tamil Nadu, built across the Kaveri River. This dam is also known as the Stanley Reservoir. It is primarily used for irrigation and hydroelectric power generation. The dam has a length of approximately 1,700 meters and a maximum height of 53 meters. It is situated in the Salem district of Tamil Nadu and plays a vital role in irrigating the delta region of the Kaveri River. The Kaveri River is one of the major rivers of South India, flowing through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Mettur Dam located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ What is the other name of Mettur Dam? → Stanley Reservoir
☛ Where is the origin of the Kaveri River? → Western Ghats, Brahmagiri hills
☛ Into which bay does the Kaveri River empty? → Bay of Bengal
☛ When was Mettur Dam constructed? → 1934

q: Which is the largest salt water lake in India?
qs.e: Lake Chilka is the largest salt water lake in India, located in the state of Odisha. It is a lagoon type lake and is connected to the Bay of Bengal. Lake Chilka is also recognized as a Ramsar site and is famous for migratory birds. Lake Vembanad is the largest lake in Kerala, but it is not a salt water lake. Lake Pulica is located on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, but it is smaller than Lake Chilka. Lake Ashamudi is a freshwater lake in Kerala. Therefore, Lake Chilka is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest salt water lake in India → Lake Chilka
☛ Which state is Lake Chilka in → Odisha
☛ Type of Lake Chilka → Lagoon
☛ Which bay is connected to Lake Chilka → Bay of Bengal
☛ Which international convention is Lake Chilka a part of → Ramsar Site

q: Which of the following rivers make India's largest delta?
qs.e: The Ganga river forms India's largest delta, the Sundarbans Delta, which is also the world's largest delta. It is created by the combined flow of the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers. The Sundarbans Delta spreads across West Bengal and Bangladesh and is rich in vegetation and wildlife. The deltas of Krishna, Kaveri, and Indus are relatively smaller. The Ganga originates from the Himalayas and empties into the Bay of Bengal, forming fertile soil in the plains.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest delta in India → Sundarbans Delta (Ganga-Brahmaputra)
☛ Sundarbans famous for → Royal Bengal Tiger and mangrove forests
☛ Source of Ganga → Gangotri Glacier (Uttarakhand)
☛ Tributaries of Ganga → Yamuna, Gomti, Ghaghara, Kosi
☛ Mouth of Ganga → Bay of Bengal

q: On which river is Hirakud dam built?
qs.e: Hirakud Dam is the longest dam in India, built across the Mahanadi River in Odisha. Constructed between 1948 and 1957, it is a multipurpose project providing irrigation, hydroelectric power, and flood control. The dam's total length is about 4.8 km. The Mahanadi originates from the Sihawa hills in Chhattisgarh and flows into the Bay of Bengal. The canal system from Hirakud Dam irrigates districts like Kendrapara and Jagatsinghpur.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest dam in India → Hirakud (Mahanadi)
☛ Hirakud Dam completed in → 1957
☛ Mahanadi origin → Sihawa hills, Chhattisgarh
☛ Type of Hirakud project → Multipurpose
☛ Length of Hirakud Dam → 4.8 km

q: Sardar Sarovar Project is situated on which of the following rivers?
qs.e: The Sardar Sarovar Project is a multipurpose river valley project located on the Narmada River in Gujarat. It is one of the largest gravity dams in the world. The project aims to provide irrigation, hydroelectric power, and drinking water. Construction began in 1987 and was completed in 2017. The dam has a height of 163 meters and a reservoir capacity of 9.5 cubic kilometers. It benefits three states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra and is named after Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, India's first Deputy Prime Minister.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the height of Sardar Sarovar Dam? → 163 meters
☛ How many states are benefited by this project? → 3 states (Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra)
☛ When did its construction begin? → 1987
☛ Where does the Narmada River originate? → Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ What is the total drainage area of Narmada? → 98,796 sq km

q: The confluence of Coil and Sankh rivers is known as ______.
qs.e: The confluence of the Coil and Sankh rivers occurs in Jharkhand, and the combined stream is known as the Brahmani River. The Brahmani flows through the state of Odisha and empties into the Bay of Bengal. It is approximately 800 km long and originates from the Ranchi plateau in Jharkhand. The river forms an estuary before meeting the sea in Kendrapara district of Odisha. Its waters are important for irrigation.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the source of the Brahmani River? → Ranchi plateau, Jharkhand
☛ Which river is formed by the confluence of Coil and Sankh? → Brahmani River
☛ Through which state does the Brahmani River flow? → Odisha
☛ Where does the Brahmani River drain? → Bay of Bengal
☛ What is the length of the Brahmani River? → Approximately 800 km

q: Which of the following rivers of Jharkhand gets alluvial gold?
qs.e: The Subarnarekha River in Jharkhand contains alluvial gold. Its name is derived from Sanskrit words 'Subarna' (gold) and 'rekha' (line), indicating its gold-bearing nature. Originating from the Chota Nagpur Plateau, it flows through Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha. Gold particles are found in the alluvial deposits of this river, making it historically significant for gold panning. The other rivers—Southern Koel, Northern Koel, and Barakar—do not have documented gold presence. This distinguishes Subarnarekha from rivers like the Damodar.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is called the line of gold? → Subarnarekha
☛ What is the origin of the Subarnarekha River? → Chota Nagpur Plateau
☛ Which states does the Subarnarekha River flow through? → Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha
☛ What type of deposit is alluvial gold? → Placer deposit
☛ Which river in Jharkhand contains gold? → Subarnarekha

q: River Basins with catchment area of more than ______________ are known as major river basins.
qs.e: In India, river basins are classified based on their catchment area. A river basin with a catchment area of more than 20,000 square kilometers is known as a major river basin. This classification is done by the Ministry of Water Resources. India has 12 major river basins, including Ganga, Indus, Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, etc. The Ganga river basin is the largest, with an area of about 8.6 lakh square kilometers. Basins with an area between 2,000 and 20,000 square kilometers are called medium river basins, while those with less than 2,000 square kilometers are called minor river basins. This classification is important for water resource management and planning.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum catchment area for a major river basin → 20,000 square kilometers
☛ Catchment area of a medium river basin → 2,000 - 20,000 square kilometers
☛ Maximum catchment area for a minor river basin → 2,000 square kilometers
☛ Total number of major river basins in India → 12
☛ Largest river basin in India → Ganga (8.6 lakh square kilometers)

q: Salal, Baglihar and Dulh are the famous hydropower projects on which river?
qs.e: Salal, Baglihar, and Dulh hydropower projects are all located on the Chenab River. These three projects are situated in Jammu and Kashmir (now a union territory) and contribute significantly to India's hydropower capacity. The Chenab River is a major tributary of the Indus River system and originates in the Lahaul and Spiti region of Himachal Pradesh. The river is ideal for hydropower projects due to its high water flow volume. The Salal project has a capacity of 690 MW, Baglihar 900 MW, and Dulh 390 MW. These projects also aid in irrigation and flood control.
qs.kf:
☛ Major hydropower projects on Chenab River → Salal, Baglihar, Dulh
☛ Chenab River is part of which river system → Indus river system
☛ Origin of Chenab River → Lahaul and Spiti region of Himachal Pradesh
☛ Capacity of Salal hydropower project → 690 MW
☛ Capacity of Baglihar hydropower project → 900 MW

q: Which of the following areas is known as the food grain of South India?
qs.e: The Kaveri Delta is known as the 'food grain of South India' because it is a major rice-producing region. Located in Tamil Nadu and parts of Karnataka, this delta benefits from fertile alluvial soil and a favourable climate, making it ideal for paddy cultivation. The Kaveri river, originating from the Western Ghats, deposits rich silt, enhancing soil fertility. This delta contributes significantly to India's rice production and is often called the 'Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu'. Its extensive irrigation system supports multiple cropping seasons, ensuring high agricultural yield. Thus, the Kaveri Delta holds a crucial position in South India's food security and economy.
qs.kf:
☛ Which delta is called the food grain of South India? → Kaveri Delta
☛ What is the Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu? → Kaveri Delta
☛ Where does the Kaveri River originate? → Brahmagiri Hills, Western Ghats, Karnataka
☛ Into which bay does the Kaveri River empty? → Bay of Bengal
☛ Which states does the Kaveri Delta cover? → Tamil Nadu and Karnataka

q: Which of the following river is a big tributary of Ganges?
qs.e: The Ganges river has many tributaries, among which Son is a major one. It originates from the Amarkantak hills in Madhya Pradesh and joins the Ganges near Patna, Bihar. Ghaghra is also a major tributary, but in the given options, Son is considered correct. The Son river is about 784 km long and is known for its dams and mineral wealth. Other options like Gossip and Coca are not tributaries of the Ganges.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the longest tributary of Ganges? → Yamuna
☛ Where does Son river originate? → Amarkantak
☛ Where does Son river join the Ganges? → Near Patna
☛ What is the origin of Ghaghra river? → Mansarovar Lake in Tibet
☛ Which is the major right bank tributary of Ganges? → Yamuna

q: Which of the following is the right-bank tributary of river Godavari?
qs.e: The Godavari is the largest river in peninsular India, often called the 'Dakshin Ganga'. Its major right-bank tributaries include Manjira, Pranhita, and Indravati. The Manjira river originates from the Ballari hills in Beed district of Maharashtra and joins the Godavari in Telangana. Its total length is about 724 km. Sabari is a left-bank tributary of Godavari. Manjira is significant for the Nizam Sagar Dam, which provides irrigation and drinking water. The Godavari basin covers Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha. The Manjira river flows through a region known for its black soil and is a key water source for Hyderabad.
qs.kf:
☛ Left-bank tributary of Godavari → Sabari
☛ Right-bank tributaries of Godavari → Manjira, Pranhita, Indravati
☛ Major dam on Manjira river → Nizam Sagar Dam
☛ Origin of Godavari river → Trimbakeshwar (Nashik, Maharashtra)
☛ Total length of Godavari → Approximately 1465 km

q: Agra is located on the banks of river-
qs.e: Agra is situated on the banks of the Yamuna River in the state of Uttar Pradesh. This city was the capital of the Mughal Empire and is home to the Taj Mahal, which is located on the banks of the Yamuna. The Yamuna originates from the Yamunotri Glacier and is a major tributary of the Ganga River. The other options—Saraswati (a lost river), Sutlej (in Punjab), and Jhelum (in Kashmir)—are not associated with Agra.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is the Taj Mahal located on? → Yamuna
☛ Source of Yamuna River? → Yamunotri Glacier
☛ Length of Yamuna River? → 1376 km
☛ Yamuna is a tributary of which river? → Ganga
☛ Agra is in which state? → Uttar Pradesh

q: From where does the Sone River originate?
qs.e: The Sone River originates from the Amarkantak Hill in Madhya Pradesh, which is part of the Vindhya Range. Along with the Narmada and Johila rivers, the Sone also rises from Amarkantak. The Sone River has a total length of about 784 km and is a major tributary of the Ganga River. It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Bihar. The source of the Sone River is Amarkantak (Maikal range), while other options like Parasnath, Trikut, and Morabadi hills are not related to its origin.
qs.kf:
☛ Where does the Sone River originate? → Amarkantak Hill
☛ What is the length of the Sone River? → 784 km
☛ Which river is the Sone a tributary of? → Ganga River
☛ Which rivers originate from Amarkantak? → Narmada, Sone, Johila
☛ Which states does the Sone River flow through? → Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Bihar

q: Which of the following rivers flows into the Arabian sea?
qs.e: The Narmada river originates from the Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat before emptying into the Arabian Sea. It is one of the few major rivers in India that flows from east to west, unlike the peninsular rivers like Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery which flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada flows through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura mountain ranges. It is approximately 1,312 kilometers long and is known for the Sardar Sarovar Dam, a major multipurpose project. The Tapti river is another important river that flows into the Arabian Sea.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Narmada river → Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Major rivers flowing into Arabian Sea → Narmada, Tapti, Indus, Sabarmati, Mahi
☛ Length of Narmada river → About 1,312 km
☛ Major dam on Narmada → Sardar Sarovar Dam (Gujarat)
☛ Westward flowing rivers → Narmada and Tapti

q: Which of the following is the highest waterfall in India ?
qs.e: The highest waterfall in India is Kunchikal Falls, located in Shimoga district of Karnataka. Its height is approximately 455 meters. The waterfall is formed on the Varahi River and is situated in the dense forests of Agumbe. Earlier, Jog Falls (253 meters) was considered the highest, but recent surveys have given Kunchikal the top spot. Kunchikal is a cascading waterfall that descends in three tiers. It is a major tourist attraction in the Western Ghats.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest waterfall in India → Kunchikal (455 m)
☛ River of Kunchikal Falls → Varahi River
☛ State of Kunchikal Falls → Karnataka
☛ Second highest waterfall in India → Jog (253 m)
☛ River of Jog Falls → Sharavathi River

q: Taj Mahal is on the banks of the river-
qs.e: The Taj Mahal, located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, is situated on the banks of the Yamuna River. It was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal between 1632 and 1653. Made of white marble, it is a UNESCO World Heritage site and is considered a symbol of love. The Yamuna River flows behind the Taj Mahal, enhancing its beauty. The river originates from the Himalayas and merges with the Ganges.
qs.kf:
☛ Builder of Taj Mahal → Shah Jahan
☛ Time taken to build Taj Mahal → 22 years (1632-1653)
☛ Architectural style of Taj Mahal → Mughal architecture
☛ Taj Mahal declared UNESCO heritage in → 1983
☛ Main material used in Taj Mahal → Marble

q: Across which river is the Idukki Dam built?
qs.e: The Idukki Dam is a double curvature arch-gravity dam located in the Indian state of Kerala. It is built across the Periyar River and is part of the Idukki Hydroelectric Project. The dam is 168.91 meters high and is one of the highest arch dams in Asia. The Periyar River is often called the 'lifeline of Kerala'. The construction of the Idukki Dam was completed in 1969 and it was inaugurated in 1976. The dam impounds the waters of three rivers: Periyar, Cheruthoni, and Kudduthodu. It serves both hydroelectric power generation and irrigation purposes.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Idukki Dam located? → Kerala
☛ Across which river is the Idukki Dam built? → Periyar River
☛ What type of dam is the Idukki Dam? → Arch-gravity dam
☛ What is the height of the Idukki Dam? → 168.91 meters
☛ Which project is the Idukki Dam part of? → Idukki Hydroelectric Project

q: Taj Mahal is built on the banks of the river -
qs.e: The Taj Mahal is located on the southern bank of the Yamuna River in Agra. It was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Construction began in 1632 and was completed in 1653. The chief architect was Ustad Ahmad Lahauri. The Taj Mahal is made of white marble and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Yamuna River provides water for the gardens and helps maintain the foundation's stability and moisture balance.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Taj Mahal located? → Agra, Uttar Pradesh
☛ Who built the Taj Mahal? → Shah Jahan
☛ When was the construction of Taj Mahal started? → 1632 AD
☛ Who was the chief architect of Taj Mahal? → Ustad Ahmad Lahauri
☛ In which year was Taj Mahal declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1983

q: In which country does the river 'Mississippi' flow?
qs.e: The Mississippi River is one of the longest rivers in North America and flows entirely within the United States of America.
