☛ Which is the longest river in Peninsular India? → Godavari
☛ Where does the Godavari originate? → Trimbakeshwar, Nashik (Maharashtra)
☛ What is the other famous name of Godavari? → Dakshin Ganga or Vriddh Ganga
☛ Which is the longest river in India? → Ganges
☛ Which is the second longest river in India? → Godavari

q: Which of the following dams in India is an example for arch dam?
qs.e: Idukki dam is located on the Periyar River in Kerala and is an arch dam, the tallest arch dam in India. Arch dams have a curved design that transfers water pressure to the abutments. Idukki is a concrete arch dam primarily used for hydroelectric power generation, with a height of about 168 meters. Among the options, Bhakra Dam is a gravity dam, Tehri Dam is a rock-fill dam, and Lakhwar Dam is also a gravity dam. Only Idukki Dam is an arch dam.
qs.kf:
☛ Tallest arch dam in India → Idukki Dam (Kerala)
☛ River on which Idukki Dam is built → Periyar River
☛ Principle of arch dam → Water pressure transferred to sides
☛ Type of Bhakra Dam → Gravity dam
☛ Type of Tehri Dam → Rock-fill dam

q: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej are the tributaries of-
qs.e: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej are the tributaries of the Indus River. The Indus originates near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and flows through Pakistan into the Arabian Sea. These five rivers together form the Punjab region, meaning "land of five rivers". The Indus has a total length of about 3,180 km. These rivers originate from the Himalayas and are part of the Indus river system. The Brahmaputra, Ganga, and Yamuna belong to different river systems.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Indus River → Near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet
☛ Length of Indus River → About 3,180 km
☛ Rivers forming Punjab region → Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej
☛ Mouth of Indus River → Arabian Sea
☛ Major river systems of India → Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra

q: Which of the following rivers is known for NOT draining into the sea but rather into salt lakes or sand?
qs.e: The Luni River is a major river of Rajasthan that originates in the Aravali Range and ends in the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat. It does not drain into the sea but into a salt lake (the Rann of Kutch). Its length is about 495 km. In contrast, Chambal, Krishna, and Mahanadi all drain into the sea: Chambal joins Yamuna and eventually the Bay of Bengal, Krishna flows into the Bay of Bengal, and Mahanadi also empties into the Bay of Bengal. The Luni flows along the western slopes of the Aravalis and forms a salt lake at its mouth.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river of Rajasthan does not drain into the sea? → Luni
☛ Into which water body does the Luni River empty? → Rann of Kutch
☛ Origin of Luni River? → Aravali Range (near Ajmer)
☛ Length of Luni River? → 495 km
☛ What is the other name of Luni River? → Lavanvati

q: The Barak River, a headstream of Meghna, rises in which of the following states?
qs.e: The Barak River, a headstream of the Meghna River, rises in the hills of Manipur. It flows through Manipur, Assam, and then enters Bangladesh to join the Meghna. The total length of the Barak River is approximately 900 km. It is one of the major rivers in Northeast India. The river originates from the Borail Range in Manipur. The Barak River is known for its rich biodiversity and supports agriculture in the region. Its basin covers parts of Manipur, Assam, and Mizoram. The river finally empties into the Bay of Bengal through the Meghna estuary.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Barak River → Manipur
☛ Major tributary of Meghna River → Barak
☛ Length of Barak River → About 900 km
☛ States through which Barak flows → Manipur, Assam
☛ Mouth of Barak River → Bay of Bengal

q: Which of the following dams is not located in Uttarakhand?
qs.e: Ramganga Dam is located in Pauri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand. Lakhwar Dam is built on the Yamuna River in Dehradun district of Uttarakhand. Tehri Dam, built on the Bhagirathi River in Tehri district of Uttarakhand, is the tallest dam in India. Nagi Dam is situated on the Nagi River in Jhajha district of Bihar, and is not located in Uttarakhand. Therefore, Nagi Dam is not located in Uttarakhand.
qs.kf:
☛ Tallest dam in India → Tehri Dam (Uttarakhand)
☛ Ramganga Dam is on which river → Ramganga River
☛ Lakhwar Dam is on which river → Yamuna River
☛ Nagi Dam is in which state → Bihar
☛ Tehri Dam is on which river → Bhagirathi River

q: Which of the following rivers is NOT a part of the Deccan river system?
qs.e: The Deccan river system includes rivers of the Peninsular India that originate in the Western Ghats and flow into the Bay of Bengal. Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery are major rivers of this system. Godavari is the longest peninsular river, while Krishna is the second longest. Cauvery is an important river in South India. Sutlej is a Himalayan river and part of the Indus river system. It originates in Tibet and flows through Punjab into Pakistan. Therefore, Sutlej is not a part of the Deccan river system.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest river of Peninsular India → Godavari
☛ Sacred river of South India → Cauvery
☛ Origin of Krishna river → Mahabaleshwar
☛ Tributary of Indus river system → Sutlej
☛ Major river of Deccan river system → Godavari

q: Which of the following river systems is responsible for the formation of the Sundarbans delta?
qs.e: The Sundarbans delta is the world's largest delta, formed by the combined flow of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers. It lies in the northern part of the Bay of Bengal, spread across India and Bangladesh. The Ganga and Brahmaputra originate from the Himalayas and carry huge amounts of sediment, which accumulates at the river mouth to form the delta. The Meghna river joins the Ganga-Brahmaputra in Bangladesh, together creating a vast river system. While the Cauvery, Indus, and Godavari form their own deltas in different regions, the Sundarbans delta is exclusively formed by the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system. The delta is famous for its mangrove forests and the Royal Bengal Tiger, which make it a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
qs.kf:
☛ Rivers responsible for Sundarbans delta → Ganga, Brahmaputra and Meghna
☛ Geographical extent of Sundarbans → India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh
☛ Year Sundarbans declared a UNESCO World Heritage site → 1987
☛ Famous wildlife found in Sundarbans → Royal Bengal Tiger
☛ Alternative name for Ganga-Brahmaputra delta → Ganga Delta or Sundarbans Delta

q: Arrange the following rivers in the descending order based on the size of their basins: 1) Godavari 2) Krishna 3) Mahanadi 4) Ganga
qs.e: The Ganga river has the largest basin, covering about 10.86 lakh sq km. It is followed by Godavari with a basin area of about 3.13 lakh sq km, making it the largest peninsular river. Krishna basin covers about 2.59 lakh sq km, and Mahanadi basin covers about 1.42 lakh sq km. Hence, the descending order based on basin size is Ganga, Godavari, Krishna, Mahanadi.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest river basin in India → Ganga
☛ Largest peninsular river → Godavari
☛ Origin of Krishna river → Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra
☛ Origin of Mahanadi river → Sihawa, Chhattisgarh
☛ Origin of Godavari river → Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra

q: Which of the following river systems in Rajasthan is the most extensive and transient with its source near Pushkar, splitting into two streams known as 'Saraswati' and 'Sabarmati'?
qs.e: The Luni River is the most extensive and transient river system in Rajasthan. It originates from the Aravalli Range near Pushkar. The river splits into two streams known as Saraswati and Sabarmati. The Luni River has a total length of about 495 km and ultimately drains into the Rann of Kutch. It is the only river that flows entirely within Rajasthan, hence it is also called the 'lifeline of Rajasthan'. The water of the Luni River becomes saline near the mouth. The Godavari, Tapti, and Yamuna rivers do not flow through Rajasthan.
qs.kf:
☛ Only river of Rajasthan → Luni
☛ Source of Luni River → Aravalli Range near Pushkar
☛ Streams of Luni River → Saraswati and Sabarmati
☛ Length of Luni River → Approximately 495 km
☛ Endpoint of Luni River → Rann of Kutch

q: The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system is composed of which of the following main sub-basins?
qs.e: The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system is one of the largest delta regions in the world. This system is primarily composed of three sub-basins: the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Meghna. The Ganga river originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas, where it is known as the Bhagirathi. At Prayagraj (Allahabad), the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers converge to form the Ganga. These two streams are the main headwaters of the Ganga and are considered its principal sub-basins. Other options like Alaknanda and Gandak or Bhagirathi and Yamuna are incorrect because the Yamuna joins later and Gandak is a separate tributary. Therefore, the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda are the main sub-basins of the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system.
qs.kf:
☛ Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system → Three main sub-basins: Ganga, Brahmaputra, Meghna
☛ Origin of Ganga → Gangotri Glacier (as Bhagirathi)
☛ Confluence of Bhagirathi and Alaknanda → Prayagraj (Devprayag)
☛ Major tributary of Ganga → Yamuna (confluence at Prayagraj)
☛ Origin of Brahmaputra → In Tibet as the Tsangpo River

q: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT with reference to dams and their related states?
qs.e: The Indira Sagar Dam is located in Madhya Pradesh on the Narmada River, not in Rajasthan. It is a major multipurpose project for hydropower and irrigation. The other pairs are correct: Karjan Dam is in Gujarat on a tributary of the Narmada; Pong Dam is in Himachal Pradesh on the Beas River; and Koyna Dam is in Maharashtra on the Koyna River. The Koyna Dam is known for being associated with induced seismicity.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Indira Sagar Dam in? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Karjan Dam is on which river? → Orsang (tributary of Narmada)
☛ What is the alternate name of Pong Dam? → Maharana Pratap Sagar Dam
☛ Which national park is near Koyna Dam? → Koyna Wildlife Sanctuary
☛ Which is the largest dam on the Narmada River? → Sardar Sarovar Dam

q: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Godavari river?
qs.e: The Godavari river is the largest river in peninsular India, often called the 'Dakshin Ganga'. Its major tributaries include Purna, Pravara, Manjra, Indravati, and Wainganga. Purna and Pravara are left-bank tributaries of Godavari, while Manjra is a right-bank tributary. The Kabini river is a tributary of the Kaveri river, flowing through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Therefore, Kabini is not a tributary of the Godavari. The Godavari originates from Tryambakeshwar in Maharashtra and empties into the Bay of Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest tributary of Godavari → Manjra
☛ Major right-bank tributary of Godavari → Indravati
☛ Major tributary of Kaveri → Kabini
☛ Origin of Godavari → Tryambakeshwar, Maharashtra
☛ Delta region of Godavari → Andhra Pradesh

q: On which river system is the National Waterway 1, developed by the Indian government, built?
o: Brahmaputra river between Sadiya and Dhubri
Ganges-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system(from Haldia to Allahabad)
Stretches of Godavari and Krishna rivers
qs.e: National Waterway 1 (NW-1) is India's longest national waterway, developed on the Ganges-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system stretching from Haldia (West Bengal) to Allahabad (Uttar Pradesh). It has a total length of approximately 1,620 km. This waterway passes through Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, and is used for cargo and passenger transportation. The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) is responsible for its development and management. Various hydroelectric projects and multi-purpose river valley projects are also being implemented on NW-1.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest National Waterway → NW-1 (Ganges-Bhagirathi-Hooghly)
☛ Length of NW-1 → 1,620 km
☛ Major cities on NW-1 → Haldia, Kolkata, Patna, Varanasi, Allahabad
☛ Project associated with NW-1 → Jal Marg Vikas Project
☛ Establishment of IWAI → 1986

q: Which of the following is NOT a source of release of smokestacks?
qs.e: Smokestack emissions refer to gases and particles released into the atmosphere during industrial processes or energy generation. Thermal power plants burn coal to produce electricity and have tall chimneys that emit smoke. Smelters release harmful gases during metal extraction. Industries use smokestacks in their manufacturing processes. In contrast, rivers are water bodies and not sources of air pollution. They are associated with water pollution, but not with smokestack emissions.
qs.kf:
☛ Main cause of smokestack emissions → Coal-based thermal power plants
☛ Harmful gas released from smelters → Sulfur dioxide (SO₂)
☛ Type of pollution caused by rivers → Water pollution
☛ Alternative name for smokestack → Chimney
☛ Use of smokestacks in industries → To release waste gases into the atmosphere

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3
q: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda join to form the Ganga at _________.
qs.e: The Ganga River originates in the Himalayas. Its two main tributaries are the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda. The Bhagirathi originates from the Gangotri Glacier, while the Alaknanda originates from the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers. These two rivers meet at a place called Devprayag in Uttarakhand. After their confluence, the combined stream is known as the Ganga. Devprayag is one of the five sacred confluences (Prayags) in Hindu tradition. In Haridwar, the Ganga enters the plains, while in Rishikesh it descends from the mountains. Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Mandakini and Alaknanda rivers.
qs.kf:
☛ Two main sources of Ganga → Bhagirathi and Alaknanda
☛ Origin of Bhagirathi → Gangotri Glacier
☛ Origin of Alaknanda → Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers
☛ Confluence at Devprayag → Bhagirathi + Alaknanda = Ganga
☛ Five Prayags → Vishnuprayag, Nandaprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, Devprayag

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following rivers flows through Rajasthan?
qs.e: Luni river originates from the Aravalli hills in Ajmer district of Rajasthan and flows westward. It passes through the districts of Nagaur, Jodhpur, Barmer, and Jalore in Rajasthan. Its major tributaries include Jojari, Bandi, Sukri, and Jawai. The total length of the Luni river is about 495 kilometers, and it finally drains into the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat. Luni is also known as the 'Lavan river' because its water becomes saline downstream. Among the other options, Jhelum flows in Jammu & Kashmir, Teesta flows in Sikkim and West Bengal, and Tapi flows in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Luni river → Ajmer (Aravalli)
☛ Length of Luni river → 495 km
☛ Old name of Luni → Lavan river
☛ Major tributary of Luni → Jojari
☛ Luni river ends at → Rann of Kutch

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following rivers is NOT a major river of the Great Plateau (Peninsular Plateau) of India?
qs.e: Major rivers of the Peninsular Plateau of India include east-flowing rivers like Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery, Mahanadi and west-flowing rivers like Narmada and Tapti. The Yamuna originates from the Himalayas and is a tributary of the Ganga. It is not part of the Peninsular Plateau. Peninsular rivers are rain-fed and originate from the Western Ghats or central Indian hills. The Yamuna originates from the Yamunotri glacier in Uttarakhand. Hence, Yamuna is not a major river of the Peninsular Plateau.
qs.kf:
☛ Godavari → Longest Peninsular river (1465 km)
☛ Krishna → Flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh
☛ Narmada → Major west-flowing Peninsular river
☛ Yamuna → Himalayan river, tributary of Ganga
☛ Peninsular Plateau → also called Deccan Plateau

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (20/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which is the largest saline wetland in India?
qs.e: The largest saline wetland in India is Sambhar Lake, located in the state of Rajasthan. It is a saltwater lake with an area of about 230 sq km. This lake is also listed as a Ramsar site and is a major source of salt production in India. Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir) is the largest freshwater lake in India, while Chilika Lake (Odisha) is the largest brackish water lagoon in India. Pulicat Lake (Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu) is the second largest brackish water lagoon. Sambhar Lake is important for migratory birds and is a key center for salt production in the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest saline wetland in India → Sambhar Lake (Rajasthan)
☛ Largest freshwater lake in India → Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir)
☛ Largest brackish water lagoon in India → Chilika Lake (Odisha)
☛ Second largest brackish water lagoon in India → Pulicat Lake
☛ Sambhar Lake is located in which state → Rajasthan

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which of the following rivers originates in the Western Ghats?
qs.e: The Krishna river originates in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra. It is about 1400 km long and flows into the Bay of Bengal. In contrast, the Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas, the Brahmaputra originates from the Chemayungdung Glacier in Tibet, and the Yamuna originates from the Yamunotri Glacier in the Himalayas. Other major rivers originating in the Western Ghats include Godavari and Kaveri.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Krishna river → Mahabaleshwar, Western Ghats
☛ Length of Krishna river → approx. 1400 km
☛ Mouth of Krishna river → Bay of Bengal
☛ Origin of Ganga river → Gangotri Glacier, Himalayas
☛ Origin of Brahmaputra river → Chemayungdung Glacier, Tibet

q: Which of the following rivers is an underground river at Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj?
qs.e: At Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj, the confluence of the Ganges, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers is believed to occur. Among these, the Saraswati is an underground river that flows invisibly according to mythological beliefs. The Ganges and Yamuna are visible rivers, while Saraswati is considered hidden or subterranean. This sangam is a highly sacred site in Hinduism and hosts the Kumbh Mela.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Triveni Sangam located? → Prayagraj
☛ Which is the third river besides Ganga and Yamuna? → Saraswati
☛ What type of river is Saraswati? → Underground (invisible)
☛ Which river bank hosts the Kumbh Mela? → Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati
☛ What is the ancient name of Prayagraj? → Prayag

q: Victoria Waterfalls are located in _____.
A. United States of America
B. Britain
C. France
D. Africa
qs.e: Victoria Falls is located on the Zambezi River at the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe in southern Africa. It is one of the largest and most famous waterfalls in the world. The falls were discovered in 1855 by Scottish explorer David Livingstone, who named them after Queen Victoria. The local name is 'Mosi-oa-Tunya' (the smoke that thunders). It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The waterfall is about 1.7 km wide and 108 meters high.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Victoria Falls located? → Zambezi River
☛ Who discovered Victoria Falls? → David Livingstone
☛ What is the local name of Victoria Falls? → Mosi-oa-Tunya
☛ Which two countries share the border at Victoria Falls? → Zambia and Zimbabwe
☛ What is the width of Victoria Falls? → Approximately 1.7 km

q: Which of the following river drains into the Arabian sea?
qs.e: Tapti river originates from Multai in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward to drain into the Arabian Sea in Gujarat. It is known for its reverse flow (westward) compared to most peninsular rivers that flow eastwards into the Bay of Bengal. Tapti, along with Narmada, is one of the major west-flowing rivers of India. Its length is about 724 km. In contrast, Godavari, Krishna, and Mahanadi are east-flowing rivers that drain into the Bay of Bengal. Hence, Tapti is the only river among the options that flows into the Arabian Sea.
qs.kf:
☛ Major west-flowing peninsular rivers → Narmada and Tapti
☛ Origin of Tapti river → Multai, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Rivers draining into Arabian Sea → Tapti, Narmada, Mahi, Sabarmati
☛ Mouth of Godavari → Bay of Bengal
☛ Mouth of Krishna → Bay of Bengal

q: What was the Indira Gandhi Canal Command Area previously called as?
qs.e: The Indira Gandhi Canal Command Area was previously called the Rajasthan Canal. It is the longest canal in India, constructed to provide irrigation facilities to the arid regions of Rajasthan. The canal originates from the Harike Barrage in Punjab and flows through the Thar Desert in Rajasthan. In 1985, it was renamed as the Indira Gandhi Canal. This canal provides irrigation and drinking water to 7 districts of Rajasthan. Its total length is approximately 649 km.
qs.kf:
☛ Where does the Indira Gandhi Canal originate? → Harike Barrage, Punjab
☛ What is the total length of the Indira Gandhi Canal? → Approximately 649 km
☛ In which state is the Indira Gandhi Canal situated? → Rajasthan
☛ What was the old name of the Indira Gandhi Canal? → Rajasthan Canal
☛ When was the Indira Gandhi Canal named so? → 1985

q: By which river is the riverine island Majuli (Assam) formed?
qs.e: Majuli is a riverine island located in the state of Assam, India. It is formed by the Brahmaputra River. The Brahmaputra originates from the Chema Yungdung glacier in Tibet and flows through Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Bangladesh. Majuli is recognized as the world's largest river island and has been designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is known for its rich cultural heritage and Vaishnavite monasteries associated with saint Srimanta Sankardeva. The island is facing severe erosion, leading to a reduction in its area over time. The other options—Kaveri, Narmada, and Krishna—are rivers of South India and are not related to the formation of Majuli.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river forms the Majuli island? → Brahmaputra
☛ What is the size of Majuli island? → World's largest river island
☛ In which state is Majuli located? → Assam
☛ What is the source of the Brahmaputra river? → Chema Yungdung glacier in Tibet
☛ What is the UN status of Majuli? → UNESCO World Heritage Site

q: The Gandhi Sagar Dam is built on which river in Madhya Pradesh?
qs.e: The Gandhi Sagar Dam is built on the Chambal River in Madhya Pradesh, located on the border of Neemuch and Mandsaur districts. It is the first stage of the Chambal Valley Project, which comprises four dams. Constructed between 1954 and 1960, the dam has a height of 62 meters and generates 123 MW of hydroelectricity. The Chambal River also has a Gandhi Sagar Dam in Rajasthan. This dam provides irrigation and power, playing a crucial role in the region's development.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Chambal River → Janapav hill near Indore, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Height of Gandhi Sagar Dam → 62 meters
☛ Dams of Chambal Valley Project → Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar, Kota Barrage
☛ Hydroelectric power from Gandhi Sagar Dam → 123 MW
☛ Tributaries of Chambal River → Banas, Kalisindh, Parvati, Ahu

q: The world's largest drainage basin is:
qs.e: The Amazon River Basin is the world's largest drainage basin, covering approximately 7 million square kilometers. It spans eight countries in South America and includes the Amazon rainforest. This basin contains the largest river system in the world, discharging about 20% of the Earth's total freshwater. The Nile Basin is the second largest with about 3.4 million sq km, followed by the Mississippi Basin at about 3.2 million sq km, and the Ganga Basin at about 1 million sq km. The Amazon Basin is also known for its immense biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ World's largest drainage basin → Amazon Basin
☛ World's second largest drainage basin → Nile Basin
☛ Area of Amazon Basin → about 7 million sq km
☛ Number of countries Amazon Basin spans → 8 countries
☛ Amazon River's contribution to global freshwater → 20%

q: The river that is known as Jamuna in Bangladesh is called ______ in India.
qs.e: The Brahmaputra river originates in Tibet as Yarlung Tsangpo, enters India in Arunachal Pradesh where it is known as Siang or Dihang, and flows through Assam as Brahmaputra. In Bangladesh, it is called Jamuna before joining the Ganga and flowing into the Meghna. It is one of the major rivers of Asia.
qs.kf:
☛ Where does Brahmaputra originate? → Chemayungdung glacier near Purang, Tibet
☛ What is Brahmaputra called in Tibet? → Yarlung Tsangpo
☛ What is Brahmaputra called in Arunachal Pradesh? → Siang or Dihang
☛ What is Brahmaputra called in Bangladesh? → Jamuna
☛ Major tributary of Brahmaputra? → Lohit, Dibang, Subansiri, Manas

q: Select the pair that is NOT matched correctly (the dam of the river it is built on).
qs.e: Nathpa Jakri Dam is built on the Sutlej river in Himachal Pradesh, not on the Jhelum river. It is a hydroelectric project with a capacity of 1500 MW. The other three pairs are correctly matched: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is on the Krishna river, Tehri Dam is on the Bhagirathi river, and Indira Sagar Dam is on the Narmada river. The Jhelum river has the Dulhasti Dam (Jammu & Kashmir).
qs.kf:
☛ Nathpa Jakri Dam is on which river? → Sutlej river
☛ Tehri Dam is on which river? → Bhagirathi river
☛ Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is on which river? → Krishna river
☛ Indira Sagar Dam is on which river? → Narmada river
☛ Dulhasti Dam is on which river? → Jhelum river

q: ________ dam on the river Congo has the capacity to produce up to 40,000 MW of electric power.
qs.e: The Inga Dam on the Congo River is one of the world's largest hydroelectric projects, with a capacity to produce up to 40,000 MW. Located in the Democratic Republic of Congo, it is being developed in phases. Once completed, it will be the largest hydroelectric plant in the world. Its enormous capacity makes it crucial for Africa's and the global energy market. Other options like Akosombo, Bloemhof, and Kouga are African dams but have lower capacities compared to Inga.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is the Inga Dam located? → Congo River
☛ What is the total installed capacity of the Inga Dam? → 40,000 MW
☛ Which is the world's largest hydroelectric plant (when completed)? → Inga
☛ In which country is the Inga Dam located? → Democratic Republic of Congo
☛ Which are the major dams in Africa? → Akosombo (Ghana), Bloemhof (South Africa), Kouga (South Africa)

q: Which of the following rivers is NOT the tributary of Ganga?
qs.e: Major tributaries of the Ganga river include Yamuna, Son, Gomati, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, etc. Yamuna is the largest tributary, meeting the Ganga at Prayagraj. Son river flows from the south and joins the Ganga near Patna. Gomati flows through Lucknow and joins the Ganga near Ghazipur. Indravati river is NOT a tributary of the Ganga; it is a tributary of the Godavari river. Indravati originates in Chhattisgarh and flows through Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh before joining the Godavari.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest tributary of Ganga is Yamuna
☛ Origin of Son river is Amarkantak, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Gomati meets Ganga at Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh
☛ Indravati is a tributary of Godavari
☛ Length of Ganga river is approximately 2525 km

q: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of Krishna?
qs.e: The major tributaries of Krishna river include Ghatprabha, Tungabhadra and Musi. The Manjira river is actually a tributary of Godavari river, not Krishna. Krishna river is the fourth longest river in India and flows through peninsular India. Its other important tributaries include Bhima, Koyna, and Malaprabha. The Krishna originates at Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra and empties into the Bay of Bengal. The Musi river flows through Hyderabad and joins the Krishna.
qs.kf:
☛ Left bank tributary of Godavari → Manjira
☛ Right bank tributary of Krishna → Tungabhadra
☛ Left bank tributary of Krishna → Bhima
☛ Ghatprabha is tributary of → Krishna
☛ Musi is tributary of → Krishna

q: Which river is associated with the Dhuandhar falls?
qs.e: The Dhuandhar Falls is located on the Narmada River in Jabalpur district, Madhya Pradesh. It is formed when the Narmada River passes through a narrow gorge at Bhedaghat, creating a mist-like effect due to the force of water, hence its name 'Dhuandhar'. The Narmada River flows through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat, and empties into the Arabian Sea. It is considered one of the holiest rivers in India. The total length of the Narmada River is about 1,312 km. Among the other options, Kaveri, Mahanadi, and Tapi rivers are not associated with the Dhuandhar falls.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Dhuandhar Falls located? → Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh
☛ What is the source of the Narmada River? → Amarkantak, Anuppur district
☛ Which sea does the Narmada River flow into? → Arabian Sea
☛ What is the height of Dhuandhar Falls? → Nearly 10 meters
☛ Which is a tributary of the Narmada River? → Tawa, Hiran

q: Among the following rivers, which is a good example of a superimposed drainage system?
qs.e: A superimposed drainage system develops when a river establishes its course over an underlying structure, disregarding the original topography. The Subarnarekha River is a classic example. Originating from the Chota Nagpur Plateau, it cuts through resistant rocks and flows into the Bay of Bengal. Its path is independent of the present geological structure and represents a pre-existing drainage imposed on a new landscape. Other rivers like Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Gomti exhibit structural or dendritic patterns, not superimposed. Hence, Subarnarekha best exemplifies a superimposed drainage system.
qs.kf:
☛ Example of superimposed drainage → Subarnarekha River
☛ Origin of Subarnarekha → Chota Nagpur Plateau
☛ Mouth of Subarnarekha → Bay of Bengal
☛ Subarnarekha basin states → Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha
☛ Feature of superimposed drainage → River imposes its course on geological structure

q: Which pair is NOT correct regarding dams and the states they are situated in?
qs.e: Shanti Sagara (Shantisagara) lake is located in the state of Karnataka, not Kerala. It is a reservoir built on the Tungabhadra River. The other pairs are correct: Stanley Reservoir in Tamil Nadu on the Kaveri River, Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna River bordering Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and Gobind Sagar in Himachal Pradesh on the Sutlej River. Hence, the pair Shanti Sagara–Kerala is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ Stanley Reservoir is located on which river? → Kaveri River (Tamil Nadu)
☛ Nagarjuna Sagar lies on the border of which states? → Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
☛ Shanti Sagara is situated in which state? → Karnataka
☛ Which dam is built on Gobind Sagar? → Bhakra Dam (Sutlej River)
☛ Which is one of the largest man-made reservoirs in India? → Gobind Sagar

q: Which of the following rivers is a peninsular river?
qs.e: The Tapti River is a peninsular river that originates from Multai in Madhya Pradesh, flows westward, and empties into the Gulf of Khambhat. Peninsular rivers mainly originate from the peninsular plateau of South India and depend on rainfall. Tapti is not navigable due to its short length and shallow waters. Beas is a Himalayan river, while Betwa and Chambal are tributaries of the Ganga and are not peninsular. Tapti, along with Narmada, is a major west-flowing peninsular river.
qs.kf:
☛ Peninsular river origin: Tapti → Multai (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Peninsular river mouth: Tapti → Gulf of Khambhat
☛ Peninsular river length: Tapti → about 724 km
☛ West-flowing peninsular rivers: Narmada and Tapti
☛ Himalayan river: Beas → originates from Himalayas

q: Ramsar Convention is related to conservation of ________.
qs.e: The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty signed in 1971 in the city of Ramsar, Iran, for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. Its primary objective is to protect wetlands, including habitats for waterbirds. Currently, 172 countries are parties to the convention. India has over 80 Ramsar sites, including Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park. This convention is not related to climate change, soil, or clean air.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of Ramsar Convention → 1971
☛ Place of Ramsar Convention → Ramsar, Iran
☛ First Ramsar sites in India → Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park
☛ Total Ramsar sites in India (2024) → Over 80
☛ Objective of Ramsar Convention → Conservation and sustainable use of wetlands

q: On which river is the Smokhara waterfall situated?
qs.e: The Smokhara waterfall is a famous waterfall located in the Dindori district of Madhya Pradesh. It is situated on the Narmada river. The Narmada is a major river in central India, originating from Amarkantak and flowing into the Gulf of Khambhat. The Smokhara waterfall is formed due to rocks in the river's path. This area is known for its natural beauty and is popular among tourists. The Narmada river flows through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. The name 'Smokhara' is given in the local dialect.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Narmada river → Amarkantak
☛ Length of Narmada river → 1312 km
☛ Narmada river falls into which gulf → Gulf of Khambhat
☛ Famous waterfall on Narmada river → Dhuandhar
☛ Smokhara waterfall is in which district → Dindori

q: Which of the following is located on the Zuari River estuary?
qs.e: Mormugao port is a major natural harbor located at the mouth of the Zuari River in Goa. It connects to the Arabian Sea and is the main port of Goa. The Zuari River originates in the Western Ghats and flows into the Arabian Sea. Mormugao port is situated on the west coast of India and is famous for the export of iron ore. Cochin port is located in Kerala on the Arabian Sea, New Mangalore port is in Karnataka on the Gurupura River, and Mumbai port is in Maharashtra.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Mormugao port located? → Zuari River
☛ What are the major rivers of Goa? → Zuari and Mandovi rivers
☛ For which export is Mormugao port famous? → Iron ore
☛ Where is Cochin port located? → Kerala
☛ On which river's estuary is New Mangalore port? → Gurupura River

q: The Mahanadi and Krishna rivers are said to be the coastal plains.
qs.e: The coastal plain formed by the Mahanadi and Krishna rivers is called the Northern Circars. This is part of the Eastern Coastal Plain of India, extending from Odisha to Tamil Nadu. It includes the deltas of major rivers like Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri. The Eastern Coastal Plain is divided into two sections: the Northern Circars (from Mahanadi to Krishna) and the Coromandel Coast (from Krishna to Kaveri). The region has fertile alluvial soil and supports extensive cultivation of rice, sugarcane, and cotton. The name "Circars" comes from the Arabic word for "provinces" and was used during the British colonial period. This area is known for its rich agricultural output and dense population.
qs.kf:
☛ Eastern Coastal Plain → Divided into Northern Circars and Coromandel Coast
☛ Northern Circars → Stretches from Mahanadi to Krishna River
☛ Coromandel Coast → Stretches from Krishna to Kaveri River
☛ Western Coastal Plain → Divided into Konkan, Kannad, and Malabar coasts
☛ Northern Circars → Also known as the Mahanadi-Krishna coastal plain

q: Which of the following is the tributary of Teesta river?
qs.e: The Teesta River flows through the Indian states of Sikkim and West Bengal and is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River. The Rangpo River is a major tributary of the Teesta in Sikkim. Hooghly is a distributary of the Ganges, while Son and Betwa are tributaries of the Ganges, having no connection with the Teesta.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is the Teesta a tributary of? → Brahmaputra
☛ Where does the Teesta River originate? → Sikkim's Soma La Glacier
☛ Name two major tributaries of the Teesta. → Rangpo and Lachung
☛ Which states does the Teesta flow through? → Sikkim and West Bengal
☛ Where does the Teesta River join the Brahmaputra? → In Bangladesh near the border with India

q: Shivsamudra project is on which river?
qs.e: Shivsamudra project is a hydroelectric project located on the Kaveri River in Karnataka, India. It was the first hydroelectric project in India, commissioned in 1902. The project utilizes the Shivsamudra Falls, a waterfall on the Kaveri River, often called the 'Niagara of India'. The project is situated in Mandya district, Karnataka. The Kaveri River originates from Brahmagiri hills in Karnataka and flows through Tamil Nadu before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is India's first hydroelectric project? → Shivsamudra (on Kaveri River, 1902)
☛ Shivsamudra Falls is on which river? → Kaveri
☛ Shivsamudra project is in which state? → Karnataka
☛ Where is the origin of Kaveri River? → Brahmagiri hills, Karnataka
☛ Major tributaries of Kaveri River? → Hemavati, Kabini, Bhavani

q: The Bhakra-Nangal dam is built on which river?
qs.e: The Bhakra-Nangal dam is India's tallest gravity dam, built on the Sutlej River. It is located on the border of Punjab and Himachal Pradesh. The dam has a height of 226 meters and is one of India's largest multipurpose projects. Its construction was completed in 1963, aiding irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control.
qs.kf:
☛ Bhakra-Nangal dam is built on which river? → Sutlej
☛ Height of Bhakra-Nangal dam? → 226 meters
☛ Year of completion of Bhakra-Nangal dam? → 1963
☛ Type of Bhakra-Nangal dam? → Gravity dam
☛ Bhakra-Nangal dam borders which states? → Punjab and Himachal Pradesh

q: The longest river of peninsular India is -
qs.e: The longest river of peninsular India is the Godavari, with a total length of approximately 1465 kilometers. It is also known as the Dakshin Ganga (Southern Ganges). Originating from Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra, it flows through Andhra Pradesh before draining into the Bay of Bengal. Other options: Mahanadi (858 km), Tapti (724 km), Narmada (1312 km). Major tributaries of Godavari include Pranhita, Indravati, and Manjira. Cities like Nashik and Rajahmundry are located on its banks.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Godavari → Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra
☛ Major tributary of Godavari → Pranhita
☛ Other name of Godavari → Dakshin Ganga
☛ Length of Godavari → 1465 km
☛ Mouth of Godavari → Bay of Bengal

q: Across which of the following rivers is Mettur Dam built?
qs.e: Mettur Dam is built across the Cauvery River in Tamil Nadu. It creates the Stanley Reservoir and is crucial for irrigation in the Cauvery Delta. The dam is about 120 feet high and was completed in 1934. It supports agriculture, hydroelectric power generation, and drinking water supply. The dam is also central to water disputes between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
qs.kf:
☛ Across which river is Mettur Dam built? → Cauvery
☛ Where is Stanley Reservoir located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ What is the height of Mettur Dam? → 120 feet
☛ When was Mettur Dam completed? → 1934
☛ What is the origin of Cauvery River? → Brahmagiri range, Western Ghats

q: The Punjab Plain is formed by which river system?
qs.e: The Punjab Plain is formed by the Indus river system. This plain is built by the alluvial deposits of the Indus River and its five major tributaries: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej. The word 'Punjab' means 'land of five rivers,' referring specifically to these tributaries. The plain extends across northwestern India and eastern Pakistan. The Indus river system originates in the Himalayas and flows into the Arabian Sea.
qs.kf:
☛ River system forming the Punjab Plain → Indus river system
☛ Major tributaries of Indus → Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej
☛ Meaning of 'Punjab' → Land of five rivers
☛ Origin of Indus river → Mount Kailash in Tibet
☛ Mouth of Indus river → Arabian Sea (near Karachi)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2
q: What is the region lying to the north of the Narmada River called?
qs.e: The region lying north of the Narmada River is called the Central Highlands. It forms the northern part of the Peninsular Plateau, lying between the Narmada River and the Deccan Plateau. The Central Highlands include the Bundelkhand, Malwa Plateau, and the Vindhya Range. In contrast, the Deccan Plateau lies to the south of the Narmada. The Chota Nagpur Plateau is located in eastern India, while the Eastern Ghats are along the eastern coast. The Central Highlands have an average elevation of about 500-1000 meters and are known for black soil, which is suitable for cotton cultivation. This region is agriculturally significant and rich in mineral resources.
qs.kf:
☛ Region north of Narmada River? → Central Highlands
☛ Major plateaus in Central Highlands? → Malwa Plateau and Bundelkhand
☛ River separating Deccan Plateau from Central Highlands? → Narmada River
☛ Geographic extent of Central Highlands? → From Narmada to Chota Nagpur Plateau
☛ Soil type in Central Highlands? → Black soil

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following rivers rises in the western slopes of the Aravalli Range near Ajmer, where it is known as the Sagarmati?
qs.e: The Luni River originates from the western slopes of the Aravalli Range near Ajmer, where it is known as Sagarmati. It is the only major river in Rajasthan that flows westward and finally disappears into the Rann of Kutch. The total length of the Luni River is about 495 kilometers. It is also called the 'Lavan River' because its water becomes highly saline. The river remains fresh from its origin up to Balotra, but turns saline afterwards. The catchment area of the Luni River is mainly spread across Rajasthan.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the other name of Luni River? → Sagarmati
☛ Where does the Luni River disappear? → Rann of Kutch
☛ What is the total length of Luni River? → 495 km
☛ Which state does the Luni River flow through? → Rajasthan
☛ Why is Luni River called Lavan River? → Because of its saline water

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which canal project plays a major role in irrigation in the Thar Desert?
qs.e: The Indira Gandhi Canal is the most important canal project for irrigation in the Thar Desert. Previously known as the Rajasthan Canal, it originates from the Harike Barrage in Punjab and extends into Rajasthan, covering districts like Sri Ganganagar, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, and Barmer. Its total length is about 906 km and it primarily uses water from the Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi rivers. The project aims to irrigate dry areas and provide drinking water. It has transformed the region, enabling agriculture in the desert.
qs.kf:
☛ Former name of Indira Gandhi Canal → Rajasthan Canal
☛ Harike Barrage is at the confluence of which rivers → Sutlej and Beas
☛ Total length of Indira Gandhi Canal → 906 km
☛ State where this canal is located → Rajasthan
☛ Districts benefited by Indira Gandhi Canal → Sri Ganganagar, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Barmer

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1
q: The Chotanagpur Plateau is drained by which river system?
qs.e: The Chotanagpur Plateau is primarily drained by the Damodar River and its tributaries. The Damodar River flows through the central part of the plateau and is often called the 'Sorrow of Bengal' due to its history of floods. It originates in the plateau region and flows through the states of Jharkhand and West Bengal. Most of the plateau falls within the Damodar Valley, which is rich in coal and mineral resources. The Tapi River flows in western India, while Krishna and Godavari are major rivers of southern India. Therefore, the Chotanagpur Plateau is drained by the Damodar river system.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river drains the Chotanagpur Plateau? → Damodar
☛ Where does the Damodar River originate? → Chotanagpur Plateau (Tilaiya)
☛ Which bay does the Damodar River join? → Bay of Bengal via Hooghly River
☛ What is the Damodar Valley known for? → Coal and mineral resources
☛ Why is Damodar called 'Sorrow of Bengal'? → Due to floods

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following rivers forms the Majuli Island, the world's largest river island?
qs.e: Majuli Island is the world's largest river island, formed by the Brahmaputra River in the state of Assam. It is situated between the Brahmaputra and its tributary Subansiri River. Majuli has been recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh. The island is formed by the deposition of sediments carried by the river. Other rivers like Ganga, Godavari, and Mahanadi do not create such large islands.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river forms Majuli Island? → Brahmaputra
☛ In which state is Majuli Island located? → Assam
☛ What is the world's largest river island? → Majuli
☛ Which is the largest tributary of Brahmaputra? → Subansiri
☛ Which organization declared Majuli a World Heritage Site? → UNESCO

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2
q: The Great Plains of India were primarily formed due to the deposition by which of the following rivers?
qs.e: The Great Plains of India were primarily formed due to the depositional work of the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers. These rivers originate from the Himalayas and carry huge amounts of sediment, which over time accumulated to form fertile plains. This region is known as the Northern Indian Plains or the Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plains. It is the largest alluvial plain in the world and highly fertile for agriculture. Other options include Narmada, Tapi, Mahanadi, Krishna, Godavari, Kaveri, Yamuna, Sutlej, and Gomti, but they do not play a major role in the formation of the Great Plains.
qs.kf:
☛ Which rivers formed the Northern Indian Plains? → Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra
☛ What type of plain is the Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain? → Alluvial plain
☛ Which is the most fertile plain in India? → Northern Indian Plains
☛ Which type of river is Narmada? → Peninsular river
☛ Where is the origin of Godavari river? → Trimbakeshwar, Nashik

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following is the largest Peninsular river?
qs.e: The Godavari is the longest Peninsular river in India, with a total length of about 1,465 km. It originates from the Trimbakeshwar hills in Nashik district, Maharashtra, and flows into the Bay of Bengal. Also known as the 'Ganga of the South', the Godavari has the largest drainage basin among Peninsular rivers, covering an area of approximately 3,12,812 sq km. The Narmada is the second longest Peninsular river, while the Mahanadi and Kaveri are shorter. Major tributaries of the Godavari include Pranahita, Manjira, and Penganga. The river flows through Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the longest Peninsular river in India? → Godavari
☛ Where does the Godavari river originate? → Trimbakeshwar, Nashik
☛ What is the drainage area of the Godavari river? → 3,12,812 sq km
☛ What is the Godavari also known as? → Ganga of the South
☛ Which is the largest tributary of the Godavari? → Pranahita

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following is a tributary of the Yamuna river?
qs.e: Major tributaries of the Yamuna river include Tons, Chambal, Betwa, Ken, Sindh, and Hindon. The Tons river originates from the Himalayas and meets the Yamuna, being its largest tributary. The Son river is a tributary of the Ganga, Teesta is a tributary of the Brahmaputra, and Gomti is also a tributary of the Ganga. Therefore, Tons is the correct tributary of the Yamuna.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest tributary of Yamuna → Tons
☛ Origin of Yamuna river → Yamunotri Glacier
☛ Length of Yamuna river → Approximately 1376 km
☛ Yamuna river is a tributary of → Ganga
☛ Origin of Tons river → Bandarpunch mountain

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 3
q: The Narmada River originates from which hills?
qs.e: The Narmada River originates from the Amarkantak plateau, which is part of the Satpura mountain range in Madhya Pradesh. It flows westward and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat. The Narmada is one of India's major rivers and is considered the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Its total length is approximately 1312 kilometers. The river flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges. It is the longest west-flowing river in peninsular India. The Amarkantak origin point is also a famous pilgrimage site.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of Narmada River → 1312 km
☛ Origin of Narmada River → Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Narmada River flows into → Gulf of Khambhat
☛ States through which Narmada flows → Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat
☛ Tributary of Narmada → Tawa

q: Which river originates from Amarkantak?
qs.e: Amarkantak is a prominent religious and geographical site located in the Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh. The Narmada River originates from here. Narmada is a major river flowing through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, also known as 'Mekal Suta'. It flows westward and merges into the Gulf of Khambhat. The source of Narmada lies on the Amarkantak Plateau, where the Son and Johila rivers also originate. Narmada is known for its reverse direction (east to west). This river is the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Amarkantak is also called 'Teerthraj'.
qs.kf:
☛ River originating from Amarkantak → Narmada
☛ Source of Narmada River → Amarkantak Plateau
☛ Narmada merges into → Gulf of Khambhat
☛ Other rivers originating from Amarkantak → Son and Johila
☛ Flow direction of Narmada → East to West

q: In which of the following does the river Godavari originate?
qs.e: The Godavari river originates from the Thriambak hills (Bramhagiri hills) located in Nasik district, Maharashtra. It is the longest river in peninsular India, often called the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganges of the South). Its total length is approximately 1,465 km and it flows into the Arabian Sea. The other options are associated with the Ganga river system: Yamunotri is the source of Yamuna, Gangotri is the source of Ganga, and the hills of Coorg are related to the origin of the Kaveri. Major tributaries of Godavari include Pranhita, Indravati, and Manjira.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Godavari river → Thriambak hills (Bramhagiri hills), Nasik, Maharashtra
☛ Godavari is also known as → Dakshin Ganga
☛ Total length of Godavari → Approximately 1,465 km
☛ Godavari ends into → Arabian Sea
☛ Largest tributary of Godavari → Pranhita

q: India's largest salt water lake is situated in:
qs.e: India's largest salt water lake is Chilka Lake, located in the Mahanadi Delta region of Odisha. It is a lagoon connected to the Bay of Bengal. Its area varies seasonally, from about 900 sq km in summer to 1,165 sq km during the monsoon. Chilka Lake is known for its rich biodiversity and hosts many migratory bird species. It was declared a Ramsar Site in 1981. The lake is also important for fishing and tourism.
qs.kf:
☛ India's largest salt water lake → Chilka Lake (Odisha)
☛ Chilka Lake lies in the delta of which river? → Mahanadi
☛ When was Chilka Lake declared a Ramsar Site? → 1981
☛ Chilka Lake is what type of lake? → Lagoon
☛ Chilka Lake is in which state? → Odisha

q: Which of the following rivers flows into the Arabian Sea?
qs.e: The Sabarmati river originates from the Aravalli Range in Rajasthan, flows through Gujarat, and empties into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). The Godavari and Krishna rivers drain into the Bay of Bengal, while the Luni river ends in the Rann of Kutch. Sabarmati has a total length of 371 km and passes through cities like Gandhinagar and Ahmedabad. The Sabarmati Ashram, associated with Mahatma Gandhi, is located on its banks.
qs.kf:
☛ West-flowing river → Sabarmati
☛ River falling into Gulf of Khambhat → Sabarmati, Narmada, Tapti
☛ River ending in Rann of Kutch → Luni
☛ River falling into Bay of Bengal → Godavari, Krishna, Ganga, Mahanadi
☛ Origin of Sabarmati → Aravalli Range

q: Which type of natural vegetation is found in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta?
qs.e: The Ganges-Brahmaputra delta, also known as the Sundarbans delta, is the largest mangrove forest area in the world. The natural vegetation found here consists of mangrove trees, which thrive in saline water environments. These trees develop specialized respiratory roots called pneumatophores to aid in gas exchange. The Sundarbans is also home to the Royal Bengal Tiger. Rosewood, mulberry, and Indian chestnut trees are found in other regions, not in this delta. Hence, the correct answer is mangrove trees.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for Ganges-Brahmaputra delta → Sundarbans delta
☛ Special roots of mangrove trees → Pneumatophores
☛ Key animal found in Sundarbans → Royal Bengal Tiger
☛ Mangrove forests are found in → Saline coastal areas
☛ World's largest mangrove forest → Sundarbans (in Bangladesh and India)

q: How many types of Indian river systems are there?
qs.e: Indian river systems are mainly classified into two types: Himalayan river system and Peninsular river system. Himalayan rivers like Ganga, Indus, and Brahmaputra originate from the Himalayas and are perennial as they receive water from both rainfall and snowmelt. Peninsular rivers like Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri originate from the Western Ghats and are seasonal as they depend mostly on rainfall. These two systems differ in their origin, water flow, and geographical features.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest river in India → Ganga
☛ Origin of Peninsular rivers → Western Ghats
☛ Major source of Himalayan rivers → Himalayas
☛ Rivers with perennial nature → Himalayan rivers
☛ Godavari drains into → Bay of Bengal

q: What is the name of only lake formed by a meteorite in India?
qs.e: The only lake in India formed by a meteorite is Lonar Lake, located in Buldhana district, Maharashtra. It was created around 50,000 years ago by the impact of a meteorite, which formed a crater that later filled with water. It is a saline lake with a diameter of about 1.8 km. Lonar Lake has been designated as a Ramsar site, highlighting its ecological importance. The lake is famous for its unique ecosystem supporting both saline and freshwater organisms. Dal Lake in Srinagar is man-made, Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in Jammu & Kashmir, and Bhimtal is a natural lake in Uttarakhand.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Lonar Lake located? → Maharashtra
☛ What type of lake is Lonar Lake? → Meteorite/Crater lake
☛ How old is Lonar Lake? → Approximately 50,000 years
☛ Which international designation does Lonar Lake have? → Ramsar site
☛ What is the water of Lonar Lake like? → Saline

q: Mechi, a trans-boundary river flowing through India and Nepal is a tributary of _____river.
qs.e: Mechi River is a trans-boundary river flowing along the border of India and Nepal. It is a tributary of the Mahananda River. The Mechi originates from the Mahabharat Range in Nepal and flows through the Indian states of Bihar and West Bengal. The total length of the Mechi River is approximately 138 kilometers. The Mahananda River originates from the glaciers of the Himalayas and flows through Bihar and West Bengal before joining the Ganga River. The other options, Gandak, Godavari, and Ganga, are not the main river of which Mechi is a tributary.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Mechi River → Mahabharat Range in Nepal
☛ Mechi is a tributary of which river → Mahananda River
☛ Mahananda River joins which river → Ganga River
☛ Length of Mechi River → Approximately 138 km
☛ States through which Mechi flows → Bihar and West Bengal

q: Which of the following rivers flows into the Bay of Bengal?
qs.e: The Kaveri River is a major river in South India that flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and empties into the Bay of Bengal. The Tapi and Narmada rivers flow into the Arabian Sea, while the Indus River also flows into the Arabian Sea. The Kaveri originates from the Brahmagiri hills in Karnataka and is about 800 km long. Major dams like Mettur Dam and Krishnarajasagar Dam are built on this river.
qs.kf:
☛ Rivers flowing into Bay of Bengal → Ganga, Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri
☛ Rivers flowing into Arabian Sea → Indus, Narmada, Tapi
☛ Length of Kaveri River → approx 800 km
☛ Origin of Kaveri → Western Ghats, Brahmagiri hills
☛ Largest dam on Kaveri → Mettur Dam

q: The tributaries of rivers Ganga and Brahmaputra together from the Ganga - Brahmaputra basin in the Indian subcontinent. Which of the following is NOT a feature of the river basin?
o: Ox-bow lakes dot the plain area.
In the south is the Sundarbans Delta.
It's a fertile area that includes most of north and east India.
It is bound on the north by mountains and the foothills of the Himalayas.
qs.e: The Ganga-Brahmaputra basin is located in northern India, bounded on the north by the foothills of the Himalayas and on the south by the highlands of peninsular India. The Sundarbans Delta, situated in Bangladesh and West Bengal, lies along the Bay of Bengal, not at the southern boundary of the basin. The basin includes fertile plains covering most of north and east India, and features ox-bow lakes in the plain area. The Sundarbans Delta is part of the basin, but stating it as 'in the south' is incorrect because the southern boundary is the Deccan Plateau. Therefore, the correct answer is the option claiming the Sundarbans Delta is in the south.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the southern boundary of the Ganga-Brahmaputra basin? → Highlands of peninsular India
☛ Type of lakes found in the basin? → Ox-bow lakes
☛ Where is the Sundarbans Delta located? → Coast of Bay of Bengal
☛ Which regions are covered by the basin? → North and east India
☛ What is the northern boundary of the basin? → Foothills of Himalayas

q: On which of the following river banks is the city of Nasik located?
qs.e: Nasik is a major city in Maharashtra, situated on the banks of the Godavari River. This city holds religious, historical, and industrial significance. The Godavari, one of India's major rivers, is known as the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganges of the South). It originates from the Trimbakeshwar hills in the Nashik district of Maharashtra. Nasik hosts the Kumbh Mela every 12 years on the banks of the Godavari. The Tapti River flows through Madhya Pradesh and empties into the Gulf of Khambhat. The Jhelum River flows through Jammu & Kashmir. The Cauvery River flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Nasik located? → Godavari
☛ Where does the Godavari originate? → Trimbakeshwar, Nashik
☛ What is Godavari also known as? → Dakshin Ganga
☛ Which fair is held in Nasik? → Kumbh Mela
☛ Where does the Tapti River empty? → Gulf of Khambhat

q: Which of the following rivers is also known as the 'River of Sorrow?'
qs.e: Damodar River is known as the 'River of Sorrow' because it frequently caused devastating floods, leading to heavy loss of life and property in Jharkhand and West Bengal. Originating from the Chota Nagpur Plateau, it flows into the Hooghly River. During the monsoon, its water level rises rapidly, causing floods in the lower regions. The establishment of the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) helped control floods, provide irrigation, and generate hydroelectricity. Major dams like Maithon and Panchet have been built on this river.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Damodar River → Chota Nagpur Plateau
☛ Damodar River merges into? → Hooghly River
☛ Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) established in? → 1948
☛ Famous dam on Damodar River → Maithon Dam
☛ Why Damodar is called 'River of Sorrow'? → Due to frequent floods

q: Yamuna and Gomati are the tributaries of river -
qs.e: Yamuna and Gomati are major tributaries of the river Ganga. The Yamuna is the longest tributary of the Ganga, originating from the Yamunotri Glacier and joining the Ganga at Prayagraj. The Gomati river originates from the Madhya Pradesh's Manhar Parvat and meets the Ganga near Saidpur, Ghazipur. The other options, Mahanadi, Godavari, and Krishna, are peninsular rivers and are not part of the Ganga river system.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the longest tributary of Ganga? → Yamuna
☛ Where does Gomati river originate? → Manhar Parvat (Madhya Pradesh)
☛ Which are major tributaries of Ganga? → Yamuna, Gomati, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi
☛ Where does Yamuna meet Ganga? → Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam)
☛ Which is the longest tributary of Ganga in Uttar Pradesh? → Yamuna

q: Which of the following is the National Waterway 2 in India?
o: West Coast canal and Champakara and Udyogmandal canals
East Coast canal and Matai river
qs.e: National Waterway 2 (NW-2) in India is located on the Brahmaputra river, stretching from Sadiya to Dhubri in Assam, covering a distance of approximately 891 km. This waterway is a crucial commercial and transport route for the northeastern region. NW-2 was declared under the National Waterways Act in 1988. India currently has 111 national waterways, with NW-1 on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly, NW-2 on the Brahmaputra, NW-3 on the West Coast canal, and NW-4 on the Krishna-Godavari rivers. The East Coast canal and Matai river, Kakinada canal are associated with other waterways. NW-2 aids the economic development of northeastern India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is NW-2 on? → Brahmaputra
☛ What is the total length of NW-2? → 891 km
☛ Where does NW-2 run from and to? → Sadiya to Dhubri
☛ When was NW-2 declared? → 1988
☛ How many national waterways are there in India? → 111

q: Which of the following waterways is located on the Tapi river?
qs.e: The National Waterway located on the Tapi river is NW-100. This waterway stretches 46 km from the mouth of the Tapi river to Surat in Gujarat. India has declared a total of 111 National Waterways. NW-10 is on the Godavari river, NW-91 on the Krishna river, and NW-1 on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system. Hence, NW-100 is the only waterway situated on the Tapi river. It is connected to Surat port and holds commercial importance.
qs.kf:
☛ National Waterway on Tapi river → NW-100
☛ National Waterway on Godavari river → NW-10
☛ National Waterway on Krishna river → NW-91
☛ National Waterway on Ganga river → NW-1
☛ Total number of National Waterways in India → 111

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which river system is known for forming gorges in the Himalayan region?
qs.e: The Brahmaputra river originates near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and flows parallel to the Himalayas before entering India through Arunachal Pradesh. This river is known for forming deep gorges in the Himalayan region due to its steep gradient and high water volume. Notably, it creates a deep gorge in the Dihang valley in Arunachal Pradesh. In contrast, other options like Godavari, Tapti, and Penner are peninsular rivers that do not originate in the Himalayas and do not form such gorges. The Brahmaputra's erosional power is enhanced by heavy rainfall and sediment load, making it one of the most dynamic rivers in the region.
qs.kf:
☛ Where does Brahmaputra originate? → Tibet near Lake Mansarovar
☛ What is Brahmaputra called in India? → Dihang or Siang
☛ World's largest river island is? → Majuli (in Brahmaputra)
☛ Type of water in Brahmaputra? → Freshwater
☛ Largest Himalayan river gorge? → Indus Gorge

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following is a key river in the Thar Desert region?
qs.e: The Luni river is the key river in the Thar Desert region, also known as the Rajasthan desert. It originates from the Aravalli hills near Ajmer and ends in the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat. The Luni is often called the 'river of salt' because its water is saline. It is crucial for life in the desert, providing water for irrigation and drinking. Other options: Yamuna is a tributary of Ganga, Sutlej flows in Punjab, and Ghaggar disappears in Haryana, not in Thar.
qs.kf:
☛ Key river of Thar Desert → Luni river
☛ Origin of Luni river → Aravalli hills (near Ajmer)
☛ Mouth of Luni river → Rann of Kutch
☛ Nickname of Luni river → River of salt
☛ Water type of Luni river → Saline (brackish)

q: The Government of India has classified ______ rivers as major rivers in India.
qs.e: The Government of India has classified the rivers of the country into major, medium, and minor categories. According to this classification, 12 rivers are placed under the major rivers category. The major rivers include Indus, Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, Narmada, Tapti, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Pennar, and Brahmani. These rivers are prominent due to their catchment area, water flow, and cultural significance. This classification is important for water resource management and river projects.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of major rivers in India → 12
☛ Longest river in India → Ganga
☛ Second longest river in India → Godavari
☛ Longest river in Peninsular India → Godavari
☛ Largest river basin in India → Ganga basin

q: Which of the following is not a river with inland drainage?
A. Rupen B. Banas C. Periyar D. Saraswati
qs.e: Periyar river flows in Kerala and drains into the Arabian Sea, making it a river with external drainage. Rupen, Banas, and Saraswati are rivers of Rajasthan that end in the desert or merge into lakes, hence they have inland drainage. Inland drainage means the river does not reach the sea but ends in an inland lake or marsh. Periyar originates from the Western Ghats in Kerala and discharges into the Arabian Sea. Therefore, Periyar is not a river with inland drainage.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state does Periyar river flow in? → Kerala
☛ Rupen river is located in which state? → Rajasthan
☛ Which river is an example of inland drainage? → Rupen, Saraswati
☛ Where does Saraswati river end? → In the desert of Rajasthan (inland)
☛ What is inland drainage? → River ending in an inland lake or marsh, not reaching the sea

q: On which river is the Sardar Sarovar Dam constructed?
qs.e: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is constructed on the Narmada River in Gujarat. It is one of the largest dams in the world and is part of the Narmada Valley Project. The dam has a height of 163 meters and its construction began in 1987. It provides water and electricity to Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh. It generates 18,000 MW of power and irrigates 7.5 million hectares of land. The Narmada River originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows into the Gulf of Khambhat.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Sardar Sarovar Dam located? → Gujarat
☛ What is the source of the Narmada River? → Amarkantak, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Which gulf does the Narmada River empty into? → Gulf of Khambhat
☛ What is the height of Sardar Sarovar Dam? → 163 meters
☛ What is the total length of the Narmada River? → 1312 km

q: Chilika Lake is famous for which of the following birds/animals?
qs.e: Chilika Lake is the largest brackish water lake in India, located in Odisha, and one of the largest brackish water lagoons in Asia. It is famous for its rich bird diversity, especially migratory birds. Every year, thousands of flamingos visit during winter, making it a vital part of the Flamingo Sanctuary. Chilika Lake was designated a Ramsar Site in 1981. It is also home to the Irrawaddy dolphin, but flamingos are its main attraction. Rhinoceros, musk deer, and penguins are not found here.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Chilika Lake located? → Odisha
☛ What type of lake is Chilika? → Brackish water lagoon
☛ When was Chilika declared a Ramsar Site? → 1981
☛ Which dolphin is found in Chilika Lake? → Irrawaddy dolphin
☛ Which migratory bird is most famous in Chilika? → Flamingos

q: Which of the following rivers makes an estuary?
qs.e: An estuary is a place where the river meets the sea and the water becomes saline due to tides. The Narmada River flows westward and forms an estuary into the Arabian Sea. It flows through a rift valley, which gives it a straight course and prevents delta formation. Rivers like Ganga, Kaveri, and Krishna flow eastward and carry more sediment, forming deltas. Narmada is the only major river that forms an estuary.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Narmada river → Amarkantak, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Narmada river falls into which sea → Arabian Sea
☛ Total length of Narmada river → about 1312 km
☛ Major dam built on Narmada → Sardar Sarovar Dam
☛ Narmada river flows through which type of valley → Rift valley

q: Through which state do the rivers Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej and Yamuna flow?
qs.e: The rivers Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej and Yamuna flow through the state of Himachal Pradesh. This state is located in the Himalayan region and these rivers either originate there or flow through it. Himachal Pradesh is also known as 'Dev Bhoomi'. Among these, Chenab and Ravi are part of the Indus river system, while Sutlej and Beas are also tributaries of the Indus. Yamuna is a major tributary of the Ganga river system. All these rivers flow through different parts of Himachal Pradesh and are important for agriculture and hydroelectric power generation.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Chenab River → Bara-lacha Pass in Himachal Pradesh
☛ Origin of Ravi River → Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh
☛ Origin of Beas River → Vyas Kund in Himachal Pradesh
☛ Origin of Sutlej River → Rakshastal Lake in Tibet
☛ Origin of Yamuna River → Yamunotri Glacier in Uttarakhand

q: Match the following rivers with their tributaries. Rivers Tributaries
1. Brahmaputra a. Betwa
2. Indus b. Chenab
3. Yamuna c. Dibang
qs.e: The Brahmaputra river has major tributaries including Dibang, Lohit, and Subansiri. Dibang is an important tributary that flows through Arunachal Pradesh. The Indus river has five main tributaries - Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej. Among these, Chenab is the longest tributary. The Yamuna river, a major tributary of the Ganga, has its own tributaries including Betwa, Chambal, and Ken. Betwa joins the Yamuna near Hamirpur. Thus, the correct match is: Brahmaputra-Dibang, Indus-Chenab, Yamuna-Betwa.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the largest tributary of Brahmaputra? → Subansiri
☛ Which is the longest tributary of Indus? → Chenab
☛ Which is a major tributary of Yamuna? → Chambal
☛ Betwa joins which river? → Yamuna
☛ Dibang river flows through which state? → Arunachal Pradesh

q: Which river is the Sardar Sarovar Dam built on?
qs.e: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on the Narmada river. Located in Gujarat's Narmada district, it is one of the largest gravity dams in the world. Its height is about 163 meters and length 1,210 meters. The project benefits Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. This dam is crucial for irrigation, drinking water and electricity generation. The Narmada river originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest gravity dam in India → Sardar Sarovar Dam
☛ Longest river in India → Ganga
☛ Sardar Sarovar Dam is located in which state → Gujarat
☛ Origin of Narmada River → Amarkantak, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Only perennial river in Rajasthan → Chambal

q: Which of the following is NOT a source of release of smokestacks?
qs.e: Sources of smoke release are those that emit smoke or pollutants into the atmosphere. Smelters, thermal power plants, and industries burn fuel or undergo chemical reactions that produce smoke. Rivers are natural water bodies that do not emit smoke. Although rivers can carry pollutants, they do not generate smoke themselves. Major sources of smoke include industrial activities, power generation, and vehicles. Therefore, rivers are not a source of smoke release.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the largest source of smoke release? → Industries
☛ What type of pollution do thermal power plants produce? → Air pollution
☛ What are smelters known for? → Metal extraction
☛ Why do water bodies not release smoke? → No combustion occurs
☛ A major man-made source of air pollution → Industrial chimneys

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following is a major river of the Indus basin system?
qs.e: The Indus river system comprises major rivers like Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej. Among these, Ravi is a major river originating from the Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh. It flows into Pakistan and joins the Chenab River. Godavari is a peninsular Indian river, Yamuna belongs to the Ganga basin, and Kaveri is in South India. Thus, Ravi is part of the Indus basin.
qs.kf:
☛ How many major rivers are in the Indus basin? → Six (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej)
☛ What is the origin of the Ravi river? → Rohtang Pass (Himachal Pradesh)
☛ Which river does Ravi join? → Chenab
☛ Under the Indus Water Treaty, which country holds rights over Ravi? → India
☛ Where does the Indus river empty? → Arabian Sea

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which of the following rivers is NOT a tributary of the Ganga but flows directly into the Bay of Bengal?
qs.e: Mahanadi is not a tributary of the Ganga; it is an independent river that flows directly into the Bay of Bengal. It originates in the Sihawa hills of Chhattisgarh and passes through Odisha. Major tributaries of the Ganga include Yamuna, Ghaghara, Kosi, Gomti, Gandak, and Son. Ghaghara originates in Nepal and joins the Ganga in Uttar Pradesh. Kosi, known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar', is a left-bank tributary. Gomti meets the Ganga in Varanasi. Mahanadi is known for the Hirakud Dam, one of the longest dams in the world. It is also called the 'Ruhr of India' due to its rich mineral deposits in the basin.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Mahanadi → Sihawa hills, Chhattisgarh
☛ Major dam on Mahanadi → Hirakud Dam
☛ Longest tributary of Ganga → Yamuna
☛ Right bank tributaries of Ganga → Yamuna, Son, Gandak
☛ Left bank tributaries of Ganga → Ghaghara, Kosi, Gomti

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which of the following lakes in Rajasthan is artificial?
qs.e: Most lakes in Rajasthan are natural, but Ana Sagar is an artificial lake. It was built in the 12th century by Anaji Chauhan, the ruler of Ajmer, by damming the Luni River. In contrast, Ramgarh lake is also artificial, but among the given options, Ana Sagar is the correct answer. Pushkar and Sambhar are natural lakes. Pushkar Lake is considered sacred, and Sambhar Lake is India's largest saline water lake. Ana Sagar Lake is a famous tourist spot, with marble pavilions and temples along its banks.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest artificial lake in Rajasthan → Jaisamand Lake (Udaipur)
☛ Largest natural lake in Rajasthan → Sambhar Lake
☛ Builder of Ana Sagar Lake → Anaji Chauhan
☛ River on which Ana Sagar Lake is built → Luni River
☛ Religious significance of Pushkar Lake → Associated with Lord Brahma

q: Alexander and Porus fought on the banks of which of the following rivers?
qs.e: The famous battle between Alexander and Porus (King Puru) was fought in 326 BC on the banks of the Jhelum River (ancient name: Hydaspes). This is known as the Battle of Hydaspes. Porus faced Alexander with a huge army and war elephants. Alexander won the battle but was impressed by Porus's courage and returned his kingdom. The Jhelum River flows in the Punjab region and this battle is a significant event in ancient Indian history. Other options: Parusni (ancient name of Ravi River) was not the site, Indus River was crossed by Alexander but no battle occurred there, and Alexander never reached the Ganga River.
qs.kf:
☛ Battle of Hydaspes → Fought on Jhelum River in 326 BC
☛ Which river did Alexander defeat Porus on? → Jhelum
☛ Modern name of Parusni River → Ravi
☛ First European ruler to cross Indus River → Alexander
☛ Porus's ancient kingdom → Punjab region (between Jhelum and Chenab)

q: Which of the following is the largest artificial freshwater lake in India?
qs.e: India's largest artificial freshwater lake is Shivaji Sagar Lake, created by the construction of the Koyna Dam in Maharashtra. This lake was formed in 1964 on the Koyna River and covers an area of about 891 square kilometers. It plays a crucial role in hydroelectric power generation. The Koyna Dam is a gravity dam located in the Western Ghats. The lake is named after Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Other options: Nainital Lake is natural, Kolleru Lake is natural and brackish, and Kodai Lake is artificial but smaller.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest artificial freshwater lake in India → Shivaji Sagar Lake
☛ Dam responsible for Shivaji Sagar Lake → Koyna Dam
☛ State where Koyna Dam is located → Maharashtra
☛ Shivaji Sagar Lake named after → Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj
☛ Largest natural lake in India → Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir)

q: Which of the following cities in Madhya Pradesh was renamed as Narmadapuram?
qs.e: In February 2021, the Madhya Pradesh government decided to rename Hoshangabad district as Narmadapuram, owing to its location on the banks of the holy Narmada River. The city was historically named after Hoshang Shah, a Sultan of Malwa. The renaming aimed to strengthen the cultural and religious identity of the region. Narmadapuram district is part of the Narmadapuram division. The town is situated on the southern bank of the Narmada River. This decision received support from locals and religious organizations.
qs.kf:
☛ New name of Hoshangabad → Narmadapuram
☛ Narmadapuram is located on which river → Narmada River
☛ Hoshangabad district is in which division → Narmadapuram division
☛ Old name associated with which Sultan → Hoshang Shah
☛ Purpose of renaming → Strengthen cultural identity

q: What is a river known as when it enters the plains where it twists and turns forming large bends?
qs.e: When a river leaves the mountainous region and enters the plains, its gradient decreases and flow velocity slows down. Due to obstacles in its path, the river flows in a winding course, forming large bends. These bends are called meanders. Meanders result from the balance between erosion and deposition by the river. The river current erodes the outer (concave) bank and deposits sediment on the inner (convex) bank. Over time, these bends become more pronounced, and sometimes the river cuts through the neck of a meander, forming an ox-bow lake. Meanders are the most common feature of a river in its plain course. Hence, the correct answer is Meanders.
qs.kf:
☛ Where are meanders formed? → In the plain course of a river
☛ Which lake is formed by meanders? → Ox-bow lake
☛ Which bank is eroded in a meander? → Concave bank
☛ Which bank is deposited in a meander? → Convex bank
☛ What is another name for meanders? → River bends

q: Which of these countries is in the Murray-Darling River Basin?
qs.e: The Murray-Darling River Basin is located in Australia and is the country's largest river system. It comprises the Murray, Darling, and Murrumbidgee rivers. The basin covers an area of about 1 million square kilometers in southeastern Australia. It plays a vital role in Australia's agricultural output. New Zealand, Kenya, and Madagascar are not part of this basin.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the longest river in the Murray-Darling Basin? → Darling River
☛ Where does the Murray River originate? → Australian Alps
☛ What climate zone is the Murray-Darling Basin? → Semi-arid
☛ Which lake is located in this basin? → Lake Alexandrina
☛ Into which sea does the Murray River flow? → Indian Ocean

q: Which of the following rivers is ephemeral?
qs.e: Luni is the only major ephemeral river in Rajasthan. Ephemeral rivers flow only during the rainy season and remain dry for the rest of the year. It originates from the Aravalli Range near Ajmer and ends in the Rann of Kutch. Its water becomes saline downstream. In contrast, Beas, Chambal and Yamuna are perennial rivers that receive water from both Himalayan glaciers and monsoon rainfall. Ephemeral rivers are important for groundwater recharge and local ecosystems.
qs.kf:
☛ Ephemeral river of Rajasthan? → Luni
☛ Origin of Luni river? → Aravalli Range near Ajmer
☛ End of Luni river? → Rann of Kutch
☛ Source of perennial rivers? → Himalayas and rainfall
☛ Characteristic of ephemeral river? → Flows only in rainy season

q: In which river is India's largest river island, Majuli, located?
qs.e: Majuli is the world's largest river island, located in the state of Assam, India. It is situated in the Brahmaputra River and is formed by the flow of the river and its tributaries. The Brahmaputra originates from the Singi Khamban in Tibet and flows through Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and then into Bangladesh.
