qs.e: Indian Railways has introduced biodiesel locomotives in its South Western Railway zone. This initiative aims to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and promote environmental sustainability. Biodiesel is a renewable fuel derived from vegetable oils or animal fats, which produces less pollution than conventional diesel. The move helps reduce carbon emissions and supports sustainable transportation. The project was launched as a pilot to test the feasibility of using biodiesel in trains.
qs.kf:
☛ Zone that pioneered experimental biodiesel locomotives → South Western Railway
☛ Primary raw material used to produce biodiesel → Jatropha and soybean
☛ First Indian railway engine to use biodiesel → Launched as a pilot in 2015
☛ Collaborating organization for biodiesel production with Indian Railways → IIT Delhi
☛ Key benefit of biodiesel locomotives → Up to 20% reduction in carbon emissions

q: There are ____ zones in Indian Railways.
qs.e: Indian Railways has a total of 18 zones. This structure represents the administrative division of Indian Railways. Each zone is headed by a General Manager. Currently, there are 17 zones (such as Northern Railway, Eastern Railway, etc.) and 1 Metro Railway (Kolkata Metro). The zones were reorganized in 2003. This information is important for railway recruitment exams.
qs.kf:
☛ Total number of zones in Indian Railways → 18
☛ Largest zone → Northern Railway (longest route length)
☛ Newest zone → Kolkata Metro (established in 1974)
☛ Year of zone reorganization → 2003
☛ Head of each zone → General Manager

q: According to National Waterways 1 (NW1) in India, what is the length (stretch) of Allahabad (Prayagraj)-Haldia in km?
qs.e: National Waterway 1 (NW-1) is the longest national waterway in India, stretching from Prayagraj (Allahabad) in Uttar Pradesh to Haldia in West Bengal. Its total length is 1,620 km. This waterway is developed on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system. NW-1 is operated by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI). It is crucial for freight and passenger transport, reducing pressure on road and rail traffic. The length of 1,620 km makes it the country's premier waterway.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of National Waterway 1 → 1,620 km
☛ Rivers forming National Waterway 1 → Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly
☛ Major cities on National Waterway 1 → Prayagraj, Varanasi, Patna, Kolkata, Haldia
☛ Authority managing National Waterway 1 → Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)
☛ Longest national waterway in India → NW-1 (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly)

q: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport is situated in:
qs.e: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport is located in Kolkata, West Bengal. It was formerly known as Dum Dum Airport and was renamed in 1995 after the Indian nationalist Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. It is the largest airport in Eastern India and the fifth busiest airport in India. The airport has two runways and handles both international and domestic flights. It serves as a major aviation hub for the region.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport located? → Kolkata
☛ What was its former name? → Dum Dum Airport
☛ When was it renamed? → 1995
☛ Which is the largest airport in Eastern India? → Kolkata Airport
☛ What is the IATA code of Kolkata Airport? → CCU

q: Which one of the following ports is NOT located on the Eastern Coast of India?
qs.e: The major ports on the Eastern Coast of India include Paradeep (Odisha), Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu), and Haldia (West Bengal). These ports are located along the Bay of Bengal. Kandla Port, on the other hand, is situated in Gujarat on the Western Coast along the Arabian Sea. It is a major port primarily serving the Kutch region. Hence, Kandla is NOT on the Eastern Coast of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Easternmost major port of India → Paradeep
☛ Major ports on Eastern Coast → Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Paradeep, Haldia, Tuticorin
☛ Kandla port is located in → Gujarat (Western Coast)
☛ Haldia port is on which river → Hooghly River
☛ Alternative name of Tuticorin port → V.O. Chidambaranar Port

q: Government of India has set ambitious target of building ________ kms of highways in FY21.
qs.e: The Government of India set an ambitious target of constructing 15,000 kilometers of highways in the financial year 2020-21. This target was set by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. To achieve this, projects like the National Highway Development Project (NHDP) and the Bharatmala Project were accelerated. This includes construction of expressways, widening of national highways, and building new highways. The government emphasized infrastructure development to improve connectivity and boost economic growth. The target was significant for enhancing the country's road network and reducing travel time.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the total target of highway construction under Bharatmala Project? → 34,800 km
☛ How many phases are there in NHDP? → 7 phases
☛ Which ministry set the highway construction target for FY2021? → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
☛ Which is the longest national highway in India? → NH 44 (3,745 km)
☛ What was the highway construction target for FY22 by Government of India? → 12,000 km

q: The Big Inch pipeline transports which among the following?
qs.e: The Big Inch pipeline is one of the longest oil pipelines in the world, located in the United States. It was built during World War II to transport crude oil and petroleum products from Texas to the East Coast. This pipeline transports millions of barrels of petroleum daily and is a vital part of the U.S. energy infrastructure. Its name comes from its 24-inch diameter, known as 'Big Inch'.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Big Inch pipeline located? → United States
☛ What is the diameter of the Big Inch pipeline? → 24 inches
☛ During which war was the Big Inch pipeline built? → World War II
☛ What does the Big Inch pipeline transport? → Petroleum
☛ Which two regions does the Big Inch pipeline connect? → Texas and the East Coast

q: The international airport of which Indian city is named after Dr. B. R. Ambedkar?
qs.e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Airport, formerly known as Sonegaon Airport, is located in Nagpur, Maharashtra. It is named after Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution. The airport is situated about 8 km southwest of the city center. It is the third busiest airport in Maharashtra after Mumbai and Pune, handling both domestic and international flights. The airport serves as a major hub for central India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the name of the international airport in Nagpur? → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Airport
☛ In which state is this airport located? → Maharashtra
☛ What was the old name of Nagpur airport? → Sonegaon Airport
☛ Which is the busiest airport in Maharashtra? → Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (Mumbai)
☛ Who is Dr. B. R. Ambedkar known as? → Father of the Indian Constitution

q: Which of the following ports lies on the east coast of India?
qs.e: Tuticorin port is located on the east coast of India in the state of Tamil Nadu. It lies on the Gulf of Mannar and is a major port in South India. Kandla and Nhava Sheva (Jawaharlal Nehru Port) are on the west coast in Gujarat and Maharashtra respectively. Kochi port is on the west coast in Kerala. Tuticorin port, also known as V.O. Chidambaranar Port (VOC Port), is an artificial harbor and plays a vital role in maritime trade, especially for coal, fertilizers, and petroleum products.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest port in India → Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva)
☛ Natural port on west coast → Mumbai Port
☛ Largest port on east coast → Chennai Port
☛ Kandla port is located in → Gujarat
☛ Kochi port is in which state → Kerala

q: Which of the following highways covers most of Rajasthan?
qs.e: National Highway 15 (NH 15) covers most of Rajasthan. This highway starts from Pathankot in Punjab and ends at Samakhiali in Gujarat, passing through major cities of Rajasthan like Ganganagar, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, and Barmer. Its total length is approximately 1,596 km, most of which lies in Rajasthan. It connects the western and northern regions of the state, making it the longest national highway in Rajasthan. NH 15 plays a crucial role in connecting Rajasthan with Punjab and Gujarat. It is also part of the National Highway Development Project (NHDP). NH 8 is the Delhi-Mumbai corridor, NH 7 connects Varanasi to Kanyakumari, and NH 47 is the Ahmedabad-Kandla route.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest national highway in Rajasthan → NH 15
☛ Total length of NH 15 → Approximately 1,596 km
☛ North-South extent of NH 15 → Pathankot (Punjab) to Samakhiali (Gujarat)
☛ Cities in Rajasthan connected by NH 15 → Ganganagar, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Barmer
☛ NH 8 connects which cities → Delhi and Mumbai

q: North-south corridor connects Srinagar (Kashmir) to which of the following?
qs.e: The North-South Corridor (NS-EW Corridor) is a four-lane national highway project in India, developed under the Bharatmala project. This corridor connects Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu). The objective of this project is to connect major cities of India with an efficient road network, boosting economic development. The North-South Corridor is approximately 4,000 kilometers long and includes several important highways passing through multiple states. This project, along with the East-West Corridor (Silchar to Porbandar), forms a vital part of India's road network.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of North-South Corridor → Approximately 4,000 km
☛ Northern terminal of North-South Corridor → Srinagar
☛ Southern terminal of North-South Corridor → Kanyakumari
☛ Eastern terminal of East-West Corridor → Silchar
☛ Western terminal of East-West Corridor → Porbandar

q: Which port is situated on the banks of the Hooghly river?
qs.e: Haldia port is situated on the banks of the Hooghly River in West Bengal. It is a satellite port of the Kolkata port, developed in the 1970s to reduce congestion at Kolkata. Haldia is a riverine port and provides deep water access for ships. It primarily handles coal, iron ore, food grains, and containers. Mormugao is in Goa, Paradip in Odisha, and Mumbai in Maharashtra.
qs.kf:
☛ Port situated on Hooghly River → Haldia
☛ Satellite port of Kolkata → Haldia
☛ River on which Haldia port is located → Hooghly
☛ State where Haldia port is located → West Bengal
☛ Major commodities handled at Haldia → petroleum products, coal, iron ore

q: Oldest operating port in India is in _____.
qs.e: The oldest operating port in India is the Kolkata Port (now Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Port), established in 1870. It was one of the major ports built during the British era and has been a crucial trading hub for eastern India. Located on the banks of the Hooghly River, Kolkata Port is a riverine port that handles a variety of cargo including raw materials and manufactured goods. Due to tidal variations in the river, the port uses a unique lock-gate system to facilitate ship movement. Also known as the Gateway of Eastern India, it remains vital for trade in states like West Bengal, Bihar, and the northeastern region.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest operating port in India → Kolkata (1870)
☛ Largest port in India → Mumbai
☛ Deepest port in India → Visakhapatnam
☛ First private port in India → Ennore (Kamarajar)
☛ Number of major ports under Government of India → 12

q: The Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust is located in ______.
qs.e: The Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT), also known as Nhava Sheva Port, is located in Mumbai, Maharashtra. It is India's largest container port and is situated on the western coast of the country. The port is located at Nhava Sheva, about 10 nautical miles from the Mumbai Port. It was commissioned on 26 May 1989 and is one of India's major ports. JNPT handles approximately 40% of India's total container traffic. The port is well connected to Mumbai by road and rail, making it a crucial hub for international trade.
qs.kf:
☛ India's largest container port → Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT)
☛ JNPT is located in → Mumbai, Maharashtra
☛ Former name of JNPT → Nhava Sheva Port
☛ Year of commissioning of JNPT → 1989
☛ Share of JNPT in India's container traffic → Approximately 40%

q: East West corridor connects Porbandar with ______.
qs.e: The East-West Corridor is one of the most important road corridors in India. It connects Porbandar in Gujarat, western India, with Silchar in Assam, eastern India. The total length of this corridor is approximately 3300 km and it is part of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP). The NHDP was launched by the Government of India to improve road infrastructure across the country. The East-West Corridor plays a crucial role in economic integration and regional development, boosting trade and transportation facilities.
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of East-West Corridor → Approximately 3300 km
☛ Eastern terminus of East-West Corridor → Silchar
☛ Western terminus of East-West Corridor → Porbandar
☛ Number of major corridors under Golden Quadrilateral → Four (North-South, East-West, Golden Quadrilateral, and Northeast Corridor)
☛ East-West Corridor is part of which project? → NHDP

q: Gorakhpur is the headquarters of which of the following Indian Railway Division?
qs.e: Gorakhpur is the headquarters of the Northeast Railway (Purvottar Railway Zone), one of the 18 regional railway zones of Indian Railways. The Northeast Railway was formed in 1952 and its headquarters is located in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh. This railway zone primarily serves the border areas of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Nepal. Under Northeast Railway, several important railway lines operate, such as Gorakhpur-Lucknow, Gorakhpur-Varanasi, and Gorakhpur-Siliguri routes. Its total route length is approximately 3,667 km and it manages 56 stations. Among other options, Northern Railway has its headquarters in New Delhi, Western Railway in Mumbai, and Eastern Railway in Kolkata.
qs.kf:
☛ Which railway zone has its headquarters in Gorakhpur? → Northeast Railway
☛ Where is the headquarters of Northeast Railway? → Gorakhpur
☛ How many regional railway zones are there in Indian Railways? → 18
☛ When was Northeast Railway formed? → 1952
☛ What is the total route length of Northeast Railway? → Approximately 3,667 km

q: Haldia port was developed as an auxiliary port of ___________.
qs.e: Haldia port was developed as an auxiliary port of Kolkata Port, located on the Hooghly River in West Bengal. It is under the Kolkata Port Trust and was built to assist large vessels due to silt accumulation in the Hooghly River. The port was primarily developed to reduce pressure on Kolkata Port and serve industrial areas. Construction of Haldia port began in the 1960s and operations started in the 1970s. The port is crucial for transporting petroleum, chemicals, fertilizers, and other bulk commodities. It plays a major role in the industrial development of eastern India.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Haldia port located? → Hooghly River
☛ Haldia port is an auxiliary port of which port? → Kolkata Port
☛ In which state is Haldia port situated? → West Bengal
☛ Main reason for development of Haldia port? → To reduce pressure on Kolkata Port
☛ Which is the oldest port of India? → Kolkata Port

q: Indian Railways is the headquarters of the southern region-
qs.e: Indian Railways is divided into 18 zones. The headquarters of the Southern Railway Zone is located in Chennai. It was established on 14 April 1951. This zone covers parts of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Puducherry, and Andhra Pradesh. Southern Railway has three divisions: Chennai, Madurai, and Thiruvananthapuram. Chennai Central Railway Station is the major station of this zone.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of Southern Railway → Chennai
☛ Establishment of Southern Railway → 1951
☛ Divisions of Southern Railway → Chennai, Madurai, Thiruvananthapuram
☛ Headquarters of South Western Railway → Hubli
☛ Headquarters of South Central Railway → Secunderabad

q: The famous hill-station Kodaikanal lies in -
qs.e: Kodaikanal is a famous hill station in Tamil Nadu, located in the Palani hills range. It is situated at an altitude of about 2,133 meters above sea level. The Palani hills are part of the Western Ghats and are known for their natural beauty and lakes. Kodaikanal is often called the 'Princess of Hill Stations'. It is famous for Kodaikanal Lake, Bryant Park, and Bear Shola Falls. The Nilgiri hills, Cardamom hills, and Javadi hills are other mountain ranges, but Kodaikanal lies in the Palani hills.
qs.kf:
☛ Which hill range is Kodaikanal located in? → Palani hills
☛ In which state are the Palani hills located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ What is the altitude of Kodaikanal? → Approximately 2,133 meters
☛ What is Kodaikanal also known as? → Princess of Hill Stations
☛ Which lake is famous in Kodaikanal? → Kodaikanal Lake

q: On 3 February 1925, the first electric train in India ran between which two stations?
qs.e: The first electric train in India ran on 3 February 1925 between Bombay VT (Victoria Terminus) and Kurla Harbour. It operated on 1500 volts direct current (DC) and was inaugurated by the then Governor Sir Leslie Wilson. This service marked the beginning of Mumbai suburban railway. The first electric train had only one coach and covered a distance of 16 km in 9 minutes, carrying passengers. This event laid the foundation for railway electrification in India.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the first electric train run in India? → 3 February 1925
☛ First electric train ran between which stations? → Bombay VT and Kurla Harbour
☛ What was the voltage of the initial electric train? → 1500 V DC
☛ How many coaches did the first electric train have? → One coach
☛ Who inaugurated the first electric train? → Sir Leslie Wilson

q: To promote Inland Water Transport (IWT) in the country, ____________ waterways have been declared as National Waterways (NWs) under the National Waterways Act, 2016.
qs.e: Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, a total of 111 waterways have been declared as National Waterways (NWs) to promote Inland Water Transport (IWT) in the country. Previously, only 5 national waterways existed. Most of these waterways are located on rivers, canals, lakes, and other water bodies. IWT is a cost-effective and eco-friendly mode of transport that reduces pressure on road and rail traffic. The government aims to increase the share of IWT in the overall transport sector.
qs.kf:
☛ How many waterways declared under National Waterways Act, 2016? → 111
☛ How many national waterways were there before 2016? → 5
☛ Which is the longest national waterway? → NW-1 (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly)
☛ What is the full form of IWT? → Inland Water Transport
☛ What is the main advantage of IWT? → Cost-effective and eco-friendly

q: Which of the following locations holds the significance of being the headquarters of the South Central Zone of the Indian Railways?
qs.e: The headquarters of the South Central Zone of Indian Railways is located at Secunderabad (Telangana). Established in 1966, this zone is divided into 6 divisions: Secunderabad, Hyderabad, Guntur, Guntakal, Nanded, and Vijayawada. South Central Railway connects southern and central parts of India, covering areas in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, and Karnataka. Hubli is the headquarters of South Western Railway, Chennai of Southern Railway, and Bilaspur of South East Central Railway. Hence, Secunderabad is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ South Central Railway headquarters → Secunderabad
☛ South Western Railway headquarters → Hubli
☛ Southern Railway headquarters → Chennai
☛ South East Central Railway headquarters → Bilaspur
☛ Total divisions in South Central Railway → 6

q: What is the approximate total length of the Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) highway network?
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) is a major highway network in India connecting the four metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata. The total length of this project is approximately 5,846 kilometers. It was the first phase of the National Highway Development Project (NHDP), launched in 2001. The GQ was constructed by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. The network consists of four to six-lane roads, reducing travel time and boosting economic development.
qs.kf:
☛ Four metros connected by GQ → Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata
☛ GQ is part of which project → National Highway Development Project (NHDP)
☛ Launch year of GQ → 2001
☛ Total length of GQ → 5,846 km
☛ Number of lanes in GQ → 4-6 lanes

q: Which place is the junction of the East-West and North-South corridors in India?
qs.e: In India, the junction of the East-West Corridor (Silchar to Porbandar) and the North-South Corridor (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) is located at Jhansi. This is part of the National Highway Development Project (NHDP) alongside the Golden Quadrilateral. Jhansi, situated in Uttar Pradesh, serves as a crucial meeting point where these two major corridors intersect. The project connects the four corners of India, enhancing transportation and trade. Jhansi's strategic location in central India makes it an important hub for both road and rail networks.
qs.kf:
☛ Which places does the East-West Corridor connect? → Silchar to Porbandar
☛ Which places does the North-South Corridor connect? → Srinagar to Kanyakumari
☛ How many corridors are there under the Golden Quadrilateral project? → 4 (East-West, North-South, and two others)
☛ What is the full form of NHDP? → National Highway Development Project
☛ In which state is Jhansi located? → Uttar Pradesh

q: As of October 2024, which of the following is the longest National Highway in India?
qs.e: The longest National Highway in India is NH-44, which runs from Srinagar (Jammu and Kashmir) in the north to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu) in the south. Its total length is approximately 3,745 kilometers. This highway was formed by merging several older highways like NH- 1A, NH-1, and NH-7 under the new numbering system introduced in 2010. NH-44 passes through 11 states: Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu. It is a vital part of India's North-South Corridor.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest National Highway → NH-44 (Srinagar to Kanyakumari)
☛ Total length of NH-44 → Approximately 3,745 km
☛ Number of states NH-44 passes through → 11 states
☛ Shortest National Highway → NH-987A (about 5 km)
☛ Old name of NH-44 → NH-7 and NH-1A

q: The Brahmaputra river is navigable by steamers up to Dibrugarh by which of the following national waterways of India?
qs.e: National Waterway 2 (NW 2) is located on the Brahmaputra river, stretching 891 km from Sadiya to Dhubri. This waterway facilitates the operation of steamers up to Dibrugarh due to the adequate depth and width of the Brahmaputra. NW 1 is on the Ganga river from Haldia to Allahabad, NW 3 is on the west coast from Kollam to Kottapuram, and NW 4 is on the Krishna and Godavari rivers. Therefore, the navigability of the Brahmaputra up to Dibrugarh is provided by NW 2.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is National Waterway 2 located? → Brahmaputra river
☛ What is the total length of NW 2? → 891 km
☛ Between which points does NW 2 lie? → Sadiya to Dhubri
☛ Which national waterway allows steamers up to Dibrugarh? → NW 2
☛ Which is the longest national waterway in India? → NW 1 (Ganga river)

q: The Gajraj System of Indian Railways, launched in December 2023, aims to use an _____.
o: AI-based system to diagnose elephant illness
AI-based system to treat respiratory diseases in elephants
AI-based surveillance system to prevent elephant deaths in railway tracks
qs.e: In December 2023, Indian Railways launched the Gajraj System, an AI-based surveillance system designed to prevent elephant deaths on railway tracks. The system uses thermal imaging and infrared sensors to detect elephants near the tracks. Once detected, it immediately alerts the loco pilot to slow down or stop the train. This system is particularly useful in Assam and Northeast India, where railway lines cut through elephant habitats. It helps reduce human-elephant conflict and contributes to elephant conservation. The Gajraj System is a significant step towards ensuring safety for both wildlife and railway passengers.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the purpose of Gajraj System? → AI-based surveillance to prevent elephant deaths on railway tracks
☛ When was Gajraj System launched? → December 2023
☛ Which technology does Gajraj System use? → Thermal imaging and infrared sensors
☛ Who benefits from Gajraj System? → Elephants and railway passengers
☛ Under which initiative is Gajraj System part of? → Elephant conservation and safety

q: Which of the following ports is NOT located in the western coastal plains of India?
qs.e: The major ports located in the western coastal plains of India include Kandla (Gujarat), Mangalore (Karnataka), and Cochin (Kerala). All these ports are situated on the western coast. Ennore port (Chennai) is located on the eastern coast, hence it is not part of the western coastal plains. Ennore port is in Tamil Nadu and is part of the Coromandel Coast.
qs.kf:
☛ Northernmost port on western coast → Kandla
☛ Major port of Kerala → Cochin
☛ Major port of Karnataka → Mangalore
☛ Port on eastern coast → Ennore
☛ Major port of Gujarat → Kandla

q: Which airport is known as Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport?
qs.e: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU) in Kolkata is the primary airport serving West Bengal. It was renamed after the Indian freedom fighter Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose in 1995. Previously known as Dum Dum Airport, it is the fifth busiest airport in India and the largest in eastern India. The airport is located about 17 km from the city center. Bose was born in Cuttack, Odisha, and was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement. He formed the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) to fight against British rule.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport located? → Kolkata
☛ What was its former name? → Dum Dum Airport
☛ Where was Netaji born? → Cuttack, Odisha
☛ When did Netaji die? → August 18, 1945 (plane crash in Taipei)
☛ What is Netaji's famous slogan? → Give me blood, I will give you freedom.

q: What is the approximate total length of the Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) highway network?
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) is a major national highway network in India that connects four metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata. Its total length is approximately 5,846 km, making it a vital part of India's road transport infrastructure. The project was implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and was launched in 2001. The GQ network plays a crucial role in the economic development of the country by facilitating faster movement of goods and passengers.
qs.kf:
☛ Which four metros are connected by GQ? → Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata
☛ Which agency oversees the GQ project? → NHAI
☛ When was the GQ project launched? → 2001
☛ Which is the longest national highway in India? → NH 44 (approx. 3,745 km)
☛ Under which scheme was GQ built? → National Highways Development Project (NHDP) Phase I

q: Which of the following is India's longest national waterway?
qs.e: India's longest national waterway is National Waterway 1 (NW 1), which runs along the Ganga River from Prayagraj to Haldia. Its total length is approximately 1620 kilometers. This waterway passes through the states of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal. NW 1 was declared a national waterway in 1986. In comparison, National Waterway 2 (NW 2) on the Brahmaputra River is 891 km long, National Waterway 3 (NW 3) on the West Coast Canal is 205 km, and National Waterway 4 (NW 4) on the Godavari-Krishna rivers is 1095 km long. Therefore, NW 1 is the longest.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest national waterway → NW 1 (Ganga River, 1620 km)
☛ NW 1 is located on which river → Ganga River
☛ Length of NW 2 → 891 km
☛ NW 3 is located in which state → Kerala
☛ Which rivers are part of NW 4 → Godavari and Krishna

q: Which of the following waterways of India is navigable by mechanical boats up to Patna and by ordinary boats up to Haridwar?
qs.e: National Waterway 1 (NW 1) extends on the Ganga river from Allahabad to Haldia, covering a length of 1620 km. It is the longest national waterway in India. This waterway is navigable by mechanical boats up to Patna and by ordinary boats up to Haridwar. NW 1 was established in 1986 under the National Waterways Act. It passes through the states of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal. The Inland Waterways Authority of India is responsible for its maintenance and operation. NW 1 is crucial for trade and tourism, especially for cargo movement between Kolkata and Patna. The waterway also supports passenger transport and helps in decongesting road and rail networks.
qs.kf:
☛ Which states does NW 1 pass through? → Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal
☛ What is the total length of NW 1? → 1620 km
☛ On which river is NW 1 located? → Ganga river
☛ What is the starting point of NW 1? → Allahabad
☛ What is the ending point of NW 1? → Haldia

q: When was the first passenger train service in India started?
qs.e: The first passenger train service in India started on 16 April 1853. The train ran from Bori Bunder station in Mumbai (then Bombay) to Thane. It covered a distance of about 34 kilometres. The train was hauled by three engines named Sahib, Sindh, and Sultan. The service was inaugurated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR). This event marked a significant milestone in Indian railway history, initiating rail transport in the country.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the first passenger train run in India? → 16 April 1853
☛ Between which stations did the first train run? → Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane
☛ What was the distance of the first train? → 34 kilometres
☛ What were the names of the engines of the first train? → Sahib, Sindh, and Sultan
☛ Which company operated the first train? → Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR)

q: Which of the following is the largest container port in India?
qs.e: India's largest container port is Nhava Sheva Port (Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust), located in Raigad district, Maharashtra. It handles approximately 65% of India's container cargo and is the country's primary container hub. Mumbai Port mainly deals with bulk cargo, while Visakhapatnam and Kandla handle diverse cargo, but in terms of container handling, Nhava Sheva leads.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest container port in India → Nhava Sheva (JNPT)
☛ In which state is Nhava Sheva Port located? → Maharashtra
☛ Alternative name of Nhava Sheva → Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT)
☛ Second largest container port in India → Chennai Port
☛ Oldest port in India → Chennai Port

q: Which of the following is the cheapest and most suitable mode of transport for carrying heavy and bulky material?
qs.e: Waterways are the cheapest and most suitable mode of transport for carrying heavy and bulky materials. This is because water transport consumes less fuel and can carry large quantities of goods at once. Heavy machinery, coal, iron ore, etc., can be transported economically through rivers, canals, and seas. Waterways are also less harmful to the environment compared to other modes. India has an extensive inland waterway system spanning about 14,500 km. This mode is ideal for long distances and heavy loads, whereas air transport is expensive, and rail/road are comparatively costlier for bulk goods.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the longest National Waterway in India? → Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly (NW-1)
☛ What is another name for waterways? → Water transport
☛ What are the main types of waterways? → Inland and oceanic
☛ When was India's first National Waterway notified? → In 1986
☛ What is a major limitation of waterways? → Slow speed and dependence on weather

q: National Highway (NH)-2, a section of the Grand Trunk Road, is a major highway in India that runs from Delhi to _______.
qs.e: National Highway-2 (NH-2), a section of the Grand Trunk Road, is a major highway in India that runs from Delhi to Kolkata. It is one of the oldest and most important highways in India, connecting North India to Eastern India. NH-2 has a total length of approximately 1,465 km and passes through the states of Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal. It has historical significance as the Grand Trunk Road was built by Sher Shah Suri. Currently, NH-2 has been renumbered as NH-19, but the old name NH-2 is still widely used. This highway serves as a vital link for trade and transportation between Delhi and Kolkata.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Grand Trunk Road? → Sher Shah Suri
☛ What is the new number of NH-2? → NH-19
☛ How long is NH-2 from Delhi to Kolkata? → Approximately 1,465 km
☛ How many states does NH-2 pass through? → 6 states
☛ What was the old name of the Grand Trunk Road? → Sadak-e-Azam

q: Which of the following is/are an example of economic infrastructure?
qs.e: Economic infrastructure refers to physical structures and facilities that directly support economic activities. It includes transportation (roads, bridges, railways), communication, energy (power plants, grids), and water supply systems. These facilitate the movement of goods, services, and labor, thereby boosting production, trade, and economic growth. In contrast, parks, museums, and schools fall under social infrastructure, which focuses on quality of life and human capital development.
qs.kf:
☛ Example of economic infrastructure → Roads, bridges, ports, railways, power lines
☛ Example of social infrastructure → Schools, hospitals, parks, museums
☛ What is economic infrastructure? → Facilities that directly support production and trade
☛ Main types of infrastructure → Economic and social
☛ Economic importance of roads → Reduce transport costs, improve market access and supply chains

q: Which public sector organisation is the largest provider of surface transport services in India?
qs.e: Indian Railways is the largest public sector organisation providing surface transport services in India. It is the primary mode of passenger and freight transport across the country, with a total route length of over 67,000 km. Indian Railways serves more than 23 million passengers daily and is one of the largest rail networks in the world. It is divided into 18 zones and its headquarters is located in New Delhi. In the financial year 2023-24, its revenue was approximately ₹2.4 lakh crore.
qs.kf:
☛ Indian Railways establishment year → 1853 (first train)
☛ Indian Railways headquarters → New Delhi
☛ Indian Railways Minister (2024) → Ashwini Vaishnaw
☛ Indian Railways total route length → over 67,000 km
☛ Indian Railways electrification target → 100% (by 2024)

q: The vast network of railways that helped people meet their family and relatives was pioneered during the latter half of which of the following centuries in India?
qs.e: The development of railways in India took place in the latter half of the 19th century. The first passenger train ran in 1853 from Bombay to Thane, laying the foundation of the railway network. In the 1850s, Governor-General Lord Dalhousie formulated a policy for railway expansion, which accelerated transportation and enabled people to meet their families and relatives. By the end of the 19th century, the railway network had spread across the country under British rule, transforming Indian society and economy.
qs.kf:
☛ First passenger train in India → 1853, Bombay-Thane
☛ Father of Indian Railways → Lord Dalhousie
☛ Railway expansion by end of 19th century → Under British rule
☛ Benefit of railways → Easier family reunions
☛ Major contribution of railways → Social and economic change

q: The Hazira–Vijaipur–Jagdishpur (HVJ) pipeline is mainly used to transport:
qs.e: The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) pipeline is the longest and first natural gas pipeline in India. It was commissioned in 1987 by GAIL (Gas Authority of India Limited). This pipeline runs from Hazira in Gujarat to Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh via Vijaipur in Madhya Pradesh. Its purpose is to transport natural gas to fertilizer plants, power stations, and other industrial consumers. It is a crucial part of India's energy infrastructure, promoting a gas-based economy.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the total length of the HVJ pipeline? → Approximately 1,700 kilometers
☛ Who operates the HVJ pipeline? → GAIL (Gas Authority of India Limited)
☛ Through which states does the HVJ pipeline pass? → Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh
☛ Under which project was the HVJ pipeline expanded? → HVJ Upgrade Project
☛ Which is the first natural gas pipeline in India? → Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) pipeline

q: India's highway network is one of the largest in the world. Which scheme focuses on the development of highways, particularly in economic corridors?
qs.e: Bharatmala Pariyojana is a flagship scheme of the Government of India focusing on the development of highways, especially economic corridors, border roads, and port connectivity. Under this project, about 34,800 km of national highways are to be constructed or upgraded. It was launched in 2017 and is implemented by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. The scheme aims to boost economic growth, reduce traffic congestion, and connect remote areas. It strengthens the national highway network and promotes trade and tourism. This is the correct answer because the other options are for different purposes: PM Gram Sadak Yojana focuses on rural roads, BharatNet on broadband connectivity, and Sagarmala on port development.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Bharatmala Pariyojana launched? → 2017
☛ How many km of roads are targeted under Bharatmala? → About 34,800 km
☛ Which ministry implements Bharatmala Pariyojana? → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
☛ What is the main focus of Bharatmala? → Economic corridors and port connectivity
☛ What is the objective of Bharatmala? → Strengthen national highway network

q: What is the main advantage of road transport over railways?
o: Cheaper and faster than railway transport over long distances
qs.e: Road transport provides door-to-door service, which makes it more convenient for short and medium distances compared to railways. Railways are limited to stations, whereas road transport can reach rural and remote areas. For long distances, railways are more economical and faster. Road transport is less environment-friendly as it generates more pollution. Thus, door-to-door service is the main advantage of road transport.
qs.kf:
☛ Main advantage of road transport → Door-to-door service
☛ Most suitable transport for long distances → Railways
☛ Cheapest long-distance transport → Railways
☛ Environment-friendly transport → Railways
☛ Transport reaching remote areas → Road transport

q: What is the name of the Super Expressway that links the metropolitan cities of New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata?
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral is an ambitious super expressway project in India that connects the four major metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata. It was implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and launched in 2001. The total length of the project is approximately 5,846 km. The Golden Quadrilateral is a vital part of India's road network and has transformed connectivity in the country by reducing travel time and boosting economic development. It is distinct from the North-South and East-West corridors, which connect other cities. This expressway has significantly improved transportation efficiency and spurred industrial growth along its route.
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of Golden Quadrilateral → Approximately 5,846 km
☛ Implementing agency of Golden Quadrilateral → NHAI
☛ Cities connected by Golden Quadrilateral → Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata
☛ Launch year of Golden Quadrilateral → 2001
☛ Purpose of Golden Quadrilateral → Connect four major metros and boost economic growth

q: Which of the following is NOT a part of urban transport infrastructure?
qs.e: Urban transport infrastructure includes facilities that facilitate movement of people and goods within cities. Metro systems, highways, and rail networks provide means of transportation in urban areas. In contrast, irrigation canals are related to water supply for agricultural purposes and are not part of urban transport. Therefore, irrigation canals are not a component of urban transport infrastructure.
qs.kf:
☛ Examples of urban transport infrastructure → Roads, metro, Bus Rapid Transit (BRT)
☛ Use of irrigation canals → To deliver water to agricultural fields
☛ Metro system → A rapid transit rail system in urban areas
☛ Highways → Major roads for long-distance motor vehicle transport
☛ Rail network → Railway lines connecting cities

q: Which of the following is a national waterway between Haldia (Sagar) and Prayagraj?
qs.e: National Waterways 1 is located on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, connecting Haldia (Sagar) to Prayagraj. It is 1620 km long and was declared a national waterway in 1986. It connects major cities like Kolkata, Patna, Varanasi, and Prayagraj. This waterway boosts cargo transport, passenger travel, and tourism. Haldia port is an important terminal. National Waterways 1 is one of the busiest waterways in India and plays a vital role in economic activities.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of National Waterways 1? → 1620 km
☛ When was National Waterways 1 declared? → 1986
☛ Which rivers form National Waterways 1? → Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly
☛ Northern terminus of National Waterways 1? → Prayagraj
☛ Southern terminus of National Waterways 1? → Haldia (Sagar)

q: Which mode of transport is most suitable for transporting heavy and bulky goods over long distances?
qs.e: Railways are the most suitable mode for transporting heavy and bulky goods over long distances due to their high carrying capacity and cost-effectiveness. Trains can carry large volumes of goods at once, reducing per-unit cost. The extensive railway network connects various parts of the country, making long-distance transport efficient. Pipelines are only suitable for fluids and gases, roadways are less economical for heavy goods, and airways are too expensive.
qs.kf:
☛ Cheapest mode for heavy goods transport → Railways
☛ Carrying capacity of railways → Up to 10,000 tons
☛ Longest railway route in India → Dibrugarh-Kanyakumari (4,286 km)
☛ First railway line in India → Mumbai-Thane (1853)
☛ Ministry controlling railways → Ministry of Railways

q: In which year was the first metro line in India, between Esplanade and Bhowanipur in Kolkata, inaugurated—marking the beginning of metro rail services in the country?
qs.e: India's first metro line between Esplanade and Bhowanipur in Kolkata was inaugurated on October 24, 1984, marking the beginning of metro rail services in the country. The Kolkata Metro is India's first underground rail system, with construction starting in 1972. The initial stretch was 3.4 km long and included four stations. The project was overseen by Indian Railways. Over time, the line has been extended, and the Kolkata Metro now operates multiple lines.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was India's first metro rail service started? → Kolkata
☛ What was the length of the inaugural section of Kolkata Metro? → 3.4 km
☛ How many stations were in the first phase of Kolkata Metro? → Four
☛ When did construction of Kolkata Metro begin? → 1972
☛ Where did India's second metro system start? → Delhi (2002)

q: Why is air transport less popular for freight movement in India?
o: It is widely available in rural and remote villages.
It requires minimal infrastructure for operation.
It is expensive and ideal only for light, high-value goods.
It is slower and less efficient than water transport
qs.e: Air transport is less popular for freight movement in India because it is significantly expensive compared to other modes. High costs of aviation fuel, aircraft maintenance, and airport charges make it unaffordable for bulk or low-value goods. Therefore, air freight is suitable only for light, high-value items such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, and perishables, where time savings justify the expense. For heavy or low-value goods, road and rail transport offer cheaper alternatives. Additionally, air transport has limited capacity and can be affected by weather conditions. India's air cargo infrastructure is also relatively underdeveloped, especially in smaller cities. Hence, due to high cost and limited suitability, air transport remains less popular for freight movement.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of goods is air freight suitable for? → Light, high-value goods
☛ What is the main limitation of air transport? → High cost
☛ Which is India's largest cargo airport? → Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi
☛ Which organization is responsible for air cargo in India? → Airports Authority of India (AAI)
☛ Advantage of rail transport over air transport? → Lower cost and higher capacity

q: Which of the following transportation systems was primarily developed in India to serve colonial economic interests?
qs.e: The railway system in India was primarily developed to serve British colonial economic interests. Its main objectives were to transport raw materials from inland areas to ports for export and to create a market for British manufactured goods. The first passenger train ran between Mumbai and Thane in 1853. Railways connected different regions of India and transformed the economy, but the primary beneficiaries were British companies. The British built an extensive network to facilitate the exploitation of India's resources and strengthen their control over the colony.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the first train run in India? → 1853
☛ What was the route of the first train? → Mumbai-Thane
☛ What was the main colonial purpose of railways? → Export of raw materials and market for British goods
☛ Total railway network length in India? → Approximately 67,000 km
☛ Which ministry governs Railways? → Ministry of Railways

q: In which year was India’s first operational six-lane expressway, the approximately 95 km long Mumbai–Pune Expressway, inaugurated?
qs.e: India's first operational six-lane expressway, the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, approximately 95 km long, was inaugurated in 2002. It was constructed by the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) and its construction began in 1997. This expressway significantly reduced travel time between Mumbai and Pune. It was also Asia's first six-lane expressway. The total cost of the project was about Rs 1,630 crore.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of Mumbai-Pune Expressway → Approximately 95 km
☛ Year of inauguration of Mumbai-Pune Expressway → 2002
☛ Year of start of construction of Mumbai-Pune Expressway → 1997
☛ Constructing authority of Mumbai-Pune Expressway → MSRDC
☛ Total cost of Mumbai-Pune Expressway → Approximately Rs 1,630 crore

q: As per the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways of the Government of India, which port is known as the largest container port in India (as of May 2025)?
qs.e: As per the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways of the Government of India, as of May 2025, Nhava Sheva Port (Jawaharlal Nehru Port) is the largest container port in India. Located in Maharashtra, it handles approximately 55% of the country's total container traffic. Chennai, Kandla, and Paradip are major ports, but Nhava Sheva leads in container handling. This port is connected to key trade routes in Asia and Europe.
qs.kf:
☛ Alternative name of Nhava Sheva Port → Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT)
☛ Largest container port in India → Nhava Sheva
☛ State of Nhava Sheva → Maharashtra
☛ Largest container port (May 2025) → Nhava Sheva
☛ Oldest port in India → Chennai

q: The Golden Quadrilateral connects which of the following four major metro cities?
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral is a major highway network in India connecting four metro cities: Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, and Mumbai. It is part of the National Highway Development Project (NHDP) launched by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government. The total length is approximately 5,846 km, linking the major economic hubs of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of Golden Quadrilateral → Approx 5,846 km
☛ Project launched in → 2001
☛ Administered by → NHAI (National Highways Authority of India)
☛ Longest stretch → Delhi-Kolkata
☛ Shortest stretch → Mumbai-Chennai

q: As per Inland Waterways Authority of India, what is the approximate total length of navigable Inland waterways of India?
qs.e: According to the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), the total approximate length of navigable inland waterways in India is 14500 km. This includes rivers, canals, estuaries, and backwaters. However, only about 5500 km of this length is currently used for cargo and passenger transportation. Under IWAI, National Waterways (NW) have been declared, with the Ganga (NW-1), Brahmaputra (NW-2), and Kollam-Kottapuram canal (NW-3) being the major ones. The government is undertaking waterway development projects to enhance the utilization of these waterways.
qs.kf:
☛ Total navigable inland waterways length in India → 14500 km
☛ National Waterway-1 is which river → Ganga
☛ National Waterway-2 is which river → Brahmaputra
☛ Where is National Waterway-3 located → Kerala (Kollam-Kottapuram canal)
☛ Headquarters of Inland Waterways Authority of India → Noida

q: Which sea route is the busiest in the world?
o: The Cape of Good Hope sea route
qs.e: The North Atlantic sea route is the busiest sea route in the world. It is located between Europe and North America and passes through the northern part of the Atlantic Ocean. Some of the world's largest ports, such as Rotterdam, New York, and London, are situated on this route. This route is extremely important for trade, with a huge volume of cargo and containers transported here. In addition, the North Atlantic route also sees large-scale fishing and passenger transport. Compared to other routes, it is more developed and congested.
qs.kf:
☛ Busiest ocean route in the world → North Atlantic route
☛ Which two continents does the North Atlantic route connect → Europe and North America
☛ Which ocean does the Suez Canal route connect → Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea
☛ Which ocean does the Panama Canal route connect → Pacific and Atlantic Ocean
☛ Where is the Cape of Good Hope route located → off the coast of South Africa

q: The first passenger train in India was operated between ______.
qs.e: The first passenger train in India ran on 16 April 1853 between Bombay (now Mumbai) and Thane. It covered a distance of 34 km with 14 carriages. The train was operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR). Three locomotives named Sahib, Sindh, and Sultan were used to haul the train. This historic event marked the beginning of Indian Railways, which is one of the oldest railway networks in Asia.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of first passenger train → 16 April 1853
☛ Locomotives of first passenger train → Sahib, Sindh, and Sultan
☛ Operator of first passenger train → Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR)
☛ Distance of first passenger train → 34 km
☛ Construction of first rail line → Started in 1850 between Bombay and Thane

q: Name the recently added 17th zone of the Indian Railway.
qs.e: In 2024, Indian Railways added Kolkata Metro as the 17th railway zone. Previously, Kolkata Metro was under Eastern Railway. Now it has become an independent zone, which will improve its administration and development. The central government took this step under the plan to make metro railways separate zones. Kolkata Metro is the oldest metro network in India, which started operations in 1984. Currently, its total length is about 60 km, including several new corridors under construction. This zone provides rapid transit in Kolkata and its surrounding areas. The creation of this new zone aims to enhance efficiency and expansion of metro services.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the name of the 17th zone of Indian Railways? → Kolkata Metro
☛ When was Kolkata Metro established? → 1984
☛ What is the current approximate length of Kolkata Metro? → 60 km
☛ Under which railway zone was Kolkata Metro earlier? → Eastern Railway
☛ How many total zones does Indian Railways have (including Kolkata Metro)? → 17

q: Which is the longest railway line in the world?
qs.e: The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world, connecting Moscow, the capital of Russia, to the far-eastern port city of Vladivostok. It spans approximately 9,289 kilometers. This railway line crosses the entire European and Asian continents, making it the longest intercontinental rail journey globally. The construction of this project took place between 1891 and 1916 and has been crucial for Russia's economic and military development. The Trans-Siberian Railway played a significant role in connecting remote regions of Russia. It remains a vital transportation artery for the country, facilitating trade and travel across vast distances.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the total length of the Trans-Siberian Railway? → 9,289 km
☛ Which two cities does this railway connect? → Moscow and Vladivostok
☛ When was the Trans-Siberian Railway constructed? → 1891-1916
☛ What is the length of the Trans-Canadian Railway? → About 4,600 km
☛ What is the length of the Australian Trans-Continental Railway? → About 3,000 km

q: The Kolkata Port is located on which river?
qs.e: Kolkata Port is a major port in India, located in the state of West Bengal. It is situated on the banks of the Hooghly River, which is a distributary of the Ganges River. The Hooghly River flows into the Bay of Bengal, and the Kolkata Port uses this river route for maritime trade. This port is located on the eastern coast of India and is one of the oldest ports in the country. It is situated approximately 203 km inland from the sea on the Hooghly River. The Kolkata Port was built during the British period and remains important for trade.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is Kolkata Port located on? → Hooghly River
☛ Hooghly River is a distributary of which river? → Ganges
☛ Kolkata Port is in which state? → West Bengal
☛ How far is Kolkata Port from the sea? → Approximately 203 km
☛ When was Kolkata Port built? → British period

q: Which statement of the following is not true regarding national highway?
o: NH-44 is the longest national highway of India.
NH-8 is the shortest national highway in India.
NH-47A is the shortest national highway in India.
NHAI has the authority for the development, maintenance and management of national highways
qs.e: The shortest national highway in India is NH-47A, located in Kerala with a length of about 5.5 km. NH-8 (now part of NH-48) connects Delhi to Mumbai and is 1425 km long, not the shortest. NH-44 (formerly NH-7) runs from Srinagar to Kanyakumari and is the longest national highway in India with a length of 3745 km. NHAI (National Highways Authority of India) was established in 1988 and is responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of national highways. Hence, statement 2 is false.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest national highway in India → NH-44 (3745 km)
☛ Shortest national highway in India → NH-47A (5.5 km)
☛ Establishment of NHAI → 1988
☛ Headquarters of NHAI → New Delhi
☛ Oldest national highway → NH-1 (now part of NH-44)

q: Select the pair that is NOT matched correctly (the port to its location).
qs.e: Paradip Port is located in Odisha, not in Puducherry. It is a major port on the eastern coast of India, known for exporting coal, iron ore, etc. Tuticorin Port is in Tamil Nadu, Mormugao Port is in Goa, and Kandla Port is in Gujarat. All of these are major ports of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Paradip Port located? → Odisha
☛ Which is India's first private port? → Mundra Port, Gujarat
☛ Which state is Tuticorin Port in? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which state is Mormugao Port in? → Goa
☛ Which state is Kandla Port in? → Gujarat

q: The institution responsible for construction and maintenance of India's highways is:
qs.e: In India, the responsibility for construction, maintenance, and management of National Highways lies with the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI). NHAI was established in 1988 under the National Highway Authority of India Act. It functions under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. NHAI is responsible for the development, upgradation, and maintenance of highways across the country, including major projects like the National Highway Development Project (NHDP). Other options like Transport Authority of India or National Roads Safety Authority do not exist or have different functions.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NHAI established? → 1988
☛ Under which ministry does NHAI function? → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
☛ Who operates the National Highway Development Project? → NHAI
☛ Approximate total length of National Highways in India? → 1.44 lakh km (2024)
☛ Where is NHAI headquarters located? → New Delhi

q: Which agency has built and is maintaining the Leh-Manali Highway?
o: National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation (NHIDCL)
qs.e: The Leh-Manali Highway (NH-21) is built and maintained by the Border Road Organisation (BRO). BRO was established in 1960 after the India-China war to construct roads in border areas. It operates under the Ministry of Defence. The Leh-Manali Highway is one of the highest motorable roads in the world, located at an altitude of 13,058 feet. It connects Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh. BRO has completed several challenging projects such as the Atal Tunnel (Rohtang Pass) and the Zojila Pass Tunnel.
qs.kf:
☛ BRO Headquarters → Delhi
☛ Length of Leh-Manali Highway → 428 km
☛ NH-21 connects which cities → Leh and Manali
☛ Motto of BRO → "Path is Progress"
☛ Year of establishment of BRO → 1960

q: Kolkata metro rail was opened for commercial services in ___________.
qs.e: Kolkata Metro Rail is India's first metro rail system. It was inaugurated on 24 October 1984 and commercial services began on the same day. It ran on a 3.4 km stretch between Esplanade and Bhowanipur (now Netaji Bhawan). Kolkata Metro is operated by Indian Railways under the Eastern Railway. It preceded the Delhi Metro by about 18 years. The system is mostly underground and covers the north-south corridor of the city. Its construction took a long time due to high population density and high groundwater levels.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first metro rail → Kolkata Metro
☛ Inauguration of Kolkata Metro → 24 October 1984
☛ First operational section → Esplanade to Netaji Bhawan (3.4 km)
☛ Operator of Kolkata Metro → Indian Railways (Eastern Railway)
☛ Start of Delhi Metro → 2002

q: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was set up in:
qs.e: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was established in 1988 by an act of the Indian Parliament. It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. NHAI's primary objective is to construct, maintain, and manage national highways across India. The organization has played a crucial role in implementing major road projects such as the Golden Quadrilateral project. NHAI's headquarters is located in New Delhi. In 1998, the NHAI Act was amended, granting it more powers.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of NHAI establishment: → 1988
☛ NHAI works under which ministry: → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
☛ Headquarters of NHAI: → New Delhi
☛ Golden Quadrilateral project is associated with: → NHAI
☛ NHAI Act was amended in: → 1998

q: Which of the following is the Indian railway station having the highest number of platforms?
qs.e: The Indian railway station with the highest number of platforms is Howrah Junction, which has 23 platforms. It is located in West Bengal and is one of the busiest railway stations in India. New Delhi has 16 platforms, Sealdah has 19, and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus has 18 platforms. Howrah Junction was established in 1854 and also serves as the headquarters of the Eastern Railway. Hundreds of trains operate daily from this station.
qs.kf:
☛ Busiest railway station in India → Howrah Junction
☛ Total platforms at Howrah Junction → 23
☛ Year of establishment of Howrah Junction → 1854
☛ Howrah Junction is headquarters of which railway → Eastern Railway
☛ Number of platforms at New Delhi station → 16

q: Who said "The Indian railways brought people of diverse cultures together to contribute to India's freedom struggle"?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi highlighted the importance of Indian railways by stating that it brought people of diverse cultures together to contribute to India's freedom struggle. He considered railways as a medium that connects different parts of the country and promotes national unity. Gandhi often used train travel to communicate with people and strengthen the freedom movement. He believed that railways played a key role in breaking geographical and cultural barriers. This statement reflects his view that railways have a significant role in unifying Indian society.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Indian Railways start? → 1853
☛ Between which two cities did the first train run? → Mumbai-Thane
☛ Where is the headquarters of Indian Railways? → New Delhi
☛ In which movement did Gandhi use railways? → Non-cooperation Movement
☛ When was railways nationalized? → 1950

q: The Golden Quadrilateral is associated with _________.
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral is a major road development project in India connecting the four major metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai. It is part of the National Highway Development Project (NHDP) initiated by the Government of India. The objective is to strengthen the national highway network and boost economic growth. The Golden Quadrilateral is approximately 5,846 kilometers long and was launched in the year 2001. The construction is carried out by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). This project promotes road transport, not sea, rail, or air transport.
qs.kf:
☛ The Golden Quadrilateral is associated with which mode of transport? → Roads
☛ What is the length of the Golden Quadrilateral? → Approximately 5,846 km
☛ Which cities does the Golden Quadrilateral connect? → Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai
☛ In which year was the Golden Quadrilateral launched? → 2001
☛ Which agency constructs the Golden Quadrilateral? → NHAI

q: Sinhagad Express, the first double-decker train in India, plies daily between _______.
qs.e: Sinhagad Express, India's first double-decker train, was launched in 2011 and runs daily between Mumbai and Pune. It features double-decker coaches that provide better amenities and increased seating capacity, catering mainly to commuters and students. This train is part of Indian Railways' initiative to enhance capacity. Named after the historic Sinhagad Fort near Pune, it can reach a maximum speed of 160 km/h and all coaches are air-conditioned. The introduction of double-decker trains helps reduce congestion and provides a comfortable travel experience. The Sinhagad Express is a popular train on the Mumbai-Pune route, known for its punctuality and efficiency.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first double-decker train → Sinhagad Express
☛ Sinhagad Express launch year → 2011
☛ Coach type of Sinhagad Express → AC Chair Car
☛ Seating capacity of double-decker coach → 120 passengers per coach
☛ Sinhagad Express train number → 11025/11026

q: How many Indian states & Union territory does NH-44 cross?
qs.e: NH-44 is the longest national highway in India, running from north to south. It starts from Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) and ends at Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu). This highway passes through a total of 12 states/union territories: Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. NH-44 was previously known as NH-1 and NH-7, which were merged into a single highway in 2010. Its total length is approximately 3,745 km. It connects seven major cities of India and serves as a crucial transport corridor.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest national highway in India → NH-44
☛ Previous numbers of NH-44 → NH-1 and NH-7
☛ Total length of NH-44 → Approximately 3,745 km
☛ Northern terminus of NH-44 → Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir)
☛ Southern terminus of NH-44 → Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu)

q: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Railways'?
qs.e: Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856) is known as the 'Father of Indian Railways'. He introduced the first passenger train between Mumbai and Thane in 1853. He is also famous for the 'Doctrine of Lapse'. Dalhousie viewed railway expansion as crucial for administration and economy. He also contributed to the development of telegraph and postal services in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who laid the first railway line in India? → Lord Dalhousie
☛ When was the Mumbai-Thane railway line opened? → 1853
☛ Under which Governor-General did Indian railways begin? → Lord Dalhousie
☛ What was Lord Dalhousie's 'Doctrine of Lapse' related to? → Annexation of princely states
☛ What was the tenure of Lord Dalhousie? → 1848-1856

q: The _______ is responsible for the construction and maintenance of national highways.
qs.e: The construction and maintenance of national highways is the responsibility of the Central government. These highways form the primary road network of the country and are managed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). The central government develops them in the national interest, while state governments handle state highways and district roads. According to the National Highways Act, 1956, the ownership and control of these roads lie with the central government. This system ensures integrated and efficient transportation across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Who manages national highways? → NHAI
☛ Who is responsible for state highways? → State government
☛ Longest national highway in India? → NH 44
☛ Year of National Highways Act? → 1956
☛ Scheme for rural road development? -> Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana

q: Which two places are connected by National Waterway-2?
qs.e: National Waterway-2 is located on the Brahmaputra River in Assam. It connects Sadiya to Dhubri, covering a distance of 891 km. This waterway is managed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI). It is one of the longest national waterways in the country and boosts transportation and trade in the north-eastern region. The Brahmaputra River is known for its vast water flow, making this waterway suitable for both cargo and passenger transport. It was declared a national waterway in 2016.
qs.kf:
☛ National Waterway-1 → Prayagraj to Haldia (Ganga River)
☛ National Waterway-3 → Kottapuram to Kollam (West Coast Canal)
☛ National Waterway-4 → Krishna-Godavari river system
☛ National Waterway-5 → Brahmani-Mahanadi-East Coast Canal
☛ National Waterway-6 → Barak River in Assam

q: The National Waterway 1 (NW 1) in the country are already operational/ navigable between which stretch among the following?
qs.e: National Waterway 1 (NW 1) is the longest national waterway in India, spanning the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system from Haldia (West Bengal) to Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh), covering about 1620 km. This stretch is fully operational and navigable, facilitating cargo and passenger transport. Among the options, Dhubri-Sadiya is part of NW 2 (Brahmaputra River), Kottapuram-Kollam is on NW 3 (West Coast Canal), and Kakinada-Puducherry is an extension of NW 4. The Haldia-Prayagraj stretch is a key route under NW 1, enabling trade and economic activities.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of NW 1 → Approx 1620 km
☛ Route of NW 1 → Haldia to Prayagraj
☛ NW 2 is on which river → Brahmaputra River
☛ NW 3 is located on → West Coast Canal
☛ Longest National Waterway → NW 1

q: The _________ is the longest section of the Golden Quadrilateral super highway.
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) is India's largest road network connecting four major metropolitan cities. The entire construction was executed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). The Kolkata-Chennai section is the longest because it covers 1,684 km along the eastern coast. This section passes through states like West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. Its length is greater compared to other sections; for instance, the Mumbai-Delhi section is about 1,419 km, the Delhi-Kolkata section is 1,453 km, and the Chennai-Mumbai section is 1,290 km long.
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of Golden Quadrilateral → 5,846 km
☛ Shortest section → Chennai-Mumbai (1,290 km)
☛ Project launched by → Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee in 2001
☛ Managing authority → NHAI (National Highways Authority of India)
☛ Connected cities → Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata

q: Which of the following is India's largest underground pipeline?
qs.e: The HBJ (Hazira-Bijaypur-Jagdishpur) pipeline is India's largest underground natural gas pipeline. It has a total length of over 2,700 kilometers. This pipeline connects Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh, and is crucial for energy supply. It is operated by GAIL (Gas Authority of India Limited). This pipeline transports natural gas to northern and western India. The Kundla-Bathinda, Barauni-Kanpur, and Haldia-Kolkata pipelines are also important, but HBJ is the largest.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is India's first oil pipeline? → Naharkatiya-Guwahati pipeline
☛ Which is the major organization for pipeline transport? → GAIL (Gas Authority of India Limited)
☛ Which is India's longest oil pipeline? → Paradip-Raebareli pipeline
☛ Which is the world's longest pipeline? → Druzhba pipeline (Russia)
☛ Which states does the HBJ pipeline connect? → Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh

q: In which city is the famous Howrah Bridge located?
qs.e: Howrah Bridge is located in the city of Kolkata. It is a famous bridge built over the Hooghly River, connecting Kolkata and Howrah. The bridge was constructed in 1943 and is one of the busiest bridges in the world. It is a cantilever bridge, meaning it is built without any supports. Its total length is 705 meters. Howrah Bridge is a major landmark of India and is used by millions of people every day.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Howrah Bridge built? → Hooghly River
☛ When was Howrah Bridge constructed? → 1943
☛ What type of bridge is Howrah Bridge? → Cantilever
☛ What is the total length of Howrah Bridge? → 705 meters
☛ Which two cities does Howrah Bridge connect? → Kolkata and Howrah

q: 'Uthagamandalam' is the other name of which of these hill stations?
qs.e: Uthagamandalam is the original name of Ooty, a famous hill station in the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil Nadu. It was established in 1819 by the British East India Company. Ooty is known for its cool climate, tea plantations, and the Nilgiri Wildlife Sanctuary. It is often called the 'Queen of Hill Stations'. Kodaikanal, Nainital and Darjeeling are also popular hill stations but Uthagamandalam specifically refers to Ooty.
qs.kf:
☛ Uthagamandalam is also known as → Ooty
☛ Ooty is located in which state → Tamil Nadu
☛ Ooty was established in → 1819
☛ Ooty lies in which hill range → Nilgiri
☛ Nickname of Ooty → Queen of Hill Stations

q: According to the basic road statistics (2017-18) provided by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, which state has the largest total surface road length in India?
qs.e: According to the basic road statistics (2017-18) provided by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Maharashtra has the largest total surface road length in India. This figure reflects the state's extensive road network, including national highways, state highways, district roads, and rural roads. Maharashtra's total surface road length was approximately 2.32 lakh km, ranking it first in the country. It is followed by Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. This data highlights the importance of roads in the state's economic development and connectivity.
qs.kf:
☛ State with the longest total surface road length (2017-18) → Maharashtra
☛ Second longest total surface road length state → Uttar Pradesh
☛ Third longest total surface road length state → Rajasthan
☛ Approximate total surface road length of Maharashtra → 2.32 lakh km
☛ Data source year → 2017-18

q: Which of the following is the longest train route in India as of 2023?
qs.e: The longest train route in India is the Dibrugarh-Kanniyakumari Vivek Express, covering approximately 4,154 km. It connects the northeastern state of Assam to the southern tip of India at Kanniyakumari and takes about 82 hours. The train stops at 57 stations and passes through 9 states. This route showcases the vastness of the Indian Railways network and the geographical diversity of the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Train name between Dibrugarh-Kanniyakumari → Vivek Express
☛ Total distance of this route → Approx 4,154 km
☛ Travel time → Approx 82 hours
☛ Number of states it passes through → 9 states
☛ Train number → 22503/22504

q: Which of the following ports is NOT correctly linked to its location?
qs.e: Visakhapatnam Port is located in Andhra Pradesh, not Telangana. It is a major port on the east coast of India and a natural deep-water port. Tuticorin Port is correctly linked to Tamil Nadu, Kochi Port to Kerala, and Mormugao Port to Goa. Visakhapatnam Port is also known as the 'Jewel of the East Coast' and is an important base for the Indian Navy.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Visakhapatnam Port in? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Which state is Tuticorin Port in? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which state is Kochi Port in? → Kerala
☛ Which state is Mormugao Port in? → Goa
☛ Which is the oldest port in India? → Chennai Port

q: Which of the following has built the Atal Tunnel?
qs.e: The Atal Tunnel has been built by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO). It is the longest highway tunnel in the world, located at the Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh. The tunnel is 9.02 km long and connects Manali to the Lahaul-Spiti valley. It is named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The project was approved in 2010 and was dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 3 October 2020. The tunnel remains open for traffic throughout the year, boosting tourism and economic activities in the Lahaul-Spiti region.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Atal Tunnel? → Border Roads Organisation (BRO)
☛ What is the length of Atal Tunnel? → 9.02 km
☛ In which state is Atal Tunnel located? → Himachal Pradesh
☛ On which pass is Atal Tunnel situated? → Rohtang Pass
☛ When was Atal Tunnel inaugurated? → 3 October 2020

q: In reference to air transport of India, what is the full form of AERA?
o: Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India
Aviation Economic Regulatory Authority of India
qs.e: AERA stands for Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India. It is a statutory body established under the AERA Act of 2008. Its primary function is the economic regulation of airports, including determining aerodrome charges and tariffs for services. It sets the maximum charges for major airports like Delhi and Mumbai and monitors the operations of private airports. AERA's headquarters is located in New Delhi. The authority ensures fair pricing and promotes efficiency in the airport sector.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of AERA? → Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India
☛ When was the AERA Act passed? → 2008
☛ Where is the headquarters of AERA? → New Delhi
☛ For which airports does AERA set charges? → Major airports
☛ What is the main function of AERA? → Economic regulation of airports

q: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport is situated in which of the following cities?
qs.e: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport is located in Kolkata, West Bengal. It is named after the Indian freedom fighter Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. It is the main airport serving Kolkata and is also known as Dum Dum Airport. It is the busiest airport in Eastern India and the fifth busiest in the country. Its airport code is CCU. The airport was built in 1924.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport located? → Kolkata
☛ What is the other name of this airport? → Dum Dum Airport
☛ What is its airport code? → CCU
☛ In which state is it located? → West Bengal
☛ When was it built? → 1924

q: Which of the following bridges is constructed over the Brahmaputra River in India?
qs.e: The Dhola-Sadiya Bridge, also known as Bhupen Hazarika Setu, is built over the Lohit River, a tributary of the Brahmaputra, connecting Assam and Arunachal Pradesh. It is the longest bridge in India and was inaugurated in 2017. The Howrah Bridge is over the Hooghly River, Mahatma Gandhi Setu is over the Ganges River, and Pamban Bridge is over the sea.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest bridge over Brahmaputra → Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Dhola-Sadiya)
☛ Longest bridge in India → Dr. Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Assam)
☛ Longest bridge over Ganges → Mahatma Gandhi Setu (Bihar)
☛ Howrah Bridge is over which river → Hooghly River (West Bengal)
☛ Where is Pamban Bridge located → Rameswaram (Tamil Nadu)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which transport system is most efficient in terms of energy consumption per tonne-km in India?
qs.e: In terms of energy consumption per tonne-km, inland waterways are the most efficient transport system in India. This is because water offers low friction, requiring less energy to move cargo compared to road or rail, where higher friction and weight increase energy use. Airways are the least efficient due to high fuel consumption to overcome air resistance. India has an extensive inland waterway network of 14,500 km, primarily used for transporting bulk goods like coal, iron ore, and construction materials. It is the most cost-effective and eco-friendly mode of transport, though its utilization remains limited in the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Most energy-efficient transport system → Inland waterways
☛ Total length of inland waterways in India → 14,500 km
☛ National Waterways Act → Passed in 2007
☛ Longest national waterway → NW-1 (Ganga River, 1620 km)
☛ Main advantage of waterways → Low energy consumption and low pollution

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (20/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which major port is NOT located on the western coast of India?
qs.e: Major ports on the western coast of India include Kandla (Gujarat), Cochin (Kerala), and Mangalore (Karnataka). These are all located on the Arabian Sea coast. Visakhapatnam is situated on the eastern coast of India in Andhra Pradesh and is a major port on the Bay of Bengal. Therefore, the port NOT located on the western coast is Visakhapatnam. It is India's second-largest port and a natural deep-water port.
qs.kf:
☛ Northernmost port on western coast → Kandla
☛ Southernmost port on western coast → Cochin
☛ Largest port on eastern coast → Visakhapatnam
☛ Major port in Gujarat → Kandla
☛ Major port in Kerala → Cochin

q: India's longest road-cum-rail bridge, connecting Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, is called the:
qs.e: Bogibeel Bridge is India's longest road-cum-rail bridge, connecting Assam and Arunachal Pradesh. It is built over the Brahmaputra River and has a total length of 4.94 kilometers. The bridge was inaugurated on 25 December 2018 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It is a double-decker bridge with a road on the upper deck and a railway track on the lower deck. This bridge is strategically and economically important for the development of Northeast India.
qs.kf:
☛ India's longest road-cum-rail bridge → Bogibeel Bridge
☛ River over which Bogibeel Bridge is built → Brahmaputra River
☛ States connected by Bogibeel Bridge → Assam and Arunachal Pradesh
☛ Length of Bogibeel Bridge → 4.94 kilometers
☛ Inauguration date of Bogibeel Bridge → 25 December 2018

q: Which port is one of the oldest artificial ports on the eastern coast?
qs.e: Chennai port is one of the oldest artificial ports on the eastern coast of India. Its construction began in 1881 and it is the second largest container port. It is located on the Bay of Bengal and is a major hub for trade in South India. It was formerly known as Madras port. It is an artificial port built with breakwaters and berths.
